bio_text: 4 Charles Prime Rib is a historic dining establishment located in New York's West Village, offering a warm and inviting atmosphere reminiscent of a bygone era. With its plush leather seating, crystal chandeliers, and dark wood accents, the restaurant provides a sophisticated yet comfortable setting for guests to enjoy classic cuts of steak, seafood, and prime rib, complemented by a robust selection of drinks and an exceptional wine list. The restaurant specializes in prime rib and classic steakhouse fare, focusing on high-quality cuts of meat and seafood. The menu features a full dinner selection, with brunch available on weekends, ensuring a diverse dining experience.
menu_items: Shrimp Cocktail - cocktail sauce, dijonnaise - $29.99
Sizzling Shrimp Scampi - garlic bread, chilies, parsley - $29.99
Alaskan King Crab - 3/4 lb - $124.99
Otoro Tartare w/ Caviar - bluefin tuna belly, yuasa white soy, brown butter toast - $125.99
Fresh Oysters - $4.99
Baked Crab Cake - 1/2 lb, preserved lemon, remoulade - $34.99
review_snippets: Went for a private event and sat in the private dining room. The food was out of this world!! If and that is a BIG IF, you can get a reservation you must eat here. There are only 9 tables in this spot. We had the crabcakes, sizzling shrimp appetizers. Ceaser salad with salmon. Menu courses were the wagyu cheese burger, prime rib and wagyu porterhouse. The sides we had were Elote Style Corn and Truffle Mac and Cheese. You are not going to have a better meal anywhere in Manhattan nor the entire country!! Highly recommend you do what you can to go here and enjoy as much of the menu as you can!!! (5 stars)

My review is slightly biased by the “untouchable” reputation this restaurant has built and the pure joy that came with just being able to eat here. Overall the food is good. It’s not the most incredible restaurant in NYC for the price, but you will have a good meal. Loved the bacon, steak, and truffle mac. The burger was also good and I appreciate that they make it a show with the glove and egg cutting. Only thing I was meh on was the French dip but I think that’s just because it was served cold. The ambience is great. Very institutional feeling. I like that it’s an intimate dining space, well decorated, dimly lit - you feel like you’re dining among NYC’s elite. Service was great. Very personable staff and clearly they can recruit the best of the best. I just wish I was on their list so I could eat here more regularly but alas. Well worth (5 stars)

Very hard to get a res but this place absolutely lived up to the hype for me. Prime rib was the best I’ve ever had. Burger was amazing (maybe top 2 in nyc) and so was the chocolate cream pie. French dip and truffle mac and cheese were also good but not must-gets. (5 stars)

Finally managed to get into 4 Charles Prime and it was worth it. How to do it: If you are a walk-in, the restaurant opens at 4pm, if you are a party of 2 or 4 (any larger is not worth trying) I suggest someone be in line by 230/3pm. We arrived at 3pm and were the 4th party in line (party of 2) and just before opening, the host accepted the first two parties and we were entered into a lottery slot for any potential openings before 8pm and we managed to get a 630 slot. Onto the experience… the decor is intimate and dark/rustic and all of the staff were very kind, accommodating and professional. The wine and cocktail lists are extensive and offer many delicious options. We ordered a lot of food, since it may be our only visit. Be prepared to take some home, as the portions are large and rich. The sizzling shrimp scampi starter was excellent, filled with flavor and accompanied by crispy garlic bread. The cheeseburger was also excellent, though adding the bacon and egg makes for a rich and filling experience, if we return I would skip the bacon and egg. The star of the night was the French dip sandwich, which we shared. The meat was so flavorful and the roll had a perfect crisp. The dip and horseradish together made for a perfect dish. I also recommend the truffle Mac & Cheese. We took most of it home, and it heats up well the next day. If you have room for dessert, the chocolate cream pie is a must. It’s a rough place to get in, but it made for a nice experience, and worth the hype. (5 stars)

bio_text: 53 is a contemporary Asian restaurant located in Midtown Manhattan, offering an audacious journey of Asian flavors within a beautifully modern, three-story space. The restaurant artfully blends the varied taste profiles of Asian cuisine with the artistic vibe of New York City, creating a vibrant dining experience that is both chic and inviting. With a bustling main dining room by day and a glowing ambiance by night, 53 also provides intimate private dining options, all beneath the iconic MoMA. 53 focuses on an elevated blend of Asian cuisine with a contemporary edge, featuring unique dishes that highlight the marriage of Asian flavors. The menu includes a three-course dim sum prix fixe and a premium lunch set, showcasing chef-driven bites and inventive plates. Founded by Ahmass Fakahany, CEO of the Altamarea Group, 53 is inspired by his nearly 10 years living in Asia. The culinary team is led by acclaimed Chef Akmal Anuar, who has a rich background in contemporary Asian cuisine, having started in his parents' hawker stand in Singapore.

review_snippets: This is a very nice Asian fusion Chinese restaurant with a great atmosphere, but you need to make reservations in advance. Overall, the flavors are very solid. I highly recommend their Foie Gras Custard (Foie Gras Steamed Egg) — it was incredibly rich, and the addition of mushrooms enhanced the overall umami. However, the Foie Gras on Toast set had a slight flaw: the toast was a bit over-charred, which slightly overpowered the dish, and the Eel component was hard to taste. The Lamb Ribs were decent but nothing extraordinary. The strong barbecue glaze slightly masked the natural flavor of the meat, though the preparation was quite creative. The Kung Pao Quail was tasty and innovative — so tender that you wouldn’t even guess it was quail. The Black Cod Clay Pot with Rice was rather average, nothing remarkable. Overall, this restaurant is quite innovative. The flavors and techniques are authentic while keeping the creative fusion style. I would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a unique dining experience. (4 stars)

I went here with my friends, and everything this restaurant served deserves a standing ovation! The food is amazingly good—every dish comes with beautiful presentation, and you can really tell they use high-quality ingredients. I loved everything; even their simple cucumber salad was incredible—spicy, fresh, nutty, and perfectly balanced. I absolutely love this place! The ambience is great, and our server was very friendly and attentive. If you’re looking for a restaurant that serves food made with love, you must visit 53. Shout-out to Chef Mark, Chef Adam, and the entire team for the amazing food. Highly recommended! ❤️ (5 stars)

The food and environment were very nice tho overpriced imo. It’s not a quiet place so expect to talk loudly. Unfortunately the main negative was the spotty service. A restaurant like this needs to do better than with accommodating guest food restrictions by making the experience feel seamless. My partner is Celiac, so gluten is an absolute no. When booking, I made sure to add that to the dietary restrictions section. The lady at the front acknowledge that when we walked in. I would expect that at a restaurant like this, our waiter would also know by the time we get to the table, but he didn’t and we told him ourselves, no problem. He was kind enough to outline on the menu which items he thought were gluten-free, so we only ordered from his list. When the clay pot arrived with table side finish, I had a hunch and decided to triple check with the chef if the soy sauce was infact gluten free… it wasn’t… that is unacceptable considering the potential severity of reactions that Celiacs can have to gluten. The chef was kind enough to take the dish back and remake it with GF soy sauce. It was quite disappointing to see that not only the staff failed to communicate such details, but when specifically told, our waiter failed to communicate that to the kitchen. I don’t think I expected too much considering that it’s a health concern and this is not a cheap restaurant. I would not expect this at a small casual spot. But a $$$$ restaurant needs to do much better on service to justify its prices on a bowl of rice with a small pice of fish. (2 stars)

Interesting restaurant with good food and friendly staff. I really liked the ground-floor interior — simple yet elegant. The main dining area, however, is two levels down, so it feels like a basement with no windows or fresh air. While the design is tasteful, you do get the sense of sitting in a box. The staff were genuinely helpful and warm, not robotic, which made the experience pleasant. The food was tasty and well-prepared. Overall, it’s a nice place for a business dinner or a quiet evening meal. (4 stars)

bio_text: 6 Restaurant is an intimate dining establishment located in Carroll Gardens, Brooklyn, offering a unique blend of New American cuisine infused with classic European and South American flavors. The atmosphere is rich and comforting, providing a warm setting where inventive dishes not only look appealing but also deliver exceptional taste. The restaurant focuses on New American cuisine, incorporating elements from European and South American culinary traditions. The menu features a variety of inventive dishes that emphasize both visual appeal and flavor.

review_snippets: We celebrated our anniversary at L’Adresse, th staff made us feel so special. They offered complimentary sparking wine & macaroons. We ordered a focaccia & crispy calamari as appetizers. My main course was a seafood risotto which was pretty good. The desert was great too. It is nice ambience and our server was helpful and friendly. I would definitely come back. (5 stars)

I searched it up… Walked a short U… and walla, I entered a restaurant that looked like a Hotel at 1st glance! Inside ambiance matched my mood and the 3 people that spoke with me were all pleasant! LOBSTER CARBONARA w/ Gold Caviar topping. Natalia & Hita were my servers & both very polite! (5 stars)

Upscale and worth it, I tried the truffle burger and it was delicious. Beef tartare too, and seafood risotto. The bartender is also too quality - mixed me a Monkey 47 martini with a dash of orange bitters and a slice of orange peel, the perfect complement to the meal! (5 stars)

My girlfriend and I had a great time at ladrese and even more amazing and delicious food. The salmon was cooked to perfection. However, the most pleasantly surprising items on the menu were syrniki and sea buckhorn tea which were my true favorites as well as Frank (who was not on the menu unfortunately ) but he provided not only a great service but he also knows some Russian. definitely coming back! 🌸 (5 stars)

bio_text: 63 Clinton is an intimate dining destination located on the Lower East Side, offering a modern American fare that emphasizes seasonal ingredients and global influences. Co-owned by Michelin-starred chef Sam Clonts and his longtime friend Raymond Trinh, the restaurant aims to create a welcoming atmosphere for friends, neighbors, and visitors seeking a memorable culinary experience that balances comfort and elegance. The restaurant features a seasonal tasting menu that showcases modern American cuisine with global influences. Signature techniques include a focus on local ingredients and innovative preparations, complemented by an eclectic wine list and a cocktail menu rooted in American classics. Sam Clonts and Raymond Trinh opened 63 Clinton after nearly a decade of working together in New York City. Sam Clonts is a Michelin-starred chef who has worked in prestigious kitchens, including Chef's Table at Brooklyn Fare, while Raymond Trinh has a strong background in both front and back of house operations, having also earned a Michelin star at Bar Uchu.
menu_items: Shima aji - rutabaga, white asparagus, chiltepin
The breakfast taco - ajitama, hash brown, smoked trout roe
Seasonal taco - sugar snap peas, tahini, plum cascabel
Bread & butter - jalapeno cornbread, sourdough tortilla
Escargot - whipped tofu, pho fat
Green asparagus - razor clams, green chartreuse, white asparagus
review_snippets: Service and vibe is on point. But I have to say the food is a bit disappointing to me. The desserts that blends chefs childhood memory was a great story. Unfortunately both the cheesecake the taco fell short with their overwhelming sweetness. The highlight to me is the cornbread with varied sauces and the breakfast taco is also delicious. However, But the other dishes don’t live up to my expectation as a Michelin restaurant. Whether the dish is too salty or is fairly mediocre. Purely our table’s opinions. (3 stars)

A Friday night escape was truly made memorable with Sixty Three Clinton and the entire team. Had the pleasure of meeting both chefs, Sam and Ray who show passion not only in their dishes but the way they greet and interact with their patrons. From the moment you step into their place you feel like you’re at home with a wood burning fireplace awaiting you to get comfortable for a home cooked meal. From start to finishing the experience was elevated with each cuisine, friendly wait staff and the ambiance of the restaurant. Our server Simon was fabulous. Each dish was displayed with such passion and decor with flavor profiles that left me guessing what the ingredients of each dish may be. The caviar hand roll is a must try, the sourdough tortilla left a core memory from the time my grandmother made her version of the tortillas and the Muhammara spread was spot on. The Le Boeuf was the savory dish one needs on a cold night like tonight with a perfectly cooked meat over a wood burning oven. The dessert was on a different level where I had to ask for seconds- the cheesecake was delicious and the Choco Taco is a must have in all their menus. I will absolutely be back with my family to enjoy these delicious dishes and experience the wonderful cuisines of Chef Ray and Sam. (5 stars)

A top-shelf experience from finish to start. Service was friendly and personal, somehow both low-key and refined at the same time. I was dining alone, which sometimes can feel odd, but the staff made me feel very comfortable and welcome, with just the right balance of friendly, casual interaction and leaving me to enjoy/absorb the dishes. They were incredibly skilled at this, it must be a cultivated vibe, and it’s a good one. The playlist was great -I wasn’t expecting Joy Division and the Cure, but somehow it was perfect. The volume was correct and unlike some places, I could hear all the descriptions easily. The food was wonderful- real food with unexpected flavor profiles, which actually worked and weren’t just for the sake of concept. A nice blend of the familiar with surprise secondary notes that elevated every dish. Someone’s review mentioned that the breakfast taco was salty, and for half a bite I had that same reaction, but there were other flavors that came behind that upfront saltiness which let me know I was in for something smart. I think the hamachi was my favorite, but every dish was really great. Somehow they gave me the best piece of bread I had on my trip to New York, and the best butter. It came dead center in the meal, and it was absolutely perfect, exactly what I needed at that moment. The final dessert was so, so good. I’ll never look at carrot cake the same. The pacing was exactly right, as was the amount of food. I added on everything, but in retrospect might have kept my add-ons to just the hand roll, most of the other dishes were fine without the extras. Really happy I chose this for my last night in NYC. (5 stars)

Sixty Three Clinton is exceptional. Each dish was creative, thoughtful, and beautifully presented — with flavors that blew us away us throughout the meal. Portions were generous without ever feeling over the top, and the wine pairings were thoughtful and perfectly matched to each dish. The service was highly attentive and perfectly paced, and they did an outstanding job with dairy- and gluten-free accommodations. Sitting at the kitchen counter made this experience even more special, watching the team have fun with each other while executing perfect service. Overall, this was one of the best dining experiences I’ve had — and the value makes this a must-visit. (5 stars)

The service was highly attentive and perfectly paced, and they did an outstanding job with dairy- and gluten-free accommodations. Sitting at the kitchen counter made this experience even more special, watching the team have fun with each other while executing perfect service. Overall, this was one of the best dining experiences I’ve had — and the value makes this a must-visit. (5 stars)

The restaurant focuses on innovative cuisine that highlights seasonal ingredients and bold flavors. review_snippets: Great spot! My fiancé booked a reservation for 8282 for Valentine’s Day and it was very nice. We got the Valentine’s special menu as well as two regular menu items. My fiancé and I’s favorite was definitely the beef steak tartare as well as the cheesy tteok-bokki. The flavors were great and the service was excellent. Would definitely come back here to try their other tartares! (The white chocolate matcha pudding was also really good!) (5 stars)

Absolutely amazing experience at 8282. Every single dish we ordered was incredibly delicious — not one miss. The flavors were thoughtful, well-balanced, and memorable from start to finish. This is the kind of place where you’re already planning your next visit before you even leave. Definitely coming back again. Highly recommend! (5 stars)

Absolutely amazing Korean food—every dish was on point and full of flavor. The customer service was exceptional: attentive, friendly, and professional. The vibe and mood are perfect—stylish, lively, and great for drinks as well. Ideal spot for both dinner and a night out. Highly recommend. (5 stars)

This modern Korean spot in LES is truly a gem, and I absolutely loved it. The interior is cozy but tables are a bit small, so I recommend reservations if you are come with a group. Service was absolutely stellar—they were so kind to talk to, attentive, and patient. We got their chestnut makgeoli to drink and for food we got their: grilled octopus, ebi ikura uni tartare, clam sujaebi, scallop jjajjang boribap, 8282 steak, and yuzu panna cotta. Everything was phenomenal. Their chestnut makgeoli was creamy and a delightful pair to the meal. Their grilled octopus was probably the favorite of the night as it was flavorful, amazing texture, and had great sauces. The ebi ikura uni tartare was also good and came with seaweed, but there was nothing super crazy/different about it (compared to other restaurants). I also loved the broth for the clam sujaebi but I felt like this leaned on the more modern side—the sujaebi was a bit different than traditionally, and the broth was also more seafood forward. The scallop jjajjangboribap was good but I wish the jjajjang sauce was a bit stronger/more saucey. And, the steak was amazing. The yuzu matcha panna cotta was the perfect way to wrap up the meal, and by the end of this I was stuffed. Absolutely loved this dinner and I highly recommend. (5 stars)

bio_text: Çka Ka Qëllu is a rustic yet stylish restaurant located in New York City, showcasing traditional Albanian and Kosovan dishes in a warm environment adorned with 18th and 19th-century artifacts. The restaurant offers a unique dining experience that combines the rich flavors of Mediterranean cuisine with a focus on healthy, fresh ingredients, making it a destination for those seeking authentic Eastern European culinary traditions. The restaurant specializes in modern Albanian and Kosovan cuisine, featuring a diverse menu that includes traditional dishes and contemporary interpretations. Signature techniques include slow-cooking in earthenware pots and the use of fresh, seasonal ingredients to create flavorful, nutritious meals. The owner, Ramiz, was inspired to open Çka Ka Qëllu after his son sought authentic Albanian cuisine in New York City. After years of research and collecting artifacts, he established the restaurant to bring Albanian culture and cuisine to the city.
menu_items: PICKLED PEPPER - Stuffed with a medley of seasonal pickled vegetables, prepared in the authentic, time honored way - $6.80
CHEESE PICKLED PEPPER - A traditional combination of creamy cheese and pickled pepper - $9.50
ROASTED PEPPER - Sautéed with garlic and olive oil - $8.40
PEPPER DIP - A rich, velvety blend of roasted peppers and cheese for a bold, savory taste - $8.40
SAUSAGE DIP - Slow-smoked sausage and two cheeses melt together in this creamy, savory dip - $9.50
TARATOR - Chilled yogurt blend with minced cucumber and garlic drizzled with parsley - $8.20
review_snippets: A cultural enrichment type restaurant. It's a quaint restaurant that gives you the feeling of being in Albania. You can tell the owners have pride in their culture. Truly a hug from Albania that makes you feel like you’re there. The authentic flavors did not disappoint. The staff is courteous and professional and super accommodating. The food over exceeded our expectations. Best dining experience I’ve had this week in NYC. (5 stars)

My first time trying Albanian food. It was very delicious and wholesome. The restaurant itself feels like you’re entering someone’s home. It felt very warm and cozy. The dishes tasted home cooked too. The flavors were full without feeling too heavy. The lamb was super tender and not gamey. Service was excellent and our waitress gave great recommendations! Id love to come back to try more of the dishes. (4 stars)

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Absolutely amazing experience at Ça Ka Qëllue in Manhattan! The food was outstanding—rich flavors, beautifully prepared, and truly authentic. Every dish on the table was delicious and comforting. The service was top-notch as well. John was incredibly attentive, friendly, and made sure we were taken care of the entire time. You can really feel the passion for both food and hospitality here. Highly recommend this place if you’re in NYC—can’t wait to come back! (5 stars)

Albanian food is completely underrated and doesn't get nearly the attention it deserves. This was my first time trying this cuisine and I wasn't disappointed. I had the pepper dip appetizer which reminded me of a mildly spicy and perfectly balanced fondue served with fresh baked bread similar to a pita or puffy Naan. For the entrée, I had the Tava Kosi, which is braised lamb served over an egg custard. The custard reminded me of the inside of a quiche but with a much softer texture. I went for Christmas dinner while visiting New York and the atmosphere and ambiance inside the restaurant could not have been better. The interior looks like an old European tavern with rustic brick walls. Cannot recommend this restaurant highly enough. Extremely tasty food at an amazingly low price point. (5 stars)

bio_text: ABCV is a vibrant American restaurant located in New York, NY, that champions a plant-forward dining experience. Helmed by renowned chef Jean-Georges Vongerichten and culinary director Neal Harden, the restaurant offers a luminous and inviting atmosphere that reflects its commitment to wellness and sustainability. With a focus on organic and innovative dishes, ABCV welcomes all diners to explore its creative menu, which is designed to inspire a cultural shift towards plant-based eating. ABCV specializes in plant-forward, sustainable, and organic cuisine. The menu features a variety of vegan and gluten-free options, with an emphasis on wellness through food. Signature techniques include the use of tonics and elixirs that promote health and vitality. ABCV sprouted from abc kitchen and is inspired by Jean-Georges’ personal journey as well as the cultural shift towards a plant-based future. The restaurant has been recognized in the New York Times Top 100.
menu_items: cherry cacao protein - morello cherries, wild blueberries, coconut water, almond butter, plant based protein powder - $18
sea buckthorn - sea buckthorn, ginger, saffron, banana, agave, tahitian vanilla bean - $17
pollen + pine - pollen, maple peanut butter, dates, banana, almond milk, himalayan salt - $17
light & fresh harry’s berries - strawberries, yogurt, rhubarb compote, granola - $23
wild blueberry bowl - toasted oats, maple peanut butter, dried and fresh seasonal fruits - $21
dosa - yogurt, avocado, sprouts - $24
review_snippets: We tried the Pre Fix menu and the course meal allowed us to try a little bit of all the flavors that the restaurant offered. We enjoyed every course. Peas hummus and butternut soup were a great start to the exciting vegetarian journey. All the three chutney that accompanied the dosa were perfect compliments and we polished it all. Yam was perfectly seasoned and tye dessert can't get any better. This is a must visit place for anyone who enjoys good vegetarian food. (5 stars)

We had a reservation for 7pm and were a party of 4. The service at the restaurant was great. We were served by Devi and Emily, both very jovial girlies xx Now, speaking about the food, we ordered 13 dishes and 4 drinks. The alcoholic drinks were fab, but the non-alcoholic mocktails were not tasty at all. All three non alcoholic drinks tasted like fruity water. Food however, was amazing! I’m attaching photos of each dish we ate, but basically all the dishes were rich in flavor, had good presentation, and ALL VEGGIE! Portion sizes were from small to medium, but that’s something you expect at such restaurants. So, not complaining here at all! Overall, a four out of five for the restaurant. (4 stars)

For a moment forget the meat. Great place for carnivores and vegans alike. A rabbit hole of flavors to delight your palate for a night. Manhattan priced but the service is exceptional and the food excellent. If you are vegetarian or vegan and here to visit and want a special night out with the loved ones or live here locally for a special occasion. This is a must try for NYC’s fine dining experiences. (without feeling guilty looking at a meat menu). And if even if this isn’t your game and you’re a guest invited….. Just try Its still damn tasty! 😋 and it’s a proper NYC Dining Experience. (5 stars)

Came here for a group dinner and we all had the new, seasonal tasting menu (Fall 2025). From start to end, every dish we had was unique, flavorful and delicious. The cuisines reminiscent of refined East and South Asian cuisines with a modern sensibility. A few surprises here and there throughout the meal, and by the end we were more full than we expected to be. Over the first few courses included three kinds of bread: focaccia, pita, and dosa - perhaps one too many? With all the dips, spreads, and chutneys I could see why (maybe better if one was pre-portioned). Cocktails were great and the service was impeccable. Overall the price is a bit steep, but aligns with the quantity and quality. Go hungry. Favorite flavors of the meal include the amuse bouche, honey nut dip, chickpea spread, sambal and chutneys, shiitake and matsutake, and the incredible dessert! Recommended. (5 stars)

review_snippets: Food was amazing! My favorite dish was probably the lambchops but I also really liked the chat service. Would definitely come back for the buttered chicken service. Cocktails were also very good. I especially liked the Raita yogurt cocktail. (5 stars)

Friend and I walked in without a reservation and got lucky they had a couple seats at the bar. Food was delicious, though we wish the server would have told us the spice levels as the pork rice and the chicken fish we had were crazy spicy. We loved the mushroom dish though. Plating was superb and cool atmosphere. Recommend if you love spicy, Northern Indian food! (4 stars)

Butter chicken experience was cool! It is a lot of heavy food so very filling. It also comes with unlimited paratha, rice and black dal. Someone came around with the chaat options available, we tried both. One aloo chaat and one Chana chaat thing. Aloo chaat had kurkure on top and it was really good. The Chana one was basically just dry mixture. The aam sutra cocktail was amazing. Raita cocktail wasn’t great. Lamb parcha app was actually my favorite. Really tender and flavorful. The tiger prawn was huge but ok. We picked the chili butter as the main butter type for butter chicken experience and you can choose a second butter for yourself. I didn’t like the tomato pickly butter I picked for myself, the fenugreek butter was best and had the more traditional taste (4 stars)

Tried the goat biryani and bhatti da murg. The chicken was decent, but definitely not the best. The goat biryani, however, was extremely disappointing, nowhere close to what a proper biryani should be. Aside from goat pieces and the fried onions on top, everything else missed the mark. The rice wasn’t fully cooked, and you could even see leftover moisture, which ruined the dish. The food feels more focused on presentation than authentic taste. Overall, mediocre at best and definitely not worth the high prices. No one would mind paying more if the flavors justified it, but that’s not the case here. Service was just okay, nothing special. There are far better restaurants serving authentic food at better value. I honestly should have trusted the low star reviews before deciding to try this place. (2 stars)

bio_text: Agi's Counter is a charming Eastern European and Hungarian restaurant located in the heart of Brooklyn, offering a unique blend of traditional flavors and contemporary culinary artistry. The intimate atmosphere, characterized by warm lighting and a cozy ambiance, invites guests to enjoy memorable meals, whether for brunch or dinner. The restaurant is celebrated for its meticulously prepared dishes that elevate Hungarian comfort food with creative twists, ensuring a delightful dining experience that feels like a home away from home. Agi's Counter specializes in authentic Hungarian and Eastern European cuisine, focusing on comfort food with modern interpretations. The menu features a variety of dishes, including a standout Tuna Melt and Caraway Caesar salad, alongside unique brunch options and creative shared plates. Signature techniques include the use of fresh, local ingredients and inventive flavor combinations.
menu_items: Duran - whipped farmer's cheese, cherry jam, & herbs on griddled housemade challah - $14
Sugared Grapefruit - served with griddled pullman & salted yogurt - $14
Szalonna & Eggs - thick cut bacon, buttered cabbage leaves with toasted caraway & two sunny side eggs - $26
Agi O's - homemade granola with toasted nuts and dried fruit served with choice of milk or yogurt & fruit compote - $8
Nokedli Soup - Hungarian teardrop pasta swimming in a bowl of rich broth finished with dill and toasted garlic oil - $12
Green Devils - add anchovy, add hot sauce - $5
review_snippets: This is a lovely Hungarian restaurant with a warm and cozy atmosphere. Although the space is small, the vibe feels intimate and welcoming, and the staff are genuinely friendly and attentive, which makes the whole dining experience very comfortable. The food is well-executed and thoughtfully balanced. The chicken liver appetizer with crispy chips, celery, and pickled cherries was a standout — incredibly smooth and rich, while the cherries added just the right acidity to cut through the heaviness and leave a clean, satisfying finish. The pork chop was also very good. It was slightly on the firmer side, but the peach sauce paired with it beautifully, adding a subtle sweetness that kept the dish from feeling greasy. The fries were crispy and flavorful, though a bit salty — a minor issue that didn’t take away from the overall enjoyment. The biggest surprise was the New York cheesecake. Served with blueberry sauce and fresh blueberries, it wasn’t overly sweet at all. The fruit balanced the richness of the cheesecake perfectly, creating a light and elegant finish to the meal. Overall, this restaurant clearly excels at using fruit to balance rich flavors. A highly recommended spot if you’re looking for a refined and enjoyable Hungarian dining experience. (5 stars)

Came here for Sunday brunch and loved it. Sunday hours run 10am–3pm, and it's been on my list forever because of the Michelin guide recommendation and so many awards that this restaurants has gotten. I came as a walk-in and waited about an hour. Reservations are definitely recommended on weekends, but the wait wasn’t too bad — I took a quick trip to the Brooklyn Botanic Garden right next door, which worked out perfectly. Their reservation system texts you when your table is ready What I ordered: • Fánk (Hungarian donut) — Sunday-only and goes fast. Light, soft, slightly sweet, and seasonal. Kind of reminds me of a challah texture • Sandwich special — mine was a pastrami beef tongue reuben; big flavor, generous portion. I love the mustard it came with • Tuna melt — griddled pullman bread, melty alpine cheddar, plus slaw and mustard. Super comforting. I can't remember the last time I enjoyed a meal as much as I did this one. First of all, the heartbroken beets, could have eaten only that all night! The Chicken Paprikas was delicious! And that cheesecake! Oh, goodness! Also, our server, Amanda was a sweetheart and was very good at helping us decide which meal by explaining the ingredients and flavors. (Who knew blue cheese and beets might work!) Also very pleasant Nico, Devon, and Sarah! We sat at the bar so had a chance to say hi to the Chefs, Mason, Louis, and David, and Our Sous Chef , "Mac" (who also explained some about the dishes!) was marvelous! The room was warm and friendly, great experience! I'll be back to NYC for this culinary experience as soon as I can! Yes, Chef! (5 stars)

This place was friendly, warm, and just plain fun. My girlfriend and I came here for our 2 year anniversary brunch/lunch and left giddy. Every dish or snack was delicious and vibrant. This place has the best tuna melt I’ve ever had by orders of magnitude. The country club plate was a personal favorite because I love to nosh. The general profiles of most things were similar across the board (funky, salty, sour, fishy) but everything had its own distinct flavor and never got boring. The service was attentive and friendly but not overbearing, and everything came out incredibly fast. (5 stars)
search_text: Agi's Counter Agi's Counter is a charming Eastern European and Hungarian restaurant located in the heart of Brooklyn, offering a unique blend of traditional flavors and contemporary culinary artistry. The intimate atmosphere, characterized by warm lighting and a cozy ambiance, invites guests to enjoy memorable meals, whether for brunch or dinner. The restaurant is celebrated for its meticulously prepared dishes that elevate Hungarian comfort food with creative twists, ensuring a delightful dining experience that feels like a home away from home. Agi's Counter specializes in authentic Hungarian and Eastern European cuisine, focusing on comfort food with modern interpretations. The menu features a variety of dishes, including a standout Tuna Melt and Caraway Caesar salad, alongside unique brunch options and creative shared plates. Signature techniques include the use of fresh, local ingredients and inventive flavor combinations. Duran - whipped farmer's cheese, cherry jam, & herbs on griddled housemade challah - $14 Sugared Grapefruit - served with griddled pullman & salted yogurt - $14 Szalonna & Eggs - thick cut bacon, buttered cabbage leaves with toasted caraway & two sunny side eggs - $26 Agi O's - homemade granola with toasted nuts and dried fruit served with choice of milk or yogurt & fruit compote - $8 Nokedli Soup - Hungarian teardrop pasta swimming in a bowl of rich broth finished with dill and toasted garlic oil - $12 Green Devils - add anchovy, add hot sauce - $5 This is a lovely Hungarian restaurant with a warm and cozy atmosphere. Although the space is small, the vibe feels intimate and welcoming, and the staff are genuinely friendly and attentive, which makes the whole dining experience very comfortable. The food is well-executed and thoughtfully balanced. The chicken liver appetizer with crispy chips, celery, and pickled cherries was a standout — incredibly smooth and rich, while the cherries added just the right acidity to cut through the heaviness and leave a clean, satisfying finish. The pork chop was also very good. It was slightly on the firmer side, but the peach sauce paired with it beautifully, adding a subtle sweetness that kept the dish from feeling greasy. The fries were crispy and flavorful, though a bit salty — a minor issue that didn’t take away from the overall enjoyment. The biggest surprise was the New York cheesecake. Served with blueberry sauce and fresh blueberries, it wasn’t overly sweet at all. The fruit balanced the richness of the cheesecake perfectly, creating a light and elegant finish to the meal. Overall, this restaurant clearly excels at using fruit to balance rich flavors. A highly recommended spot if you’re looking for a refined and enjoyable Hungarian dining experience. bio_text: Ai Fiori, translating to 'Among the Flowers' in Italian, is a sophisticated dining destination located on the second floor of The Langham Hotel in New York City. The restaurant embodies a playful and celebratory spirit, offering a modern interpretation of French and Italian Riviera cuisine. With a newly redesigned space that exudes relaxed glamour, Ai Fiori invites guests to indulge in an immersive dining experience that engages all the senses, from sound to taste. Ai Fiori focuses on coastal-inspired small plates, hand-made pastas, and seasonal ingredients, emphasizing shareable and inviting dishes. The menu features both classic and reinvented main courses, showcasing modern flair and a nod to the nautical-chic life of the 60s and 70s. Ai Fiori has received numerous accolades, including three stars from The New York Times and a four-star Forbes Travel Guide rating since its opening. The restaurant is part of the Altamarea Group, which operates 20 restaurants worldwide.
menu_items: Kanpachi - sliced kanpachi, honeynut squash, cherry agrodolce, pumpkin seeds - $29
Tuna Tartare Niçoise - bigeye tuna, pole bean, potato, niçoise olive, quail egg - $34
Passera e Caviale - atlantic fluke, american sturgeon caviar, crème fraîche, meyer lemon - $47

review_snippets: We had an incredible experience at Ai Fiori, and my girlfriend and I truly can’t say enough good things about the team and the level of hospitality they showed us. We dined there on Valentine’s Day, and while there was a delay with the set-course meal, which was a bit disappointing in the moment, the way they handled it completely turned the experience around. The staff acknowledged the delay sincerely and professionally, and they went above and beyond by inviting my girlfriend and me back for dinner on them. When we returned, everything was exceptional. The food was absolutely amazing and I thoroughly enjoyed every plate on the menu, especially the lobster and ravioli! What impressed us most was their professionalism and integrity. It’s not every day that a restaurant takes responsibility in such a generous way, especially during a busy holiday service. That level of care speaks volumes about their standards. My girlfriend and I would absolutely love to come back again, and we’ll be recommending Ai Fiori to everyone, friends and family included. Wishing them continued success and all the best moving forward. (5 stars)

Everything was outstanding at Ai Fiori. We each chose the prix-fixe option, which allows one to choose an appetizer, pasta, entree, and dessert. Because each dish was fairly small, we didn't feel stuffed at the end of dinner. We would definitely recommend this restaurant! (5 stars)

Went for Restaurant Week ($60 per person). The food and drinks were incredible. Three course meal of the most delicious food. Well prepared and beautiful. The restaurant was gorgeous and the service was great. I would love to come back here again. The highlight for me was the Butternut Squash Soup. It was so good! The portion sizes were perfect for me. (5 stars)

Absolutely loved our experience at Ai Fiori. The flower decorations and overall ambiance are beautiful, elegant, warm, and inviting. The food was outstanding: the lobster bisque was rich and flavorful, and both the Maine lobster and the ink squid dishes were absolutely delicious. Even the coffee was excellent. Special shoutout to Ismail, our server, who provided exceptional service, attentive, warm, and professional. Everyone we encountered was friendly, and the hospitality was truly top-notch. A wonderful dining experience from start to finish. Highly recommend. (5 stars)

bio_text: Al Badawi is a vibrant Middle Eastern restaurant located in the heart of Brooklyn, NY. Known for its lively atmosphere and commitment to using the finest ingredients, Al Badawi offers a welcoming dining experience that invites guests to explore the rich flavors of Middle Eastern cuisine. The restaurant specializes in authentic Middle Eastern dishes, focusing on traditional recipes and fresh ingredients. The menu features a variety of options that highlight the diverse culinary heritage of the region.
review_snippets: If you’re craving authentic Middle Eastern flavors in New York, this spot is an absolute must-try. The food is excellent: fresh, flavorful, and made with real care. The standout for me? The pistachio and cheese pie. It was rich, perfectly balanced, and one of the best I’ve ever had. The service is impressively fast, and the kitchen clearly knows what they’re doing. One of my favorite parts: they bake their bread in-house, and the warm pita keeps coming to your table throughout the meal. Soft, fresh, and straight from the oven! Honestly, it could be a meal on its own. A fantastic dining experience from start to finish. Highly recommend! (5 stars)

Al Badalwi was the most heartfelt dining experience I had during my short trip to New York. The atmosphere blends the comfort of home with the beauty of an artistic New York restaurant with the incorporation of murals and greenery. The service team works together to create a memorable experience for guests which is compounded by the quality of the food. I could tell the restaurant took pride in its services as it rightfully should. Despite how busy the restaurant became around 7:30PM, the food came quickly. The Baba Ghanoush and Salata bi Tahina ($13) were a great way to start the meal to warm up the palate and excite my taste buds for the main course. I enjoyed the texture of my Falafel Platter ($18) with all the dish elements complementing one another. The salad was acidic, sweet, and fresh with the restaurant’s specialty pomegranate molasses dressing. The falafel was spiced perfectly and had a great texture crunch. I’m not normally a sweets person but the dessert I had, mint tea and baklava, was very special. The crispy, flaky layers of the pastry with the rich pistachio and sweetness in the honey was textbook. The mint tea was otherworldly and ruined all other teas for me as none will compare to this quality. The tea was very bright, flavourful, and perfectly steeped, warming me to my core. I never knew something hot could be refreshing but their tea managed to do this. I will definitely come back when I get the chance to visit New York. Thank you Al Badalwi team! (5 stars)

This place is delicious! I’ve never had Palestinian food, so my boyfriend and I decided to try it. We got the dip platter and then split the mixed grilled platter (lamb, beef, chicken) with rice and salad. The dips were all to die for and the meats were so juicy. I have to admit, we loved it so much we came back a few days later. The best perk is that they have free BYOB so we brought a nice bottle of wine. Highly recommend! (5 stars)

BYOB, fantastic staff and food, fun/busy environment, amazing value. Make reservations for dinner because it was POPPIN on a Friday night. I will definitely be back for more of their “pizza” / flatbreads! It is soo so good. The lamb kabob plate was giant and could be shared for two people. (5 stars)

bio_text: Alley 41 is a Sichuan restaurant located on a secluded side street in Flushing, Queens, designed to evoke the spirit of Chengdu, the 'Land of Abundance.' The restaurant's ambiance is crafted to resemble the alleyways of Sichuan, featuring a unique layout that includes a front lane, an atrium, and a backyard, all adorned with traditional Chinese design elements. Alley 41 aims to provide an authentic dining experience that transports guests to the heart of Sichuan cuisine, making it a welcoming space for both locals and visitors. Alley 41 specializes in authentic Sichuan cuisine, focusing on bold flavors and traditional cooking techniques. The menu features a variety of dishes that highlight the rich culinary heritage of Sichuan, with 80% of ingredients sourced directly from the region. The restaurant offers a casual dining experience that emphasizes accessibility and affordability. Alley 41 was founded by a chef who grew up in Sichuan Province and longed to recreate the authentic flavors of his childhood in the United States. Opened in January of last year, the restaurant reflects the chef's dedication to authenticity, having undergone a careful preparation process before its launch.
menu_items: Homemade spicy radish - $8.95
Cucumber w. spicy sauce - $11.95
Peanut and black figs in chili sauce - $11.95
Spicy mung bean jelly salad - $13.95
Mung bean jelly w. chef's special sauce - $17.95
Sesame cold noodle w. sliced pork belly in garlic sauce - $17.95
review_snippets: Nice Sichuan cuisine! I like here so much especially this sichuan cold noodles ! Every time I order it. Today tried Kung Pao Chicken， this is also very delicious. Had my lunch alone. So just two orders. And I posted two years ago pictures ate here. Spicy beef is really great ! If u like spicy and beef , this is must try dish. ! Highly recommend! (5 stars)

Visited the Flushing location and was surprised by how affordable it is. Most dishes are $10+, and even the more expensive ones are just low $20s. We ordered a lot and still felt it was great value. Food quality was excellent—no misses at all. Everything was flavorful and satisfying. Will definitely come back! (5 stars)

Really good and authentic Sichuan food! I tried most of the classic dishes and I loved all of them. My only complaint is that everything was a bit too salty but I think that’s inevitable since Sichuan food just has so many spices and is packed with flavor. The place looks small initially but is actually really long and there’s a basement too with extra seating. I would definitely come back here when craving Sichuan food. Sautéed beef w. two kinds of pepper 7/10 - Too spicy for my liking (though it does have a spice level of 2 chilis on the menu) Double cooked pork belly w. chili leeks 9/10 Sesame cold noodle w. sliced pork belly in garlic sauce 9/10 - This was one of my favorite new dishes! Sautéed baby shrimp w. egg 8/10 Steamed whole fish w. fresh green pepper (tilapia) 9/10 (5 stars)

Pork noodles were delicious! Good service. Food came quickly and we all enjoyed it a lot. Fish was very flavorful. We were able to request for the crispy beef to be more dry instead of oily, so that tasted great as well! (5 stars)

bio_text: Alta Calidad is a vibrant restaurant located in the Prospect Heights neighborhood of Brooklyn, offering a unique dining experience that celebrates innovative Mexican cuisine. With a commitment to high quality, the restaurant aims to provide a fun and engaging atmosphere for its guests, whether dining indoors, on the outdoor patio, or during the lively OpenStreets summer weekend program. The culinary focus at Alta Calidad is on innovative Mexican cuisine, featuring a delicious selection of tacos, pintxos, and margaritas. The menu is designed for dine-in, delivery, or takeout, allowing guests to enjoy their meals in various settings. Chef Akhtar Nawab is the driving force behind Alta Calidad, bringing his passion for cooking with pride and integrity to the restaurant.
menu_items: Guacamole - tortilla chips, guajillo salsa - $18
Alta Queso Fundido - chorizo, chihuahua, halloumi, mezcal, tortillas - $18
Spinach, Chihuahua Cheese Queso Fundido + Tortilla Chips - $14
Mushrooms, Rajas, Mojo De Ajo Queso Fundido - $17
Short Rib Birria - $19
Old Bay Crab, Pico De Gallo - $21
review_snippets: Mexican spot that is featured on the Michelin Bib Gourmand list. The list features restaurants that serve good food for reasonable prices and Alta Calidad delivered. Must Try’s: Yuca Fries + Chipotle sauce - out of the park delicious and salty Alta Queso Fundido - probably the best thing we had. Make sure you order this. SO GOOD. Churros - do yourself a favor and leave some room for dessert Solid choices: Carne Asada Tacos - would be on my must but the price point for tacos feels a little criminal. Very good but damn almost $10 per taco is rough Pork Shoulder Carnitas - very good but again the other plates just put this to shame Leave it: Drinks - not a fan. Hot chocolate came out tepid and the mixed drink was just okay. Next time I’ll stick to water or coke Verdict - solid choice for Mexican, would recommend, not in a rush to come back NYC just has too many other places to try (5 stars)

I visited Alta Calidad while on the hunt for a Mexican spot during NY Restaurant Week and it did not disappoint. I ordered the Snapper Tostaditas, Carne Asada, and Churros. My favorite of the bunch was the Carne Asada. I would order that again if I returned. The service was great. The waitress answered any questions we had and the drinks came out fast. This was great value for a price of $45 (because it was during restaurant week). The ambiance was great, with natural lighting and good music. I would recommend this place to someone looking for slightly upscale Mexican food. (5 stars)

We had a really good meal at this Mexican restaurant. We ordered chicken tacos, shrimp tacos, and a margarita, and everything was fresh and full of flavor. The sauce on the tacos was absolutely delicious, adding the perfect touch to each bite. The presentation was neat, and the restaurant itself was clean and well-organized. The atmosphere was pleasant, and we especially enjoyed the music playing in the background, which added to the experience. If you’re looking for tasty food, a nice ambiance, and good music, this place is definitely worth a visit. (5 stars)

Taste-wise, the food was delicious, and the drinks were very good. The service was amazing, and I really like the location of this place. However, the portion sizes were quite small. If you’re coming here just to have a drink and a light bite, it’s perfect. But if you’re arriving hungry and expecting a full meal, even two plates might not be enough to fill you up. (4 stars)

Must Try’s: Yuca Fries + Chipotle sauce - out of the park delicious and salty Alta Queso Fundido - probably the best thing we had. Make sure you order this. SO GOOD. Churros - do yourself a favor and leave some room for dessert Solid choices: Carne Asada Tacos - would be on my must but the price point for tacos feels a little criminal. Very good but damn almost $10 per taco is rough Pork Shoulder Carnitas - very good but again the other plates just put this to shame Leave it: Drinks - not a fan. Hot chocolate came out tepid and the mixed drink was just okay. Next time I’ll stick to water or coke Verdict - solid choice for Mexican, would recommend, not in a rush to come back NYC just has too many other places to try (5 stars) I visited Alta Calidad while on the hunt for a Mexican spot during NY Restaurant Week and it did not disappoint. I ordered the Snapper Tostaditas, Carne Asada, and Churros. My favorite of the bunch was the Carne Asada. I would order that again if I returned. The service was great. The waitress answered any questions we had and the drinks came out fast. This was great value for a price of $45 (because it was during restaurant week). The ambiance was great, with natural lighting and good music. I would recommend this place to someone looking for slightly upscale Mexican food. (5 stars) We had a really good meal at this Mexican restaurant. We ordered chicken tacos, shrimp tacos, and a margarita, and everything was fresh and full of flavor. The sauce on the tacos was absolutely delicious, adding the perfect touch to each bite. The presentation was neat, and the restaurant itself was clean and well-organized. The atmosphere was pleasant, and we especially enjoyed the music playing in the background, which added to the experience. If you’re looking for tasty food, a nice ambiance, and good music, this place is definitely worth a visit. (5 stars) Taste-wise, the food was delicious, and the drinks were very good. The service was amazing, and I really like the location of this place. However, the portion sizes were quite small. If you’re coming here just to have a drink and a light bite, it’s perfect. But if you’re arriving hungry and expecting a full meal, even two plates might not be enough to fill you up. (4 stars)

bio_text: Altro Paradiso is a vibrant Italian restaurant located in the heart of SoHo, New York City, known for its lively atmosphere and elegant design featuring high ceilings and a striking brass bar. Since its opening in 2016, it has become a beloved dining destination for both locals and visitors, offering a warm and inviting space that feels like a second home. The restaurant's commitment to celebrating Italian culinary traditions is evident in its thoughtfully crafted menu and welcoming ambiance. The culinary focus at Altro Paradiso is on authentic Italian cuisine, drawing inspiration from various regions of Italy. The menu features a range of dishes that highlight timeless craftsmanship, with an emphasis on fresh ingredients and traditional techniques. From globally acclaimed chef Ignacio Mattos, Altro Paradiso opened in 2016 and has since garnered a loyal following.
menu_items: OSTRICHE - oysters with white balsamic mignonette* - $27
PROSCIUTTO - 18 month cured ham - Villani DOP - $32
PUNTARELLE ALLA ROMANA - chicory salad with anchovy and garlic - $26
ARANCINI - fontina and Calabrian chili - $16
TACCHINO TONNATO - sliced turkey breast, tuna aioli, celery, and egg* - $24
ZUPPA - Roman cauliflower, skate, and maltagliatti - $17
review_snippets: Went here with friends and cute atmosphere. Service was nice and quick… and spacious location. Went with a friend— enjoyed fennel salad (dressing was amazing) as well as some pasta dishes ( had the staple carbonara). Enjoyed wine as well as tiramisu which was so so good. Cute classic Italian spot and really good quality- really recommend (5 stars)

We had a mixed experience here with the food, however the service was good. We started with the finocchio fennel salad which was the best thing I ate all day, the dressing was superb. The arancini was crunchy with good flavor but it was served cold, which we didn’t like. Chicken Milanese parmesan was huge and tasty enough. Pasta cacio e pepe was decent. The biggest disappointment was the dessert. The pear galette had a super salty crust that was challenging to eat, perhaps it should have been an appetizer. The meringue-ata cake had a weird texture and was basically inedible. It felt like biting into butter, not in a good way. I am glad I tried the restaurant but don’t think I will go back. (3 stars)

This restaurant has a beautiful interior and the service is good, but I wasn’t impressed with the food. The antipasti mussels were just okay, the swordfish was too salty, and the spaghetti pomodoro was underwhelming. Overall, the food felt below average compared to the ambiance. (4 stars)

Altro Paradiso checks all the boxes. Superb food, attentive but never intrusive friendly service, warm atmosphere, inventive delicious cocktails, and approachable and thoughtful wine list. The sommelier was also warm and friendly and is clearly passionate as well as knowledgeable about wine and he took his time to explain the history of each wine he recommended and what makes it so special and how it pairs with each plate (many of which we have not seen anywhere else). The Caio e Pepe is the best we have ever had and beats any version of this dish we have had in Rome. How they prepare a basically three-ingredient dish so beautifully is nothing short of magic. The same applies to the other dishes on the menu that we have tried. Simple, fresh ingredients that Italy is famous for, prepared beautifully with just the right balance to enhance the flavors both individually and as a whole. Altro Paradiso makes the whole experience seem effortless, and we always leave feeling happy and taken care of, looking forward to our next visit. Delizioso! (5 stars)

Calamari - squid, squid ink mostarda, black garlic - $9
Gamberetti - shrimp, garlic chive salmoriglio, lime - $10
Sunchoke - saltbaked sunchoke, hazelnut pesto, yogurt, granny Smith apple, Pecorino Romano - $22

Barbabietole - roasted beets, smoked ricotta, pickled figs, pistachio - $19
review_snippets: Cozy & intimate spot w/ solid plates & great drinks. Reasonably priced, ambiance suited for conversation, a bartender that crafts bliss in a glass(ask for Eric), a well maintained restroom, suitable for small & extra large groups & a relaxing playlist. Check them out! (5 stars)

The ambiance at this restaurant was lovely, with the added bonus of outdoor seating. The service was exceptional—our server was incredibly patient and attentive throughout the evening. However, the food did not meet expectations. The pasta dishes, priced around $25, were served in very small portions, slightly undercooked, and the flavors lacked cohesion. We left quite hungry! While I appreciate having had the opportunity to try it, I likely wouldn’t return. (3 stars)

Honest Review of Ammazzacaffè Atmosphere & Service: 10/10 We grabbed a late 10 PM Saturday night Resy and the space still felt welcoming. The bar was spotless, the decor stylish but comfortable, and the service was excellent. Josh was warm, attentive, and service never felt rushed. Presentation on every dish was elegant and thoughtful. Starters : 9/10 • Sunchoke ($22): Beautiful salt-baked prep with hazelnut pesto, yogurt, and apple. Creative, layered, and earthy. • Barbabietole ($19): Roasted beets with smoked ricotta and pickled figs. Gorgeous on the plate, subtle on the palate. It was balanced but leaned more refined than bold. Mains : 8.5/10 • Cavatelli ($30): Crab, corn, Sungold tomato, coral butter. Fresh, seasonal, and well-executed. It was light yet rich, a summer-forward pasta. • Linguini ($30): Cockle clams with ramp pesto and yuzu kosho. Briny and bright, with a nice pop of citrus. Well-made but didn’t quite deliver a “wow” factor. Drinks : 8/10 • Hazy Tropics ($17): Tropical, refreshing, and slightly smoky. A solid cocktail. • Espresso Martini ($17): Smooth and well-balanced. As expected, no complaints. Value : 8/10 Subtotal: $135 With tax + tip: $179.32. For two people, it’s on the pricier side, but aligned with Williamsburg dining standards. Overall Impression : 8/10 Ammazza Café delivers excellent service, gorgeous plating, and a stylish, clean setting. The food was thoughtfully prepared, but none of the dishes quite leapt off the table as unforgettable. Still, it left us wanting to return and explore more of the menu. A great dining experience. The experience was elegant, and enjoyable, even if the food didnt completely blow us away. (4 stars)

Such a cute, cozy spot for lunch. The food was genuinely delicious. We did the prix fixe menu which was way more than we could eat (great value and super generous portions). Everything we tried was really well done, and the vibe felt relaxed and welcoming. Would definitely recommend for a bite to eat, and it also seems like a perfect place to swing by for a glass of wine. (5 stars)

bio_text: Aquavit is New York's premier Nordic restaurant, offering an exquisite dining experience in a sophisticated setting at Park Avenue Tower. The restaurant is dedicated to transforming traditional Nordic cuisine with a modern twist, showcasing seasonal ingredients and innovative techniques that reflect a commitment to excellence. Aquavit specializes in seasonal Nordic cuisine, focusing on fresh, high-quality ingredients. The menu features a blend of traditional dishes and contemporary interpretations, emphasizing innovative cooking techniques. Aquavit has received notable accolades, including two Michelin Stars in the 2023 New York City Guide and three stars from The New York Times in May 2015.
menu_items: razorclam tartlet - walnut, sugarsnap peas
elk tartar - mustard emulsion, pommes paillasson
SALMON - horseradish cream, beet sorbet, rye crisp
HOKKAIDO SCALLOP - cauliflower, gooseberry, dashi foam
OSSETRA CAVIAR - pickled potato, potato chip, bonito cream
Danish rye bread - seaweed butter
review_snippets: Aquavit is pure class. Its status is shown in the details- as most amazing things are. I dined here for lunch and participated in their three course meal option. The value of my meal greatly exceeded the price I paid- which is rare in this day and age. I started with the scallops which where incredibly fresh and rich. I then ordered the Ora King Salmon which was perfectly cooked, although I should have went with my gut to try the Swedish meatballs. The trout roe on the salmon was a perfect addition though, and didn't feel too 'fishy'. Now... onto the star of my meal, The Artic Bird's nest. Iconic and one of the best desserts I'd ever had. It was balanced, fresh yet indulgent and decadent. I will definitely be back to try the full tasting menu! (5 stars)

Wonderful lunch at Aquavit. Did a 5-course tasting which is such a great deal for the city for what you get. Everything was good to exceptional with the wagyu sup, birds nest (obvious) and Chilean sea bass winning out for me. Other secondary components/dishes like the creamy elk opener, Swedish caviar, and Iberico rillettes were awesome bites or compliments to the primary dishes. The pairing was very complimentary and service was excellent. Highly recommended (5 stars)

Aquavit is an excellent 2 star rated Michelin restaurant! We ordered the 7 course Chefs tasters menu. Everything that came out of that kitchen was excellent. The service was very good. The ambiance was equally very good. I must say, in all my life- i've never had a more fun time eating the Chefs special dessert. The Birds Nest! This dessert is absolutely one of the best deserts i've ever eaten. (5 stars)

Beautiful dining experience from start to finish. We chose to eat in the bar room because we wanted to choose our items rather than have a tasting menu. We started with the breads which included a traditional sourdough and a danish rye. Both delicious but the danish bread was the star and worth ordering the bread to try. The tartare was very good, a small portion but tasty. We ate at the bar and the bartender was great, he provided very welcomed recommendations and descriptions of the food. We also shared the shrimp skagen pancake. I will ruin the description but it was like a light crepe filled with shrimp in a creamy sauce. I am not doing it justice but it should be a must try. We then split the meatballs and KROPPKAKOR. Both were delicious but the kroppkakor was the star. A light dumpling like potato filled with mushroom and surrounded by crispy mushrooms and accoutrements. Again not doing this justice but it was delicious. We ended with chestnut cake and the tasting menu dessert that has apparently been on the menu since opening. Both delicious, beautiful presented and complex in flavor. All the food was great and the portions are small which allows you to try many things. You also need to try some of their Aquavit selections. I was unfamiliar with this alcohol but it is Nordic and they have several selections including some of their own. Our bartender was very helpful in explaining these and helping us choose. Overall a beautiful restaurant with interesting food. Completely recommend. (5 stars)

bio_text: Ariari is a vibrant Korean restaurant located in New York's East Village, drawing inspiration from the coastal city of Busan. The restaurant embodies a unique interpretation of Korean gastronomy, aiming to introduce diners to the rich flavors and comforting dishes of Busan while also evoking nostalgia for those familiar with the cuisine. With a commitment to quality and authenticity, Ariari invites guests to experience the essence of Busan in a warm and welcoming atmosphere. Ariari focuses on traditional Korean cuisine with an emphasis on fresh seafood, reflective of Busan's culinary heritage. The menu features a variety of comforting dishes that highlight the unique flavors of Korean gastronomy. Signature techniques include the use of fresh, locally sourced ingredients to create authentic and innovative interpretations of classic recipes. Ariari is inspired by the port city of Busan and aims to introduce its unique culinary offerings to New York.
menu_items: Raw Mak- Hwe - Thin Sliced Seasonal Fish with Onion and Tobiko over a Bed of Greens. Served with SsamJang, ChoJang, Gim - $32
DIY GIMBAP - Scallops, Squid Jeotgal, Chungyang Mayo, Apple Kimchi, Gim, Rice - $31
Busan Caesar Salad - Romaine, Napa, Shrimp Jeotgal, Anchovy Ssamjang - $16
Nurungji Yook-Hwe - Beef Tartare, Gochujang, Blanched Baby Octopus, Korean Pepper, Cilantro, Gim - $19
Spicy Baby Octopus - GochuJang, Crab Bisque, Cilantro, Sunchoke, Charcoal Mayo - $21
Bossam - Steamed Pork Belly, Oyster Emulsion, Anchovy Ssamjang, Garlic, Chive Salad - $18
review_snippets: ARIARI is a fantastic spot if you're looking for very modern Korean dishes in the city. Every dish I tried with friends was good, especially the fried soft-shell crab, the seafood pancake, the steamed egg with chives, and the bulgogi. The restaurant environment itself is full of people and it is actually very lively, which makes for such a fun and energetic dining experience. The flavors are fresh and the presentation is top-notch. It’s definitely a must-visit for anyone who enjoys high-quality food in a vibrant setting! (5 stars)

This meal was absolutely delicious!!! I was here a couple of weeks ago and have thought about it every single day since. I got the Scallop DIY Gimbap. The apple kimchi and chungyang mayo that came with it were two of the tastiest condiments I've ever had. I also got the Yook-Hwe which is beef tartare and baby octopus. They were also kind enough to give me a compliment salad of cabbage with what I believe was a kimchi dressing. I will be coming back to this spot every single time I visit New York, without fail. (5 stars)

Amazing seafood-forward busan specialty restaurant. Every dish we ordered was thoughtfully innovative and tasted fantastic, especially the spicy baby octopus Even the dessert was a unique take on a traditional Korean bingsu with soy sauce caramel, nuts, ginger, and basil. Amazing! (5 stars)

I visited Ariari because I wanted to introduce it to friends visiting from the Bay Area. Every time I come here, I’m blown away by the quality of the food, the staff’s service, and the cozy atmosphere of the restaurant — it’s a solid 10000/10 every time. With the chilly weather, I was craving DAESUN soju and seafood like in Busan, and this place turned out to be the perfect choice. We had assorted Mak-hwe, mackerel, and scallop gimbap topped with uni and sweet shrimp. The rice is the most important part of Gimbap — and theirs is unbelievably good! The accompanying ssamjang and mayo sauces were just fantastic. At one point, my friend accidentally dropped a spoon, and the staff immediately replaced it with a new one — even bringing over a Tide stain remover stick just in case it got on her clothes. Their attentiveness and kindness were truly impressive...🥹 We ended the meal with Dolsot Al-Bap and Hap-Cheon Pork Soup the perfect pairing with soju that just went down so smoothly. My friends who were visiting said they were so touched by the taste and service that they almost cried. Ariari is one of those rare spots in New York that never fails to make me happy. The food is amazing, complemented by the warm hospitality that’s rare to find in New York!!!!!!❤️❤️❤️ Writing this review is making me crave it again — I think I’ll go back this week. Now that it’s getting cold, it’s the perfect time to visit Ariari. Highly, highly recommend! (5 stars)

We had assorted Mak-hwe, mackerel, and scallop gimbap topped with uni and sweet shrimp. The rice is the most important part of Gimbap — and theirs is unbelievably good! The accompanying ssamjang and mayo sauces were just fantastic. At one point, my friend accidentally dropped a spoon, and the staff immediately replaced it with a new one — even bringing over a Tide stain remover stick just in case it got on her clothes. Their attentiveness and kindness were truly impressive...🥹 We ended the meal with Dolsot Al-Bap and Hap-Cheon Pork Soup the perfect pairing with soju that just went down so smoothly. My friends who were visiting said they were so touched by the taste and service that they almost cried. Ariari is one of those rare spots in New York that never fails to make me happy. The food is amazing, complemented by the warm hospitality that’s rare to find in New York!!!!!!❤️❤️❤️ Writing this review is making me crave it again — I think I’ll go back this week. Now that it’s getting cold, it’s the perfect time to visit Ariari. Highly, highly recommend! (5 stars)

bio_text: Asian Jewels is a vibrant seafood restaurant located in Flushing, NY, offering a unique dining experience that celebrates the rich flavors of Asian cuisine. The restaurant's atmosphere is lively and welcoming, making it an ideal spot for both casual dining and special occasions. The culinary focus at Asian Jewels centers around authentic Asian seafood dishes, with a particular emphasis on dim sum and traditional casseroles. The menu features a variety of signature dishes, including Shrimp & Eggplant w. Creamy Egg Casserole and Braised Goose Web w. Dried Fish Maw, showcasing expert techniques in preparation and presentation.
menu_items: Fried Bean Curd Skin Spring Roll
Steamed Rice-Rolls w. Shrimp & Yellow Chives
Baked Roast Pork Bun
Sticky Rice in Lotus Leaves
Crispy Fried Dumpling
Crispy Fried Shrimp Balls
review_snippets: My friend and I went without reservations and were seated right away. The atmosphere felt very homey — large round tables that could easily seat 8+ people, giving it that family-style dining vibe. As soon as we sat down, they brought out green tea and peanuts, which was a nice touch. The waiter initially hovered a bit but seemed to notice we were still deciding, so he stepped away and came back later to take our order. The restaurant mainly focuses on seafood, but since my friend has an allergy, we ordered from the American Chinese menu instead. We got the veggie egg fried rice, chicken wings, veggie steamed buns, and the star of the night — sesame chicken. The fried rice was unfortunately very dry; we ended up using the sesame chicken sauce just to make it more enjoyable. The wings were disappointing. I was expecting traditional wings, but they were more buffalo-style and didn’t taste good at all. The veggie steamed buns were just okay — nothing special. The sesame chicken, however, was amazing. If I ever came back, it would honestly just be for that dish. At the end of the meal, they brought out fruit, which was surprisingly fresh and delicious. When it was time to pay, we noticed something that felt a bit odd. Our waiter took the card to the counter and then handed it to another woman on the other side of the restaurant. We didn’t see this happen with any other tables, so it stood out to us. While that was happening, he continued attending other tables. We stopped him to give him a cash tip directly, but he told us to leave it when the receipt came back. We’re not sure if that’s standard practice there or if they pool tips, but it felt unusual to us. Overall, it wasn’t the best experience, and we likely wouldn’t return. (2 stars)

I’ve been craving some authentic dim sum for a while, and Asian Jewels really hit the spot. The whole atmosphere took me right back to Hong Kong—spacious, lively, and full of energy, with servers pushing carts around the room. Not many dim sum places still do that, and I love the vibe it creates. As for the food, everything was pretty solid. The highlights were exactly what you’d expect from a place like this: the shumai were outstanding, and the har gow were just as good. Some of the other dishes were decent, though I’d skip the soup dumplings since you can get much better versions elsewhere. Overall, a great and reasonably priced lunch. I’d happily return. (5 stars)

One of the best dim sum spots in NYC - great service with carts, great food options, exactly what you want from a dim sum place. Great shu mai. Had to wait about 30 minutes indoors for a Saturday morning walk in, but it went fast. Servers are helpful and courteous. (4 stars)

Old standby for dim sum in Flushing. Good variety, prompt service, dim sum served in carts. Visited in January and some of the dishes were lukewarm. Otherwise, excellent and well worth the wait (which one will usually face). (4 stars)
