bio_text: Aska is a refined dining establishment located in a beautifully restored 1860s warehouse in Brooklyn, New York. With a focus on creating a unique connection between nature and urban life, the restaurant offers an intimate experience with only ten tables available each night, allowing for personalized service and attention to detail. The ambiance is a harmonious blend of Scandinavian influences and local charm, making it a destination for those seeking an exceptional culinary journey. Aska specializes in a tasting menu format that highlights the rich culinary heritage of Sweden while incorporating local ingredients from the Northeastern U.S. The dishes are meticulously crafted in an open kitchen, showcasing signature techniques that emphasize seasonal flavors and artistic presentation. Chef Fredrik Berselius opened Aska in 2012, earning his first Michelin star within a year. The restaurant reopened in 2016 in a new location, quickly receiving a second Michelin star and a three-star review from the New York Times. Berselius has also published a cookbook titled 'Aska' in 2018.
menu_items: Aska Tasting Menu - A multi-course tasting menu rooted in Nordic sensibilities. - $375
Optional wine pairings - Wine pairings available for the tasting menu. - $250
review_snippets: This was my first Michelin experience, I went here a couple of months ago. The food is immaculate, absolutely exquisite. The Sea Oak was by far the best bite of food I've experienced, tied with the Oscitera Caviar. I was blown away, physically reeling from just how expertly crafted each bite was, down to the placement of sauce and the variety of textures. The service was excellent. The waiters worked together beautifully and they were very kind and attentive. My only gripe is that they seemed more interested in explaining these dishes to my Michelin savvy friend instead of myself, as they would turn to him and I'd be hearing every other word from them on account of low volume. The atmosphere was beautiful. Peaceful and calm, lighting was perfect for pictures, and seeing the cooks in front of us operating at such a high level with no stress was awe inspiring. The wine selection was also excellent, with each wine being selected to pair with a dish from the tasting menu, we tasted many kinds and it was great hearing stories about each one. (5 stars)

The ingredients at Aska are undeniably fresh and of very high quality, and you can tell that a lot of care goes into sourcing and preparation. However, the overall experience wasn’t quite for me. The environment is extremely serious and almost austere, which sets the tone for a very focused dining experience. The flavors throughout the tasting menu were very subtle — almost too subtle for my personal taste. The cuisine leans heavily into natural, earthy elements, and at times it felt like there was a bit too much nature on the plate. While it wasn’t my personal favorite, I can absolutely appreciate the craft and precision behind it. If you’re curious about experiencing Nordic cuisine at a very high level, Aska is definitely worth trying. (3 stars)

Had what I feel to be the best Michelin experience in NYC to date. Every dish was so incredibly on point with a few that will be stored in the memory food bank forever. The majority of the ingredients are sourced within 60 miles of the restaurant with the exception of a few items (mostly Nordic) that were imported. I thought the notes of each dish were clean, delicate, and beautifully balanced. Nothing was a smack to the palette with too much intensity which I think is exactly the story that Aska is trying to tell, it's clearly hyper-focused on the seasonality and quality of the ingredients. I will say there was a Madagascar caviar used in a dish that tasted like Serrano ham- like nothing I've ever had before. We did both the wine and non-alc pairing and both were very well suited for each course. A million extra points for continuously topping us off throughout the night. Ambiance is dark and intimate with an open kitchen to admire throughout the evening. Service was next level, with Missy the beverage director and her team seamlessly flowing about throughout the evening. The team was so warm, kind, and genuine- absolutely nothing felt sterile or forced, which is always a breath of fresh air. Not sure what more a restaurant needs to do to merit that third star. Also an awesome touch, my wife has a thing for beautiful dinnerware/flatware and was admiring theirs for the entirety of the meal. To our surprise, they printed out an extra menu with each dinnerware vendor they used for each dish. Pretty cool stuff. (5 stars)

This is a very late review because I was too lazy to write reviews. But even after more than half a year, this restaurant is still easily in my top five places in NYC after a few years of living here. The food was excellent. I had the best caviar I’ve ever had at this place. I remember the server specifically mentioned that the caviar was carefully sourced and brought in from Europe, though I’ve forgotten the exact details over time. Everything else on the menu was also very well executed. The only dish I personally couldn’t finish was the venison—not because it wasn’t good or fresh, but simply because it’s not a protein I enjoy. What truly stood out was the service. I was unsure about which wine or cocktail to order, and the server patiently offered multiple tastings of different wines and cocktails before I made a decision. At one point, my friend and I were discussing the beautiful tableware in another language and I briefly picked up a plate to look at it. At the end of the meal, the server brought us a dedicated tableware menu without us asking, simply because she noticed my interest. A friend who visited on another occasion mentioned feeling slightly cold, and a server immediately brought a blanket without being asked. I have never experienced this level of attentiveness at any other Michelin-starred restaurant—whether in NYC, elsewhere in the US or in Europe. Even now, the service still stands out in my memory as genuinely impressive. Many restaurants blur together for me after the meal is over, but this one hasn’t. The presentation of the dishes was distinctive, and the overall experience left a lasting impression. It’s one of the very few places in NYC that I still remember clearly—and one of the even fewer that made me want to write a review at all. (5 stars)

bio_text: Atera is a sophisticated dining destination located in New York City, offering an intimate and refined atmosphere for guests. The restaurant features a seasonal, continuously evolving tasting menu that showcases the artistry of contemporary cuisine, complemented by an extensive selection of wines and nonalcoholic pairings. With a focus on providing a unique culinary experience, Atera invites guests to indulge in a meticulously crafted meal that reflects the changing seasons. Atera specializes in a seasonal tasting menu format, priced at $325 per person, with optional wine pairings available. The culinary focus is on contemporary cuisine, utilizing signature techniques to create innovative dishes that highlight seasonal ingredients.
menu_items: Tasting Menu - Seasonal, continuously evolving tasting menu. - $325
review_snippets: I had an unforgettable dinner at Atena NYC on November 19, 2025 at 7:00 PM, and it was exceptional from beginning to end. The moment we arrived, the staff welcomed us with warmth, professionalism, and genuine hospitality. Every team member we interacted with was knowledgeable, attentive, and truly made us feel taken care of. A very special thank you to the chef, who graciously gave us a tour of the entire restaurant. It was such an unexpected and memorable experience, and it really showed why Atena has earned its 2 stars…the passion, precision, and pride behind every detail are unmistakable. The food was outstanding, beautifully executed, balanced, and full of flavor. Each dish was thoughtful and refined, with high-quality ingredients showcased in a way that felt both creative and comforting. The pacing of the meal was perfect, and every plate demonstrated the kind of technique and consistency worthy of its accolades. The wine selection was equally impressive. Our server guided us through pairings that elevated each course without overpowering the dishes. The wine program clearly reflects the same level of care and expertise as the kitchen. Overall, Atena delivers a truly remarkable dining experience, exceptional hospitality, refined cuisine, thoughtful wine pairings, and a team that genuinely cares. Their 2 stars are well-deserved, and I highly recommend Atena to anyone looking for an elevated and memorable dinner in New York City. (5 stars)

We hosted a work dinner in a private room at Atera and I will say it was the perfect choice! Food was amazing, wine pairing was fab, service was excellent, and the ambience was just right for hosting customers, prospects, and execs. The entrance was interesting and a bit mysterious (slightly dark and narrow halls) but as soon as you get in, you have a private room with 3 dedicated chefs waiting. Every single plate served was lovely and the ambience allowed for great conversations making the evening memorable. Would like to come back with my husband next! (5 stars)

This is a fantastic restaurant for a private event, the room they have is incredible. The service was fantastic. If I were Michelin I would give this 1.5 stars. It will beat any 1 star restaurant but it was not as memorable or special food wise as other two stars I’ve been to. The meat (beef and duck) and dessert courses were surprisingly disappointing. The restaurant shines in its seafood courses. (4 stars)
Heckuva meal here. Every course was inspired. Great wine pairings. Wonderful selection of Madeira. (5 stars)

With a focus on fresh ingredients and authentic flavors, Atla provides a unique dining experience that invites guests to explore the richness of Mexican culinary traditions. Atla specializes in contemporary Mexican cuisine, emphasizing fresh and seasonal ingredients. The menu features a variety of dishes that highlight traditional flavors with a modern twist, creating a delightful dining experience.

review_snippets: Very disappointing. I was a huge fan, long time since last time I came for brunch. I tried again and it was a terrible experience. We ordered margaritas to start, and these were tequila, lime and ice. I am sure you can make your own much better. We also ordered guacamole to start and it was spicy but no salt, so do not even try. As mains, I got the gringa which was huge, greasy and not very tasty. Very little cheese and no flavor. My wife got the fried chicken breast, which was deeply fried, soaking grease and unsalted. Finally, to try to get by, we got micheladas, which were acceptable but not great. Try a less trendy/ brand name and support smaller Mexican spots which would give you a much better experience. For completeness, we paid $146 :/ (2 stars)

I really wanted to like this place but it just didn’t quite hit the mark for me. The flavors were a bit bland, and some dishes felt like they were missing that special touch. I had high hopes based on the reviews, but it seems like the hype didn't translate into the actual experience. The ambiance is nice, and the staff was attentive, but when it comes to the food, I was left wanting more. The prices are so expensive almost $30 for 2 pieces of tacos. We ordered guacamole as well the chips are stale and oily. I hope the management look into it and considering their market prices. (2 stars)

Loved it. Dropped in for Sunday lunch after Bethel Noho service. Tostada del mar - super fresh mackerel with a bite. Then pork. Classic margarita. Restaurant is light and airy. Do try Bethel NYC. You can’t help but be changed. (5 stars)

Delicious Mexican spot, loved the pork Al pastor and all the sauces 😍 it was absolutely delicious, all the ingredients were fresh and the service was amazing! Even with all the tortillas and the generous portions, we (a table of 4) felt full (but not heavy and stuffed) after the meal. HIGHLY recommend (5 stars)

review_snippets: From the sea urchin with egg and nori to the wagyu ribs and Spanish mackerel, we enjoyed every course and the attentive service. This was our second time and it was every bit as good as the first. The fried chicken strikes me as more of a tempura, twice fried, with two dipping sauces and tasty banchan. We really liked the fluke as well and the squid stuffed with shrimp. We highly recommend Atoboy. (5 stars)

Went on Oct 15th. The sweet potato ice cream was absolutely fantastic and my favorite dessert of the year. And I eat a lot of dessert. It tasted so sweet potato-y, and had charred smokey little crumbles and a date caramel sauce that evoked the taste of a nice fire roasted sweet potato. If I could just buy this dessert, I would every week. I went with a friend, so we tried 2 prie fixe orders. The sea urchin egg jjim was also great. The rest were okay or not great for the price. We had the bluefin tuna, the fluke, the squid, sweet shrimp, suyuk, pork galbi and fried chicken. (4 stars)

Atoboy delivers an exceptional modern Korean dining experience that feels thoughtful, refined, and deeply satisfying. The prix fixe format allows each dish to shine, with courses that balance comfort and creativity while highlighting bold, clean flavors. Definitely come with friends to try everything on the menu! Every plate is beautifully executed--layered, precise, and never overcomplicated. The progression of the meal feels intentional, keeping you engaged from start to finish, while showcasing both traditional Korean elements and contemporary techniques. The space is warm and minimalist, and the service is polished yet relaxed, making the experience feel special without being intimidating. It's the kind of restaurant that reminds you how powerful restraint and balance can be when done well. A standout choice for a memorable night out in New York and a must-visit for anyone interested in modern Korean cuisine done right. (4 stars)

Went on 2025-02-14. It was valentine set menu. Uni egg custard was absolutely delicious. Squid and octopus were both really well executed and the caviar pairing was a great idea. Was a bit skeptical about the fried chicken at first, but I’m glad we ordered it. It was marinated with pineapples and double fried. Couldn’t really taste the pineapples but it does have a subtle refreshing taste to it. Dipping sauce was great. Love that they have a good variety of seasonal dishes. Overall 5 stars! (5 stars)

bio_text: Atomix is a sophisticated dining establishment that showcases New Korean cuisine, crafted by the talented husband and wife duo, Chef Junghyun Park and manager Ellia Park. Located in New York City, the restaurant offers an immersive experience through a meticulously curated tasting menu that reflects the rich traditions and techniques of Korean culinary heritage. The restaurant specializes in New Korean cuisine, focusing on innovative interpretations of traditional dishes. Guests can enjoy a tasting menu format that highlights the depth and complexity of Korean flavors, utilizing signature techniques that elevate the dining experience. Atomix is a follow-up to the well-loved restaurant Atoboy, created by Chef Junghyun Park and manager Ellia Park.
menu_items: Pumpkin & Cinnamon sikhye
Scallop - Gim bugak, Mustard kimchi
Littleneck clam - Dashima, Chrysanthemum
Half beak fish - Granny Smith apple, Sea grape
Monkfish liver - Squid, Tangerine
Kohlrabi - King crab, Kristal caviar
review_snippets: Atomix delivered. I've been trying to come here for years now, but reservations are incredibly hard to get. This is easily a top three dining experience of all time for me. There are two options: the chef's counter and the bar tasting. I went with the chef's counter. I don't drink, so I'm not totally sure how the experiences differ. The restaurant is a bit hard to find and looks pretty unassuming from the outside. The first floor is where the bar tasting happens, and then a flight of stairs takes you down to the basement where the main tasting counter is located. The space is beautiful. There's a giant silver-gray bow installation on the wall that spans both floors. When we walked downstairs, someone greeted us with sikhye and showed us some of the ingredients that would appear in the meal, including truffles and caviar. It was such a cool introduction and showed the level of attention to detail here. Before the meal started, we were also given hand towels with "Atomix" printed on them, which was a cute touch. Because we had to reschedule our reservation due to the NYC snowstorm stay-inside mandate, they also gave us complimentary champagne. Atomix Tasting Menu: Pumpkin & Cinnamon sikhye Scallop*, Gim bugak, Mustard kimchi Littleneck clam*, Dashima, Chrysanthemum Half beak fish*, Granny Smith apple, Sea grape Monkfish liver, Squid, Tangerine Kohlrabi, King crab, Kristal caviar* Abalone, Pomegranate, Red cabbage Celtuce jangajji, Pearl onion, Cashew nut Golden eye snapper, Potato, Sea urchin* Red endive & Cilantro salad Lobster, White asparagus, Cheongju Lobster jeotgal rice Lamb*, Goji berry, Broccoli rabe Gochujang lamb noodle Passion fruit, White lotus tea, Tapioca Burdock, Dark chocolate, Black truffle * indicates items that may be served raw. The sikhye was a warm and comforting start to the meal. The scallop and littleneck clam were delicious but extremely small bites. Honestly, I wanted more. The scallop might have been one of the best I've ever had, and the clam was easily one of the best bites of my life. The half beak fish was fantastic. It was incredibly light and the sauce around it complemented the fish beautifully. I usually don't care for liver, but the monkfish liver dish was so balanced and full of umami that I really enjoyed it. I had never had kohlrabi before, but the kohlrabi noodle dish was amazing. It was light and refreshing, and the generous amount of caviar on top added richness and contrast. I usually avoid abalone, but I figured I should try it since I was at Atomix. It was a bit tough, though I'm not sure what the typical texture is supposed to be. The sauce reminded me a little of General Tso's chicken, which I actually loved. The accompanying side dish was refreshing and well balanced. I remember the snapper being incredibly delicious, and the side salad was fresh and vibrant. It was one of my favorite fish bites of the night. The lobster was cooked perfectly and incredibly tender, as you'd expect. The lamb course was the only miss for me, but that's entirely because I personally don't like lamb. I'm sure it would be great for someone who enjoys it. The desserts were outstanding. The passion fruit dessert, which reminded me of a bingsoo, was icy, crunchy, refreshing, and tangy. The chocolate dessert was also excellent, even though I normally don't gravitate toward chocolate. The truffle added a really unique finishing touch. We also received a white chocolate mini dessert to celebrate our anniversary, which was amazing. Yes, the meal costs an arm and a leg, but it was absolutely worth it. At the end, they give you a sleeve to hold all the postcards from the meal so you can remember the experience. Even the bathroom had Le Labo Santal 26 candles burning, which is one of my favorite scents. The staff were incredible and tried to remember little personal details about guests while chatting with us throughout the meal. The service was top notch and the execution of every dish felt meticulous. This was truly one of my favorite meals of all time. (5 stars)

Truly a wonderful dining experience deserving of the world ranking and Michelin stars. The beautiful seafood heavy tasting menu, most of which included savory broth to enhance taste and smell of the dishes. Each drink pairing featuring unique infusions from fruits I have never heard of. The non dairy dessert to accommodate lactose issues. Chef and sommelier entertained the diners with stories and anecdotes while prepared the meal. Found out one of my favorite spots in Ktown New Wonjo is a regular crew hangout. (5 stars)

This is a rather late review, as I visited back in September, but the experience stayed with me. ATOMIX is famously hard to book. Getting a reservation felt like buying TS concert tickets, and we set alarms well in advance with high expectations for the meal. Unfortunately, while the atmosphere was fine, the food was underwhelming. I would give the food around a 6/10. The wine pairing was worse, closer to a 3/10. I couldn’t finish most of it, and during the second half of the meal, I stopped drinking the pairings after a single sip because they were unpleasant. We chose the bar seating when booking. Compared to other Michelin chef’s counters or bar seatings I’ve experienced, this one felt much smaller and more minimal. I understand that some people may enjoy this setup for the closer interaction, but personally it wasn’t my preference. What surprised me most was the reaction when I shared this opinion. A friend who loves ATOMIX completely dismissed my comments and said she wouldn’t listen to anything negative about the restaurant. It made me question the level of hype surrounding it. I don’t understand the extreme praise. Given the effort required to secure a reservation, the experience did not live up to expectations. (3 stars)

Every dish — even the snacks — was spot on. The white truffle add-on was excellent; for the first time at a Michelin restaurant, I actually felt an add-on of white truffle truly enhanced and harmonized with the dish rather than just adding to the price. The non-alcoholic drink pairing was thoughtfully designed and complemented the courses beautifully. The clay pot rice was phenomenal. The fish course was good but the least surprising of the night — well executed, but essentially a nicely cooked piece of fish in a familiar kimchi broth. Service was friendly, attentive, and present without being intrusive. (5 stars)

bio_text: Avant Garden is a celebrated modern vegan restaurant located in the East Village of New York City, known for its decade-long commitment to plant-based artistry. The restaurant offers a refined and heartfelt dining experience, showcasing the beauty and complexity of vegetables in a warm and inviting atmosphere. Avant Garden focuses on innovative plant-based cuisine, emphasizing fresh, natural vegetables and global flavors. The menu features a variety of beloved vegan dishes paired with curated selections of natural wines, creating a unique and memorable dining experience. Founded in 2015 by CEO & Founder Ravi DeRossi, Avant Garden has served as a blueprint for his plant-based hospitality group, Overthrow Hospitality. The restaurant has quickly become a staple in New York's vegan dining scene.
menu_items: CELERY ROOT PASTA - shaved black truffle, shiitake veloute, gremolata (GF, NF) - $29
SCORCHED CAULIFLOWER - toasted garlic, fried capers, cauliflower puree (GF, NF) - $27
HEN OF THE WOODS - mushroom puree, kohlrabi, pickled hon shimeji (GF, NF) - $22
STUFFED POBLANO - cilantro béchamel, pomegranate, huitlacoche (NFO) - $28
RISOTTO - seasonal mushrooms, watercress, balsamic pearls, basil oil (GF, NF) - $28
TAMAL - mole, epazote crema, jackfruit & trumpet ragu, pickled onion - $26
review_snippets: I had high expectations, but the food was a hit or miss. The Brussel sprouts and toast were wonderful. However, with the “paella”, we had issues (i put it in quotes because it was reimagined paella, not the real deal). There was a big piece of squash that was more or less uncooked and inedible. Also I’m not sure what the purpose of the piece of mushroom was either. I’m no Michelin star connoisseur, but putting a big piece of unseasoned mushroom doesn’t seem like it enhances the dish. Finally, the lava cake was a flop. The entire joy of eating a lava cake is the hot molten core surrounded by a moist gooey cake. We got neither. The cake was cold and plasticy. The “lava” wasn’t flowing. The additional things like banana, additional sauce, ice cream didn’t really do much to enhance the dish. Frankly Domino’s lava cake is better. I would not go there again. (3 stars)

Avant Garden is one of those Manhattan restaurants that completely changes your expectations of plant-based food. Located in the East Village, this place is creative, thoughtful, and genuinely exciting from the first dish to the last bite. The artichoke presentation alone is a showstopper. Perfectly cooked, layered with flavor, and plated beautifully. It’s rich without being heavy and balanced in a way that makes you slow down and actually appreciate what you’re eating. The cucumber and radish dish was bright, refreshing, and incredibly clean. Light but full of texture, with that subtle acidity that keeps you coming back for another forkful. One of the standouts for me was the roasted cauliflower. Deeply caramelized, crisp on the outside, tender inside, and sitting in that silky sauce that pulls everything together. It’s bold without being overpowering. Every dish feels intentional. You can tell the kitchen cares about composition, contrast, and presentation. Even the dessert was impressive. Not overly sweet, beautifully plated, and a perfect way to close out the meal. Beyond the food, the atmosphere feels intimate and refined without being stuffy. It’s the kind of East Village restaurant you’d confidently bring someone to, whether it’s a date night, dinner with friends, or an out-of-town guest who thinks Manhattan dining is all hype. As someone who spends most of his time walking through Manhattan neighborhoods for real estate, I’m always paying attention to the places that define a block. Restaurants like Avant Garden are part of what makes this area special. The energy, the creativity, the detail. It’s the same reason people fall in love with living in Manhattan in the first place. If you’re looking for one of the best plant-based restaurants in Manhattan, especially in the East Village, Avant Garden is absolutely worth experiencing. (5 stars)

presentations were great but it wasn’t enough to convince me that maybe my tastebuds were novice. flavors and textures were just okay. first time I’ve had to send a dish back- the pepper was undercooked and difficult to cut. By the time you get a piece, the filling was mixed into the huge amount of sauce you were hoping to not eat as soup. I found a lot of the dishes were difficult to eat without getting messy. dang, looking back even the dessert was underwhelming and flour-y to an easy chocolate lover despite us remaining positive! I am possibly spoiled coming from Chicago’s vegan landscape lol. I didn’t take photos of all the dishes, i realized I wasn’t coming back:/ We all know what it’s like to not agree with a dish that’s not for you, and to also go crazy over something that has never tasted so excellent. But we noticed a trend with every dish, a bit flavorless and always off with ratios of sauce or dryness. If you find yourself not exactly going crazy for anything here, me too. (3 stars)

I stopped by early evening on the weekend out of curiosity. The cozy, stylish interior drew me in, so I ordered a Peach Toast and a cocktail (forgot the name). The cocktail was fine, but the mix of peach and nuts on the toast didn’t really work for me. Next time, I’d like to try their dinner menu instead. (5 stars)

bio_text: Emilio's Ballato, located in the vibrant heart of New York City, offers an authentic Italian dining experience characterized by a cozy atmosphere and friendly service. This charming eatery has become a local favorite and a celebrity hotspot, where every dish is celebrated, from the renowned Chicken Parmesan to the fresh Linguini with clams. The warm, familial vibe, complemented by the restaurant's decor featuring celebrity photos, creates an inviting space for both locals and visitors to enjoy exceptional Italian cuisine. Emilio's Ballato specializes in traditional Italian cuisine, focusing on classic dishes that highlight fresh ingredients and authentic flavors. The menu features a variety of options, including standout items like Chicken Parmesan and Linguini with clams, showcasing the simplicity and richness of Italian cooking. Signature techniques include careful preparation and presentation, ensuring each dish is a memorable experience.

review_snippets: Emilio’s Ballato 55 E. Houston St. New York, NY 10012 This restaurant is high profile. Several celebrities have frequented this spot and the dining area has photos of all the icons who visited. There is usually a line; all customers are required to wait outside because there is no indoor lobby. The focaccia bread was one of the best starters I ever had. It especially went well with olive oil. The cutlet was gigantic. It was pounded thin with crispy edges. While there was a decent ratio of sauce, it was too sweet for my taste. For the most part, I enjoyed the cutlet. However, a major disadvantage is that pasta is not included; I would have to buy a separate entrée. Reminded why this is truly a staple of the new York City Italian and dining scene, came in for lunch about two + months go on a Thursday afternoon and was not disappointed. Then for our mains we split two pasta dishes and one entree...between the tagliatelle bolognese, Penne w red sauce and the star of the show the veal milanesa (bone in) with the arugula and cherry tomatoes... Sadly we were too full for dessert. But definitely will be back again (5 stars)

bio_text: Bangkok Supper Club is a vibrant dining destination located in New York City, inspired by the lively late-night food scene of Bangkok. The restaurant offers a relaxed yet refined atmosphere, perfect for social gatherings and culinary exploration. Guests can enjoy a selection of shareable dishes paired with a curated list of alcoholic beverages, all while experiencing the rich flavors and convivial spirit of Thai cuisine. The restaurant specializes in inventive Thai cuisine, focusing on shareable dishes that highlight the use of traditional Thai charcoal grilling techniques. The menu is designed to foster a communal dining experience, encouraging guests to savor a variety of flavors together. Bangkok Supper Club is a visionary creation by Chef Max Wittawat, drawing inspiration from the vibrant late-night food culture of Bangkok.
menu_items: Khao Mun Gai - Deboned deep fried chicken wings stuffed with aromatic ginger sticky rice and soy bean powder.
Goi - Northeastern Thai beef tenderloin tartare, makrut lime leaves, shallots, mint, culantro, chili flakes, toasted rice powder served with rice crisps.
Prawn Satay - Charcoal grilled tiger prawns, cilantro, pickled cucumber, shallot, red chilies, over curry cashew butter sauce.
Hokkaido Scallop Ceviche - Hokkaido scallop, pickled watermelon rind, diced watermelon, mint, garlic, topped with chili watermelon granita.
Chilean Sea Bass Chakram Curry - Pan seared wild caught Chilean Sea Bass over Chakram curry, red chili, topped with sea beans with a side of Jasmine rice.
Pork Jowl - Deep fried pork cheeks served with savory garlic baked rice topped with spiced pork cracklings.
review_snippets: Although I was born and raised in Thailand, I've never been to a Thai restaurant that offers a tasting menu before. So I was very excited to come here. Although my expectations were high (as a big foodie myself) this place did not disappoint! There was not a single moment or dish that I didn't enjoy. All the dishes looked very strange and unfamiliar to me tbh, but once I took the bite, I recognized them immediately. The flavors were so spot on, very authentic and homey, yet so elegant and delicate. My personal favorite was the first course, the crab tratlet. I grew up in a small town next to the ocean, and this cute little crab tart was packed with flavors that just brought me back to a meal with my family. The seabass was also another dish that impressed me more than I expected. The cook on the fish was purely impeccable. The curry was rich with a nice level of heat. I am also obsessed with the desserts. They looked nothing like the desserts I had growing up but they tasted exactly like them. I felt like a child again. I enjoyed all the dishes a great deal. This was such a wonderful experience. Of course, I will be back here again.. and again... and again! :) Reservation is recommended as the wait could be long, especially the tasting menu. (5 stars)

How does this place not have a Michelin star yet? This was my favorite fine dining experience in New York by far, and we have tried a range of Michelin starred spots (1*, 2*, 3*—for celebrations/special occasions). I don’t know how the politics of the food industry works, maybe some places are better at schmoozing than others, but there have been 1 star tasting menus/restaurants that have been good, but nowhere nearly as impressive or memorable as Bangkok Supper Club’s tasting menu was. Each course was intentional and thoughtfully put together (I wrote more details in captions of photos). I can genuinely say I loved each course and actually remember what it was. Sometimes the experience of a tasting menu can feel like a blur, and we remember maybe one or two things we ate, but here I can clearly recall each one. We also tried a wine pairing and loved each selection. Another note: I noticed tasting menus are shorter in NYC, compared to other cities, which has made me less interested in visiting certain restaurants (like I find myself wondering more frequently in New York, will we walk out hungry?) Bangkok Supper Club’s tasting menu length was perfect, not too short or too long. By far my favorite meal in NYC so far. Award this place a star already! (5 stars)

Hmmm think of this as what Coqodaq did to fried chickens but for Thai food. I cannot believe a Thai restaurant does not have Thai iced tea, they don’t have Thai iced tea. The alternative, a non alcoholic beet drink was not the best alternative. The foyer with the hostess stand is very chilly, uncomfortable to wait in for your table before the meal and for your jackets after the meal, could be warmer. The pork jowl is great, the garlic crisps were slightly overboard for our taste, wish there was more rice. I highly recommend avoiding the chutoro laab, it’s the worst chutoro I’ve ever had. I could not taste it at all in every bite of the dish. It is overpowered by the other ingredients and was very spicy. Based on the texture of the tuna, I’m inclined to say it does not resemble the fatty, tender texture of chutoro, maybe that’s why it’s heavily masked by the other ingredients. The pandan cake was great, truly an exception everyone should make if they’re watching how much coconut they consume. The khao mun gai was wonderful. The environment is very busy and social, not really intimate. The tables are fairly tight if you want to see 6 people at any of their booths, and cozy for 5 people. The service was on par with the atmosphere. Gave it a try, but won’t be back. (3 stars)

Bangkok Supper Club was an outstanding experience from start to finish. Every dish felt intentional and exciting — each bite was a discovery. From the chu toro and ceviche to the prawn satay and yum khai dao, everything was beautifully balanced and full of flavor. The mains were just as impressive: rich pork jowl, comforting beef massaman, juicy gai yang, and even the green beans with tofu stood out. The service was exceptional. The entire staff was attentive and welcoming, and the chef even came to our table to personally explain a few of the dishes, which made the experience feel even more special. I truly hope to be back soon ♥️✨ (5 stars)

bio_text: Bar Miller is an intimate omakase restaurant located in the vibrant East Village, offering a unique dining experience that emphasizes sustainability and quality. As a showcase for the sustainable sushi brand Rosella, the restaurant provides a carefully curated atmosphere that invites guests to indulge in a thoughtfully crafted culinary journey. Bar Miller specializes in omakase, focusing on sustainable sushi that highlights the freshest ingredients. The menu is designed to offer a personalized dining experience, showcasing the artistry of sushi preparation and presentation. Bar Miller is the showcase omakase restaurant from the sustainable sushi brand Rosella.
review_snippets: One of the best and most unique omakase experiences in the city! We absolutely love Rosella so we really wanted to try Bar Miller. Jeff and James are incredible. Such a friendly and cozy experience. Everything’s locally sourced, and as far as I know, they’re the only ones doing that in the omakase/sushi space. But as far as the fish, it tastes as good as anything flown in from Japan; you’d never guess the fish are all sourced from the east coast. Can’t wait to come back! (5 stars)

We had a birthday dinner here and it was incredible. Not only the food but the service was exceptional. The flavor pairings were perfect. The list of what they served is below with some notes. I would highly recommend this place. The host was so friendly and knowledgeable. He guided us to a Sake that paired well with the food. There is a pairing where they give you different Sake and wine through the meal. He genuinely wanted to help us find what we liked. Oyster strawberry Arctic char sashimi. Strawberries Little clams chowder. Roasted and crispy sun chokes. Gouda clams. Like razor clams. Little salty. But not tooo much. So good. Clams not chewy. Stripped bass ceviche. Wine lemon grass sauce. So light and citrus taste. Vibrant Pickled strawberries to cleans palate between sushi Sushi: Porgy Trout from Hudson valley. Smoke applewood Spanish mackerel from North Carolina Bluefin tuna from North Carolina Fatty cut of same tuna taste comparison is really interesting Amberjack from California . Sunflower seeds. Citrus taste Torch seared main uni. Which is Urchin. If you haven’t had it’s worth trying South Carolina shrimp. Crispy shallots shrimp chili oil. This is not too spicy Main mussels poached glazed in it’s own cooking juice Tuna tartar. Chip made from fish. Chip is salty and pairs well with the tuna. In roe. Chowanmushi sable fish Toasted barley ice cream with caviar. Crazy good combination. If you found this helpful follow me. I don’t give many 5* because I reserve that for the very best in food, service and experience. I try to be quick to the most important stuff, the food. Then add notes about the rest. Enjoy! (5 stars)

My wife and I had a wonderfully memorable night at Bar Miller with Chef James and TJ as our host/server. Have never felt more welcome at an upscale place. Great food, service, ambiance, playlist, and people. Definitely recommend if you're in the area craving something unique! (5 stars)

The most amazing experience! Every dish was a flavor explosion – my taste buds were on cloud nine. The wine and sake pairings were spot-on, like they knew exactly what my palate needed with each bite! Gorgeous interior, intimate space and the service from Baxter our waiter and James the phenomenal chef were fantastic. If you're looking for a memorable dining adventure you won't be disappointed! (5 stars)

bio_text: Barawine is a vibrant dining destination that combines a relaxed atmosphere with a sophisticated culinary experience. The restaurant offers a diverse menu that caters to a variety of tastes, featuring both classic and contemporary dishes, all served in a warm and inviting setting. With a focus on quality ingredients and a commitment to exceptional service, Barawine aims to create memorable dining experiences for its guests. Barawine specializes in a blend of Mediterranean and contemporary American cuisine, offering a diverse menu that includes a variety of appetizers, main courses, and desserts. The restaurant features a pre-fixe menu and a bar menu, showcasing signature dishes such as the Barawine Burger and various seafood options, all prepared with a focus on fresh, high-quality ingredients.

review_snippets: This pace and the ambiance is so amazing the only thing that disappointed me was I purchased wine from there and if you see pictures below that’s the wine price for me to be charged $60 for a bottle of wine was really unreasonable. I believe the host should’ve been more informative and suggested that I don’t purchase there. The bill was little Steep it was $245.00 that was the chauture board, the wine. I got salmon my friend got the tuna tar tar and the ravioli truffle I don’t believe that should total up to that but. I enjoyed myself the music was great the costumer Service was amazing. And the ambience is something I will return for and the chature board was so good. But I would like a refund on the over priced wine bottle (1 stars)

This place is very calm vibes. The decor is immaculate with the different placements of all the displays of wine. I was greeted with multiple menus & decided to participate in restaurant week. The food was tasty & the service was on point. I didn't have to look for my waiter, my table was always checked on. The wine that was suggested was a simple rose , which wasn't too sweet. The desert was my highlight , because I just love crème brûlée (5 stars)

Barawine is truly a hidden gem. The atmosphere is cozy and inviting, the food is consistently delicious, and the crowd is always a great mix. One of my favorite spots to unwind and enjoy a great night out. (5 stars)

I went to Barwine on Lenox Avenue in Harlem with my friend and her husband, and it was such a nice experience. The place has an upscale but cozy vibe—very clean, stylish, and tucked away in a great spot. My friend’s husband ordered the leg of lamb, my friend had a steak, and I went with the chicken Caesar salad. Everything looked amazing, and we all agreed the food was delicious. I had to drive, so I just had a ginger ale, but it paired perfectly with my meal. It wasn’t too busy since we went kind of late, which made it even better—calm, relaxing, and a perfect setting to enjoy a good meal. The service was on point, and overall I’d give the food and the whole experience a 10/10. Definitely a place I’ll be coming back to! (5 stars)

review_snippets: The cutest bar and seating decor. So much character and great vibe. Service was excellent and sever we had was knowledgable, accomodating. Everyone was so friendly and welcoming. Cocktails were not impressive but food was amazing. Chicharron and anchovie is must have if you like those dishes. Price is high for the app portion but so good. Quality here, not quantity. Mandatory garlic shrimp egg app was huge and good for sharing; yummy and well priced. The mushroom or dishes for vegeterians, not so exciting. Ended with a good flan dish. (5 stars)

As a fan of Ernestos, I finally got to experience Bartolo and it exceeded my expectations. The space itself was incredibly stylish and the food was fantastic. A few standouts for me were the Anchoa Y Matequilla, Champinones Al Ajillo, Huevos Fritos Con Patatas Y Gambas, Callos A La Madrilena, and Chuleta De Buey, amongst others. Don't sleep on the cocktails here. I would put their martini up with some of my other favorites in the city. I was also a big fan of the Espresso De Brandt which is an Espresso Martini with Pastis and Cacao. Top level! Really awesome staff, service, and vibes. Can't wait to return. (5 stars)

World class dining experience! It brought be back to Spain instantly! Chef Ryan is using the best ingredients and cooking with incredible technique. Each bites makes you want to try the next! (5 stars)

Sexy, beautiful little restaurant... It's a sprawling but tight space, so newbie fabulous-affective passive-aggressive transplants are fortunately forced to actively engage with and experience actual New Yorkers... It's a great Spanish restaurant, in the West Village, and it's flippin' delicious... (5 stars)

borough: Welcome to Bayona Restaurant | A Taste of New Orleans
michelin_category: Since 1990, BAYONA has been a staple in the romantic New Orleans French Quarter with the vision of providing fine dining in a comfortable, casual setting.
bio_text: Bayon offers a captivating dining experience that transports guests to Cambodia through its vibrant aromas and warm hospitality. The restaurant's ambiance reflects the cultural splendor of Cambodia, creating a welcoming environment that invites diners to explore a menu that honors traditional Cambodian cuisine while incorporating innovative culinary techniques. With a focus on resilience and revival, Bayon stands as a testament to the enduring legacy of the Angkor era. Bayon specializes in Cambodian cuisine, blending classic recipes with contemporary culinary innovations. The menu features a variety of meticulously crafted dishes that highlight the use of aromatic spices such as lemongrass and galangal. The dining format encourages exploration of both traditional and modern interpretations of Cambodian flavors. Bayon emerged from the challenges of the pandemic, evolving from its predecessor, Angkor Cambodian Bistro, to offer a renewed culinary experience.
menu_items: Summer Rolls - Shrimp, lettuce, rice vermicelli, fresh mint and sweet basil, rice paper wrap, and chili fish sauce - $20
Shrimp and Crabmeat Spring Rolls - Shrimp, crabmeat, vermicelli, wood ear mushrooms, carrots, taro, deep fried, and plum sauce - $20
Khmer Fish Cakes - Deep fried fish patties, shrimp, string beans, curry powder, and house dipping sauce - $18

Fried Vegetable Dumplings - Fried dumplings garnished with chives, and ginger soy sauce - $20
review_snippets: First time at a Cambodian restaurant and there were so many good options. Server was super nice and very helpful with selections, although most were the favorites recommended by others. I really enjoyed the Khmer Noodles and got the one with shrimp and thin rice noodles. The Loc Lac is a traditional Cambodian dish and had a nice black peppery zing. The Baked Amok is also a very traditional dish and great place to start the Cambodian food journey. I would recommend this restaurant. (4 stars)

We had a great meal at this Cambodian spot. The atmosphere is lovely—very upscale, like a premium Asian restaurant. The service was impeccable, and the food was delicious. What made it special was dining next to the large Buddha statue, which gave the entire experience a wonderful sense of calm. (5 stars)

It was busy when we got there probably around 7pm. But service was super nice and our server helps us a lot with the food since it’s our first time trying Cambodian food. Love the spicy noodle (almost like drunkman noodle) and we really liked the appetizers with 3 dipping! So good! And we’ll definitely would come back again! (5 stars)

One of the best restaurants I’ve ever been to! Not only did the food blow us away and was clearly made to order, but the staff were incredibly attendant and personable. Excellent meal!!! Can’t wait to return. Highly reco the shrimp & scallops, the pork skewers and the Ari noodle. Chefs kiss! (5 stars)

bio_text: Benoit is a charming Parisian bistro located in the heart of Manhattan, offering a sophisticated yet inviting atmosphere for diners. With a focus on classic French cuisine, the restaurant combines traditional culinary techniques with modern innovations, creating a unique dining experience that appeals to both locals and visitors alike. Benoit specializes in classic French cuisine, featuring a menu that highlights familiar yet unexpected flavors. The restaurant offers a variety of dining options, including private dining experiences, and emphasizes the use of high-quality ingredients and expert techniques. For over 15 years, renowned Chef Alain Ducasse and his team have welcomed guests to this iconic French restaurant, celebrated for its blend of classic tradition and modern culinary innovation.
menu_items: ARTICHOKE VELOUTÉ - $60
HALF DOZEN OF ESCARGOTS - garlic & parsley butter - $16 / $32
FENNEL SALAD - grapefruit & walnut - $60
FRESH PEA RISOTTO - $60
SEARED BRANZINO - braised leeks, potatoes & garlic cream - $60
ROASTED CHICKEN - mashed potatoes & morel sauce - $60
review_snippets: I went to this French restaurant, open since 2008, for Winter Restaurant Week on one of these recent snowy days. As per many of the other spots, they serve three courses for $60 or two courses for $45 during lunch only. In terms of the food, it wasn't the biggest portion size, but they gave extra dishes, so it felt somewhat worth it, even if the food itself wasn't the best for any particular bistro dish. The service, whether it was the maître d', the busboy, the waiter, or otherwise, was all friendly and professional. The inside is a bit sparse but still feels refined, and the clientele was mostly middle-aged, with many ordering from the main menu, aside from the table next to me and a few others. To drink, I thought of getting a glass of the Bourgogne Aligoté, but instead went for a cocktail, the $18 Not Too Far From The Tree with Calvados, ABC Drouin, apple cider, caramel, and lemon. The drink was pleasant with plenty of apple flavor from the calvados, cider, and drouin, but it wasn't too sweet. There was a bit of booziness, but not overly so, and a piece of brûléed apple on top was a nice touch. Before the appetizer came out, they first gave me a couple of gougères. This consists of a choux pastry with a bit of cheese baked inside. It was airy with a slight chew, and if you have never had one before, it's pretty similar to a pão de queijo in terms of saltiness and chewiness, but smaller. This was warm and good. Afterwards, there was a bread course with two types of bread as well as butter with a B carved into it. Both breads were of pretty good quality, but they weren't warm, and the butter was unfortunately also a bit chilled. This was alright, but would have been much better if either of these two things had been at the proper temperature. From the menu, I ordered the Onion Soup Gratinée, which was alright, with some cheese, onions, and a standard broth comparable to most bistros. I would say there were fewer croutons than usual, but since I still had some bread, I used it as a replacement. There was also less crispy cheese around the edges than in some other places, and the broth was a bit less rich and nuanced. The soup is normally $20 on the dinner menu, and I hope it's at least larger to make up for all these other shortcomings. In terms of places nearby, it doesn't really compare to Le Bonne Soupe, for instance, which offers a larger portion and a much better-flavored broth. For my entrée, I had a choice among three courses not listed on the main menu. I went with the Coq Au Vin, as I am generally a fan of this classic bistro dish, and I also saw someone else's fish at the table next to me, which looked paltry. Along with some button mushrooms, the dish had a nicely cooked-down red wine sauce, though it wasn't as rich as in other places. I did notice a lack of lardons, which could be the reason. The chicken, while tender, consisted of two small bony pieces, which I didn't really appreciate. Outside of them being more difficult to scrape off and enjoy with the sauce, a piece of chicken breast would have honestly worked better and been more substantial. My favorite thing on the plate was surprisingly the purée, which was silky smooth with likely plenty of butter. This was just fine. For dessert, I went with the $12 Chocolate Mousse since it was the only item on the regular dessert menu. The mousse was presented in a unique way, with one of the waitstaff coming around with a large serving dish, removing a piece of mousse, and plating it. The bitter-sweet mousse was silky smooth, and there was also some unexpected crunch, maybe from hazelnuts or something else, which added a nice extra texture. This was my favorite dish overall and a satisfying end. After dessert and while arriving with the check, they came around with a pan of freshly baked madeleines, which was a nice touch. This was an alright experience. I get there have to be shortcomings when the main dishes here tend to be $45 and up, but this was barely worth it and wouldn't have been at all without the freebies. Upper 2. (3 stars)

Worst service ever! When we ordered, we had asked to switch something (from Skirt Steak to Filet Mignon, which was a more expensive item), at most 5 minutes after we ordered, and our server, Miguel, rudely said it was “too late”. We didn’t receive our food for another half hour at least. I am sure it was not too late to switch. I understand this can be annoying, but we were very nice about it and it was right after we had ordered. He could have at least been kinder or tried to accommodate. Regardless of this, our server hardly paid attention to us after we ordered / had gotten our food. Didn’t check on us ONCE. We had originally wanted to order some coffee and dessert, but our server didn’t come over to us for another 20 minutes, so we just decided to leave. This is ridiculous for such a well rated restaurant. It was not overly busy and did not seem understaffed whatsoever, so that can’t be the reason. Note: The bussers however were kind and working very efficiently. We told a manager about this on our way out and he sort of tried to console, but didn’t really seem to care. The food itself was good, and the interior of the restaurant was nice, but the service made us never want to come again. Service makes or breaks a customer experience. It ruined the atmosphere in the restaurant and at our table especially. (1 stars)

The food was unfortunately disappointing. I had high hopes since it was an Alain Ducasse restaurant. All of the proteins (escargot, halibut, and veal) needed some love; salt, acidity, or just something. Simply put the food was a bit lacking. Not only that, the service was a little bit questionable. I asked for extra baguette if possible to go with my escargot. It took more than 15min to get my bread and I'm already more than half way done with my escargot. The kicker at the end, we got our check. We were charged $8 for still water. We didn't get like a bottled water like a Saratoga water, we got what seemed like filtered water from a fountain. All I asked was why was I charged. I don't mind paying that extra couple dollars but it just didn't make sense to be charged for filtered water. Instead of informing me of the reasoning, they took back the check and got rid of the charge. The manager (I think) who was handling that situation didn't even say sorry or informed me of what was happening. To me, that quick action of getting rid of the extra charge seemed very sus to me like they have done this to other guests who don't properly look checks. But other than that, wine list is pretty good. (1 stars)

I had mixed feelings about this place. The fish and filet mignon were good, but the chicory salad deserves its own comedy show. . $22 for a few bitter chicory leaves with barely any goat cheese is hard to justify. There was so little cheese that it honestly felt like a joke. I laughed about it all night, but at that price point, it’s not funny. (2 stars)

bio_text: Bohemian Spirit Restaurant offers an authentic Czech dining experience in a warm and inviting atmosphere. With a focus on traditional Czech cuisine, the restaurant provides a unique culinary journey that reflects the rich cultural heritage of the Czech Republic. The restaurant specializes in authentic Czech food and drinks, featuring a menu that highlights traditional dishes. Guests can enjoy a brunch menu on weekends and a dinner service that showcases the depth of Czech culinary techniques.
menu_items: Sauerkraut & Kielbasa Soup - $16
Roasted Half Duck w/Sauerkraut, Red Cabbage, Potato & Bread Dumplings - Sauerkraut, Red Cabbage, Potato, Bread Dumplings - $38
Hunter’s Potato Pancake w/House Salad - Potato Pancake, House Salad - $29
Smoked Kielbasa w/Potato Salad - Kielbasa, Potato Salad - $29
Roasted Pork w/Horseradish Sauce & Bread Dumplings - Pork, Horseradish Sauce, Bread Dumplings - $29
Potato Pasta “Halusky” w/Bryndza Cheese & Bacon - Potato Pasta, Bryndza Cheese, Bacon - $29
review_snippets: A real gem on the upper east side. The food is excellent - while we didn’t eat this trip we’ve had the schnitzel in the past. The beers are special - czechvar is a very special, hard to find lager that only select bars will get. Glasses are cleaned and served in the authentic Czech style - via Lukr pour and washed by hand, to ensure the temperature is not too hot to warm the beer and there is no soap residue. The staff is friendly, kind, inviting. This is an incredible place to eat and drink and we’re so lucky it’s right here in Manhattan! (5 stars)

We heard about this restaurant on social media and had it saved on our to go list for a while. We had never had Czech food and they're the only Czech restaurant in Manhattan. So, we finally decided to take the 1 hour trip and try it out for our date night. Staff was helpful, warm, and friendly. They answered all our questions and made sure we felt confident about everything. Restaurant itself was clean and inviting, the bathrooms were kept up and everything was good. We ordered the goulash, jagershnitzel, sviekova, a Czech beer, and fruit pudding for dessert. Unfortunately, both of us got pretty sick by the next morning. I'm not sure if it's just the cuisine itself since we'd never had it before and maybe it was heavy on our system or if something maybe wasn't cooked properly and we didn't catch it since we're not familiar with the dishes. I don't want to point any fingers, because we truelly don't know but this ended up not being a fun experience. I tried calling the restaurant to just let them know, but the line goes to voicemail. We're still recovering from our visit, I personally haven't been able to leave the house because it's been that bad. Not really the experience we were aiming for. (2 stars)

I'm giving this restaurant a top rating even though I barely ate anything - the person who made the reservation didn't know I was vegetarian. Nonetheless I had a great time, as I love experiencing cuisines that I've never been exposed to, and this time, it was Czech food. We were a party of 7, all carnivores except for me, all drinkers except for me and my husband, and one of them is a beer connoisseur, so I learned that Pilsner, a pale lager, is the most famous Czech beer. The only option on the menu for me was a selection of salads, and I opted for one of my favorite vegetables - beetroot. Their servings are quite generous, and according to my fellow diners, the taste was impeccable. They ordered a lot of beer, and together we ordered a lot of food - salads, appetizers, mains, breads, and desserts. It's a large space, its walls covered with photos and objects of antiquity. One can definitely go around like in a museum and learn a bit about the history of Czech immigrants in New York City. If you love hearty meat dishes, exotic flavors and great beer, this place is definitely for you! (5 stars)

Went for brunch for the first time this weekend and it was such a pleasant place. The food was delicious and well-seasoned. The service was warm and welcoming. Also the brunch deal is great - we will definitely be back! (5 stars)

The staff is friendly, kind, inviting. This is an incredible place to eat and drink and we’re so lucky it’s right here in Manhattan! (5 stars) We heard about this restaurant on social media and had it saved on our to go list for a while. We had never had Czech food and they're the only Czech restaurant in Manhattan. So, we finally decided to take the 1 hour trip and try it out for our date night. Staff was helpful, warm, and friendly. They answered all our questions and made sure we felt confident about everything. Restaurant itself was clean and inviting, the bathrooms were kept up and everything was good. We ordered the goulash, jagershnitzel, sviekova, a Czech beer, and fruit pudding for dessert. Unfortunately, both of us got pretty sick by the next morning. I'm not sure if it's just the cuisine itself since we'd never had it before and maybe it was heavy on our system or if something maybe wasn't cooked properly and we didn't catch it since we're not familiar with the dishes. I don't want to point any fingers, because we truelly don't know but this ended up not being a fun experience. I tried calling the restaurant to just let them know, but the line goes to voicemail. We're still recovering from our visit, I personally haven't been able to leave the house because it's been that bad. Not really the experience we were aiming for. (2 stars) I'm giving this restaurant a top rating even though I barely ate anything - the person who made the reservation didn't know I was vegetarian. Nonetheless I had a great time, as I love experiencing cuisines that I've never been exposed to, and this time, it was Czech food. We were a party of 7, all carnivores except for me, all drinkers except for me and my husband, and one of them is a beer connoisseur, so I learned that Pilsner, a pale lager, is the most famous Czech beer. The only option on the menu for me was a selection of salads, and I opted for one of my favorite vegetables - beetroot. Their servings are quite generous, and according to my fellow diners, the taste was impeccable. They ordered a lot of beer, and together we ordered a lot of food - salads, appetizers, mains, breads, and desserts. It's a large space, its walls covered with photos and objects of antiquity. One can definitely go around like in a museum and learn a bit about the history of Czech immigrants in New York City. If you love hearty meat dishes, exotic flavors and great beer, this place is definitely for you! (5 stars) Went for brunch for the first time this weekend and it was such a pleasant place. The food was delicious and well-seasoned. The service was warm and welcoming. Also the brunch deal is great - we will definitely be back! (5 stars)

bio_text: Bonnie's is a vibrant dining establishment located in Brooklyn, New York, that celebrates the evolution of Cantonese cuisine through a personal lens. The restaurant embodies a warm and inviting atmosphere, reflecting the cultural journey of its founder, Calvin Eng, who aims to honor his heritage while contributing to the modern culinary landscape. With a focus on community and family, Bonnie's invites guests to experience a unique blend of traditional flavors and contemporary interpretations. Bonnie's specializes in Cantonese cuisine, showcasing a modern twist on classic dishes. The menu features a variety of offerings that highlight the rich flavors and techniques of Cantonese cooking, with an emphasis on fresh ingredients and authentic preparation methods. Bonnie's was founded by Calvin Eng, who draws inspiration from his upbringing as a Chinese American in Brooklyn. The restaurant is named after his mother, from whom he learned everything about Cantonese food.
menu_items: sang ho east coast oyster - ginger white peppercorn mignonette + apple - $4
chrysanthemum green salad - chrysanthemum leaves, greens, creamy soy sesame + crispy shallots - $17
tinned dace dip - tinned dace fish, fermented black beans + ritz - $9
dao gok - chinese long beans, fermented bean curd garlic butter + yauh ja gwai - $17
lo bak go - caramelized onion daikon radish cake, preserved radish + shrimp chili oil - $14
hup to ha - shrimp, candied walnuts, apple + honey kewpie mayo - $20
review_snippets: Nice little restaurant in Williamsburg. They had a special friend fish sandwich that was bomb. We also shared some fried squid and fries. The squid was probably small to share with four people. My husband and I shared some fries and the special sandwich. We also shared the sundae. I got one of the mocktails. My friend of the pork sandwich, which was large, but looked good too. I would go back if I was in the area. (5 stars)
Walnut shrimp was standout, the shrimp had perfect texture and flavor. Prob skip the cacio e Pepe and the crispy rice skate wings. interesting fusion food and cute vibes (4 stars)

Came here with my friend for a nice girls night! We got a reservation at 9 pm and it was crazy packed when we walked in. A bunch of people waiting. Took a bit to get our table but seemed like it was just people staying too long that caused backup. The place was sooo cute and cool and the bathroom was like a mini club which I loved. Music was perfect, playing all my favorites. Waitress was AWESOME and super helpful. We got espresso martinis which came out quick and green beans and wontons to start. Green beans turned out to be our fav fish and were delicious with some fried bread on top. Great flavor. Wontons were good too and had a curry/Indian flavor. I thought they could have been hotter (temp and spice level), but we enjoyed them. we also got the noodles. I personally don't like the rolled noodles and I thought the flavor was weird. But my friend loved them. Overall really thought this was a cool place and enjoyed our experience but didn't wow me like other spots in NYC. I'm also really tired of cocktails being $20, but I guess that's just what the reality is these days. (4 stars)

Made the “trek” to Brooklyn and was excited to try Bonnie’s. Service was good- the server was knowledgeable about the menu and very pleasant. Had heard ravings about the MSG martini which we tried, and also tried the sour cherry Negroni - neither were spectacular and the martini had a strange aftertaste. For food, we ordered the chrysanthemum salad (Don Angie’s is so much better) - which was a large portion but mostly cabbage (?), the long beans were too mushy for my liking (liked the fried crullers but they were overly salty), the fuyu cacio e pepe mein which was just ok, and the sundae for dessert which was not that interesting (I liked the fried condensed milk). We also had the shrimp with walnuts and broccoli which was pretty basic. Overall, the food was pretty disappointing and I would not go back… (2 stars)

menu_items: Duck and celery broth with ginger - $12
Chicken and foie gras terrine with rhubarb - $23
Sardine with kohlrabi and anchovy - $25
Sea urchin custard with fluke - $29
Tuna tartare with caper leaf - $22
Cured tuna with dates and young onion - $28
review_snippets: Loved and valued my entire experience here! From Cyrus being welcoming at the door, to my service from Kai and Onyx at the bar, the entire team glowed with hospitality and team work! The food was absolutely impeccable. Really enjoyed the Tuna, Mackerel, and the Pork Sausage! They all paired so well and effortlessly with Onyxs wine suggestions. I even got to make new friends too. Definitely recommend this lovely vibrant restaurant! :) (5 stars)

This restaurant was recently awarded a Michelin star, so of course I had to make the trek to try it. It's a bit funny walking into a classic French restaurant right in the middle of Chinatown. I ordered a few dishes to get a good sense of the menu: - Live Maine sea urchin, potato and brown butter - Cured tuna, dates, and spring onion - Pork collar with salsify and boudin noir - Comté tart with chanterelle and chestnut - Warm hazelnut tart, quince and chamomile cream The uni served inside the urchin shell was rich, creamy, and warm. It was one of the freshest uni servings I've had. But it's a whopping $22 for a very small portion, and realistically each person needs their own. The cured tuna came with five pieces and leaned a bit too sweet for my taste. The pork collar, on the other hand, was cooked to perfection -- tender, juicy, and balanced nicely by the savory boudin noir. The Comté tart topped with mushrooms was extremely dense and intense in flavor. It's apparently a classic French combination. It was $38 for a single slice, and I definitely wouldn't recommend ordering it on your own. The hazelnut tart was also pricey at $33, but this one I actually loved. It's a large round tart served with cream on the side, and the crust and warm hazelnut filling were comforting and delicious. Overall, the dishes were hit or miss, though the service was smooth and attentive. I'd say it's worth trying once if you enjoy classic French cooking and seasonal ingredients, but be prepared -- this place will absolutely break your wallet. (4 stars)

Bridges exceeded my expectations I was expecting like really good but nothing too crazy, but it was actually quite unique. I definitely had flavors that I haven't had before here. It's also a lot bigger than I was expecting which is cool the seats are very spaced out and it was elegant. Simple interior really good lighting which for some reason it's kind of hard to come by in New York. I really appreciated that about this place. I recommend going, get whatever calls to you I bet it will be good My favorites were the scallops, the Uni custard but mostly because the shrimp tartar on top is so crazy tasting and texture, the lobster bisque, and the chicken. I got the hazelnut tart because it's their special dessert, I never usually like hazelnuts that much and this was extremely hazelnutty and so I did not enjoy it so if you're on the fence because you don't like hazelnuts I would say do not get it because the hazelnut flavor is not mild whatsoever it is certainly the star of the show. (5 stars)

My favorite restaurant in NYC! Staff is super chill Kai, Samantha and Oniyx are spectacular. The food is priced really well. Ordered the Comte tart, uni, tuna and Vin Jeune ice cream. The Uni itself is worth the price of admission. The Comte tart was also unreal. And the wine by the glass list was lovely. Ambiance is elevated, professional but approachable. Can't recommend a place more than this one (5 stars)

bio_text: Bungalow is a vibrant culinary destination in the heart of New York City, offering an immersive experience that celebrates the rich history, culture, and exceptional cuisine of India. Helmed by Michelin-starred Chef Vikas Khanna, the restaurant invites guests on a journey through India's 28 states, showcasing time-honored recipes alongside reimagined classics. With a warm and welcoming atmosphere, Bungalow is not just a restaurant but a celebration of Indian hospitality and flavors, where every dish tells a story. Bungalow focuses on Indian cuisine, featuring a menu that highlights both traditional and contemporary dishes. The culinary experience is rooted in comfort food, drawing inspiration from cherished family recipes and regional specialties. Signature techniques include the use of authentic Indian spices and innovative presentations. Bungalow is the latest flagship restaurant from Michelin-starred Chef Vikas Khanna and Bombay House Hospitality, known for their other successful ventures like GupShup. The name 'Bungalow' is inspired by the Bengali term 'Bangla' and reflects the nostalgic essence of India's vintage clubhouses.
menu_items: PANEER LAZEEZ - Homemade Paneer, Cashew, Cardamom - $30
ALLEPPEY SHRIMP CURRY - Coconut, Tamarind, Green Mango - $34
CHICKEN AMRITSARI - Charred Tomato, Tandoori Spice Mix, Fenugreek, Cashew - $29
LAMB TELLICHERRY FRY - Coconut Chips, Black Pepper, Curry Leaves, Whole Wheat Crisps, Green Mango Sauce, Chickpea Droplets - $36
ACHARI STUFFED PANEER - Passion Fruit Chilli Chutney, Jackfruit Pickle - $28
MAL WANI FISH TIKKA - Salmon, Spicy Banana Ketchup, Lotus Root, Semolina Puffs, Beetroot Raita, Pineapple, Green Papaya Ribbon - $30
review_snippets: We recently visited Bungalow to celebrate our anniversary, and overall it was a lovely experience. The ambiance is beautiful and perfect for a special occasion. We really enjoyed the vibe of the place—it feels elegant but still warm and welcoming. For drinks, we tried the Guava Lemonade and a Falsa mocktail (I don’t remember the exact name), and both were refreshing and delicious. For appetizers, we ordered the Dahi Kebab and Achari Stuffed Panner. Dahi Kebab was absolutely amazing—definitely one of our favorite dishes of the evening. For the main course, we had the Okra dish and Old Delhi Chole. We really liked the okra—it was flavorful and well prepared. However, the chole was just okay and didn’t stand out as much as we expected. For dessert, we tried the Rose Kulfi. If you are a big fan of rose flavor, you’ll probably enjoy it. For us, it was good for a one-time try. One small detail that made the experience special was the little candy in a red packet at the end. It instantly reminded me of my childhood, which was such a sweet nostalgic touch. Overall, it’s good to visit Bungalow at least once for the experience. (4 stars)

Today we celebrated my son and wife’s birthdays together at Bungalow. It was an amazing dinner here. Truly a multi sensory experience! We’ve been following Chef Vikas Khanna on social media and it would have been amazing to meet him, but he’s in India right now to promote the latest season of Master Chef. We ordered Yogurt Kebab, Anarkali Chicken, Chicken Amritsari, Spice Roasted Pineapple, and Rose Kulfi Falooda. The yogurt kebab was absolutely delicious and highly recommend this unique dish. Both the chicken dishes were really good and all the sauces were tasty with a modern twist. The five cheese kulcha stuffed with Amul cheese reminds you of your childhood for those who grew up in India. Rose Kulfi Falooda was wonderful and it has all the classic falooda flavors and looks nothing like it. The atmosphere, service, fantastic desi music, and hospitality is unmatched from the moment you walk in. We had an absolutely fantastic experience at the Bungalow! (5 stars)

Bungalow is an experience. The moment you enter, the decor mesmerizes you. Sweet treats are kept for you to gorge on while you wait to be seated. You can grab a cocktail from the bar while you wait. The paan flavored old fashioned was the highlight drink of the night. To start with, the dahi kebabis a must!! That's the best food on the menu. All the other stuff we ordered were also very good but didn't stand out from a slightly lesser priced Indian restaurant. The service is amazing, the atmosphere amazing and overall an excellent experience. We didn'teet Vikas Khanna as he was out for a food show filming and hence missed the best part of the Bungalow experience. (4 stars)

Let me start by giving you important details: 1) Food - Overall 8/10 2) Ambience - 8/10 for us. If you like quiet tables where you can chat, this isn't the place. The restaurant is full for dinner (when we went), and tables fill up quickly. 3) Service - 10/10. Truly a "Atithi devo bhava" vibe. They are vigilant and very good in terms of service. Vegetarian food - I liked the pineapple curry and dahi ke kebabs the most. We ordered the okra dish and the sweet potato chaat too, but I did not feel "omg this is different". On the other hand, the pineapple dish was fantastic! The mixture of spice, sweetness, and coconutty flavors was worth it. The dahi ke kebabs are famous! If you've seen Chef's Instagram videos, this is his personal favorite on the menu, and for good reason. The yogurt is very well balanced with the dip. We did not try the lamb as we don't eat mutton, but the chicken and prawns were good. The dal was good too, but in my opinion, not the star dish of the night. You can take a look at the photos for the dishes, but I would say definitely say it's worth a visit. (4 stars)
