review_snippets: We really enjoyed our experience at Banh Anh Em. Even though we didn’t have a reservation, they were able to accommodate us within 10 minutes of our arrival, which we truly appreciated. We ordered the Cha Gio, Grilled scallop with butter , Banh Beo, Banh Xeo pancake, and Banh Mi. Each dish was fabulous in its own way — fresh, flavorful, and beautifully prepared. The Banh Mi and Grilled scallop with butter were definitely our favorites. Highly recommend trying them! The friendly service made the whole experience feel extra special and welcoming. We would absolutely come back again. (5 stars)

The BEST bánh mì I’ve ever had. The OG bánh mì was packed with flavor. It was savory, balanced, and the pork floss was such a nice touch, adding a light, airy texture with a subtly sweet-savory richness that complemented the fillings really well. The grilled ribeye steak bánh mì was just as good. I don’t know what they put in that sauce, but it was insanely savory and umami. Every bite was bursting with flavor without being overwhelming. The steak itself was juicy, tender, and really well-charred, with a deep beefy flavor that paired so well with the freshness of the pickled vegetables and herbs. Fun fact (from the server we talked to): the owner started this spot after working at Hanoi House, another popular Vietnamese restaurant nearby. (5 stars)

The best Vietnamese food in town I’ve ever had. This wasn’t my first visit, if I remember correctly, it was already my fourth time here. This time I came with friends, and we had to wait in line. When the restaurant opened, we put our names on the waitlist and waited at the bar nearby. After about an hour, we got a text that our table was ready. Totally worth the wait. The food came out quickly and tasted amazing. We ordered Bánh Bèo, summer rolls with shrimp, scallops with scallion oil, Thịt Kho, Bánh Cuốn Hà Nội, and several other dishes I can’t even remember - there was a lot of food, and everything was phenomenal. For drinks, I had the coconut cream coffee 🥥 and the egg cream iced coffee both were incredible. The prices are very reasonable for the quality and experience. Great vibes, and the staff were so kind and friendly. I highly recommend this place and can’t wait to come back again. (5 stars)

We arrived at 5:15 PM and were 4th in line by 5:25 PM. This place is famous for its Banh Mi, and as a native of Hai Phong, I had to try the Banh Mi Pate Hai Phong. The dipping sauce was a great touch! We also tried the Heo Quay and OG Banh Mi—all very delicious, though I personally prefer a slightly chewier baguette over one that is crunchy all the way through. The Bun Cha Ha Noi was nearly perfect; the sauce and sides were spot on, though the Cha Nem could have been fried a bit longer to get that deep golden brown shell. Skip the scallops with melted cheese if you don't like sweets—they were a bit too sugary for me. The decor and vibe are stylish and authentic to Northern Vietnam. It is definitely worth trying for the food, but the long wait in the NYC cold makes it hard to justify a second trip during winter. (5 stars)
search_text: Bánh Anh Em We really enjoyed our experience at Banh Anh Em. Even though we didn’t have a reservation, they were able to accommodate us within 10 minutes of our arrival, which we truly appreciated. We ordered the Cha Gio, Grilled scallop with butter , Banh Beo, Banh Xeo pancake, and Banh Mi. Each dish was fabulous in its own way — fresh, flavorful, and beautifully prepared. The Banh Mi and Grilled scallop with butter were definitely our favorites. Highly recommend trying them! The friendly service made the whole experience feel extra special and welcoming. We would absolutely come back again. (5 stars) The BEST bánh mì I’ve ever had. The OG bánh mì was packed with flavor. It was savory, balanced, and the pork floss was such a nice touch, adding a light, airy texture with a subtly sweet-savory richness that complemented the fillings really well. The grilled ribeye steak bánh mì was just as good. I don’t know what they put in that sauce, but it was insanely savory and umami. Every bite was bursting with flavor without being overwhelming. The steak itself was juicy, tender, and really well-charred, with a deep beefy flavor that paired so well with the freshness of the pickled vegetables and herbs. Fun fact (from the server we talked to): the owner started this spot after working at Hanoi House, another popular Vietnamese restaurant nearby. (5 stars) The best Vietnamese food in town I’ve ever had. This wasn’t my first visit, if I remember correctly, it was already my fourth time here. This time I came with friends, and we had to wait in line. When the restaurant opened, we put our names on the waitlist and waited at the bar nearby. After about an hour, we got a text that our table was ready. Totally worth the wait. The food came out quickly and tasted amazing. We ordered Bánh Bèo, summer rolls with shrimp, scallops with scallion oil, Thịt Kho, Bánh Cuốn Hà Nội, and several other dishes I can’t even remember - there was a lot of food, and everything was phenomenal. For drinks, I had the coconut cream coffee 🥥 and the egg cream iced coffee both were incredible. The prices are very reasonable for the quality and experience. Great vibes, and the staff were so kind and friendly. I highly recommend this place and can’t wait to come back again. (5 stars) We arrived at 5:15 PM and were 4th in line by 5:25 PM. bio_text: bōm offers an immersive dining experience that engages all the senses, featuring a progressive Korean tasting menu served at an intimate chef’s counter equipped with custom built-in grills. Under the guidance of Michelin-starred chef Brian Kim and the OIJI MI team, guests are treated to an elevated sensory journey that combines a unique steakhouse concept with a front-row view of the culinary artistry in action. The restaurant specializes in a modern interpretation of traditional Korean cuisine, presented through a highly curated tasting menu. Each course highlights seasonal ingredients, showcasing creative techniques that elevate the dining experience. bōm, meaning 'Spring' in Korean, is an abbreviation of 'behind OIJI MI.'
review_snippets: A phenomenal experience! Bom was top tier in every element- food, drinks, service, decor, etc. I celebrated my birthday here and the staff were exceptionally sweet. They are very attentive and will take care of you. The food was creative and every bite was balanced in flavour. You also get a lot of food for a tasting menu. Expect to leave stuffed. We opted for all of the upgrades available at the time, which were caviar, truffles, and A5. The first two were used as enhancements to dishes in the menu, and the A5 was grilled as extra protein for the congee set at the end. It was all incredible! If I had to pick my favourite dishes of the night, they would be the tofu course with perilla oil dressing, or the dry aged ribeye course. We will definitely be back! (5 stars)

What an experience!! I celebrated my birthday in December and enjoyed the tasting menu with champagne pairing. I was told the champagne pairing was only an option during December so lucky me! The food was amazing. From the small bites to the dessert, I was constantly wanting more. Not because I wasn’t satisfied by the amount but because I didn’t want it to end. There was one dish, as beautiful as it was, I wasn’t a fan. I think it was tofu and I don’t like the texture. The champagne paired nicely, however, I wouldn’t do it again next time. The pairing cost more than the dinner, so I would have preferred slightly heavier pours :) I often dine alone and I didn’t feel out of place. The presentations from the chef’s and somm were on point and the small chats with the somm made me feel a part of the whole room. None of my words can do Bōm justice. Run don’t walk and treat yourself to an unforgettable night of beautiful and tasty dishes. (5 stars)

I celebrated my birthday here with my wife and we had a great experience. From the 1st bite of housemade jerky to the final dessert course we enjoyed it all. We added 1 serving of the a5 wagyu to our tasting menu and it was well worth the price. The service and atmosphere were top tier (5 stars)

My fiance and I went here as a christmas present to ourselves; we'd never done a culinary experience before with multiple courses. The food was exquisite. Such thought and time was put into every bite of this meal. Flavors exploded with one small bite. The presentation was flawless. We did an NA pairing that consisted of tea and NA alcohol that went beautifully with each course. (5 stars)

bio_text: C as in Charlie is a vibrant dining establishment located in the heart of New York City, offering a unique blend of culinary creativity and a welcoming atmosphere. The restaurant is characterized by its playful yet sophisticated vibe, making it an ideal spot for both casual diners and those seeking a more refined experience. The restaurant focuses on innovative dishes that reflect a modern take on classic flavors. With a menu that emphasizes seasonal ingredients, C as in Charlie offers a diverse selection of dishes designed to delight the palate. THREE BOYS FROM ATL OPEN A RESTAURANT IN NYC
menu_items: tofu ricotta spread - honey, orange, brioche - $12
green pea salad - avocado, cucumber, gooseberry - $17
soy salmon crudo - oboro kombu, cucumber, granny smith - $14
mushroom bibimbap - hen of the woods, shimeji, egg - $12
oxbone cream pasta - spaghetti, bacon, scallion - $13
crab drop - silken tofu, holy trinity, bonito cream - $12
review_snippets: A nice tapas place. Service was friendly and very fast. I think we were in and out in 45 min on Sunday night. The two of us had four tapas dishes (see photos). The popcorn chicken and oxbone cereal pasta are def worth trying and very tasty. The tuna tartare and seoulsbury steak were fine, seemed pretty standard. We weren’t really sure what the Korean twist on those two dishes was. We didn’t order any drinks, but they did give us two small shots on the house. I would go back to try other tapas. (4 stars)

Incredible experience. Food was amazing and made with finesse and deep flavors. Service is quick friendly and you feel welcome right from the start. Menu is well explained. Atmosphere is packed but cosy - a very lively NYC neighborhood experience. I would come back any time - our highlights were the Steak with a cream that was outstanding, the Popcorn chicken, Pasta and Mushroom Bibimbap (little marinated button mushrooms for extra pops of deep flavor which we found genius) - must tries when you are there! (5 stars)

We were incredibly impressed at C as in Charlie. Every single dish we had was very good - 3 of them were exceptional. The mozzarella/green pepper with soy balsamic was insanely good, the ribs were melt in your mouth and the prawn roll delicious too. Service was excellent and the restaurant had a real buzz/warmth to it. Absolutely shouldn’t be missed. Surprisingly reasonably priced too. (5 stars)

While visiting the town, we met up with friends to catchup. I saw this place listed on the Michelin Bib Gourmand list and snagged a reservation. They do enforce a two-hour time limit for parties of four. As my friend was running late, the servers frequently reminded us of the time constraint. Fortunately, we finished our meal within the allotted time; I have never encountered a restaurant that did so many reminders about the dining time. This was the only minor drawback; otherwise, I would have given it a perfect rating. The mushroom bibimbap was exceptional; I could have easily eaten just a big bowl of that and been happy. The potato nuggets were also quite delicious, with the truffle aioli. The popcorn chicken, however, was not my favorite, as it seemed excessively sauced. The food portion sizes were ideal for sharing among our group of four. It came out at a pretty good price point per diner, especially for the area. (4 stars)

bio_text: Cafe Commerce is an upscale neighborhood restaurant that embodies the philosophy of bistronomy, offering a warm and inviting atmosphere for both regulars and newcomers. With an intimate setting featuring 15 carefully arranged tables, the restaurant aims to be a hidden gem, providing a relaxed dining experience enhanced by exceptional cuisine and genuine hospitality. The menu reflects a unique blend of American cuisine crafted in the French tradition, complemented by cleverly crafted cocktails and a curated selection of wines. Cafe Commerce focuses on bistronomy, merging the vibrant spirit of New York City with the soulful essence of France. The menu features American cuisine prepared in the French tradition, with an emphasis on small, well-executed dishes. Established in 2024, Cafe Commerce was founded by Chef Harold Moore, Managing Partner Charles Pouchot, and Business Partner Patrick Corbett, drawing on their extensive experience in the culinary field. Chef Harold Moore has a distinguished career, having worked in renowned kitchens and earned accolades including a Michelin star.
menu_items: Herb Salad - manchego & lemon vinaigrette - $24
Chicken Noodle Soup - grandma’s vegetables & chives - $22
Marinated Hamachi - avocado, ginger, jalapeño & yuzu - $34
Half Dozen Island Creek Oysters - pickled shallot mignonette - $26
Beef Carpaccio - capers, horseradish & crispy hash browns - $27
Sea Scallops - leeks, mushrooms & escargot butter - $28
review_snippets: I dined at Cafe Commerce on Valentine’s Day for the prix-fixe menu and had such a wonderful experience. The food was truly excellent — the sweet potato tortellini was rich and perfectly balanced, and the short rib was incredibly tender; the perfect comfort meal. What really made the evening special, though, was the service — especially Raymond. He was an absolute pleasure to chat with, explained the menu in detail, answered all of our questions with care, and gave top-tier recommendations. His warmth and professionalism elevated the entire night. I’ll definitely be back and strongly recommend! (5 stars)

Food was very good. Scallops, burger and Branzino were highlights. Birthday cake was nostalgically good. Prices were high, especially for alcohol (friend had an $18 mocktail - there's no alcohol!! How are we paying $18 for juice and carbonated water?!? Even the birthday cake, which is just yellow cake with chocolate icing was $24!). If prices were more reasonable I'd say 5 stars, but factoring in value, 4 stars. (4 stars)

I recently dined at Cafe Commerce and had an exceptional experience that I just had to share! We started our meal with the Hamachi, which was nothing short of excellent—perfectly fresh and beautifully presented. For the main course, we indulged in the Rigatoni Carbonara and the Chicken Schnitzel. The carbonara was creamy and rich, with just the right amount of seasoning, while the schnitzel was crispy on the outside and tender inside, making it a delightful comfort food choice. To top off our meal, we ordered the birthday cake for dessert. It was a sweet celebration that was simply delicious—moist, flavorful, and the perfect ending to our dining experience. What truly stood out was the staff; they were beyond nice, attentive, and made us feel welcome throughout our visit. Everything about Cafe Commerce was over the top in the best way possible. This spot has quickly become one of my new favorite restaurants in New York City, and I can't wait to return! Highly recommend it to anyone looking for a fantastic dining experience! (5 stars)

Stopped by yesterday for lunch before a visit to the new Frick and felt like a local and a regular right away. The place was filled with people who seemed like they’ve been coming for years. Each person more interesting than the last. We sat next to an a friendly couple who lived in the neighborhood and struck up a conversation. The service was superb and the team made sure our water glasses were never empty and we were sat right away and offered all the seasonal specials including the mulled wine, Gruyère grilled cheese with tomato soup and chicken salad. Started with the deviled eggs and table bread and butter. All were delicious. Will definitely stop back by when in the area again. Thanks team! (5 stars)

bio_text: Cafe Mado is a charming neighborhood restaurant located just steps from the Brooklyn Museum and the Brooklyn Botanic Garden. With a focus on creating a warm and inviting atmosphere, it offers a delightful dining experience for both brunch and dinner, accommodating both reservations and walk-in diners. Cafe Mado specializes in a diverse menu that reflects high standards of hospitality and quality. The restaurant serves seated dining for brunch and dinner, emphasizing a collective narrative enriched by its staff. The restaurant is named in homage to Marie Louise 'Madame Mado' Point, known for her exceptional hospitality at La Pyramide in Vienne. Cafe Mado occupies the space previously home to Oxalis and aims to continue the legacy of quality and service.
menu_items: Bien Cuit Baguette, Our Butter - None - $11.0
Le Caesar - None - $23.0
Butter Bean Puree, Grilled Escarole - None - $22.0
Smoked Trout, Avocado, Frisee - None - $19.0
Red Endive, Bayley Hazen, Pecan - None - $18.0
Fingerling Potatoes, Espelette Hollandaise - None - $14.0
review_snippets: It’s great for shareable plate and date night, so get 4-6 dishes will be idea! We loved salad, freshly grated cheese created a umami taste and it was very refreshing! Pork was juicy and tender which we also enjoyed. Ragu was alright - way too al dente and salty in our opinion. (4 stars)

We LOVED our dinner experience in their cutest backyard, super peaceful and memorable! We also really enjoyed the food, the butter was out of this world, the baguette was amazing, the eggplant sesame dip was delicious, the smoked date provolone farinata was insane, the Caesar salad was perfect, the cabbage dish was soooo mouthwatering and my favourite dish of all, followed by the bean purée and the crazily yummy sourdough bread next to it as rank two! I didn’t try the rib chops but my friends were dying for it loool The only thing I didn’t like (but the rest of tbh party did) was the trout crudo, for which I blame Theodora for shooting my expectations for crudos to the roof! Also I couldn’t get my head around the price for that little amount of harissa, which wasn’t even that special, neither were the fries (and this one, everyone else was on the same page as me) Oh and there was this empanada shaped dumpling bread dish that we loved but don’t recall the name. Overall, we really enjoyed our meal and we will be back :) (5 stars)

Delicious and refreshingly original take on lunch and brunch. Every dish is refined and inventive, blending different cuisines and flavors in a way that really works. Most of our dishes had a subtle kick. The experience felt energizing compared to the usual predictable brunch scene. (5 stars)

Very interesting place with not too big, but very creative menue. You better ask the server or Google some terms that they using to describe their dishes. But don't get me wrong, this sophistication matches the taste. Everything including bread was a top notch. Personally my favorites were the pasta, skate wing and the pork. Unfortunately I was so full that had no space for a dessert, but from what other people having it looked very interesting. The place has inside seating as well as outside on the backyard. They are quite popular so reservation is highly recommended. (5 stars)

bio_text: Café Sabarsky offers a refined dining experience inspired by the iconic Viennese cafés of 20th century Austria. Located within the Neue Galerie New York, the café is adorned with period furnishings and art, creating an atmosphere that reflects the intellectual and artistic vibrancy of its historical roots. Guests can enjoy a blend of culinary excellence and cultural performances, including cabaret and classical music, in a setting that is both elegant and inviting. Café Sabarsky specializes in elevated Austrian cuisine, featuring a menu that includes breakfast, lunch, and dinner options. The dining experience is complemented by a three-course dinner served during cabaret performances, showcasing the restaurant's commitment to both culinary artistry and cultural heritage. Café Sabarsky is named after Serge Sabarsky, co-founder of the Neue Galerie New York, and has been a distinguished dining destination for two decades under the direction of Executive Chef Christopher Engel.

review_snippets: Beautiful dining room and prompt service and gorgeous plating. The waiters can’t really pronounce the names of the menu items either so English or pointing works well. I decided to add rum to the Viennese hot chocolate and it was perfect. The whipped cream was rich but not sweetened which balanced out the sweetness of the hot chocolate. It was also served at the perfect temperature. Hubby got the smoked trout crepe which was delicious. My roasted potatoes with egg, cheese, bacon, and pickles was also tasty although I did add salt and pepper. The bread and butter that came with the entrees was a nice touch. There were two types of bread. My only complain is that the butter could’ve been a bit softer for spreading purposes. We arrived right at 9:00 (opening time) and there were already a few people in line ahead of us. Note: The Cafe is in a museum. Your bags will be searched upon entry and they also dump out any water bottles you may have. There is a water filling station in the basement near the restrooms that can be visiting after your meal. (5 stars)

(July 5, 2025) This restaurant was in my bucket list for about a year then as an Austrian cuisine restaurant where I wanted to try the Sacher Torte cake. The décor was posh with tall ceilings and live piano music. The three of us tried the following: 1. Beet salad -- Cold and refreshing. The beets were sweet in a nice way. 2. Pea soup -- Warm and thick. Felt wholesome. The floating oil (unmixed with the soup) was noticeable to taste. Went well with the bread. 3. Sachet torte --- It was NOT like the original in Vienna. The icing isn't solid enough, the cake isn't chocolatey enough. It felt like "too much alcohol", my friend pointed out. A fancy place at a very nice location that requires advance table reservations where the food is decent and somewhat overpriced. (3 stars)

Typically only walk in only (unless you're a member), but worth the wait! Beautiful sprawling tall ceilings and tiny marble tables. Once you are seated, service is quick and precise. Any of the open face fish sandwiches are a great choice, along with a nice slice of chocolate cake to top off the brunch. Beware, the coffee is VERY STRONG (rightly so), I had to ask for extra steamed milk. (5 stars)

As a Swiss person, I was so pleasently suprised by this place. You can expect veeery authentic Austrian dishes, I loved the Schnitzel, Sauerkraut and Kaiserschmarrn. Really so good, also the ambiente felt like in a Café in Vienna. Absolutely loved it! (5 stars)

bio_text: Café Boulud, helmed by renowned chef Daniel Boulud, offers a sophisticated dining experience that blends French culinary traditions with a contemporary flair. Located in vibrant cities such as New York City, Palm Beach, and Toronto, the restaurant exudes an elegant yet inviting atmosphere, making it a perfect destination for both casual diners and special occasions. Café Boulud focuses on French cuisine, showcasing seasonal ingredients and classic techniques. The menu features a variety of options, including à la carte selections and tasting menus, highlighting the chef's signature dishes. Café Boulud is led by celebrated chef Daniel Boulud, known for his contributions to the culinary world and his commitment to excellence.

review_snippets: My boyfriend and I went for Valentine’s Day. It was so wonderful. The prix fixe meal was delicious. The mushroom risotto was the best risotto I’ve ever had in my life! And the desserts were so artfully displayed. Every bite was amazing. Service was impeccable, with strong attention to detail. The restaurant itself is gorgeous. Highly recommend. (5 stars)

My family and I had an excellent brunch at Café Bouloud. The restaurant provided the type of service that you would expect at a refined restaurant. The food was top notch from beginning to end. We started with viennoisesies basket and the bloody Mary shrimp ceviche. We all agreed that the ceviche was truly outstanding. For the main course, we ordered the croque monsieur, french toast and eggs benedict with smoked salmon. All three were shared and enjoyed. The dining experience was completed with the assortment de cookies and Paris brest noisette et chocolat. We left the restaurant full and happy. (5 stars)

We tried the restaurant week 3 course lunch. The food tasted great, well seasoned and balanced. I loved every bite. I felt underfed at the eof my meal, whereas my two friends felt very full. I assume it’s bcz one of them got risotto and the other a chicken dish while I got the fish which was a thin slice and light to eat. Again during dessert I liked my dessert the best over the other two we ordered at the table to taste all three dessert options. the bread was too cold for me to enjoy and we didn’t get any butter at our table! But overall the visit was pleasant with nice tasting dishes. (5 stars)

Exceptional service & unforgettable wine pairing We had such a beautiful evening at Café Boulud. The food was refined, perfectly executed, and felt both classic and exciting. But what truly made the night special was our server, Simone. Simone was absolutely outstanding!!!! warm, attentive, and incredibly knowledgeable. His wine pairing recommendations were spot on. Every selection complemented the dishes perfectly and elevated the entire meal. You can tell he genuinely understands wine and cares about the experience he creates for his guests. At the end of the evening, he even gave us a tour of the space, which was such a thoughtful and memorable touch. That level of hospitality is rare. If you’re dining here, ask for Simone, he is truly one of the best servers we’ve ever had. (5 stars)

bio_text: Café Carmellini is a distinguished fine dining restaurant located in New York City, helmed by James Beard Award-winning chef Andrew Carmellini. The restaurant offers a modern and sophisticated culinary experience that seamlessly blends Italian and French influences with a classic New York sensibility. Set within a beautifully reimagined neoclassical mansion, the ambiance is characterized by lush maximalist design, creating an elegant and inviting atmosphere for diners. The menu at Café Carmellini features a creative fusion of Italian and French cuisine, showcasing both reimagined classics and innovative seasonal dishes. The dining experience is complemented by a carefully curated wine program, boasting an extensive 1,800-bottle list curated by Master Sommelier Josh Nadel. Café Carmellini marks Chef Andrew Carmellini's return to fine dining, drawing on his 30-year career in New York City. The restaurant's name pays homage to the chef's family coffee importing business, which thrived in Tuscany for 120 years.

review_snippets: If you are looking for a venue that screams "New York Glamour," Café Carmellini in the Fifth Avenue Hotel is a top-tier contender. It is a stunning, high-energy space that feels like a modern tribute to the Gilded Age, complete with sculptural trees and sapphire-blue velvet booths. The "good looking" factor here is undeniable. From the moment you walk into the neoclassical dining room, the scale and design are breathtaking. The service is equally polished; the staff operates with a level of professionalism that makes you feel genuinely cared for without being overbearing. It’s the kind of place where your water glass is never empty, and the timing of the courses is handled with precision. The menu is sophisticated. Everything we tried was technically flawless and high-quality. While the food is undeniably "great," it leans toward the classical and safe. If you’re a frequent diner at NYC’s smaller, experimental "hidden gems," you might find it lacks that elusive "wow factor" or creative edge that smaller kitchens often provide. It’s delicious, but perhaps more "perfectly executed" than "groundbreaking. The Budget ? Be prepared ! This is a high-end experience, and the bill reflects it ! I strongly recommend Café Carmellini for a one-time event—an anniversary, a milestone birthday, or a business dinner where you need to impress. It’s a beautiful spectacle and a solid meal, even if it doesn't quite reach the soulful heights of the city’s smaller cult favorites. (4 stars)

Love the elegant and grand space - I felt a bit theater vibe. The service was the top notch, attentive, warm and welcoming. We started with crab & meyer lemon mille feuille and finished with chocolate & pear mille feuille. The textures of the mille feuille were different, but both were delivered well. While the risotto was a bit cold, but lobster frittata was fantastic. The team offered us a complementary dessert as a makeup for the not-too-perfect risotto - very sincere and thoughtful hospitality! (5 stars)

went for lunch. food was well plated and served on such beautiful plates, but it was missing flavor. my black bass was not seasoned or spiced at all and the sauce it came with did not combine with the filet at all. (they did not play together) however, the mashed potatoes it came with was damn good. their sourdough bread was also lack of any flavor or sour notes you would expect from a typical sourdough… again the butter it was served with was better than the bread itself. i have now confirmed chef carmellini’s food and i do not go well together. feel the same way about any jean george restaurants also… with that said, the space is very nice and welcoming. staff was very attentive and friendly. i will not be returning. (2 stars)

Came for our wedding anniversary and had a wonderful experience. Service was the highlight as they made the experience superb. Foodwise the chocolate dessert was my favorite as well as the bavette where the layered fried potatoe was nice. Chicken was feally well cooked and the peppers on the side where even better than the chicken. I wanted to come for brunch but realized it was lunch only at 1pm, but worked put the pre fix menu and went for it. Place is trendy, smells incredible and fancy. (5 stars)

review_snippets: My family and I walked in over Labor Day weekend for brunch on Sunday and loved everything about this place (the food, the garden) except for the service. My boyfriend and I both work in hospitality so we appreciate great service, but we're not unrealistic with our expectations. We just appreciate kind people who aren't overbearing or pressing, but the woman who served us was so cold and rude, it truly made us feel uncomfortable. There was no warm greeting, not even a smile, she barely spoke a word to us the entire time we were there. We were one of two tables in the garden and there were 3 tables in the front, so it's not like she was busy or anything. The 3 of us ordered the dandelion salad, French toast, poached eggs entree, zucchini blossoms, bacon and hasbrowns. Our server didn't check on us once. Never asked how our meal was, if we needed anything, literally not a word. She literally just took our order, put the plates down and we never heard from her again. The service was very robotic, truly it was like a robot was serving us, because there was just nothing personable about it. There are a lot of places in NY with good food, but it's the service that sets it apart. I dont think we'll be returning or recommending this place. (3 stars)

Sam, the general manager, made this an unforgettable night for my mom and me. We agreed it was one of the best meals we’ve ever had. The bread and the halibut were delicious beyond words. The tuna with greens was surprisingly delightful (more my mom’s taste than mine, but I’m glad I tried). We could have done without the chilled shrimp crudo, missed the mark for us. The drink list was incredible, and our bottle (the Patapon white) was perfection. Well worth the trek to Red Hook! Thanks to Helen Rosner for the rec and lovely write-up! (5 stars)

I’d say this place is really good value in NYC. For me, everything pictured here (split with my friend) represented about $75 (including tip). The experience is very similar to eating in a Parisian bistro, with the tables being right next to each other in a small environment. The upside to that is that the service was very good—shout out to the staff who were consistently filling my water since I drink a lot 😂 For the food, I was very impressed by the “toast” which is just a grilled baguette. I really like the charred flavor that was imparted onto the bread, which I would gladly have eaten on its own. We were both surprised by the cafe salad, where the cheese blindsided us. We assumed it was going to be something like butternut squash, but were pleasantly surprised by how everything came together. It was a rather unusual combination that just worked. I really enjoyed the swordfish due to how deeply charred it was. One thing that my friend and I do at the end of these types of meals is to rank the dishes. Something that he pointed out with this establishment was that the variance of the enjoyment of our dishes was actually quite low—our favorite dish was not too far away from our least favorite dish. This observation I believe perfectly encapsulates the experience to be had here: everything is very well executed, and it’s unlikely that any individual item will leave one unsatisfied. I give this place my recommendation, but be sure to make a reservation in advance. (5 stars)

this place is such a gem! i love how intimate and cozy it felt, it was perfect for date night. highlights on the menu were the baguette with seaweed butter (so good), yellowfin tuna with blood orange & avocados, and the apricot cake (a must). will have to come back to try their spring menu next. (5 stars)

bio_text: Café Mars is an innovative Italian restaurant located in the heart of Gowanus, Brooklyn, that seeks to redefine the Italian dining experience. Opened in May 2023, the restaurant combines traditional Italian roots with modern interpretations, creating a vibrant atmosphere that celebrates culinary creativity. With a focus on community and collaboration, Café Mars invites guests to explore a diverse menu that reflects the global influence of Italian cuisine. Café Mars specializes in Itameshi, a unique fusion of Italian and Japanese culinary traditions. The menu features innovative dishes that incorporate Japanese ingredients into Italian frameworks, such as fluke cured in Parm and white miso, and pan-fried tortellini-gyoza. The restaurant offers a dynamic dining experience with a focus on seasonal and unexpected flavors. Café Mars was opened in May 2023 by co-chefs Paul D’Avino and Juan David Gracia, along with Service Director Stephen Puntillo. The restaurant occupies a former pasta factory and Italian grocer, and is inspired by the legacy of Paul’s great grandfather, who immigrated to Brooklyn from Campania, Italy in 1901. The team aims to honor Italian traditions while expanding the definition of Italian cuisine.

review_snippets: Everything was great, and appreciated the friendly service. Highly recommend checking this place out. + Fires of Vesuvius was our favorite cocktail. Strong flavor and great spice level. + Enjoyed the crudo. It was light and fresh, packed with flavor. + Monkey bread seems popular, so I don't have much to add. I will say, it was larger than expected and pretty filling! + Definitely preferred the riggies over the rotalini. I just don't think we had the palate for the broccoli rabe. + Panna cotta had three or four layers, so satisfying to take a spoonful. + Baba-yaki was interesting. Great texture, and fun to eat. Cafe Mars is one of the most creative dining experiences I’ve had in Brooklyn. The gel olives were super unique a really fun, flavorful dish that shows how playful their menu is. I tried the Riggies, which is originally an Ithaca, New York dish that’s normally made with chicken, but here they do a version with mussels. It ended up being really good and full of flavor definitely worth ordering if you want something different. The decor is beautiful, with a cool, modern vibe, and the service is extremely friendly and attentive. Overall, a great spot if you’re looking for something creative and memorable in Gowanus. (5 stars)

Café Mars is such a funky place from their creative dishes to their interior design. The staff were all super friendly and welcoming throughout our time there! My favorite was the girelle pasta. Ended up being pretty pricey for each person (I somehow forgot to take all photos, but we’ve ordered more than what’s shown here). (4 stars)

The inside is cute and we appreciated the creativity! The food was 50/50: monkey bread and lemon pasta were ah-mazing and worth the trip! The service was good, however, it was really odd to have the utensil drawer being restocked at our table multiple times during our meal. (3 stars)

bio_text: Caleta 111 Cevicheria is a vibrant and welcoming Peruvian restaurant located in Richmond Hill, NY, known for its authentic flavors and cozy atmosphere. With a focus on providing a fast yet quality dining experience, the restaurant is perfect for both quick lunches and relaxed dinners. The friendly staff and lively ambiance create an inviting space for guests to enjoy a culinary journey through Peru, complemented by a well-curated selection of beverages. Caleta 111 specializes in authentic Peruvian cuisine, featuring a menu that highlights traditional dishes such as ceviche, lomo saltado, and causa de pulpo. The restaurant emphasizes fresh ingredients and bold flavors, with signature techniques that celebrate coastal Peruvian traditions.

review_snippets: Food was phenomenal. Portions were kinda small for the price (everything is pricey ) I recommend the ceviche appetizer and the rice with seafood was amazing. One server was super nice but the one with the long hair had an attitude. Then there's the whole, machine is broken cash only thing which was not cool. Other than that the decor is amazing. (4 stars)

The chef is crazy. The food even crazier...in the BEST way. Ceviche second to none...can and do drink the tigers milk by the glass. Chicken? Stupid tasty, marinated with peruvian magic. Pisco sours are very solid. The ambiance feels like being transported to a different realm, forgetting one is in queens and not lima, peru. (5 stars)
My wife and I went to Caleta 111 and had the ceviche mixto,and the arroz con mariscos. The food was amazing. I haven't had ceviche that was so fresh in a long time. (5 stars)

Ordered ceviche mixto, arroz de mariscos and lomo saltado for take out. I’m Peruvian and this food was awful. The lomo tasted like vinegar and it didn’t come with rice. The ceviche didn’t taste authentic at all. And the worst dish was the arroz de mariscos. Soggy rice and barely any flavor. This place is overhyped. The worst part is how expensive the food was (1 stars)

bio_text: Carbone is a celebrated Italian restaurant located in the heart of New York City, offering a quintessential dining experience that blends old-world glamour with contemporary sophistication. The restaurant features charismatic service, with captains in tuxedos, and a vibrant atmosphere enhanced by vintage and contemporary artworks. Guests are welcomed into an intimate space that evokes the elegance of mid-century New York, making it a perfect setting for both special occasions and casual dining. Carbone focuses on Italian-American cuisine, drawing inspiration from the culinary history of Little Italy. The menu features classic dishes that emphasize top-quality ingredients and traditional techniques, presented in a glamorous and fun dining format. Signature offerings include a variety of Italian classics that reflect the chef's deep-rooted connection to his heritage. Founded in 2013 by Chefs Mario Carbone, Rich Torrisi, and Jeff Zalaznick, Carbone was created to be a modern Italian-American restaurant that honors the culinary traditions of the past while delivering exceptional hospitality. Chef Mario Carbone's culinary journey began in Queens, New York, and was further enriched by a year spent in Italy, which inspired his cooking and identity.
menu_items: Carpaccio Piemontese - $34
Calamari Marco - $36
Beets Siciliana - $21
Prosciutto & Mozzarella - $35
Octopus Pizzaiolo - $38
Assorted Baked Clams - $39
review_snippets: Carbone brought Italian-American dining back to the center of New York and did it with style that nobody else has been able to touch. The spicy rigatoni vodka is the dish that launched a thousand imitations and none of them come close. The veal parmesan is a two-person commitment and worth every bite. Walking into the dining room feels like stepping into a 1950s supper club dark leather tuxedoed waiters Frank Sinatra energy without the costume. Mario Carbone and Rich Torrisi understood something that most chefs miss entirely you do not need to reinvent Italian food you need to perfect it. Every dish on this menu is a love letter to the red sauce joints that built this city and every bite proves they studied the originals until they could do it better. The Caesar salad is prepared tableside and it is theater and substance in equal measure. The wine list is Italian-heavy with deep cuts from regions most people have never heard of. Getting a reservation requires either patience or connections and the fact that the waiting list is months long tells you everything. I have eaten here multiple times and I have never once been disappointed. New York is full of Italian restaurants claiming to be the best. Carbone does not claim anything. It just proves it every single night. Go hungry and bring someone you want to impress. (5 stars)

EPIC. INCREDIBLE. BEST MEAL IN NYC! I’ve been wanting to come here for years! Bucket list experience ACHIEVED! I will be trying to find spicy vodka rigatoni that good for the rest of my life. Lemon cheesecake was the best I’ve ever had as well. Start to finish, the meal was indulgent and the service was unparalleled! (5 stars)

Carbone absolutely lives up to the hype. The spicy rigatoni is perfect—rich, decadent sauce with just the right kick. The chicken Massimo was surprisingly good: sweet, beautifully charred on the outside, tender on the inside, and finished with a deliciously creamy sauce. It came with shallots which were cooked perfectly! The baked clams were excellent (loved that you can substitute bacon for breadcrumbs), and the Caesar salad was a generous portion made tableside with anchovies—classic and delicious. The bread was good with a solid assortment and one that was cheesy and a bit oily. There was no fresh mozzarella available that day, but they made up for it with olive oil and pickled cauliflower. Some folks say the place is cramped, but we were seated at a round table so we thought it was more than enough space for us to enjoy a nice meal. Finished with a delicious raspberry sorbet, which was solid. Overall, a flawless meal and a true 10/10 experience. Would absolutely return. (5 stars)

We were there for an early lunch. Couldn’t believe that we had a table. It was so hard to get a reservation. We were greeted by really nice professional staffs. The bread with salami and fresh mozzarella served at the beginning of our meal was yummy! We ordered a Caesar salad that was prepared on a cart for our table specifically. The pasta vodka sauce was amazing not so much about the meatballs ( a little bit undercooked for our tasting and a bit fatty) I’ve had better but the marinara sauce was good. And then deserts oh boy! The display was mesmerizing and it tasted even better. The whole experience was Definitely worth the wait and the vibe! (4 stars)

bio_text: Welcome to Cardamom Indian Cuisine, a cozy neighborhood gem located in Sunnyside, NY, where authentic Indian flavors meet warm hospitality. The restaurant offers a diverse menu that caters to various dietary preferences, including halal, vegan, and vegetarian options, all served in a family-friendly setting. With dine-in, takeaway, and delivery services available, Cardamom ensures a delightful dining experience from lunch to dinner, featuring fresh ingredients and bold spices in every dish. Cardamom specializes in traditional and contemporary Indian cuisine, offering a menu that includes flavorful curries, tandoori grills, and a variety of vegetarian and vegan dishes. The restaurant emphasizes the use of fresh ingredients and authentic spices to create a memorable dining experience.

review_snippets: Best food, service, and quality in the neighborhood and beyond! Every dish we've had here, both dine in and take out, have been incredible. The butter chicken (it's shredded for maximum flavor), lamb chops, biryani, garlic naan, all appetizers, all the curries have been hits. Their desserts are also underrated. You have to try their homemade pistachio ice cream and if it's on the menu, carrot pudding. The owner and staff are warm and friendly, so you always feel welcome and taken care of. Highly recommend this spot! (5 stars)
We love this place — we’ve been here more than 10 times, and every time it’s a hit! Our friends enjoyed it too! We love everyone who works there! Bahut bahut dhanyavaad! 🇮🇳💛 (5 stars)

My favorite Indian in the neighborhood, the food is always fresh, hot, and delicious. I love hoe crispy the naan is when you dine in. This time we got the garlic naan, chicken caldeen, cardamom mix grill, lemon and garlic shrimp, and lamb potato croquettes. (5 stars)

A friend and I had dinner at Cardamon last week, and we both agree it was some of the best Indian food we have ever had. Very flavorful and absolutely delicious! Our experience was only made better by the restaurant team. Everyone with whom we had contact was exceedingly helpful and friendly, although special mention needs to go to Ashma, our server. She is exceptional at what she does! (5 stars)

bio_text: Carlotto is a modern urban trattoria located in the heart of Union Square, New York, designed by the award-winning Rockwell Group. The restaurant offers an intimate dining experience that celebrates Italy’s most celebrated regions, featuring a stunning bar with a curated cocktail list and an extensive selection of amaro and Italian wines. Carlotto focuses on authentic Italian cuisine, with an emphasis on handmade pastas prepared daily. The menu is designed to reflect the diverse culinary traditions of Italy, offering a blend of classic and contemporary dishes. Carlotto is part of Vancouver’s award-winning Toptable Group, which has been defining elegant yet approachable dining for over four decades. Executive Chef Andy Kitko leads the culinary vision for the restaurant.
menu_items: HOUSE MADE FOCCACIA - marinated olives - $8
TUNA STUFFED PEPPERS - capers - $13
CANTABRIAN ANCHOVIES & BUTTER - garlic toast - $14
BURRATA PUGLIESE - crispy cruschi peppers, garlic oil - $25
MORTADELLA & STRACCIATELLA - sicilian pistachio pesto - $23
PROSCIUTTO DI PARMA & PARMIGIANO REGGIANO - “white gold” - $27
review_snippets: We went back to Carlotto for the third time last night and left with even more confidence we want to return. The dishes were all fantastic. We especially enjoyed the Yellowfish Crudo, Beef Short Rib and Lobster pasta dishes. Each had excellent flavor and were perfectly prepared. (5 stars)

This restaurant was wonderful. The atmosphere is perfect for drinks out with the girls. They had special gluten free bread (I am celiac) and the pasta was delicious. My favorite highlight was the strawberry parfait dessert! The vanilla whipped cream was divine. Would love to go back! (5 stars)

What a fantastic experience. Lucrative space with an intimate setting connected to the famous “oceans” restaurant sits this modern Italian restaurant. I started off with the focaccia which was a light and fluffy. House made focaccia with oil and butter. They also added a side of PITTED olives which went PERFECTLY with my Negroni. Afterwards we order the beet carpaccio, and a charcuterie like board with assorted meats, jam, cheese, and pickled veggies. FANTASTIC!!! Of course to accompany this I ordered their Bianco Negroni which was also FABULOUS. overall I had above and beyond and EXCEPTIONAL service from the host and both of my bartenders. All ladies by the way, showing nothing but intentional hospitality and genuine connection. (Thank you for assisting me, and thank you for all your recommendations). This is gonna be my new spot to bring guest I want to IMPRESS. Keep up the great work. I’ll see you next time! (5 stars)

Exceptional Italian cuisine! House made pastas especially Malfadine with lobster were perfectly cooked. Chef Andy Kitko is doing it right here! Veal parmigiana is so tender and juicy, not to be missed. Cozy ambiance and great service! Gem of a restaurant. (5 stars)

bio_text: Carne Mare is an Italian chophouse located in the vibrant Seaport District of New York City, helmed by renowned Chef Andrew Carmellini. The restaurant offers a sophisticated dining experience with stunning views of the Manhattan waterfront and the Brooklyn Bridge, featuring a two-story space designed by Martin Brudnizki Design Studio. Guests can enjoy a blend of prime cuts of steak, fine seafood, and traditional Italian specialties in a stylish setting that includes both indoor and outdoor seating, a wrap-around bar, and a wood-fired oven. The culinary focus at Carne Mare centers on prime-aged beef, including wagyu and prime rib, complemented by housemade pastas and a selection of seafood. The menu features a variety of Italian specialties, traditional antipasti, and a selection of steakhouse contorni, creating a well-rounded dining experience. Carne Mare is led by Chef Andrew Carmellini and Chef della Cucina Dwight Sanon.

review_snippets: Carne Mare is one of our favorite restaurants and among the best steakhouses we have ever been to (the best in NYC). Everything about this restaurant is perfection. The ambiance, the food, and the friendly/professional waitstaff all contribute to an amazing and elevated dining experience. Every course is so flavorful, from the bread, to starters, and of course the steak. The Ribeye was seasoned so well and cooked perfectly. I could not recommend a better place for a romantic and delicious meal that lives up to the hype. (5 stars)

I recently discovered Carne Mare, and it has quickly become one of my favorite spots worth recommending to friends. From the outstanding flavors to the inviting atmosphere and attentive service, this is the kind of restaurant that leaves a lasting impression. The ambiance strikes a perfect balance between elegant and relaxed, and the staff’s warmth and professionalism truly enhanced our dining experience. ￼ ⚪ The Yellowfin Tuna Tartare 🐟 was refreshingly clean and bright on the palate, with a perfect balance of acidity and freshness — an excellent choice to start the meal. ￼ 🦆 The Whole Roast Duck d’Ivan 🦆 arrived beautifully presented, generously portioned, with tender, juicy meat and crisp skin that brought rich aroma and flavor — perfect for sharing with your table. ￼ 🥩 The 8 oz Center-Cut Filet Mignon 🥩 showcased superbly tender beef, and I absolutely loved the accompanying green sauce — likely a spinach-herb blend — which elevated the dish with vibrant savory notes. ￼ 🍸🍷 The cocktails and beverage program also stood out — visually appealing and wonderfully balanced in flavor. That night happened to be my friend’s birthday, and we were surprised (and delighted) to see his name on the menu, which made the evening even more unforgettable 🥳🎉. The service was exceptional throughout, making for a truly memorable night. Overall, Carne Mare is a dining destination worth returning to, whether for celebrations, date nights, or special dinners with friends. 🌇🥂 (5 stars)

Highly recommended date night dinner. We've come here twice now, two years apart and both times were superb. The restaurant interior is like stepping into a movie and the staff go above and beyond in making your experience memorable. The food is presented and cooked with great detail. The brussel sprouts as a side were a surprising highlight. Be prepared to splurge on your meal here, but is definitely worth it for a special ocassion. (5 stars)

Carne Mare nails the atmosphere immediately. The space leans into a rich, old-school chophouse aesthetic, and the service is polished, confident, and exactly what you want in a New York steakhouse. We stopped in just for appetizers and worked our way through the chophouse snacks. The oysters were exceptionally fresh, clean, and easily the highlight of the table. The house bread was a genuine surprise and far better than expected. The remaining snacks, crab, burrata, and mozzarella with caviar, felt like they were loaded with promise but landed just fine rather than memorable. That said, this is a chophouse, and appetizers aren’t the reason you come here. Based on the room, the service, and the foundation they’ve built, I’m absolutely coming back to give the steaks their proper moment. I’m hopeful the main event delivers at the level the setting suggests. (4 stars)

The restaurant offers a sophisticated dining experience with stunning views of the Manhattan waterfront and the Brooklyn Bridge, featuring a two-story space designed by Martin Brudnizki Design Studio. Guests can enjoy a blend of prime cuts of steak, fine seafood, and traditional Italian specialties in a stylish setting that includes both indoor and outdoor seating, a wrap-around bar, and a wood-fired oven. The culinary focus at Carne Mare centers on prime-aged beef, including wagyu and prime rib, complemented by housemade pastas and a selection of seafood. The menu features a variety of Italian specialties, traditional antipasti, and a selection of steakhouse contorni, creating a well-rounded dining experience. Carne Mare is led by Chef Andrew Carmellini and Chef della Cucina Dwight Sanon. bio_text: Casa Enrique is a Michelin-rated Mexican restaurant located in Long Island City, New York, known for its authentic and artistic expressions of traditional Chiapas cuisine. The restaurant offers a warm and inviting atmosphere, where guests can enjoy a unique gastronomical journey that celebrates the flavors and ingredients of Chef Cosme Aguilar's childhood. With a commitment to serving family recipes, Casa Enrique has quickly established itself as a local hotspot since its opening in 2012. Casa Enrique specializes in traditional Mexican cuisine, particularly from the Chiapas region. The menu features a variety of dishes that reflect home-cooked flavors, with an emphasis on authenticity and quality ingredients. Signature techniques include a blend of traditional cooking methods and modern presentation. Chef Cosme Aguilar, inspired by his mother's cooking in Chiapas, opened Casa Enrique on March 15th, 2012. After years of experience in French cuisine, he embraced the opportunity to reconnect with his roots. The restaurant was awarded its first Michelin star in September 2014 and has since received a total of 6 Michelin stars over the years. Chef Cosme is also a James Beard award nominee for excellence in Mexican cuisine.

review_snippets: The place has a modern feel, the service was excellent, very attentive. The sauce and the tortilla work is very impressive. We got the shrimp ceviche that was a special of the day and it had an interesting fusion sauce, with Asian notes to it. The sopecitos were outstanding. I thought the carne asada lacked flavor a bit. But the tortillas were some of the best I have had. The flautas were disappointing. The entire filling was super crispy and over fried so there was no texture contrasts in the dish. (4 stars)

We had brunch on a Sunday and it was great. We had reservations, but it wasn't too busy at about noon. Here are the positives: the service was really wonderful - perfect mix of attentive and leave you alone; the table hot sauces are FANTASTIC; the guacamole was really delicious and the pan frances (french toast) was phenomenal. Okay, I don't really have negatives...but the other dishes were just good (nothing spectacular). The fish tacos and albondigas were tasty, but not standouts. Overall a lovely brunch, but I definitely want to return for dinner. (4 stars)

Food was AWESOME! Everything tastes homemade and packed with tons of flavors and spice. We had the special shrimp ceviche, the enchiladas, branzino, the cheese ice cream was out of this world and the tres leches was the best. Cocktails were delicious and made with fresh juices not that sugary bottled stuff. Can’t wait to return, I highly recommend. (5 stars)

Casa Enrique continues to be one of the best restaurants in Long Island City and it fully deserves its reputation. Every time we visit, the food is consistent, fresh, and full of bold flavor. You can taste the care in the cooking, whether it’s the guacamole, ceviche, enchiladas, or their signature mole. The dishes are beautifully balanced without being overly complicated, which makes the experience feel both comforting and special. The service is another reason we keep returning. The staff is warm, patient, and genuinely welcoming. Even on busy nights, they make you feel taken care of and always offer thoughtful recommendations. It is clear they care about creating a positive experience for every guest. The atmosphere is relaxed but polished, making it a great spot for a casual dinner or celebrating something meaningful. It has become one of those rare neighborhood restaurants where you want to bring friends and family just to share how good it is. We also love that the quality has never slipped no matter how popular it gets. Casa Enrique is a true gem in Queens. If you are in LIC and want an amazing meal with great service, this should be at the top of your list. (5 stars)

bio_text: Casa Mono is a celebrated Spanish restaurant located in New York City, known for its intimate atmosphere and exceptional culinary offerings. With a focus on the vibrant flavors of Spain's Costa Brava, the restaurant features a cozy interior adorned with mosaic tiles and an extensive selection of wines. Guests can enjoy a unique dining experience at the bar, where they can watch dishes being prepared à la plancha, enhancing the overall sensory experience. Casa Mono specializes in tapas, offering a menu that includes adventurous proteins and classic Spanish dishes. The restaurant is known for its innovative takes on traditional recipes, such as Razor Clams a la Plancha and Bone Marrow with Tomato Jam. The dining format encourages sharing and exploration of flavors. Casa Mono opened in 2004 and has been awarded a Michelin Star since 2009. Executive Chef Andy Nusser, who hails from the fishing village of Cadaqués in Spain, draws inspiration from his heritage to create a menu that reflects the essence of Spanish cuisine.

review_snippets: Cute and intimate. Haven’t been in a few years so decided to give it a go again. A really nice wine selection for any Spanish wine lover. The staff is top notch attending to every need a clearing at just the right moments. The biggest disappointment is the food. It’s just a little too far all around, a little too twisted. I mean even the patatas bravas- long fingerlings in a homogenized sauce? Give me the cubed potatoes and both sauces drizzled over! You need the damn white sauce! I will say that the fluke crudo was absolutely delicious. That needs to stay as is. Everything else was just a little too weird and different. (3 stars)

A cozy small restaurant with expensive tapas. The space is super tight. Three of us ordered 5 dishes and it was enough. They recommended 6-9. My favorite was Pan con Tomate. It may look like something you can make at home but for some reason, there was something special about it. I’m not impressed at all with creamy eggs with sea urchins because it just tasted like egg scramble with uni. Definitely not worth $40. Skirt steak and negro arroz were good. We were looking through the wine menu and a server or sommelier came over and offered to pick wine for us. He didn’t even ask for what kind of taste we like. I’m not sure if it was worth the price we paid per glass (4 stars)

Fantastic tapas all around. Each dish was tasty, well portioned to share for four people. Main complaint was table space to house all the plates. Bottles of wine recommended by the sommelier were great. We had the Ensalada mono, Sardines with Endives, Razor clams, Pulpo, Fideos, Arroz negro, Pork sobrasada, Skirt steak, Duck breast, Pork meatballs, Patatas bravas, and Artichokes. Fideos were phenomenal, favorite dish of the night. Loved the sardines and Arroz negro as well. (5 stars)

This is just my opinion. Overall, everything was good, but in trying to modernize traditional cuisine, some dishes no longer taste like the original recipes; for example, the black rice (arroz negro). The way the fideos are presented is also quite inconvenient, as you end up dropping a lot of the food when serving. The seafood was probably the highlight: both the sardines and the fluke on top of the black rice were excellent. I also went there specifically for the bone marrow, but unfortunately they didn’t have it available. (3 stars)

bio_text: Casa Ora is an upscale Venezuelan cuisine and cocktail bar located in Williamsburg, Brooklyn. The restaurant offers a unique dining experience that combines refined farm-to-table plates with modern cocktails, all set in a nostalgic atmosphere reminiscent of 1980s Latin culture. Casa Ora is dedicated to showcasing the beauty and nature of Venezuela while also supporting families affected by political injustice through charitable contributions. The culinary focus at Casa Ora is on modern Venezuelan cuisine, emphasizing comfort food with a contemporary twist. The menu features farm-to-table dishes and innovative cocktails, highlighting the rich flavors and traditions of Venezuelan gastronomy. Casa Ora aims to bring the essence of Venezuela to New York City and is committed to donating a portion of its revenue to support Venezuelan families seeking asylum due to human rights issues.
review_snippets: The atmosphere felt very intimate, it was dark but inviting and a great spot for a date. Service was phenomenal, they were very attentive and gave great recommendations. The cocktails were a 9/10, I had a spicy mango drink. The arepas were incredible but the number one dish was the bollitos pelones. Highly recommended. The baby shark dish was our least favorite but each dish was plated with care and very aesthetically pleasing. (4 stars)

Tried Venezuelan food for the first time and it didn’t disappoint. The whole spot had a warm vibe with a really inviting ambiance. Drinks were flavorful and a little strong in a good way. The food was the star though. The red snapper on tostones was fire, perfect coating and great flavor. The brisket with black beans and egg was incredibly flavorful and the meat was super tender. Overall, a really nice experience. (4 stars)

We went to Casa Ora last night to celebrate my birthday, and I’m still thinking about every single bite. The asado negro alone deserves its own love letter. If you’ve never had it, imagine a piece of beef that has been brined, marinated, and slow-cooked for hours until it becomes as tender as butter, then finished with a deep, glossy caramelization of papelón that gives you that slightly charred, smoky sweetness. It is the kind of dish that stops conversation at the table, an art piece with soul. And everything else? Perfection with nostalgia woven in. The plantains, the mini cachapas, the tequeños, and a pan de jamón so good it could make your abuela cry, warm, tender, slightly sweet, salty, comforting. Every plate felt like someone was inviting us into their home, letting us taste the food their family grew up on, the food that fills the kitchen on a Sunday afternoon. Casa Ora is full of heart. You can feel the love, the purpose, the passion in every corner, not just in the dishes but in the way the team carries themselves. It is rare to find a place that feeds you and moves you at the same time. This is the restaurant you will rave about. The one you will bring friends to, brag about, and keep thinking about long after you leave. An unforgettable meal, and a perfect birthday. Thank you, Casa Ora. 💛 (5 stars)

I came all the way from Manhattan to meet friends here for dinner, and it was absolutely worth it. From the moment we arrived, we felt incredibly welcome. We ordered a variety of dishes from the menu, and I had the chance to try almost everything, every single dish was delicious and beautifully prepared. The atmosphere is very cozy and inviting, making you feel comfortable right away. It’s the kind of place where you want to stay longer and truly enjoy the evening. A big thank you as well to the lovely staff for their warm hospitality and excellent service. I can wholeheartedly recommend this place and would definitely come back again. (5 stars)

bio_text: Caviar Russe is a distinguished caviar house with locations in New York City and Miami, offering an unparalleled dining experience centered around the luxury of caviar. Established in 1997, the restaurant has earned a Michelin star for ten consecutive years, showcasing its commitment to excellence in both cuisine and hospitality. The ambiance is refined and elegant, making it a perfect destination for connoisseurs and those seeking a unique culinary adventure. Caviar Russe specializes in high-quality caviar sourced from artisanal farms, focusing on Osetra, Sevruga, and other sturgeon varieties. The menu features a seasonal tasting format that highlights the delicate flavors of caviar, complemented by gourmet dishes such as smoked salmon and duck foie gras. Signature techniques include traditional malossol curing methods to enhance the caviar's natural taste. Caviar Russe was founded in 1997 and has been awarded a Michelin star for the past ten years. The restaurant prides itself on sourcing caviar exclusively from a small batch sturgeon farm in Germany, ensuring the highest quality and sustainability.

review_snippets: We really enjoyed our evening at Caviar Russe. I’m a genuine caviar fan, and this is a place that clearly understands how to do caviar right. The caviar service was excellent, with thoughtful accompaniments and culinary flair. The dining room is beautiful and comfortable, making the evening feel special without being stiff. The seating was welcoming, and the large plate-glass window looking out onto Madison Avenue gave the room an open, lively feel. Service was attentive and upbeat, adding to the energy of the night. Caviar is clearly the focus here, but the experience goes beyond well that. They’ve found their lane and execute it with confidence & precision. We definitely recommend Caviar Russe. (5 stars)

If you like caviar and exquisite food, this place is a gem. We had the caviar with different starch, especially the new one that we had never tried- the potato and was really delicious with the champagne. Service was impeccable I thought the food was perfect and the staff was thoroughly attentive with Pedro giving us a wonderful tour of the whole beautiful restaurant. Matthew is a great host and conversationist we thoroughly enjoyed our visit and upstairs There are some beautiful rooms and also private dining areas… will be back again on our next visit to the city! (5 stars)

This is the most incredible restaurant for Caviar connoisseurs. 5 star service from the second you step out of your car they’re holding the door for you, presentation, all the way up until the very end. The customer service from every single employee blew me away, I can’t recommend Caviar Russe enough! ⭐️ (5 stars)

Their steak and pork is chef kiss, highlight of this restaurant (sorry not the caviar). Other food is great too but not as impressive as their entrees. Service is so so. It’s a Michelin restaurant so I don’t know if it’s ok to have the front desk serving food. We also heard the chef yelling in the kitchen when we were dining there which I do not appreciate. I would only come back for their entrees, nothing else. (4 stars)
search_text: Caviar Russe Caviar Russe is a distinguished caviar house with locations in New York City and Miami, offering an unparalleled dining experience centered around the luxury of caviar. Established in 1997, the restaurant has earned a Michelin star for ten consecutive years, showcasing its commitment to excellence in both cuisine and hospitality. The ambiance is refined and elegant, making it a perfect destination for connoisseurs and those seeking a unique culinary adventure. Caviar Russe specializes in high-quality caviar sourced from artisanal farms, focusing on Osetra, Sevruga, and other sturgeon varieties. The menu features a seasonal tasting format that highlights the delicate flavors of caviar, complemented by gourmet dishes such as smoked salmon and duck foie gras. Signature techniques include traditional malossol curing methods to enhance the caviar's natural taste. Caviar Russe was founded in 1997 and has been awarded a Michelin star for the past ten years. The restaurant prides itself on sourcing caviar exclusively from a small batch sturgeon farm in Germany, ensuring the highest quality and sustainability. bio_text: Cervo's is a vibrant seafood restaurant located in the heart of New York City's Chinatown, offering a unique dining experience that pays homage to the rich seafood traditions of the Iberian Peninsula while celebrating sustainable ingredients sourced from the Northeast. With a focus on creating a lively atmosphere, Cervo's invites guests to enjoy their meals both indoors and outdoors, particularly during the warmer months when outdoor dining is available on Canal Street. Cervo's specializes in seafood cuisine inspired by the Iberian Peninsula, featuring a menu that emphasizes fresh, sustainable ingredients. The restaurant offers a diverse selection of dishes complemented by a carefully curated wine list showcasing bottles from coastal Spain and Portugal, along with innovative cocktails crafted behind the bar. We opened in the summer of 2017 on Canal Street in New York City's Chinatown.
menu_items: Olives with paprika - $7
Spicy mussels escabeche - $14
Crispy shrimp heads - $10
Croquetas with serrano ham and idiazabal - $13
Black sea bass with preserved lemon - $23
Stuffed peppers with yellowfin tuna - $21
review_snippets: Third time dining. Was a bit disappointed with quality of food. Tortilla was served almost cold and was more of a frittata with eggs and leeks. Shrimp head was good. Calamari also came almost in salad style in winter with cold onions. Off-season temperatures with food disappointed us. Room was also very cold to dine in, we asked if heaters could be turned on but servers just said they’ll see and never turned it on. Burger was good. Fish came really buttery… almost excessively. But was fine. (3 stars)

Small restaurant with mostly barstool seating that is uncomfortably close together. Thankfully the food and service is fantastic. Based in Spanish cuisine, the menu has a solid array of seafood options with a few meats thrown in the mix. The burger is well known but not my favorite, the texture of the meat is slightly gamey and with the anchovies it’s approaching over salted. The staples of the menu are strong including the skate fillet and the roasted chicken. The small plates get seasonal refreshes. During this visit the beefsteak tomato salad was beautiful with a surprising spice and the pea shoots were refreshing with a kick of acid at the end. Dessert here could be stronger and feels like an afterthought. The flan is good but doesn’t frequently get updates and the cake is usually not great. I wish things got updated more frequently here but the food never disappoints. (5 stars)

My partner and I visited Cervos for the last dinner of our trip to NYC. Overall we enjoyed dinner but it probably wouldn’t be somewhere we would recommend/return. We ordered the prawns and clams for starter but unfortunately they forgot our clams. We also ordered the sourdough but that was pretty dry and clearly had been cut hours ago. We ordered the skate and chicken for main. The skate was ok but not something we would order again. The chicken was amazing and probably one of the best chicken dishes of this type we have ever had, was really really delicious. The waiting staff were great when our dishes were forgotten (/generally) we were offered a glass of wine on the house. Being sat on the “chef table” whilst sounded good was pretty awkward/weird when the chef asked us to move, through the waitress, as we had been sat too close to the serving spot. Overall the restaurant had a good vibe but would not recommend sitting on the counter by the chefs. (3 stars)

The food and service were 👌👌👌 i really wanted to try their prawn head but the menu has changed. A lot of food were sour but right level of sourness. This is a perfect date spot. Piri piri chicken and croquettes were mediocre tbh but other seafood options were amazing (5 stars)

bio_text: Cha Kee is a vibrant Cantonese restaurant located in the heart of Chinatown, New York City. With a cozy yet lively atmosphere, it invites guests to indulge in a delightful blend of traditional and modern flavors. The restaurant is known for its attentive service and a diverse menu that caters to both casual diners and those seeking a more refined experience, making it a popular choice for locals and tourists alike. Cha Kee specializes in authentic Cantonese cuisine, offering a menu that features standout dishes such as Macao Curry Chicken and Dan Dan Noodles. The restaurant emphasizes a creative approach to drinks, highlighted by their Coldbrew Highball, and provides a selection of comforting and hearty meals.
menu_items: Happy Buddha's Delight - Vegan. Lotus root, burdock root, carrot, shishito peppers. - $15.00
Soy Milk Braised Romaine Lettuce - Gluten free, vegetarian. Scallion oil, chili oil, pumpkin seed. - $14.00
Wok'd Water Spinach - Sambal, dried shrimp, bird's eye chili. - $16.00
Tiger Salad - Vegan. Mint, basil, butter, lettuce, turmeric, carrot, vinaigrette. - $13.00
Cha Kee Salad - romaine, nappa cabbage, kohlrabi, taro chips, cilantro, peanuts, sesame dressing(vegan) - $13.00
Crispy Baby Bok Choy - sea salt, shichimi togarashi, furikake - $9.00
review_snippets: We tried some other things here, but don’t have pictures for them. Butter with condensed milk toast was good. Fried bun with condensed milk was good. Milk teas were good. Beef chow fun was very tasty and silky. Beef chow mein was very good also. Usually don’t like chow mein too much, but their noodles were a bit on the softer side and I prefer that over the super crispy crunchy version. Didn’t like the pork chop onions on rice. It was bland. Their wings were okay. Overall, this place was way better than I expected, so I give it a solid 4. (4 stars)

If you miss (or dream of) the classic Hong Kong lunch spot, this is it. Located in the heart of NYC Chinatown. Its clean modern deco, and conversation able environment makes it the prefect place for a power lunch or catch up time with friends. The staff is kind and patient when you are overwhelmed with the extensive menu. Protip: take their suggestions. The menu covers Hong Kong style sandwiches and dumplings (plus more). Bonus a gorgeous bathrooms with heated toilet that made me weak in the knees. The Hong Kong tea is one to try. My understanding is at night it transforms into a Japanese restaurant. I'll have to come back for that experience. (5 stars)
For so long i didnt come to eat here,and everything taste the same good but the ppls use to work there all gone but good thing is check the toilet is funny (5 stars)

Date & time of visit: Tuesday, 10/21/2025 at 10:45am Today was my first time visiting Cha Kee with my family since when it used to be Cha Chan Tang. My family and I walked in looking forward to have breakfast here. There wasn’t a sign about waiting to be seated or person at the front when we came in. My Dad, who is a senior then went ahead walking toward a table then the lady staff appeared and came toward us. We asked if we can sit at the table with the booth and she responded with, “I’m seating you now aren’t I?” in a rude tone and expression on her face. The rest of our dine-in experience was like this. This lady also took our order. I don’t know if she is having a bad day or what’s going on with her. She made us feel like we’re annoying or she is tired of working there? I don’t know what. We hoped the food will at least be decent to make up for it but it didn’t really =/ Food: The bread served with Western Set meal was rock hard. Restroom: Decent bathroom. Best part of dine-in experience. It was a very disappointing experience overall especially by the lady in the front that served us ruined it. Side note: My family and I were going to head to a funeral after this. (1 stars)
