bio_text: Chalong Southern Thai offers an authentic dining experience that celebrates the rich culinary heritage of Southern Thailand. With a focus on fresh seafood and traditional flavors, the restaurant creates a vibrant atmosphere where guests can enjoy expertly crafted dishes and unique cocktails inspired by the region's culture and stories. The inviting space is perfect for both casual dining and special occasions, making it a beloved spot for locals and visitors alike. Chalong specializes in Southern Thai cuisine, emphasizing fresh seafood and bold flavors. The menu features a variety of dishes, including signature items like crab curry and green curry brisket, alongside a cocktail series that tells stories of the South. The dining format is designed for sharing, encouraging a communal experience. Chef Nate Limwong, a native of Suratthani, has decades of culinary experience across three continents. She aims to celebrate her roots by establishing Chalong as the first Southern Thai-focused restaurant in NYC, elevating local tastes to a world-class culinary platform.
menu_items: Jeeb Pu - Steamed dumpling with crab meat, shrimp, and pork, fried garlic, and southern-style dipping sauce. - $19.00
Baerng Golae (S) - Coconut crisp, grilled shrimp, and famous curry paste from southern Thailand. - $18.00
Yum Som-O (S) - Fresh Pomelo, fried cured branzino, chili, lemongrass shallot, mint, cilantro with nahm pla whan dressing. - $18.00
Lumpu Salad (GF, S) (Limited) - Fresh dry scallops, seafood sauce, chili paste, fried shallots, cilantro, mint, and pea shoots. - $19.00
Phuket pak mor (VG) (Peanut) - Steamed rice dumplings filled with sweet radish, peanut, black pepper, and salted coconut dressing. - $16.00
Potato Puff Stick (VG) - Crispy puffs filled with savory curried potatoes, onions, carrots, peas, and black pepper. - $16.00
review_snippets: Chalong brings the ไฟ!!... This is the real deal, and is the best Thai I’ve had outside of Phuket!! I started with the Lumpu Salad, built around pristine scallops that were bright, citrusy, and layered with that classic Thai balance of heat, acidity, and herbs. The scallops were incredibly fresh and the dish had a punchy vibrance that woke up the palate immediately. Next up were the Baerng Golae shrimp tacos…juicy shrimp with deep, smoky southern Thai spices wrapped in a soft bite that delivered savory, slightly sweet, and the right amount of heat. The steamed fish was beautifully executed. Clean, delicate, and perfectly cooked, with aromatic herbs and broth that made every bite feel light but deeply flavorful. To finish, the mango sticky rice hit the spot..nothing standout about this dish but after getting hit with all that flavor, I didn’t mind. I washed all that down with a Surat Thani “After School” cocktail which was dangerously easy to drink so I just sipped on it rather than drank! Across the board, the taste profiles at Chalong were dialed in and dialed up! The service, perfect! It’s the kind of spot that reminds you how exciting Thai food can be when the kitchen leans all the way into its roots. A seriously impressive meal. (5 stars)

I recently visited Chalong NYC for dinner with friends, and overall it was a solid experience worth sharing! Located in the heart of Hell’s Kitchen, this Thai restaurant blends modern Southern Thai flavors with a lively atmosphere that’s perfect for dinners out, pre-theater meals, or casual nights with friends. The space feels warm and welcoming, with thoughtful décor and an inviting vibe that made our group feel comfortable right away. The restaurant tends to be popular, so reservations are definitely recommended — it can get busy, especially on weekend evenings. The service throughout the night was friendly and attentive; staff were happy to explain the menu and adjust spice levels based on our preferences. We tried several standout dishes that left a great impression. The Green Curry Brisket was rich and flavorful, perfectly tender and aromatic. The Mee Pum Riang had a unique, savory taste that paired beautifully with the noodles. Khao Pad Mun Goong was comforting and well-seasoned, while the special Baerng Golae offered a bold, complex flavor that really showcased Southern Thai cuisine. Each dish was generous in portion and carefully prepared, making the meal very satisfying. The vibe inside Chalong is energetic and vibrant — lively enough for a fun night out, though it might be a bit loud if you’re hoping for a quiet, intimate dinner. In summary, Chalong NYC offers flavorful, well-prepared Southern Thai food, attentive service, and a buzz-worthy setting. While some dishes might feel a bit pricey for what you get, the quality and creativity make it worth trying. I would definitely go back to explore more of the menu and enjoy another night of great Thai flavors! (4 stars)

ทางร้านมี 10 ดาวให้กดมั้ยคะ❤️ Every time I visit NYC, having Thai food is a must. This trip, a fellow Thai recommended that I try Chalong, especially because they specialize in Southern Thai cuisine and as someone from the South of Thailand, I had to see if it lived up to the hype. Let me just say: 200/10. The flavors were absolutely incredible, it truly felt like I was enjoying a proper, high-quality meal back home in Thailand. I went with my husband, and we both agreed that every dish was beautifully executed and packed with authentic flavor. You can really taste the freshness of the ingredients. What impressed me even more is that their curry pastes are made fresh in-house, not from a can. That makes such a difference, and you can tell they take pride in doing things the right way. The service was also outstanding. Mr. Mung Korn was our server , so polite, attentive, and genuinely warm. He made the whole experience even more memorable. I sincerely hope Chalong opens a location in DC one day! Until then, I will definitely be back whenever I’m in NYC. Highly, highly recommend. ขอบคุณทุกคนในร้านมากๆนะคะ รบกวนฝากบอกเจ้าของร้านมาเปิดที่ DC ได้มั้ยคะ 😝❤️ (5 stars)

Visited Chalong and overall it was decent but not particularly memorable. The squid ink seafood fried rice was flavorful and had squid and crab that tasted fairly fresh, with balanced seasoning. The curry shrimp taco was interesting — the shell was more like a crispy egg roll wrapper, almost snack-like, and the shrimp itself was well seasoned. The curry lamb was also good and not overly soft or stewed down, which I appreciated for the texture. That said, portions felt small for the price, and while everything tasted fine, nothing really stood out. Considering the pricing, the overall experience felt a bit underwhelming. (4 stars)

bio_text: Chambers is a destination-worthy restaurant located in TriBeCa, New York City, that combines a neighborhood vibe with an exceptional dining experience. The restaurant, led by Executive Chef Jon Karis, offers a meticulously prepared seasonal menu that changes weekly, showcasing the best of New York City cooking. With a focus on comfort and pleasure, Chambers aims to create an inviting atmosphere for both special occasions and casual visits, complemented by an exploratory beverage program curated by renowned sommelier Pascaline Lepeltier. Chambers specializes in seasonal New York cuisine with European influences, featuring a menu that changes frequently alongside a selection of staple dishes. The culinary focus includes signature techniques and dishes such as Veal Sweetbreads and Snowdance Chicken, expertly paired with a diverse range of natural wines. Chambers was established in 2022 by Chef Jonathan Karis, Beverage Director Pascaline Lepeltier, and General Manager Jared David, who previously worked together at Racines. Chef Karis brings a wealth of experience from his time at Gramercy Tavern, while Lepeltier is recognized for her expertise in natural wines.

review_snippets: Chef’s counter here is a must. I had been seeing a lot of hype about this place on social media and randomly snagged a reservation not realizing what a special experience I was walking in to. We tried most of their popular dishes the hiramasa, castelfranco, farfelle, snowdance chicken, and fingerling potatoes. My favorite by far was the hiramasa but all the dishes were quite wonderful. For dessert we got the chocolate basque cheesecake. I was really impressed by how well it paired with the sweet cream on the plate (we wished there were more)! Now the wine was just incredible. To which the master sommelier, Pascaline Lepeltier, deserves all the praise in the world. She is the sweetest woman, I mean she entertained my attempt at speaking French so graciously. But seriously, she knows what is up. She truly picked out the perfect wine based on our request, which was a bottle from Domaine de la Bergerie, Sous la Tonnelle. We really enjoyed watching the magic in the kitchen and asking questions to the chef right in front of us. Unforgettable, 100% worth a visit. (5 stars)

An excellent dining experience from start to finish. The food was delicious, and the wine list is top notch, with plenty of thoughtful pairing options. The staff was knowledgeable and attentive, which made the evening feel seamless and special. We had a wonderful time and plan to return soon! (5 stars)

This dinner was a night to remember! From the food and wine, to service and atmosphere... Every moment, every bite, every sip was to be savored and an experience in itself. The food was some of the best you'll find in the city, cooked to perfection. Our server, Ivan, took excellent care of us. But the star of the evening was Sommelier, Pascaline Lepeltier. She easily has the best palate in the world and no one knows wine better than she does. We did a wine pairing with our meal, knowing everything she would bring us would be again, perfection. She did not disappoint and brought so much culture and class to our experience. We appreciated so much learning about everything she brought us and it only made this experience better. One we shall never forget. We finished our time here, having dessert and tea at the bar. Even the tea paired beautifully with our dessert and just like everything else we had all evening, was mind blowingly delicious. We will be sure to visit Chambers and Pascaline again on our next visit. (5 stars)

4.5 really. Really tasty food, ordered a la carte. Slightly unusual tastes, but they worked well. Friendly staff. Fun ambience. Slightly odd wine pairing experience: the staff clearly took a lot of care about testing the wines were ok, but struggled a bit to explain why their recommendations matched the food. (5 stars)

bio_text: Chavela's is a vibrant Mexican restaurant located in Brooklyn, New York, known for its authentic flavors and warm, welcoming atmosphere. The restaurant's colorful décor and lively ambiance create a festive dining experience that transports guests to the heart of Mexico. With a focus on community and hospitality, Chavela's has become a beloved local hub where diners gather to enjoy delicious food, great cocktails, and the joy of shared meals. Chavela's specializes in traditional Mexican cuisine, drawing inspiration from Chef Arturo Leonar's childhood flavors. The menu features a variety of authentic dishes that highlight the rich culinary heritage of Mexico, served in a casual, inviting format. Chef Arturo Leonar, originally from Mexico City, opened the first incarnation of Chavela's in 2007 after years of experience in the restaurant industry. The restaurant quickly became a local favorite, leading to a relocation in 2011 to accommodate growing demand.

Some dishes stood out more than others, but my favorite was definitely the signature scallop. Something that took me by surprised me was the pallet cleanser, to transition from the savory to sweet dishes. It was a cold treat, sort of magical, small bite. The only reason I didn’t give it 5 stars is because they ran out of ice cream that paired with the main dessert which made it lack substance. Although it was still delicious they didn’t inform us about it, which we would’ve appreciated. (4 stars)

The experience here was very good! It's inside a grocery store, has a high quality tasting menu. Would recommend the none alcoholic drinks pairing, can share between 2 people comfortably with water also. The coconut ice cream with the muffin for dessert was my favourite of the courses. (5 stars)

I chose this restaurant for our anniversary after hearing many glowing recommendations and arrived with high expectations. While there were highlights — notably the skill and attentiveness of the sommelier — the overall experience left room for improvement. We were seated directly under a heater, which provided warmth at first, but wind repeatedly blew my hair into my face. When the heater was turned off at my request, it quickly became chilly due to a draft each time staff passed through a nearby door to the back. We asked to move, noticing that several tables remained empty throughout our visit, but were told this was not possible. Service began slowly, with roughly 30 minutes passing after our reservation time before the first course arrived. As someone who grew up by the ocean, with seafood being a regular part of our family meals, I especially look forward to seafood when dining at this level. That’s why I was disappointed by the langoustine, which lacked freshness, and the turbot, which had a strong metallic taste. Neither dish was finished, yet no one inquired about them. For a two-star Michelin restaurant, I had expected a higher level of attentiveness and engagement about the dining experience. Throughout the three-hour meal, service felt reactive rather than proactive. Staff members delivered dishes and cleared plates but never checked in between courses, something I noticed was handled differently at other tables that evening. The sommelier was the clear standout, taking time to understand my preferences and thoughtfully recommending a drink I genuinely enjoyed — no small feat, as I’m not a wine drinker and avoid spirits like bourbon or whiskey. Her professionalism and determination reflected the caliber I had expected across the board. (2 stars)

Our experience at the chef’s table was nothing short of exceptional. Each course was meticulously crafted, showcasing fresh, high-quality ingredients and beautifully layered flavors. I enjoyed the non-alcoholic pairing, while my sister opted for the standard pairing; both were thoughtfully curated and complemented the dishes perfectly. The service was exemplary, with an impressive level of attention to detail and seamless teamwork that enhanced the entire experience. A truly memorable evening — we highly recommend it and look forward to returning (5 stars)

bio_text: Che Li is a distinguished Chinese restaurant located in the heart of New York, offering a unique dining experience that intertwines the rich cultural heritage of the Song Dynasty with the sophisticated flavors of Shanghai cuisine. The restaurant's ambiance reflects a harmonious blend of historical elegance and contemporary sophistication, creating an immersive environment that transports diners to an era celebrated for its artistic and culinary achievements. Each meal at Che Li is designed to be a visually captivating and gastronomically rewarding experience, celebrating the communal spirit of traditional feasts. Che Li specializes in Shanghai cuisine, focusing on the delicate flavors and meticulous preparation characteristic of Jiangnan culinary traditions. The menu features signature dishes such as Beggar's Chicken and Braised Pork Belly, presented with an emphasis on elegant presentation and storytelling. The dining format encourages communal sharing, reminiscent of traditional banquet culture. This summer marks the 10th year of operation for Che Li, which has successfully transformed family recipes into a beloved dining destination in New York.

review_snippets: Unique and delicious meal in a special atmosphere. Friendly, helpful staff. With reservations, we were seated immediately on a Friday night. People without reservations were waiting as CheLi was bustling. Reasonable prices, generous portions. Loved the dumplings, Beggar's Chicken and sautéd green beans. "Crispy Lava", black sweet buns filled with warm, liquid duck egg custard made a wonderful dessert. Would love to go again and try more. (5 stars)

We had an amazing dinner here at Che li! The service was so great and attentive. The food came out perfect timing and everything was delicious. The soup dumplings were the best and the portion were great for sharing. We left so full and they even gave us a complimentary dessert on the house which was warm and delicious. I’ll definitely be coming back here for a date night or girls night out. The vibe is so cute and the drinks are also amazing! The tea is perfect for a cold winter night. (5 stars)

We visited Zhe Li during Chinese New Year and made an online reservation in advance for 8:15 pm. I had confidently told my friend beforehand that Zhejiang cuisine has many delicious dishes and that this restaurant had strong online ratings. Unfortunately, we left feeling extremely disappointed. First, the seating situation was chaotic. When we arrived, there wasn’t even a proper space to queue — everyone was crowded together near the entrance. The staff were clearly overwhelmed, and despite having reservations, guests were not seated in any clear order. We watched people with the same reservation time — or even later time slots — get seated before us. We ended up waiting about 20 minutes past our reservation time. Second, service organization was lacking. It didn’t seem like servers were assigned to specific sections. Ordering and paying depended entirely on finding someone available. We had to repeatedly remind staff, and during busy moments it was easy to be overlooked. To be fair, the young staff members were hardworking and polite despite the chaos — the issue seemed more like management and organization rather than individual effort. Third, the food was underwhelming, especially for New York, where the overall dining standard is quite high. The vegetable shoots had many tough stems and were slightly too salty. The mushroom rice was fragrant and nicely mixed for us by the server, but surprisingly sweet — I don’t understand why so much sugar would be added to mushroom rice. The chicken and intestines were spicy as expected, but again leaned overly sweet and salty. The owner even mentioned to a neighboring table that because many students dine there, the flavors are intentionally heavier. Dishes also arrived in a very irregular order. The crispy duck was served one hour and fifteen minutes after we were seated — by that point, we were already full. The dessert, however, was decent. We spent around $140. The price itself wasn’t the issue, but the overly sweet and salty flavors do not represent authentic Zhejiang cuisine in our view. Unfortunately, this was not a good experience for us. (2 stars)

The first time we came, the restaurant was so popular that we couldn’t get in. On our second visit, we were seated in a wonderful spot. We would especially like to thank the kind and attentive server, Ting Ting. Her detailed introductions to every dish helped us choose exactly what we loved. Her warmth made us want to come back again. During the meal, when we accidentally started coughing, she thoughtfully brought us a gentle warm drink that soothed our throats. The manager, Jimmy, was also very humble and professional. His service was thorough and attentive, he handled our requests perfectly, and greeted us sincerely. He truly went the extra mile to take care of every guest’s needs. The level of professionalism we experienced was outstanding, just like the food itself. Thank you all for taking such great care of us. We are already loyal fans and look forward to our next visit. (5 stars)

bio_text: Chez Fifi is a charming Upper East Side restaurant that offers a refined and inviting atmosphere, reminiscent of a classic Parisian bistro. Guests can enjoy an a la carte menu crafted by Executive Chef Zack Zeidman, featuring innovative cocktails and a curated selection of wines from around the globe, making it a perfect destination for both casual dining and special occasions. The culinary focus at Chez Fifi is on Parisian bistro classics with influences from coastal northern Spain. The menu features an a la carte format, highlighting signature dishes such as foie gras terrine, steak tartare, and wild Dover Sole a la plancha. Executive Chef Zack Zeidman leads the kitchen, bringing a unique perspective to the menu that blends traditional French techniques with modern flair.

review_snippets: It is very good french food. That being said it's nothing beyond that which i feel like i should mention given the hype around Chez Fifi. The interior really is so beautiful a total escape from manhattan, it is reason to go. The food was good, salad was good, tartare was not near the best ive had but good, basque crab was very good, not heavy at all actually quite invigorating, steak frites were good and chicken i found to be not as moist as i would've expected from a place like this. It helped to get the foie gras. My fav dish from the night is the fromage blanc ice cream. I ordered a second one. The somm was probably doing her best to guide us to what i requested : a unique, flavourful, maybe bready sort of sweet, easy to drink champagne. I felt i was led astray. We ordered a 500 dollar bottle of 2012 Les Mont Fournois Montagne, and we weren't even able to finish it. Not delicious. Its rare that i go to dinner and have a high budget for a bottle, so on this occasion with Chez Fifi's reputation of having an insane wine list i was very excited to splurge, and for this to be what i end up with is so disappointing. I get 2012 is a good year for champagne, does that automatically make it superb? I don't know. I wish the somm led me correctly with the budget i was working with (sub 500) If you are a foodie and have been wanting to come, do not set expectations very high. This place really is for looking good, showing off a bit, feeling luxe, and escaping manhattan, all great reasons to go. The food is not worth the visit, nor was the wine in my experience. (4 stars)

So hard to get a reservation but so worth it. Our servers were amazing! Great wine selection. We LOVED the Basque deviled crab, roast chicken with foie gras, and the Filet mignon au poivre, and of course Pommes Fifi. All delicious, and reasonably priced. Our Chocolate mousse for dessert was a perfect ending. Really hope I can get another reservation to come back again!! (5 stars)

Amazing! Probably the nicest new restaurant and one of the only few that will bring us downtown folk uptown. Everyone who works here is so friendly and attentive, service amazing, food was amazing. The foie gras, tuna tartar, steak and chicken are superb. Even the basic green salad had an amazing dressing. Cocktails were also fantastic. Beautiful decor. 10 out of 10 (5 stars)

If you’re looking for a dining experience that hits all the high notes: flavor, atmosphere, service, look no further than Chez Fifi. From the moment you walk in, you feel transported: the townhouse setting, the elegance of the wood-panelled dining room, and the buzz Let’s talk the Steak Frites: it’s a master class in simplicity done right. The steak arrives with that perfect crust, the juices still singing, paired with golden, crisp-on-the-outside, fluffy-on-the-inside fries that you want to keep dunking again and again. The martinis are no afterthought, they make a cocktail crafted with intention. Clean gin, the right amount of brine, a blue cheese olive (or three) that carries its own swagger. The service here is the kind you don’t always find—but absolutely want when you want to feel remembered and well-taken-care-of. On that note: a heartfelt shout-out to Markyia, the sommelier whose professionalism, graciousness and genuine helpfulness elevated the evening further. Whether you needed a wine pairing, a suggestion or just someone who knew the menu inside-out and made you feel seen, Markia delivered. It’s clear that the team believes service is part of the craft. The atmosphere blends the formality of a classic French bistro with the ease of a modern New York dining room. You come dressed, you come excited, you come ready to savour and you leave fully satisfied. (5 stars)

Guests can enjoy an a la carte menu crafted by Executive Chef Zack Zeidman, featuring innovative cocktails and a curated selection of wines from around the globe, making it a perfect destination for both casual dining and special occasions. bio_text: Chez Ma Tante is a charming eatery that draws inspiration from the unpretentious pubs, cafes, bistros, and trattorias found across Europe. With a focus on the enjoyment of food, drink, and good company, the restaurant features a warm atmosphere characterized by white-washed brick walls and an uncluttered bar, making it a perfect spot for both casual dining and special occasions. The culinary focus at Chez Ma Tante is on simple yet delicious dishes that highlight fresh ingredients. The menu includes a variety of offerings such as pig’s head terrine and grilled pork shoulder, showcasing a blend of Canadian and New York influences. Signature techniques include classic cocktail preparation and a well-edited wine list that emphasizes value. Canadian born Aidan O’Neal and native New Yorker Jake Leiber were introduced by their mentors Hugue Dufour of M. Wells and Johnathan Waxman of Barbuto, leading to the establishment of Chez Ma Tante.
menu_items: Oysters - green tomato mignonette - $4 ea
Olives - $7
Anchovies - fire roasted peppers - $10
Chicken liver pâté - $9
Country pâté - pork, foie gras, pistachio - $15
Melons and Culatello - $20
review_snippets: I stopped in here with a group of 4 on Saturday for brunch, our group had a reservation and was seated promptly. The server came to our table not to long after we were seated and took our drink orders. We ordered beers, coffees and Bloody Marys ,which were the star of the show. As for food we ordered the chicken Caesar sandwhich, quiche, chicken liver pate, gigante beans, pancakes and chips with aioli. The star of the show was the chicken liver pate, it had a great rich savory flavor with a hint of sweetness and was served on a nice soft piece of sourdough. The Scottie Pippen of the food order had to be the pancakes, they were savory and sweet with a hint of lemon. The only weak link of the bunch was the under seasoned gignate beans, which had an off day. Would recommend this spot to anyone looking for a brunch spot in WB or Greenpoint. (5 stars)

I really enjoyed this place a lot. The screw driver with tangerine juice was awesome and strong. The waiter was very knowledgeable about everything on the menu. The country pate looked kind of like spam but tasted magical. The chips (French fries) and aioli was outstanding reminded me of the ones at 4 Charles or Au Cheval. The Shakshuka egg and tomatoes was fire too. The sausage biscuit in the gravy was really good. The star of the show however was the pancakes they were perfect. Crispy edges but fluffy and the perfect amount of syrup. The cutlet that was with the Cesar salad was awesome too. I definitely would return. (4 stars)

Finally got here for one of their famous brunches and completely lived up to the hype. The food was outstanding, the sausage gravy and biscuits was pepper, creamy delicious with every bite. Honestly every plate that arrived on every table looked magazine quality. The service and atmosphere were perfect for a group or table for two. Looking forward to coming back again and again (5 stars)

Been here for both brunch and dinner. Love the elevated takes on simple, European-style dishes. My pork shoulder this evening came out purple and impossible to cut. The team happily refired it, delivering a dreamingly tender cut with a deep pink blush. Beautiful piece of meat in the end, and they even took it off our check. Thanks for being on top of it. Duck was beautiful too. Can't wait to come back for another neighborhood meal. (5 stars)

bio_text: Chick Chick is a vibrant dining destination located in NYC's Upper West Side, dedicated to bringing together good food and good company. With a focus on creating a welcoming atmosphere, the restaurant aims to provide a joyful experience through its culinary offerings, which are inspired by the owner's personal favorites. Chick Chick specializes in Korean-inspired fried chicken and ramen. The menu features a unique blend of comfort food, emphasizing bold flavors and quality ingredients, with a focus on delivering a satisfying dining experience. Owner Chef Jun Park was inspired to create Chick Chick from his love of fried chicken and ramen. The restaurant faced challenges during its construction due to the COVID-19 pandemic but persevered to bring joy and comfort food to the community.
menu_items: K&Q by Christine - Add Chicken Tender $5, Kale, Quinoa, Roasted Sweet Potato, Apples, Parmesan, Pumpkin Seed, Maple Lemon Dressing - $18
Kale Caesar - Kale, Brussel Sprouts, Serrano Peppers, Parmesan, Croutons, Lemon Parmesan Dressing - $18
Chick Chick Fried Rice - Chinese Sausage, Kimchi, Fried Egg, Tobiko - $19
Dirty Truffle Rice - Truffle, Lemongrass, Scrambled Egg, Mushroom - $19
1/2 Chicken - $19
Whole Chicken - $37
review_snippets: I stopped by Chick Chick with a couple of friends for a quick bite, and omg what a find! The chicken sandwiches and tenders were incredibly flavorful and juicy. The portions were generous, way more than what you’d get at most places in the city. And the honey bread? Chef’s kiss. Definitely coming back to try more items on the menu! (5 stars)

The chicken was huge, juicy and flavorful. Service was super fast, takeout until closing. I got the Nashville and Korean BBQ. The sauces were not huge flavor, was hoping for more of a punch with the big piece of chicken. (4 stars)

Chick chick was a seriously fantastic place to eat. Its in the city, Upper West Side, so parking is on the street and its close to public transit. The service was friendly, quick and knowledgeable and the food....... oh goodness, the food. I wanted to try every single thing, literally. I would have been thrilled to have that ability.. what I did eat was absolutely incredible and the pictures are attached. The chicken bites had these amazing pops of spice and flavor, and the waffle chicken sandwich looked as good as it tasted; each bite was simply delicious. Next time, and believe me, there will be a next time, I'm simply going to use the menu as a food check list! 10/10 highly recommend! (5 stars)

Chick Chick delivers a mouthwatering fried chicken experience that goes beyond expectations, both in flavor and service. The Nashville fried chicken sandwich was a highlight, crispy, juicy, and perfectly spiced, nestled in a soft, buttery bun with creamy slaw that tied it all together. The chicken and waffles brought a delightful balance of sweet and savory, with golden, fluffy waffles and crunchy, well-seasoned chicken. The truffle fries were crisp and addictive, with just the right hint of truffle oil to elevate them without overpowering. The fried chicken and mac n cheese combo was pure comfort food bliss, featuring creamy, cheesy pasta paired with more of their signature crispy chicken. On top of the fantastic food, the service was incredible, friendly, fast, and genuinely attentive, making the whole dining experience feel warm and welcoming. Chick Chick is a must-visit for anyone who loves bold flavors, hearty portions, and top-notch hospitality. (5 stars)

bio_text: Cho Dang Gol is a renowned Korean restaurant located in New York City, celebrated for its dedication to homemade tofu dishes. Since its establishment in 1997, the restaurant has cultivated a warm and inviting atmosphere, where guests can enjoy a variety of traditional and creatively inspired Korean meals. Each dining experience begins with a complimentary tofu starter, setting the stage for a culinary journey that emphasizes freshness and authenticity. Cho Dang Gol specializes in homemade tofu-based dishes, showcasing the versatility of this key ingredient. The menu features a blend of traditional Korean fare alongside innovative recipes, with weekly and seasonal specials that invite exploration of diverse flavors. Cho Dang Gol has been serving the community since 1997, establishing itself as a 'Tofu House' with a commitment to quality and freshness.
menu_items: CDG Best Seller Set(for 2) - Braised short ribs, Cod roe omelet, Eggplant rice with Kimchi biji or Kong Biji - $93.99
Mussel Radish Rice - Mussel and radish rice with dallae(wild chive) soy sauce - $15.99
Beef Dureup Sanjeok(2pcs) - Tender chuck flap tail (Salchi - Sal) and spring dureup (Korean wild shoots), delicately skewered and grilled - $17.99

Perilla Seed Monkfish Hot Pot - Tender monkfish with monkfish liver, minari (watercress), mideodeok (sea squirt cluster), and bracken in a deep, savory seafood broth enriched with nutty perilla - $49.99
CDG Dubu Duruchigi - Homemade tofu and assorted vegetables cooked in a spicy sauce - $29.99
Add-On Whole Squid - $8.99
review_snippets: Conveniently located where we stayed at, it was cold that night and so we decided to eat here. We were starving so we ordered a couple of things that looked appetizing. Surprisingly, everything was delicious! Big serving for sure, there were three of us with quite an appetite and we had left overs. The rice was $2 but it was a huge bowl enough for four people. Plenty of side dishes too, all of which are good. Personally, I enjoyed the fish. Wait was fast, we did not make a reservation, it was Sunday at around 7pm. Service was quick and prompt too. (5 stars)

3/7/26 from nyc. went in to try Korean fried chicken, my daughter found this spot after our convention. We find out it’s not the typical Korean fried chicken spot you would go to so we tried something else and I’ll Leave my curious crunchy Korean friend chicken hunt for another time. Nice service, good eats. Glad we waited to snag a table. Love trying new spots (4 stars)

We waited 90 minutes for a table, and it was certainly worth it! We ordered the Spicy Seafood Tofu Stew, Bossam, Seafood & Scallion Pancake, and the CDG Royal Oxtail Soup. All of the dishes were prepared perfectly, but personally, the Oxtail Soup stood out as exceptional. Its broth was remarkably clean yet flavorful, partly due to the abalone, and the oxtail was wonderfully tender. This has been, by far, the best restaurant experience during our five-day trip to New York. (5 stars)

There’s always a long waitlist (1 hr+), but I don’t think it’s worth it. They make their tofu in house, and it’s pretty good, but overall lowkey mid and overhyped given the wait. Dubuhaus is way better imo - Cod roe omelet ($14.99): 4/10, everyone on Beli got it, so we got it, but there wasn’t that much cod roe. Skip - Spicy kimchi soondubu ($17.99): 8/10, pretty solid and flavorful but not mind blowing. Tofu quality was good - Bossam ($20.99): 8/10, similar to other places - Banchan: Standard, liked the tofu one a lot (4 stars)

bio_text: Chola Coastal Indian Cuisine is a timeless classic located in the upscale Upper East Side of New York City, celebrated for its authentic Indian flavors and chic ambiance. With a legacy spanning 26 years, the restaurant embodies a commitment to culinary excellence and Indian hospitality, ensuring that every guest feels revered. The dining experience is enriched by a thoughtfully curated wine list and a cocktail program designed to complement the vibrant menu. Chola specializes in authentic Indian cuisine, with a focus on traditional recipes and innovative dishes. The menu features a variety of house-made spice blends, chutneys, and sauces, highlighting the rich tapestry of Indian flavors. Signature techniques include the meticulous preparation of each dish from scratch, ensuring a unique and memorable dining experience. Chola was founded by Shiva Natarajan, a pioneer of the Indian dining scene in New York City, and is currently owned by his protégé, Min Bhujel. Shiva remains involved in menu development, having recently added 25 new dishes inspired by his travels in India.
review_snippets: Had a wonderful dining experience here! The food was absolutely delicious, and you can really tell the quality from the first bite especially the meats, which were perfectly cooked, tender, and full of flavor without being over or underdone. We ordered the Achari Murgh Kebab, Royyala Veppudu, Tandoori Murgh, Mughlai Chicken Biryani, Malabar Parota, purani Delli Ki Papri Chaat, and Lamb Madras, and every single dish was outstanding. The kebabs were juicy, the seafood was flavorful, the biryani was rich and aromatic, and the lamb madras was cooked to perfection with deep, balanced spices. Each dish was oozing with freshness and taste. The staff were also very down-to-earth, welcoming, and attentive, which made the experience even better. This place is a must-try, and I highly recommend these dishes if you visit definitely coming back again! (5 stars)

Food: Went with my girlfriend, it’s my favorite cuisine, it was delicious. Cashew curry is an old favorite, and tikka masala is classic so we tried and loved both. Not spicy at all if you prefer the mild side you’d enjoy the options here. And there were spicy options that I will be trying next time. Service: There were strands in our food that I was worried were something like plastic but it was just ginger and the manager and server were very attentive to the request to check. Also we did have a reservation that we were on time for but had a 5+ minute wait. Not a huge issue for me but it should be mentioned. Atmosphere: We dined around 7:30pm, it was quite busy, all tables taken and a few groups waiting outside from time to time. Also I eat a toooooon but the food was quite filling. I left feeling satiated and honestly looking forward to my next dinner here (5 stars)

We came here for dinner and the food did not disappoint, every meal item we ordered was cooked to perfection. We had the lamb chops one of the best lamb chops I have ever eaten, the lamb biriyani fell right off of the bone. (5 stars)

review_snippets: One of the best Chinese meals I've ever had. The food was all well prepared. The service was as good as it gets. The dragon dumplings and the mala cold noodle were out of this world. Everything was so well prepared and came out fast. The cumin lamb was dry but yet still tender. The spicy fried fish was crisp soft on the inside. They have some magic sauce that they use on the Szechuan vegetable dish that makes the cabbage into something like I've never had before yet Flavorful. I hope I get the chance to eat here again (5 stars)

Very good mapo tofu. Could be a bit spicier though. However I brought a white person with me so maybe that’s why it wasn’t so spicy. Munch munch. Waiters kept refilling our hot tea which was very nice on a cold day. (5 stars)

So we came with 7 friends to have a nice dinner. First time trying out this cuisine and it did not leave us disappointed. They focus on spicy dishes such as Mapo tofu but the non spicy ones are very excellent as well, like the black pepper steak. All the protein was nice and tender and quite exquisite. (5 stars)

This place is so god damn good! Best Szechuan spicy flavor Intestine very spicy and flavorful Crispy pork and spicy chicken are all good The best side dish is their DAN DAN noodles. Perfection (5 stars)

bio_text: Ci Siamo is a vibrant dining destination located in the heart of Manhattan West, where traditional Italian cuisine meets contemporary culinary techniques. The restaurant features an inviting atmosphere with floor-to-ceiling windows offering stunning views of the Empire State Building, creating a perfect backdrop for an intimate dining experience. With a focus on live-fire cooking and housemade pasta, Ci Siamo celebrates the beauty of simplicity in its dishes, complemented by a robust selection of Italian wines. Ci Siamo specializes in live-fire Italian cooking, emphasizing seasonal ingredients and purposeful preparations. The menu is crafted by Chef Hillary Sterling, who draws inspiration from her extensive travels in Italy. The dining experience is designed to be straightforward and rooted in authentic Italian flavors. Chef Hillary Sterling draws inspiration from her extensive travels in Italy.
menu_items: Cast Iron Focaccia - tomato conserva - $18
Pizza Bianca - anchovy • salsa verde • aioli - $15
Pizzette - tomato • soppressata - $16
Pizzette Formaggio - buffalo mozzarella • olives • chilies - $20
Gnocco Fritto - goat gouda - $16
Mortadella con Pistacchio - $15
review_snippets: Instantly became one of my favorite restaurants in NYC. Everything is delicious. The Gnocco Fritto is a standout, alongside the rib eye. The focaccia bread is so fresh, no notes. It’s on the pricey side but totally worth it. I made a reservation for the wrong date and they kindly sat us at the bar, best decision, the service was impeccable. I highly recommend Ci Siamo. (5 stars)

Ci Siamo is one of those places where you can’t really go wrong no matter what you order! For apps, we started off with the insalata verde with toasted garlic. I actually loved this salad because it didn’t have too much going on. No major callout here but if you need a tasty green just to say you had one, I’d recommend. Next, and know I’m not usually a fan of goat cheese, I loved the thin layer they added to the bottom of the light yet crispy gnocco frito made for the perfect pairing. Definitely a must order in my opinion. The last starter was the scallop tartare and unfortunately, this was the most disappointing part of the meal. I just felt like it was too fishy, but the texture and citrus within the dish was well balanced. For our mains, we shared the pappardelle with beef and the cavatelli with spicy crab. Both were a 10/10 so I highly recommend, but if I have to pick between the two I’m leaning more towards the pappardelle… just because the spicy crab had a couple of shells in it. For dessert, they gave us a complementary glass of white wine as a pallet cleanser to go with our lemon sorbet. Call me crazy but even though the sorbet was refreshing, it was too lemony/sour-y for me (geez I’m making up words). (5 stars)

I had such a great experience at Ci Siamo. I was in the city for work, and my aunt from Long Island met me for dinner before I headed back to Boston. My husband had eaten here before while he was in NYC for work and told me I had to try the onion torta—he was absolutely right. Our server, Jonathan, was truly wonderful. He was so inviting and kind without being overbearing. He helped me choose dishes that worked with my dietary restrictions, and my water glass was never even close to empty before he refilled it. His overall presence was just so pleasant, and he really made us feel taken care of. The food was amazing—big compliments to Chef Hillary—and honestly the whole staff made the entire experience feel special. I’ll definitely be coming back, and I’m happy to recommend Ci Siamo to anyone looking for a great dinner in NYC. (5 stars)

Dina was our waiter and was fantastic, speaking French, Italian and she gave us great wine recommendations. The rabbit pasta was great and I’d recommend getting the focaccia and use it to get the thin sauce. The smoked carrots had a mix of fresh herbs, and were good, but really only a slight hint of smoke. A great experience. (5 stars)

With a focus on high-quality ingredients and meticulous presentation, Claud aims to create a unique culinary journey that reflects the essence of European cuisine. menu_items: chicory and coffee ice cream - $11
rice pudding with luxardo cherries - $12
pistachio bundt with whipped ricotta - $13
devil’s food cake - $22
review_snippets: Great food, wine, and dessert! Ordered the chicken liver agnolotti, half chicken, chips, and devil’s food cake. We also enjoyed excellent Spanish white wine and a few mocktails. The service was great from the moment we walked in. Every member of the staff was incredibly attentive and helpful. We had a reservation, arrived on time and were seated promptly. We never felt rushed but we were just two people and dined on a weekday night so that could be why. (5 stars)

(We did reserve online. I recommend people to check that out as well!!) Red Shrimp with Olive Oil and Garlic - the best dish of the night. The shrimp was sweet and tender, and the oil underneath it added great aroma and richness. We had like 3 plates of bread to eat w the oil. Beef tongue w salsa verde - The presentation was nice, but the slices were very thin so the texture was not very impressive. The sour cream in the center was actually good and helped balance the acidity. Veal sweetbreads w pepperoncini aioli - This was the weakest dish. The frying was very oily and heavy, and the portion was quite small. The flavor did not justify the texture, so I would not order this again. 🐟- This came out last. The flavor was mild and the fish was tender, and it did help us feel full by the end. The lemon 🍋 is an extra bonus. Very refreshing. (3 stars)

Cute place, great wine, and food was really solid. I hesitated between 4-5 stars because the appetizers, which usually are the best in restaurants, where OKish here (a bit too fat IMO). But the ribs were amazing, and the chicken liver pasta was out of this world. So definitely a 5 stars. PS: oh and unlimited bread like in civilized countries? that's also a 5-star deserving thing to do (5 stars)

The food was good but not as good as I feel like my friends raved about. The pork stood out to me, really liked the sauce that was on top. Mille feuille is a total skip, was seriously flavorless and basically just a some puffed pastry sheets stacked on top of each other. Other things were just okay. We ordered a ton of food and drinks just between us girls but didn’t really have time to enjoy it all. They were very adamant about the 2 hour time limit even though we spent a lot and rushed us out of there. (3 stars)

bio_text: Comal is a vibrant restaurant located in the Lower East Side of Manhattan, New York, that celebrates the rich culinary traditions of Mexico City. The restaurant embodies warmth and simplicity, creating a welcoming atmosphere that reflects the essence of Mexican hospitality. With a focus on peak-season produce from the Northeast US, sustainably caught seafood, and heritage meats, Comal offers a dining experience that is both flavorful and thoughtfully curated. Comal specializes in Mexican cuisine, emphasizing fresh and sustainable ingredients sourced from local farms. The menu features a variety of dishes that highlight the use of chiles, spices, and other traditional ingredients from Mexico, aiming to create deep and complex flavors. Founded by Gaz Herbert, who hails from Cuernavaca, Mexico, Comal is influenced by his experiences in both Mexico City and London's diverse dining scene.
menu_items: Spring Peas, Smoked Salmon & Jalapeño
Artichoke Heart Tostada, Cotija & Salsa Macha
Bluefin Aguachile, Chiltepín, Lime Oil
Mixed Grilled Greens, Marigold, Salsa Seco

review_snippets: From the moment the dishes arrived, everything felt carefully chosen and full of character—the colors, the freshness, the way each element complemented the other without feeling forced. The food felt indulgent yet balanced, with flavors that were bold but not overwhelming, and textures that kept every bite interesting. The seafood was cooked just right, rich and satisfying, while the dessert felt delicate, comforting, and quietly luxurious. It’s the kind of meal that doesn’t need explaining—you simply enjoy it, and it stays with you long after the table is cleared. (5 stars)

The dining room has such a great atmosphere, lively, stylish, and super welcoming. The Striped Bass Aguachile was absolutely fantastic, so fresh, bright, and full of flavor. We also loved the drinks, perfectly crafted and really complemented the meal. And the desserts were incredible, a perfect ending. Highly recommend! (5 stars)

had an amazing meal here. it felt really special coming back its in the old gem wine spot. The skewers were great!! we ordered the lengua. The layered potato was a little overcooked but still tasty. I loved the aguachile and beef crudo appetizers. The first fish dish is a must-try — we had tilefish that day, and it paired so well with the comal rice. They also recommended a German orange wine, which was absolutely delicious! (5 stars)

We checked out this LES hot spot and left disappointed. The vibe and drinks were great, but the food was overpriced and underwhelming. The appetizers were especially bad — $30 for a few thin slices of salmon, and mussels that smelled so off we sent them back. The mains tasted better, but still weren’t worth it: a $95 12-oz steak and a $50 half chicken. Overall, great atmosphere but I wouldn’t recommend it for the food or value (2 stars)

bio_text: COQODAQ is a vibrant culinary destination in New York City, celebrated for its unique take on Korean fried chicken and an exceptional dining atmosphere. The restaurant combines modern design elements with a warm ambiance, creating a stylish yet welcoming environment perfect for both intimate gatherings and lively outings. With a focus on high-quality ingredients and attentive service, COQODAQ ensures that every guest enjoys a memorable dining experience, whether indulging in their signature fried chicken or exploring a variety of flavorful appetizers. COQODAQ specializes in Korean fried chicken, offering a range of flavors including classic soy garlic and spicy gochujang. The menu features a limited yet satisfying selection of dishes, emphasizing high-quality, locally sourced ingredients and innovative culinary techniques. Signature offerings include the original Soy Garlic Glaze and the Bucket List fried chicken, paired with an extensive Champagne list for a unique dining experience. COQODAQ began as a vision to redefine the experience of Korean fried chicken, quickly becoming a culinary landmark known for its fusion of traditional flavors and modern dining aesthetics. Key milestones include the introduction of signature dishes that garnered rave reviews, reflecting a rich culinary heritage while embracing contemporary techniques.

review_snippets: I love COQODAQ!!! Every time is an amazing experience - I love bringing friends here whenever I’m in the city. Whether it’s for a celebration or a regular day, it’s always an incredible time. The food is so perfect - both a feast for the eyes and the mouth. Champagne and wine selections are so well done, and cocktails and NA options are excellent too! The menu is conscious of dietary restrictions while also leaning towards a shared group-friendly dining experience. Service from the maître d’, host staff, service team, and sommelier were outstanding. Knowledgeable, friendly, welcoming and helpful. The atmosphere is incredible too - fun lighting and decor, fun all around. (5 stars)

What a great spot! Would definitely make a reservation, we came with one thankfully on a Sunday evening and on our way out around 7 PM overhead it was a 1.5 hour wait for a table. The food is on point and we shared we just got engaged when making the reservation on resy in the notes, they brought us free chicken nuggets with caviar and put candles in our yogurt as part of bucket we each ordered. The service was one of the best service experiences we have had, on our way to the table alone at least 3 of the staff said welcome to us. When we ordere drinks our waitress waited until my fiancé returned from the bathroom the pour his so it wouldnt get warm. They kept the drinks and food flowing while ensuring our every need was met. Would highly recommend! Oh and the egg cocktail is amazing. (5 stars)

If you come here just for the vibes, that alone is enough. The restaurant is sexy despite coming for a family friendly Sunday Brunch. The music is also what I call sexy pop. The wash station when you first walk in is very welcoming and very instagrammable. The free coat check is nice as well. It was extremely busy that day (although I expect that it is ALWAYS busy), yet the staff was super friendly and attentive. The place is a hit, getting a reservation is like winning a lottery. Once you tried their amazing food, you know it worthy of the wait and efforts. The star dish is the bucket list, including two types of friend chicken - original and glazed (you can choose from two flavors or do a mix). It is the best Korean fried chicken I had so far, including those I had in Seoul. The original, skin is crisp, meat is soft and tender, filled with flavor. My favorite dip sauce is gochujiang. For glazed, I choose the mix, both soy garlic and gochujiang taste amazingly. There are many side dishes to choose from, I had fennel salad, however the bucket list also comes with scallion salad and kimchi, plus a small bowl of cold noodle, which fresh and tasty, perfect for after eating the friend chicken. For the cocktail, I highly recommend the egg, it's fruity and refreshing. (5 stars)

bio_text: Corima is a vibrant culinary destination in New York City that embodies the spirit of sharing and community, as suggested by its name, which translates to 'circle of sharing.' The restaurant showcases the rich culinary heritage of northern Mexico, particularly the states of Sonora and Chihuahua, through a modern lens. With a focus on both traditional and innovative techniques, Corima offers a unique dining experience that celebrates the flavors of Mexico while incorporating local Northeast ingredients. Corima specializes in Progressive Mexican cuisine, blending traditional recipes with contemporary techniques. The menu features a diverse array of dishes that highlight a wide Mexican pantry, complemented by local ingredients. Signature techniques are influenced by Chef Fidel Caballero's experiences in Basque Country and his culinary roots in Ciudad Juárez and El Paso. Chef Fidel Caballero, inspired by his upbringing and culinary experiences, opened Corima to represent northern Mexico in New York's dining scene. Within a year of opening, the restaurant received a Michelin star and was recognized as one of Bon Appetit's Best New Restaurants of 2024.

review_snippets: Food was delicious and the experience was lovely. Taking off a star because a couple sat down at the table next to us 30 minutes into our meal and by the end of the meal they got their last course before us. Service just slowed down a lot for us until the table next to us eventually surpassed us and it didn’t feel like the level of service you should get from a place with a Michelin star. We also ordered a cocktail mid-way through the meal and we were about to receive our last course and the cocktail still hadn’t come so we canceled it since they had clearly forgotten and my partner didn’t want to continue drinking so close to the end of the meal and instead of cancelling and making it up in another way they ended up bringing out multiple drinks for us to taste which is definitely nice but we didn’t really want to continue drinking (hence us canceling the drink). Not a big deal but definitely to be noted! Otherwise the meal was yummy. (4 stars)

Such an incredible and unique tasting menu. I had fish (and a fish head that tasted like a chicken wing) that I would've never ordered on my own. The highlights of the menu were 1. Steak with the sourdough tortilla 2. Taco 3. Potato with onion 4. Dessert of macarons, bonbons, and custard 5. Chicken wing fish head thing I did the spirit pairing and got to taste a lot of unique Mezcal, Tequila, and Sotol. Probably something like 8-10 oz of liquor by the end. My wife did the wine pairing which was very hearty. Probably 3-4 oz pours for each portion of food. I am definitely going to go back. We saw lobster leaving the kitchen that I want to get my grubby hands on. We ended up spending a little over 2 hours on dinner (5 stars)

Excellent! Food was delicious! We will definitely be returning for a la carte. We did the tasting menu and it was a great introduction to what we can look forward to on a future visit. Sourdough tortilla was divine. The perfect tortilla. 1st bite was my favorite. Thanks for a great night and outstanding food. 100% recommend. (5 stars)

Loved the menu and food at Corima. We made reservations 2 days before so coukd not get the tasting menu, but tried few things from their regular menu. Lobster was one of the best I have ever had and the tortilla with butter was very addictive. Will be back again! (5 stars)

bio_text: Cosme is a contemporary restaurant located in New York City’s Flatiron District, founded by renowned Chef Enrique Olvera. The restaurant offers a vibrant dining experience that celebrates Mexican flavors and traditions, utilizing local and seasonal ingredients to create memorable dishes. With a focus on artisanal spirits and high-quality ingredients, Cosme aims to provide guests with an authentic taste of Mexican culture in a warm and inviting atmosphere. Cosme specializes in contemporary Mexican cuisine, featuring a menu that highlights seasonal ingredients and traditional flavors. The dining format includes a la carte options as well as family-style dishes, allowing guests to share and experience a variety of flavors. Signature techniques include innovative presentations and the use of artisanal ingredients. Enrique Olvera is the Chef Founder of Cosme, which reflects his dedication to Mexican culinary traditions and local sourcing.

review_snippets: A complete delight, don’t miss the opportunity to come here. I had the pleasure of coming with my wife during Restaurant Week, and everything we tried was incredible. If I go again, I would definitely order the Icelandic Arctic Char Everything Bagel Tostada, the duck enmoladas, and the hazelnut flan. The mole is unbelievable, and the flan is so enjoyable. Even the tortillas were amazing, they truly taste like authentic handmade Mexican tortillas. The place itself is beautifully decorated, perfect for a date night or even a more formal dinner. The staff was extremely nice, Alejandra and Fidel were the best. I truly loved this place and I’m definitely coming back. (5 stars)

I’ve been here twice, once for a group birthday dinner and another time for an anniversary, and would gladly come back. The food here is phenomenal and perfect for sharing - my favorites are the duck carnitas, guac, and octopus. Do keep in mind that most items lean on the saltier side, but the warm tortillas accompanying every dish helps balance everything out. Service is consistently great and everyone working there seems to be extremely knowledgeable about the restaurant dishes, never hesitating to answer questions or provide recommendations. Overall, an amazing restaurant in Flatiron that’s perfect for all occasions! (5 stars)

The restaurant combines modern Mexican flavors with a relaxed, stylish atmosphere, and everything felt very well thought out. We started with the guacamole, which was outstanding — rich, fresh, and with a gentle spicy note that added a nice touch. We finished it almost immediately. The Montauk fluke was light, refreshing, and perfectly tender. The octopus was incredibly soft, and the sauce brought all the flavors together beautifully. The Pékin duck carnitas were another highlight — flavorful, satisfying, and even better with the warm tortillas. Although we were already full, we still decided to try the Meringue dessert, and it was absolutely worth it. A lovely finish to the meal. Overall, the food, service, and atmosphere made the evening really special. I’d happily return, especially to try their brunch churros next time. (5 stars)

Good atmosphere and nice service. The octopus was good even though it was a bit too salty. The Peking duck carnitas tacos were interesting but probably not worth it. It does come with a ton of meat! Corn meringue was interesting. (4 stars)

bio_text: COTE Korean Steakhouse is America’s first and only Michelin-starred Korean Steakhouse, renowned for its unique blend of Korean barbeque and classic American steakhouse elements. The restaurant offers a vibrant and interactive dining experience, where guests can enjoy the highest quality USDA Prime beef in a convivial atmosphere, complemented by an extensive wine list and creative cocktails. COTE specializes in Korean barbeque with a focus on USDA Prime and American Wagyu beef. The menu features a combination of grilled steak and innovative cocktails, creating a dynamic dining experience. The restaurant emphasizes an interactive format, allowing guests to engage in the cooking process.

review_snippets: One of the best dining experiences ever. I came with my partner and my best friend from out of town. Not only was I able to celebrate my birthday here, but my friend got to experience a lot of firsts! We splurged and got the Steak Omakase, and got a little too excited with 12 lychee martinis. They're to die for. Of the two sides they offer for the omakase, I suggest the hot one over cold (I don't remember the names) cold one is just a bit too intense with flavor, and hot is surprisingly smooth despite having anchovy. The caviar dish was really harmonious and delicious, wasnt fishy at all. The meat selections really out done themselves, every one had a unique taste, by the last 3 cuts, I wasn't even bothering to eat them as lettuce wraps and just ate them alone (we sometimes added additional salt). All of the staff were very kind and professional. It was very loud, you kind of had to shout to talk, but it added to the boisterious vibe. By the end, our bill was about $1k before tip (omakase was about $230 per person if I recall correctly). Easily by far the most expensive meal I've ever witnessed, but with such good company, and delicious food, it was hard to regret. (5 stars)

An outstanding dining experience at COTE Korean Steakhouse. The quality of the beef was exceptional. Perfectly marbled, expertly cooked, and deeply flavorful, each cut reflected a high level of sourcing, technique, and respect for the ingredient. From the grill to the table, everything was executed with precision and confidence. The service was equally refined and thoughtful. Knowing my son is about to begin a new chapter of his life in New York, the team surprised us with a meaningful gift and a beautifully presented fruit plate. Throughout the evening, we were met with genuine warmth, encouragement, and kindness. In the cold of a New York winter, COTE offered not only an excellent meal, but a moment of humanity and connection. A truly memorable experience. (5 stars)

If you can manage to snag a reservation here, don't hesitate. COTE was fantastic. The Butcher's feast was very reasonably priced and featured a great variety of steaks and banchan (side dishes). The steaks were cooked to perfection. A small soft-serve cup capped off the meal. Staff were very attentive and friendly. I can't wait to go back :) (5 stars)

We visited COTE for a Thanksgiving lunch while traveling from California, and it truly exceeded every expectation. We ordered the Thanksgiving preset menu, and the experience from start to finish was flawless. The meal opened with a turkey dumpling in a clear, soothing broth—simple, elegant, and the perfect warm beginning on a cold and windy Thanksgiving Day in New York. From there, each course showcased COTE’s signature balance of Korean flavors and elevated steakhouse finesse. The progression of dishes was thoughtful, beautifully plated, and incredibly satisfying. The meats were outstanding—perfectly marbled, expertly grilled, and full of rich flavor. Each bite reminded us why COTE is one of the most celebrated restaurants in Manhattan. The side dishes and accompaniments were equally memorable, complementing the main courses without ever overwhelming them. Service was impeccable. The staff was warm, attentive, and knowledgeable, guiding us through the menu with ease and making us feel truly welcomed on this holiday. The ambiance added to the experience as well: modern, stylish, and buzzing with that New York energy, yet still comfortable enough for a special Thanksgiving meal. This was more than just lunch—it was a holiday memory we’ll cherish. Highly, highly recommend COTE for anyone looking for an elevated dining experience in Manhattan. (5 stars)

bio_text: Covacha is a vibrant neighborhood restaurant located in the Upper West Side, where the culinary traditions of Western Mexico seamlessly blend with the American Northeast. With a focus on authenticity and artisanal processes, Covacha offers a warm and inviting atmosphere that celebrates the rich heritage of Mexican cuisine, particularly inspired by the Jalisco region and its Milpa culture. Covacha specializes in authentic Mexican cuisine, emphasizing traditional recipes and high-quality, small-batch ingredients. The menu features a variety of dishes that reflect the culinary roots of the western Mexican 'Ranchos', alongside a curated selection of boutique Mexican spirits and natural wines. Covacha was established in Spring 2021, emerging from the legacy of Café Frida, which closed in March 2020 due to the pandemic. Founded by Cristina Castañeda and Milena Gernandt, both experienced in the restaurant industry, Covacha represents a new vision and approach to hospitality.

review_snippets: My birthday luncheon! I was welcomed and promptly seated as a walk-in. I was fortunate to have Alexia as my server, knowledgeable, smiling face, prompt and attentive to my food tastes. She was very helpful with her suggestive dishes. Thoroughly enjoyed my first visit. Great ambiance and the restaurant is full of energy. Seemed like a smooth flow auto run place. I had a list of a few IG’s dishes that I realllllllllly wanted to try Chef Lilly’s specialties, but none were available- I guess seasonal. I had a mental palate to try’em all, but was disheartened…maybe another time. Kudos to the team for a very well run operation. 👏😋🫶‼️ Ty Alexia for friendly service. (4 stars)

Mexican restaurant on UWS on the Michelin guide, pretty self explanatory! Saturday afternoon quite busy, lots of reservations and walk ins. Portions were generous and flavours top tier. The guac had a chilli oil on it that was immense and homemade tortillas. Homemade lemonade was gorgeous! Sometimes they can be a little tart but this was perfectly sweet and lemony. Birria quesadilla was a highlight, birria not too spicy which was great for me but my partner would’ve rathered more fire. The chipotle shrimp taco was lovely and had the spice missing from the birria. Pork taco spot on. Overall excellent meal!! (5 stars)

The service here is amazing. Our server at the bar gave great dish recommendations and everything was incredible. The cocktails are definitely worth coming for— I recommend the cilantro gimlet. We loved the pork belly carnitas tacos and Zarandeado. (5 stars)

I wandered around the Natural History Museum and happened to find this restaurant, which was rated Michelin 2025. The food was amazing. I ordered fish tacos and chilaquiles rojos, both very authentic, spicy, layered, and full of flavor. Sergio is also incredibly nice, and he introduced the restaurant’s signature dishes and even shared stories about his hometown. Now I really want to go to South America this year. (5 stars)
search_text: Covacha Covacha is a vibrant neighborhood restaurant located in the Upper West Side, where the culinary traditions of Western Mexico seamlessly blend with the American Northeast. With a focus on authenticity and artisanal processes, Covacha offers a warm and inviting atmosphere that celebrates the rich heritage of Mexican cuisine, particularly inspired by the Jalisco region and its Milpa culture. Covacha specializes in authentic Mexican cuisine, emphasizing traditional recipes and high-quality, small-batch ingredients. The menu features a variety of dishes that reflect the culinary roots of the western Mexican 'Ranchos', alongside a curated selection of boutique Mexican spirits and natural wines. Covacha was established in Spring 2021, emerging from the legacy of Café Frida, which closed in March 2020 due to the pandemic. Founded by Cristina Castañeda and Milena Gernandt, both experienced in the restaurant industry, Covacha represents a new vision and approach to hospitality. bio_text: Crane Club is a sophisticated dining destination in New York, offering a vibrant atmosphere that combines elegance with a lively social scene. The restaurant features a stunning raw bar and a diverse menu that showcases a blend of seafood and contemporary American cuisine, making it an ideal spot for both casual gatherings and special occasions. The culinary focus at Crane Club centers around fresh seafood and high-quality meats, with a menu that includes a variety of raw bar selections, pasta dishes, and grilled specialties. Signature techniques include the use of premium ingredients and innovative flavor combinations, presented in a refined manner.

review_snippets: Oh. My. GOD. Crane Club was excellent. I was genuinely blown away from the minute we stepped inside. The entire space is a masterpiece, the soaring arches, the warm, sculptural lighting, the way the architecture frames each room so thoughtfully. And speaking of welcoming… the staff was amazing. Every single person we interacted with was warm, attentive, and genuinely excited to walk us through the experience. Then the food started arriving, and it honestly just kept getting better with every course. We kicked things off with what might genuinely be the best bread basket I’ve ever had - even the basket itself was edible. Such a fun, unexpected detail that immediately tells you the kitchen is playing at a very creative, elevated level. We followed that with the croquette topped with caviar, which was outstanding! We also ordered a salad that leaned a bit more seafood-forward than expected, but still super fresh. Oh, and the warm tomatoes. It sounds simple, but these were unbelievable!! Bursting with flavor and the way they paired with the feta on top was just perfection. We finished with the short rib, which was incredibly tender and full of depth. All in all, Crane Club completely exceeded expectations. It’s the kind of restaurant that gets every detail right, from the atmosphere and service to the creativity and execution of the dishes. (5 stars)

Went last night for my wife's 50th birthday. We arrived early and our table was ready. The waitress told us all her recommendations. We ordered the Article Char, Rib Eye , add the Agnolotti and the Balsamic Bordelaise sauce. Artic Char was nice and crispy in a butternut squash sauce. The fish itself tasted very fishy and couldn't finish it. Bone in rib eye was cooked perfect, very moist. The Bordelaise sauce took it over the top. Agnolotti pasta stuffed with braised pork with an aged basaltic. This was ridiculously good. Overall really great place. Very upscale. Quality is the best a must visit. Thanks for a great experience (5 stars)

Beautiful space with much attention to detail, from the decor to the service. The bread basket has a delectable assortment of breads, along with labne and butter. The golden beets are rich and flavorful due to the labne and pistachio. The Agnolotti has a nice umami flavor with the aged balsamic, but is quite small in portion. The bone in rib eye was delicious and probably everyone’s favorite of the night. (5 stars)

The Crane Club is the kind of place that turns a great night out into something truly memorable. From the moment you walk in, the atmosphere feels celebratory, refined yet welcoming, with every member of the staff genuinely invested in making the evening special. The steak is nothing short of spectacular, perfectly seared with a caramelized crust and tender, juicy center that melts with each bite. You can taste the care in its preparation and the quality of the cut. The sweet potatoes are an unexpected standout — silky, subtly sweet, and beautifully balanced with a touch of seasoning that complements the richness of the steak. It’s a perfect example of how The Crane Club takes comfort classics and transforms them into something elevated and memorable. One of the most special touches of the evening was the champagne toast for a birthday celebration. It wasn’t just a gesture, it felt personal, joyful, and perfectly orchestrated. The service deserves its own standing ovation. The sommelier and wine director curated pairings that elevated every course, thoughtful, precise, and clearly driven by passion and deep knowledge. The entire team, from the servers to the hosts, radiated warmth and professionalism without ever feeling overbearing. It’s rare to see hospitality executed with this much grace and attention to detail. At The Crane Club, everything from the food to the service to the ambiance works in harmony. It’s a place that makes you feel celebrated, whether you’re there for a milestone or simply an unforgettable meal. Special thank you to Abe for checking in on us throughout the night and ensuring it was a social experience. Cannot recommend highly enough! (5 stars)

review_snippets: I found Crevette when looking up new lunch spots near SoHo and I am very glad that I stumbled upon this place. They serve upscale French cuisine but the space did not feel overly formal during the day. I can see how it might be more upscale at night though. We started with a Merguez & Morcilla Skewer and two pieces of Bluefin Tuna. Both were delicious (perhaps the best part of the meal). The Morcilla was so good that we ended up getting a second one. Next, we split the Grilled Cabbage, Chickpea, and Jamón Ibérico salad and the Grilled Chicken w Fries. Both were really good. It was nothing too inventive but both dishes were done really really well! The fries were cooked perfectly and the chicken was delicious. We left feeling full, but not too full. Honestly, I hope to go back. There were so many things on the menu that looked good. Definitely try this place. Either for date night or a weekend lunch with friends! (5 stars)

We stopped by Crevette in the West Village to see if we could move our reservation, and the staff was so accommodating—they were able to switch us to an earlier time right away. We were seated in a cozy corner booth, which ended up being the perfect spot for a relaxed dinner. Service throughout the night was excellent. Our server was attentive, warm, and always on top of things without feeling intrusive. The food overall was good. The Little Gem Salad was fresh and flavorful—simple but really well done. The Lobster Tagliatelle was rich and tasty, with great texture on the pasta. The Dover Sole had nice flavor, but it was a bit too buttery for us; it would’ve been much better with a lighter hand on the sauce. We ended with dessert, and both treats were enjoyable—the soft serve sundae was fun and nostalgic, while the chocolate tart was rich and deep in flavor. Crevette sits right in a great spot in the West Village, making it an easy and charming place for dinner. Service is truly the highlight, and the food has some solid hits, especially if you enjoy richer dishes. Overall, a pleasant neighborhood dining experience. (4 stars)

Truly incredible dining experience! Absolutely gorgeous and inviting interior. Our server was super knowledgeable and recommended incredible dishes and wine. The poached cod was the star of dinner but the dessert rum cake was close your eyes and say thank you good. This is what going out to dinner should feel like! (5 stars)

Very comfortable restaurant with great food. The red shrimp carpaccio and grill cabbage is the best of all. The scallops is nicely done but I like white sauce more than red one. Dover sole can be better if we can cook it less for one to two minutes. (5 stars)
