bio_text: Crown Shy is a Michelin-starred restaurant located in the historic Art Deco building at 70 Pine Street in Manhattan’s Financial District. This neighborhood establishment combines fine dining techniques with a warm, friendly service, creating an inviting atmosphere for guests. The restaurant's design and ambiance reflect a modern yet classic aesthetic, making it a perfect spot for both casual dining and special occasions. Crown Shy focuses on a menu rooted in European culinary techniques while drawing inspiration from global flavors, particularly those reminiscent of childhood and the diverse culinary landscape of New York City. The restaurant offers a thoughtfully curated menu that showcases seasonal ingredients and innovative cooking methods. Crown Shy opened in 2019 and was awarded a Michelin star just six months after its debut, maintaining this prestigious recognition every year since.
menu_items: Oysters, Sherry Consommé, Celery* - None - $21.00
Spiced Shrimp Cocktail, Yuzu, Sweet Chili Sauce - None - $20.00
Romaine, Green Goddess, Breadcrumbs - None - $19.00
Snap Pea, Walnut, Apicot, Nuớc chấm - None - $25.00
Spring Grain Salad, Yogurt, Almonds - None - $25.00
Ricotta Ravioli, Calabrian Chili, Chicken Broth - None - $35.00
review_snippets: Approachable fine dining exceeds all expectations. Every aspect of the experience is top-notch, from the impeccable service to the warm and welcoming atmosphere. Paul at the bar is incredibly knowledgeable and helpful, and his cocktails are beautifully balanced. We had a delightful conversation about gin and mezcal, and his expertise was evident. Our table had a lovely view of the well-appointed and choreographed kitchen, adding to the overall ambiance. The service was impeccable, and there was no need to rush. We were given ample time to enjoy the food and the highest level of service. When we made our selections, our server, Noelle, described each menu item in beautiful detail. The scallops in blood orange and romaine with green goddess were a standout dish, followed by bucatini for me and monkfish for him. The sommelier, Allie, paired the perfect wine for each course, enhancing the dining experience. The attention to detail and the overall experience for laid back fine dining were truly exceptional. It was an honor to be their guest, and I highly recommend their offerings to anyone seeking a truly memorable dining experience. Don’t skip dessert Thank you Silvia for attention to detail. (5 stars)

Great service food and atmosphere. Had the 3 course restaurant week menu. The first course of beef carpaccio/sates was visually not great but tasted absolutely amazing. The flavor is some of the best for the type of raw beef taste you may look for. The entree of jerk octopus was very unique fresh and nicely flavored. The sticky toffee pudding is legendary and one of the best desserts I’ve ever had. Not a bad price either. Good portions. Great service. Probably the easiest Michelin star to eat at in that it had a laid back not pretentious vibe. Highly highly recommend whether it’s your first or tenth Michelin experience (5 stars)

Our experience at Crown Shy was generally very good. Below are the key highlights and lowlights of our visit. Highlights • The Gnocchi is a Must-Try: Without a doubt, the absolute best part was the gnocchi. If you dine here, you must order them, they were truly exquisite. • Exceptional Bread: The initial pistachio bread served was spectacular. • Wonderful Ambiance: The overall setting and ambiance of the restaurant were really well done. • Outstanding Service: I also want to highlight the excellent attention from the entire staff. Lowlights • Late Seating: Despite having a 9:30 PM reservation, we were seated about 20 minutes late. The waiting area isn't the best, as there's constant foot traffic. • Spicy Dish Issue: While the server did warn me, the dish I received was genuinely too spicy. After mentioning it to the waiter, they were kind enough to bring me a replacement dish free of charge, which was excellent customer service on their part. • Inconsistent Portion Sizes: My wife ordered a pumpkin dish that was surprisingly small, especially when compared to my massive pork portion. Summary Overall, while there are a few points for potential improvement (the wait and portion size consistency), the total experience was very good. (4 stars)

I really enjoyed everything from Crown Shy- the vibe, the food, the staff, the chanting from the kitchen! We shared everything, our server recommended 5-6 plates for the us to share would be good, depending on how hungry you we were. They started us with complimentary bread for the table which was truly so good, took everything inside me not to keep eating it to save room for our orders to come! We ordered 2 cold starters the Spicy Tuna, Pineapple, Nori Chip and the Snapper Crudo, Persimmon, Leche de Tigre. They both have a nice kick and were delicious. The Spicy Tuna, Pineapple, Nori Chip was fun to eat, different textures and flavors in each bite. I could not get enough of the Snapper Crudo, Persimmon, Leche de Tigre -it was my favorite cold starter! We also ordered a hot starter, The Gruyère Fritters, Chili, Lime. Sooo good, they were like savory churros. I forgot what our server said was inside exactly aside from the obvious, but the inside also taste like there was potato inside. Our entrees were the Ricotta Gnocchi, Chanterelles, Vin Jaune and the Pork Katsu, Curry Béarnaise, Gooseberry. They were both delicious. The Pork Katsu is a pretty big portion. In the end we were pretty full but could not resist in getting the Sticky Toffee Pudding for Two, Pecans, Apple Sorbet for dessert. I forgot to take a photo, but it was really good. OHHH almost forgot the drinks, we had the 2 Mezcal drinks which were truly great, The Flightplan and Oro Maya. Honestly, our order was the best order and wouldn't have done anything differently. Another thing to note that I appreciated was that we were not rushed, even with it being busy for a Wed night. (5 stars)

bio_text: Dagon is a modern Israeli restaurant located in the heart of the Upper West Side of Manhattan, celebrated for its vibrant interpretation of Levantine cuisine. With a warm and inviting atmosphere reminiscent of Tel Aviv, the restaurant features vintage decor and a cozy ambiance that embodies the spirit of 'la dolce vita.' Dagon aims to be a culinary voice of peace, drawing inspiration from the Mediterranean and offering a unique dining experience that combines cultural heritage with contemporary flair. Dagon specializes in modern Israeli cuisine, focusing on flavors from across the Mediterranean. The menu features a variety of dishes inspired by the diverse cultures of the Levant, including signature items like Harissa BBQ Chicken and Whole Roasted Branzino. The restaurant also offers a creative cocktail list and an award-winning wine selection. Dagon was founded by restaurateur Simon Oren and partner David Sasson, inspired by the former Dutch cargo vessel MV Peace, which broadcast from the Middle East. Executive Chef Ari Bokovza, drawing on his Tunisian and Israeli heritage, leads the kitchen.
menu_items: FLATBREAD - $6
KUBANEH - Yemeni pull-apart bread with za’atar & feta, large size is served with labneh - $8 / $16
FARM STAND GREEK SALAD - cucumber, tomato, fennel, radish, oregano, feta cheese, crispy pita chips - $17
ISRAELI SALAD - cucumber, tomato, red onion, parsley, mint, green schug - $17
LEVANTINE “CAESAR” - fried chickpeas, toasted sesame, anchovy tempura, tahini, parmesan - $17
HARISSA/OLIVE TAPENADE - $10
review_snippets: I am finally getting around to writing this review after a stellar experience at Dagon back in December, and the memory of that meal is still just as vivid. From start to finish, it was a flawless 5-star experience. The atmosphere was immediately festive and welcoming with their beautiful Christmas decor, setting the perfect mood for a holiday meal. The service was truly top-tier; our waitress, Mejda, and the entire staff were incredibly kind and attentive. What really stood out to me were the "little things" that demonstrate true culinary professionalism. I was so impressed when one of the servers, while helping us plate our shared dishes, was careful not to use the same utensils for the seafood and non-seafood items. That level of mindfulness and attention to detail is rare and highly appreciated. As for the food, every single dish was a hit. The steak skewers, cauliflower, and broccolini were standouts and absolute must-orders, but truly, nothing disappointed. The portions were very generous, and you can tell the kitchen takes great pride in the quality of their ingredients. I would return to Dagon in a heartbeat and highly recommend it to anyone looking for incredible food paired with thoughtful, professional service. Thank you to Mejda and the team for a memorable evening! (5 stars)

I enjoyed an absolutely wonderful Thanksgiving dinner. Spencer, our server, was truly exceptional, warm, gracious, incredibly knowledgeable, and his wine pairing suggestion was nothing short of perfect. Thank you Dagon and Spencer for an unforgettable meal. Best! (5 stars)

I randomly found Dagon while walking down Broadway and decided to give it a try. I ordered the three mezze plate, and the bread it came with was incredibly fresh—a must for dipping. I chose the marinated beets, the matbucha, and feta. All of them were excellent, but the beets really stood out; the horseradish yogurt was a fantastic touch and paired with the roasted chickpeas it elevated the whole dish. Finished with the panna cotta which if you're a fan of rose water, you will love it. Overall, a great find and a fantastic meal! (4 stars)
Excellent dinner here! The food was unmatched in flavor, breads were soft and delicious, soup was hearty and the best veggie risotto I have ever had. The highlight was the dessert - Silan. (5 stars)

review_snippets: App was weak - maybe felt a bit low on the salt, not as flavorful as it could be (oysters, cured mackerel) - cucumber salad w smoked mussels was good tho Main was a hit - poached cod with chorizo was really good, perfectly cooked and flavorful. Fish and chips can’t go wrong but it was extra crispy and the fish was so soft and tasty. Oh, the drinks — the non-alcoholic vinegar shrub or something was amazing. Overall good but not the top of my list. (3 stars)

food is good, but nothing really stood out except the fish and chips. the curried crab was decent. basically a fried curry rice. the fish and chips were good but the batter had a strange grainy texture to it. overall solid food but not worth a line. (4 stars)

Ambiance (5/5): The space is so incredibly small which is why the reservations are so hard to get. We managed to get a reservation at 9:30pm! The space is tight but also quaint. Some seating by the chefs prep that overlooks the kitchen. Service (5/5): Service was on point throughout the meal. Our server provided us with some recommendations as well. Grilled Oysters (5/5): These were phenomenal, super flavorful, juicy! Get at least 2 per person. Chilled Scallops (5/5): The sauce is divine. The scallops are soft and complemented from the texture of the melons Fried Squash Blossoms (4/5): There was a nice crunch to the fried blossoms Tuna tartare (5/5): So much flavor in this but a tiny piece of bread. Skate cheeks (4/5): The breading was full of flavor and a hit of spice and sweet. Scottish Trout (5/5): The trout was so tender and juicy. Every one of the dishes was packed with different textures and flavor, providing a dynamic bite to each beautiful dish. Expect very small portions for what you’re paying for! (5 stars)

We dined 10/16 so this is a late review. 1 star for the food as the batter for the fish and chip was still raw and runny inside. It tasted like beer and raw dough. I know it wasn't the intended taste as we ordered 2 fish and chips and the other one came out fully cooked. The rest of the appetizers were interesting, but the fish and chip orders were our intended main, so we were super disappointed. Told the staff what happened and nothing was done in response. (1 stars)

bio_text: Restaurant Daniel, the flagship establishment of Chef Daniel Boulud, has been a cornerstone of New York City's dining scene since its inception in 1993. Nestled in the historic former Mayfair Hotel, the restaurant exudes elegance and sophistication, offering a transportive dining experience characterized by gracious hospitality and refined European cuisine. With a commitment to seasonal ingredients and a world-class wine cellar, Daniel invites guests to indulge in a culinary journey that celebrates both tradition and innovation. Restaurant Daniel specializes in modern French cuisine, focusing on seasonal ingredients sourced from around the globe. The menu features a blend of time-honored techniques and contemporary flair, with an emphasis on fine meats, wild game, and seafood. The restaurant also boasts an impressive selection of wines, particularly from the Rhône and Burgundy regions. Since opening in 1993, DANIEL has earned numerous accolades for its culinary excellence. The restaurant is steeped in French culinary history, located at the original site of Le Cirque.

JAPANESE YELLOWTAIL - Vodka Cured, Arugula-Oishi Strawberry Chutney Kohlrabi, “Sauce Caipiroska” - $56

review_snippets: Had our anniversary dinner here. We chose the 5 course dinner and it was great. Food was delicious and service was amazing. If you have a small appetite like my wife, 5 course might be a lot. She was full by dessert. All of the dishes were amazing. The server was great and provided good recommendations and later gave us a quick tour of the kitchen. (5 stars)

Fantastic service and overall meal for an upscale lunch. The staff was attentive and kind. The courses were a bit hit or miss for this level of Michelin star for me but overall a wonderful experience. The main courses of lamb and buffalo were stellar. I HIGHLY recommend the wine pairing. That was the highlight for us. It was fantastic wine and brought the food to the next level. Overall a lovely experience. I'll mention most men were wearing jackets even at lunch time though it is not required. (4 stars)

This was my second time dining at DANIEL, and once again it reminded me why this restaurant is so special and why I return every time I’m in New York City. From the moment we walked in, we were greeted with genuine warmth and gracious hospitality. The host and the manager who seated us were welcoming, attentive, and made us feel truly cared for. Throughout the evening, the service was impeccable ,polished yet friendly, professional without ever feeling distant. The sommelier was exceptional, offering thoughtful wine recommendations that paired beautifully with each course. The tasting menu was a true work of art: beautifully crafted dishes, elegant plating, balanced flavors, and pairings that elevated the entire experience. Every course felt intentional and refined, yet comforting at the same time. One of the highlights of the evening was having the pleasure of meeting Daniel Boulud himself. Despite being incredibly busy and on his feet all evening, his passion for cooking and hospitality truly shines through. He took the time to stop, chat with guests, and make everyone feel welcome and happy a rare and meaningful gesture from a world-renowned chef. DANIEL is not just about extraordinary food; it’s about heart, warmth, and genuine hospitality. An unforgettable experience, every single time. (5 stars)

I recently visited Daniel in New York City and experienced their tasting menu, and the entire evening was truly exceptional. From the moment I arrived, the service was warm, welcoming, and incredibly professional. The staff guided each course with genuine knowledge and attention, making the meal feel effortless and perfectly paced. The tasting menu itself was a remarkable journey. Every dish was beautifully presented with meticulous detail, showcasing refined technique and bold yet balanced flavors. Each course felt intentional—textures, colors, and tastes coming together in a way that showed the kitchen’s skill and creativity. The ingredients were clearly top-quality, and the transitions between courses were thoughtful and harmonious. The wine pairings elevated the experience even further, complementing each dish without overwhelming it. The ambiance of the dining room added to the enjoyment—elegant, serene, and polished without feeling stiff or overly formal. It created an atmosphere where you could relax and truly savor every moment. Overall, my experience at Daniel was extremely pleasant and memorable. The tasting menu was refined, artful, and satisfying, and the impeccable service made the evening feel special from start to finish. I would gladly return for another celebration or fine-dining experience. (5 stars)

bio_text: Daphne's is a vibrant Italian restaurant located in the heart of Bed-Stuy, offering a warm and inviting atmosphere for diners. With a focus on fresh, in-house made pasta and seasonal share plates, the restaurant provides a unique dining experience that emphasizes quality ingredients and thoughtful preparation. Daphne's specializes in Italian cuisine, featuring a frequently rotating menu that highlights seasonal ingredients. The dining format includes share plates and entrees, complemented by a carefully curated selection of natural wines and signature cocktails.
menu_items: Sourdough Focaccia - salted isigny butter - $9
Marinated Olives - seasonal citrus - $6
Grilled Salami Rosa - pistachio, sweety drop pepper, hot honey - $15
Broccolini - almonds, boquerones, herbs, nuoc cham - $18

review_snippets: Walked in and luckily we were able to be seated at the bar (best to make reservations ahead even if it says there are time slots open) The beet salad was delicious, especially with the bits of dates to add a touch of sweetness. The Caesar salad was a nice portion (not pictured). The rigatoni was excellent, really love how large the pasta was, and the sauce had a great butteriness to it; nice short rib flavor as well. The coffee and creme desert was a highlight; the description also said small lady fingers but it resembles Rice Krispies to me, either way, delicious. (5 stars)

To be honest I wasn’t expecting much, I think there are way too many of this kind of restaurant out there, but I was SHOCKED at how good everything was. The delicata squash tempura was FANTASTIC. It was so unassuming but the light batter leaves room for the sweetness of the squash to come through. The focaccia was fantastic although $3 extra for a singular tablespoon of salted butter is kind of off-putting. The half chicken was INCREDIBLE. It might’ve been the juiciest chicken I’ve ever had in my life. The fries were really well salted which is HUGE And the spicy rigatoni is not to be slept on! Pasta was the perfect doneness and the sauce was really perfect. I was worried it would be a throwaway dish but for a classic it was UNIQUELY good. Amazing! Can’t wait to come back (5 stars)

The pastas were delightful. Really loved the textures and different combinations of flavors. The menu is definitely small. It would be a better place for an intimate meal for a smaller group. (4 stars)

While I came just before closing after being denied service/food at Les Mars (Thai)-which closed at 10 (I arrived at 9:50) so I applaud the kitchen/bar for serving me just before kitchen closing rendering service until the closing hour. So had a quick meal of a Caesar Salad-excellent, Tanqueray Martini and an Iberico Pork Chop with a seared cabbage and pear soubise-very good. I think my only observation is that if you serve a guest(s) just before closing, you accept the responsibility of giving the same service for a 7 pm reservation at nearly 11 pm walk in. I’m a professional chef and while I’m not being as critical as in the 80’s or 90’s, service should not taper off-at the bar where I sat or at a table to be lackluster at best. I will return as I have always had a curiosity about this place since it opened-so I took a chance. I’ll return at a more decent hour and Jackie-thank you. I enjoyed my food and experience. (4 stars)

bio_text: Dhamaka is an Unapologetic Foods restaurant that immerses diners in the rich, bold flavors of India's forgotten culinary traditions. Nestled in Essex Market on the Lower East Side, the restaurant showcases regional dishes that are often overlooked, offering an authentic experience that is both intensely spiced and deeply rooted in memory. Dhamaka invites guests to explore the powerful stories behind these dishes, creating a dining atmosphere that is unapologetically vibrant and culturally rich. Dhamaka focuses on the provincial cooking of India, emphasizing regional dishes that are rarely seen outside of Indian homes and roadside stalls. The menu features a variety of intensely spiced offerings, including a selection of vegetarian and non-vegetarian options, and highlights signature techniques such as slow braising and grilling. Dhamaka is part of Unapologetic Foods and aims to celebrate the forgotten side of Indian cuisine.

Aged Basmati Rice - (vg, gf) - $4
Paratha - (v) (1 pc) - $4

review_snippets: Exceeded my already high expectations. An excellent dining experience. The biryani is indeed the best ive had, I got the okra dish which I mostly liked I found it a little bit too salty for my taste but the texture of the okra is insane and I would have it again honestly, the side of yogurt helped balance it out a bit. THE CRAB IS A MUSTTTTT. it's like the best cacio e pepe you've ever had in your life but make it crab. And lotsss of it, they do not skimp on the meat but you're still gonna want two of these😂😍 The house made paneer texture is incredible, we got the appetizer version it was delicious with the chutney and onion. As for drinks I was very impressed with they're not alcoholic menu, I did take a gander at the regular cocktail menu and it also looked very delicious and impressive, their lassi is the best I've ever had, it's not mango it's something even better it's like everything you would want from a creamy semi sweet beverage, nothing more nothing less. Utterly perfect it almost was my favorite thing I had and that is saying a lot considering the food was outstandingly good. I also was very happy with their dessert wine section, they feature Kopke for port and a late harvest hungarian sweet wine that i absolutely loveeee. Service was excellent also, and seats are nicely spaced out. Music was cool lots of stuff I've never heard before. Looking forward to my next dining experience here for sure (5 stars)

“Busy” is not the word for this popular Indian spot in Essex Market. It’s just as packed as the sister restaurant, Adda, that recently re-located from Queens. Alex, our waiter, was fantastic and walked us through the menu with his favorites. They also have unique cocktails and a decent wine selection. The cocktail I ordered was a little too sweet and reminded me of mouthwash so I switched it for a glass of wine. We definitely ordered way too much for two people, but every dish was layered with incredible flavor. If you’re not big on spice, ask about the heat level, a dish or two had an extra kick. The Butter Pepper Garlic Crab was my favorite. They level up the presentation by bringing it out in the shell and flipping it at the table. Raita isn’t listed on the menu, but they do have it . Reservations are a must, even if you are planning to sit at the bar. Their dining area is suitable for all size parties. FYI: they’re also participating in Restaurant Week (4 stars)

This place had been on my friend’s must-try dining list since it first opened, but it was always fully booked and reservation-only. Today was finally the day we got to experience it—and it was well worth the wait. The staff, from the maître d’ to the waiters, were genuinely warm and welcoming. A special shout-out to Alex, who was fantastic—patiently explaining the dishes, keeping our water glasses full, and checking in on us throughout the meal. The ambiance is funky and hip, with a unique vibe that doesn’t immediately give away the type of cuisine being served, which I personally loved. The authentic Indian music added an extra layer to the experience and complemented the food beautifully. This is not the place for chicken tikka masala lovers looking for a familiar take. This is real, authentic Indian cuisine (with some selective meat dishes). From the appetizers to the main course—especially the lamb shank for two—everything was flavorful, well-seasoned, and thoughtfully prepared. We both truly enjoyed our time and will definitely be back. Making a reservation is a must. (4 stars)

Hard reservation to land and tucked inside a food market, which made Dhamaka feel like a great find before we even sat down. Top dishes: the beef pepper fry was the standout. Tender, spicy in the best way, served with chutney and onions. The butter pepper crab tasted like a richer shrimp scampi, incredible. The malai murgh had bold butter and spice flavors - crispy onions were excellent, just wish the portion was bigger. We also ordered the paratha and it was perfect for dipping into all the sauces. The balli biryani was huge and could feed four easily. Great presentation, and yes, we ate the bread sealing the pot. Service from Alex was patient and helpful, guiding a table of opinions. Our group eats a lot of Indian food around the city, so this was a bucket list stop. Albarino wine was great with the meal, and the Old Fashioned and beers held up too. Overall a fun, flavorful night with a lot of surprises! (4 stars)

Nestled in Essex Market on the Lower East Side, the restaurant showcases regional dishes that are often overlooked, offering an authentic experience that is both intensely spiced and deeply rooted in memory. Dhamaka invites guests to explore the powerful stories behind these dishes, creating a dining atmosphere that is unapologetically vibrant and culturally rich. Dhamaka focuses on the provincial cooking of India, emphasizing regional dishes that are rarely seen outside of Indian homes and roadside stalls. The menu features a variety of intensely spiced offerings, including a selection of vegetarian and non-vegetarian options, and highlights signature techniques such as slow braising and grilling. Dhamaka is part of Unapologetic Foods and aims to celebrate the forgotten side of Indian cuisine. bio_text: Dim Sum Go Go is a Michelin-rated restaurant located in the heart of Chinatown, New York City, celebrated for its fresh, made-to-order dim sum. With a contemporary ambiance, the restaurant offers a vibrant dining experience that honors traditional Chinese cuisine while incorporating modern twists. Known for its meticulous preparation and high-quality ingredients, Dim Sum Go Go has established itself as a go-to destination for dim sum enthusiasts since its opening in 2000. The restaurant specializes in Cantonese dim sum, featuring a menu that includes delicate dumplings and savory buns. Dishes are crafted with authentic flavors and a focus on freshness, with orders taken by staff rather than traditional carts to ensure quality. Signature items include sweet shrimp wrapped in rice paper and rich duck dumplings. Established in 2000, Dim Sum Go Go has been recognized as the Best Dim Sum in New York City for over 24 years.
menu_items: Fresh Cucumbers with Cellophane Noodles - Lightly pickled cucumbers with sesame seeds and glass noodles - $8
Cold Sesame Noodles with Peanut Sauce - Cold egg noodles (lo mein) with a housemade peanut sauce - $10
Fried Stuffed Eggplant - Sliced Chinese eggplant stuffed with minced shrimp paste - $8
Crispy Tofu stuffed with Shrimp - Tofu with shrimp paste and a housemade garlic vinaigrette - $8
Fried Stuffed Hot Peppers - Fried hot peppers stuffed with minced shrimp paste - $8
Steamed Chinese Broccoli (small) - Freshly steamed Chinese broccoli with oyster sauce on the side - $8
review_snippets: Dim Sum Go Go is a fantastic find, especially considering its reputation as a budget-friendly Michelin-recommended spot. The food quality is exceptional and absolutely lives up to the hype. The standout of the meal was the seafood and meat platter - the colors and shapes were stunning, but the taste was even better. Anything involving the shrimp was simply incredible. We also tried the duck spring rolls, pork soup dumplings, and the Malaysian buns for dessert, all of which were great. A few crucial tips for your visit: Book ahead: The restaurant is very busy, and seating is quite limited inside. Consider Delivery: Because the dining area is small, they seem to prioritize deliveries, so that’s a solid option if you can't get a table. Must-Order: If you go, the platter is a must - it's a showstopper both visually and in flavor. Overall, this is a top-tier recommendation for anyone looking for high-quality dim sum that won't break the bank. (5 stars)

Came here for dim sum during lunch. Ordered the meat and seafood dim sum platter and pork pan fried dumplings. Everything was delicious. That green sauce is addictive. I requested for a single beef dumpling in platter to be substituted with anything else to which they refused. This is such a simple ask but was not accomodated. I just asked them to remove it which they did. Michelin guide yeah, but don't hold your breath for service as it was pretty blunt. (4 stars)

Saw it was on the Michelin bib gourmand list. Ordered the 10 piece platter which was like a sampler plate. Ingredients were fresh and skin was delicate but broke apart too easily. Overall, while some of the items were not typical chinese dim sum items, everything passed the taste test (4 stars)

Fast, helpful service and plenty of food for the price. Our table filled up quickly with steamer baskets, and it was easy to order for a mixed group. There was good variety of vegetarian and meat options. The space is tight and gets busy, and I’m not sure how to explain it other than it felt it catered or drew in a more Americanized crowd. The food wasn’t bad by any means but nothing really stood out either. Not my first choice for dim sum, but a fine option if you’re already in the area. (3 stars)

bio_text: Dirt Candy is a pioneering vegetarian restaurant located in New York City, renowned for its innovative approach to vegetable-centric cuisine. With a Michelin Star, it offers a unique dining experience that transforms the perception of vegetables into something extraordinary. The atmosphere is vibrant and playful, reminiscent of a child's birthday party, where each dish invites guests to explore the depths of flavor and creativity in plant-based cooking. Dirt Candy specializes in a single, seasonal tasting menu that showcases the versatility and potential of vegetables. The restaurant employs avant-garde techniques, including tableside grilling and the use of unusual broths, to elevate the dining experience. The focus is on making vegetables as crave-worthy as traditional comfort foods. Award-winning chef Amanda Cohen leads the kitchen, pushing the boundaries of vegetable cuisine since the restaurant's inception. Dirt Candy is committed to ethical labor practices, ensuring fair wages and benefits for its staff.
menu_items: Brussels Sprout Tacos - Brussels sprouts, Mexican bistek, iceberg lettuce, smoked avocado, pickled red onion, cotija cheese, radishes, crispy brussels sprout leaves, tortilla strips, pickled jalapenos, salsa verde, crema - $110
Spinach Mille Feuille - Spinach puff pastry, spinach mousse, smoked pistachio butter, lilac spinach, dehydrated grapefruit, smoked pistachio salad - $110
Portobello Mousse - Portobello mousse, cherries, Asian pears, truffle toast - $110

Smoked Cabbage Hot Pot - Smoked cabbage broth, ramen noodles, lotus root, ginger kimchi, spicy watermelon radish kimchi, pickled ginger, raw radishes, fresh cilantro, mint, sesame fu, grilled cabbage, sesame braised cabbage, homemade chili oil, black vinegar, soy sauce - $110
Brassica - Ricotta dumplings, pickled purple cauliflower, pernod, pak choi, smoked cabbage broth - $110
Forager's Salad - Wild plants, roots, berries, mushrooms, sea rocket, lambsquarters, lemon balm, anise hyssop, clammy goosefoot - $110
review_snippets: This is such a unique dining experience. Their all vegetarian menu is excellent. The menu can vary, so I can only comment on what we were served. While I liked the entire menu, here are some highlights. We had Brussel sprouts roasted on the stock. This was covered with a slightly spicy sauce. One picked it up with the one’s fingers to eat each sprout. After finishing the sprouts, the stalk was turned over and the soft core was scooped out with a marrow spoon I did not know the core was edible! Root vegetable chips with sauce and a type of coleslaw were delicious. The dessert course featured a spice cake, sorbet and a coconut pudding. This was excellent! The staff are amazingly friendly and helpful in explaining the menu. I will not soon forget our visit and can’t wait to return. (5 stars)

Wonderful dining experience here! The staff was great, the food was excellent. I wasn’t particularly impressed with either one of the soupy dishes; but everything else was unreal. The off-the-menu chips course was sooo addictive. Loved that the tip was already included. Tipping has gotten out of control. We’ll be back! (5 stars)

I’ve been here three times (Winter and Summer previously), and this season’s Fall tasting menu is the best yet. Truly phenomenal, abounding with creative flavor combinations and textures, and genuinely elevating the vegetables that serve as the base. The cauliflower dessert is one of the best desserts I’ve ever had, and the candied beets and curry, the onion tart, and mushroom dish were standout as well. The kitchen always does an amazing job with the surprise dishes too, from radish carpaccio to sesame dumplings. Highly recommend the desert sunrise as an NA cocktail, and try to get a seat at the chef’s counter. Also love a restaurant that pays its workers a living wage and includes gratuity. Please go! (5 stars)

I’m giving Dirt Candy in New York a full five stars, and honestly, it deserves every bit of that rating. The food here is exceptional — creative, flavorful, and executed with real precision. Every dish feels unique, thoughtful, and beautifully balanced. The atmosphere is relaxed but polished, making it an easy place to enjoy a long, satisfying meal without feeling rushed or overwhelmed. One thing I strongly recommend is choosing the wine pairing. Each course comes with a different wine selected specifically to match the flavors of the dish, and they absolutely nail it. The pairings elevate the food instead of overpowering it. You can tell the team put real effort into curating drinks that enhance the entire dining experience. If you’re coming here, don’t skip that option — it’s worth it. The service was outstanding. The staff were attentive, warm, and genuinely enthusiastic about what they were serving. Dirt Candy is a no-tip restaurant, which I respect, but my server took such good care of me that I felt compelled to insist on giving her something extra. It took a bit of convincing, but she eventually accepted it with a big smile, and I could tell it truly made her day. That level of kindness and professionalism deserves recognition. Dirt Candy isn’t just a place to eat — it’s a place to appreciate food. If you’re looking for an excellent dining experience in New York, this spot should be at the top of your list. (5 stars)

bio_text: Don Angie is a critically acclaimed Italian-American restaurant that offers a warm and inviting atmosphere, perfect for enjoying modern interpretations of classic Italian dishes. Founded by chefs Angie Rito and Scott Tacinelli, the restaurant embodies a neighborhood charm while delivering an exceptional dining experience that has garnered numerous accolades, including a Michelin star. The culinary focus at Don Angie is on modern Italian-American cuisine, featuring a creative menu that highlights comforting dishes with a contemporary twist. The restaurant offers a unique take on traditional recipes, including their signature lasagna, and emphasizes high-quality ingredients and innovative cooking techniques. Don Angie was opened in 2017 by chefs Angie Rito and Scott Tacinelli, who both have deep roots in Italian cooking and a shared dream of creating a special neighborhood restaurant. The duo has received multiple nominations from the James Beard Foundation and has been recognized by the New York Times and Esquire for their culinary excellence.
menu_items: Sicilian Saffron, Toasted Almond, Fennel Buttermilk - $34
Blackened Sausage, Capocollo, Anaheim Chilies - $32
Horseradish, Speck, Caraway - $39
Charred, Cured & Confit Lemons - $44
Gigante Beans all'Amatriciana, Red Dandelion - $36
Smoked Vodka Sauce, Spicy Polenta Tortelli, Lobster Polpette - $135
review_snippets: We scored a reservation for 4:15pm for a part of 4. We arrived on time and were seated pretty promptly. Where we were seated initially was pretty cramped and we realized fairly quickly it just wasn’t going to be comfortable for us. When we asked if a larger table that wasn’t so close to neighboring tables might be available we were quickly and graciously accommodated without hesitation. We ordered stuffed flatbread, chrysanthemum salad, buffalo milk caramelle, calamari fried rice, sourdough pasta cacciatore, steak limone, and the ravioli for the table to share for dinner. Our party also shared the tiramisu and pear sorbet for dessert. Everything we ate was a home run, not one bite missed, not even a little. Also worth mentioning, every dish was measurably different from the next, Don Angie plays many notes on our palates it seems. The atmosphere is upscale but not uptight. (5 stars)

As always, Don Angie is the most incredible culinary experience — the food is outstanding, unique, and special. The service is unparalleled and the staff leads all their actions with kindness and attention to the guest experience. It is always such a special occasion to join them for a meal and I certainly hope to be back soon! Dish Highlights: The Japanese sweet potatoes and the chrysanthemum salad are MUST gets. The BBQ calamari were a unique and yummy app. The sourdough pasta cacciatore never disappoints, nor does the shell steak al limone or lasagna for two. (5 stars)

Decent vegetarian options for appetizers / pasta. Was able to grab a seat at the bar when they opened with no res. Cocktails and everything we ordered was very delicious, and fairly quick service. Very nice atmosphere, didn’t feel too crowded / loud despite restaurant being almost at full capacity. Would definitely come back to try more dishes here (: (5 stars)

I was able to get a lunch reservation a week in advance on OpenTable and it was worth it! Everything was delicious and lived up to expectations. We ordered the chrysanthemum salad, calamari w/pepperoni rice, caramelle pasta, and the lasagna to share and everything was beyond expectations. The calamari really surprised us, but the salad is a must order. The lasagna is delicious and the portions are huge. The bread it is served with is amazing. Highly recommend this restaurant as “worth it” if you’re trying to get a reservation: keep trying! (5 stars)

Cocktails and everything we ordered was very delicious, and fairly quick service. Very nice atmosphere, didn’t feel too crowded / loud despite restaurant being almost at full capacity. Would definitely come back to try more dishes here (: (5 stars) I was able to get a lunch reservation a week in advance on OpenTable and it was worth it! Everything was delicious and lived up to expectations. We ordered the chrysanthemum salad, calamari w/pepperoni rice, caramelle pasta, and the lasagna to share and everything was beyond expectations. The calamari really surprised us, but the salad is a must order. The lasagna is delicious and the portions are huge. The bread it is served with is amazing. Highly recommend this restaurant as “worth it” if you’re trying to get a reservation: keep trying! (5 stars)

bio_text: Don Antonio is a celebrated Neapolitan pizzeria located in the vibrant heart of Midtown Manhattan, specifically in Hell’s Kitchen and the Theatre District. The restaurant prides itself on delivering authentic Neapolitan pizza, crafted in a traditional wood-fired oven, ensuring a genuine taste of Naples. With a casual, welcoming atmosphere, Don Antonio offers a diverse menu that includes classic pizzas, unique pizza fritta, and a selection of Italian craft beers and wines, making it a go-to destination for pizza enthusiasts. Don Antonio specializes in authentic Neapolitan pizza, featuring over 30 varieties crafted with high-quality Italian ingredients. The menu includes traditional pizzas and innovative pizza fritta, all available in gluten-free options. The pizzas are baked at 850°F in a wood-fired oven, achieving a perfect balance of crispness and softness. Founded in 2012 by renowned chefs Roberto Caporuscio and Antonio Starita, Don Antonio is now led by Giorgia Caporuscio, an award-winning master pizzaiola. Giorgia has received numerous accolades, including being named Pizza Maker of the Year by 50 Top Pizza USA in 2024.
menu_items: burrata & Caponata - imported organic burrata from Puglia, marinated red & yellow bell peppers, roasted eggplant, baby kale, sun-dried tomatoes, olives, crispy peperone crusco
Mozzarella e prosciutto - fresh mozzarella, prosciutto di Parma, basil

Panzanella di Bufala - lightly fried gluten-free pizza dough croutons, heirloom farm tomatoes, sun-dried tomatoes, cucumbers, olives, pickled red onions, basil, fresh oregano, 4oz imported mozzarella di bufala
Ricotta & Indivia - local whipped ricotta, white and red endive, arugula, brussels sprouts, pecorino cheese, balsamic dressing
arancini al pomodoro - two riceballs with tomato sauce, fresh mozzarella, and cream of cacio e pepe
crocchette di patate al limone - two fried potato croquettes, imported smoked buffalo mozzarella, lemon zest
review_snippets: A true gem of NYC vibes!! I came without a reservation on, what seemed a pack night, but we were able to sit in the next 10 mins as the service is very quick and efficient. We dined before going to a Broadway show and it was PERFECT!! The pizzas came incredibly fast and were so good. In and out with dessert included in basically 45 mins. Highly recommended!! Ps: Don’t you dare to skip the Nutella Pizza! 🤎 (5 stars)

Insane! The pizza was off the chain. The fresh sauce and mozzarella were bursting with flavor. Basil...yum!Definitely more New York style crust. Different from the crispy New Haven style that I'm more used to. I only cut a star because it was just so cramped. They packed us in like sardines. Worth it though. I couldn't recommend any more highly. (5 stars)

Having a pizza from a world champion pizza maker is a unique experience. We enjoyed every bite of every pie we tried!!! Thanks Giorgia for such an amazing xmas taste gift!!! You should try the diavola and the fried pizza (5 stars)

A beautiful American Italian restaurant in the heart of midtown. Gluten-free options are available and clearly marked on the menu. The gluten-free pizza is excellent, the dough taste just as regular one does. The restaurant can get loud when all tables are filled, the bar area is quieter, even though it’s at the front of the restaurant. The staff is friendly and the food is fast even when the restaurant is full. (5 stars)

bio_text: Dons Bogam Wine Bar & BBQ offers an authentic Korean dining experience in a beautifully designed space located in the heart of New York City. With floor-level seating and tabletop grills, guests can enjoy a unique atmosphere while watching skilled chefs prepare traditional Korean dishes in an open kitchen. The restaurant prides itself on delivering the rich flavors of Korea through a diverse menu that caters to all palates. Dons Bogam specializes in traditional Korean cuisine, featuring a menu that includes BBQ specialties and classic dishes such as Galbi, Bulgogi, and Bibimbap. The dining format includes both a la carte options and lunch specials, allowing for a flexible dining experience.
menu_items: Yuk Gae Jang - Spicy beef soup with vegetables - $21.95
Kimchi Stew - Kimchi, tofu, pork, and vegetables - $21.95
Galbitang - Beef short rib soup with radish - $20.00
Spicy Fish Stew - Fish, vegetables, and spicy broth - $21.95
Kimchi Dumpling Stew - Dumplings, kimchi, and vegetables - $21.95
Sundubu Jjigae - Soft tofu stew with seafood or meat - $21.95
review_snippets: Some friends brought us to dinner here. It was an amazing experience. The food was incredible & the service was great also. We had pork dumplings & shrimp shumae for appetizers. For dinner we had the marinated chicken & the ribeye. Both meats were delicious. The chicken literally melted in your mouth. (5 stars)

If you’re craving Korean BBQ in the city, this spot is a must. The Prime Marinated Beef Platter was packed with flavor and cooked perfectly at the tabletop grill. We also loved the crispy kimchi pajeon, the kkaenip bulgogi, and the comforting kimchi jjigae. The house-infused lychee soju was a standout. They’re also running a promo free Korean stew with any beef platter which makes the experience even better. (5 stars)

Well known kbbq spot near ktown offering pricey, but delicious marinated meats, casseroles and more. Started with half a dozen banchan, there is a variety of meat set options for the table to choose from or a la carte. The items are cooked by staff so the usual designated kbbq chef can relax and eat😆. Seating is a bit cramped, and can be an issue for people with accessibility problems. Blue handball is used to hold the burner controls, very random. (5 stars)

At Nubiani (half a block away) you eat better, for less money, and they even give you a free dessert. The platter came without the usual Korean stew and egg, and on top of that they didn’t bring the rice, which was the only thing that was actually included in the platter besides the side dishes — we had to ask for it halfway through dinner. Once you’re done eating, they completely forget about you — good luck trying to get the check. To make matters worse, a 25% tip is automatically added and you’re not allowed to change it. The meat itself is good, but I’d recommend going somewhere else where you get more (and better) food for the same price. (2 stars)

bio_text: Dubrovnik Restaurant in New Rochelle, NY, offers an authentic Croatian dining experience that transports guests to the heart of Croatia. With a warm and inviting atmosphere, the restaurant features both indoor and outdoor seating, allowing diners to enjoy their meals in a setting reminiscent of a seaside escape. The establishment prides itself on exceptional service and a commitment to showcasing the rich culinary traditions of Croatia. Dubrovnik specializes in classic Croatian cuisine, focusing on succulent meat roasts and fresh grilled seafood. The menu includes traditional dishes prepared using age-old techniques, such as the 'peka' method of slow-cooking. Guests can expect a variety of seafood options, including daily fresh catches and signature dishes like grilled octopus and lamb chops. Dubrovnik Restaurant was founded with the goal of providing customers with classic Croatian cuisine in a warm, friendly atmosphere. It is the first authentic Croatian restaurant in Westchester, established to bring the flavors of Croatia to New Rochelle.
menu_items: Crispy Calamari - With homemade tartar sauce. - $13.00
Shrimp 'Raznjici' - $13.00
Spring Rolls - With beef tenderloin, pine nuts and julienne vegetables, spicy tartar dip. - $13.00
Octopus Salad - Steamed octopus with capers, red onion, potatoes, fresh baby arugula in extra virgin olive oil and red wine vinegar. - $13.00
Shellfish 'Buzara' - Little neck clams and mussels in white wine and garlic, finished with extra virgin olive oil and parsley. - $12.00
Caesar Salad - Chopped romaine lettuce with croutons and parmesan shavings. - $8.00
review_snippets: Dubrovnik is one of those rare places where dining is an experience, not just eating out. First, I was surprised to see that this place has dedicated parking for guests - rarest of the rare for someone from NYC! The host was super quick to offer a table and help us with their best seasonal offerings. Their seafood menu is one of the best in the region. Whether you like oysters or fish, you're not gonna be disappointed. The drinks are prepped with attention to detail as well. I had Sangria, and it was so good I had a repeat. The place maintains high hygiene standards. After dining in hundreds of restaurants in NYC, for the first time, I witnessed a restaurant replace the tablecloth after it's been used. What deserves a special mention? The food and hygiene standards just make this one of the best places to dine. What could be better? Nothing for now - they're doing a great job! (5 stars)

I visit Dubrovnik Restaurant about four or five times a year, and it never disappoints. The parking can be quite difficult, so I highly recommend using the valet service to start your evening comfortably. This place offers a level of Croatian cuisine that is hard to find in the NY/NJ area. Their philosophy is clearly about respecting the ingredients. The wood-grilled Branzino is exceptional; the fire gives it a subtle sweetness and the texture is perfect. We also enjoyed the Lamb Chops and Aged Rib Eye Steak, both cooked beautifully. The appetizers are always fresh and vibrant. The Marinated Anchovies and Nona’s Octopus Salad had great texture with no fishiness. I particularly love the Pear and Apple Salad—the crisp fruit provides a wonderful balance to the savory dishes. The Cuttlefish Risotto is served perfectly al dente, rich with flavor but not heavy. The service is generally skilled and attentive. We did have a small mix-up where a server mistook soy sauce for black vinegar, but it was an understandable mistake that didn't affect our enjoyment of the meal. The wine list is a real highlight, especially the Croatian selections. We had the Stina Cuvée by the glass; it was excellent for the price, with enough acidity to pair perfectly with the seafood. It’s a dining experience I always look forward to returning to. (5 stars)

This was a delightful Croatian dining experience. Admittedly, while enjoyable, I wasn't blown away. I liked the free valet parking, as parking can be difficult in this area. The atmosphere was very noisy, making it difficult to carry on a conversation. While I enjoyed the 2 piece live band, they too were quite loud. My meal itself was very good, but not spectacular. I started with the chicken soup. I enjoyed the large pieces of tender chicken in a savory broth, but didn't find this to be much different from any non-Croatian chicken soup. For my main, I had the stuffed chicken breast with asparagus. The chicken was tasty, but surprisingly was a bit tough. Lastly, for dessert, we shared the palacinke with walnut cream. It was creamy and delicious, and was a nice way to wrap up the meal. Others in my party ordered the Branzino and had a much more positive dining experience. I suppose if you dine here, you might be better off with the seafood options. (4 stars)
Great food and service! The appetizers have really large portions, almost like a main course portion. All delicious! (5 stars)

bio_text: East Harbor Seafood Palace is a celebrated Chinese restaurant located in Brooklyn, NY, known for its vibrant atmosphere and exceptional dim sum offerings. With a legacy spanning decades, the restaurant has evolved from a modest eatery into a cornerstone of the community, renowned for its commitment to authenticity and quality in Cantonese cuisine. The bustling environment, particularly on weekends, reflects the restaurant's popularity, where guests can enjoy a diverse selection of meticulously crafted dim sum dishes served from traditional carts, ensuring a memorable dining experience. East Harbor Seafood Palace specializes in authentic Cantonese cuisine, with a particular focus on traditional dim sum. The menu features a variety of classic dim sum items, including steamed shrimp dumplings and pork buns, presented in a communal style that encourages sharing. Signature techniques include the use of dim sum carts for service, allowing diners to select from an array of freshly prepared dishes. The restaurant has been a staple in the community for decades, initially gaining traction for its exceptional dim sum. Over the years, it has undergone renovations to enhance its appeal while maintaining its dedication to excellent service and cultural authenticity.
menu_items: Siu Mai - Pork, shrimp, and seasonings wrapped in a delicate dumpling skin - $16
Steamed Shrimp Dumplings - Shrimp wrapped in a translucent dumpling skin - $16
Zongzi - Sticky rice, pork, and mushrooms wrapped in tea leaves - $12
Peking Duck - Duck served with thin pancakes, hoisin sauce, and scallions - $32
Pan Fried Noodles - Noodles stir-fried with vegetables and choice of meat or seafood - $18
Roast Pork Buns - Fluffy buns filled with savory, sweet pork - $10
review_snippets: A 12 degrees evening before the anticipated arrival of the first big ice and snow storm of 2026 and wanted to have "last meal" of sorts before the great hibernation. We had 5 lobsters-split broiled, braised abalone-sea cucumber-shitake, a giant steamed branzino (live from the on-site fish tank), dried scallop fried rice, braised crab yee-noodles, cold platter with suckling pig, beef, pickled vegetables and jellyfish, a sautéed seafood dish with sugar snap peas-squid-conch, chicken-abalone soup, fried chicken, fried crab claw with shrimp, deserts were a fruit platter and also sweet red bean soup. Service was quick, but very, very rushed. Dishes came out every 5 minutes and were served and distributed. The next dish arrived before the current one could be finished and they brought us plastic boxes to pack what we couldn't finish. Food quality was fresh, but not particularly flavorful, slightly overcooked as seafood needs to be pretty exact. Difficult to stay fully booked in the current economy, but the entire restaurant of about 400 seats, was filled, as well as the private rooms, on this evening. (3 stars)

Came here before and it was very good. Today’s visit was on New Year’s Day so it was super chaotic. We waited about 30-40 mins for a table for 8. The carts moved quickly and we were able to get what we wanted almost immediately. There were a few items we had to wait for. Today they didn’t have turnip cake. Some waiters were very helpful and scouted the dimsum items we wanted and ordered additional items. Others were typical and brushed us off. Any ordered food takes very long. They also have Hong Kong milk tea. Service is in Cantonese. Didn’t notice if they were super quick to help in English. (4 stars)

Pretty good dim sum, bookmarked this place for a while since my friend recommended it. A little bit far to get to in brooklyn's chinatown. Expect to wait before you get seats. I didn't see that many carts that went around, might be because we got there a little closer to 12:30pm, busy even on a weekday during lunch. You might want to ask them for the menu to bring the food out if the carts don't come by. I think the food is flavorful, but the service was a little bit questionable since we were waiting for the carts to come by for a while and it didn't feel like there was a lot of variety. There were definitely more items on the menu that they didn't bring out. Overall, I think it's good place to try once, I'm not sure if I would be back again. (4 stars)

It serves really authentic and traditional push cart style dim sum at all hours. Do expect a queue on weekend. You will also find extra ordinary and non typical dim sum dishes that please your appetite such as beef offal and pepper beef ribs. (4 stars)

bio_text: El Fish Marisquería is a vibrant seafood restaurant located on the Upper West Side of New York City, offering a unique blend of Mexican-inspired dishes. The restaurant features a thoughtfully designed interior that reflects an oceanic theme, creating a serene dining atmosphere that invites guests to enjoy a culinary journey through the flavors of the sea. The restaurant specializes in Mexican-inspired seafood, focusing on both traditional and innovative dishes. The menu is influenced by Chef Julian Medina's culinary exploration in Ensenada, Mexico, and emphasizes fresh, high-quality ingredients sourced from local markets. review_snippets: Absolutely delicious food! The ingredients were fresh and high quality. Flavors with so much depth you couldn't quite remember the entire experience of tasting it, and wanted to keep having more. They could be vibrant and delightfully surprising as well. I wish I knew how they pulled it off, but I didn't think I'd get away with sneaking into the kitchen to watch! The dishes were a treat for the eye as well. The best items we got were the Enchiladas De Camaron, Cob Seafood Caesar, and best of all, the Brochetas De Salmon Kung Pao. The only thing that was disappointing was the Chilaquiles. My party shared everything so we all got to experience more of their cooking. The salmon in the Brochetas De Salmon Kung Pao was perfectly cooked and amazingly fresh. It easily flaked under a fork, the texture was almost creamy. The creamy Mexican rice was good on its own, but came with a caramel-colored sauce with a light zing that made it hard to stop eating it! The Cob Seafood Caesar had a wonderful interplay of flavors and textures. Tomatoes and avocado were so fresh they shone on their own. The gentle vinegar on the tomatoes helped make the flavor pop without overwhelming the tomato. Fun chewy pieces of savory meat. The Enchiladas De Camaron came drenched in a beautiful orange sauce. Perfectly uniform coloration that's hard to achieve at home. The enchiladas were soft with a lovely bite to the (shredded?) shrimp inside. Wonderful depth of flavor. It's like they put all the effort into the food and none into the advertising. This might be the second time I've ever written a review, but the food was so amazing it's a pity no one knows about this place. The outside of the restaurant is nondescript, with a small sign saying "El Fish" far above eye level. You just see the large window with mostly empty tables and an indoor plant inside. The ambiance was wonderful. It was quiet and calm. We could talk easily. Lots of natural sunlight, airy open space, soft tones on the walls. (5 stars)

We came here to celebrate my mom’s birthday but imagine the first impression upon entering is to be greeted by someone with a disgusting attitude and zero manners. He pretended not to hear me when I told him I had a reservation and instead of saying “I’m sorry I can’t hear you” he says "huh." It’s clear that I’m not the only person who has felt this way about this individual and you can see other reviews pointing out his horrendous attitude. It's the male manager with the hat that is mentioned in multiple other reviews. I’m surprised he’s still employed, it's incredibly surprising that an individual with such a terrible attitude holds a position where you interact with paying customers. I will echo that the rest of the wait staff was incredibly friendly and I am sorry that they need to work alongside this individual. You can see their discomfort when he is around and I'm sure it is a toxic work environment that should be investigated. The food itself was subpar and though creative lacks flavor. My recommendation is to stay away from this place. We will not be coming back. (1 stars)

Elevated Mexican dishes on the upper west side. Food is a little slow to come out but the service and atmosphere are lovely. The Cob Caesar salad is very generously portioned and filled with seafood - highly recommended! (5 stars)

The food in this restaurant is pretty good. the atmosphere is pretty good, but keep in mind. You are in the upper west, so the crowd was mostly older people, but still with good vibe. Overall, at dinner, the restaurant was almost full. I wish that you would have more privacy. many tables are just 2 people, one next to the other. So you hear Everyone's conversation, so some lack of privacy, the cocktail where good the Margarita, the chef's Margarita, it was good. The mule was just okay, and the service was okay as well. Nothing too exciting. I wish they would pay more attention to our requests. Also they suggested more food than we could consume. So we had a lot of leftovers are on the table. (4 stars)

bio_text: Eleven Madison Park is a distinguished fine dining restaurant located in the heart of New York City, offering a unique culinary experience with a view of Madison Square Park. Owned and operated by Chef Daniel Humm, the restaurant is housed in a historic Art Deco building and is known for its elegant atmosphere and exceptional service. The dining experience is centered around a fully plant-based tasting menu, with the option to include select animal proteins, reflecting a commitment to sustainability and seasonal ingredients. The restaurant specializes in a fully plant-based tasting menu, showcasing hyper-seasonal produce sourced from their partner, Magic Farms. Guests can also enjoy a bar menu featuring à la carte snacks, wine, and cocktails, allowing for a more casual dining experience. Owned and operated by Chef Daniel Humm, Eleven Madison Park introduced a fully plant-based tasting menu in 2021 and has since evolved to offer options that include select animal proteins.
review_snippets: Eleven Madison Park redefined what fine dining means in New York and then redefined it again when they went fully plant-based. Daniel Humm took one of the most celebrated tasting menus in the world and rebuilt it from scratch without animal products and somehow made it even more creative. The multi-course experience is a journey through technique presentation and flavor that challenges everything you think you know about vegetables grains and fruits. Each course arrives like a small piece of art and tastes even better than it looks. The sunflower butter with sourdough bread is so good that it could be the entire meal and you would leave satisfied. The dining room overlooking Madison Square Park is one of the most beautiful restaurant spaces in the city high ceilings natural light and an energy that is both serious and joyful. The service is beyond anything I have experienced elsewhere every member of the team is knowledgeable passionate and genuinely invested in your experience. They explain each dish with enthusiasm that is contagious. The wine and beverage pairings are inventive and perfectly matched. This is a restaurant that asks you to trust the kitchen and rewards that trust completely. Whether you agree with the plant-based direction or not you cannot deny the ambition and execution. Eleven Madison Park is not just a restaurant it is a statement about what food can be when creativity has no ceiling. (5 stars)

As a Michelin Star restaurant lover I was looking forward to try 11 Madison. Unfortunately the food was either too salty, or too plain, lobster dish was just fine but we didn’t enjoy any other dish ( we took both regular and vegan menu to try). I’m honestly very confused how this restaurant received any Michelin star. On top of that they low key ruined the birthday we booked to celebrate. It was such a long boring service with little knowledge of what they were serving with long wait between meal. Drinks were fine but didn’t compliment the food which is not ok for the price of the restaurant. When they asked how was our experience at the end - we mentioned that the birthday was not celebrated they said they ran out of candles sorry. What a lame excuse for $1000 dinner, you’re in Manhattan - go buy a candle from any pharmacy nearby!! The desert was shaved ice in the coldest winter ever in NYC ,they offered us tea before serving dessert which obviously won’t go with shaved ice! I get they want to sale the tea but offer something that goes with the desert at least! Beware and don’t waste your time and money. Better go to - Le Bernardin - it delivers what 11 Madison promises. (1 stars)

Likely the most amazing dinner you'll have. Every course was to die for; the staff was beyond perfect. Do not fear, carnivores, their vegan items will astound and delight you! There's a few courses where you have the choice between a plant-based dish like the rest of the menu and an animal protein dish. We got both, and though the animal proteins were still amazing, I felt the plant based dishes stacked up slightly better. (5 stars)

Good experience, but not even close to worth the cost of the dinner. The food was very good, and the service was very good as well, but neither were to the standard that we expected for what was voted the best restaurant in the world. The sommelier talked us into a wine that was around double the price of a bottle we were looking at and it was just decent. He also promised us a glass of the cheaper wine we were looking at, but we never received that, and by the time we asked to speak with him he was gone. Besides the bread, which was the best bread I have ever had in my life, nothing else left a lasting positive impression on me. The kitchen tour, which we had to ask for, was pretty cool, but the kitchen tour at Alenia in Chicago is far and above a better experience. For a place that prides itself on customer service, it seemed as if you were bothering people to ask for things. I was even dumb enough to leave a 20% tip on top of my meal (maybe it was the overpriced wine bottle), and it seemed as if the staff was still learning. The one thing I would give them is if they did not know something they would not lie to you, but they would ask others. It was also cool to see how they move around the room in patterns. Unless they greatly improve, I think that there are much better dining experiences in the city for much more reasonable prices. (3 stars)

bio_text: Eléa is an upscale Greek restaurant located on the Upper West Side of New York City, designed to evoke the ambiance of a romantic island getaway. With its open split-level layout adorned with traditional Grecian pottery and a cozy Mediterranean aesthetic, Eléa offers a warm and inviting dining experience that caters to both casual diners and those seeking a more formal meal. The restaurant's atmosphere is enhanced by soft lighting and a contemporary decor that reflects the essence of Greek culture. Eléa specializes in modern Greek cuisine, focusing on bold flavors derived from seasonal ingredients. The menu features approachable dishes, including seafood and meat preparations, as well as a variety of traditional spreads known as Pikilia. Signature offerings include Tuna Tartare, Octopus, and a selection of daily whole fish. Meaning 'olive' in ancient Greek, Eléa aims to blend true Greek cuisine with a modern twist, creating a unique dining experience that reflects the diverse flavors of Greece's many islands.

review_snippets: Went for a birthday dinner and it was amazing. They spoiled the whole party and brought out a huge sparkler for my boyfriend. The staff was attentive, accommodating and nice. On top of that the food was amazing. We all shared or plates and I really loved everything I ate. The lavraki and white fish appetizer were my favorites ❤️ Plus dessert 🤤 delicious (5 stars)

We came to this restaurant for a birthday celebration and upon entering it immediately brought back pleasant memories from our vacation in Greece this past summer. The staff greeted us warmly and with excitement. We had multiple appetizers and entrées, being that we were a party of five, which you can see from the pictures below. Our waitress was amazing, the food was exquisite, and I would definitely recommend this place to everyone! (5 stars)

Went for their winter restaurant week (muni only available on Friday for lunch). It is definitely great value , portion to price wise. The phyllo was ok but my main sea bass was well cooked, skin is crispy , capers accompanied well with the taste, sauce is tangy and lovely on top. Vibe is chilled, decoration is elegant, low noise. (4 stars)
My husband and I celebrated Valentine's Day here. The restaurant had a wonderful atmosphere, with roses on every table, and the staff were exceptionally friendly：） (4 stars)

bio_text: Enoteca Maria is a unique dining experience located in Staten Island, where the culinary traditions of grandmothers from around the world come to life. This restaurant serves as a platform for senior women to share their authentic heritage through food, creating a warm and inclusive atmosphere that fosters intergenerational connections and cultural understanding. The restaurant not only offers a meal but also a heartfelt journey into the rich tapestry of global culinary traditions. The restaurant focuses on authentic, home-cooked dishes from various cultures, prepared by grandmothers who take turns in the kitchen. The menu is a rotating selection of traditional recipes that highlight the culinary heritage of the women involved, emphasizing the importance of cultural preservation and community spirit. Founded in 2007 by Jody Scaravella in honor of his mother and grandmother, Enoteca Maria has evolved from a personal tribute into a global movement celebrating grandmotherly wisdom. The restaurant's story was further popularized by the Netflix film 'Nonnas' in 2025, which showcases the emotional journey behind its founding.
menu_items: Sri Lankan Cutlet - Delicious vegetable croquettes filled with a great blend of seasonal vegetables and traditional spices. - $18
Hoppers with Chicken Curry - Popular crepe like bowls made from rice flour and coconut milk. Includes three plain hoppers and one egg hopper. Served with delicious traditional chicken curry. - $30
Sri Lankan Noodles - Authentic Sri Lankan noodle dish with mixed vegetables, served with red lentil curry and mango curry. - $28

Harvest Salad - Roasted beet salad with strawberries and crumbled feta cheese served on bedded mixed greens, drizzled with a red wine vinaigrette. Topped with candied walnuts, oranges and fresh parsley.
Insalata del Giardino - Mixed greens with cucumbers, radish, tomatoes, and onions in a flavorful light vinaigrette.
Peperoni Ripieni Piccanti - Long hot peppers stuffed with seasoned pork, cheese and breadcrumbs served with roasted potatoes. *very spicy*
review_snippets: Absolutely, undeniably, incredibly spectacular!! We had 7:30PM reservations on 12/27 with two adults and three kids. Joe was so nice and kind; he knew us by name because we made the reservation directly with him. Nonna Maria herself greeted us and told us a bit about her. She was delightful! We ordered her perfectly made meatballs and scrumptious lasagna. We also ordered from the Puerto Rican menu (fried fish cod — it was delicious). The food was fantastic, the wait staff precise and friendly and the atmosphere was everything we expected. Our recommendation is to contact them via phone because reservations are always needed (and rightfully so — the food and people are amazing). This is worth every penny and we will be coming back again! Remember!! It’s cash only! Thank you Joe & company! (5 stars)

We came in during the snowstorm getting lucky calling for a last minute reservation. If you have not been here please go. What a idea to have different foods prepared by Nonnas. A delicious opportunity to try unique dishes from all over the world. The service was just beyond warm and inviting. I cannot wait to come back- already looking at the Nonnas calendar. YUMIKO thank you for coming and chatting with us- the chicken Katsu just wow- it was a privilege to meet you. We loved seeing you in the kitchen prepping!! Everyone there was lovely. The burrata was so beyond creamy, basil so fresh, the meatballs were like my grandma made them - really I do not have enough words for this review !!!! Please go try. Staten Island gem. (5 stars)

I first heard about this place from a documentary, then saw the movie last year, had to make sure I got over to Staten Island for a bite. The food offered today was Italian, Japanese and Sri Lankan. It all looked amazing. The owner is still taking non-stop calls for reservations. I was lucky to have gotten in since I came in on my own. I was sat at the counter and enjoyed watching all of the hustle and bustle in this cozy kitchen. The size helps you feel like you're waiting for your Mama to finish cooking your meal as you watch. I ordered the lasagna which was very good, but really, the star of the meal was the fresh banana pudding. Never have I enjoyed such a delicious, creamy, well-balanced and fresh pudding. It was divine. The cost is a little high but it is so worth it for the freshness. They serve some alcohols but they offer good pairings for the meals offered. I am so happy to have been able to enjoy this meal I had waited so long for. They only take cash and for now reservations are done in person or by phone. From what I heard they will soon have an online platform to do these. Also, they only take reservations on a rolling, monthly basis. If you get to go, I hope you enjoy it too. (5 stars)

The heart warming film staring an amazing cast made us want to come here to see it in ‘real life’ all the way from the UK 🇬🇧 It did not disappoint. We were greeted by the fabulous owner ‘Joey’ and we got to meet today’s ‘Nonnas’ who were cooking. The food was of the highest quality and the service was second to none. We had the Mozzarella starter which was beautifully presented and tasted superb. For mains we had the lasagna and meatballs again absolutely top notch! THIS FOOD IS MADE WITH LOVE ❤️ and that’s the difference……. The wine is of excellent quality and it truly represents great value for money 💰 The service again gets a 10 out of 10 for us so well done 👏 We enjoy good food and wine and Nonnas was as good if not better than anything we could ask for! Thank you Joey for your beautiful concept and following your dreams! You are an inspiration. (5 stars)
