Served with delicious traditional chicken curry. - $30 Sri Lankan Noodles - Authentic Sri Lankan noodle dish with mixed vegetables, served with red lentil curry and mango curry. - $28 Harvest Salad - Roasted beet salad with strawberries and crumbled feta cheese served on bedded mixed greens, drizzled with a red wine vinaigrette. Topped with candied walnuts, oranges and fresh parsley. Insalata del Giardino - Mixed greens with cucumbers, radish, tomatoes, and onions in a flavorful light vinaigrette. Peperoni Ripieni Piccanti - Long hot peppers stuffed with seasoned pork, cheese and breadcrumbs served with roasted potatoes. *very spicy* Absolutely, undeniably, incredibly spectacular!! We had 7:30PM reservations on 12/27 with two adults and three kids. Joe was so nice and kind; he knew us by name because we made the reservation directly with him. Nonna Maria herself greeted us and told us a bit about her. She was delightful! We ordered her perfectly made meatballs and scrumptious lasagna. We also ordered from the Puerto Rican menu (fried fish cod — it was delicious). The food was fantastic, the wait staff precise and friendly and the atmosphere was everything we expected. Our recommendation is to contact them via phone because reservations are always needed (and rightfully so — the food and people are amazing). This is worth every penny and we will be coming back again! Remember!! It’s cash only! Thank you Joe & company! (5 stars) We came in during the snowstorm getting lucky calling for a last minute reservation. If you have not been here please go. What a idea to have different foods prepared by Nonnas. A delicious opportunity to try unique dishes from all over the world. The service was just beyond warm and inviting. I cannot wait to come back- already looking at the Nonnas calendar. YUMIKO thank you for coming and chatting with us- the chicken Katsu just wow- it was a privilege to meet you. We loved seeing you in the kitchen prepping!! Everyone there was lovely. The burrata was so beyond creamy, basil so fresh, the meatballs were like my grandma made them - really I do not have enough words for this review !!!! Please go try. Staten Island gem. (5 stars) I first heard about this place from a documentary, then saw the movie last year, had to make sure I got over to Staten Island for a bite. The food offered today was Italian, Japanese and Sri Lankan. It all looked amazing. The owner is still taking non-stop calls for reservations. I was lucky to have gotten in since I came in on my own. I was sat at the counter and enjoyed watching all of the hustle and bustle in this cozy kitchen. The size helps you feel like you're waiting for your Mama to finish cooking your meal as you watch. I ordered the lasagna which was very good, but really, the star of the meal was the fresh banana pudding. Never have I enjoyed such a delicious, creamy, well-balanced and fresh pudding. It was divine. The cost is a little high but it is so worth it for the freshness. They serve some alcohols but they offer good pairings for the meals offered. I am so happy to have been able to enjoy this meal I had waited so long for. They only take cash and for now reservations are done in person or by phone. From what I heard they will soon have an online platform to do these. Also, they only take reservations on a rolling, monthly basis. If you get to go, I hope you enjoy it too. (5 stars) The heart warming film staring an amazing cast made us want to come here to see it in ‘real life’ all the way from the UK 🇬🇧 It did not disappoint. We were greeted by the fabulous owner ‘Joey’ and we got to meet today’s ‘Nonnas’ who were cooking. The food was of the highest quality and the service was second to none. We had the Mozzarella starter which was beautifully presented and tasted superb. For mains we had the lasagna and meatballs again absolutely top notch! THIS FOOD IS MADE WITH LOVE ❤️ and that’s the difference……. The wine is of excellent quality and it truly represents great value for money 💰 The service again gets a 10 out of 10 for us so well done 👏 We enjoy good food and wine and Nonnas was as good if not better than anything we could ask for! Thank you Joey for your beautiful concept and following your dreams! You are an inspiration. (5 stars)

bio_text: Ensō Omakase is a culinary sanctuary that embodies the principles of Zen philosophy, focusing on enlightenment, strength, and elegance. The restaurant offers a unique dining experience rooted in respect for tradition, nature, and sustainability. Each dish is meticulously crafted, reflecting a commitment to balance and integrity, while showcasing the rich flavors of Baja's local harvests and responsibly sourced seafood. The restaurant specializes in Edomae sushi, a traditional Japanese style that emphasizes using only the freshest local ingredients. The omakase menu is a curated experience that highlights seasonal produce and seafood, prepared with techniques that honor both heritage and sustainability. Signature practices include composting organic waste and utilizing 110-year-old ice boxes for ingredient preservation. Chef Rob Ruiz brings a wealth of experience, including three years of classic French training, five years in Hawaiian Regional Cuisine, and an apprenticeship with Master Sushi Chef Etsuji Umezu. He has over 15 years of sushi experience and has been cooking in Valle de Guadalupe for more than a decade.
review_snippets: Have dined at Enso three times with family, and have loved the experience each time. We only have experience with the countertop menu so I can’t speak to the lounge menu and its service. The fish is the freshest we’ve had in New York, and the overall level of professionalism and dedication to omakase is next to none. The service by Chef Nick Wang and his team is impeccable and we always have a great time here. Highly recommend if you’d like to have an omakase experience that’s akin to one you’d find in Japan. (5 stars)

Just want to start off by saying the ambiance was impeccable unfortunately i cant say the same for the omakase. For some reason 3 out of the 4 tastings the fish kept tasting fishier. I’m not sure if that’s their way of trying to stand out but it was extremely unpleasant. We had the omakase tasting in the lounge room and even the waiter said this is the fishiest fish but no worries the ginger on top will mask the taste. I didn’t believe him until my friend had to try it first and let me tell you she had to force herself to swallow it. I also just googled that fresh fish should not taste fishy. Unless the fish was poorly handled. I’ve been to plenty of omakase places and never had I ever tasted the fishiest fish. We waited about 20 minutes in between each course for the next to come. We left starving and went across the street to Lucy’s :/ But overall the ambiance once again was amazing. The interior designer had great taste. (1 stars)

I went the other day after booking the omakase experience. I have to say, stunning. I got there a little early for the 6pm session, and was seated at the bar while the chefs got ready. The whiskey selection is incredible and unique, the wine and sake are plentiful and the cocktails are carefully constructed. I was seat at a bar setup with three others and proceeded to have the time of my life. Both chefs were fun, lovely and knowledgeable. All the dishes were crafted with a kind of skill that you have to see to believe. I thoroughly enjoyed myself and am already recommending this place. I understand why Michelin is eyeing this place (5 stars)

Such an incredible meal and experience that transports you out of Brooklyn. We booked the Chefs Counter and while it's a bit pricey, 100% worth it. Every single bite was packed with flavor. The hospitality was remarkable and made everything that much more enjoyable. Looking forward to my next visit already! (5 stars)

Croquetas de gallina
Pintxo matrimonio
Tosta de gambas
Croquetas de jamón
Tartaletas de Txangurro
review_snippets: Side notes- Prices aren't online, and the menu changes frequently. In general, as of a few months ago, the pintxos/bites are $14 to $16, the entradas/appetizers are mostly in the low or mid-$20s, and the platos/entrees are mostly in the $30s and $40s. Anyway, I was at this dimly lit Basque restaurant a while back with a small group. The place got pretty loud eventually, and the service was friendly. As we were waiting, I had some time to kill and ordered a tasty vermut. In this case, it was the Lustao Blanco for $16 on the rocks with an olive. In terms of small bites/Pintxos, someone ordered the Gildas for $14 while waiting, and another person enjoyed the similarly tiny Croquetas de Jamón for the same price point. Speaking of prices, I am unsure exactly how much everything cost, and I can't find descriptions of everything I ate, so I'm approximating, which is why you'll see the "~" before each price point. My entrada, or appetizer, was the Salmorejo de Atún for ~$25. Salmorejo is essentially a much thicker version of gazpacho, with olive oil, tomato, bread, and a few other ingredients. In this case, it was topped with plenty of raw tuna, cucumbers, and other greens. The cold soup worked surprisingly well with the high-quality fatty tuna, and I would order this again if I came back here. Another person ordered one of the appetizers as their entree, the Bikini Hemingway, which is a type of sandwich. In this case, it was ~$25 and was filled with txistorra, queso, shrimp, and pan de cristal. They seemed to like it but not love it. My main dish/plato was, unfortunately, the Magret de Pato for ~$40, with grilled magret duck breast, port and foie sauce, and pomme purée. Unfortunately, a few pieces of the duck were a little chewy, especially the ones with more fat. The sauce was alright, tasting like a slightly above-average red wine demi-glace with a touch more richness and sweetness than usual. The pomme purée was good, being rich with a nice texture. Overall, I think a bit of acid would have helped as well. This was alright, and I would have appreciated some bread to mop up the remaining sauce. Another person thought the Bacalao for ~$35, which was topped with two shrimp in this presentation, was pretty good. This place reminded me of Txikito in many ways. Both are a bit too pricey for the quality, with comparable food. For spending around $100, there are many other spots I would prefer, such as Casa Mono, El Pote, or a few others. If I were to go back, I'd probably just order appetizers. I'll leave the same score as the other restaurant, a bare 4/upper 3, and I would give a 3.5 if available. (4 stars)

This is a typical trendy Manhattan restaurant. Charming interior, great mixed drinks, delicious food but like all Manhattan restaurants expensive. You’ll drop $100 per person if you include drinks. That being said the food and mixed drinks were delicious so absolutely no complaints. We walked in early and had no problems getting seating but I would recommend getting a reservation if you plan to eat later. The restaurant was quickly filling up. (5 stars)

had the chance to sit down at the chef's counter for a great meal last night. service was spectacular. tried most of the menu and cant recommend the counter experience more. favorites included the short rib stuffed peppers, jamon croquetas, pintxo matrimonio (!!!!), bikini hemingway, and the duck confit. (5 stars)

All style, no substance" describes this place best. The service has some great aspects—attentive water refills, napkin folding, smiling food delivery—but the true Basque hospitality is missing. You have to flag down the indifferent waitress, and their policy of ordering everything at once for immediate coursing screams "get 'em in and out." Some dishes were rushed, like the crab tarts that went soggy quickly. The standout dishes were the incredible octopus with crispy peppers and tender meat, and the simple yet elevated artichokes with almond sauce (highly recommend getting bread to mop it up). The bland morcilla was disappointing, but they did graciously take it off the bill. Overall, a "meh" experience in a city with far better options. (2 stars)

bio_text: Essential by Christophe is a Michelin-starred French restaurant located on Manhattan’s Upper West Side, offering a refined dining experience that celebrates modern French cuisine and thoughtful hospitality. The restaurant features seasonal tasting menus that highlight pristine ingredients and vibrant, house-made sauces, all crafted with precision and a focus on simplicity, allowing the natural flavors to shine. With an elegant and romantic setting near Lincoln Center, Essential by Christophe is recognized for its warmth, artistry, and ingredient-driven approach to fine dining in New York City. The culinary focus at Essential by Christophe is modern French cuisine, presented through seasonal tasting menus and à la carte options. Signature techniques include classic French methods combined with subtle global influences, emphasizing ingredient-driven dishes and curated wine pairings. Chef Christophe Bellanca has over 35 years of experience and continues to refine his craft at Essential by Christophe.
menu_items: Mushroom Cappuccino - sweet potato / madeira reduction - $28
Razor Clams - eventail / chawanmushi inspired / fennel shoyu - $28
Blue Prawns - smoked pike roe / genmaicha tuile / dill & chive bouillon - $32
Toro Saku - mi cuit / tamarind / mandarinquats / sea condiment - $28
Scallop - lightly smoked / gold ossetra caviar / champagne hazelnut - $36
Black Bass - braised / artichoke & manila clams / turmeric - $39
review_snippets: An underrated and underdiscovered elegant restaurant with amazing service. A Well deserved Michelin star, they went out of their way to make my friend's birthday a fabulous experience. The burger (not on a tasting menu) was top class and tasting menu was also a hit, especially caviar topped scallops. The dessert was a bit too sweet though. (5 stars)

Came here with my friend on the second day of my NY trip and it was great! From start to finish, every dish was creative and beautifully balanced in flavor. I ordered a drink that was a bit too spicy for me, and when they asked how it was, I jokingly said that I liked my friend’s better. They immediately offered to make me a new one. I didn’t take it because it was honestly fine, but I was genuinely touched by their generosity :) The pacing of the dishes was just right, they gently wiped our table between each course. They were super thoughtful. I had a truly wonderful experience, and this was definitely one of the highlights of my short trip. (5 stars)

9.30.2025 i celebrated my birthday here with mom & i can say with full confidence that this is the best meal ive had this year. comparing to other michelin french fine dining establishments, i would pick this as my top 1 for overall hospitality, food and price point. essential offers a truly unique seafood-focused menu with every course being as memorable or even better than the last. the flavor combinations are rich, perfectly well-balanced & all-around luxurious. dont underestimate the simple presentations because the taste will blow you away. alfonso was our server—he was AMAZING! very attentive & made my night feel extra special with personal touches, check-ins throughout the meal as well as assisting me with my annoying vlog/photo sessions. cant forget to mention that the dining room is extremely gorgeous with its warm yellow hues, flowers & intimate table settings—perfect for date night. im already looking forward to revisiting & telling all my friends about it. simply exceeded all my expectations—wont be surprised to see essential gain another star soon. thank you so much team! (5 stars)

Absolutely Exceptional Dining Experience We had the most incredible experience at Essential by Christophe. We were there celebrating the newlyweds, and choosing the Chef’s Room truly made the evening unforgettable. The level of service was unlike anything I’ve ever experienced, every single staff member made us feel welcomed, comfortable, and genuinely cared for. They anticipated what we needed before we even asked and made sure every guest had exactly what they wanted. The food was outstanding. The Wagyu beef cap was melt-in-your-mouth perfection, the scallop was a clear highlight, and the mushroom cappuccino was one of the most unique and delicious dishes. Every course was beautifully executed and thoughtfully balanced. If you’re looking for a place to celebrate a special occasion or want a dining experience that exceeds every expectation, I cannot recommend this restaurant enough. Absolutely five stars. (5 stars)

bio_text: Estela is a celebrated modern American restaurant located in the heart of New York City, offering an intimate bistro experience. Guests can enjoy a thrilling dinner in the dining room, a leisurely weekend brunch, or a late-night drink at the bustling bar. Since its opening in 2013, Estela has become known for its signature dishes that have achieved classic status in New York City, all while consistently introducing new culinary delights. Estela focuses on modern American cuisine, showcasing a blend of innovative flavors and seasonal ingredients. The menu features a variety of dining formats, including dinner and brunch, with an emphasis on signature dishes that highlight the chef's creativity and technique. Estela was opened in 2013 by chef Ignacio Mattos and has since earned one Michelin star along with numerous accolades.
menu_items: Sourdough miche with butter - $6
Charcuterie - $25
Fruit plate with Brillat Savarin - $18
Oysters with yuzu kosho mignonette - $6/ea
Duck kofta with cinnamon skewer - $1 / ea
Scallop with dates and uni - $32
review_snippets: I thoroughly enjoyed my lunch at Estela. I loved most of the dishes, especially the pork belly and the endive salad. I found the chocolate cake too bitter and slightly burnt for my taste, but overall a great experience. Also our server was so friendly and professional. Would love to come back for dinner (5 stars)

We had a wonderful experience at Estela today. All the dishes we had were both outstanding and unique. The restaurant is small inside but beautiful, and the service at the bar was excellent. This establishment has definitely earned it's Michelin star, we highly recommend a meal here! (5 stars)

Sourdough - 5.5/10; it was a very okay bread with generic butter and olives. I would've at least liked the bread warmed. But the fact that I paid for it knocked it down a lot, I would expect specialty bread and butter if it comes with a price tag. Endive - 6.5/10; Crisp, crunchy, and overall complimentary flavors. However it could've used a bit more sweetness to round out the bitterness of the endive personally. Wagyu - 6.5/10; Very good crust, the sunchoke and spinach were very flavorful, and the coffee sancho was a sleeper hit that added a lot to the wagyu. However the wagyu itself lacked flavor. Although the dish was good, I don't feel that it can justify that price tag. Chocolate cake - 8/10; Rich dark chocolate flavor w. a nice toasted note from the sesame, and a hint of savory. Crunchy exterior and gooey interior. However I feel that the whipped cream actually detracted from the overall dessert. If it were slightly sweetened, it could've added another element of sweetness to round out the richness of the chocolate. Overall I personally feel that many of the dishes could be exciting and interesting. The actual execution of these dishes does not match concepts. The service was nice. The restaurant itself is dimly lit and a bit cramped. (3 stars)

Sat at the bar booked on Open Table and Chase Sapphire Reserve for the $150 dining credit. We ordered the beef tartare, mackerel, endive salad, ricotta dumplings, and wagyu, plus 2 wines, a beer, a cocktail, and the parsnip gelato. It was as you can imagine a $$$ night out. But the bar seating was so cozy and no rush for the table. Favorites that I would come back for are the parsnip gelato (so nice we ordered it twice), the dumpling, and the mackerel. Skip the tartare, the endives are great to balance the overall meal with some crisp and fresh bites. Good wine selection. (5 stars)

Sourdough miche with butter - $6 Charcuterie - $25 Fruit plate with Brillat Savarin - $18 Oysters with yuzu kosho mignonette - $6/ea Duck kofta with cinnamon skewer - $1 / ea Scallop with dates and uni - $32 I thoroughly enjoyed my lunch at Estela. I loved most of the dishes, especially the pork belly and the endive salad. I found the chocolate cake too bitter and slightly burnt for my taste, but overall a great experience. Also our server was so friendly and professional. Would love to come back for dinner (5 stars) We had a wonderful experience at Estela today. All the dishes we had were both outstanding and unique. The restaurant is small inside but beautiful, and the service at the bar was excellent. This establishment has definitely earned it's Michelin star, we highly recommend a meal here! (5 stars) Sourdough - 5.5/10; it was a very okay bread with generic butter and olives. I would've at least liked the bread warmed. But the fact that I paid for it knocked it down a lot, I would expect specialty bread and butter if it comes with a price tag. Endive - 6.5/10; Crisp, crunchy, and overall complimentary flavors. However it could've used a bit more sweetness to round out the bitterness of the endive personally. Wagyu - 6.5/10; Very good crust, the sunchoke and spinach were very flavorful, and the coffee sancho was a sleeper hit that added a lot to the wagyu. However the wagyu itself lacked flavor. Although the dish was good, I don't feel that it can justify that price tag. Chocolate cake - 8/10; Rich dark chocolate flavor w. a nice toasted note from the sesame, and a hint of savory. Crunchy exterior and gooey interior. However I feel that the whipped cream actually detracted from the overall dessert. If it were slightly sweetened, it could've added another element of sweetness to round out the richness of the chocolate. Overall I personally feel that many of the dishes could be exciting and interesting. The actual execution of these dishes does not match concepts. The service was nice. The restaurant itself is dimly lit and a bit cramped. (3 stars) Sat at the bar booked on Open Table and Chase Sapphire Reserve for the $150 dining credit. We ordered the beef tartare, mackerel, endive salad, ricotta dumplings, and wagyu, plus 2 wines, a beer, a cocktail, and the parsnip gelato. It was as you can imagine a $$$ night out. But the bar seating was so cozy and no rush for the table. Favorites that I would come back for are the parsnip gelato (so nice we ordered it twice), the dumpling, and the mackerel. Skip the tartare, the endives are great to balance the overall meal with some crisp and fresh bites. Good wine selection. (5 stars)

bio_text: Eulalie is a charming restaurant located in Tribeca, New York City, known for its warm and inviting atmosphere. With a focus on creating memorable dining experiences, Eulalie welcomes both returning guests and newcomers to enjoy its unique offerings. The restaurant embodies a blend of personal touches and culinary passion, making it a delightful spot for food enthusiasts. Eulalie specializes in contemporary American cuisine, emphasizing seasonal and locally sourced ingredients. The menu features a variety of dishes that highlight the chef's creativity and commitment to quality, with an emphasis on elegant yet approachable flavors. The name 'Eulalie' is inspired by a memorable wine from Cahors, Chateau de Cenac, which holds personal significance for the owners. The restaurant aims to reflect a romantic notion of dining, drawing from personal experiences and connections.

review_snippets: This is a charming French restaurant in Manhattan. It was extra special because we were there around Christmas time and the owners opened the restaurant up for a couple of extra days around the holidays. They only take reservations over the phone and there are very few tables. The service was extraordinary, and I believe this was driven by both owner philosophy and the small number of tables versus wait staff. One thing I noticed immediately was the distance between tables: : much greater than most New York restaurants. As a result, conversation with your partner was easy and it was very quiet. This is a special event restaurant, and as such commands a premium for the experience. This premium is justified by the quality of the food and the attentive service. Highly recommend. (5 stars)

Very grateful for the experience. The space is cozy and beautiful. Every dish was thoughtfully prepared—showcasing amazing ingredients elevated by fantastic culinary craftsmanship. The wine pairing was lovely and complemented the dishes perfectly. (5 stars)

Eulalie is pure magic. From the moment Tina welcomes you, you’re transported far from the outside world into an evening of true hospitality. Every detail is intentional—from the handwritten menus to the impeccable wine pairings that elevate each course. Chef Chip’s dishes, from the delicate rabbit ravioli to the perfectly cooked steak, are simply sensational. This isn’t just dinner—it’s an experience of elegance, warmth, and flawless execution. (5 stars)
Incredible experience. The staff / service is exceptional. The food superb. Not fussy or pretentious at all. You’ll feel like you’re in France. (5 stars)

bio_text: Family Meal at Blue Hill offers a unique dining experience that emphasizes community and connection through food. The restaurant embodies a warm and inviting atmosphere, where guests can enjoy thoughtfully prepared meals that celebrate the bounty of local farms. The culinary focus is on farm-to-table cuisine, highlighting seasonal ingredients sourced from local producers. The menu features a communal dining format, encouraging shared experiences among guests.
review_snippets: A great friend and I went for brunch. And I can't wait to go back!! The room is intimate and inviting. The service was out of this 🌎. Schuyler, our sommelier, offered nothing but helpful and informed recommendations. The menu, itself, was second to none. Each course was AMAZING!! The skillet Millet is stupendous! The surprise of the tasting meal added to the experience. Also, it started to snow... (5 stars)

The place has a beautiful and cozy ambience and the service was great. The first course of our meal was fantastic and set high expectations - the crème fraiche and buckwheat soil was so delicious I could eat that everyday. Unfortunately the later courses were a bit of a let down for us. The leeks were too tough, the raw chicory was too bitter and not sufficiently complemented by the sauces, the turmeric ice cream was interesting at best. The focus was on featuring the fresh produce and I think they did a good job at that. (3 stars)

This has to be one of the best Michelin-starred meals I've ever had in NYC. I randomly went for lunch because I'm trying to visit every Michelin spot in the city, and honestly I don't know why it took me so long to finally get to Blue Hill. The restaurant is tucked away in the cutest neighborhood, and the interior has a Scandinavian-meets-farmhouse vibe that feels clean, calm, and cozy. As soon as I sat down, it felt warm and homey in the best way. Lunch is $85 for a three-course menu, and I highly recommend it. There's no printed menu; they simply bring you what's in season, which I loved since I'm in my veggie era. Leave the thinking to them. First Course: We started with a plate of raw radishes, baby turnips, rye crisps, and an herbed crème fraîche dip topped with dill. Simple but so fresh. The only thing I didn't love was the crackers, which had a bit of a cardboard-like mouthfeel. Then came a seasonal vegetable broth with squash, greens, and a dollop of crème fraîche. It was genuinely one of the best soups I've had anywhere Second Course: The main course came with a perfectly balanced little gem salad, roasted carrots, the creamiest mashed potato purée, slices of homemade whole-grain bread, and a flaky, crusty meat pie that was rich and comforting. Everything tasted super seasonal and thoughtful. Dessert: We finished with a warm apple crumble topped with a silky, tangy cream. The perfect ending. Blue Hill completely exceeded my expectations. The food is incredibly clean, seasonal, and well-executed, and the space is beautiful. I'd absolutely come back, especially at such a reasonable price point. (5 stars)

Honestly words can’t explain the experience, everything was perfect! The food, the service, and the atmosphere were top notch and well curated. The family style was extremely unique, with ingredients I’ve never or rarely seen in other restaurants. Bonus points for a very interesting wine pairing throughout the meal. The atmosphere is very cozy and welcoming, honestly perfect for a special date, a business meeting, or catching up with friends and family. (5 stars)

bio_text: Farra is an intimate neighborhood wine bar that embodies a warm and inviting atmosphere, seating just 22 guests. Located in close proximity to its sister restaurant Atera, Farra focuses on bringing people together through a carefully curated selection of wines and a diverse a la carte menu, perfect for light snacks or shared dinners among friends. Farra specializes in a contemporary a la carte dining experience, featuring a menu that highlights seasonal ingredients. The culinary offerings include dishes such as Halibut Ravioli and Dry Aged Ribeye, complemented by an evolving selection of wines curated by the wine director. Farra is a sister restaurant to Atera, inspired by the Basque word meaning 'to drink', which reflects its mission to foster community through shared beverages.

review_snippets: We dined at Farra during a later seating, and it immediately felt more like an intimate theater than a restaurant. The open kitchen is the stage, the chef at center, while the staff moves with precise, almost balletic rhythm. Watching the room flow was captivating in itself. The food was exceptional—each dish visually composed with clear intention. We started with a raw tuna preparation that delivered a refined balance of spice and texture. The standout of the evening was the ravioli, coiled elegantly in a comforting miso broth. The mild shrimp filling allowed the deep umami of the broth to shine, creating a dish that was both thoughtful and memorable. The duck showcased subtle asian influences, with a peanut layer and grapefruit providing a striking contrast of richness and brightness. Dessert was also visually pleasing and had a wonderful taste as well. Service elevated the experience even further. Sage and Heather were warm, approachable, and genuinely engaging, with an impressive grasp of the wine list and intuitive pairing recommendations. Some come to New York for Broadway—we come for food. Farra delivers a performance worth applauding: beautifully synchronized, expressive, and deeply satisfying from start to finish. (5 stars)

This is one of my go-to places for treating myself/others for the special occasions in life (birthday, anniversary, graduation, New Year’s, etc). They have access to Atera’s wine cellar which is obviously incredible. Some of the dishes can be a bit hit or miss but if you know what to get, it will never disappoint. In particular, the rice with scallops is one of the best bites in NYC. But what makes Farra Wine Bar the most special is its hospitality. The staff is so knowledgeable, warm and kind without being overbearing. Their sommelier Sage in particular is always there who is amazing and today we were served by Heather who was wonderful too. To go off on a tangent, I have been reflecting on AI and how eventually it will be able to improve on what humans can do in every field and industry. But where AI will never be able to surpass humans is hospitality - in tourism, hotels, restaurants, events, etc. Sometimes you need a reminder of what is truly unique and special about the human touch. Go and experience Farra if you want to understand what true hospitality is like! (5 stars)

We loved how cozy this wine bar was, especially when we walked here on a November night. Both the burrata and the comté cheese were flavorful and well-executed small plates. We shared the rice for mains. Even though it was a bit too rich for me, the texture was so nostalgic of the 锅巴 (Chinese crispy rice snacks) I loved. The apple elderflower mocktail was SUPER unique and memorable. Our server was super attentive and nice! (5 stars)

Good location, close to the Financial District. The vibe is relaxed and chill, with friendly staff and a welcoming crowd. The food looks nice and is solid, nothing mind-blowing, but decent (maybe I’m just picky after living in Japan). A good experience with friends. (4 stars)

bio_text: Fasano Restaurant, located in the heart of New York City, embodies a century of Milanese gastronomy, offering a timeless setting for both lunch and dinner. The restaurant is characterized by its traditional hospitality and authentic Milanese cuisine, creating a classic fine-dining experience that is refined yet approachable. With an elegant atmosphere and a commitment to quality, Fasano serves as a beacon of the family’s long-standing tradition in fine Italian dining. Fasano specializes in elevated Northern Italian cuisine, focusing on classic Milanese dishes. The menu features a selection of signature items such as Ossobuco alla Menighina con Risotto alla Milanese and Tortelli di Vitello con Fonduta di Parmigiano Reggiano. The dining experience is complemented by an award-winning wine list. Fasano's gastronomic history began in 1902 when Vittorio Fasano opened an outpost named 'Brasserie Paulista' in São Paulo. Gero Fasano, the fourth generation of the Fasano restaurateurs, joined the business in the 1980s and has since expanded the brand to include 30 restaurants and 10 hotels across Brazil, the United States, and Uruguay. The New York location stands as a testament to the family's commitment to excellence and Italian heritage.

review_snippets: We had an absolutely perfect experience. Everything was truly 10/10 from start to finish. The ambiance is beautiful and refined, with elegant décor, a warm atmosphere, and the perfect background music that sets the tone for a special night. The service was impeccable attentive, professional, and genuinely welcoming. For food, we started with the burrata, which was incredibly fresh and perfectly balanced. The ravioli al pesto was outstanding rich, delicate, and full of flavor. We paired our meal with an excellent Barolo Mura Mura, which elevated the entire experience. To finish, we enjoyed a creamy gelato and a delicious chocolate tart. Since it was our anniversary, the team surprised us with a small complimentary cake, which was a lovely and thoughtful touch and absolutely delicious. This place is now officially on my list of the best restaurants in NYC. Highly recommended for special occasions or anyone looking for an exceptional Italian dining experience. (5 stars)

Right when we walked in we were greeted with smiles from coat check and receptionist! The ambiance was great, chairs were comfy and the recommendations by the staff were wonderful! The tortellini was the best meal and the tartar as the best app in my opinion! (5 stars)

The entire experience was amazing and I cannot wait to go back! I had a Caprino salad and the Emiliana pasta and let me just say the combination of flavors were blended so perfectly. There wasn’t nothing I could ask for because the customer service and attentiveness was beyond my expectations. Huge shout out to Steven and Jimmy and William for making my birthday dinner so special. After you eat dinner, go upstairs and listen to some jazz in a very intimate cozy setting you won’t regret it thanks again! (5 stars)

I’ve been several times but last week I visited by myself for a light meal . I was blown away by the attentiveness of the staff! Thanks for the complimentary champagne! :) I am a creature of habit so I always have their caviar service when I go. Perfect for sharing but works as a single portion too. Tried the pistachio mouse for dessert and it was 10/10! If you go for a full dinner try their gnocchi and filetto! Both amazing entrees (5 stars)

review_snippets: brilliant meal. first, we got VERY LUCKY and walked in without a reservation and got a clutch table. kudos to the host for problem-solving and getting us in at a busy time. the waitstaff were friendly, fun and helped us select the right amount of food for our party that was balanced and created a spectacular food experience. the bursts of delight from the arancini, beet carpaccio, lamb -- seriously... EVERYTHING was more incredible than the bite of the thing before. we shared and loved it all around our table. the cappelletti was a new adventure for us -- and it was magic. most of all, we felt the entire team, from host, bartender, to servers, those crumbing the table, to kitchen alchemists were working in tandem to ace every detail seamlessly. plus, we learn the phrase, "fire the next dish." it was perfect fire. (5 stars)

We have been to Fausto many times and love it. The food and drinks are delicious and the ambiance is great. It’s one of our go tos for a nice night out. The pastas, focaccia, and cauliflower salad are personal favorites. (5 stars)

Went for a casual dinner at the bar after the movies. For a fancier experience I’d say book a table. The potatoes and spicy vodka were SO GOOD. Very simple meals done perfectly. Have tried to recreate the potatoes at home unsuccessfully. Will be back! (5 stars)

The salad was excellent, fresh, flavorful, and perfectly balanced. The bread was disappointing since it wasn’t warm or crusty as expected. Of the three pasta dishes we ordered, only one was good while the other two missed the mark on flavor and texture. The service was excellent, attentive, and friendly! (3 stars)

bio_text: Forsythia is an upcoming Italian restaurant located at Nine Stanton Street, designed to evoke the warmth and hospitality of a traditional Italian home. The restaurant aims to provide a relaxing environment where guests can enjoy hand-crafted Italian comfort food, whether dining in or through their innovative Forsythia At Home service, which allows patrons to recreate the dining experience at home. Forsythia specializes in authentic Italian cuisine, with a strong emphasis on fresh, house-made pasta prepared daily. The menu features a selection of 3 or 4 course dinners that can be enjoyed at home or during their summer pop-up events. The restaurant's opening has been delayed due to COVID-19, but it draws inspiration from the founders' experiences living in Italy.

review_snippets: Bit of a mixed bag here. The room is cool, chill vibes, good music and lighting and professional, friendly service. We had the “surprise” 6 course tasting menu. There was definitely a problem in the kitchen because there were some extremely long delays between courses, our meal took 2 1/2 hours. We started with the complimentary focaccia, delicious and we went for the ricotta upcharge, $10 for 2 tablespoons of ricotta. Not sure the value proposition was there. Flavors were generally on point, the eggplant with some charred greens was OK but didn’t love it. Favorite dish was the crab agnolotti, scrumptious. The bucatini served before that was perfectly cooked, but was excessively salty, apparently because of the capers as we mentioned the issue to the server. However, it definitely tasted like someone slipped with the salt shaker. Our main was a kind of disappointing plate of mini meatballs in a sweet and savory sauce. Interesting but for $129 menu maybe we expected more than mini meatballs. Dessert was a scoop of peach and Prosecco sorbet, refreshing, but a little bit underwhelming for dessert on a tasting menu. I guess as I am writing this I kind of wanted to like it more than I actually ended up liking it. (4 stars)

This place was spectacular! We got the agnolotti and the rabbit ragu along with the salad. I make pasta art from scratch at home as a hobby so visiting here and eating the handmade pasta has been a dream of mine. The service was so friendly and efficient. Everything lived up to the hype! I only visit NYC one day a year and this restaurant is worth it. (5 stars)

We didn’t have a reservation and only stopped by for a glass of champagne. When they realized we were celebrating our marriage, they surprised us with a delicious dessert on the house, which was incredibly kind and thoughtful. The entire place has such positive energy — great atmosphere, beautiful presentation, and amazing food (looking good on the tables). Every detail felt special. Without a doubt, we will be coming back the next time we’re in New York. (5 stars)

Cozy small restaurant great for groups of 2-4ppl. They have a curated seasonal menu and nice wine pairings. The Foccacia was so fresh and almost croissant flaky 🥐 All of our pastas were excellent (5 stars)

bio_text: Four Twenty Five, a distinguished restaurant by renowned Chef Jean-Georges Vongerichten, is located at 425 Park Avenue in New York City. This establishment seamlessly combines culinary excellence with architectural beauty, featuring a design by the acclaimed Lord Norman Foster. Guests can enjoy extraordinary dining experiences across its Mezzanine and Street levels, highlighted by a captivating cocktail lounge and an intimate dining room that overlooks Park Avenue. The restaurant focuses on innovative cuisine that emphasizes sustainability and local sourcing. Signature techniques include the use of vegetable juices, fruit essences, and herbal vinaigrettes, moving away from traditional meat stocks and creams. The menu reflects a commitment to working with local farmers and sustainable seafood suppliers. In 2023, Jean-Georges opened Four Twenty Five, marking the 62nd restaurant in his global repertoire. His culinary journey began in 1986 at Lafayette, just steps away from the current location.
menu_items: wild blueberry, hemp, chia, date, omega seed butter, raw almond milk - $18

Grapefruit - $12
review_snippets: Everything about Four Twenty Five feels like a modern love letter to New York City glamour. The moment you step inside, you know you are in for something special. I like what they do during restaurant week, they change up the menu each week. Of course I am going back to taste something else. The butternut squash soup with cabbage dumplings was flavorful. The pan roasted Hake, was creative genius and was plated superbly. The apple confit was the perfect ending. I enjoyed hearing about the vineyard and the tasting notes for the wine I had selected. This place is special and I highly recommend it. (5 stars)

Per usual another great Jean Georges restaurant. #18 for us! The server, Christian (sorry if I misspelled it) was absolutely fabulous. We shared great stories as he provided wonderful food! The coddled egg with caviar was insane! Also loved the tempura squash. The tuna tartare was amazing. Can not wait for #19! (5 stars)

I really enjoyed the cocktails here and would definitely return for drinks. However, the host staff were surprisingly unaccommodating. We were seated much later than our reservation, and they prioritized other newly arrived parties before us, even though we checked on our table three times while at the bar. The highlight of the dinner was definitely the amuse-bouche. While the fluke sashimi and kampachi were good, they didn’t blow me away. The roasted chicken was decent, but the flavorful skin was the only standout part. The crab tagliatelle was overwhelmed by dill, making it hard to appreciate other flavors; it felt very unbalanced. The strawberry shortcake and banana custard were delicious, but not quite enough to justify the price of the meal. On a positive note, they suggested a fantastic bottle of wine. Overall, I would return for the drinks but would skip the meal next time. (3 stars)

We had the tasting menu here for our anniversary dinner. It was an excellent choice. We started with a drink at the bar. The bartender was pleasant and made us some excellent cocktails to get started. There is an Asian overtone that runs through the meal (the coddled egg, the tuna and the beef all have Asian influences). Having lived in Japan at one time, we like that a lot. Everything was delicious, but I would say the highlights for us were the beet salad and the Wagyu beef. The salad was incredibly fresh and bursting with flavors. The beef, served with pistachio broccoli, which was also excellent, was done perfectly. We asked for rare and were glad we did with such delicious meat. The sauce with it is also delicious but the meat itself is the star. You’ll just need to try it! The Strawberry shortcake, and this is from someone that doesn’t usually even eat dessert, was outstanding! They also gave us an extra lemon meringue-like dish for our anniversary. The dining room is constantly busy with staff, but they never made us feel like they were hovering over us. They were always very pleasant and friendly and took the time to explain and answer our questions. A pricey meal yes, but worth the price if that’s what you want. It is very fine dining in midtown Manhattan after all. (5 stars)

bio_text: Francie is a Michelin-starred restaurant located in the heart of Williamsburg, Brooklyn, offering a warm and convivial atmosphere reminiscent of a neighborhood brasserie. Housed in a beautifully restored limestone-clad former bank building, the restaurant features an open kitchen that invites guests to experience the culinary artistry firsthand, creating a welcoming dining environment for both locals and visitors alike. Francie's menu is inspired by European flavors and designed for flexibility, featuring a variety of snacks, shellfish, handmade pastas, and main courses. Signature dishes include The Market Salad, Lobster Ravioli, and Crown Roast of Duck for Two, complemented by a modern twist on classic desserts and a renowned Cheese Cart. Francie debuted in December 2020 as the first independent collaboration between Chef-Owner Christopher Cipollone and Owner-Operator John Winterman.
menu_items: Roman Army Sourdough - sunflower spread, whipped lardo - $15
Crudités - marcona almond, truffle - $14
Soufflé Cakes - seaweed butter, green meyer lemon, caviar - $23
English Pea Bomboloni - preserved truffle, parmesan fonduta, pancetta pepato - $23
Duck Mortadella - brioche, pistachio mustard - $21
Foie Gras Canelé - earl grey, prune, armagnac - $15
review_snippets: Had a wonderful experience at Francie. Both the ambiance and the food were excellent — the space feels elegant yet comfortable, perfect for a special night out. The roast duck is the must-order dish. It’s absolutely delicious and beautifully prepared — definitely worth trying, even though it’s a bit on the pricier side. I would also highly recommend the clam pasta, which was flavorful and very satisfying. Overall, a great spot for a memorable dinner. Would happily come back again. (5 stars)

The food here was incredible! I loved the bread and the sunflower butter! The lamb, bombolini, market salad, and the foi gras were so good! We also had the citron dessert which I loved! They have a great mocktail menu as well (5 stars)

Francie is really all about the Duck, and the Pastas too! The starters vary between some misses like the bomboloni and carpaccio, but the Market salad was actually so horrible it’s not even pictured. But then there’s the outstanding Roman Army Sourdough, this bread is perfect and comes with two nice spreads. The soufflé cakes are tasty with a nice caviar butter spread. The Fussiloni was really good, a flavorful wintery sauce with some big bites and truffle. Then the Duck, it’s amazing, perfect roasted skin delivered with a huge portion in great sauce. Now, the fries are very great, but at any restaurant $20 for fries is a very high price and one that isn’t even listed on the menu. Additionally, we had no real waiter most of the night, on a slow Tuesday night we had what seemed to be the manager for the first half of the night, then no waiter at all till dessert. The vibe inside is cool and overall the restaurant is fine, but why it has a Michelin Star doesn’t really make sense compared to the objectively better restaurants in NYC that do or don’t have one. (4 stars)

We ordered a lot at Francie, but the clear highlights were the family duck ($152) and the steak ($225). Both arrived beautifully presented without feeling overdone. The steak had a perfect sear, tons of flavor, and was incredibly tender. The duck fully lived up to its reputation — crisp, deeply golden skin, juicy meat, and a really clean, balanced plate. The vibe was polished but comfortable, not stuffy at all. Service was attentive and well paced, and nothing felt rushed. Definitely one of the better meals I’ve had in Brooklyn and a place I’d happily go back to. 😋 (5 stars)

bio_text: FREVO is a Michelin-starred restaurant and contemporary art gallery located in Greenwich Village, New York City. Co-founded by Chef Franco Sampogna and Bernardo Silva, FREVO offers a unique dining experience that combines exquisite cuisine with a rotating art exhibition. The ambiance is elegant yet casual, inviting guests to indulge in a culinary journey that is both sophisticated and accessible. FREVO specializes in sauce-centered cuisine that is rooted in classical French techniques, enhanced by South American and Asian influences. The menu is presented in a tasting format, with offerings that rotate every four months, allowing for a fresh and dynamic dining experience. Signature techniques include a focus on flavor layering and innovative pairings with a curated wine selection. FREVO was opened on May 17, 2019, after a five-month renovation of its Greenwich Village location. Chef Franco Sampogna and Bernardo Silva, who have extensive backgrounds in Michelin-starred establishments, sought to create a space that merges fine dining with contemporary art. The restaurant quickly gained recognition, receiving two stars from The New York Times just three months after opening and has since been awarded multiple Michelin stars.

Butternut Squash - Parmesan, Truffle

review_snippets: Excellent food & service, but skip the add-ons I’ve been to Frevo a few times now, and it consistently delivers very good, beautifully presented food with impeccable service. Entering through an art gallery sets a unique, intimate tone for the whole experience, and it’s one of the touches that makes Frevo feel special. The cooking was excellent across the board: the fish was perfectly prepared, and the beef was spot-on. Their signature transition course — a 36-month Comté served over a scoop of honey ice cream — is an unusual pairing that works incredibly well. Dessert was also outstanding: a chocolate cake with wasabi ice cream that was both creative and delicious. Their wine selection is strong and fairly priced, especially considering this is a Michelin-starred restaurant. My only real complaint is the upselling of additional dishes. This time, for the first time, I tried one of their extra options — a scallop dish with white truffle. Not only was it extremely expensive (about a third of the full menu price), but it was also underwhelming, with a sauce that overshadowed both the scallop and the truffle. My friend added uni to one of his dishes for a similarly steep markup and felt the same way. In past visits, skipping these add-ons actually led to a better overall experience. This is usually a 5 stars for me, but only got 4 stars this time. I would still go back, but will definitely skip the add-ons next time. (4 stars)

Frevo is a full-on experience. Came here to celebrate my husband’s birthday and everything—from the service to the food—was flawless. We even got to meet the chef, which made the night feel extra special. Every course was wildly creative, with flavors I honestly didn’t know were possible. Thoughtful, bold, and beautifully executed dishes from start to finish. This is the kind of place that reminds you why NYC dining is unmatched. Absolute must for food lovers (5 stars)

Frevo is a fun, unique spot tucked inside a gallery that almost feels like a speakeasy. Starting with the highlights: the ambience, the energy of the staff, and the service were all 10/10. The space is artsy, modern, and genuinely enjoyable to spend an evening in. The dinner began on a strong note—the first two dishes were especially tasty—but the rest of the tasting course didn’t resonate with me as much, with a few items feeling a bit salty or less memorable. That said, I’m definitely open to returning when the menu changes. For now, I’d give this experience a solid 4.2/5. (4 stars)

Frevo NYC is, without question, one of the most exceptional dining experiences in the city. What amazes me every time is how they constantly tweak and evolve the menu yet somehow everything remains flawless. Every dish feels like a new discovery, but with the same depth of flavor and precision that makes Frevo truly world-class. The service is impeccable from start to finish. Attentive without hovering, warm without being overfamiliar exactly what you expect from a Michelin-star restaurant, but executed even better. And the food… honestly, it’s the best I’ve had in NYC. I’ve been to countless Michelin-starred spots across the city, but nothing compares to the creativity, balance, and sheer deliciousness that Frevo delivers consistently. The ambience ties it all together sexy, intimate, romantic yet never stuffy or pretentious. It feels special without trying too hard. If you’re looking for the perfect blend of flawless cuisine, top-tier service, and a beautifully curated atmosphere, Frevo is in a league of its own. Highly recommended. (5 stars)

Sweet Nori - Shima Aji, Trout Roe, Shishito Pepper Butternut Squash - Parmesan, Truffle Carrot - Almond, Red Curry Norwegian King Crab - Ikura, White Pepper Focaccia - Stracciatella, Olive, Lettuce Bluefin Tuna - Pineapple, Kombu Excellent food & service, but skip the add-ons I’ve been to Frevo a few times now, and it consistently delivers very good, beautifully presented food with impeccable service. Entering through an art gallery sets a unique, intimate tone for the whole experience, and it’s one of the touches that makes Frevo feel special. The cooking was excellent across the board: the fish was perfectly prepared, and the beef was spot-on. Their signature transition course — a 36-month Comté served over a scoop of honey ice cream — is an unusual pairing that works incredibly well. Dessert was also outstanding: a chocolate cake with wasabi ice cream that was both creative and delicious. Their wine selection is strong and fairly priced, especially considering this is a Michelin-starred restaurant. My only real complaint is the upselling of additional dishes. This time, for the first time, I tried one of their extra options — a scallop dish with white truffle. Not only was it extremely expensive (about a third of the full menu price), but it was also underwhelming, with a sauce that overshadowed both the scallop and the truffle. My friend added uni to one of his dishes for a similarly steep markup and felt the same way. In past visits, skipping these add-ons actually led to a better overall experience. This is usually a 5 stars for me, but only got 4 stars this time. I would still go back, but will definitely skip the add-ons next time. (4 stars) Frevo is a full-on experience. Came here to celebrate my husband’s birthday and everything—from the service to the food—was flawless. We even got to meet the chef, which made the night feel extra special. Every course was wildly creative, with flavors I honestly didn’t know were possible. Thoughtful, bold, and beautifully executed dishes from start to finish. This is the kind of place that reminds you why NYC dining is unmatched. Absolute must for food lovers (5 stars) Frevo is a fun, unique spot tucked inside a gallery that almost feels like a speakeasy. Starting with the highlights: the ambience, the energy of the staff, and the service were all 10/10. The space is artsy, modern, and genuinely enjoyable to spend an evening in. The dinner began on a strong note—the first two dishes were especially tasty—but the rest of the tasting course didn’t resonate with me as much, with a few items feeling a bit salty or less memorable. That said, I’m definitely open to returning when the menu changes. For now, I’d give this experience a solid 4.2/5. (4 stars) Frevo NYC is, without question, one of the most exceptional dining experiences in the city. What amazes me every time is how they constantly tweak and evolve the menu yet somehow everything remains flawless. Every dish feels like a new discovery, but with the same depth of flavor and precision that makes Frevo truly world-class. The service is impeccable from start to finish. Attentive without hovering, warm without being overfamiliar exactly what you expect from a Michelin-star restaurant, but executed even better. And the food… honestly, it’s the best I’ve had in NYC. I’ve been to countless Michelin-starred spots across the city, but nothing compares to the creativity, balance, and sheer deliciousness that Frevo delivers consistently. The ambience ties it all together sexy, intimate, romantic yet never stuffy or pretentious. It feels special without trying too hard. If you’re looking for the perfect blend of flawless cuisine, top-tier service, and a beautifully curated atmosphere, Frevo is in a league of its own. Highly recommended. (5 stars)

bio_text: Gabriel Kreuther is a distinguished dining destination located in the heart of New York City, where the essence of culinary tradition meets innovative creativity. The restaurant embodies a commitment to authenticity, offering a refined atmosphere that celebrates the artistry of food and storytelling. Under the guidance of Chef Gabriel Kreuther and his team, guests are invited to experience a unique blend of flavors and techniques that reflect both heritage and modernity. The restaurant specializes in contemporary Alsatian cuisine, focusing on seasonal ingredients and traditional techniques. The menu features a variety of offerings, including a tasting menu that highlights the chef's signature dishes and innovative presentations. Gabriel Kreuther is led by Chef Gabriel Kreuther, who has built a reputation for excellence in the culinary world. The restaurant is part of a growing family of brands and experiences that emphasize culinary traditions.

review_snippets: I tremendously enjoyed the 4-course menu at Gabriel Kreuther, and couldn’t recommend it more for anyone looking to celebrate a special occasion. Other than the sheer excellence of the food - the team went above and beyond to make this a special night for us. I would go as far as saying this was the best meal I’ve had in the city. I’ve been to a quantity of Michelin star restaurants across the world, and I can say this truly earned its stars. I’m a tough critic and I can’t say the same for a lot of the other NYC Michelin restaurants - which have generally been a disappointment in comparison to those in Europe. (5 stars)

The incredible staff deserve a third star for the incredible evening they curated seamlessly for my wife & I. As hospitality professionals ourselves, we always love to see team operate on a different level & this group is a well run machine with invisible systems, unreasonable hospitality & the perfect level of comfortable mixed with professional. I've had, in my lifetime, maybe 4 "memorable meals" & this is one more. It's a shame we live 2 hours away up north, however we will be using our experience as a benchmark of excellence to strive for when we train our own team back home at Lone Wolf in Kingston, NY. Hats off to the entire FOH & BOH teams. I hope management read this aloud & shares with you why your role matters. (5 stars)

Outstanding evening at Gabriel Kreuther. Last night, my wife and I dined at Gabriel Kreuther, and it’s one of those rare restaurants where—while you’re still seated, mid-course—you find yourself planning your return. (We actually said, “We have to bring the kids here.”) We chose the tasting menu, and from the very first course, it was clear how much thought and intention went into each dish. Every plate was a success—beautifully composed, flavorful, and creative. Each course flowed naturally into the next, making the tasting feel cohesive rather than just a collection of highlights. The beverage pairings were equally well executed. Each drink was thoughtfully selected to elevate the dish it accompanied, adding nuance and balance without stealing the spotlight. Together, the food and pairings felt precise, measured, and complete. Service is where the evening truly stood out. At this level, hospitality must be a seamless team effort, guided by calm leadership and real awareness of the room. Angie, our captain for the evening, embodied that role perfectly—warm, attentive, and always a step ahead. Zanetta, one of the managers, worked tirelessly throughout the night to ensure every detail was handled with care. Mission accomplished. The dining room itself deserves praise. The interior design, lighting, and seating are all beautifully considered, and the view into the open kitchen adds an extra layer of energy to the experience. The large, inviting bar is a destination on its own—we arrived early and enjoyed a drink there before being seated, and it set the tone for the evening perfectly. An exceptional dining experience from start to finish. Highly recommended. (5 stars)

Have eaten in the lounge before and decided to try the dining room, where I had a wonderful 4 course meal. Especially loved the festive holiday decorations and music playing. Food was great, especially their new Black Forest indulgence dessert (solid recommend for dark chocolate lovers). Two visits and the service has been excellent, from the hosts who check you in to the servers in both the lounge and dining room; everyone is attentive and professional while also being friendly and welcoming. (5 stars)

bio_text: Gage & Tollner is a historic oyster and chop house located in Downtown Brooklyn, renowned for its rich legacy dating back to 1879. After a significant closure, the restaurant reopened in 2021, offering a blend of classic and contemporary dining experiences in a beautifully restored landmarked space. The ambiance is warm and inviting, making it a perfect gathering place for both locals and visitors seeking comfort and community. The restaurant specializes in seafood and meat dishes, focusing on high-quality ingredients that are simply yet expertly prepared. The menu features a mix of traditional favorites and innovative offerings, with an emphasis on meticulous sourcing and technique. Gage & Tollner was a cornerstone of the Brooklyn restaurant scene for over a century, closing in 2004 and reopening in 2021 under the guidance of celebrated local restaurateurs Sohui Kim, Ben Schneider, and St. John Frizell.

review_snippets: I took my girlfriend to Gage & Tollner for her birthday. The service overall was fantastic, your water glass is constantly being filled up and you never feel forgotten (especially for how busy the place was on a Thursday night). We had a reservation and were seated immediately, and our drink orders were taken after our water preference. To start we had the Caesar salad and the hot rolls and both were delicious, our server even brought extra butter when we used all of ours. The croutons in the Caesar salad were delicious. For dinner we had the T-Bone for 2 which can be ordered pre-sliced. It was a very good cut of meat with a little too much fat but still amazing. For dessert we had the Brooklyn Blackout Cake which was also very good and not too rich for a completely chocolate cake. Finally, since I indicated on OpenTable that we had a birthday in our party there was a Happy Birthday card waiting at our table when we sat down and a candle in our cake complete with Happy Birthday written on the plate! (All a surprise). Overall, a great spot for steak dinner and especially a special occasion! (5 stars)

In a landmarked building in Brooklyn, this remarkable, Victorian- design restaurant harkens back to 1879. We invited friends for brunch there and enjoyed a first class experience. First, the decor is exquisite (see photos) and their wait staff couldn't be friendlier. Then the food and drinks came! Their cocktails were well crafted (the Bloody Mary is a brunch favorite). We then enjoyed their poached eggs and sprouting broccoli on toast (so good!), fried chicken w/hush puppies & sriracha honey (to die for!), G&T steak and eggs (perfectly cooked steak & eggs) and finished the meal with their Brooklyn blackout cake (amazing!!) and fresh brewed delicious coffee. All this while surrounded by wonderful furniture, wall decor and lighting that transports you to an earlier, more civilized era. We have to return there for dinner! (5 stars)

Visited on 11/16 in the morning and had a reservation for one. I got seated quickly and the service started off well. The food was good overall, I had the House Rolls, steak with eggs, and fries. The fries were too salty and the rolls were average, but the steak with eggs was excellent with the sauce. The only downside was the constant check-ins; two different servers came by about every 15 minutes. I know they’re trying to be attentive, but it felt a bit rushed for someone who likes to eat slowly. (3 stars)

What an incredibly special place! Perfect for our anniversary celebration, although it's also the type of place you could go regularly without needing a special reason. Beautiful space where you just feel the history of it. Service was top notch from start to finish and the food was fantastic! Highly recommend the devila on horseback (bacon wrapped dates stuffed with cheese and almond), bone-in rib eye for two, and the baked Alaska. I already want to go back! (5 stars)

bio_text: Gallaghers Steakhouse, a historic dining establishment located in the heart of New York City and recently expanded to Boca Raton, offers a quintessential steakhouse experience steeped in nearly a century of tradition. Known for its vibrant atmosphere, adorned with memorabilia of Broadway stars and sports legends, Gallaghers provides a unique blend of classic charm and modern elegance, making it a favored destination for both locals and visitors alike. Gallaghers specializes in prime steaks, expertly aged and grilled to perfection. The menu features a classic steakhouse format, with an emphasis on high-quality cuts and traditional accompaniments, ensuring a memorable dining experience. Signature techniques include dry-aging beef in their iconic meat locker, enhancing the flavor and tenderness of their steaks. Gallaghers opened in 1927 as a speakeasy during Prohibition and transformed into Broadway's first steakhouse after the repeal of Prohibition in 1933. Over the years, it has been owned and operated by notable figures, including Helen Gallagher and Jack Solomon, and has undergone several renovations to preserve its legacy. In 2013, Dean Poll acquired Gallaghers with the vision of restoring its status as a premier steakhouse, and in 2023, a second location was opened in Boca Raton.

review_snippets: We had an excellent time at Gallaghers Steakhouse during our stay in New York. We chose to diner at the bar, which allowed us to fully enjoy the authentic and lively atmosphere of the place. As for the food, everything was outstanding. The filet mignon beef is of exceptional quality: it was perfectly cooked, beautifully seared on the outside while remaining warm at the center absolutely delicious. We also tried the veal parmigiana, which was incredibly generous. The portion is huge ! A special thank you as well to Stewart, who served us at the bar with great professionalism and kindness. His welcoming attitude and attention really made the experience even more enjoyable. An iconic address that we highly recommend. (5 stars)

Our experience at the Gallagher’s was excellent! We went for late lunch arrived at 2:15pm for our reservation on Tuesday and place was pretty packed. Appreciated the welcoming hospitality from staff members and old school yet dapper atmosphere. Very importantly the food did not disappoint. We ordered porter house for two and two lunch specials ( 3 course deal is probably the best lunch deal in the city). Manhattan chowder was very good and Lamb chops with house made mint sauce was also nice. and filet mignon was very tender and cooked well. Highlight of the meal was the flavorful dry aged porter house. Waiter told us it was 28days old , but wasn’t too buttery and was cooked to perfection! Very delicious and flavorful. I saw the banana split on the dessert menu and had to order them. And It was an excellent decision. Wonderful classic spot to visit can wait to return. I highly recommend Gallagher’s to everyone. (5 stars)

I’ve lived in NY and been back countless times, and somehow this was my first visit to Gallagher’s. No idea how I waited this long. The steaks were seriously impressive. Both the tomahawk and the strip loin came out perfectly charred on the outside, tender and juicy inside, exactly what you hope for at a classic steakhouse. Easily one of the top 10 steaks I’ve ever had. That deep, smoky crust with the rich beefy flavor… so good. The bacon was decent, personally I’d love it a bit thicker but it still hit the spot. The sides were solid and generous, nothing flashy, just dependable and well done. Service was surprisingly warm and attentive, honestly better than some other old-school spots around town. The whole experience just felt right. My only regret is not discovering this place sooner. Definitely coming back. (5 stars)

Gallagher’s was a great steakhouse experience. We just flew in and wanted to find a steakhouse in Manhattan. When we arrived we were warmly greeted (we had a reservation). The staff was attentive and our waiter, Mr. Nicholas, was fantastic. We ordered: Appetizers - Crab cake (you get one giant one per order), was awesome. Great flavor and a ton of crab. Calamari - tender and lightly breaded, and a wedge salad with blue cheese - delicious. Entrees- Rib Steak, medium rare - cooked perfectly and seasoned just right. Great char and incredibly tender., with sides of Mac and cheese and garlic fried green beans (this was the best side dish). It was a pricier dinner, but for the experience, quality of food, and the ambiance of a great Manhattan, New York restaurant - it was well worth it. I would highly recommend Gallagher’s, what a great dinner experience and service. (5 stars)

bio_text: Genesis House Restaurant offers an authentic journey into the heart of Korean cuisine, where bold flavors and traditional techniques come together in a modern dining experience. The restaurant features a living menu that harmonizes surprising flavors with fresh, locally sourced ingredients, inviting guests to explore a culinary expression of Korea. With a beautifully composed atmosphere, it caters to both relaxed daytime meals and intimate evening gatherings, ensuring a memorable dining experience. The culinary focus is distinctly Korean, with a menu inspired by centuries-old recipes. Guests can enjoy a variety of formats including a tasting menu, a la carte options, and curated lunch sets that allow for a personal dining experience. Signature techniques include the use of traditional preparation methods and seasonal ingredients.

review_snippets: Overall, this place is cute. It’s above a car dealership, which is still a little strange but it’s cute. The first time I went the drinks were just OK so I personally won’t get mixed drinks so the second time I went we got wine. My experience here have always been good when it comes to staff and the space. The drinks is iffy, but the food is also good. I may actually consider coming back here again for a third time which is very rare for me. Food – everything I ate was good and everything looked very presentable, beautiful even however, they stand out here with the tuna tartare. However, the tuna tartare does not come with chips or bread, which is kind of annoying, but the staff did recommend to get these crispy chip appetizer as a great side for that and honestly kudos to the staff that was a genius idea and it made me very happy. bio_text: Glin Thai Bistro offers a vibrant and modern dining experience that celebrates the rich flavors of Thai cuisine. With a focus on both classic and contemporary dishes, the restaurant provides a welcoming atmosphere perfect for casual dining, special occasions, and catering events. Guests can expect expertly crafted meals made from the freshest ingredients, served with a touch of love and attention to detail. Glin Thai Bistro specializes in authentic Thai cuisine, featuring a diverse menu that includes traditional favorites and unique interpretations. The restaurant offers a variety of dishes, including curry, pad see ew, and clay pot rice, served in a manner reminiscent of traditional Thai dining. Signature techniques include the use of heated serving trays and a focus on fresh, high-quality ingredients.
menu_items: Khai Look Keuy - Thai-style fried eggs in sweet tamarind sauce, topped with crispy shallots - $12.00
Muek Yang Prik Ong - Grilled baby squid served with olive oil and Northern Thai style tomato-chili dip (contains cilantro, garlic, shallots) - $15.00
Tuna Man Muang Salad - Fresh tuna salad with purple sweet potato, shallot, lemongrass, mint, and chili lime dressing - $15.00
Gui Chai (Chive Pancake) - Deep-fried chive pancake served with sweet soy sauce topped with fried shallot - $9.00
Thai Dumpling - Thai chicken and shrimp dumpling served with tangy soy sauce - $9.00
Chicken Satay - Grilled marinated chicken thighs with curry powder served with peanut sauce, Chinese fried dough and cucumber salad - $12.00
review_snippets: Service was great. Very friendly and patient server. However, I’m docking a star as it’s not 4.9/5 standard for food and overall experience compared to others in the city. The high rating here is little overrated. Generally good Thai but I wouldn’t travel here for Thai. Pad see yew had no wok taste, very ordinary 3/5. Branzino was good with a slightly spicy yellow curry sauce. Nicely grilled with crispy skin. But again I’m not blown away. 3.8/5. Mangosteen salad had mango, nuts and shallots which was sweet and yummy. Very unique fruit blend. 4/5. (4 stars)

I dine at this Thai restaurant over the holidays and I can see why they were selected to be in the Michelin Guide 2025. The floral decorations and creative wallpaper give ease and relaxation to its patrons. The low lighting and music makes this a perfect opportunity for birthday celebration, date nights, or just a fancy night out with friends and/or family. The food were phenomenal! My family and I enjoy the Ghang Phed Ped Yang (Duck Curry) the most. The curry was sweeten by the coconut milk, but it was not overly creamy. The bell peppers and basil gave it a nice kick, but did not make it too spicy. The curry was perfect with the rice and the crispy duck was tender and juicy too! Another favorite of ours was the Kra Pow Nuer. The Short ribs are crispy and flavorful. You can definitely tastes the various seasoning and spices used. The Crying Tiger was the dish that surprised me the most. I was worried that the grilled strip loin would be chewy or dry, but it was actually very tender and juicy! The spicy sauce was a nice touch to the meat, adding more flavor to the rice powder and fried garlic. I was disappointed that the Ghang Som Goong (Southern Curry) was sold out. Hopefully, when I return, I will get to try it! (5 stars)

My friends took me here to celebrate my birthday, and everything was amazing. The food was absolutely delicious, full of flavor, and beautifully prepared. The atmosphere was great, cozy and perfect for a special occasion. The staff were very friendly and attentive, especially JB, who provided excellent service with a warm smile and made the experience even more memorable. Overall, everything was perfect. Highly recommended! 🌟🍽️ (5 stars)

Glin Thai Bistro truly lives up to its high ratings. From the atmosphere to food quality, service, and overall value for money, everything is impressive and well above average for a neighborhood Thai spot. Here’s what I ordered: •Thai Dumpling: Thick and flavorful with a nicely seasoned filling. The only downside is the dipping sauce, which runs a bit too sweet. •Chive Pancake: Crispy on the outside and soft inside. It can get a little greasy after a few bites, but the dipping sauce helps balance it out. •Tom Yum Hotpot: Generous portion with shrimp, squid, mussels, and assorted mushrooms. The heavy use of cilantro adds a unique aroma that sets it apart from typical tom yum soups. The flavor leans slightly too sour, but overall it’s still worth trying. •Pad Thai Goong: This was the weakest dish, not much wok aroma, and the flavor felt somewhat flat. •Crab Curry: Packed with plenty of real crab meat and a richly flavored curry. Excellent when paired with rice, and arguably the standout dish of the meal. Overall, Glin Thai Bistro is a solid choice for anyone seeking Thai food that’s comfortably above average in every aspect. It’s a place I’d gladly return to. (4 stars)

bio_text: Gordo's Cantina is a vibrant dining destination located in Bushwick, Brooklyn, offering a lively atmosphere for both indoor and outdoor dining experiences. With a focus on casual, walk-in service, the restaurant invites guests to enjoy a relaxed meal without the need for reservations, making it an accessible choice for locals and visitors alike. Gordo's Cantina specializes in contemporary Mexican cuisine, featuring a menu that highlights bold flavors and fresh ingredients. The dining format is casual, with an emphasis on shareable plates and traditional dishes reimagined for a modern palate.
menu_items: Pork Shank - Pork shank, green beans, onions, tortillas, salsa

Tacos - Steak, peppers, onions, tortillas, sauces

review_snippets: Amazing gem in Bushwick. As a native New Yorker, this is the best Mexican I’ve ever had in NYC. Food combinations are stellar and pack a punch of flavor. The shrimp tacos were top notch, get those and the quesadillas with steak and also rajas leave you happy and satisfied. I wish my stomach could handle more food, I will be coming back over and over to this one. (5 stars)

My mom and I were visiting a family member at the nearby hospital and we wanted to get some lunch. She specifically wanted shrimp tacos and when we asked if they had them we were in luck because it was on their specials that day! We sat down around 2:30pm on a Saturday and we had a calm delicious lunch! I had the chicken tacos with some guacamole on the side. My portion was filling for me. The staff were upbeat and kind which we always love to see. I would definitely recommend a stop here!! (5 stars)

The food was great, chips and salsa variety were a nice touch (loved the garlic salsa the most). Their Michelada was exquisite and extremely flavorful. The tacos and pulled pork tacos hit the spot. Service was good too — would totally come back. (5 stars)
