bio_text: Gramercy Tavern, located in a historic landmark building just north of Union Square, is one of America's most beloved restaurants, celebrated for its contemporary American cuisine and warm hospitality. With a vibrant yet casual atmosphere, the restaurant offers a seasonal menu that highlights the best of local farms and purveyors, ensuring a unique dining experience for both lunch and dinner. The culinary focus at Gramercy Tavern is on contemporary American cuisine, featuring dishes prepared with ingredients sourced from local farms. The menu is served à la carte, with an emphasis on soulful flavors and techniques such as open wood-burning grilling. Opened in 1994 by restaurateur Danny Meyer, Gramercy Tavern has earned numerous accolades, including nine James Beard Awards and a Michelin Star since 2006. Chef Michael Anthony leads the kitchen, showcasing an ever-evolving seasonal menu.
menu_items: Seafood Platter - $54
Grilled Flatbread Seasonal Dips - $28
Roasted Oysters - Smoked Paprika, Garlic Breadcrumbs, Lemon - $27
Kabocha Squash Soup - Collard Greens, Turnips, Fennel - $20
Broccolini Salad - Walnuts, Turnips, Escarole - $25
Winter Citrus - Peanuts, Chicories, Roomano - $23
review_snippets: If I had to become a regular anywhere, this would be my pick. You can tell how impressive this restaurant is by the way they execute American cuisine—which, as you know, is usually my least favorite. But they absolutely nailed it. I was genuinely so pleased with everything. The farm chicken with the onion rings were standouts. Crispy, perfectly fried. The beef steak sandwich looked incredible, but I was way too full to even take a bite—so I’ll definitely be back and will keep you posted. The beef carpaccio was delicious, and while the mushrooms pasta were slightly salty, the creamy, flavorful sauce paired perfectly with the sweet potato bun. (This is their restaurant week menu!) And let me just say—the desserts are a must. You have to get the apple pie. It was amazing, especially with the hint of balsamic vinegar and Parmesan—holy moly!! The chocolate cake came with a woodside-flavored ice cream that I had never tried before, and I absolutely fell in love. The back room is stunning, and the service is easily the kind to deserve 30% tip—attentive, polished, and welcoming. This is also an amazing spot to bring your partner to meet the family! (5 stars)

We had lunch at Gramercy Tavern on Sunday with a group of four, seated in the Tavern area rather than the formal dining room. The cocktails were a fantastic start—absolutely 5 out of 5. The staff was warm and attentive, and the atmosphere was lively and welcoming. The flatbread was excellent, one of the highlights of the meal. But overall, I was hoping for a bit more from the rest of the food. We tried the burger, pork shoulder, swordfish, tomato salad, and liver mousse. While some dishes were fine, the burger and pork shoulder in particular were disappointing and just didn’t hit the mark. The salad and mousse also felt a little ordinary. For a place with such a strong reputation—and at this price point—I expected the dishes to shine more. Still, the service and vibe were wonderful, which made the experience enjoyable overall. If I had to rate it: 5 stars for service and ambiance, but about 3 stars for the food, so overall a solid 3 stars. (3 stars)

Excellent dinner from start to finish. The seasonal menu was thoughtful and well executed, with great balance and high-quality ingredients. The lamb main was cooked perfectly and full of flavor, and the overall pacing of the meal felt just right. Desserts were refined and not overly sweet. Professional service and a relaxed, elegant atmosphere. Would definitely return. (5 stars)

First off; special shout outs to Kamor and Morgan for exceptional service and for an exquisite experience. My daughter brother and I went out for my brothers birthday and had a phenomenal time. Thank you to the whole staff for their fluidity and expertise on every single dish that was presented. We shall return soon (5 stars)

review_snippets: A flight up the stairs, to the left of an infinity mirror and you enter Gui. It's a surprisingly big dining space, mixing moody contemporary with a bit of Korean tradition you can see in the mother of pearl decorating the restaurant and in the dishes. Their lunch options are select, so you won't see some of their dinner mains like their kimchi fried rice with wagyu but I think the options they do offer are currated really well. We tried their steak frite, their Gui burger, and their eggplant katsu. The steak has a charcoal cook and to really enjoy the meat it's cooked red in the center. Now, this can be off-putting to some and look raw but it is properly cooked and a good cut for such a cook. The burger was very good, just good meat, good components like the bun and cheese choice to make it a very satisfying choice. The eggplant katsu is a bit salty but I thought it was also worth trying. A great fry, good eggplant taste layered up like a lasagna, and a ragout sauce with good acid and tomato flavor to it. As for the desserts we tried their black and white cake and their Paris Jeju. Moist chocolate cake, layered with a spiced chocolate ganache and a small bit of miso caramel, not too sweet and so good. Their Paris Jeju was a deal stunner though. A spin off a Paris breast with a tea cream and blackberry jam all in a cream puff ring. Delicate, light, and perfectly balanced. With great service and great food, I feel like you can't go wrong coming here at least once. (5 stars)

At Gui Steakhouse in Times Square, the familiar rituals of the New York steakhouse are subtly reimagined through a Korean lens. The result is a menu that respects tradition while gently unsettling expectations—in the best way. The meal opens with a crudo of remarkable freshness, its clean flavors sharpened by thoughtful seasoning rather than overwhelmed by it. A shared plate of kimchi fried rice with wagyu follows, rich and deeply savory, each bite balancing fermented tang with the unmistakable depth of well-marbled beef. It is indulgent without tipping into excess. The prime rib, the restaurant’s centerpiece, arrives tender and carefully cooked, accompanied by a sauce that enhances rather than masks its natural flavor. Even dessert avoids heaviness: a baked Alaska that feels unexpectedly light, its sweetness restrained and precise. Gui Steakhouse succeeds not by reinventing the steakhouse, but by refining it—introducing Korean accents that feel integrated rather than ornamental. In a neighborhood known for spectacle, it offers something rarer: a sense of intention, and a meal that lingers in memory long after the last course. (5 stars)

Upon entering Gui, there’s a nice and elegant bar on the ground level where you can grab a quick drink. The elevator takes you to the second floor, which is where the restaurant is. Our waiter was friendly, walked us through the specials, and recommended a few entrées to share. We started with a few specialty cocktails, and each one was amazing in its own way. For appetizers, we ordered the A5 wagyu katsu sando and the yookhwe. The wagyu katsu sando literally melts in your mouth. I could eat ten of these! The seaweed chips paired perfectly with the yookhwe. For mains, we ordered the galbi, tomahawk, creamed corn, and roasted brussels sprouts. The galbi absolutely stole the show. It was thick cut, tender and flavorful. The presentation of the tomahawk was amazing, but didn't stand out, as it could've been seasoned better. Overall, we had a great experience, and I'll definitely be back to try more of their other dishes and drinks! (4 stars)

Great spot in Times Square for an upscale dinner before or after a show. The steak was cooked perfectly and had excellent flavor, and the Korean-inspired sides added a unique twist you don’t usually get at a classic steakhouse. The atmosphere is modern and stylish, though it can get a bit loud during peak hours. Service was friendly overall, but timing felt slightly rushed at times. Prices are on the higher side, but expected for the location and quality. Good for: date night, special occasions, pre-theater dining. Would come back for the steak and cocktails. (4 stars)
search_text: Gui A flight up the stairs, to the left of an infinity mirror and you enter Gui. It's a surprisingly big dining space, mixing moody contemporary with a bit of Korean tradition you can see in the mother of pearl decorating the restaurant and in the dishes. Their lunch options are select, so you won't see some of their dinner mains like their kimchi fried rice with wagyu but I think the options they do offer are currated really well. We tried their steak frite, their Gui burger, and their eggplant katsu. The steak has a charcoal cook and to really enjoy the meat it's cooked red in the center. Now, this can be off-putting to some and look raw but it is properly cooked and a good cut for such a cook. The burger was very good, just good meat, good components like the bun and cheese choice to make it a very satisfying choice. The eggplant katsu is a bit salty but I thought it was also worth trying. A great fry, good eggplant taste layered up like a lasagna, and a ragout sauce with good acid and tomato flavor to it. As for the desserts we tried their black and white cake and their Paris Jeju. Moist chocolate cake, layered with a spiced chocolate ganache and a small bit of miso caramel, not too sweet and so good. Their Paris Jeju was a deal stunner though. A spin off a Paris breast with a tea cream and blackberry jam all in a cream puff ring. Delicate, light, and perfectly balanced. With great service and great food, I feel like you can't go wrong coming here at least once. bio_text: Gus's Chop House is a welcoming neighborhood restaurant located in the heart of Brooklyn's Carroll Gardens. It offers a cozy atmosphere where guests can enjoy honest food and a curated selection of wines and cocktails, making it a perfect spot for both casual dining and special occasions. The restaurant focuses on classic American cuisine with an emphasis on high-quality meats and seasonal ingredients. The menu features a variety of dishes that highlight traditional cooking techniques, ensuring a memorable dining experience.
menu_items: Buttermilk Biscuits - Sorghum, Butter & Pimento Cheese - $14
Nduja Stuffed Dates - Goat Cheese & Aged Balsamic Vinegar - $17
Hash Browns - Crème Fraîche, Trout Roe & Everything Spice - $21
Simple Salad - Radishes & Bistro Vinaigrette - $17
Crispy Skate Cheeks - Tartar Sauce - $19
Gem Caesar - Anchovies, Parmesan & Focaccia Croutons - $21
review_snippets: Went for Thanksgiving lunch special and it was awesome and very filling and delicious. The service was Al’s excellent. Looking forward to coming back. (5 stars)

The place has an upscale casual feel. The service is excellent, fast and attentive. The dishes are creative and delicious. The hash browns were perfectly cooked and the topping is outstanding. The croquettes didn't have a lot of fish taste, the tomato sauce was great. The burger was outstanding, juicy, cheesy, the crust was a bit salty. The cheesecake was fluffy, creamy. Would definitely recommend! (5 stars)

Food was mediocre at best. Service was fine. Spacious. Mediocre across the board. Nothing bad at all. But also nothing remarkable. Seems popular with the locals. The green salad was good. Crisp. Fresh. Good flavors. The hash browns were crispy on the outside and tender on the inside. Great creme fraiche dip. The pork chop was small. You can sort of share it. The salsa verde was just okay. Not evenly cooked. One side was more tender than the other. Rather thin. A unremarkable dish I would. Very pedestrian. More like someone's home cooking. The gemelli pasta was okay. I can make the same dish at home. Just a few shavings of guanciale. Nothing bad about this dish. But again nothing remarkable. The burger we saw on Instagram was good. But it's a mix of beef and pork. The taste and texture is more like an Italian sausage. The slaw on top was good. But definitely not worth the trip to get to. Again, just mediocre food. I can make a more beefy burger at home. The basque cheese cake was a tad overcooked. I think 15 min LESS in the oven would have resulted in a more creamy center. It was a big slice but it was dry. The texture was spongy and cakey overall. Not great. The maple pie was the star of the entire dinner. It was light and velvety. There was a hint of brown butter. Not overly sweet. With a night amount of maple 🍁. The crust was flaky and crispy. The dollop of cream on top was just excellent. This was an incredible slice of pie. Service was good overall. Water was filled. Dishes were taken away promptly. The wait staff were attentive. The bathrooms were clean. But the food was overall underwhelming. (3 stars)

We hosted a private event at Gus's (dinner after a city hall wedding) and had an AMAZING experience. The manager, Megan, was so helpful to work with throughout -- she was a thought partner on food and decor choices, she coordinated with our other vendors, and most importantly made sure that the event itself went off without a hitch! The ambiance was on point and the food was DELICIOUS -- all of our guests have been raving about it since then!! The staff was also super warm and helped make the event feel extra special. (An extra shout out to the bartender Andrew for cracking jokes all night). Highly recommend Gus's under any circumstance!! (5 stars)

bio_text: Haenyeo Restaurant is a tribute to the legendary female divers of Jeju Island, South Korea, embodying their spirit of resilience and community. Located in Park Slope, Brooklyn, this serene and charming space features a modern aesthetic with white hues and brick walls, creating a welcoming atmosphere for diners. The restaurant offers an authentic Korean home-cooking experience, focusing on traditional dishes with a contemporary urban twist, making it a beloved destination for both locals and visitors. Haenyeo specializes in authentic Korean home-cooking, emphasizing everyday dishes that are both delicious and approachable. The menu features a variety of seafood and traditional ingredients, with signature dishes like the Rice Cake Fundido that showcase a blend of Korean and urban culinary influences. Haenyeo is led by chef Jenny Kwak, a pioneer in introducing authentic Korean cuisine to New York City. She previously opened Dok Suni's and DoHwa, further establishing her reputation in the culinary scene.
menu_items: Rice Cake Fundido - Korean rice cakes, cheese, chorizo - $16
French-Korean Bouillabaisse - Seafood, spicy Korean fish stew base - $24
Scallion Pancakes - Scallions, batter - $12
Oysters - Oysters, breadcrumbs, lemon - $18
Dumplings - Dough, filling - $14
Salmon Salad - Salmon, avocado, greens - $16
review_snippets: What a fantastic experience!! We entered with high expectations and enjoyed a meal that exceeded them. The food and service were impeccable. Starters we sampled included the expertly composed Fluke Crudo (which was refreshing and delicious), Gamja Buchim (tuna sashimi on a potato pancake with wasabi-infused sour cream!), Dukboki Fundido (an incredible internationally-influenced dish incorporating Oaxacan cheese and Mexican chorizo alongside thick Asian noodles) and Grilled Oysters (savory and delicious with butter and herbs). All were exceptional. For entrees, we greatly enjoyed Maine Uni Bibimbap (possibly our favorite dish of the night, absolutely delicious!) and the Bulgogi (some of the best I’ve had anywhere). Throughout the evening, we tried 3 cocktails: The Squid & The Whale was my first drink of the night, and the sesame oil and egg whites were a fantastic treat for my palate. Drink 2 was Seoul Train, similar to a Manhattan with a clever addition of plum wine. My final drink of the night was the NY Sleepover, a delightful sour topped with a Chianti float. The desserts are impressive as well — the Beignets were soft, fluffy, fresh, and impossible to deny even with a full stomach. The crème brûlée was a sweet and elegant finish to a perfect meal. Thanks to the kind and attentive staff, the talented chefs, and everyone who made our meal and evening unforgettable. Park Slope is blessed to have Haenyeo, but diners from all over should make an effort to visit this exceptional restaurant. (5 stars)

Beautiful spot in Park Slope. This time around I only had a cocktail because of limited time. Our bartender was still training and he was so friendly and knew the menu very well to help make suggestions. My friend and I both loved our drinks, will try the food next time-smelled amazing. (5 stars)

This is definitely not average Korean restaurant, it is so contemporary that you get hint of it's Korean heritage only by reading menu (for better or worse). The place, if I am not mistaken it is mentioned in Michelin Guide, but in my opinion worth a star. The food was delicious and although by the end I was so full I couldn't stop eating until the plate was clean. Kalbi jjim which is short ribs and Bulgogi were out of this world! Again I have failed to try their dessert, but definitely will make another trip to this place, hopefully getting chance to try them. The place is very popular so reservation is recommend. (5 stars)

I wish I came to Haenyeo earlier on because I’d hands down say this is the best restaurant in Park Slope. The vibe inside, the staff, and the food are up to standard with some of the best restaurants in the city. Some standouts are their kimchi and bulgogi but I really didn’t have anything that was below average. I 100% will be back soon, hopefully when people are in town so we can show them some delicious food. Would highly recommend if you’re in the area (or even outside the area and are reading this). (5 stars)

review_snippets: Note- Shortened review due to character limits. I was at this unique restaurant a couple of months ago with one of my groups for their PWYC Farm Dinner Series, which featured a changing five-course menu each week and featured produce from the Union Square Farmers Market. The staff were friendly, and I liked the design inside. The menu was as stated PWYC (Pay What You Can,) and an abridged version of their standard $165/$125 prix fixe, with a suggested price of $100, regardless of whether it was the Omnivore or Vegan version. For a drink, I went with a Yesfolk hojicha non-alcoholic kombucha for $13, which was delicious. In general, the portions were rather meek, so I'm not going to mention this again, or else I'd be repeating. The first course was Marinated Spigarello with charred balmuda potatoes, tarragon, and dashi. Spigarello is similar to a milder broccoli rabe, and the few pieces had a light herbal flavor from the tarragon. The dashi was very light while the potatoes were lightly fried. This was fine, though the flavors were a little bit too mild for my taste. The next course was the Polenta with ratatouille. The polenta itself was both silky and a bit gloopy. The vegetables had a mix of textures, though I didn't find that any of them paired well with the polenta. There was also something which I'm pretty sure was pimento cheese, which was a unique and fun idea, even coming from someone who isn't the hugest fan of said condiment. The dish was alright, though desperately missing a sauce. For instance, a very similar dish at a Mediterranean/Italian place added a bright tomato sauce that added some depth. Next was the Black Bass with grilled pole beans and golden tomatillo. While not the largest portion, this was presumably one of the mains and the largest dish, with the fish cooked nicely. While another person felt that it could have had a bit of char or firmness, I liked the texture and how soft and buttery it was. The beans had a lightly firm texture that went well with the fish, while the tomatillo had a pleasant sourness. This was my favorite dish of the night. The fourth course was the Quail with sweet potato greens, hazelnut, and okra. This dainty dish consisted of half a quail with a leg and some meat next to it, with some greens on top of the meat and some on the side with the okra, which I believe was pan-fried. The greens had a similar texture to cooked spinach, which was nice with the small bit of quail, though I couldn't taste hazelnuts in any of the dish. The bit of okra was nicely cooked and went well with the greens. Aside from the listed ingredients, there was also a slightly dark green sauce on the side, which I believe was yuzu kosho, a fermented condiment used in some Japanese cooking. This added a slightly punchy flavor to the dish, which was otherwise pretty light, and was a much-needed addition. This was also good, and I'd likely pay around $30 at a similarly fancy spot for a whole quail version, though I am not sure if the greens would work well enough for an entire dish/if the flavor would get boring after a while. The final course was dessert, which was a Plum Cobbler with lemon thyme and jalapeño. The cake itself on the bottom had a peculiar texture, being soft, thick, and slightly chewy, and it didn't really remind me of any cobbler I've had before. I'm not exactly sure if I liked it, and the others weren't particularly happy with it either. The dish was on the bitter-sweet side, being very citrusy with a bit of spice from the pepper. Otherwise, the ice cream on top added a slight sweetness to the dish. I personally thought that this was fine, but others disliked it. While I like and fully support this restaurant's messages and themes, I didn't think the food was worth the price point (we paid $78 each, or $60 + tax/tip.) We left half full, and I would be hesitant to go back and try their much more expensive tasting menu, as some of the flavors just didn't really work together either. (3 stars)

Celebrated an anniversary here this week—the food was delicious and the staff are wonderful. Three highlights for me were the vegan cheese course, the caramelized tempeh, and the carrot dessert! They have an excellent wine selection and a beautiful space. (5 stars)

Absolutely phenomenal! This was hands-down one of the most exceptional and creatively executed tasting menus I’ve ever had—vegan or otherwise. Every course was a masterclass in flavor, texture, and presentation. You can tell the chef isn’t just cooking plant-based food; they’re creating art with it. From the first bite to the last, each dish was thoughtfully composed, showcasing unexpected ingredients and bold, vibrant flavors that played off each other beautifully. The pacing of the courses was perfect, and the staff were incredibly knowledgeable, walking us through the inspiration and elements of each plate. Whether you’re vegan or simply a lover of great food, this is the kind of dining experience that sticks with you. It’s a rare gem that pushes boundaries while staying deeply satisfying. The all female chef staff was also amazing to see in action. Highly recommend! (5 stars)

The food and service at HAGS was flawless. The various dishes were delicious and creative. There was perfect timing between the courses. Everything was done with genuine love. It’s obvious that a tremendous amount of thought and care went into everything — from the menu — to the decor — to the service. There’s an amazing vegan and omnivore menu. The vegan cheeses and butters are made in-house — and taste incredible. The kitchen staff accommodated my dietary restrictions — and added a creative flair. It’s a really cute, queer-owned restaurant. It’s a tiny spot — but everything is very well organized. Everyone feels welcomed, with the full complexity of their identities. HAGS was perfect in every way. I highly recommend it. 5/5 stars. (5 stars)

From the first bite to the last, each dish was thoughtfully composed, showcasing unexpected ingredients and bold, vibrant flavors that played off each other beautifully. The pacing of the courses was perfect, and the staff were incredibly knowledgeable, walking us through the inspiration and elements of each plate. Whether you’re vegan or simply a lover of great food, this is the kind of dining experience that sticks with you. It’s a rare gem that pushes boundaries while staying deeply satisfying. The all female chef staff was also amazing to see in action. Highly recommend! (5 stars) The food and service at HAGS was flawless. The various dishes were delicious and creative. There was perfect timing between the courses. Everything was done with genuine love. It’s obvious that a tremendous amount of thought and care went into everything — from the menu — to the decor — to the service. There’s an amazing vegan and omnivore menu. The vegan cheeses and butters are made in-house — and taste incredible. The kitchen staff accommodated my dietary restrictions — and added a creative flair. It’s a really cute, queer-owned restaurant. It’s a tiny spot — but everything is very well organized. Everyone feels welcomed, with the full complexity of their identities. HAGS was perfect in every way. I highly recommend it. 5/5 stars. (5 stars)

bio_text: HanGawi is a serene Korean restaurant located in the heart of Manhattan, offering a unique dining experience that transcends mere sustenance. Since its inception in 1994, the restaurant has provided a tranquil sanctuary where guests can immerse themselves in the rich traditions of Korean plant-based cuisine. The ambiance is designed to promote calmness and mindfulness, featuring low tables, warm wooden floors, and muted lighting that encourages diners to savor each moment. HanGawi specializes in Korean plant-based cuisine, focusing on harmony with nature through the use of root vegetables, mountain greens, heirloom grains, and herbal infusions. The menu features signature dishes such as sizzling stone bowls and hand-wrapped ssam bap, all prepared with intention to nourish and uplift. Since 1994, Hangawi has offered more than just a meal, welcoming guests into a quiet sanctuary rooted in the deep traditions of Korean plant-based cuisine.
menu_items: Vermicelli delight - Korean sweet potato noodles with assorted vegetables marinated with soy sauce - $17
Spicy Korean cauliflower bites - with vegan mayonnaise dip - $18
Spicy perilla leaf tofu patties - minced oyster mushrooms and tofu wrapped in perilla leaves - $19
Stuffed shiitake mushrooms - plant based Korean ‘bulgogi’ bossam bites with pickled radish and mushrooms in spicy sauce - $19
Korean kochi skewers - skewers featuring mushroom head, asparagus, scallion and sweet chili - $19
Organic wheat free kale pancakes - made with sweet rice flour - $20
review_snippets: I recently visited Hangawi and had such a unique and memorable experience. We chose the traditional floor seating option, which instantly made the evening feel special and immersive. It was a fun way to enjoy the meal and really added to the authenticity of the experience. From the moment we walked in, the service stood out. The attendants kindly took our shoes and jackets, which felt incredibly thoughtful and welcoming. The servers were attentive and patient, taking the time to explain the menu in detail and answering all of our questions with care. The cauliflower bites were absolutely amazing and easily my favorite dish of the night. They were packed with flavor and had the perfect texture. The dumpling soup was also comforting and delicious, making it another highlight of the meal. The pancakes, however, were not as appealing to me. I usually enjoy seafood pancakes, and since this is a fully vegan restaurant, I understand the limitation. That said, I felt the flavors could have been a bit more innovative or bold, as they came across slightly bland compared to the other dishes. The plant based Korean bulgogi stone bowl rice was excellent. It came with kimchi, spicy sauce, and a milder sauce, and everything together was flavorful and satisfying. Each bite felt well balanced and thoughtfully prepared. Overall, Hangawi is a lovely place to visit at least once or twice, especially if you want to experience traditional Korean floor seating in a calm and beautifully maintained setting. It is more than just a meal, it is an experience. (4 stars)

This restaurant is an absolute gem and one of its kind. Having a vegan Korean restaurant in the city is truly a blessing and the food, experience, and staff here are all truly exceptional. We tried the emperors mini lunch menu that includes a soup, appetizer, entree, and dessert and it was so worth it! It was a great way to try a little bit of everything and the portions were very substantial. All of the food tasted so fresh, flavorful, and packed with vegetables. I loved the pumpkin porridge, sweet corn soup, and rice cakes. Both the stuffed mushrooms and combination rolls were delicious and so unique. Soy chocolate ice cream for dessert was light and tasty. Lastly, it’s so wonderful sitting without shoes in the cozy environment and heated floors. Would absolutely come here and again and it’s now one of my favorite spots! (5 stars)

Hangwai is an absolute standout—one of those restaurants where every detail feels intentional, from the warm atmosphere to the beautifully plated dishes. The menu is creative without being pretentious, and the flavors are exceptionally well balanced. We especially recommend the mushroom truffle dish, which was the star of the night. The truffle aroma hits you before the first bite, and the combination of earthy mushrooms and rich, silky truffle is unbelievably good. It’s the kind of dish you instantly want to order again, even before you’re finished with it. Service was friendly and attentive, and the pacing of the meal was perfect. Hangwai strikes that rare balance of being refined yet comfortable—an excellent choice for a special night out or a memorable meal with friends. (5 stars)

Hangawi offers a serene, temple like dining experience that complements its food beautifully. The spicy perilla tofu bites were outstanding, packed with flavor from minced oyster mushrooms and tofu, while the black truffle dumplings were earthy and pleasant though not the most memorable. The spicy kimchi stone bowl bibimbap was a clear standout with bold kimchi and crunchy vegetables, and the combination kimbap with garden veggies,bulgogi, kimchi, and crispy mushroom stuffing was deeply satisfying, with the kimbap and bibimbap being my favorites overall. The date paste tea was also very good, with small chunks of dates that added natural sweetness and texture. Service was warm and attentive throughout, with thoughtful greetings and care, and the shoes off seating added to the calm, meditative atmosphere. Overall, I was genuinely a fan, it felt intentional, comforting, and well executed. (5 stars)

bio_text: Hart's is a charming neighborhood restaurant located in Brooklyn, New York, offering a warm and inviting atmosphere for diners. With a focus on seasonal ingredients sourced from local farms, the restaurant provides a unique dining experience that changes daily, reflecting the best of what is available. Guests can enjoy their meals indoors year-round or, during the warmer months, dine al fresco on the patio. Hart's specializes in a seasonal menu that is updated daily, emphasizing fresh, local ingredients. The cuisine is rooted in a commitment to quality and sustainability, showcasing the best of what local farms have to offer. Hart's opened in the fall of 2016, inspired by a desire to create a community-focused dining experience.
menu_items: Olives - $8
Grilled asparagus with vermouth butter and lemon - $17
Tuna conserva on toast with spinach and capers - $19
Cara caras with olives, green garlic and colatura - $18
Shrimp with calabrian chili - $21
Little gems with anchodinas and pecorino - $18
review_snippets: I’m glad I got to try this restaurant. Located right next to the S train, Hart’s is a seafood, olive oil, simple menu focused eatery. I appreciated the quality of the olive oil and the bread. The lamb burger was pretty damn good too. The tomato salad was one of the best I’ve had. A bit too pricey for the food and quantity, but hey, I’d come back again. (5 stars)
Most dishes except clam toast polish panceda were awesome. Clams were bit too tiny with not much of meat in it. Atmosphere was good. Service was great. (4 stars)

Loved everything about this place! The food was uncomplicated in the best way - fresh, straightforward, and delicious. The clam toast and gem salad stood out as particularly incredible. It's a great place for a date or small group to share plates so you can try a lot of different things! The atmosphere is cozy and cute, and the service was great. We will be coming back here regularly! (5 stars)

Hart’s is a stylish and cozy spot. Made a reservation earlier this week for a 6:30PM dinner and there were a few other patrons. By the time we were done, the place was full and lively! Since it is a small spot, making a reservation is a good call. The food was delicious and all had a fun ingredient detail to it. Drinks are great too! Go check out Hart for an intimate dinner experience. (5 stars)

bio_text: Hav & Mar is a vibrant seafood house located in the renowned arts district of Chelsea, NYC, created by Chef Marcus Samuelsson. The restaurant features a stunning dining room and bar that blend contemporary and classical design, adorned with original artwork by award-winning artist Derrick Adams. With a focus on gracious hospitality, show-stopping cocktails, and a groundbreaking wine list, Hav & Mar offers a convivial and festive atmosphere, making it a standout destination for seafood lovers. The menu at Hav & Mar is globally inspired, emphasizing thoughtfully sourced seafood and seasonal greenmarket produce. It showcases a variety of dishes that reflect Chef Samuelsson's culinary expertise and creativity. The restaurant is known for its energetic approach to seafood dining. Hav & Mar is led by Chef Marcus Samuelsson and Executive Chef Fariyal Abdullahi, and has received notable recognition, including two stars from The New York Times.
review_snippets: A friend and I tried the new chef's table experience, and it was spectacular. A front seat view to the bustling kitchen, and personalized attention from the executive chef herself. Plus chef Samuelsson also made an appearance, though I imagine that's not the typical experience. But the treating menu was varied, creative, and delicious -- everything one would expect from Hav & Mar, which is overdue for a Michelin star. (5 stars)

This is THE fav in my top 10. Celebrated my birthday here this year and it was a vibe. Though a snow storm was approaching the atmosphere led you down another path and made you forget about all that was going on outside those doors. Tried the ribeye this time around. Succulent and well seasoned.. the perfect temp that I requested. We got the bread basket this time and I vacuumed every crumb. The plantain chutney was the best condiment I’ve had in a while and I’d love to explore more combinations with it. Apple of my Thyme was the perfect end to the meal and the pavlova was bursting with citrus. I need to rotate here every month just to get a feel of the overall menu. (5 stars)

Had an amazing dinner at Hav + Mar! The food was so good , literally everything we ordered was delicious except the crêpes, which were honestly the only miss of the night. The service was excellent from start to finish, super friendly and attentive without being overbearing. The ambiance is really cute too: warm lighting, great music, and a vibe that works perfectly for a date night or a dinner out with friends. Overall, definitely recommend and would happily go back! (5 stars)

This was the best meal I’ve had in nyc and I’ve been dining out 2x a week here for 5 years. Incredible setting, service and the food was warm, engaging, incredibly well integrated and interesting. 11/10 ⭐️ can’t wait to return. Ps. Thanks Christian for great service. (5 stars)

restaurant_name: Hometown Bar B Que New York
bio_text: Hometown Bar-B-Que, located in Red Hook, Brooklyn, is celebrated for its authentic pit-smoked barbecue, earning accolades as New York's best barbecue restaurant. The vibrant atmosphere invites diners to enjoy their meals served on butcher paper-lined metal trays, complemented by a selection of traditional sides and desserts. With a focus on community and flavor, Hometown offers a unique dining experience where guests can engage with one another while savoring expertly crafted dishes and live music on weekends. Hometown specializes in authentic, pit-smoked meats prepared using classic Southern techniques, particularly smoking on oak wood. The menu features a variety of flavor profiles that reflect the local community, alongside traditional sides and desserts. The dining format includes walk-up service on a first-come, first-served basis until sold out. Hometown Bar-B-Que opened in Red Hook, Brooklyn, in September 2013.
menu_items: Brisket - $20
Pulled Pork - $17
Turkey - $20
Spare Ribs - $16
Beef Rib - $40
Korean Sticky Ribs - Korean BBQ sauce, scallion, cashews, fried shallots & garlic - $32
review_snippets: This was easily one of the best steaks I’ve tried. I’ve had similar preparations in many places, but this one truly stood out. From the moment I walked in, the aroma of smoke and perfectly cooked meat immediately caught my attention and set the tone for the experience. The atmosphere is very pleasant and comfortable, making the whole visit even more enjoyable. I left very satisfied and will definitely be coming back again.🥩❤️ (5 stars)

WHAT DO THEY DO TO THIS NACHO CHEESE DIP TO MAKE IT SO PERFECT?! It’s perfect. I’d never order this of my own will but my friend ordered it and what a great decision that was. The cornbread is great. All the meat is great. A 1/2 lb of meat per person is definitely enough, especially if you get 1-2 sides. This isn’t the cheapest spot. 2 sides and 2 1/2 lbs of meat was $75 (fed 2 people and was a lot of food). I LOVE that they have Stiegl! And they have special really great mugs for the radlers. Lots of seating. There was a long line on a Saturday at 7pm and it moved slow. (5 stars)

Absolute hands down best BBQ joint in NY and perhaps best I’ve ever had. All the hype about Hometown is on point. Super casual and super friendly staff. You have the choice of both indoor and outdoor seating. Every item on their menu is to die but the ultimate is the pastrami sandwich. YES you heard me right! This sandwich is even better than Katz’s. More bark, more tender, juicier and let’s not forget the buttered rye bread. Bottom line, there is not a single item on their menu that is not worth devouring. (5 stars)

10/10 experience. Food, drinks and service, seriously all outstanding. I like the laid-back atmosphere and the fact that they have good quality napkins. Meat was beautifully cooked and so flavorful. The sides? Perfection. As a southwestern girl I could dream of nothing better. And they were playing steely dan 💯 (5 stars)

bio_text: Hungry Thirsty is a vibrant Thai restaurant located in Brooklyn, dedicated to bringing the authentic flavors and culinary traditions of Thailand to the local community. The restaurant offers a warm and inviting atmosphere, perfect for enjoying home-style dishes that celebrate the rich heritage of Thai cuisine. With a focus on vibrant flavors and a commitment to quality, Hungry Thirsty provides a unique dining experience that transports guests to the heart of Thailand. Hungry Thirsty specializes in authentic Thai cuisine, featuring a menu that highlights home-style dishes inspired by the diverse regions of Thailand. The restaurant offers a selection of signature dishes, including Spicy Beef Curry and Hat-Yai Styled Fried Chicken, showcasing bold flavors and traditional cooking techniques.
menu_items: Khao Soi - Chicken & Creamy coconut curry noodle soup - $33
Kai Tod Hat-Yai - Hat-Yai Styled Fried Chicken & Sticky Rice - $35
Khoong Ma-Kham - Jumbo prawn & special tamarind sauce - $38
Chu Chee Kai Pu - Crab, Fried boiled eggs & Chu Chee Curry - $55
Khoong Muk Kai Kem - Shrimp, Squid & Salted duck egg yolk - $29
Kua Kling - Ground pork & Kua kling curry paste - $37
review_snippets: Loved our dinner at Hungry Thirsty. Every dish was incredibly flavorful, loved the pad krapow and moo waan. They aren’t joking about the spice levels they denote, so if you’re sensitive Mae sure you pay attention. They have a really large beer menu, so you have plenty of fun options to choose from to break the heat. The service is fast and super friendly. They seem to change the menu often, looking forward to trying more of their wonderful dishes! (5 stars)

We stopped into Hungry Thirsty on a freezing night, and boy did they warm us up! The people are so genuine and welcoming, and the food does not disappoint! It’s some of the most authentic Thai in the city, the chef specials are to die for, and the spice level is real. If you wanna go to Thailand, but not spend the money on the ticket, this is the place for you!!! (5 stars)

The menu was unlike any other Thai place I’ve ate at before. The branzino dish was phenomenal with perfectly crunch garlic topping and a zesty sweet sauce. The prawns were massive and paired very well with the tamarind s sauce. Our server Sherlyn was very kind and helped us navigate our dietary restrictions and provided great recommendations. Loved this meal and will be back to try other things. (5 stars)
Food is authentic as it could be! Can’t wait to try their other dish in the menu. Good selection of dishes and very friendly staff! Will definitely come back :) (5 stars)

(5 stars) Food is authentic as it could be! Can’t wait to try their other dish in the menu. Good selection of dishes and very friendly staff! Will definitely come back :) (5 stars)

bio_text: Hupo is a vibrant dining destination in Long Island City, NY, specializing in authentic Sichuan cuisine. The restaurant is known for its fast, friendly service and a welcoming atmosphere, making it a go-to spot for those seeking bold flavors and a satisfying meal. Guests can enjoy a variety of dishes, including spicy dumplings, savory stir-fries, and flavorful rice bowls, all crafted with fresh ingredients and traditional techniques. Hupo focuses on authentic Sichuan flavors, featuring a menu that includes spicy dumplings, bold noodle dishes, and savory stir-fries. The restaurant emphasizes fresh ingredients and traditional cooking methods, with signature dishes like pork soup dumplings and Dan Dan noodles.
menu_items: Chungking Spicy Chicken
Crispy Fish Fillet
Ma-La Szechuan Prawns - 8 Pcs
Ma-la Szechuan Wonton - 8
Cumin Lamb - $25 - $30
review_snippets: Good food and a nice atmosphere. I do wish the Szechuan food was a little more spicy, but the dishes we got, like Shrimp with silken tofu, Szechuan fish fillet with tofu, Dan Dan noodles, and Green Beans was very good. Prices are a little high and portions were small compared to Flushing, but the difference was not extravagant, and for three people we were able to be full for about $90 pre-tip, which is respectable. (5 stars)

Spent a chill late afternoon here. The cocktail is soooooo good! Highly recommended. The Chinese food is authentic although the chicken dish is bit plain. Tofu with beef is the best one out of the 5 dishes we ordered. (5 stars)

I had a such a satisfying experience here. Everything tasted freshly made and well-prepared. The mapo tofu stood out the most. Soft tofu in a rich, savory sauce with just the right amount of numbing Sichuan spice. I also got the ma-la wontons another favorite Everything felt well-seasoned, comforting, and combined with the quick, efficient service, HUPO is definitely a place I’d return to when I’m craving bold, comforting Chinese food done right! (5 stars)

been going here for years but the portions have gotten so much smaller... Not sure if I can justify the price anymore. Ordered a dry Hotpot for $36! This was the portion. Laughable. 3 pieces of beef, 3 pieces of fish tofu and some mushroom. Will never be ordering here again. (1 stars)

bio_text: Huso, located in Tribeca, offers a refined fine-dining experience under the guidance of Executive Chef Buddha Lo. With a focus on warm hospitality and thoughtful service, the restaurant presents an evolving tasting menu that highlights the best seasonal ingredients. The ambiance reflects a commitment to precision and creativity, making it a standout destination for discerning diners. Huso specializes in contemporary tasting menus that emphasize seasonality and technique. The culinary approach is ingredient-driven, showcasing a range of caviar and other seasonal delicacies. The menu is designed to balance creativity with restraint, ensuring a memorable dining experience. Huso originally began in 2019 inside Marky’s Caviar on Madison Avenue as an intimate 12-seat tasting counter. It has since moved to a larger location in Tribeca, where it has earned a One MICHELIN Star in 2025 and recognition as one of Robb Report’s 10 Best New Restaurants in America.
menu_items: Scallop, Ajo Blanco, Caviar
Steelhead Trout, English Peas, Tarragon
Violet Artichoke, Comte, Barigoule
Young Potatoes, Smoked Sturgeon, Caviar
Foie Gras, Ham Presse, Brioche
Bluefin Tuna, Kohlrabi, Tomato
review_snippets: Huso is my new favorite restaurant in NYC, and the finest overall dining experience I’ve had in nearly 19 years of living here and eating at the very best. From start to finish, the evening was pure perfection. The ambiance was serene and beautiful — like a high-end spa — setting the tone for a meal that was as thoughtful as it was exceptional. The 10+ course tasting menu was exquisite, highly original, and perfectly portioned; unlike most prix fixe meals, I left feeling neither hungry nor overfull. While the entire meal was one collective standout, the egg and lobster with caviar, scallop with sunchoke and kombucha, beef with mushroom and périgord, and the grape, Sauternes, and olive oil palate cleanser were especially memorable. The flavors were unusual, precise, and utterly flawless. Pacing was spot on throughout. Now, onto the service, which was not merely excellent but genuinely rare. Every interaction was intuitive, seamless, and perfectly calibrated: warm but professional, polished without stiffness, attentive without intrusion. The staff anticipated needs before they arose and executed each moment with calm confidence and absolute precision. It was, quite simply, the most refined and enjoyable service experience I have ever had, anywhere. I regret not noting every name, but I want to give special thanks to Gurman, Holly, and Madeline, each of whom exemplified this standard. You are all outstanding at what you do — thank you so much! An unexpected highlight was a tour of the kitchen, which is itself stunning (and immaculately clean). Getting to watch Buddha Lo and his team in their element was a privilege and underscored just how much intention and craft sits behind every course. Additional Michelin recognition feels inevitable, and I already can’t wait to return for the spring menu. (5 stars)

Had a wonderful dining experience at Huso celebrating my birthday. It's been somewhere I've wanted to try for a while having followed chef Buddha Lo's journey. The experience did not disappoint. The Fall 2015 tasting menu is phenomenally innovative, with nods to seasonal ingredients, flavors and presentation. They are very much deserving of their recent Michelin star. I highly recommend a wine pairing. The non alcoholic pairing was wonderful and went perfectly with each course. Although every course was delicious and memorable, my favorite was the milk roll, foie gras, truffle course with mushroom tea. The hospitality team also went above and beyond to ensure my birthday was memorable. I loved the birthday dessert presentation, tour of the kitchen, and signed Polaroid to remember the experience. Huso is a beautiful restaurant to spend a special occasion and I can't wait to see what chef does next. I might just have to come back for each seasonal menu! (5 stars)

Huso was probably the most special meal I’ve ever had. It truly felt like an experience from start to finish. The food was incredibly unique, elegant, and complex, with nothing feeling like an afterthought. Every course was beautifully prepared and memorable, making it impossible to choose a single favorite. The staff were exceptional, and I especially appreciated the kitchen tour and the chance to talk with Chef Buddha Lo. The food was unlike anything I’ve had before, and the entire evening truly special. (5 stars)

We celebrated my birthday at Huso not long after they opened, and it was such a memorable night. One of the coolest things about the restaurant is that they own their own caviar farm in Florida, and it definitely shows with caviar is woven into the tasting menu in a really generous way. It’s a very small, intimate space with only about 8–10 tables, which made the whole evening feel special and personal. The service was smooth and attentive. The food itself was incredible, with really interesting flavor combinations and beautiful presentation, though it’s definitely a caviar-forward experience. The tasting menu was easily 15–20 courses including all the little bites. By the end I was completely stuffed and honestly a little nauseous (in the best way?), and I haven’t done another tasting menu since. :)) Still, it was an unforgettable way to celebrate and a truly unique dining experience. It was clear they’d get a Michelin star and i was delighted to hear they recently did. Well deserved! (5 stars)

bio_text: Hyderabadi Zaiqa is a culinary haven located in the heart of Manhattan, New York, where the vibrant and diverse cuisine of India comes alive. The restaurant offers an exquisite ambiance that combines elegance and charm, featuring intricate artwork and a harmonious fusion of rich colors that pay homage to Indian cultural heritage. Guests are welcomed into a warm and inviting atmosphere, enhanced by soft lighting and comfortable seating, setting the stage for an unforgettable dining experience that transcends borders. Hyderabadi Zaiqa specializes in authentic Hyderabadi cuisine, showcasing a captivating fusion of flavors inspired by royal kitchens and bustling streets of India. The menu features a diverse selection of dishes, including biryanis, kebabs, and flavorful curries, crafted using traditional recipes and innovative techniques. The restaurant is led by Chef Mohammad Tarique Khan, who has a deep passion for Hyderabadi cuisine and a commitment to excellence. Chef Jayesh Naik, another esteemed chef, brings his creative approach to traditional Indian cuisine, blending time-honored techniques with contemporary methods.
menu_items: INDO CHINES STREET CHOWMEIN - VEG/EGG/CHICKEN STIR WITH JULLIENE VEGETABLE, NOODLES HOMEMADE SAUCE - $11.99
SPECIAL SPICY CHOWMEIN - VEG/EGG/CHICKEN STIR WITH VEGTABLES, NOODLES SPICY HOMEMADE SAUCE - $12.99
STREET FRIED RICE - VEG/EGG/CHICKEN STIR WITH VEGATABLES, RICE HOMEMADE SAUCE - $11.99
GULAB JAMUN (2PCS) - MILK SOLIDS(KHOYA) MIX WITH FLOUR, GREEN CARDAMON - $6.49
RASMALAI (2PCS) - SOFT COTTAGE CHEESE/CHENNA COOK IN SUGAR SYRUP SERVED WITH SAFFRON MILK - $6.49
HOME MADE FRIES - HAND MADE CUT FRIES WITH TOMATO KETCUP - $6.99
review_snippets: Best Indian food I’ve had in Manhattan, and it’s not even close! Fragrant, satisfying, expansive menu, huge portions with GREAT PRICES and friendly/FAST service. I ordered an aromatic egg biryani, a garlic naan with that perfect crispy-to-doughy ratio, and lamb tikka masala with more depth than your typical. No charge for side of refreshing raita and plain rice. Could not recommend more for takeout or a quick dine-in; they also have a newer and bigger space in Kips Bay. Warning that they don’t serve alcohol. Will be ordering again and again! (5 stars)

The food here is just amazing...You will remember the Biryani here once you try it. We visited from Houston and can safely say its one of the Best Biryanis we had In a long time. Pls open one in Houston !! Food is served piping hot and fresh...Naan and curries were delicious too...overall very satisfied !! (5 stars)

(June 6, 2025) We went here as a group of about 10 people for a friend's treat. I was excited that this restaurant advertised itself to serve Hyderabadi cuisine, and a lot of the items on the menu were indeed what I used to uniquely see in restaurants in Hyderabad, India. I tried the following. 1. Kubani ka meetha -- sweet jam, nice sourness. Mild spices. Delicious. 2. Double ka meetha -- warm, milky and not buttery, satisfying bread and cashew nuts. Semolina on top is a distraction. 3. Baigan bagaara --- While the name of the dish is in Hindi, it felt closer to the Telugu/Andhra dish that I know as Ennai kathirikkai (எண்ணெய் கத்திரிக்காய்), and it was very close in taste to what is served in Indian Institute of Science (A Mess). 4. Nizami paneer -- mild, thick, and yummy. 5. Dahi kebab -- soft in the mouth to the extent that it was tongue-biteable. The roti and rice items were normal. I wish I also tried the Irani chai, but I was too full to order one by myself, at the end. They gave rice with every gravy we ordered, sadly we couldn't even get to some of the several bowls of rice. The waiter was kind enough to request us to take it home parceled, but we were guilty of refusing. (4 stars)

Came here a bit before closing on a Saturday night last week. The Goat Dum Biryani was great! The goat was tender and flavorful, the rice was aromatic and dynamic, and the raita complemented the flavors really nicely. The portion was also huge, maybe it's meant to be shared but I ate it all up myself 🤤. I also got the Chaat Samosa with the tamarind sauce which I really liked too. The pastry was crispy and soaked in flavorful sauce 😋. I would totally recommend this place. (5 stars)

bio_text: Hyun is a stylish and minimalist Korean barbecue restaurant located in New York City, dedicated to providing an authentic experience of Korean food and culture. The restaurant emphasizes harmony between food, atmosphere, and space, ensuring a pleasurable dining experience that reflects the rich traditions of Korean cuisine. Hyun specializes in Korean barbecue, focusing on the meticulous selection and preparation of high-quality meats, particularly top-grade Japanese wagyu beef. The menu features dishes prepared on the same day, showcasing expert techniques that highlight the natural flavors of fresh ingredients.
menu_items: daily special cuts selected by the chef - 12+ cuts with marinated wagyu - $159
sot-bap - pot-cooked rice topped with japanese uni and seasonal truffle - $24
doenjang-jjigae - soybean paste stew with a5 rib finger and assorted vegetables - $24
cheese - grillable cheese from imsil, korea - $14
uni - fresh sea urchin from hokkaido, japan - $45
bingsu - green tea flavored korean shaved ice dessert - $15
review_snippets: Came here Saturday night with friends—had reservations but we ended having to wait a bit for our table (for 6 ppl). The restaurant was extremely hot, they had the heat turned up so high everyone was struggling to stay cool—we voiced our concerns several times. Our party got the HYUN-makase, supposedly all-you-can-eat wagyu for $159. The Wagyu meats were good—they cooked it and let us eat a few different cuts at a time, but honestly by the end we couldn’t remember exactly which ones were which. Some cuts were very tender yet some were too chewy. The Marinated Wagyu (Galbi) was my favorite. For dipping, the truffle sea salt was so delicious, extra flavor with the meat! Banchans were okay—kimchi, salad and veggies, not a huge selection. We also ordered the Doenjang-jigae (stew) and the Naeng-myun (cold noodles) which were good. Service here was top notch. Restaurant vibe is more intimate type of setting. Food was good but I’m not sure the HYUN-makase was really worth it, would have preferred an à la carte option. (4 stars)

Hyun in K-Town is absolutely amazing! We had the Hyun-makase set, and the A5 Miyazaki Wagyu was incredible — so tender and flavorful. The staff helped grill the meat perfectly, and the 12 different cuts were all delicious. We also tried the sea urchin with Wagyu — such a heavenly combination! The Korean-style sides, fresh salad, and dipping sauces made the meal even better. The drinks and desserts were excellent too — Hallabong Ade, Genmai-cha, Shiso Sorbet, and Hōji Ice Cream were perfect to refresh the palate. The atmosphere is cozy and stylish, with private rooms available. Highly recommend for anyone who loves Wagyu or wants a fun dining experience in NYC! (5 stars)

We went to Hyun for all-you-can-eat wagyu and had a really great experience. The place was pretty quiet when we went, which was nice because we didn’t have to wait long at all. The service was amazing. The servers were super accommodating and cooked everything for us, which made the whole experience feel very easy and relaxed. After we finished the pre-set wagyu, they asked what cuts we wanted next and everything came out really fast, so there wasn’t much downtime. I liked that we could order from lean to super fatty wagyu, and even though I couldn’t remember which cut was which, the servers were really helpful and walked us through the options based on what we liked. Overall, great food, great service, and a really smooth experience. I’d definitely come back. (5 stars)

Hyun has such a gorgeous and intimate atmosphere — definitely one of those places that makes you feel like you’re treating yourself to something special. The food was absolutely delicious, and the first hour of service was top-tier. They take the time to present each cut of meat, explain how it should be cooked and what toppings to pair the cuts with, and it really adds to the experience. You’re given 90 minutes total, with the first hour focused on the guided tasting and the rest being “all you can eat.” The only downside is that once that first hour passes, the service noticeably slows down — it became a bit tough to get attention for refills or additional orders, which cut into that remaining time. It’s definitely on the pricey side, but for the quality, presentation, and overall vibe, it’s worth it for special occasions. I left full, happy, and already thinking about my next visit! (4 stars)

(5 stars) Hyun has such a gorgeous and intimate atmosphere — definitely one of those places that makes you feel like you’re treating yourself to something special. The food was absolutely delicious, and the first hour of service was top-tier. They take the time to present each cut of meat, explain how it should be cooked and what toppings to pair the cuts with, and it really adds to the experience. You’re given 90 minutes total, with the first hour focused on the guided tasting and the rest being “all you can eat.” The only downside is that once that first hour passes, the service noticeably slows down — it became a bit tough to get attention for refills or additional orders, which cut into that remaining time. It’s definitely on the pricey side, but for the quality, presentation, and overall vibe, it’s worth it for special occasions. I left full, happy, and already thinking about my next visit! (4 stars)

bio_text: I Sodi is a celebrated Tuscan ristorante located in New York City, known for its commitment to traditional Italian cooking and the integrity of its ingredients. Established in 2008 by Chef Rita Sodi, the restaurant offers a warm and inviting atmosphere that reflects the sacred ritual of meal preparation and enjoyment, inspired by Sodi's upbringing on a family farm in Tuscany. Guests can enjoy a dining experience that emphasizes understated elegance and a deep respect for culinary heritage. I Sodi focuses on authentic Tuscan cuisine, utilizing time-honored methods and high-quality ingredients. The menu features a variety of traditional dishes, showcasing the flavors of Italy with a modern touch. Signature techniques include the careful preparation of house-made pastas and seasonal dishes that highlight the essence of Tuscan cooking. I Sodi was established in 2008 by Chef Rita Sodi, who draws inspiration from her childhood on a family farm near Florence. Sodi is a self-taught chef and won the 2019 James Beard Award for Best Chef, NYC.
review_snippets: The main stay west village romantic spot at the larger location. Was finally able to snag a reservation at a reasonable hour. The traditional Tuscan dishes is hard to find in the city. The back area is darkened to set a romantoc mood. Pork loin and rabbit were delicious along with wine and sweet tiramisu. (5 stars)

painfully average. been waiting to try this place for ages and it really like hit and it didn’t. wasn’t salty enough, or maybe some things were too salty? i’m not sure. the lasagne wasn’t great, super heavy and dry. i expected it to be either more moist or more lightweight. the pasta was the best thing we had. the fried mushrooms were quite of addicting but yet still not anything to write home about. (3 stars)

Enjoyable but not my fav Italian in the city (or west village for that matter). Was only able to get a res for weekday lunch. The meh looked extensive but we only ordered the pappardelle al limone and lasagne on the menu. Both very good. Also got potato croquettes which were one of the many specials they had which I always appreciate interesting specials. Really like the vibes of this place and the outdoor/courtyard seating looked very nice if the weathers warm as well. (4 stars)

Disclaimer ***** Regardless of any experience had with an establishment, good or bad, 5 stars will be rewarded. Existing as a business is hard enough. I will always however, be honest as to what my personal experience was. Let's get into it. The day after the Knicks' choking incident the city was palpably quieter. It was a gloomy grey drizzly Thursday and I needed something to take my mind off of what had happened the night before. A bowl of pasta to quell this sickness. Scouring food pages searching for the finest pastas in the land, I Sodi stuck out to me. No res, fingers crossed, it was about 2:15 (45 min before lunch ends) when we walked in and was greeted by a server with long hair and William H Macy's cool younger brother vibes who informed me that if we could order and eat by 3, we could get a table. Me and Dani said **** yeah we already know what we're ordering. They sat us down and told us he usually does the whole wine and specials schpiel but It wasn't necessary. We ordered the Spinach Raviolis, Tha Paccheri, and the Pappardelle al Limone. Me and Dani just got back from a pasta making class in Florence where we made spinach raviolis. They came out amazing and we had a great time making them. Cute. I tasted one of these raviolis at I Sodi and understood that you cannot make a ravioli THAT DISRESPECTFULLY TASTY without years and years of pasta making and creation. INCREDIBLE. What was even more incredible was that the pasta got better. The pappardelle al limon was our fav dish of 2025. I've dreamt of it ever since, and we have gone back for it, and it still blew us away. The table next to us had the lasagna which looked aesthetically stunning and I am sure was delicious, but our paccherri seemed to have more sauce which was the perfect bowl of pasta for a rainy day. Affogato to finish out one of my most memorable meals in NYC ever and we were out of there before 3 p.m. We couldn't finish that last pasta so we asked for it to go. I guess being wrapped in the end of service, the team forgot the leftovers so we just paid and kept it moving. No worries, it was an amazing meal. One minute later William H Macy's hippy brother comes bustin out of the restaurant with the doggy bag like WAIT!!! Hands it to us and we all just start laughing like, How did that meal get even better. Drop the Mic. 10 outta 10. I wish I remembered that legends name but I will be back again and again because that experience was magical and restored my faith in the Knicks. The fourth pasta shown from the second time we went was also one of the best dishes of 2025 although I don't exactly remember what it was because it was on the specials. Short rib maybe? It kinda reminded me of an elevated beef stroganoff. Oh and lastly I am not a big fan of a Negroni (sorry Bourdain I will keep trying) but the Terra cocktail was an extremely light and balanced companion to my pastas. Go here. ***** (5 stars)

bio_text: Icca is a refined dining establishment that embodies the essence of Japanese culture through its unique culinary offerings. The restaurant aims to create a memorable experience for its guests, inviting them to enjoy a harmonious blend of hospitality and exquisite cuisine, reminiscent of the first bloom of spring. Icca specializes in Omakase, a traditional Japanese dining format where the chef curates a personalized tasting menu. The focus is on seasonal ingredients and meticulous craftsmanship, highlighting the beauty and flavors of each dish. The name 'icca' is inspired by a Zen saying, symbolizing the plum blossom as the herald of spring, reflecting the restaurant's philosophy of bringing joy and warmth to its guests.
review_snippets: Chef was excellent. As far as nyc high end omakase goes some of the best, if not the best, rice preparation there is. And his use of the abalone in both dishes was amazing. Loved talking to him about sushi and food in general. Highly recommend! (5 stars)

What a great night for my 64 birthday. I get there and tell them I'm 64 by singing verse when I'm 64 and the gut says I love the Beatles, anyway we seat and Kazu starts serving us appetizers then sushi . It was so much food I was stuffed and happy I will leave pic of menu to see what I had . At end brought bday candle and played when I'm 64 on speakers. Brought tear to my eyes . (5 stars)

I had my good bye dinner with my manager here. It was absolutely amazing. I like how the food is not strictly traditional. I feel that the chef put a lot of heart and feeling into each of his dishes, which is very special. We tasted an abundance of flavors for all the dishes and absolutely love the chef’s touch of modern innovation. The atmosphere was fun and friendly, which we enjoy as well. My favorite is definitely the unbelievably delicious beef, the Uni and crab pasta, and the melon dessert, which are all refreshing and very enjoyable. (5 stars)

Very nice place! A bit hard to find given being on a Main Street. The interior is welcoming and modern. There were a few minor odd choices for a Michelin star restaurant: disposable chopsticks, and laminated plastic signs on the doors. The food was a fusion of Japanese and Italian cuisine, and felt completely unique. Flavors that i I didn’t know worked together were delicious. Would definitely return. (5 stars)

bio_text: Il Fiorista is a unique Italian restaurant located in NoMad, New York City, that combines the charm of a floral boutique with a community education center. The restaurant emphasizes local farming and the beauty of botanicals, creating a vibrant and inviting atmosphere for diners seeking a connection to nature and quality ingredients. Il Fiorista focuses on Italian cuisine, highlighting seasonal and locally sourced ingredients. The menu features a blend of traditional dishes and innovative interpretations, with an emphasis on the use of botanicals to enhance flavors.
menu_items: Charcuterie Board - salumi, formaggio - $35
Soup - $16
Lotus Crisp - lotus root, pine pollen - $14
Olives Marinated - $8
Wild Mushroom Arancini - arborio rice, wild fresh mushrooms, truffle aioli - $20
Heirloom Tomato Salad - organic heirloom tomato, ricotta salata, balsamic - $24
review_snippets: very pretty space, especially for brunch w the girls. the service was a little slow (granted we were a big group of 12 people), but our server was very friendly!! highly recommend the egg benedict, although the carbonara could use a bit more flavor. overall cute place:) (4 stars)
Cute space and great service. They had a great selection of wine and I got the lavender pasta and it was very different in a good way.! Desserts were also delicious. (4 stars)

IL Fiorista is a true gem in the city. We’ve been four times now, and every visit has been consistently excellent. The food is always fresh, delicious, and beautifully presented, with thoughtful portions that leave you satisfied but never stuffed. They’re also incredibly accommodating with dietary requests, which is always appreciated. The space itself is charming—bright, cozy, and full of character. We’ve had the same server each time we’ve gone on the weekend, and he is just lovely: attentive, kind, and clearly passionate about what he does. This place is an absolute must-try if you're looking for a reliably great meal in a beautiful setting. I belive they even do flower making classes on occasion ❤️ (5 stars)

My friends and I tried the tasting menu. Overall, we felt it was good, but not great. Most of the items appetizer and dessert items were just okay. We didn't enjoy the ham on the charcuterie board or the tiramisu (too sweet). The mains- lobster ravioli and the fish- were great. It felt like an okay portion size to me, though one person in my group did still feel a bit hungry afterwards. The drinks were just okay, but not something I would recommend. I also felt we were missing the storytelling aspect of a tasting menu. I prefer when a server helps us understand why those items are all on the menu and how it's all connected. One person in our party had previously experienced their flower-inspired tasting menu, so we had hoped for a similar experience. Overall, the experience was just alright, which makes is hard to justify $100-$150 per person after tax and tip. If I went back, I would do al a carte and just get a main dish. (3 stars)

bio_text: Il Gigante is a charming trattoria located in the heart of Ridgewood, designed to evoke the warmth and comfort of traditional Italian home cooking. The restaurant offers a welcoming atmosphere where guests can enjoy hearty, unfussy dishes reminiscent of beloved family recipes from central Italy, making it a perfect spot for gathering and sharing meals with loved ones. Il Gigante specializes in authentic Italian cuisine, focusing on comfort foods such as ragù and lasagna. The menu features generous portions and emphasizes home-style cooking techniques, ensuring each dish is prepared with care and love. Il Gigante is inspired by the culinary traditions of Bologna and Florence, reflecting the founders' desire to recreate the feel of their old home in their new community.
review_snippets: My wife Yuni and I walked by Il Gigante out of curiosity, and one day finally decided to take a break from work and try it. We only had a short time to dine, but we were so glad we did. The pasta was incredible. A week later, we were craving brunch and looked at a few spots, but honestly, we just wanted to go back. That’s when I met their lasagna, and it completely won me over. We went back again the next weekend with my in-laws just so I could have it again. We all shared our plates, as you should at an Italian restaurant, and every dish was fantastic. Since then, Il Gigante has become one of our favorite places in Ridgewood. The food is amazing, but it’s the people who make it special. Everyone we’ve met has been kind, genuine, and welcoming. When you work long, stressful hours, meals like this remind you to slow down and enjoy life. Ridgewood’s lucky to have a place like this. Ps. They’re very dog friendly! (5 stars)

A divine dining experience. The friendliest staff. Amazing dishes. Phenomenal wine list. Cozy, warm interior. Baby friendly (they brought us a high chair) and babe loved the meatballs. Do not miss the cotoletta, it’s unreal. We were very excited to find a place with northern Italian dishes — the gramigna alla sasiccia is absolutely incredible! A solid choice to end on the panna cotta. We will be back again and again. (5 stars)

Il Gigante has a piece of my heart. It genuinely feels like a home away from home. The kind of place where you walk in for the first time but you’re treated like a regular. And that doesn’t just “happen.” You can feel the care in every detail, the consistency, the hours, the pride. It’s the kind of spot that reminds you what hospitality is supposed to feel like. If you haven’t been, go soon. If you have, go back and bring someone you love. (5 stars)

So happy I finally tried this place! Came here on a recommendation from a friend and it did not disappoint! Our server Elena was brilliant - take her reccomendations when you come! We let her decide our appetisers and they were just fantastic! The pecorina salad was my favourite. The food was so good that, as a vegetarian, I was even tempted to try the lasagna and it was so good. Don’t skip the drinks, the espresso martini and Bianco spritz were 10/10. Will definitely be back. (5 stars)

bio_text: ILIS is a unique dining establishment that embodies a warm and inviting atmosphere, centered around a wood-fired kitchen. The restaurant emphasizes a seamless dining experience with its innovative 'One House' service style, where chefs prepare and serve meals directly from the central kitchen, fostering a sense of community and connection between the kitchen and guests. ILIS specializes in seasonal cuisine that highlights the diverse plants, seafood, and game of North America. The menu is crafted to showcase the natural flavors of the ingredients, utilizing wood-fired cooking techniques to enhance the dining experience.
menu_items: Market Menu - Seasonal plants, seafood, and game of North America - $150
Field Guide Menu - Omakase-style tasting menu with seasonal ingredients - $250
Beverage pairing for Market Menu - Selection of cocktails, spirits, wine and sake - $85
Beverage pairing for Field Guide Menu - Bar and cellar pairing throughout the meal - $175
review_snippets: From high to low.. the space is beautifully done and sets the tone for what we thought would surely be a special meal, however, after 3 hours we had only received half of the 10 course meal. (30 mins waiting between each bite sized course). I'm happy to pay for a great meal (as I imagine most who come here are) but the food was sadly lacking in both flavor and depth. I understand the restaurant business is hard and this felt like a difficult night for the kitchen, but after reading reviews (which I should have done before booking) It seems this might be commonplace. I rarely leave reviews, and often reserve them for exceptionally good experiences as I know how hard running a restaurant is - but what we experienced tonight felt criminal, especially to anyone who might have saved up for a special experience, bday, or anniversary - save yourself the disappointment and an outrageous bill (1 stars)

From the moment you walk in, the first thing you notice is the huge open space of the restaurant, it’s visually impressive and immediately sets the tone. I came here to celebrate my birthday, and it turned out to be one of the most memorable dining experiences I’ve ever had. Here’s why: 1. Service truly top notch. I was genuinely impressed. In my experience, the level of service here is on par with and honestly even surpasses places like Jean Georges and Brooklyn Chef’s Table. Every detail was handled with care and professionalism. 2. Ingredient presentation that creates identity. They introduced the ingredients that define the character of the restaurant, explaining what each one was, how it would be used, and what we would be having throughout the night. That level of transparency and storytelling makes the experience feel thoughtful and unique. 3. Highly attentive servers. The staff checked in with us during almost every course, making sure everything was perfect without ever feeling intrusive. 4. Exceptional storytelling through food. The way each dish was explained its background, intention, and concept was simply wow. That’s how you create a connection that makes people want to return, just to learn more about the story behind the food. 5. Outstanding drink pairing. I opted for the drink pairing, and it was incredibly well thought out. Each drink complemented the food perfectly. If you enjoy drinking, I highly recommend getting the pairing it truly elevates the experience. Overall, this was an experience unlike any other I’ve had. Not just a meal, but a journey one that I won’t forget. (5 stars)

Service didn't meet the expectation for a fine dining restaurant at this prics range. Sommelier is particularly rude and condescending as opposed to advising customers on picking the right drink for that pairs well with the tasting menu. The food also has its flaws. It ranges from lack of flavor to too salty... Also, the doneness were off for a few dishes. However, I do enjoy the ambiance of the restaurant and its interior design. The place is spacious and easy to have a good conversation with friends. (2 stars)

Came here on 10/17/25, service was amazing, dishes were to die for and drinks were amazing. Everything is so good and I definitely recommend coming here. If you come here please try the meringue angel foodcake, trout and cotton candy drink. FYI: THE WHOLE COURSE TAKES 2 TO 3 HOURS SO BE READY TO WAIT. In general though this restaurant is amazing! 🔥👌🔥 (5 stars)
