(30 mins waiting between each bite sized course). I'm happy to pay for a great meal (as I imagine most who come here are) but the food was sadly lacking in both flavor and depth. I understand the restaurant business is hard and this felt like a difficult night for the kitchen, but after reading reviews (which I should have done before booking) It seems this might be commonplace. I rarely leave reviews, and often reserve them for exceptionally good experiences as I know how hard running a restaurant is - but what we experienced tonight felt criminal, especially to anyone who might have saved up for a special experience, bday, or anniversary - save yourself the disappointment and an outrageous bill (1 stars) From the moment you walk in, the first thing you notice is the huge open space of the restaurant, it’s visually impressive and immediately sets the tone. I came here to celebrate my birthday, and it turned out to be one of the most memorable dining experiences I’ve ever had. Here’s why: 1. Service truly top notch. I was genuinely impressed. In my experience, the level of service here is on par with and honestly even surpasses places like Jean Georges and Brooklyn Chef’s Table. Every detail was handled with care and professionalism. 2. Ingredient presentation that creates identity. They introduced the ingredients that define the character of the restaurant, explaining what each one was, how it would be used, and what we would be having throughout the night. That level of transparency and storytelling makes the experience feel thoughtful and unique. 3. Highly attentive servers. The staff checked in with us during almost every course, making sure everything was perfect without ever feeling intrusive. 4. Exceptional storytelling through food. The way each dish was explained its background, intention, and concept was simply wow. That’s how you create a connection that makes people want to return, just to learn more about the story behind the food. 5. Outstanding drink pairing. I opted for the drink pairing, and it was incredibly well thought out. Each drink complemented the food perfectly. If you enjoy drinking, I highly recommend getting the pairing it truly elevates the experience. Overall, this was an experience unlike any other I’ve had. Not just a meal, but a journey one that I won’t forget. (5 stars) Service didn't meet the expectation for a fine dining restaurant at this prics range. Sommelier is particularly rude and condescending as opposed to advising customers on picking the right drink for that pairs well with the tasting menu. The food also has its flaws. It ranges from lack of flavor to too salty... Also, the doneness were off for a few dishes. However, I do enjoy the ambiance of the restaurant and its interior design. The place is spacious and easy to have a good conversation with friends. (2 stars) Came here on 10/17/25, service was amazing, dishes were to die for and drinks were amazing. Everything is so good and I definitely recommend coming here. If you come here please try the meringue angel foodcake, trout and cotton candy drink. FYI: THE WHOLE COURSE TAKES 2 TO 3 HOURS SO BE READY TO WAIT. In general though this restaurant is amazing! 🔥👌🔥 (5 stars)

bio_text: Inga's Bar, located in the heart of Brooklyn Heights, offers a cozy yet elevated dining experience that has quickly become a neighborhood favorite. The restaurant features an inviting atmosphere with tin-pressed ceilings and flickering candlelight, making it an ideal setting for both casual dinners and special occasions. With a menu that celebrates seasonal flavors and a commitment to quality, Inga's Bar provides a memorable dining experience for locals and visitors alike. Inga's Bar focuses on contemporary American cuisine with a creative twist on comfort food. The menu is ever-evolving, highlighting seasonal ingredients and innovative dishes such as duck poutine croquettes and a double-patty cheeseburger. The restaurant also features a well-curated beverage program with expertly crafted cocktails and a selection of wines.
menu_items: Duck Poutine Croquettes - Duck, poutine, aioli - $12
Mortadella - Aged gouda, brown butter - $13
Giardiniera - Pickled seasonal vegetables, olives - $7
Celery Victor - Anchovy, parmesan - $16
Crab Omelet - Avocado, crème fraîche - $26
Bulgogi Beef Hanger - Grilled cabbage, habanero, plum - $20
review_snippets: An unforgettable experience. From the warm welcome to the thoughtful birthday touches, everything felt genuine and full of care. The team and the restaurant owners truly made me feel special. The meal was exquisite, the halibut with parsnip purée and lobster reduction was perfectly balanced, and the onion soup to start was comforting and flavorful. The dessert was the perfect ending, gently confirming the sweetness of the entire experience. A place with heart, and I will definitely be back (5 stars)

Dinner at Ingas Bar was lovely! It wasn't perfect, but I loved the coziness of the restaurant and food was overall fantastic. It will definitely be a go to spot in our neighborhood. The good: gem salad, octopus, burger, and the poached pear dessert (which I think might be a seasonal item). The octopus was amazing - it may have been my favorite octopus dish I've ever tried. Not the best: the roasted chicken was too salty for me. I would skip this item. Service wasn't bad but it wasn't the best. It was fast/efficient but the way our server put down our starters felt off (like I wasn't sure if they wanted me to take the plate from their hands or if they were going to put it down) and they seemed kind of annoyed. It was a packed and busy restaurant so I get it. (5 stars)

A hidden gem and one of the top restaurants in Brooklyn heights / downtown Brooklyn. Everything is a must try, you can’t go wrong. Great for sharing. Vibe is excellent at night and when it’s dark. Top picks: fish stew (small portion, very unique), agnoli, burger and fries, gem salad (5 stars)

Inga’s is the perfect middle ground between fine dining and a classic American bar. The decor is effortlessly cool with vintage prints lining the walls. The space is open, with a large dining room and a semi-secluded bar area towards the back. Tables in the dining room are quite cozy, so prepare to be close to your neighbors. Moody lighting and votive candles add to the intimate feel. The food is delicious, boasting unexpectedly complex flavors without being pretentious. We shared a bunch of small plates, two entrees, and a dessert (Beef Tartare, Fluke Crudo, Agnolotti, Duck Breast, Steak Au Poivre and Olive Oil Cake). The agnolotti with butternut squash and hazelnuts may be seasonal but if it is on the menu when you go, it’s a MUST. Literally to die for. Highly recommend Inga’s if you’re looking for a spot to grab dinner in Brooklyn Heights. (5 stars)

bio_text: Ishq is a vibrant dining destination in the heart of New York City, where the essence of Indian culinary heritage is celebrated through innovative and artistic presentations. The restaurant embodies the spirit of 'Ishq', meaning love or passion, and offers an unforgettable experience for both private celebrations and corporate functions. With a focus on storytelling through food, each dish is a tribute to age-old recipes, meticulously crafted to evoke the warmth of home-cooked Indian meals while appealing to modern palates. Ishq specializes in Indian cuisine, featuring a menu that includes aromatic curries and flavorful tandoori dishes. The culinary approach combines traditional recipes with contemporary plating techniques, creating a unique dining experience that highlights the richness of India's diverse culinary regions. About Chef Vamshi adi
menu_items: GOL GAPPE - Semolina puffs, spicy potato stuffing, asafoetida & mint flavored water - $13
METHI MATTAR KULCHA - Indian stuffed flatbread, fresh fenugreek, green peas, cheese, sweet corn raita - $13
THARI SAMOSA - Black chickpeas, thari, bhujia, cilantro - $15
SET PODI DOSA - Savory rice pancakes, gunpowder, coconut chutney, tomato pachadi - $17
VEGETABLE PANIYARAM - Shredded mixed vegetables & rice dumplings, dry garlic thecha, tomato peanut chutney, curry leaves - $17
DAL BURRATA - Fried garlic, ghee, kasoori methi - $21
review_snippets: Ishq means love and there was no better place to go for a valentines brunch than this place! The drive was peaceful and there is enough parking garages nearby with a walking distance to the restaurant. The ambience was a tad let down, we expected the decor and ambiance to be much more evocative than what it really was. No offense, there was an understate elegance and calmness to the place with the dim mood lighting. The food was wonderful and we tried many options from their brunch menu. The kokum flavors cocktail was spice and potent and a perfect pick me up! The jalebi chaat and Raj kachori were earthy and flavorful. The Ishq dal makhani was a signature dish and we kept going back to the bowl for helpings. The unique Himachali gucchi was a perfect umami flavor bomb in a curry gravy. Finished off with a great khubani ka meetha and a perfect sweet ending to a wonderful valentines brunch! Would love to come back for dinner sometime soon! (4 stars)

Great place to sit at the bar and enjoy punchy food and mellow drinks, or to sit at a table to get lost in conversation while sharing bread and curries. My favorite was the dum ka gosht where the curry was spiced without being spicy and the goat was tender while keeping the goat's lean taste. I also highly recommend the hara paneer mattar kulcha. Kulchas are always good and the peas provide a vegetal depth to the salty fatty cheese kulcha. The gongura shrimp had good shrimp and amazing bajji underneath, I loved eating this separately with bread. The lahsooni oysters had a great sauce where the oysters played a briny complementary role. The Gobi was well-fried and nice. The breads were moist and reasonable. But those two curries, the bajji and the goat, were another level. From the cocktail side the jaan-e-maan had the best balance due to the faba and the extra flavors. I also recommend the kiss me in goa for the sweetness. The hoth rasiley has a cool vibe with a betel leaf taste that is home for some including myself. Overall a great place that I'm adding to my rotation. Prices are reasonable given the portion size: a date should get one main and two appetizers with two breads. (5 stars)

Ishq is a lovely Indian restaurant with a great vibe and solid food. I tried the jalebi chaat, lamb chops, daal, and bhuna gosht—everything was flavorful and well prepared. The lamb chops were especially impressive, and the daal was comforting and rich. Plus, they serve halal meat, which is a big plus. Overall, a nice place to dine, and I’d definitely go back again. Highly recommended. (5 stars)

Ishq is a true gem in New York for anyone craving authentic Indian flavors. Every dish is layered with depth, warmth, and care — you can taste the quality of the ingredients and the respect for tradition in each bite. The spices are beautifully balanced, not overpowering, and the flavors feel both nostalgic and refined. From the aroma to the presentation, everything feels intentional. If you’re looking for Indian food that feels soulful, comforting, and genuinely authentic, Ishq absolutely delivers. (5 stars)

bio_text: ITO is a modern Japanese omakase restaurant located in Downtown Manhattan, featuring an intimate 16-seat sushi counter. The restaurant offers a unique dining experience that emphasizes inventive interpretations of traditional sushi, creating a sophisticated yet welcoming atmosphere for guests. With a focus on quality and craftsmanship, ITO invites diners to indulge in a carefully curated culinary journey. ITO specializes in omakase, a Japanese dining style where the chef selects and serves a series of dishes. The menu is priced at $295 per person and showcases seasonal ingredients, with fish flown in from Japan. Signature techniques include meticulous preparation and presentation of sushi, complemented by seasonal beverage pairings of wines and sake.
menu_items: Omakase - Seasonal fish and seafood, prepared in traditional Japanese style. - $295
review_snippets: Terrific dining experience at ITO. This restaurant is one of the finest omakase dining in NYC. It's my second time eating here, and the quality of food and service remained very high. Fresh and delicious food, masterfully prepared by our chef. Each dish was like an art both visually and taste wise. A vast selection of fresh ingredients. Service was top-notch, alway attentive and cordial. The setting was also very pleasant, sinmple, elegant and welcoming. I highly recommend this restaurant. (5 stars)

Dinner at ITO was an amazing experience. The omakase was outstanding—fresh, high-quality sushi with incredible flavor in every bite, and the fish was truly exceptional. They also offer a great variety of sake, and the tea is so good as well. The atmosphere is intimate, and I loved being so close to the chefs, they explained each dish in detail, which made the experience even more special. The service was attentive, welcoming, and knowledgeable from start to finish. I highly recommend this restaurant. Unforgettable experience. (5 stars)

One of the best omakase experiences I’ve ever had! I came in with very high expectations after dining at Ito in Las Vegas at the Fontainebleau Hotel—which was phenomenal—and I was excited to see they had a location in NYC. I’m happy to say this experience exceeded my expectations. From the moment we arrived, the staff was warm, welcoming, attentive, and prompt. We had the honor of meeting Chef Kevin, who was incredibly gracious and truly an artist in his craft. Every course showcased the highest quality ingredients, with a burst of flavor in every bite. From the appetizers to dessert, each dish was beautifully presented and thoughtfully crafted. I especially loved that we were given the option to add additional pieces at the end of the course, and that Chef Kevin offered this before dessert—it was a thoughtful touch that elevated the entire experience. The drink menu is also very well curated, with an excellent selection of sake and other alcoholic beverages to complement the meal. This is absolutely a place I will continue to visit every time I’m in town. A must-try for any omakase lover in NYC. (5 stars)

Very delicious meal with quality fish. The cod was soft and paired nicely with the miso. The standouts for me were the truffle mushroom soup which was just nice on a cold day and the mushroom tasted so fresh. The seared otoro had a smokey flavor to it and melted in my mouth. The truffle Wagyu was definitely my favorite because what’s not to love?? Truffle was strong and freshly shaved. Wagyu torched to the perfect fatty level. The dessert was very lovely liked the buttery cream on top with the crunchy popcorn and miso base. The counter does get quite crowded and seats more than the typical amount of people at an omakase (5 stars)

bio_text: Ivan Ramen is a celebrated dining destination located in New York's Lower East Side, known for its authentic and innovative approach to Japanese ramen. The restaurant offers a vibrant atmosphere that reflects a blend of American and Japanese cultures, providing guests with a unique culinary experience that is both casual and refined. With a focus on high-quality ingredients and traditional techniques, Ivan Ramen has garnered critical acclaim and a loyal following since its opening. Ivan Ramen specializes in Japanese ramen, offering a menu that features both classic and inventive variations of the dish. The restaurant emphasizes the use of fresh, high-quality ingredients and traditional cooking methods, including house-made noodles and rich, flavorful broths. Signature dishes showcase Ivan's unique culinary perspective, appealing to both Japanese and American palates. Ivan's journey began with a dishwashing job at a sushi bar at the age of 15, leading him to major in Japanese language and literature. After culinary training at the Culinary Institute of America and successful ventures in Tokyo, he opened his first U.S. restaurant, Ivan Ramen Slurp Shop, in 2013, followed by the flagship Ivan Ramen in 2012. Ivan has been recognized as an authority on ramen and was featured in the Netflix series Chef's Table in 2017.
menu_items: Japanese Fried Chicken - toasted garlic caramel, togarashi, shiso ranch - $15
Wagyu Pastrami Buns - housemade pastrami served on a steamed bun with sauerkraut + japanese-russian dressing - $14
Curry Cauliflower - cauliflower, curry koji butter, pickled ginger, katsuobushi - $12
Schmaltz Fried Gyoza - housemade chicken gyoza, almond taberu rayu, crispy skin, gyoza sauce - $13
Tokyo Shio - sea salts, dashi + chicken broth, shoyu-glazed chashu, soft egg, roasted tomato - $18
Tokyo Shoyu - soy sauce, dashi + chicken broth, shoyu-glazed chashu, soft egg, toasted nori - $18
review_snippets: I stopped by Ivan Ramen last month as it was close to where I was staying in the LES. It did not disappoint. The space is small, but cozy and relaxed, and the servers were excellent and very attentive throughout the meal. I ordered the tonkatsu ramen, which was very rich and flavorful. We also had the potato salad and pork buns which were both very good. Everything tastes fresh, portions are generous and the presentation is really nice. For dessert, I highly recommend the ube pudding, it’s definitely one of the best ube desserts I’ve had. If you’re in the Lower East Side and craving ramen, this is definitely a place worth stopping by. (5 stars)

Been wanting to check out this place for years and it was truly exceptional! I enjoyed every drop of the chicken Paitan broth, extra crispy chicken karaage, and the gyoza. Not to mention a kind and professional service from the waitress (we were a party of three sitting in the corner table by the window in the back right at noon on 2/22/26). Thank you! (5 stars)

Hands down some of the most fantastic ramen I've eaten. Having visited Japan multiple times, I can confidently say this place is authentic and top-tier. If you appreciate high-quality ramen, you have to eat here. You absolutely have to try the Tonkotsu. A must-visit! (5 stars)

One of the BEST ramen I've ever tried! Before you come at me, I'm referring to a fully vegetarian/vegan ramen - it's hard to come across a delicious, hearty, packed with flavor broth (unless you go straight to the motherland). We came here with a group of friends (shout out to our friend for bringing us here) and we sat in the quieter area to the back with the bench chairs. Loved this little room it's perfect for a cozy night with friends and definitely a lot quieter than the regular room. Of course, this place is pretty small to begin with but attention to detail, service and food flavors is what it's all about. We started things off with the spicy kyuri pickles which were absolutely delicious. The rice vinegar is what gave it that perfect amount of punch without making you feel like you were eating salt and vinegar chips (which I LOVE). Spice level wasn't too spicy for me but it does have a kick. Me and my husband ordered different ramens so we could try the different flavors and I'm SO glad we did. The veggie spicy miso red chili is what stole my heart and lives rent free in my taste buds (they too have a memory hehe). I think that dish was perfectly balanced without being overpowering or too spicy. The biggest amount of spice does sit at the bottom of the bowl and as I was siping my last bits of broth away that's when I noticed my pleasant little wake up call - which again for me it wasn't that spicy since I have a pretty high tolerance. IT WAS SO SO SO SO SO DELICOUS! Hubby's ramen was out of this world in its own way. He ordered the truffled vegan shoyu and WOW. It was one of those broths that can stand alone and make your taste buds dance and go crazy. It was absolutely incredible and one slurp lead to the next. Both of the ramen dishes were incredible - I personally don't eat eggs but even the eggs were beautiful. Absolutely love this place and can't wait to go back. It's definitely a great spot during the winter to warm you up. Bowls are pretty generous and if you're hungry enough you'll eat it all. If you want to leave some room for dessert or grab something else in the area, then you're good to go if you share one. My greedy self would never at this spot but hey, you do you :) One last thing, LOVED that everyone can pay for their own thing at your tables bill using the QR code to split and pay what you want. That way you don't have to awkwardly make your server do it for you and try to figure it all out while that one lemonade someone forgot to pay for etc haha. Super cool feature! (5 stars)

The restaurant emphasizes the use of fresh, high-quality ingredients and traditional cooking methods, including house-made noodles and rich, flavorful broths. Signature dishes showcase Ivan's unique culinary perspective, appealing to both Japanese and American palates. Ivan's journey began with a dishwashing job at a sushi bar at the age of 15, leading him to major in Japanese language and literature. After culinary training at the Culinary Institute of America and successful ventures in Tokyo, he opened his first U.S. restaurant, Ivan Ramen Slurp Shop, in 2013, followed by the flagship Ivan Ramen in 2012. Ivan has been recognized as an authority on ramen and was featured in the Netflix series Chef's Table in 2017. Japanese Fried Chicken - toasted garlic caramel, togarashi, shiso ranch - $15 Wagyu Pastrami Buns - housemade pastrami served on a steamed bun with sauerkraut + japanese-russian dressing - $14 Curry Cauliflower - cauliflower, curry koji butter, pickled ginger, katsuobushi - $12 Schmaltz Fried Gyoza - housemade chicken gyoza, almond taberu rayu, crispy skin, gyoza sauce - $13 Tokyo Shio - sea salts, dashi + chicken broth, shoyu-glazed chashu, soft egg, roasted tomato - $18 Tokyo Shoyu - soy sauce, dashi + chicken broth, shoyu-glazed chashu, soft egg, toasted nori - $18 I stopped by Ivan Ramen last month as it was close to where I was staying in the LES. It did not disappoint. The space is small, but cozy and relaxed, and the servers were excellent and very attentive throughout the meal. I ordered the tonkatsu ramen, which was very rich and flavorful. We also had the potato salad and pork buns which were both very good. Everything tastes fresh, portions are generous and the presentation is really nice. For dessert, I highly recommend the ube pudding, it’s definitely one of the best ube desserts I’ve had. If you’re in the Lower East Side and craving ramen, this is definitely a place worth stopping by. (5 stars) Been wanting to check out this place for years and it was truly exceptional! I enjoyed every drop of the chicken Paitan broth, extra crispy chicken karaage, and the gyoza. Not to mention a kind and professional service from the waitress (we were a party of three sitting in the corner table by the window in the back right at noon on 2/22/26). Thank you! (5 stars) Hands down some of the most fantastic ramen I've eaten. Having visited Japan multiple times, I can confidently say this place is authentic and top-tier. If you appreciate high-quality ramen, you have to eat here. You absolutely have to try the Tonkotsu. A must-visit! (5 stars) One of the BEST ramen I've ever tried! Before you come at me, I'm referring to a fully vegetarian/vegan ramen - it's hard to come across a delicious, hearty, packed with flavor broth (unless you go straight to the motherland). We came here with a group of friends (shout out to our friend for bringing us here) and we sat in the quieter area to the back with the bench chairs. Loved this little room it's perfect for a cozy night with friends and definitely a lot quieter than the regular room. Of course, this place is pretty small to begin with but attention to detail, service and food flavors is what it's all about. We started things off with the spicy kyuri pickles which were absolutely delicious. The rice vinegar is what gave it that perfect amount of punch without making you feel like you were eating salt and vinegar chips (which I LOVE). Spice level wasn't too spicy for me but it does have a kick. Me and my husband ordered different ramens so we could try the different flavors and I'm SO glad we did. The veggie spicy miso red chili is what stole my heart and lives rent free in my taste buds (they too have a memory hehe). I think that dish was perfectly balanced without being overpowering or too spicy. The biggest amount of spice does sit at the bottom of the bowl and as I was siping my last bits of broth away that's when I noticed my pleasant little wake up call - which again for me it wasn't that spicy since I have a pretty high tolerance. IT WAS SO SO SO SO SO DELICOUS! Hubby's ramen was out of this world in its own way. He ordered the truffled vegan shoyu and WOW. It was one of those broths that can stand alone and make your taste buds dance and go crazy. It was absolutely incredible and one slurp lead to the next. Both of the ramen dishes were incredible - I personally don't eat eggs but even the eggs were beautiful. Absolutely love this place and can't wait to go back. It's definitely a great spot during the winter to warm you up. Bowls are pretty generous and if you're hungry enough you'll eat it all. If you want to leave some room for dessert or grab something else in the area, then you're good to go if you share one. My greedy self would never at this spot but hey, you do you :) One last thing, LOVED that everyone can pay for their own thing at your tables bill using the QR code to split and pay what you want. That way you don't have to awkwardly make your server do it for you and try to figure it all out while that one lemonade someone forgot to pay for etc haha. Super cool feature! (5 stars)

bio_text: Izakaya Futago offers a unique dining experience that blends the casual charm of traditional Japanese izakayas with the vibrant energy of New York City. The restaurant features a warm and inviting atmosphere, characterized by soft lighting and wooden accents, making it an ideal spot for gatherings with friends, romantic dates, or quiet moments alone. Guests can enjoy a diverse selection of creative Japanese dishes, expertly crafted cocktails, and a lively ambiance that reflects the spirit of Japan. The culinary focus at Izakaya Futago is on innovative Japanese cuisine, featuring playful dishes such as Spoon Sushi, a one-bite reimagining of traditional nigiri. The menu includes carefully prepared skewers grilled to perfection and handcrafted Soba Noodles made from Ni-Hachi buckwheat, alongside an extensive selection of izakaya dishes. Founded in Japan by twin brothers, the Futago Group began with a single yakiniku restaurant and has since expanded to nearly 100 locations worldwide.
menu_items: Edamame - $5
Gobo Chips - $6
Tsukemori - $7
Miso Cheese - $12
Shishito Pepper - $7
Takoyaki - $11
review_snippets: This is a surprising hidden authentic Japanese izakaya, tucked away neatly by Grand Central Station Terminal only a short walk away. It is a Michelin-rated restaurant with a full bar and excellent dining spaces within its interior layout, that includes private rooms for guests and large parties. The cuisine is highly popular and the price ranges are moderated and based on market prices reflecting the seasonal factors for the menu items. Otherwise a place notably like ones found in Osaka, Tokyo, and Kyoto. Very authentic and hugely popular. Overall a superb experience and would definitely recommend to anyone looking for truly authentic Japanese cuisine. (5 stars)

Had dinner at Izakaya Futago in Midtown and it was a great experience. The space feels cozy and sleek, perfect for an after-work meal with drinks. We ordered the grilled eel with simmered egg, which was rich and buttery, and the All Stars sushi spoon, great bites w/ high quality fish. The large yakitori platter came with a great variety. The gyudon was really comforting. Their 4-stacking soba came with 3 different sobas and tempura. Ended with the chestnut ice cream which was delicious perfect: Everything was beautifully plated and balanced, definitely a spot I’d go back to. (5 stars)

My first time visiting, I immediately liked the atmosphere and found the food to be delicious. There are so many dishes to try, either visit in a bigger group to order and share more dishes or make a couple of visits. The washu beef hot pot was my favorite dish this first visit, and the mont blanc ice cream at the end was a great way to end the meal. (5 stars)

Excellent experience overall! We came here to try to soba and boy the quality was top notch. Wasabi was delicious. Sukiyaki was ok. Cold soba was just as nice as the hot soba. Portion was on the smaller side, making the price a bit high. But service was really pleasant and atmosphere was good. Not loud at all on a Saturday night. Just a perfect Saturday evening! Highly recommend. (5 stars)

bio_text: J.G. Melon is a quintessential New York City dining establishment located on the Upper East Side, renowned for its vibrant atmosphere and rich history since 1972. The restaurant embodies a classic saloon vibe, featuring Melon decor, green and white tablecloths, and an old-time jukebox, creating a nostalgic yet lively dining experience that attracts both locals and visitors alike, including celebrities and families. J.G. Melon specializes in classic American cuisine, with a particular focus on their famously juicy hamburgers and cottage fries. The menu is straightforward, emphasizing quality ingredients and traditional preparation methods, ensuring a memorable burger experience. J.G. Melon has been serving its loyal clientele since 1972, developing a strong following from the very beginning.
menu_items: Soup of the Day - $7.75
Chili Cup - $9.75
Chili Bowl - $13.00
Hamburger - $14.25
Cheeseburger - $15.25
Baconburger - $15.25
review_snippets: Would have got 5 stars but horrible ipa selection. I only drink good ipa and they only had Laganitas brewed by anheiser bush. Garbage ipa like a Budweiser! Burgers are legendary with good round fries. Prices are fantastic especially forvthe burgers on the upper east side like $16 with bacon and cheese. Waitress very attentive and kind. I used to live 3 blocks away in the 80s and 90s. The charm of the place still remains. They just need a better beer selection should support a local brewery and have a NY brewing company ipa! Go for the burgers. (4 stars)

If you’re looking for a classic New York burger experience, JG Melon is a solid choice. The food is decent and consistent, and it’s even mentioned in the Michelin Guide, which says a lot about its reputation. The burgers are simple, juicy, and done right — no fuss, just quality. And the cottage fries are a must-try — crispy, golden, and the perfect side to their classic cheeseburger. The cozy, old-school atmosphere makes the whole experience feel very “New York.” (4 stars)

While visiting my favorite butcher last week two sanitation employees were talking about Skinflints. Being the busybody I am, I joined their conversation & was told if I liked Skinflints then I would love JG Melon. I figured since we liked two of the same businesses I’d give JG a try. I’m glad to say they were correct. It’s 1st come 1st served at JG. Even though it was pretty busy I was able to get a seat at the bar easily enough. (Though I was told it gets much much busier than it was during my visit) Tommy the bartender was a down to earth people person which is always a plus in my book. The bacon cheeseburger I ordered was cooked just the way I like it & cottage fries happen to be one of my three favorite types of fries (four if I count sweet potato). The restaurant is small but the food food & service were amazing. I had two glasses of Jameson neat with my meal & lunch still ended up just under $50. So I’d say it’s reasonably priced. If you’re in the area & you enjoy a great burger definitely check it out. It’s a short walk from Bloomingdales if you enjoy walking on nice days. (5 stars)

JG Melon – 3rd Ave Unfortunately, this was a very disappointing experience. The only positive thing I can say is about the hostess, who was very kind, welcoming, and genuinely tried to help. Aside from that, the service was very poor. The staff showed no friendliness, no smiles, and no sense of care or attention. We waited outside for about 40–50 minutes to be seated. After placing our order, we waited almost another 40 minutes for the food to arrive. When the burger finally came, it was overcooked and burnt. We ordered the burger medium well, but it arrived well done and dry. Overall, the long wait times, lack of service, and incorrect food preparation made this a frustrating experience. Very disappointing, especially given the restaurant’s reputation. (2 stars)

bio_text: Jean-Georges is a renowned dining destination in New York, offering a sophisticated yet inviting atmosphere that reflects the culinary artistry of Chef Jean-Georges Vongerichten. The restaurant features a blend of contemporary design and classic elegance, making it an ideal setting for both casual and formal dining experiences. The restaurant specializes in French cuisine with Asian influences, showcasing a menu that includes breakfast, lunch, and dinner options. Signature techniques include the use of fresh, seasonal ingredients and innovative flavor pairings, presented in a refined tasting format. Chef Jean-Georges Vongerichten is the driving force behind the restaurant, known for his exceptional culinary skills and contributions to the fine dining scene.
review_snippets: My first NYC trip and stop at one of the finest dinning in the city. Undoubtedly would visit again. Every course was meticulously prepared and presented. The attention to detail was beyond impressive. Thank you to all the staff who made this experience memorable. (5 stars)

Wonderful and friendly staff. Delicious tasting menu. We selected the 6 course menu and we were not disappointed. Great selection of wine; but apparently they don’t offer wine and food pairing options. (5 stars)

Amazing experience, but for a 2 Star Michelin, it needs some improvement! I was expecting something more intimate and the restaurant was packed. We were seated in a table with a long couch with two other families very close to us. We had the six course omnivore and two courses were disappointing: the caviar taste disappeared in the green garbanzo beans; the wagyu per se was tasteless and needs improvement! The last thing was the restroom, which was very basic and not compatible with the restaurant sophistication! (4 stars)

I mean, would you expect less than 5 stars for a 2-Michelin Star restaurant? The food was delicious, but beyond that, creative and thoughtful. I picked Jean-Georges for my Michelin Star dining experience because the menu sounded stellar. Too many restaurants either over-simplify or over-complicate food. Jean-Georges walks the line of creativity and sophistication without crossing over into absurdity. I will definitely be back once my budget recovers! (5 stars)

bio_text: Jeju Noodle Bar is a unique dining establishment that celebrates the art of Korean comfort food, offering a modern interpretation of traditional dishes. Located in New York City, the restaurant embodies a creative spirit that brings depth of flavor and culture to the table, inviting guests to experience a blend of skill and talent in every bite. The restaurant focuses on Korean cuisine, emphasizing comfort food with a contemporary twist. The menu features a variety of dishes that reflect the rich culinary traditions of Korea, presented in a way that showcases the chefs' creativity and skill.
menu_items: TORO SSAM BAP - Fatty Tuna, Scrambled Egg, Tobiko, Shallots, Jalapeño, Toasted Seaweed, Golden Osetra Caviar - $57
TRUFFLE SCALLOP - Scallop, Truffle Soy, Pickled Radish, Truffle Aioli, Shimeji Mushroom, Seasonal Truffles - $41
AMBERJACK & ONION - Amberjack, Cucumber, Radish, Serrano, Onion, Smoked Onion Oil Dressing - $28
TUNA YUKHWE SALAD - Tuna, Fennel, Scallion, Soy Onion Dressing, Avocado, Lolla Rosa - $28
CLAM & SEA BREAM SOMYEON - Manilla Clams, Sea Bream, Serrano, Kohlrabi, Dill, Thin Noodles - $27
FLUKE HWE - Fluke, Red Onion, Cucumber, Plum Gochujang Olive Oil Dongchimi Emulsion - $26
review_snippets: A delightful experience! The young gentleman with the fashionable perm and pretty smile was so very kind and gave wonderful service. The food came out in an orderly manner and met every expectation you would have for a reoccurring Michelin star winning restaurant. The wagyu slices were tender and the ribs sweet and savory. The selection of entrees came out to be quite eye-catching and can only be described as a work of art in itself. Even the water tasted exceptional, but that is perhaps because I’ve been saving my appetite for this dinner. The dessert, chocolate soft serve ice cream topped with sea salt caramel and truffles, perfectly balanced sweet and salty that left a nice chocolate-y but not too sweet after taste by the time we walked out the restaurant. If I had to choose a favorite dish tonight, it would be the toro ssambap. The rice, meat, corn, orange sauce (not sure what but very delicious), and caviar paired very nicely with the seaweed and had a wonderful flavor profile that reminded me of gimbap. The atmosphere itself is dimly lit and sensible. I have no complaints with any part of the experience and I would recommend this place to every person I know!! (5 stars)

Loved our entire experience at Jeju Noodle. Our server Chang was amazing. He had great attention to detail and we loved all of his menu recommendations. But you can’t go wrong with any of the menu items here! The service was amazing, food top notch, ambience felt cozy and exclusive. Highly recommend! (5 stars)

This was, unfortunately, one of the most disappointing dining experiences I’ve had in New York, and the first time I’ve felt the need to write a negative review. I genuinely do not understand how this restaurant has earned a Michelin star. We made a 5:30 PM reservation based on multiple recommendations. The atmosphere was lovely, and the host was very welcoming, which initially set high expectations. However, once seated, the service fell well below standard. Our server did not introduce himself(which is fine but there was also no indication that he would be our server) None of our dishes (toro ssambap, yukhoe salad, gochujang ramyun) were explained when served, and there was no check-in throughout the meal. Meanwhile, the table next to us was checked on multiple times, which made the lack of attention toward our table feel particularly uncomfortable. The only positive service moment came when a different server brought dessert and provided a proper explanation. Unfortunately, shortly after, our original server abruptly placed the payment device on our table without us requesting it. This was especially confusing, as we had been seated for less than an hour and there was clearly no wait for tables. I rarely write reviews, especially negative ones, but this experience stood out for the wrong reasons. The space has potential, but the inconsistency and lack of basic hospitality do not reflect the reputation or recognition of this restaurant. (1 stars)

We had a wonderful experience. Highly recommend the lobster ramen, spicy pork ramen, and fluke (pictured). Special chicken sandwich is a must as well. The flavors in each dish were so unique and blend so well together. Also, we cannot say enough good things about our waiter, Kai. He was not only knowledgeable and attentive, but it was a pleasure to chat and get to know more about the restaurant and himself. Can’t wait to go back. (5 stars)

bio_text: Jiang Nan NYC is a culinary gem located in the heart of New York City, offering an authentic dining experience that showcases the rich flavors of Chinese cuisine. With a focus on dishes from regions such as Beijing, Shanghai, and Sichuan, the restaurant provides a warm and inviting atmosphere complemented by attentive service. review_snippets: First off the food and atmosphere was amazing. Best authentic food I’ve ever experienced. Igor seen I was struggling with the iPad and quickly came over and helped me navigate it and suggest some of his favorites on the menu and made the most amazing drinks. He ended up serving us the entire time because no one else approached us free. We had such a great time. Made the lunar parade day the best time. Worth the wait on the busiest day of the year (5 stars)

really great service! we arrived 45 minutes late to our reservation and they still were able to seat us within 10 minutes. food was great all around, with the duck and beef brisket w potatoes as highlights. the string beans were also very solid. complimentary cabbage was quite tasty. clean, fast, and delicious! (5 stars)

We visited on New Year’s Eve, and even though the restaurant was crowded and clearly very popular, there was surprisingly no waiting time at all. We ordered the full-sized Peking duck, which was absolutely fantastic. It came with scallions, cucumber, pineapple, white sugar, and their special house sauce, along with 20 pancakes for wrapping the duck—more than enough to enjoy every bite. We also tried several vegetarian dishes, including shredded cabbage (手撕包菜), fried pumpkin, and baby bok choy (娃娃菜). Every dish was incredibly flavorful and well-prepared. A special shout-out to the complimentary pickled cabbage—it was delicious and such a thoughtful touch. Overall, everything was excellent, from the food to the efficiency of the service. We loved every dish and would definitely come back again. (5 stars)

Truly worthy of it's Michelin recognition. Their food is bursting with flavor, and I got to try quite a lot of it. Everything taste vastly different but delicious in their own right. I recommend their beef dishes the most! The atmosphere was beautiful and stylish. The service was great, pretty attentive, and patient. My only slight concern is the size of the menu, it's huge, and a little confusing to navigate on their tablets; it took my friends and around 10 minutes to decide what we wanted. So that was a little overwhelming, but I can't complain too much about having a large selection :) Also, I'm not fully sure they allow you to split the check so just keep that in mind. Overall I highly recommend, this is really a gem of a restaurant! (5 stars)

bio_text: JoJo is a sophisticated dining establishment that embodies the essence of contemporary cuisine with a touch of elegance. The restaurant offers a warm and inviting atmosphere, making it an ideal destination for both casual dining and special occasions. JoJo specializes in modern American cuisine, focusing on seasonal ingredients and innovative flavor combinations. The menu features a variety of dishes that highlight the chef's creativity and commitment to quality, often presented in a tasting format.
review_snippets: Very nice but not amazing place. Has a lot of classic Jean Georges dishes. The duck was the better than the filet and the sea bass. Appetizers were all very good. Portions are small. Nothing really stood out. Very nice atmosphere. Service was good but they couldn’t get us out desserts in time for our show. (4 stars)

Amazing experience! ❤️ My husband and I had dinner at JoJo Restaurant and absolutely loved it. The food was delicious — juicy chicken, perfectly cooked salmon with light mashed potatoes, and incredible desserts. The pavlova with passion fruit is a must-try, and the warm chocolate cake stole my heart 🥰 Beautiful interior, unique plates that make you feel special, and a place you definitely want to come back to. Highly recommend! (5 stars)

I wanted to love JoJo’s brunch, but I couldn’t quite get there. The atmosphere is lovely, nestled inside of a renovated townhouse in Manhattan’s UES. Jojo feels like you’re going to your friend’s house to eat, albeit a fairly affluent friend. The atmosphere is perfect for a date night, or like many at the restaurant when we went, a group of friends. We ordered the frittata with crispy potatoes, burrata with fig and toasted sourdough, warm shrimp salad. I’ll start with the highlights. The warm shrimp salad is heavenly, an absolute must try. A great plan on textures with crunchy and creamy, the shrimp is perfectly cooked and smothered in a beurre blanc sauce, the vinaigrette adds a nice bright acidity to balance the creamy avocado, and the dill provides a welcome umami. It’s an excellent salad. The burrata and gallete were both great, balancing sweetness and acidity well. I was disappointed with the frittata. It had the makings of a great dish, but missed the mark. The pickled jalapeño was excellent, but was too far between to add zip to the dish. The herbs were great, but not enough. I was left just wanting more of every component. It felt like a dish that focused more on presentation than execution of the flavors. The biggest miss for me were the crispy potatoes as many were under done. They had a beautiful golden brown crust, but that needs to be followed by a pillowy center that was supremely lacking. Highly disappointing. All in all I expect more from a restaurant Jean-George is putting his name to and my review reflects that. (3 stars)
Great and cozy atmosphere but also a bit crowded. Their sourdough was pretty amazing. The rest was fine but not impressive (4 stars)

bio_text: Joo Ok, meaning 'threading precious jade marbles', is a Michelin-starred restaurant founded by Chef Chang-ho Shin, located in a Hanok-inspired setting in New York City. The restaurant offers a refined dining experience that harmonizes seasonal, locally sourced ingredients with traditional Korean culinary techniques, emphasizing sustainability and a deep respect for the cultural heritage of Korean cuisine. Joo Ok specializes in contemporary Korean cuisine, featuring a 12-course tasting menu that highlights the seasonality and traditions of the culinary art. The restaurant is committed to in-house fermentation and the use of traditional jang, Korea's mother sauces, to create complex flavors in their dishes. Founded by Chef Chang-ho Shin, Joo Ok opened in 2025 and was awarded two Michelin stars within its first year. The restaurant's concept is rooted in the chef's dedication to cultivating traditional Korean flavors using locally sourced ingredients.
menu_items: Gochujang - yellowtail hoe, jaso leaf
Ganjang - deul gi reum - razor clam, house pressed perilla oil, caviar
Doenjang - yugwak - snow crab, dubu, pyogo
Jeon - du reup, shrimp, taro
Makgulli - gim makgulli bread, eel, ganjang jelly
Jeup Chae - roots vegetables, Hokkaido scallop, pinenut yuja sauce
review_snippets: Joo Ok — a new Korean restaurant that opened last year and has already earned two Michelin stars. The chef originally had the restaurant in Seoul and later decided to relocate it to New York. The space is aesthetically beautiful, designed in calming earthy tones. The experience begins in what feels like a traditional garden before entering the restaurant, where guests are welcomed with fermented drinks. The concept revolves around locally sourced and house-made fermented ingredients. The restaurant has its own farm in New York, while many ingredients are also brought directly from Korea. The 12-course tasting menu was very well balanced, highlighting vegetables and seafood with one meat dish. The staff did a wonderful job explaining each course, which made the meal both delicious and educational as we learned about different Korean ingredients and traditions. One of our favorite moments was the sochok roasted tea served with the assortment of desserts at the end of the tasting menu. The ambience is calm and relaxing, with warm and attentive service throughout the evening. We’re already looking forward to coming back. (5 stars)

This was one of the most memorable meals I've had. All the staff were so smiley and welcoming. We each got a welcome drink and shimp snacks; small but packed with flavors. Then we were directed to our table which was prepared with an envelope with the menu inside. We were so excited and our expectations were through the roof! The dishes did NOT disappoint! Oh my goodness their first course, the yellowtail, was so delicious! The combination of the Gochujang and buttery yellowtail really brought up our appetite. My personal favorite course was the lobster. The AROMA of this dish just made me salivate I secretly wanted to speed up with service so I could dive in! and it was so scrumptious indeed! The main dish, the steak, was actually a big surprise as well because the cookery of the meat was so good even though this place is not a steak house. One of our company is from Texas and he was very impressed. I can talk about the food forever but what I have to mention was the service here. The staff were so warm, so welcoming, and very attentive to details. Every time someone left the table, the staff would come and refold our napkins. I also noticed that they would serve the food only when everyone was seated, and would clear the dishes when everyone finished. The pace of the courses was also great! 2+ hours went by so fast we thought it was just an hour. They also gave us a small bag with some memorabilia. It was such a wonderful meal for a celebration. Highly highly recommended! (5 stars)

After your interesting 100 year old elevator ride to the 16th floor of this building right in the center of KTown, you emerge into a serene setting where you sit with a non-alcoholic welcome drink. You are then guided to your table in the attractive main dining room with an elegant Korean home vibe. I had requested a window seat with a view of the Empire State building, and was kindly granted the requested seating. Unbalanced, I would say don’t bother with this since you are way too close to the Empire State building to actually see anything but its base. Some of the captions that Google maps AI has added to my photos are weirdly inaccurate, but I’m not going to get down and correct each one. as an example, it added a caption calling tins of caviar “wine on ice”. The service is crisp and professional with varying degrees of warmth. There were a couple of courses that were introduced by a woman wearing an N 95 mask and it was difficult to understand what she was saying. We enjoyed a couple of the signature cocktails. The tasting menu was artfully, prepared and thoughtfully presented. Some of the dishes were more interesting and flavorful, some were a little bit bland, but we enjoyed all of them. In particular, I thought the beef course was fantastic. The meat was cooked too perfection, juicy and flavorful, and a generous portion. Some of the flavors were fantastic and memorable, and there was a lot of cultural pride in the experience. Overall, I would say that we left feeling full, but not overly stuffed in an uncomfortable way. Having been too many Michelin starred restaurants around the world I would not dispute that this restaurant is worthy of two Michelin stars. On balance, I would say that it is perhaps a bit pricey for the experience, but it is definitely a suitable special occasion venue. (5 stars)

Really attentive & friendly service. Pacing of the meal was good, and in my opinion it’s a lot of food (despite the first few bites being small, it adds up quickly). I appreciate the attention to detail in the decor and in each course - everything was presented so beautifully. My favorites were the gochujang hoe, ganjang perilla oil egg dish, gui wagyu set, and the chestnut chocolate black sesame dessert! And all the byung gwa. (5 stars)

bio_text: Jua is a unique Korean wood-fired restaurant that offers an intimate dining experience, showcasing the artistry of Chef Hoyoung Kim. The ambiance reflects a blend of modern elegance and traditional Korean elements, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere for guests to enjoy a thoughtfully curated meal. Jua specializes in Korean cuisine, utilizing various wood-fire techniques to enhance the flavors of each dish. The restaurant features an original 7-course tasting menu that highlights seasonal ingredients and Chef Kim's culinary expertise. Jua is the creation of Chef Hoyoung Kim, a former executive chef of the two-Michelin-starred restaurant Jungsik. The restaurant is named after his firstborn daughter, Jua, which signifies 'joie' in French.
menu_items: Caviar Kim - $150
Mulhoe - $32
Jook
Branzino
Lamb & Chan
Strawberry Goguma
review_snippets: Amazing experience here. One of the most affordable tasting menu's in NYC at $150 - especially for a Michelin star restaurant. Quality is amazing, the food fresh and cooked to perfection, seasoning on point. My standout dishes were the Caviar Kim, Uni Kim, Jook and Branzino. Staff is friendly and crisp in terms of watching and anticipating what diners need. Special shoutout to Tenzin! She is such a sweet server. I plan to come back in the late spring/early summer to see what changes on the menu but definitely to experience the Caviar Kim again!! (5 stars)

JUA offers a modern and thoughtful Korean tasting menu in an intimate, contemporary setting. There were so many highlights throughout the meal: the caviar Kim opened with decadent, punchy flavors, followed by the Uni Kim with deep umami and crisp seaweed. The mulhoe ceviche was refreshing with a good kick, and the abalone jook was hearty and comforting, if a bit risotto-like. The smoked branzino was a standout - rich, crispy-skinned, and served in a smoky, zesty broth - and the lamb with banchan delivered a fun mix of flavors and inventive sides. Dessert also ended things on a high with a bright mandarin–yuzu ice cream and a chewy, deeply satisfying goguma juak. Overall, the meal was beautifully composed and thoroughly enjoyable. (5 stars)

What a special meal - one of the best, more affordable fine dining spots in the city. Each course has its unique taste, leaving you both satisfied while anticipating the next dish. My personal favorites were the caviar kim, jook, and donut. Coming in, I was worried that my expectations would not be met, but Jua exceeded all of them. (5 stars)

The service, the food, the experience - everything is top tier. It’s $140 for a 7 course tasting experience with 3 “apps”, 2 entrees and 2 desserts. Some of the bites were the best I’ve ever had. The Jook, branzino and the goguma juak were my favorites. I think this is a must try spot! (They’re changing their menu next week) (5 stars)

Octopus - Gochujang Aioli - $40

review_snippets: The octopus is truly something you can only experience here - unlike anywhere else on Earth! The banchan was great too. It was presented as an appetizer that set a really high bar, followed shortly by the octopus. Overall, the food uses acidity to cut through the richness, making everything very well balanced. The greens from the chef's garden in Ohio were great as well, though I felt they could have been introduced a bit earlier in the tasting menu. (5 stars)

One of the best three star dining experience recently. I really like the Korean Contemporary fusion. The octopus and galbi rice roll and splendid. We ordered mixed pairing and were so impressed by the non-alcohol mocktails. Hope the chef will have more seasonal fusion dishes each season. (5 stars)

It had been a while since I treated myself to a fine dining experience, so I came into this meal with high expectations—and it absolutely delivered. The banchan set the tone right away: beautifully presented, full of little tasty surprises that made me wonder what else was coming. The striped jack that followed was even better—the acidity of the white kimchi lifted the fish and gave it such a refined balance. Then came the standout: the octopus. Honestly, it was the best I’ve ever had. Perfectly tender inside, crisp on the outside, and paired with an umami-rich sauce that just lit up my palate. After that, the yellowtail kimbap looked deceptively simple, but the flavor was so elegant and clean—it really stayed with me. The other dishes were great as well, but those three seafood plates really stole the show, they’re the ones that will stick in my memory the longest. Dessert was a thoughtful touch, especially since I had mentioned I was celebrating. Service was attentive, though a bit on the mechanical side, it lacked that extra warmth that would’ve made the night flawless. Still, the food itself was so incredible that I can’t help but give this place top marks. Even now, I can still taste those dishes as I write this. An absolute must try! (5 stars)

I went to Jungsik when it was a 2 star but I wanted to write a review anyways. That's how much i thoroughly enjoyed this place. Top 3 restaurant of all-time for me if not Top 1 in terms of food. Best and most fancy amuse bouches I've ever had. Great lobster and fish. And of course the universally renowned, the greatest tasting Octopus on Earth, Mind-blowing. As well as the most innovative and best kimbap in the world. Glad they had a meat dish which also tasted good. Only falloff may have been their desserts. Pretty looking but lacked strength in flavor. Not sure if it was because their head pastry chef left at the time to start her own shop. Aside from that, perfection. I hear now that they've become a 3-star, they have dolsot bibimbap and something that comes with the kimbap. I'm so anticipating it, that Jungsik might be the only Michelin restaurant that I ever spend that kind of money to eat twice at. I do hope their desserts improve a bit though, either in volume or flavor impact. And just for fun maybe adding a gastronomic touch/performance to a dish or two. (5 stars)
search_text: Jungsik New York Banchan - Baek Kimchi, Yukhwe, Yun-dubu, Saewoo Jang, Joomukbap, Baesook Tartlet - $35 Striped Jack - Oscietre Caviar, Smoked Fish Sauce - $35 Octopus - Gochujang Aioli - $40 Mandoo - Wagyu Beef, Gomtang, Foie Gras - $45 Arctic Char - Cured and Dry-aged, Perilla Emulsion - $45 Sea Urchin Bibimbap - Seaweed Rice, Kimchi, Crispy Quinoa - $80 The octopus is truly something you can only experience here - unlike anywhere else on Earth! The banchan was great too. It was presented as an appetizer that set a really high bar, followed shortly by the octopus. Overall, the food uses acidity to cut through the richness, making everything very well balanced. The greens from the chef's garden in Ohio were great as well, though I felt they could have been introduced a bit earlier in the tasting menu. (5 stars) One of the best three star dining experience recently. I really like the Korean Contemporary fusion. The octopus and galbi rice roll and splendid. We ordered mixed pairing and were so impressed by the non-alcohol mocktails. Hope the chef will have more seasonal fusion dishes each season. (5 stars) It had been a while since I treated myself to a fine dining experience, so I came into this meal with high expectations—and it absolutely delivered. The banchan set the tone right away: beautifully presented, full of little tasty surprises that made me wonder what else was coming. The striped jack that followed was even better—the acidity of the white kimchi lifted the fish and gave it such a refined balance. Then came the standout: the octopus. Honestly, it was the best I’ve ever had. Perfectly tender inside, crisp on the outside, and paired with an umami-rich sauce that just lit up my palate. After that, the yellowtail kimbap looked deceptively simple, but the flavor was so elegant and clean—it really stayed with me. The other dishes were great as well, but those three seafood plates really stole the show, they’re the ones that will stick in my memory the longest. Dessert was a thoughtful touch, especially since I had mentioned I was celebrating. Service was attentive, though a bit on the mechanical side, it lacked that extra warmth that would’ve made the night flawless. Still, the food itself was so incredible that I can’t help but give this place top marks. Even now, I can still taste those dishes as I write this. An absolute must try! (5 stars) I went to Jungsik when it was a 2 star but I wanted to write a review anyways. That's how much i thoroughly enjoyed this place. Top 3 restaurant of all-time for me if not Top 1 in terms of food. Best and most fancy amuse bouches I've ever had. Great lobster and fish. And of course the universally renowned, the greatest tasting Octopus on Earth, Mind-blowing. As well as the most innovative and best kimbap in the world. Glad they had a meat dish which also tasted good. Only falloff may have been their desserts. Pretty looking but lacked strength in flavor. Not sure if it was because their head pastry chef left at the time to start her own shop. Aside from that, perfection. I hear now that they've become a 3-star, they have dolsot bibimbap and something that comes with the kimbap. I'm so anticipating it, that Jungsik might be the only Michelin restaurant that I ever spend that kind of money to eat twice at. I do hope their desserts improve a bit though, either in volume or flavor impact. And just for fun maybe adding a gastronomic touch/performance to a dish or two. (5 stars)

bio_text: Junoon is a sophisticated Indian restaurant located in the heart of New York City, offering a vibrant and contemporary dining experience. The restaurant combines traditional Indian flavors with modern culinary techniques, creating a unique atmosphere that invites guests to explore the rich tapestry of Indian cuisine. Junoon specializes in Indian cuisine, focusing on authentic flavors and innovative presentations. The menu features a variety of dishes that highlight traditional spices and cooking methods, with an emphasis on seasonal ingredients.
menu_items: Eggplant Chaat - crispy eggplant, raita, tamarind chutney, red onion, chaat masala - $43
Palak Shammi Kebab - spiced spinach patty, walnut radish chutney, watermelon radish, pickled red onion - $43
Kurkuri Bhindi Chaat - crispy okra, amchoor powder, raspberry chutney, raita, mango - $43
Mirch Pakora - shishito peppers, whipped paneer and goat cheese, everything chutney - $43
Tuna Puchka - tuna, black salt, caviar, mint cilantro jaljeera, semolina puff - $43
Ghost Chicken Tikka - ghost chili marinated chicken thighs, smoked carrot-coconut puree, carrot & orange salad - $43
review_snippets: Junoon definitely lives up to its reputation as a Michelin-star restaurant. The food was beautifully executed and full of bold, balanced flavors. The mango fish curry was very flavorful, with a great mix of sweetness and spice that didn't overpower the dish. For dessert, the ma rice pudding was excellent creamy and comforting, topped with toasted almonds and pomegranate that added a really nice texture and contrast. One of the highlights was the pani puri with tuna. It was very good and refreshing, and a creative, modern take on a classic Indian street food. Overall, a great dining experience with thoughtful dishes and high-quality ingredients. Definitely worth a visit if you're in Flatiron and looking for elevated Indian cuisine. (5 stars)

Michelin-starred Indian restaurant in Midtown Manhattan. We came here for dinner and enjoyed the special fixed menu option for Valentine’s Day. Course #1 (Starter): three tiny handheld bites. The first was an interpretation of Pani Puri, the second was a Saag Rota with Truffles and the third was Uthappam topped with a seaweed caviar. Course #2 (Appetizer): we got the Smoked Chicken Vindaloo Tikka and the Tuna and Caviar Phuckha. Both were absolutely perfect, I particularly enjoyed the grilled flavor of the chicken. Course #3 (Entree): we chose the Lobster Moilee served on a bed of coconut cream sauce along with the Xacutti Chicken, served in a gravy of coconut, tamarind and red chilies. We loved both dishes, especially the lobster which was cooked to perfection. The entrées were served with rice, daal done two different ways, crispy stringy okra and a basket of naan. Course #4 (Palatte cleanser): A small Dragonfruit sorbet. Course #5 (Dessert): We chose the chocolate mousse/cake served with this frozen fruit circle which we couldn’t identify but tasted pretty interesting and we also got the sticky toffee pudding which had whole pieces of dates in them. Both desserts were fantastic. Special shout out to the service team: we ordered some mocktails in the beginning that we absolutely hated and they were so generous to switch them out for mango lassi free of charge. On the bill they even deducted the charge for the mocktails. We really enjoyed this Valentine’s Day dinner. (4 stars)

Junoon in New York City, a former Michelin-starred restaurant, in my opinion, still deserves that star status. My experience was absolutely spectacular—from the aesthetics, to the ambiance, to the perfect noise level, and, of course, the food and service. I can’t give a higher review—if I could, I would call it a 10-star restaurant. We enjoyed a four-course meal on a Friday evening, March 6th, for my wife’s birthday. They acknowledged her birthday, took our coats, and every waiter was attentive and on point. The dishes were phenomenal, from the small plates to the dessert. The menu included standout small plates: I had the tandoori octopus, and my wife had the Ghost Chicken Tikka. For the main course, I ordered the Bhuna Murg Tadka, and my wife had the tellicherry duck with peppercorn sauce—both were absolute showstoppers. And for dessert, we had the Mumbai Bar, a white chocolate coconut mousse with pistachio, alongside a junoon plum sorbet, and my wife also had a mango kulfi pop. The entire experience was exceptional—every bite was crafted to perfection. The bill was worth every dollar, and we left with huge smiles—especially compared to other fine dining experiences like Gallagher’s. If we ever return to New York, Junoon will be at the top of our list. I had considered Bungalow, a fusion restaurant, but I’m so glad we chose Junoon for a traditional Indian feast. This was a dining experience we’ll be talking about for days. (5 stars)

We came for lunch hoping for the tasting menu, not realizing it’s usually only offered at dinner. The team kindly accommodated us with a mini five-course menu, which was such a thoughtful touch. Every dish was delicious, beautifully balanced, and clearly made with care. The service was warm, attentive, and exceptional. An unforgettable lunch — we can’t wait to come back. (5 stars)

bio_text: Jupiter is a vibrant dining destination located at Rockefeller Center, offering a lively atmosphere that celebrates the joy of Italian cuisine. With a focus on handmade pastas and a curated selection of New Italian wines, the restaurant invites guests to indulge in a culinary experience that is both comforting and sophisticated. Jupiter specializes in handmade pastas and seasonal vegetables, complemented by grilled meats. The menu emphasizes a New Italian culinary approach, showcasing the richness of Italian flavors paired with a diverse wine selection. Jupiter is the second restaurant from Clare de Boer, Annie Shi, and Jess Shadbolt, the team behind King.
menu_items: FRITTO MISTO - with shrimp, calamari, and zucchini with herby creme fraiche and pomodoro - $28
BRUSCHETTA - with mashed peas, ricotta, lemon and mint - $16
BURRATA - soft mozzarella with fennel fronds and Capezzana olive oil - $18
FLUKE CRUDO - with fennel and Sorrento lemon - $26
OLIVES - $10
FOCACCIA - with confit garlic - $12
review_snippets: My sister & I recently visited our hometown NYC and met some old friends at Jupiter for lunch. We had a wonderful experience. It’s a beautiful restaurant adjacent to the Rockefeller Center skating rink with views of the rink while you're dining. It certainly put us in the Christmas spirit. The food was wonderful but the portions are small for the price but it was delicious. My sister & I were wanted to eat light so we shared the arancini (rice balls) which were outstanding and the pspardelle pasta with slow cooked beef ragu. Delicious! Pancetta dessert was fabulous! Staff was great. It was an overall fun & enjoyable experience. (5 stars)

Let’s start with the elephant in the room: what on earth happened to the concourse area? I was expecting something in the vein of the former Sea Grill — you know, elegant, polished, maybe even a hint of nostalgia. Instead, we got… whatever this is. A far cry from what once was, and not in a poetic way. As for the food: perfectly fine. Not life-changing, not offensive — just fine. The real shocker was the $65 “pasta water” candle, which feels like performance art about modern dining prices. Bold of them to charge museum gift shop money for something you can generate yourself by boiling noodles. On the bright side, the olives appetizer was extremely plentiful — the kind of plentiful that makes you wonder if they know something you don’t, like an impending olive shortage they’re trying to single-handedly prevent. The rigatoni was tasty and came in a decent portion, so no complaints there. The gnocco (or what they called gnocco) was… not something I would’ve recognized as gnocchi in any universe. I would’ve been disappointed, but my wife thoroughly enjoyed it, so I’ll go ahead and declare it a victory. Dessert was a tiramisu that landed squarely in the “good but not postcard-worthy” category — perfectly adequate to scratch the itch without inspiring poetry. Overall? Jupiter is a decent meal wrapped in a baffling setting, with a pasta water price tag that will haunt me for a while. (3 stars)

An unlikely location for such a tasty meal. Jupiter is swanky without being pretentious and does a phenomenal job marrying classic Italian dishes with a few more elevated twists scattered throughout the menu. Aside from a great meal, their manager, Pat, is a class act. After learning that the restaurant no longer offered matchbooks, Pat went above and beyond to make sure I got one mailed to my home once they came back into production. A handwritten card is not something you see in your mailbox every day, let alone from a restaurant you dined at 3 months prior. To feel like a priority even after the bill has been paid is a wonderful feeling. More people should be talking about Jupiter and I hope to dine there again soon. (5 stars)

Had a wonderful experience at Jupiter Restaurant in Rockefeller Center! The atmosphere was beautiful, the food was delicious, and the service was top-notch. A special shoutout to Sam, who was so sweet and helpful throughout our meal such a genuinely kind person who made our evening even better. Highly recommend stopping by if you’re in the area! (5 stars)

bio_text: Jōji is a Michelin-starred restaurant located in the heart of Midtown’s One Vanderbilt, offering an intimate dining experience infused with authentic Japanese character. The serene atmosphere is designed to reflect a deep reverence for nature, creating a refined setting that inspires and delights guests. With a focus on personalized service, Jōji provides a sophisticated culinary journey that is both elegant and memorable. Jōji specializes in a traditional multi-course Omakase experience, where each meal is uniquely crafted for the guest using the finest seasonally available ingredients. The menu is complemented by premium sake and fine wine, enhancing the overall dining experience. The restaurant is led by Chef-partners George Ruan and Wayne S. Cheng, with dining operations overseen by Michelin-Starred Chef Daniel Boulud’s The Dinex Group. Jōji has been awarded a prestigious Michelin star.
review_snippets: We had a truly unique omakase experience here. The atmosphere feels authentically Japanese from the chef’s technique to the presentation and pacing of each course. Every bite was thoughtfully prepared, beautifully plated, and genuinely delicious. The service was attentive and professional.However, it’s important to note that the price is extremely high. We paid $997 for two, before tip, which makes this one of the most expensive omakase experiences I’ve ever had. While the quality is excellent, the cost may not be justifiable for everyone. If you’re looking for a luxurious, authentic Japanese omakase and don’t mind splurging, this place is worth trying at least once. (4 stars)

each dish was beautifully presented. the fish was fresh and there were some interesting bites like deep sea rockfish and a mushroom sushi. also a great uni and caviar handroll. also when you order hot tea you get free refills on your cup until the end of the meal which was nice. (5 stars)

Joji was a pleasant surprise. The execution, service, and atmosphere were all 10/10. If anything, the 90s playlist was a bit distracting 😌—I would’ve enjoyed something more relaxing—but it didn’t take away from the experience. I’ll absolutely return. (5 stars)

★★★★★ Five Stars — Jōji is an absolute knockout. Jōji is the kind of place that makes Midtown feel like Tokyo for a couple of hours: tucked beneath One Vanderbilt/Grand Central, serene and intimate, but never stiff or pretentious. ￼ The room has that “hidden counter” energy people rave about—quiet confidence, immaculate pacing, and a vibe that somehow feels both elevated and genuinely fun. ￼ Chef Wayne is the real deal: cool, funny, easy-going, and clearly operating at a very high technical level. You can tell he’s not just serving you—he’s hosting you, teaching you, and keeping the whole counter engaged without ever breaking the flow of the meal. (It’s no surprise he’s part of the chef team that’s built Jōji’s reputation.) ￼ The fish was spectacular—clean, vibrant, and obviously handled with obsessive care. Course after course, everything tasted fresh and intentional, with that refined omakase discipline you expect from a top NYC counter. ￼ And the beverage program is not an afterthought—it’s a co-star. Jōji literally frames the experience as a chef-and-sommelier pairing on equal footing, and it shows. ￼ Our sommelier dialed us in with phenomenal Champagne—ranging across styles and landing on a memorable 2012 Laurent-Perrier that drank beautifully with the sushi. ￼ (The broader buzz about the pairings and drinks program is deserved—French wines and thoughtful selections come up repeatedly.) ￼ Bottom line: this place was fire. The vibe was phenomenal, the food was flawless, and the hospitality felt personal. I’d come back again and again—Jōji delivers the kind of night you talk about afterward. (5 stars)

bio_text: Bar Kabawa is a vibrant dining destination located in New York, offering a unique blend of casual atmosphere and high-quality culinary experiences. The restaurant embodies a modern aesthetic, inviting guests to enjoy a relaxed yet sophisticated environment while indulging in a diverse menu. Bar Kabawa focuses on innovative dishes that highlight fresh ingredients and bold flavors. The menu features a variety of options, emphasizing a contemporary take on traditional cuisine, with an emphasis on shareable plates and creative cocktails.
menu_items: Tuna Carpaccio - avocado, yuzu, sesame - $20
Sliced Yellowtail - passionfruit, chive, daikon - $24
Cultured Butter & Caviar - $40
Ricotta, Jam & Chili Crunch - $14
Eggplant & Pine Nut Gremolata - $14
Chickpea & Sesame - $14
review_snippets: I really enjoyed dining here. Everything was delicious, and from our seats at the counter, it was so interesting to watch the chefs prepare each dish. It's a 3 course prix fixe menu, but you get several side dishes which are all great. I particularly liked the Japanese sweet potato which was roasted with pineapple juice. I loved the cobia, especially as it evoked memories of when I ate kingfish in Trinidad. Best of all, the staff are all so warm and friendly, reflecting the spirit of the Caribbean. (5 stars)

I went here the other night to celebrate my wife's new job. I stayed up until midnight two weeks before the reservations were available so I could get my pick on Open Table (this was a new experience for me). What can I say about this place that everyone isn't already saying? The space was cool. The service was impeccable. The drinks were creative and spirit forward. The food was plated beautifully and packed with flavor. If I have one complaint, it is the price for the experience. The price is justified because of the high level of service and food quality. It just means I can't go here once a week to eat this delicious, delicious food. Maybe Paul Carmichael will eventually open an a la carte restaurant that uses slightly less luxe ingredients, so then I can bear witness to his genius as often as I please. (5 stars)

Kabawa deserves all the flowers it has been getting from the NY Times and James Beard foundation. It’s inventive but most importantly it’s delicious. Standouts include the iconic goat curry which will be hard to remove from the menu because it’s so delicious. Everything was so good but what sets this restaurant apart is the warm, personable hospitality. We were able to talk to Chef Carmichael and what a kind, funny and incredibly warm human being. His ethos is infused into every part of the restaurant. At the bottom of the menu he puts the phrase. “Love yuh self.” You will feel the love after dining at Kabawa. (5 stars)

I visited Kabawa on a recent trip to New York. The open kitchen at the bar makes fantastic viewing as you get to see all the prep. The atmosphere is modern, but also warm and upbeat, including the adjoining bar. The food itself was one of the best meals I have ever eaten. Great balancing of the main (goat) and accompanying sides. Could not recommend enough. I had 1 Plantain/cod/caviar, 2 Goat, 3 Sorbet. Really liked the Tamarind palate cleanser too. (5 stars)

The restaurant offers a premier dining experience with a focus on fresh, high-quality ingredients and a commitment to providing an outstanding atmosphere for both dine-in and take-out customers. With a reputation for excellence, Kanoyama invites guests to indulge in a diverse array of Japanese cuisine, ensuring a memorable culinary journey. Kanoyama specializes in sushi and Japanese cuisine, featuring a menu that includes a variety of appetizers, entrees, soups, salads, and sake. The restaurant is particularly noted for its omakase offerings, showcasing a selection of the freshest fish, including bluefin, bigeye, and yellowfin tuna, as well as seasonal specialties. Kanoyama has achieved top ratings from Zagat and Michelin, and has recently expanded to accommodate a greater capacity while maintaining a spotless and well-maintained dining space.
