review_snippets: Disappointing sushi place. Went here for Valentine's Day, and got seated promptly. Ordered a sushi sashimi platter for 2; one of their pricier options. Waiter forgot my beer until after we finished our appetizer, which was a solid 20 minutes after order. The main platter took quite a while to come out; at least 30 minutes between when we finished the appetizer and the actual food, which was pretty ridiculous. The platter included a "chef chosen sushi roll". Very disappointingly, it was a California Roll. The most expensive platter on their menu, and their "chef" chooses a California Roll? The sashimi cuts were some of the smallest I've ever seen. This place really has a Michelin star? lmfao (1 stars)
Great spot for sushi! Family had a great time with the nakaochi. Manager was so friendly and accommodating. Would come back again! (5 stars)

Selection, atmosphere and overall standard of service. The execution was excellent, specially in timing the presentation of the order of sashimi and sushi as well as cooked dishes. The Gen Zers amongst us were impressed too. Well done. Will be back. (5 stars)

Walked in here on a Sunday afternoon for dinner and was seated right away. The sushi was overall pretty good. We got the sushi special and sashimi special. It is kind of on the pricey side but overall the price isn't too bad given the quality of fish. One thing that takes away one star from atmosphere is that it was quite warm inside the restaurant and the temperature outside was 90s at the time. (5 stars)

bio_text: Kanyakumari is a vibrant dining destination located near Union Square, dedicated to showcasing the rich culinary heritage of Southern India, particularly the Tamil community. The restaurant offers a warm and inviting atmosphere where each dish is crafted to celebrate the diverse flavors and spices of the region, making every meal a festive experience. Kanyakumari specializes in Southern Indian coastal cuisine, featuring a menu that includes dishes like kochi vegetable stew, crab masala fry, and baby goat biryani. The restaurant emphasizes spice-forward flavors and traditional cooking techniques, offering a unique tasting experience that highlights the culinary diversity of Tamil Nadu. Kanyakumari is the latest venture by Salil Mehta, a veteran restaurateur known for his Michelin-starred restaurant Laut. The restaurant opened in 2023, following Mehta's previous establishment, Kebab aur Sharab, which focused on Northern Indian cuisine.
menu_items: Steamed Prawns Idli - Garlic Podi, Gunter Coconut Chutney - $19

review_snippets: One of the best Indian restaurants in NYC with food and service that’s simply exceptional. The Vada Pav is divine as they make their bread that’s just fluffy and fresh. The goat biryani and Fish curry are full of flavor and have a nice spicy flavor. Special shout out to Sunny who’s simply an incredible guy and made our meal special. (5 stars)

Kanyakumari Indian Restaurant was a really great experience. The food was very flavorful across the board, and you can tell the menu is well thought out with a nice balance of dishes. Everything came out fast, which I always appreciate. The ghee rice was especially flavorful and paired perfectly with the curries. The fish curry stood out it had deep, rich flavor with a really nice charred taste that added something extra. The shrimp curry was very good as well, nicely seasoned and cooked just right. Overall, a solid spot if you're looking for flavorful Indian food that comes out quickly and is clearly prepared with care. I'd definitely come back. (5 stars)

The dosa was spectacular, I loved it so much I preferred two!! The waiter was wonderful but I want to also give a special shout out to the host because she was such a sweetheart! She did a great job. I loved the chicken curry dish but the fried chicken was not as memorable, I’d say you can skip it. I also loved the vegetable stew but warning it is spicy! I also liked the creativity of the shrimp idli. Great drinks - loved the lassi (5 stars)

Absolutely loved our experience here! The food was delicious, especially the fish dishes—so flavorful and perfectly prepared. Every bite felt thoughtful and authentic to South Indian cuisine. Our waiter Sunny was amazing—attentive, knowledgeable, and genuinely made the experience even better. The atmosphere was everything: vibrant, welcoming, and beautifully done. Already can’t wait to go back. Highly recommend! (5 stars)

bio_text: Katz's Delicatessen, established in 1888, is New York City's oldest deli and a cherished institution in the heart of the Lower East Side. Renowned for its vibrant atmosphere and rich history, Katz's offers a quintessential New York dining experience, where locals and tourists alike gather to enjoy classic deli fare. The restaurant's walls are adorned with photographs of famous patrons, reflecting its longstanding connection to the cultural fabric of the city. Katz's specializes in traditional Jewish deli cuisine, focusing on high-quality meats such as pastrami, corned beef, and brisket. The menu features classic items like the iconic pastrami sandwich and matzoh ball soup, with a commitment to slow curing methods that enhance flavor without additives. The deli operates in a casual format, allowing guests to enjoy their meals on-site or through nationwide shipping. Katz's Delicatessen was originally founded as Iceland Brothers in 1888 and was renamed after Willy Katz joined in 1903. The deli has been family-run for over a century, with significant ownership transitions leading to its current management. The establishment has become a cultural landmark, known for its slogan 'Send A Salami To Your Boy In The Army' during World War II and its role as a gathering place for the Yiddish theater community.
menu_items: Katz's Pastrami Sandwich - $28.95
Katz's Potato Latkes - $16.95
Katz's Dinner for 2 - $80
Matzoh Ball Soup - $9.95
Pastrami - Sliced by the Pound - $40
Corned Beef - Sliced by the Pound - $38
review_snippets: I tried the pastrami and corned beef sandwiches, and honestly, I think this is why I don’t usually get excited about viral food spots. The sandwiches were pretty mediocre. The meat didn’t have much flavor, the sandwich was served super cold, and the texture was too tough to really enjoy. The bread, though, was excellent, probably the best part of the whole thing. The russian sauce is sweet relish nothing special. I felt that the restaurant was overrated and that’s why I didn’t enjoy that much. It’s not something I’d go back for, and if you haven’t tried it yet, you’re not really missing much. That said, the historical vibe of the restaurant was cool. But it has a crazy line to wait to go in and then wait for available cutter. I wouldn’t personally recommend it, but if you’re curious about viral places, it might still be worth checking out just for the experience. (3 stars)

Just left Katz’s Delicatessen and it absolutely lived up to the hype. There was a huge lineup when we got there, but it moved fast. We were inside in about 10 minutes. We lined up at cutter #7 and that took another 15 minutes or so. Even with the crowd, they were running a super smooth operation. You can tell they’ve been doing this for a long time. We ordered the pastrami on club with cheese, corned beef on rye, a potato latke, and fries. The sandwiches came with pickles, both half sour and full sour, which were great. The pastrami was out of this world. Easily the best I’ve had. Tender, juicy, packed with flavor. The latke was also excellent, crispy on the outside and soft inside. The corned beef just wasn’t for me, but that’s personal preference. I do wish I had tried the brisket instead. Overall, a classic NYC experience and definitely worth the visit. (5 stars)

Katz’s Delicatessen is definitely an NYC classic and a must-visit at least once. The atmosphere is super authentic and chaotic in a fun way — it really feels like a piece of New York history. The food is very good, especially the pastrami sandwich. The meat is tender, flavorful, and the portions are huge (easily enough to share). You can tell the quality is there and that they know what they’re doing. That said, it’s extremely crowded and the system can feel a bit stressful and confusing, especially if it’s your first time. Sometimes it’s not very clear where you’re supposed to pay or if you can add more items to your order, which makes the experience a little overwhelming. Prices are also quite high for what you get, even though it’s iconic. Overall, it’s a great experience and worth trying for the vibe and the food, but probably not a place I’d go to regularly. Still, a solid 4 stars for the quality and the legendary NYC feel. (4 stars)

The food was fine and about what you would expect from a decent delicatessen. They're fairly consistent with their level of quality and portion sizes as well. If your goal was to get a great pastrami sandwich, you're probably better off just going somewhere else (and it would be a lot cheaper, too). But this is a NY staple and is a great place to visit once (and I mean just once). Their prices reflect their mainstream popularity so just keep that in mind. Their portion sizes are also huge so that offsets it somewhat. Just something to keep in mind. Lines can get long but you can avoid that by going earlier or later. You could also order pickup if you don't want to stand inside for long. I mentioned earlier that if your goal was to get a great pastrami sandwich, you could go elsewhere. I'm not going to list any places since that would be inappropriate on someone else's business page, but you could find them through google. Alternatively, if your goal was just to go to any random delicatessen, you could walk down the street. (5 stars)

review_snippets: Came here for a date night with my partner and we had such a great experience. Our reservation was at 5:30 PM, and it wasn’t too busy yet (it started getting packed around 6). The host was very kind and explained that they didn’t have any private seating areas, but he still tried his best to find us a good spot since we wanted to take pictures without using flash and disturbing others. We ordered the chicken tandoori, which was a little salty in my opinion, but eating it with the onions balanced the flavor out really well. We also got the crispy potatoes, which were amazing. For our main dishes, we ordered garlic naan, butter chicken, and a side of white rice. The butter chicken was rich, flavorful, and super buttery. Surprisingly, my partner’s favorite dish was the white rice—he said it had so much flavor on its own. We also tried two drinks: the mango lassi and a mint drink (I forgot the name), and we absolutely loved them. The mango lassi was especially delicious—honestly one of the best mango lassis we’ve ever had. For dessert, we ordered the carrot pudding, which came with shredded carrots and vanilla ice cream on top. Everything we tried was so good and definitely did not disappoint. The atmosphere was cozy and really nice, and the bar was huge with lots of wines and beautiful decorations. Since it’s Valentine’s season, they also has heart balloons floating around, which was super cute. At the end of the night, our server even gave us two balloons to take home. The service was great overall—our server was friendly and checked in on us often. If you haven’t tried this place yet, you should definitely come check it out! (5 stars)

Kebab & Sharab never disappoints! It is hands down one of the best in the city for Indian food. We tried the lamb chops, chicken Kashmiri kebab, another lamb dish I can’t remember the name, and the waygu kebabs, bone marrow pulao, soya chaap, naan, their famous butter chicken, Kerala prawn curry and roomali roti everything was outstanding. The lamb chops were tender and perfectly spiced, the Kashmiri kebab was packed with flavor, and the bone marrow pulao was rich and comforting. The butter chicken truly lives up to the hype, and the fresh naan and roomali roti were the perfect finishing touch. The desserts were honestly the highlight, so unique and beautifully crafted. Their gulab jamun dessert was this perfect modern twist on a classic, warm and indulgent with just the right balance of sweetness. And the guava dessert was unbelievable: refreshing, fragrant, and layered with Indian flavors in a way that felt both nostalgic and completely new. Amazing food, great vibe, and attentive service. Definitely a spot I’ll keep coming to. (5 stars)

Oh my god, where can I start — Kebab Aur Sharab is hands down one of the most memorable dining experiences I’ve had in NYC. I came here with my friends and from the moment you walk in, the vibe pulls you in with warm lighting, stylish interiors, and an energy that feels upscale yet welcoming. It’s the kind of place where every detail feels intentional(even with the plating of the menu items!). To start off it is vegetarian friendly and has amazing variety. The soya chaap to the paneer to gol gappe and to their vegetable kebab - everything was packed with amazing flavor. I really loved the Dal Makhani and Paneer Butter Masala which went really well with the Garlic Butter Naan! We ordered 2 orders of the paneer and one order of the Dal which was more than enough for my friends and I! I am a big fan of green chutney and I have to say the one here was top notch - it complemented everything!!! What truly takes Kebab Aur Sharab to the next level, though, is the service. The staff is attentive, knowledgeable, and genuinely passionate about the menu. They’re happy to make recommendations and make you feel taken care of without ever hovering. Overall, Kebab Aur Sharab isn’t just a restaurant — it’s an experience. Incredible food, amazing drinks, great vibes, and top-tier service all in one place. If you’re in NYC and don’t check this spot out, you’re seriously missing out. Will definitely be coming back soon! (5 stars)

If you want to go eat Indian food and feel happy about spending money at an Indian restaurant THIS IS NOT THE PLACE. The food is overpriced for the quantity. The flavors are okay. We ordered the dori kebab and it was $30+ for one small string of kebab. I thought Punjabi's love to feed and give a good portion size. The chicken curry your mother could cook better. The biriyani was also very ordinary but good sized mutton pieces. I've had much better food at Baar Baar, GupShup, Utsav. I would not come here the second time. (2 stars)

We ordered the chicken tandoori, which was a little salty in my opinion, but eating it with the onions balanced the flavor out really well. We also got the crispy potatoes, which were amazing. For our main dishes, we ordered garlic naan, butter chicken, and a side of white rice. The butter chicken was rich, flavorful, and super buttery. Surprisingly, my partner’s favorite dish was the white rice—he said it had so much flavor on its own. We also tried two drinks: the mango lassi and a mint drink (I forgot the name), and we absolutely loved them. The mango lassi was especially delicious—honestly one of the best mango lassis we’ve ever had. For dessert, we ordered the carrot pudding, which came with shredded carrots and vanilla ice cream on top. Everything we tried was so good and definitely did not disappoint. The atmosphere was cozy and really nice, and the bar was huge with lots of wines and beautiful decorations. Since it’s Valentine’s season, they also has heart balloons floating around, which was super cute. At the end of the night, our server even gave us two balloons to take home. The service was great overall—our server was friendly and checked in on us often. If you haven’t tried this place yet, you should definitely come check it out! (5 stars) Kebab & Sharab never disappoints! It is hands down one of the best in the city for Indian food. We tried the lamb chops, chicken Kashmiri kebab, another lamb dish I can’t remember the name, and the waygu kebabs, bone marrow pulao, soya chaap, naan, their famous butter chicken, Kerala prawn curry and roomali roti everything was outstanding. The lamb chops were tender and perfectly spiced, the Kashmiri kebab was packed with flavor, and the bone marrow pulao was rich and comforting. The butter chicken truly lives up to the hype, and the fresh naan and roomali roti were the perfect finishing touch. The desserts were honestly the highlight, so unique and beautifully crafted. Their gulab jamun dessert was this perfect modern twist on a classic, warm and indulgent with just the right balance of sweetness. And the guava dessert was unbelievable: refreshing, fragrant, and layered with Indian flavors in a way that felt both nostalgic and completely new. Amazing food, great vibe, and attentive service. Definitely a spot I’ll keep coming to. (5 stars) Oh my god, where can I start — Kebab Aur Sharab is hands down one of the most memorable dining experiences I’ve had in NYC. I came here with my friends and from the moment you walk in, the vibe pulls you in with warm lighting, stylish interiors, and an energy that feels upscale yet welcoming. It’s the kind of place where every detail feels intentional(even with the plating of the menu items!). To start off it is vegetarian friendly and has amazing variety. The soya chaap to the paneer to gol gappe and to their vegetable kebab - everything was packed with amazing flavor. I really loved the Dal Makhani and Paneer Butter Masala which went really well with the Garlic Butter Naan! We ordered 2 orders of the paneer and one order of the Dal which was more than enough for my friends and I! I am a big fan of green chutney and I have to say the one here was top notch - it complemented everything!!! What truly takes Kebab Aur Sharab to the next level, though, is the service. The staff is attentive, knowledgeable, and genuinely passionate about the menu. They’re happy to make recommendations and make you feel taken care of without ever hovering. Overall, Kebab Aur Sharab isn’t just a restaurant — it’s an experience. Incredible food, amazing drinks, great vibes, and top-tier service all in one place. If you’re in NYC and don’t check this spot out, you’re seriously missing out. Will definitely be coming back soon! (5 stars) If you want to go eat Indian food and feel happy about spending money at an Indian restaurant THIS IS NOT THE PLACE. The food is overpriced for the quantity. The flavors are okay. We ordered the dori kebab and it was $30+ for one small string of kebab. I thought Punjabi's love to feed and give a good portion size. The chicken curry your mother could cook better. The biriyani was also very ordinary but good sized mutton pieces. I've had much better food at Baar Baar, GupShup, Utsav. I would not come here the second time. (2 stars)

bio_text: King is a relaxed yet elegant dining establishment that embodies a neighborhood charm while also serving as a destination for special occasions. The restaurant features a serene ambiance with muted tones and white tablecloths, creating a welcoming atmosphere for guests. With a menu that changes daily, King offers seasonal dishes that highlight traditional flavor pairings and techniques, making each visit a unique culinary experience. King focuses on seasonal cuisine with influences from Southern France and Italy. The menu is designed to change daily, emphasizing simple yet exceptional food. Signature techniques elevate each dish, showcasing the restaurant's commitment to quality and flavor.
review_snippets: the menu rotates, but all the food was incredible. the best were the chickpea fries (panisse) which were so smooth on the inside and crispy, and the apple tarte tatin. gooey sweet apple and buttery pastry underneath. the roast chicken was also very solid, well cooked with an interesting bread sauce. (5 stars)

Great relatively small restaurant. Had a very tasty ravioli, topped with crushed hazelnuts and shaved parmesan followed by braised shortribs. Dessert options were a bit limited. Just had some chocolate ice-cream. Service was a bit too fast to my personal taste. (4 stars)

We have loved this restaurant for ever! (And would like to send King chefs Jess and Clare special greetings from the Mothership; River Cafe in London, where we are having lunch a the moment. Ruth, Charles and Sian send their continued congratulations for a job well done…across The Pond. For us, you bring the inventiveness, dedication to craft and superlative local products to your restaurant. Thank you! (And yes, I have your cookbook… not your incredible skill of course!) (5 stars)

I first visited King on Saturday when I was in town for my friends’ 60th wedding anniversary. I had lunch here and was served three appetizers, all of which I truly enjoyed. I’ve always loved Italian food, but the salami I had at King was exceptional — it left such an impression on me that I kept thinking about it even while at work on Monday. So after work on Monday, I came back again, this time sitting at the bar, and once again ordered the salami along with all the appetizers. Everything was just as delicious as the first time. The bar staff who served me (I wish I knew his name) was incredibly kind — when I told him how much I loved the salami, he went the extra mile to write down on a card where I could find and buy it in the city. It’s this kind of thoughtful detail that makes King such a special place. Even if I never go out to buy the salami myself, I’ll continue coming back here regularly because of the consistently wonderful food and the genuine hospitality. Thank you for making each visit memorable — I’ll be back often! (5 stars)

bio_text: Kochi is a Michelin-starred restaurant located in Hell’s Kitchen, New York, that offers a vibrant and youthful take on traditional Korean cuisine. Opened in late 2019, Chef Shim's first solo project combines the accessibility of street food with the depth of authentic flavors, creating a unique dining experience that resonates with both locals and visitors alike. Kochi specializes in an eight-course tasting menu that pays homage to Korean royal cuisine while drawing inspiration from street food. The menu features seasonal ingredients and presents a variety of dishes that highlight the nuances of Korean fine dining, including delicate hwe and texturally rich bibimbap. Opened late in 2019, Kochi is Chef Shim’s first solo project.
menu_items: White Asparagus Soup 백 아스파라거스 - Pine Nuts, Tofu, Purple Sweet Potato
Hwe 도미 - Madai, Rhubarb, Cucumber, Wasabi Chimichurri
Halibut 넙치 - jiri consommé, radish jorim, napa and purple cabbage (Caviar+25)
Octopus Twigim 문어 - Celtuce, Perilla Aioli, Crispy Potato
Duck 오리 - Acorn Jelly, Squash Jeon, Fried Eggplant, Cucumber Kimchi (A5 Wagyu +59)
Tuna Bibimbap 참치 비빔밥 - Blue Fin Tuna, Kimchi Marmalade, Seaweed Rice (Sea Urchin +16)
review_snippets: The tasting menu here is very unique. The mushroom soup was actually the highlight of the whole menu for me! Definitely do the Abalone dish add on. The sea urchin add on was also very interesting to taste. To wrap up, both desserts were very refreshing. Service was very good and the whole restaurant has very cosy vibes, without the “corporate” style that some Michelin stars have. (5 stars)

As a Korean, this maybe very far from the Korean food that I am used to but it was my first fine dining experience so bear with me. All the dishes were Korean inspired, I wouldn’t say they were necessarily Korean food. All the dishes and their ingredients scream Korean but it didn’t feel or taste like it. The tuna bibimbap I got was good and my favourite of the night but it’s not the one that your family would eat of a communal bowl with literally every single fixing. The banana milk dessert also didn’t taste like banana milk at all, I was chasing that nostalgic feeling the entire night but was left feeling a longing for my mom’s cooking instead. Great food and experience but just not Korean. I expected more from a fine dining experience but maybe it’s a me problem. (3 stars)

Instagram: @jojo_gourmand Last year, I checked out Chef Sungchul Sim’s creative take on hand rolls at Mari. Now, a year later, I’m back in his world at the restaurant that originally launched him into NYC’s Korean fine-dining scene. I’d seen photos of Kochi’s cozy dining room, but I didn’t expect it to be this cramped. Kochi (꼬치) means skewer, which is fitting for a menu where most courses arrive threaded. MENU HIGHLIGHTS MUSHROOM SOUP | Shiitake Meringue | Perilla Oil Reminds me of Korea’s chilled pumpkin soup. The sweetness balances the deep mushroom notes, and as the meringue melts, it coats the palate with earthy shiitake richness. HOKKAIDO SCALLOP | Chestnut | White Kimchi The scallop’s natural sweetness worked well with the crisp acidity of white kimchi. A refreshing reset between heavier bites. ABALONE | Shrimp Jeon | Yuja Soy An optional add-on, but absolutely worth it. Tender abalone layered over shrimp jeon, dipped in spicy yuja soy = one of the night’s standout bites. BANANA MILK | Banana Parfait | Banana Compote The nostalgic Korean drink, reimagined as a popsicle. The compote hits with piercing banana intensity, but together with all the components, it became the best version of banana milk ever. 🗺️ Korean ⭐️ Michelin One-Starred 🏷️ US$150+ (4 stars)

Overall, It would have been a 4-star experience if not for the failed duck course. Felt a bit overrated. Favorite courses: abalone, hwe (Hokkaido scallop), and banana milk dessert. The course combinations were creative, and I enjoyed almost all of the dishes—up until the duck. The duck tasted great, but the skin was a little too charred. The staff offered to replace it, which I later regretted, as the second time was poorly executed: very chewy and definitely not up to the standard. Unfortunately, this inconsistency brought down my overall rating of the restaurant. They should really look into why the second preparation was significantly worse than the first. Environment: I don’t think I can give a completely fair rating for the environment because I was seated outdoors with a heater. On two occasions, customers waiting for tables were standing behind me (about a table’s distance). For someone who values a quiet dining experience, this was a major downside. Customers should be seated rather than standing behind diners while waiting—especially when some were in groups. This made the experience feel disorganized. (3 stars)

menu_items: OMAKASE Bar - seasonal otsumami, sashimi, daily selected sushi course, soup, dessert - $295
OMAKASE Table - seasonal otsumami, sashimi, daily selected sushi course, soup, dessert - $270
review_snippets: Everything is fantastic: the food, the service and the sake. Some of the freshest and most delicious sushi I had this year. Really appreciated the warm service as well. I would gladly return if it just wasn't so darn expensive. There are other omakase restaurants in New York City that now offer a similar experience at a much lower price point (easily half of what Kosaka charges). Plus, you must pay up front when you make the reservation. Additionally, it's worth mentioning that this is a very small client restaurant. Not good for loud/large celebrations. Totally fine by me -- but just worth mentioning. (5 stars)

While the presence of high-quality sushi, particularly Omakase, is widespread in New York City today, Kosaka distinguishes itself through several key attributes. The restaurant's fundamental mastery of flavor profiles and technical execution is exceptional. This is complemented by an impeccable service standard, meticulous attention to detail, and a deliberate focus on optimizing the customer's overall experience throughout the meal. Though the cost is commensurate with its status—as is expected of a Michelin-starred sushi establishment—dining at Kosaka represents a truly worthwhile experience. Furthermore, the opportunity to attend the occasional private events hosted here adds another layer of unique value. Sincere appreciation is extended to the entire staff for a magnificent evening (5 stars)

I don’t usually eat raw fish. But my partner convinced me to try it out. And surprisingly they are so tasty. They don’t smell fishy at all. Service was attentive and the space is cozy. Would highly recommended! (5 stars)

I eat omakase a lot and I’m really starting to believe that it’s not necessary to pay over 300 in nyc because of the options available. Although Kosaka comes in just u see 300 its a good use case. Can one sushiya be 3x better than the avg 100 option available? Possible, but it’s really difficult. Is that o-toro nigiri 3x better than any other place? Unlikely. Kosaka is a Michelin star sushiya with a very experienced chef soma steering the ship. What sets it apart: the appetizers, some creative dishes (the one with monk liver was amazing) and the service which was fine dining level and expected with a 1 star rating. The space is also very chic with dramatic lighting and a gorgeous sushi counter bar. So a very satisfying experience with excellent food quality but 3x better than your standard $100 options? Well, that’s up to you but I’d probably choose a cheaper spot and put t at extra money toward a better bottle of wine or sake. Verdict: will not return based on value only. (4 stars)

bio_text: KRU is a modern Thai restaurant located in North Williamsburg/Greenpoint, celebrated for its sophisticated dining experience and refined cooking. The restaurant offers a contemporary interpretation of 100-year-old Thai recipes, showcasing a thoughtful approach to technique and flavor. With a lively atmosphere, KRU also features a front-room bar concept that serves playful Thai drinking food and street-inspired flavors, making it an ideal spot for both intimate dinners and social gatherings. KRU focuses on modern Thai cuisine, reimagining historic dishes with a contemporary twist. The menu features a curated selection of wines that complement the flavorful fare, enhancing the overall dining experience. Signature techniques include a blend of traditional and worldly ingredients, rarely seen in the U.S. Chef Ohm Suansilphong, the head chef, was the opening head chef of Fish Cheeks in Manhattan and has a rich culinary background, having worked under renowned chefs at Nahm in Bangkok, where he earned a Michelin star. His journey from Sukhothai to New York City reflects a deep commitment to Thai culinary tradition.
menu_items: SAVORY FRUIT BITE - caramelized coconut sugar, peanut, peppercorn - $8
SQUID - lemongrass, ginger, chili, lime - $18
STEAK TARTARE - cured egg yolk, spice, bird's eye chili, served with crispy tripe - $19
SUMMER KISS MELON - sweet chili jam, coconut yogurt, pecan - $18
LOBSTER TARTARE - tomato three ways, basil, nori - $8
BONE MARROW - galangal, turmeric, tamarind, toasted white bread - $17
review_snippets: Entrees were the absolute highlight of the meal. The sauce of the lamb shank left a lasting impression and made it so you just want more! The pork belly was on the sweeter side so came in second place. I would order both of these dishes again. For appetizers, the steak tartar was delicious. The salmon was very fresh and clean. Squid was refreshing too. We should have gave our appetizers a bit more thought before ordering. The restaurant was chilly and cold appetizers didn’t help. Great service! All dishes came out in a timely fashion. Staff were attentive and professional. Can’t wait to go back! Hopefully we can have some new items next time. This spot is available with InKind. Can get gift cards on Costco. (5 stars)

This modern Thai/Thai fusion spot in Williamsburg is a good spot for a date night. The interior is intimate, and cozy. Service here is good. I came here for a group dinner with three friends and we ordered their steak tartare, lamb shank, and branzino (they have a fairly small menu). Everything was pretty solid. I enjoyed their steak tartare and thought that it was really unique that they paired the dish with fried tripe. Notes of lemongrass and other spices were really strong, reminding me of Southeast Asia. The lamb shank was flavorful and the meat was so tender. And, the branzino was also delicious. I would note that the portions were a lot smaller than we expected, and everything was a bit on the pricier side. Overall, a nice restaurant for some good food but I would personally prefer more authentic, casual Thai food. (4 stars)

Pre- fixed menu from nyc restaurant week. Food was tasty, we had to order more. Staff is friendly and attentive. The environment, nyc curse of lack of space makes for a loud restaurant and tables very close together. Still enjoy but it was very loud for me. (5 stars)

We enjoyed a special dinner arranged by Kru Restaurant, and the experience was exceptional. The food was delicious, the staff provided warm and attentive service, and the atmosphere was perfectly suited for the occasion. A well-deserved five stars. (5 stars)

bio_text: Kubeh is a vibrant Middle Eastern restaurant located in Greenwich Village, NYC, founded by Chef Melanie Shurka and her husband David Ort. The restaurant is dedicated to showcasing authentic and lesser-known cuisines of the Middle East, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere perfect for both large gatherings and intimate dinners. With a focus on comfort food that evokes nostalgia, Kubeh encourages sharing and communal dining, complemented by a selection of fantastic cocktails and happy hour specials. Kubeh specializes in Middle Eastern cuisine, particularly the versatile dish Kubeh, which can be boiled, fried, or baked. The menu features a variety of mezes, spreads, and main dishes, with an emphasis on fresh, high-quality ingredients sourced from small family farms. The restaurant offers gluten-free, vegan, and vegetarian options, making it suitable for diverse dietary preferences. Chef Melanie Shurka, a native New Yorker of Israeli-Iranian and Ashkenazi Jewish descent, opened Kubeh in July 2017 to share the Middle Eastern dishes of her childhood. After studying law in Israel and discovering her passion for cooking, she honed her skills through various culinary experiences, including working at Balthazar and hosting pop-ups focused on Kubeh. Melanie has also gained recognition by winning Food Network’s Chopped and competing in Alex VS America.

review_snippets: Came for restaurant week and it was so nice seeing the portion sizes didn’t change and a good variety on the menu. I started with the saffron shrimp, had the lamb shank for my main and ended it with the warm brownie for dessert. I also tried their torshitini cocktail which was on the savory side but very delicious. Saffron shrimp was great and I loved the bread to help finish up the sauce. My lamb shank fell off the bone which is always a positive. While I did like it I didn’t feel it stood out for me. The brownie at the end was great and helped close the meal nicely. Overall it was a great experience, the service was excellent and it was a fun and lively dinner spot (3 stars)

solid spread - muhammara is a must. great dips and the chicken shawarma was really good. sweet potato and salmon were phenomenal as well. great flavor all round, smaller portions. really nice spot to catch up with friends and easier res to get. not a omg wow but super solid and good neighborhood go to. (4 stars)

Great spot for a ME dishes to sample. Nice portions, good for sharing and tasting many things. The menu features unique dishes from several cultures in the ME region like Iraqi and Kurdish dishes. We shared all the dishes and loved them all. Would go back to try some more. The atmosphere is modest, this is not a fancy restaurant. Good prices for what you are getting as well. Included the bill so you can see what it cost for 3 people and multiple dishes and coffee at the end. They have bar seating as well as indoor and outdoor tables. We opted to sit indoors at a table. Go and Enjoy! (4 stars)

This is a Michelin star Resturant? Literally the worst middle eastern dishes I’ve ever tasted in my entire life. If you go to Steinway and go to the worst rated Arab Resturant, that would be 10 folds better than their best tasting dish. You can tell they are trying too hard to copy middle eastern food but it just isn’t working out. (1 stars)

restaurant_name: Kung Fu Little Steamed Buns Ramen
bio_text: Kung Fu Little Steamed Buns Ramen offers a vibrant and inviting dining experience, focusing on delivering delicious and authentic Asian cuisine. Located at 146 E 55th St, the restaurant prides itself on its warm atmosphere and commitment to quality, ensuring that every dish is served with love and care. The restaurant specializes in a unique blend of steamed buns and ramen, showcasing a variety of flavors and textures. The menu features a wide range of options, emphasizing fresh ingredients and traditional cooking techniques.
review_snippets: Their food was super authentic and everything was wonderful. Their soup dumplings in this weather was fantastic. Their pan fried pecking duck buns was also very good. This location is cash only but that will not stop you from coming over here. It didn't stop me! 🥟 (5 stars)

The food was great. Fresh, tasty and authentic. Service was incredible. My only note would be that my food was so immensely hot, that my face got burnt once I bit into the pork buns. Probably could have waited a little but the food looked so delicious I had to dig in! Will definitely return but will wait a little before biting into my food 🙂 (4 stars)

Was craving dumplings and found this place by chance with a group of friends. We ordered several different kinds to share. It was all delicious and authentic. Definitely adding it to the rotation. (5 stars)

Finally, the food taste like real Asian food.. I ordered take-out spicy beef Ramen.. they put Ramen and soup in different containers🩷 and even the take-out bag was thermal bag to keep them warm🙏🏼 the portion was really really big and soup was enough amount for almost 2 portion of Ramen and it was really delicious.. and they even put extra spicy sauce, even if I didn't ask for and it was free which I'm not used to it here.. 🩵 (5 stars)

bio_text: Kyma is an upscale Greek and Mediterranean seafood restaurant that seamlessly blends the traditional charm of a Greek taverna with the stylish ambiance of Mykonos. Guests are invited to experience a culinary journey through the sun-drenched islands of Greece, where the rich character of traditional dishes is celebrated in a modern setting. The restaurant emphasizes quality, service, and hospitality, ensuring memorable dining experiences for all occasions. Kyma specializes in Greek and Mediterranean seafood cuisine, featuring a menu that highlights traditional dishes made with the highest quality ingredients. The restaurant prides itself on using extra virgin olive oil from the Peloponnese and fresh fish flown in daily from the Mediterranean.

Dolmades - Grape leaves stuffed with rice & dill, served with tzatziki
Octopus - Grilled, roasted peppers, onions, capers, fava
Kolokithokeftedes - Zucchini fritters, lemon yogurt
Spanakopita - Spinach, leeks, feta phyllo pie
Halloumi Fries - Herb aioli & tomato sauce
review_snippets: Exceptional food and experience. This restaurant was a perfect way to end my week. For what it is the price is extremely reasonable for NYC. Our favorite dishes were the “Pikilia” trio of dips with warm pita bread which complimented each other very well. A good thing to note is that mains are very large and perfect for sharing. We did not know that so we ended up with a lot of takeaway! Overall, the atmosphere of the restaurant was very lively and energetic. The service was very attentive and kind. In total I think our bill came out to be 125 including tax. (5 stars)

I recently celebrated an anniversary with my girlfriend at Kyma, and the entire experience was amazing from start to finish. Our waitress, Nicole, was fantastic — incredibly knowledgeable about the menu and spot on with her recommendations, especially the caramel espresso martini, which was perfect. For appetizers, we had the crab cakes, which were delicious. Our entrées — the lobster pasta and the lamb chops — were cooked beautifully and full of flavor. We ended the night with baklava and pistachio ice cream, the perfect sweet finish to a great meal. Kyma made our special night even more memorable. Highly recommend! (5 stars)

This is a beautiful restaurant in Flatiron with some very good Greek food. Definitely order the dips and Greek salad. All the starters were delicious. Roast chicken was good but not earth shattering. Our server was excellent. I love this space and would definitely return. (4 stars)

Went on a Sunday night and the place was basically empty, which was ok. Service was awesome, super friendly and fast. Food was good as always — everything tastes the same (in a good way). Menu hasn’t changed in forever though, getting a little bored of the same stuff . Would love some new things to try. Clean, chill vibe, no complaints. Still one of my fave Greek spots even if it feels stuck in 201 (4 stars)

bio_text: L'Abeille is an elegant French restaurant with Japanese influences, located in the heart of Tribeca on a charming cobblestone street. With a capacity of 48 seats, the restaurant offers a warm and sophisticated atmosphere, centered around a seasonal Chef’s Tasting Menu complemented by a rotating selection of seasonal à la carte dishes, all paired with an award-winning wine and cocktail program. The culinary focus at L'Abeille is on French cuisine infused with Japanese elements. The menu features a seasonal Chef’s Tasting Menu and a variety of à la carte options, showcasing Chef Mitsunobu Nagae's signature techniques and creative flavor combinations inspired by fresh market ingredients. L'Abeille is the brainchild of Chef Mitsunobu Nagae, a veteran Michelin-starred chef with a rich background in prestigious kitchens across Tokyo, Paris, and New York. Chef Nagae's culinary journey began at the age of 15, leading him to culinary school in Lyon, France, where he was awarded Student of The Year.

Asperge Blanche et Langoustine au Lait Ribot - White Asparagus from Loire, Langoustine, Orange Blossom Scented Buttermilk Foam

Crème Brûlée au Foie Gras - Foie Gras Crème Brûlée, Carrot-Ginger Sorbet
review_snippets: Every dish was a surprise — not only beautifully executed, but genuinely making us discover new flavors and combinations. The food managed to be both creative and comforting at the same time, with each plate presented like a small piece of art. The service was truly exceptional: attentive, knowledgeable, and perfectly paced, making the whole evening feel effortless and special. A must-visit for anyone who loves gastronomy and thoughtful fine dining. We’ll definitely be back (5 stars)

Most of the reason for taking out stars is the price. I think the food was good, but was a little flat for me. I appreciate the presentation and I liked the courses, but I left hungry and I didn’t think the flavors were all that creative or delicious for a Michelin star which such expensive prices. The bread was cold, the butter was cold. I got the petite tasting menu, and I’m glad I didn’t do the full tasting menu. There’s only really three courses that are very very small and dessert. They had a nice place card and gave me a candle for my bday which was nice. The host and the waiters were also wonderful. I think the food just fell flat. For the very very high prices, it just wasn’t worth it for me. I was not impressed unfortunately. For an almost $300 meal, i should be astounded (3 stars)

I knew within the first 30 minutes of this experience that it was going to be one of the best meals of my life, and I was not wrong. I have eaten at many great/Michelin starred restaurants throughout the United States and Europe, and L’Abeille just catapulted its way into my top 5. The space itself is fantastic, beautiful and intimate yet not overbearing, and the service even better. The sommelier was extremely knowledgeable about the wine list and was able to provide us with a bottle that gave us exactly what we were looking for within our price range. And then the food. Chef Mitsunobu walks the line between indulgent decadence and childlike creativity in the greatest way. It is rare that a menu is able to be clearly committed to giving you the best versions of food you have had before, while also introducing you to completely new flavors and culinary ideas. A rarity at most restaurants, the most memorable dish may have been the chicken course. Granted, it was helped with foie gras and whisky infused jus, but still, some of the flavors found on that plate made me stop to reconsider the possibilities of a what a chicken dish can provide. Some other highlights include the most incredible combination of prawns and grilled eggplant inside the flower of a courgette, then a peking duck au poivre with intense peppercorn, and a citrus-forward dessert that played with temperature, acid, and sweetness like not many can. I cannot give any higher praise to Chef Mitsunobu and his team at L’Abeille, and I cannot recommend it enough. My only regret is that I wish I could’ve thanked him myself after the meal. (5 stars)

An incredible dining experience for our birthday! We visited l'abeille recently and every dish had its own personality. The stuffed squash blossom was full of flavor and impeccably plated. The tile fish with tomato sauce vierge was sublime. Loved how the scales were cooked crispy. The desserts were awesome too, the celery popsicle was playful and refreshing — such a fun way to begin the sweet part of the meal. The lemon dessert was creative, bright, and the perfect finish to the evening. (5 stars)

bio_text: L'Abeille à Côté offers a unique dining experience that blends the elegance of French cuisine with the artistry of Japanese culinary traditions. The restaurant is characterized by its warm and sophisticated atmosphere, inviting guests to indulge in a thoughtfully curated menu that reflects a playful interpretation of Michelin-starred dishes. With a focus on quality and creativity, L'Abeille à Côté provides an exceptional dining experience complemented by an award-winning wine list featuring both adventurous and classic selections from around the globe. The restaurant specializes in a refined fusion of French and Japanese cuisines, presenting a menu that emphasizes seasonal ingredients and innovative flavor combinations. Guests can expect a focused selection of wines to enhance their dining experience, with options for corkage available for personal bottles. Chef Mitsunobu Nagae, the owner and executive chef, has an extensive background in Michelin-starred restaurants, having trained under renowned chefs and honed his skills in prestigious culinary institutions. His journey began in Japan and led him to France, where he developed a deep appreciation for French culinary techniques.

The matcha tiramisu was a standout, and the truffle ice cream was also delicious. A place that focuses on doing fewer things, but doing them very well. Will plan another visit soon. (5 stars)
I visited for a special occasion and had a very good experience. The dishes were well-prepared with clean, balanced flavors. Overall, it matched the level of quality I was hoping for. (5 stars)
The sweet potato and spring rolls were a highlight of the meal. The sweet potato was well flavored, and the spring rolls were light and crisp. Both were simple and well done. (5 stars)
One of the better tonkatsus I’ve had. The crust was crisp, the pork was tender, and the yuzu dipping sauce added a nice lift. The service was quick and friendly 👌 (5 stars)

bio_text: La Devozione: The Oval is an intimate 30-seat Italian fine-dining restaurant located in New York, NY, offering a unique pasta tasting menu. The restaurant features an open kitchen that immerses guests in the culinary process, showcasing seasonal ingredients and classic Neapolitan recipes. Under the guidance of Michelin-starred chef Peppe Guida, diners embark on a gastronomic journey that reflects a blend of Italian roots and global influences, culminating in a harmonious dining experience. The Oval specializes in a fine-dining pasta tasting menu, emphasizing the creativity and versatility of PGI Gragnano pasta. The menu features a variety of dishes inspired by global cuisines, reimagined through the lens of Italian culinary traditions. Helmed by Michelin-starred chef Peppe Guida, The Oval represents a culinary journey that begins in New York and traverses various global influences before returning to its Italian roots.

Guests are invited to explore a culinary journey that spans the diverse flavors from North to South Vietnam, all while enjoying a warm and welcoming atmosphere where hospitality is paramount. review_snippets: Love coming here! I have been here multiple times and the food and service is so amazing everytime. Our waitresses Jaycee and Sophia are soooo nice. They were so attentive and sweet, we had such a great experience because of them. 10/10 ⭐️ (5 stars)

This place is such a solid neighborhood spot. Everything we ordered was thoughtfully done and full of flavor. The Pate and Bone was a great starter. The chicken liver mousse was smooth and rich, and the bone marrow with toasted baguette made it extra indulgent without being too heavy. I really loved the Pomelo Salad. It was fresh and bright, with grilled shrimp and a nice balance of citrus, herbs, and a slightly spicy tamarind dressing. Super refreshing, especially with the crispy rice cracker. The Wagyu Pho was excellent. The broth was fragrant and well seasoned, and the wagyu was incredibly tender and comforting. We finished with the avocado coconut ice cream, which was light, creamy, and not overly sweet. The crispy sliced banana a really nice texture. Comfortable, well-executed food. Definitely a spot I’d come back to. (5 stars)

This was my first time trying Vietnamese cuisine, and overall it was a great experience, I’d definitely come back. Went for lunch without a reservation and waited about 10 minutes, which wasn’t bad. The restaurant is nicely decorated and feels warm and welcoming. Staff were very attentive and friendly. As a welcome snack, they served rice crackers with a spicy paste (not sure of the name), which tasted really good. We ordered the tofu and mushroom banh mi and the crab fried rice. The banh mi is a good shareable option, though it could use a bit more sauce to enhance the flavors since tofu can be on the milder side. It came with a house truffle soup on the side, which was absolutely delicious. The crab fried rice, however, had an unusual smell and taste, possibly from the way the egg and crab were cooked together. We’ve had this dish elsewhere without any issues, so this stood out. Despite that, I’d still like to return and try other items on the menu. (4 stars)

I haven’t been to New York in over 10yrs and had to find a Pho spot. Google showed 4.8 stars so I had to come try it for myself. The place was full so reservations and queues are a given. Came alone so I was able to get a seat at the bar fairly quick since someone cancelled. I had the Wagyu Pho (flavorful and no additives needed) with added meatballs (soft and juicy), the Sugarcane Shrimp (tastes like shrimp patty), and Steamed Rice Cake (a little on the oily side but amazing!!). Amazingly delicious!!!! The services provided by both bartenders Sophia and Nikki were amazing and had great recommendations on what to try. They made it feel like I was with friends and didn’t feel like I was having dinner alone! Truly love the food and atmosphere here!!! Highly recommend this place. (5 stars)

bio_text: La Mercerie is a sophisticated dining establishment located within the Roman and Williams Guild in New York. The restaurant offers a warm and inviting atmosphere, blending a modern aesthetic with classic French influences, making it an ideal spot for both casual and special occasions. La Mercerie focuses on French cuisine, featuring a menu that includes lunch, dinner, and weekend offerings. The culinary experience emphasizes seasonal ingredients and traditional techniques, creating a refined yet approachable dining experience.
review_snippets: The restaurant is absolutely beautiful! The decor is stunning feels like you are in Europe! Our server Gabriella was so attentive and her energy and vibe was giving a girlfriend who was taking care of you! Her recommendations were great Andy girlfriends and I had an amazing time! The food is rich so it’s good to share and get a variety of meals! I highly recommend the anchovies with bread because it comes with the most amazing vanilla bean butter and also crème brûlée! (5 stars)

It was our first time visiting this restaurant, and we went here during restaurant week. We love the ambience, and the service was excellent from the host to the server. Everyone was accommodating and friendly. We tried one of each on the menu, and everything was delicious except for the duck and the dessert that has peanuts on it. We also tried the cookie, but it was okay and expensive. My husband likes this restaurant, so we will brunch next time. (5 stars)

I went to La Mercerie for my birthday, and it ended up being one of the most memorable dining experiences I’ve had in New York. The restaurant is absolutely gorgeous, with that unmistakable Roman and Williams design aesthetic, since it’s located inside the stunning Guild furniture store. The décor, tableware, and overall atmosphere feel chic, calm, and beautifully curated — and the best part is that many of the pieces around you are actually available for purchase. It creates a truly immersive experience that blends dining and design in such a unique way. One detail I really appreciated is that the restaurant is dog-friendly, which made my birthday feel even more special. There’s also a lovely shop inside that carries everything from home décor to thoughtful gifts, so it’s easy to lose track of time wandering around before or after your meal. The food was excellent from start to finish. I ordered the crepe, which was perfectly cooked and full of incredible flavor, and the oysters were fresh, delicate, and a great start to the meal. For dessert, the staff surprised me with a crème brûlée for my birthday, and it was absolutely delicious — creamy, silky, and beautifully caramelized on top. Highly recommend for any special occasion. (5 stars)

La Mercerie in New York is one of the most beautiful dining experiences I’ve had. The ambience is stunning — soft light, elegant décor, and that warm French aesthetic that makes you want to stay for hours. Every detail feels intentional and romantic. The food was just as impressive: refined flavors, perfectly balanced dishes, and presentation that looked sexy as hell. From the starters to the dessert, everything tasted thoughtful and beautifully executed. It’s the kind of spot you remember long after you leave. Absolutely worth visiting again for both the atmosphere and the incredible food (5 stars)

bio_text: La Tête d’Or is a sophisticated dining establishment that pays homage to timeless flavors and traditions, seamlessly blending American and French culinary influences. The restaurant's elegant ambiance, characterized by soaring ceilings and deep blue banquettes, creates a welcoming atmosphere that reflects the spirit of France while celebrating the artistry of Chef Daniel Boulud. The menu features Chef Boulud's distinctively French interpretation of steakhouse classics, including wagyu beef, lobster, and tableside-carved prime rib. Emphasizing the use of seasonal ingredients, the culinary approach is guided by the 'triple S' philosophy—soul, seasoning, and sauces—resulting in refined flavors and creative presentations. Chef Daniel Boulud, a native of Lyon, France, has been a prominent figure in the New York culinary scene since 1982. La Tête d’Or is named in tribute to the park in his hometown, reflecting the harmony between his French roots and his life in New York City.

review_snippets: I had the most amazing experience at La Tête d’Or, from the moment we walked in. The restaurant itself is absolutely beautiful. The food was outstanding. Everything tasted incredibly fresh and high quality. The filet mignon was hands down the best I’ve ever had — perfectly cooked, melt-in-your-mouth tender, and full of flavor. Truly unforgettable. The crab cake was delicious, the popovers were incredible, and the Brussel sprouts were amazing (I’m already thinking about when I can have them again!). My husband had the 28 day ribeye and it was EXCELLENT. The vanilla berry soft serve was like nothing I’ve ever experienced.. literally the perfect ending to our night. Can’t wait to try the other flavor. The service was just as impressive as the food. Everyone was fantastic — from the servers, to the hosts and hostesses, and even the QUEEN running the coat check. You can tell they take pride in creating a top-tier experience. This was an amazing night all around. La Tête d’Or has officially made its way to the top of my steakhouse list in NYC. I can’t wait to come back!! (5 stars)

Amazing experience at this restaurant. The food and drinks were outstanding, and the service was top-notch. My favorite dishes included the yellowfin tuna tartare, and the filet mignon was the best I’ve ever tasted! Geraldo, our server, was fantastic—very kind, friendly, and attentive, just like the rest of the staff. It made my birthday dinner truly special. This restaurant is excellent overall. I give it a 10/10 and will recommend it to everyone. I’ll definitely be returning! (5 stars)

To start the place was beautiful. As a starter we ordered a bone marrow which was good but the red stuff on top overpowered the taste of the actual bone marrow. As for the filet mignon it was cooked to perfection. The NY strip was also delicious. We finished our dinner with a delicious ginormous coffee Sundae! The coffee taste wasn’t as strong and the different toppings were a great pair with the ice cream. (5 stars)

I had the pleasure of dining at La Tête d’Or by Daniel, and it was an absolutely exceptional experience from start to finish. Every detail was on point. We began with the hamachi crudo, which was incredibly fresh and beautifully balanced. The wood-fired bone marrow was rich and indulgent, packed with deep flavor. For our mains, the filet mignon topped with foie gras was cooked to perfection — tender, flavorful, and perfectly executed. The Chateaubriand was equally impressive, prepared exactly as requested and simply outstanding. Beyond the food, the service elevated the entire evening. Our server, Victor, was knowledgeable, attentive, and made excellent recommendations that truly enhanced our experience. The manager, Elvir, personally stopped by to ensure everything was going well, which speaks volumes about the level of hospitality here. Even Jenny at coat check was warm and welcoming — every touchpoint felt thoughtful. This is not just dinner — it’s a full experience. Exceptional cuisine, impeccable service, and an atmosphere that makes you want to stay all night. Highly recommend, and I can’t wait to return. (5 stars)

bio_text: La Vara is a celebrated dining destination in Cobble Hill, Brooklyn, that invites guests to experience the vibrant flavors of Spanish cuisine. With a focus on the rich tapestry of Spanish culinary traditions, the restaurant offers a warm and inviting atmosphere where every dish tells a story. The heartfelt hospitality and meticulous curation of dishes create an authentic dining experience that embodies the essence of 'comida casera'—homemade cooking that speaks to the soul. La Vara specializes in Southern Spanish cuisine, exploring its Jewish and Moorish influences. The menu is bold and improvisational, featuring contemporary and original dishes that highlight the aromas of saffron, cumin, and orange blossom. Guests can expect a unique blend of traditional and modern culinary artistry. Chefs Alex Raij and Eder Montero, a husband and wife team, are the driving force behind La Vara, which has been a beloved establishment for 11 years. The restaurant celebrates the Jewish and Moorish legacies in regional Spanish cuisine.

review_snippets: Came here for the first time and was delighted by the good food. We were two persons and had over 8 to 10 dishes including dessert and a few drinks. The most outstanding dishes were the salchichon, arroz meloso and morros prensados, I was pretty impressed of their taste. We had a vermut and wine to drink with the dishes. Service was superb and the atmosphere great, even though the place was full. The desserts were also very good. Overall this is an excellent Spanish tapas plates with a twist and I will definitely comeback here again. (5 stars)

just … wow. our expectations were high after just having dined (and enjoyed!) next door at saint julivert recently. they were met and exceeded! we were in on a thursday, on the later end for la vara so even though we were only two we were able to take a booth. started with delicious cocktails and ordered the anchovies, chicories salad with persimmon, blue cheese and the most interesting coffee-infused vinaigrette, and had the tosta tomaca which was so good we ordered a second! there was a special cogote—roasted kanpachi fish head with sofrito butter that was so tasty we cleaned it to the bone, and the cochinillo with tximitxurri was so succulent and flavorful and the crispy skin just takes it over the top. dessert for us was basque cheesecake and a mini of the chocolate flan that we were gifted because we just couldn’t decide and there was a birthday involved…both had a bit of salt that did exactly what it was meant to and both were incredible. Sari, our server was delightful and Rob the GM was the perfect host! i’d love to visit with a bit of a group to be able to sample more of the menu in one sitting. either way, we’ll be back … so many other dishes to try. (5 stars)

La Vara serves outstanding Spanish cuisine with remarkable attention to detail. The morros prensados and cochinillo were perfectly fatty and tender with rich, complex flavors. Their arroz meloso and rossejat delivered buttery grains perfectly seasoned with complementary spices. Everything we tried was delicious but we left slightly hungry despite sharing more than 10 dishes among our group of five, which was disappointing (5 stars)

La Vara serves excellent Spanish tapas, cocktails, and wine in a quiet but lively atmosphere. The menu explores the Jewish and Moorish heritage of Spain with really tasty and creative small plates. Plan to order 3-4 per person, as they really are on the small side. We especially loved the butter served with the anchovies and toast, and appreciated that our server refilled the toast. Also outstanding were the Judios a la Plancha and Rossejat (like a seafood paella made with noodles instead of rice.) Service was friendly and attentive. (5 stars)

The menu is bold and improvisational, featuring contemporary and original dishes that highlight the aromas of saffron, cumin, and orange blossom. Guests can expect a unique blend of traditional and modern culinary artistry. Chefs Alex Raij and Eder Montero, a husband and wife team, are the driving force behind La Vara, which has been a beloved establishment for 11 years. The restaurant celebrates the Jewish and Moorish legacies in regional Spanish cuisine. ACEITUNAS - citrus & herb marinated olives - $6 GARBANZOS FRITOS - crispy spiced chickpeas - $5 PIMIENTOS - blistered peppers, sea salt - $9 CROQUETAS - del día - $10 HUEVOS RELLENOS - deviled eggs, green tahini - $7 ANCHOAS - cantabrian anchovies, dukkah butter, preserved citrus, charred sourdough - $19 Came here for the first time and was delighted by the good food. We were two persons and had over 8 to 10 dishes including dessert and a few drinks. The most outstanding dishes were the salchichon, arroz meloso and morros prensados, I was pretty impressed of their taste. We had a vermut and wine to drink with the dishes. Service was superb and the atmosphere great, even though the place was full. The desserts were also very good. Overall this is an excellent Spanish tapas plates with a twist and I will definitely comeback here again. (5 stars) just … wow. our expectations were high after just having dined (and enjoyed!) next door at saint julivert recently. they were met and exceeded! we were in on a thursday, on the later end for la vara so even though we were only two we were able to take a booth. started with delicious cocktails and ordered the anchovies, chicories salad with persimmon, blue cheese and the most interesting coffee-infused vinaigrette, and had the tosta tomaca which was so good we ordered a second! there was a special cogote—roasted kanpachi fish head with sofrito butter that was so tasty we cleaned it to the bone, and the cochinillo with tximitxurri was so succulent and flavorful and the crispy skin just takes it over the top. dessert for us was basque cheesecake and a mini of the chocolate flan that we were gifted because we just couldn’t decide and there was a birthday involved…both had a bit of salt that did exactly what it was meant to and both were incredible. Sari, our server was delightful and Rob the GM was the perfect host! i’d love to visit with a bit of a group to be able to sample more of the menu in one sitting. either way, we’ll be back … so many other dishes to try. (5 stars) La Vara serves outstanding Spanish cuisine with remarkable attention to detail. The morros prensados and cochinillo were perfectly fatty and tender with rich, complex flavors. Their arroz meloso and rossejat delivered buttery grains perfectly seasoned with complementary spices. Everything we tried was delicious but we left slightly hungry despite sharing more than 10 dishes among our group of five, which was disappointing (5 stars) La Vara serves excellent Spanish tapas, cocktails, and wine in a quiet but lively atmosphere. The menu explores the Jewish and Moorish heritage of Spain with really tasty and creative small plates. Plan to order 3-4 per person, as they really are on the small side. We especially loved the butter served with the anchovies and toast, and appreciated that our server refilled the toast. Also outstanding were the Judios a la Plancha and Rossejat (like a seafood paella made with noodles instead of rice.) Service was friendly and attentive. (5 stars)

bio_text: Lakruwana is a celebrated Sri Lankan gourmet restaurant located in Staten Island, New York, known for its authentic and vibrant culinary offerings. Established in 1995, the restaurant has evolved from a humble 20-seat venue to a spacious dining experience accommodating 85 guests, catering to both the local Sri Lankan community and adventurous diners seeking the rich flavors of Sri Lankan cuisine. Lakruwana specializes in authentic Sri Lankan cuisine, featuring a menu that highlights the use of indigenous spices known for their health benefits. The restaurant offers a diverse selection of dishes that reflect the island's rich culinary heritage, focusing on bold flavors and traditional cooking techniques. Lakruwana was founded on September 6, 1995, by Jayantha Wijesinghe, who serves as the owner and chef. The restaurant began with a small seating capacity and has grown significantly due to the increasing popularity of Sri Lankan food among both locals and tourists.
menu_items: Watalappan - $5.95
Mango Mousse - $4.95
Kiri-Pani - $5.95
review_snippets: This is such a beautiful place with amazing traditional Sri Lankan décor that makes the dining experience feel special. The atmosphere is warm and unique. I had the lumpice and kiri pani, and both were superb. The lumpice was very flavorful, not too spicy, and wrapped perfectly in a banana leaf. Everything tasted fresh and authentic. The kiri pani was creamy and lightly sweet, a perfect dessert. Highly recommend Lakruwana if you want authentic Sri Lankan food in NYC (5 stars)

When I first saw the exterior of this restaurant, I was absolutely intrigued. The ornate carvings, majestic statues, and shimmering golden doors beckoned me to come in. The place was crowded and everyone seemed to be enjoying their meal. Upon being seated in one of the elaborate chairs, I had to pause and take in the visual feast around me. The cozy interior was adorned with 360 degree of stunning ornate collectibles from Sri Lanka, exquisite tchotchkes adorning the walls and hanging from the ceilings, creating a continuous visual stimulus. The hostess greeted me and explained that I could either scan the menu code or enjoy the wonderful lunch buffet for $21. (Since I visited during the weekend lunch hour, I'm unsure if the price changes at other times.) Noticing that everyone else was enjoying the buffet, I decided to follow suit, and I'm so glad I did. I'm a huge fan of Sri Lankan cuisine, and the buffet was a delight. They have hot entrées in shallow cauldrons that are constantly being refilled. The spread consisted of many vegetarian delights alongside a few meat entrées, such as deviled chicken and pork curry. My personal favorites were the eggplant, dal lentils, and the kale and coconut salad. Their papadam was light and delicious, so definitely don't skip those! Along another wall, the dessert station featured sago, chocolate, caramel, mango, and gooseberry puddings. The latter two were my absolute favorites. (4 stars)
A pleasant Sri Lankan authentic spot on staten island. Nicely decorated with delicious food and pleasant service. I suggest to visit. Enjoy! (5 stars)

An amazing exotic atmosphere adds to your dining experience. Food is presented well and almost like eating art. Friendly staff. It would have been better if the waitress could have explained the dishes. As a 1st time , it was tasty and well presented. I’d like to try the buffet to be able to experience a variety of options. (4 stars)

bio_text: Laliko is a charming Georgian restaurant located in the heart of New York City, offering an authentic dining experience steeped in tradition and warmth. The restaurant's cozy atmosphere is complemented by beautiful wall murals and a welcoming staff, many of whom are authentically from Georgia. Guests can expect a delightful culinary journey through Georgia's rich flavors, with a menu that features both classic and modern interpretations of Georgian cuisine. Laliko specializes in traditional Georgian dishes, including khinkali (dumplings) and khachapuri (cheese bread), showcasing bold flavors and rich textures. The menu is designed to highlight centuries-old recipes while incorporating thoughtful modern touches, and the restaurant offers a well-curated selection of Georgian wines to enhance the dining experience. The restaurant opened about a year ago and has quickly gained recognition for its authentic cuisine and warm hospitality.
menu_items: GEORGIAN SALAD - Fresh cucumbers and tomatoes with vegetable and walnut paste, Kakhetian oil - $19
AJAPSANDALI - A mix of eggplant, bell peppers, tomatoes, spices, topped with a slice of cheese - $18
PKHALI - Traditional Georgian vegetable spreads with walnuts and herbs spinach / eggplant / beet - $12
EGGPLANT ROLLS - Roasted eggplant rolls filled with a silky walnut and garlic purée, pomegranate - $18
KHINKALI - Juicy, hand-folded dumplings, bursting with rich, flavorful broth and tradition beef and pork / beef / cheese - $18
FRESHLY BAKED BREAD - with garlic and rosemary - $4
review_snippets: Amazing food with great service. Nothing more to say. Everything was so good!! Highly recommend the Acharuli and Megruli. So tasty!! The Mother Khinkali was huge! The soup base and meat filling was so comforting. Also ordered the Shkmeruli which had the tastiest sauce. I dipped the bread from the Acharuli in it too. Georgian salad tasted incredibly fresh and refreshing. (5 stars)

Well worthy of its Michelin recognition! LALIKO is a beautifully curated Georgian restaurant. Between the beautiful wall murals showing points of cultural significance, to the Georgian staff, to the absolutely scrumptious food, this restaurant is steeped in tradition. The staff are very knowledgeable, and are more than happy to share the history of the food with you. The food itself is delicious, and I left eating much more than I expected, because everything was so delightful. Will be coming back here again soon, and bringing friends. (5 stars)

I recently visited Lalico for a brunch event and it exceeded all expectations. The restaurant has such a cozy and stylish ambiance — you instantly feel relaxed and at home. The Georgian cuisine was outstanding: rich flavors, beautiful presentation, and generous portions. Our group was especially impressed with the wine selection and the overall dining experience. The staff was incredibly professional and attentive, making sure everything ran smoothly and every guest felt comfortable. Come here just once, and you’ll instantly become one of their regular guests! (5 stars)

I was a guest at a brunch hosted at Lalico and I was absolutely impressed with this place. The restaurant has a warm, stylish atmosphere where you immediately feel comfortable and welcome. The cuisine was incredible — everything was delicious, beautifully presented, and full of authentic Georgian flavor. I was especially impressed by the large selection of wines and how perfectly they complemented the dishes. The service is truly top-tier: attentive, professional, and genuinely friendly. The team made sure every guest felt special and taken care of throughout the event. I wholeheartedly recommend Lalico to anyone looking for a place with amazing food, a great atmosphere, and excellent service. I will definitely be coming back again! (5 stars)

bio_text: Laser Wolf is an Israeli rooftop restaurant located atop The Hoxton in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, offering a unique dining experience with breathtaking views of the Manhattan skyline. The restaurant embodies the spirit of a 'shipudiya' or skewer house, serving award-winning Israeli cuisine that is deeply rooted in tradition and enhanced by modern culinary techniques. Guests can enjoy a vibrant atmosphere complemented by top-notch cocktails and a menu that celebrates the rich flavors of Israeli cooking. The culinary focus at Laser Wolf centers around the charcoal grill, an ancient cooking method that is fundamental to Israeli cuisine. The menu features a variety of grilled dishes, including signature items like za'atar-spiced half chicken and chicken liver pâté. The dining format emphasizes communal sharing, allowing guests to experience a diverse array of flavors. Laser Wolf is the first collaboration between Philadelphia’s CookNSolo and Chicago’s Boka Restaurant Group, bringing together renowned chefs Michael Solomonov and Andrew Henshaw. Executive Chef Andrew Henshaw previously served as Chef de Cuisine at Zahav, where he honed his expertise in Israeli cuisine.
menu_items: BEEF TARTARE - harif, eggplant, shipka peppers + homeade potato chips
TUNA CRUDO - grilled artichoke, lemon labneh + smoked trout roe
STEAK FRITES - charred kale chermoula, harif aioli, fries
French Fries - tehina ketchup - $15
Halloumi - apple, burnt honey + pistachio dukkah - $24
Grilled Baby Carrots - herb labneh, chili crisp - $22
review_snippets: Great quality food and beautiful views. Went in the winter so imagine views better as it gets warmer. Large area and good temp despite the email notice. Went with friends for Prefix - meat and small bites were all delicious as well as ice cream. Overall was soo good- great service, atmosphere, and food. Seasoning was delicious and recommend (5 stars)

I had a wonderful experience at Laser Wolf. Its been high on list of spots to try and it did not disappoint. While the food was exceptional and everything we ordered was delicious what really stood out to me was the amazing service. Our waitress, Savannah was fantastic, warm and attentive. She really set the tone for a great night. And I have to give a big shout-out to manager Matthew, who checked in on us and made sure we felt like truly valued guests. Can't wait to come back and try some new dishes! (5 stars)

Went during the summer without a reservation and managed to snag two seats at the bar with only a 10-minute wait. The views of Manhattan, especially at sunset, are absolutely stunning and set the tone immediately. Food – The French fries were flawless: thick-cut, shatteringly crisp on the outside, fluffy on the inside, and seasoned just right. Truly perfect. The mezze plate for two was good but felt like a rip-off. At $40 per person with an “unlimited” setup, you mostly end up filling up on bread. While the presentation was beautiful and a few of the dips were delicious, others were completely skippable. It also felt unreasonable that when a third friend arrived, they wouldn’t allow her to sit with us because of the per-person mezze charge. the soft serve for dessert was absolutely worth it, creamy and refreshing, and the perfect sweet bite on a warm summer night. (4 stars)

This place is amazing, The menu is inventive and yummy. We had price fixe, lamb and beef. The salatim is perfect - 11 small appetizers, original and tasty. The coal grilled meat is fantastic. Cocktails are good, and great beer options. We always eat a lot at this place, but it’s not heavy or tough. (5 stars)
