bio_text: Restaurant Le B. is a distinguished dining establishment located in the historic Greenwich Village neighborhood of New York City. Renowned for its Four Stars by Forbes and multiple accolades as one of the Best New Restaurants, Le B. offers a vibrant atmosphere that reflects the energy of modern downtown New York. The restaurant features a jewel-like dining room that enhances the experience of Chef/Proprietor Angie Mar's innovative cuisine, which is characterized by dramatic table side preparations and a commitment to exceptional hospitality. Le B. specializes in contemporary Continental cuisine, blending flavors from the East with classic Western techniques. The menu includes both à la carte options and a seasonal tasting menu, showcasing intricate flavors and forgotten culinary pleasures. Chef/Proprietor Angie Mar draws inspiration from her previous cult favorite restaurant, The Beatrice Inn, and has built upon a 100-year culinary history to create a dining experience that emphasizes excellence.
menu_items: A cook’s Snack: Bread & Butter - foie gras, guava confiture, perigord truffle
Tasmanian Sea Trout - dill, sansho, horseradish emulsion
Spring Vegetable “Pot-au-feu” - norwich farms winter vegetables, tempura of rapini blossom & enoki mushroom, cèpe consommé
Tagliatelle with Crab, caviar & Cucumber - smoked trout roe, royal osetra, poached oyster, beurre blanc
Halibut “en brioche” - halal pastures farm hakurei turnip & savoy cabbage “bonne femme”, sauce champagne
Pigeonneaux & plum - locust grove damson, celeriac, vin rouge
review_snippets: We took a client & his family to this beautiful jewel box of a restaurant in December - it was an amazing experience. Of course all the food was delicious and beautifully prepared - so many courses - each dish amazing. But I have to say- more than the food, I thought the service stood out. Even the process of making the reservation was a pleasure- Katrina was so professional and kind. The servers were all at the top of their game (not easy to be graceful while squeezing in between tables). And after dinner, the chef invited us to tour the kitchen and she chatted w/ our guests- these are the things that made the dinner stand out for us, this is the type of personal treatment that is hard to find in a NYC restaurant, even a pricey one. (5 stars)

The atmosphere was very nice and intimate. Refined but relaxed. The service was fantastic. The food was superb. The garlic soup was excellent and the pastry was flaky and buttery. Le Burger was the absolute epitome of umami. The blend of beef and french cheeses was out of this world! (5 stars)

The food was good, but the portions were pretty small. The burger was solid though I wouldn’t say it was worth the money. The appetizer was interesting, and both the lamb and salmon were so good. I especially loved how they split the dish into two servings. And the dessert was amazing, super rich and chocolatey. They also had $4 per person for dining fee if you don’t sit in a bar and it reminded me of dining in Paris lol (3 stars)

We celebrated our wedding anniversary here last night and everything was excellent. I should say, beyond excellent. Yes, it is a really pricey restaurant, even for NYC, even for a fine-dining spot. But every bite we ate was truly memorable (and this is coming from foodies who’ve dined all over the world), and service was attentive, polite and old-school. We were skeptical after reading some reviews but we were treated with utmost courtesy. They even went above and beyond for certain things. I was unhappy with our initial table and they changed it, with a smile. Even though we didn’t order dessert, the chef sent out something amazing in celebration of our special day, on the house. The sommelier guided us towards a most delicious bottle of red, and the burger was impeccable. We ordered a la carte and found the portions to be perfectly sized. I’m sure they are much smaller for the tasting menu, but why would you want big portions for a 6+ course meal? Bonus points for their lovely china. All around outstanding. Thanks, Le B! (5 stars)

review_snippets: Le bernadin has been on my bucket list restaurants ever since I could afford to go out to fine dining restaurants. Just the legend behind it and the amount of accolades it has achieved over the years. I finally went after all these years and came out of dinner thinking it was just okay. Nothing bad about any of it but also nothing very spectacular or mind blowing. The service was excellent. I sat at the bar as a walk in and got the full chef’s tasting menu. My server / bartended was very kind and knowledgeable with the menu. She made me probably the best espresso martini I’ve had in my life. The meal itself was fine. As I said previously nothing was bad. I felt like everything was one note. Maybe my favorite dish was the Peruvian chocolate tart. Was I happy that I went? Yes extremely happy. Would I go back? Maybe just for the espresso martini. (4 stars)

Absolute perfection. The food was skillfully prepared. The complex and unbelievably delicious flavors. The staff clearly loves thier career choice every member of this team was not only ready to serve, but they truly enjoyed every minute of making the experience a first class culinary adventure. If you have the opportunity to request Matthew, he was knowledgeable and a pleasure. (5 stars)

Such an amazing Christmas Day dinner!! We have been planning for ages to come here when we are visiting New York and it was amazing! We had the 4 course meal and the selection was insane, I think we took a good 20mins trying to decide what to eat but Angel our waiter was ready to give recommendations which helped ALOT. When the food arrived it was delicious, so light but at the same time decedent and so full of flavour. Barbara helped me and my sister out with some dessert wine and the rest of our drinks which was lovely and she was so friendly with us, made us feel right at home. To finish we had some desserts and they bought out a little birthday tart for me and my mum which was such a lovely touch!! Oscar helped us out with the end of our meal and the bill and again he was friendly and asked us about England which was fun to discuss. Overall an amazing lovely meal with amazing staff helping us every step of the way We will definitely return if we ever get back to America again ❤️ Thank you Le Bernardin ❣️🎉😊 (5 stars)

Every plate, and bite, a beautiful work of art. It was remarkable. And I cannot stop thinking about the creamy lobster and how authentic the sherbet tasted—the grapefruit was impeccable and the pear captured the grainy texture perfectly. The atmosphere was elegant, modern and tres chic and the staff attentive and engaged. My thanks to the generous team for surprising me with the most decadent and delicate birthday treat. (5 stars)

bio_text: Le Coucou is a sophisticated dining establishment that brings the essence of fine French cuisine to New York City, crafted by internationally acclaimed chef Daniel Rose. The restaurant features a beautifully designed space by Roman and Williams, characterized by crisp linens, flickering candles, and whitewashed brick, creating an inviting atmosphere that pays homage to European gastronomy. With a focus on updating classical French dishes, Le Coucou offers a vibrant dining experience that bridges the culinary traditions of Paris and New York. Le Coucou specializes in modern French cuisine, emphasizing seasonal ingredients and classical techniques. The menu is designed to reflect the charm and verve of traditional French dining while incorporating contemporary elements. Signature dishes showcase the richness of French culinary heritage, presented with a modern twist. Chef Daniel Rose, originally from Chicago, has a rich culinary background that began in France, where he studied at the Institut Bocuse and opened his first restaurant, Spring, in 2006. Le Coucou marks his first restaurant in the United States, in collaboration with restaurateur Stephen Starr.
menu_items: Poireaux vinaigrette - leeks, hazelnuts - $20
Thon à l’espelette* - yellowfin tuna, espelette oil - $28
Caille frite au sarrasin - buckwheat fried quail, maître d’hôtel butter, lemon jam - $22
Tartare de bœuf* - hand chopped prime filet, traditional condiments, caviar - $98
Homard et rémoulade de céleri - chilled lobster, celery root salad, horseradish - $46
Aubergine voyageuse - glazed eggplant, sauce tonnato - $26
review_snippets: Le Coucou has been on my list for what feels like forever, and I’m so happy we finally made it in to experience it. From the moment we sat down, it was clear why this spot has the reputation it does. The menu, while reading as incredibly exotic and uniquely curated, reveals so many thoughtful intricacies once the dishes actually arrive. Each plate feels like a quiet little masterpiece! Bold in flavor and elegant in technique! We decided to lean into our server’s recommendations, and happy we did! Every single dish was truly mouthwatering in its own way. We started with the eggplant, then came the sliced tuna, perfectly seasoned and impossibly fresh, with a silky texture that practically melted the moment it touched your tongue. The fish dish with the buttery mousse was to die for, one of those plates you already start craving again halfway through eating it. Beyond the food, the entire experience felt intentional and intimate, from the knowledgeable service to the way each dish was delivered with just enough context to make you appreciate the craftsmanship behind it Safe to say Le Coucou fully lived up to the hype fand then some!!) (5 stars)

Came here for my partners birthday celebration and it was a hit ! First off, you’re greeted with lovely staff where you check in and they do have coat check. You wait patiently with some nice seating beside their beautiful entrance bar. We took our seats in the inner dining area and loved the open kitchen concept. You can see the chefs/team preparing your food as well as hear them too. We decided to split everything we ordered and they did such an awesome job serving us with our own dishes for each ordered enter (hence why the portion looks smaller). One of my favorite parts was the servers left the sauce pan on the side for us especially with the Ris de veau à l'estragon. That sauce was my favorite and would have scrapped it with the bread if given another chance. Lastly, if I were to order a dish over again… it would have to be the Ris de veau à l'estragon or the Canette à l'orange. I believe that my partner enjoyed the side pan they left for us. Please see photos and videos for more context on our orders ! (5 stars)

The fish was phenomenal. Definitely get the steak with bone marrow too. The duck was very good. We shared everything between two so the photos we took are half portions of the original dish. (5 stars)

Service was magnifique! Tasting menu is delicious, we came for lunch and got some cocktails too. We hope to come back and try the dinner menu. A beautifully decorated restaurant, not stuffy and felt really cozy inside! (5 stars)

bio_text: Le Jardinier New York is an award-winning French restaurant located in the heart of Midtown Manhattan, designed to be a serene oasis that connects guests to nature through its culinary offerings. The restaurant embodies refined elegance and celebrates seasonality, presenting dishes that highlight the rich offerings of the land with every plate served. Le Jardinier focuses on seasonal French cuisine, offering both À La Carte and curated seasonal menus. The culinary experience is led by Michelin-starred Chef Alain Verzeroli, emphasizing the use of fresh, local ingredients and classic French techniques. Created by Michelin-starred Chef Alain Verzeroli and the global hospitality group The Bastion Collection.

review_snippets: Pros • The dishes were very tasty and beautifully presented, with clear attention to detail in both flavor and plating. • Service was relatively efficient and fast throughout the meal, which made the experience smooth and enjoyable. • The restaurant has a quiet atmosphere, and the music volume is kept at a very acceptable level, making it easy to have a conversation. • The bread selection was very nice, although the butter could have been better. Cons • The amuse-bouche was a bit disappointing compared with the rest of the meal. • Staff did not offer coffee or tea at the end, which felt like a missed touch in the overall dining experience. Overall Le Jardinier offers a refined and pleasant dining experience in a calm setting, with well-executed dishes and efficient service. While there were a couple of small misses, especially the underwhelming amuse-bouche and lack of attention at the end of the meal, the overall experience was still positive. (4 stars)

Great service Le Jardinier is definitely a must try! Nice and quiet atmosphere. Great service. Food is delicious and fresh! One of my favorite things was the bread basket, their bread is something very special! High level of baked goods!! The small bread with the spinach flour was unbelievable. Can’t wait to come back !! (5 stars)

Such perfection. Decor nicely to see Lex but not from outside. Uniform leafy insignia for butter, menu. Outdated tablet likely better without. Taking advantage of restaurant week. Leek impressive. Sashimi bit sourish. So was foam refresher. Portion nice for tendered beef with mashed potato. Both dessert nice crisps combo. Overall elegant. Nano fandom. (5 stars)

Out of all restaurants week tried and tested , Le Jardinier is one of the best. It has the charming attentive but not over the top service, food is consistent (yummy and small portion 🙃🙂) with one star rated Michelin level. Desserts need a little polishing (egg foam was well eggie, tart base was rock hard) Decor is great inside though, great vibe for romantic or family or party get togethers. Bonus point for partnering with InKind. (5 stars)

bio_text: Le Pavillon, located in the iconic One Vanderbilt skyscraper, offers a refined yet inviting dining experience that celebrates seasonal French cuisine. With a design that incorporates lush gardens and olive trees, the restaurant evokes a sense of natural splendor, making it a unique setting for both intimate gatherings and larger celebrations. The atmosphere is relaxed yet elegant, reflecting Chef Daniel Boulud's culinary roots and his commitment to fine dining in New York City. Le Pavillon focuses on seafood and vegetable-forward cuisine, rooted in French tradition while embracing contemporary techniques. The menu is innovative and seasonal, highlighting the richness of Northeast fishermen and farmers. Signature techniques include a close attention to seasonality and a celebration of local ingredients. Chef Daniel Boulud, a native of Lyon, France, has been a leading culinary authority in New York since 1982. His culinary journey has led to numerous accolades and the evolution of his cuisine across various locations, while remaining grounded in the rhythm of the seasons.
menu_items: TASTING OF VEGETABLES - six courses - $165
CANAPÉ | AVOCAT & PANISSE - grilled avocado, einkorn berries, yogurt green goddess
AGNOLOTTI | POIS - english pea, mint, spring onion
ASPERGES BLANCHES | CANTAL - provençal white asparagus, sicilian pistachio, frisée mustard, pomme aligot
CAROTTE | FALAFEL - charred carrot, falafel, fava leaves, magnolia blossom chimichurri
RACINE DE CÉLERI | RAISIN - roasted celery root farci, couscous, sesame seed, candy snap grape, sauce véronique
review_snippets: I was in NYC for a girl's trip a few weekends ago and we went to Le Pavillon for dinner before our Broadway show. The meal was unforgettable! The food was delicious, beautifully presented, and perfectly portioned. We had the 3 course fixed menu. The staff was attentive, friendly, funny and engaging. The atmosphere was relaxed and warm. It wasn't too loud and had a beautiful view of the Chrysler building. Would definitely recommend and return to as well. (5 stars)

Visited on Valentine’s Day and ordered the holiday set menu. The space feels comfortable and airy, with high ceilings that make the dining room feel open and relaxed. Real indoor plants are placed throughout the seating area, adding a pleasant touch of greenery while also softening the noise and creating a calm atmosphere. The set menu is thoughtfully designed. Each of the four courses offers three options, allowing both diners to choose different dishes and try a wider range of flavors. Overall, the food was satisfying across the board. The only drawback was the lobster pasta, which was a bit too firmer than I prefer. However, the scallops, as another option, were delicious, with both the texture and flavor being truly enjoyable. Portion sizes follow the typical date-night approach. Nothing feels overly heavy, but the meal remains filling enough to feel complete. It makes for a nice spot for a date, and the row of hanging lights above the bar adds a polished, romantic touch to the space. (5 stars)

The Pavilion Restaurant is a wonderful choice for a romantic dinner or to celebrate a special occasion. The setting is beautiful, with a quiet and intimate ambiance that makes it easy to enjoy meaningful conversations without feeling rushed or distracted. It’s the kind of place where you can truly relax and be present with the people you’re dining with. The menu offers a great selection of food and wine, with options that feel thoughtfully curated and perfect for a special night out. Each dish is well-prepared and flavorful, and the wine list complements the menu nicely. The service was good overall—attentive and professional—though there was a bit of a wait between courses. That said, it didn’t take away from the overall experience. All things considered, I’d rate Pavilion Restaurant an 8.5/10. A lovely spot for date nights, anniversaries, or any celebration worth savoring. (4 stars)

Excellent meal for my friend's birthday. The service was attentive while remaining at a distance. In addition the vibe was fancy without pretension. Ok but let's talk about the food. The best thing I ate was probably the onion tart. The tart was an excellent start to a meal, an appetizer with a soup's depth. The onions are really well made, firm yet easily chewable, with a good tart base. The cheese foam added salt and funk to the onion well. The steak was well made but the real fun for that dish was the short rib croquette and the caramelized onion. Those were really flavorful and strong. Going after the onion tart worked too; I recommend choosing the same flavor twice for courses 1 and 2. The fig dessert was pretty and good. The cream provided a good contrast to the fig, with the mille feuille adding texture to those two. The wine selection is expectedly good, as is the cocktails. But I don't recommend the egg white drink, the flavor is muted. Overall a great experience, fine dining but with a price point that is not the craziest. I want to be at the bar next to try their bar menu. (5 stars)

That said, it didn’t take away from the overall experience. All things considered, I’d rate Pavilion Restaurant an 8.5/10. A lovely spot for date nights, anniversaries, or any celebration worth savoring. (4 stars) Excellent meal for my friend's birthday. The service was attentive while remaining at a distance. In addition the vibe was fancy without pretension. Ok but let's talk about the food. The best thing I ate was probably the onion tart. The tart was an excellent start to a meal, an appetizer with a soup's depth. The onions are really well made, firm yet easily chewable, with a good tart base. The cheese foam added salt and funk to the onion well. The steak was well made but the real fun for that dish was the short rib croquette and the caramelized onion. Those were really flavorful and strong. Going after the onion tart worked too; I recommend choosing the same flavor twice for courses 1 and 2. The fig dessert was pretty and good. The cream provided a good contrast to the fig, with the mille feuille adding texture to those two. The wine selection is expectedly good, as is the cocktails. But I don't recommend the egg white drink, the flavor is muted. Overall a great experience, fine dining but with a price point that is not the craziest. I want to be at the bar next to try their bar menu. (5 stars)

bio_text: Le Rock is a vibrant dining destination located in the heart of Rockefeller Center, offering a modern interpretation of a classic French brasserie. The restaurant is housed in a beautifully restored Art Deco space, providing a warm and inviting atmosphere that reflects both its historic roots and contemporary flair. With its prime location adjacent to iconic New York landmarks, Le Rock promises an exceptional dining experience that combines culinary excellence with a lively ambiance. Le Rock specializes in French cuisine, showcasing a menu that emphasizes high-quality ingredients and traditional techniques. The restaurant offers a diverse selection of dishes that highlight the essence of French culinary artistry, making it a perfect spot for both casual dining and special occasions. Le Rock is the creation of James Beard Award-winning chefs Lee Hanson and Riad Nasr, who are known for their work at some of Manhattan's best restaurants, including Frenchette and Le Veau d'Or.
menu_items: Bread & Butter - $7
1/2 dz Oysters w/ Chipolatas - $28
Chilled Shrimp Cocktail - $27
Tuna Tartare - $25
Avocado Pâté de Campagne - $26
Chickpea Panisse Frites - Chili Aioli - $19
review_snippets: Last Saturday we went for dinner at LeRock. Our experience was wonderful. The food, the atmosphere, the staff… From the first to the last minute, everything felt special, and every person in my party had an awesome time. (5 stars)

We had Christmas Eve dinner here and it was a wonderful experience! There was a partial view of the tree from our seat but it was still very special. The dining room isn’t super large and feels cozy and festive. It wasnt too noisy either. Service was great, very professional. There was a moment when they cleared crumbs off the table and accidentally brushed some onto my dads lap😅 The food was wonderful! The flavors were delicious and filled us up. I read other reviews that the portions were small but I wouldn’t agree. Only the lobster was “small” as the serving was only half a lobster. I had the Dover sole and got very full. The starter burrata pasta was so delicious I almost wished it was my main! (4 stars)

Exceptional dining experience I had for my birthday. We particularly enjoyed the snails, steak, and the traditional French dessert, as well as the table with a view of the Rockefeller Center Christmas tree. Our waiter’s suggestion regarding the excellent fries was also correct. He is also very helpful with recommending the menu items and super friendly to the children. A wonderful evening, we look forward to dining again. (5 stars)

A perfect restaurant in a prime touristy location if you want to see Xmas tree or a skating ring. Elevated enough buy not pretentious and decently priced for the area. The cheeseburger is a bit underwhelming with not much flavors but the quality of meat was very good. My friend's tuna tartar was ok, on a smaller side. The bread basket use to be much better, now it is just 5 pieces of a baguette. (4 stars)

bio_text: Le Veau d'Or, located in the heart of New York City, is a celebrated dining destination that combines a rich history with a modern culinary approach. Established in 1937, the restaurant has been revitalized by renowned chefs Riad Nasr and Lee Hanson, who bring their expertise from Frenchette and Le Rock to create an elevated dining experience that pays homage to the nearly century-old legacy of the space. Le Veau d'Or focuses on neo-bistro cuisine, offering a menu that reflects both classic and contemporary French influences. The dining experience is characterized by meticulous execution and a thoughtfully curated beverage program. Established in 1937, Le Veau d’Or reopened under neo-bistro extraordinaires, Chefs Riad Nasr and Lee Hanson of Frenchette and Le Rock.
menu_items: Pommes Souflées - $135
Caviar Rouge a la Crème - $135
Assiette Bouchon - $135
Pâté en Croûte - $135
Salade de Betteraves - $135
Petite Omelette - $135
review_snippets: Finally checked out the new Le Veau D'Or for lunch and it far exceeded my expectations. Staff is wonderful, helpful, welcoming, super friendly. I ordered the mackerel, the lobster salad (sublime) and the Il Flottante (the best I've ever had). Also had two gin gimlets and big shoutout for the bread service (really scrumptious). The mackerel was the only thing that, for me, was underwhelming. I was also extremely happy to see that they have redone the restaurant in a very gentle way that still pays homage to the past. Very warm and cozy ambiance. (5 stars)

I’ve been torn about writing this review but 2 stars it is. We heard about this place through Kaitlyn Lavery, a NYC food reviewer who rated this her #1 spot of 2025. We came here for an anniversary dinner with high hopes and unfortunately left disappointed. Ambience is great. Small, intimate space that feels like an NYC institution (like 4 Charles or Carbone). Service was excellent and saved the review. Staff are all extremely friendly and good at their jobs. Really enjoyed our cocktails though on the pricey end (even for NYC) at $26 a pop. The food was the disappointment. $135 tasting menu and they were out of the duck. Their most popular dish. Kaitlyn’s favorite dish of 2025. The entire reason we came here. I think it’s just unacceptable to run out of your most popular dish for a $500 meal. The rest of the food was fine - nothing blew me away (and this might just be because it’s French food) but we enjoyed each dish and liked the chicken and steak. Sadly I think this was a “one and done” spot and the fact that they didn’t have the one dish that we wanted to try kind of ruined the experience. I wouldn’t come back here to take a shot at being able to have the duck when there’s so many other great returants you can eat at for less than $500 and actually get what you want (a meal for 2 at Torrisi is less than this and is arguably the best in the city). Came with high hopes but left disappointed. (2 stars)

I think there are some pros and cons about this place! We really enjoyed the service and a few of the dishes. In particular the duck was amazing, and the fries were perfect. Beet and boudin appetizers were good. I really enjoyed the chartreuse ice cream on the chocolate dessert, though the crepes suzettes were too sweet with the tropical addition. However it’s overpriced in our opinion. $135 for 3 courses (plus one green salad) is a lot when it would be $80-90 at an equivalent à la carte restaurant. The set menu is required for dining at tables. It’s basically like a main dish costs $90 if dessert and app cost $45. Plus, I thought it was frustrating that there was no wine by the glass menu. Just a verbal list from the waiter with 3-4 options. (No list means no prices unless asked) It ended up being $440 for 2 people with 3 drinks included. I can certainly see why people like it here, it just wasn’t the right value to us knowing other options in NYC. (4 stars)

Much hyped French bistro was good but nothing outstanding. Stopped in for $85 two course fixed price lunch. Mackerel was a good starter. The steak frites was ok but nothing outstanding better than the plethora of other French bistros in NYC. Service was prompt and friendly. The space is beautiful though with an old world charm about it and probably the only thing you’re going to remember. Plus at this price point value rating is pretty low too. Place is still very buzzy, completely full at 2p on a Thursday. Verdict: will not return but recommend once for the vibe. (3 stars)

bio_text: Legend of Taste is a welcoming dining establishment located in Whitestone, NY, offering a cozy atmosphere for guests to enjoy a variety of delicious dishes. The restaurant emphasizes convenience with options for online ordering, making it easy for patrons to savor their favorite meals. The restaurant focuses on a diverse menu that highlights a range of flavors and culinary techniques. It aims to provide a satisfying dining experience with both dine-in and takeout options.
menu_items: Spicy Seafood Stir Fry - Seafood, vegetables, spices - $24
Crispy Chicken with Peppers - Chicken, bell peppers, spices - $22
Chili Fish - Fish, chili peppers, spices - $26
Spicy Cabbage Stir Fry - Cabbage, chili peppers, spices - $18
Vegetable Medley - Mixed vegetables, spices - $20
Braised Beef - Beef, spices, herbs - $28
review_snippets: I love spicy food. Szechuan cuisine specializes in that, going for a mouth numbing spiciness. So I had to come here. The atmosphere is nice. They were playing country music, which I thought was funny. And the service is great. I got the lunch special, triple pepper chicken (as you see in the photo) with pork fried rice and wonton soup. The soup is perfect for a cold, winter day, and was absolutely delicious. The chicken, meanwhile, was nice and spicy (though I was expecting much spicier for 3 hot pepper emojis). Though, when I asked, they told me it was more "mild" — I gotta ask for spicier next time! But please get something milder if you can't handle spice — my spice tolerance is VERY high. Excellent food, excellent service, funny random country music. Five stars. (5 stars)

We’ve visited this restaurant well over a dozen times across the years, dining in regularly. It has also received Michelin recognition, which was part of what initially drew us in. Based on our most recent visit, while the food was not bad, it felt noticeably different from what we remembered from earlier visits. The flavors were more restrained, and the dishes lacked the boldness and depth that previously stood out. I wouldn’t say the food is poor — it’s still solid — but based on our past experiences, the dishes felt more moderate and less distinctive than before. Given its reputation and history, there is room for improvement, particularly in terms of flavor intensity. (3 stars)

A consistent and authentic Sichuan style in a local area. The lunch specials are tasty and their chef specials are also great. I recommend the braised fish filet in chili oil as well as the fried fish filet in with ginger peanuts. Great for takeout and always fast delivery! (5 stars)

I’ve ordered from Legends of Taste a few times and thought it was decent at first, but my last order of orange chicken was absolutely disgusting. The pieces were mostly fried crust with barely any chicken inside, and what little meat there was was dry, rubbery, and chewy like jerky. It was inedible ! The sauce tasted bitter and off, almost medicinal, and the broccoli was dull and lifeless, clearly cooked hours before. This meal made it clear they don’t care about quality. It felt like leftovers reheated and thrown together at the end of the night. After this experience, I’ll never go back — they lost me as a customer for good. It was so bad I threw the entire meal straight into the trash. (1 stars)

bio_text: Nestled in the historic Doyers Street of Manhattan's Chinatown, Lei is an intimate 28-seat wine bar that offers a unique blend of classic and emerging wines. The ambiance is warm and inviting, making it an ideal spot for both casual diners and wine enthusiasts looking to explore a thoughtfully curated selection of wines paired with dishes inspired by regional Chinese home cooking. Lei focuses on regional Chinese home cooking, offering a menu designed to complement its diverse wine selection. The dishes are crafted to enhance the wine experience, with a constantly changing menu that reflects seasonal ingredients.
menu_items: Pickled pearl onion, radish, and celery - $14
Chilled celtuce with kombu jelly, shallots and red vinegar - $15
Crudo of Montauk scallop with lily buds, ginger, and lime - $20
Chinese omelette with aged white jade radish and scallion oil - $13
Lady Edison Jin Hua ham with seasonal fruit - $22
Sesame shao bing - $9
review_snippets: Came here for my birthday, this was one of the loveliest meals I've had in a while. I recommend having a reservation, they say they take walk ins but its a small space so that really only seems to work if you show up around the time they open. The sommelier was very helpful in choosing wines and we enjoyed them with all of the food we ordered. We had the celtuce, scallop crudo, shaobing with lardo, short rib, cats ear noodles and sticky toffee eight treasures pudding. The cat ear noodles were probably our favorite, the dish reminded us of the lamb cumin noodles we used to eat in china (5 stars)

Laughably difficult to get a table here but the host was kind enough to make a res for us a week later instead of fully turning us away after waiting on the waitlist for 3 hours on a Friday night. Service is great, my water was never empty. Very very small inside but so cute and well decorated. Same team behind king and stissing house in upstate (some of my favorite spots). In love with the broth that’s with the mushroom and cabbage rolls and the egg yolk squash incredible. Massive list of wines. Played some cantomando pop remixes which was nostalgic. Insanely expensive but that’s New York wine bars these days (5 stars)

I was lucky enough to snag a seat at the bar right as they opened at 5pm on a Saturday. Within 10 minutes, the whole restaurant was jam-packed. Staff is very friendly and welcoming and the vibe is great. I ordered the chilled celtuce, the scallop crudo, the ham and pear, and the shao bing along with a glass of cotes du rhone. The highlight was the ham (really good). The other dishes that I ordered after reading rave reviews about were not remarkable for me but that may be on me. I am not especially savvy in terms of this cuisine. (4 stars)

Such a hospitable team!! We walked in without a reservation and were told they had a spot for us but had a reservation coming in 30 mins. They immediately made us feel welcome and even made us feel comfortable and confident we could order a few plates of food in that time. We ordered three plates that all came out quickly with enough time for us to enjoy. Every plate was uniquely Lei, perfectly balanced and seasoned. It was a quick visit but I’m already looking forward to my return (5 stars)

bio_text: Lingo is a Japanese-American restaurant located in Brooklyn, NY, that offers a unique dining experience blending traditional Japanese flavors with American culinary techniques. The restaurant features a warm and inviting atmosphere, perfect for families and friends to gather and enjoy a diverse menu that caters to all ages. With a focus on community and connection, Lingo aims to create memorable dining adventures for every guest. Lingo specializes in Japanese-American cuisine, offering a menu that includes small plates, izakaya-style dishes, and brunch options. Signature techniques include the use of fresh, high-quality ingredients and a blend of traditional Japanese cooking methods with contemporary American influences. At Lingo, the chef emphasizes the importance of sharing good food with families, aiming to introduce children to the joys of dining and cultural experiences.
menu_items: JAPANESE POTATO SALAD - cucumber, carrot, preserved tuna - $11.00
SPRING ONION - grilled, karashi mayo, shio kombu, katsuobushi - $8.00
TOSAKA-NORI SEAWEED - tri colored seaweed, sesame dressing - $7.00
CHILLED SUGAR SNAP PEA - edamame yuzu sauce, red radish - $7.00
WARM HOMEMADE TOFU - hokkaido crab, sea beans, tosazu (add uni $8) - $10.00
Hokkaido Milk Bread - fresh baked daily, hijiki parm butter - $7.00
review_snippets: We came here for brunch as a group of 3 and the food did not disappoint! Portions were extremely generous - sharing a single apple pancake, chicken sando, and beef pie was more than enough. Service was also attentive, but they were strangely rushing us throughout our entire meal. We stayed here for about 1 hour, which is within their time limit, but our table was cleared after 45 minutes, and the whole experience just felt extremely uncomfortable towards the end. Maybe this just happened to be an especially busy day, but this does not excuse rushing customers when their food is clearly not finished. (4 stars)

This place is delightful. The food is really delicious and well executed. We ordered several dishes to share including the beef pie which I thought was good. Standouts for me were the potato mille-feuille (the sauce was one of the highlights of the night) and the Hokkaido somen (the dish I wish I didn't have to share). We split two desserts - the panna cotta and banana sundae. That sundae was mind-blowingly good. There was no reason that it should be that good, but it was unanimously our favorite. Service was outstanding and the restaurant was understated and lovely. (5 stars)

This was a fun place to meet friends for dinner. I like the atmosphere and energy and appreciated the kindness and generosity of the staff. The food was presented very nicely and looked like it had been cooked with care. Unfortunately, with the exception of the pot pie, the other dishes were under seasoned. (4 stars)

Cute little restaurant in Greenpoint! A group of us 3 were here on a Wed night and shared everything: - Hokkadio milk bread - Fuyu burrata - Bone marrow tartare - Miso black cod - Snow crab udon - Duck - Lingo beef pie - Squash and sage rice Everything was plated beautifully and tasted great. The beef pie could definitely use a side of rice since it's pretty rich and savory. Service was great and super attentive throughout the night. This is definitely on the pricier side though, given the portion sizes. We each got one drink (1 being a yuzu soda), and total after tax & tip came out to $320ish. I'd definitely come back to check out their brunch menu. (4 stars)

With a focus on community and connection, Lingo aims to create memorable dining adventures for every guest. Lingo specializes in Japanese-American cuisine, offering a menu that includes small plates, izakaya-style dishes, and brunch options. Signature techniques include the use of fresh, high-quality ingredients and a blend of traditional Japanese cooking methods with contemporary American influences. At Lingo, the chef emphasizes the importance of sharing good food with families, aiming to introduce children to the joys of dining and cultural experiences. Portions were extremely generous - sharing a single apple pancake, chicken sando, and beef pie was more than enough. Service was also attentive, but they were strangely rushing us throughout our entire meal. We stayed here for about 1 hour, which is within their time limit, but our table was cleared after 45 minutes, and the whole experience just felt extremely uncomfortable towards the end. Maybe this just happened to be an especially busy day, but this does not excuse rushing customers when their food is clearly not finished. (4 stars) This place is delightful. The food is really delicious and well executed. We ordered several dishes to share including the beef pie which I thought was good. Standouts for me were the potato mille-feuille (the sauce was one of the highlights of the night) and the Hokkaido somen (the dish I wish I didn't have to share). We split two desserts - the panna cotta and banana sundae. That sundae was mind-blowingly good. There was no reason that it should be that good, but it was unanimously our favorite. Service was outstanding and the restaurant was understated and lovely. (5 stars) This was a fun place to meet friends for dinner. I like the atmosphere and energy and appreciated the kindness and generosity of the staff. The food was presented very nicely and looked like it had been cooked with care. Unfortunately, with the exception of the pot pie, the other dishes were under seasoned. (4 stars) Cute little restaurant in Greenpoint! A group of us 3 were here on a Wed night and shared everything: - Hokkadio milk bread - Fuyu burrata - Bone marrow tartare - Miso black cod - Snow crab udon - Duck - Lingo beef pie - Squash and sage rice Everything was plated beautifully and tasted great. The beef pie could definitely use a side of rice since it's pretty rich and savory. Service was great and super attentive throughout the night. This is definitely on the pricier side though, given the portion sizes. We each got one drink (1 being a yuzu soda), and total after tax & tip came out to $320ish. I'd definitely come back to check out their brunch menu. (4 stars)

bio_text: Little Alley is a charming Chinese restaurant located in the heart of Manhattan, dedicated to recreating the authentic flavors of Shanghainese cuisine. With a nostalgic ambiance reminiscent of Shanghai's narrow alleyways, known as 'long tang', the restaurant offers a comforting dining experience that evokes memories of home. The interior design and carefully curated menu aim to provide a sense of familiarity and warmth for both Shanghainese locals and those eager to explore the rich culinary traditions of Shanghai. Little Alley specializes in traditional Shanghainese cuisine, featuring a menu that highlights essential dishes recognizable to those familiar with the region. The culinary focus is on recreating the flavors and techniques that Chef Cheung grew up with, ensuring an authentic dining experience. Chef Yuchun Cheung, born and raised in Shanghai, leads the kitchen at Little Alley, drawing on his extensive experience from renowned establishments such as Quanjude Restaurant and China Blue. The restaurant is inspired by Chef Cheung's childhood memories and the culinary traditions of his family.

review_snippets: Came here for dinner a few weeks ago and thought it was pretty good overall. We unintentionally got to the restaurant still within dim sum happy hour pricing so got a variety of little things like soup dumplings, scallion pancakes. Overall, solid choices. For main dishes, I really loved the prawns and would definitely recommend. The menu is fairly extensive and we tried a few things but I feel like there's much more! While nothing stood out as truly stellar, it was all fairly good and reasonably priced. (3 stars)

We didn’t make reservations at Little Alley, just showed up around 7:30, but with just a short wait we were able to grab a table. The hostess and our various waiters (they all seem to assist all diners) were all very friendly and welcoming. We love to try new things so we had to check out the Little Alley Pig Ear appetizer, and I also wanted to try the Shanghai Crispy Eel. For entrees the husband ordered the Eight Delicacies in Chili Sauce and I got the Soft Shell Crab with Rice Cake. Pro tip- their appetizers and entrees are hefty, with two apps and two entrees we were stuffed at the end. The food! The pigs ears were our favorite thing we tried- they well seasoned and so unique I’ve never had anything quite like it. We didn’t read the menu carefully and were surprised it was a cold dish- I imagined the crispy was from being fried but it’s just the texture of the cartilage! It’s probably not for everyone but I really enjoyed the new experience and the flavor and spice were great. The crispy eels were also tasty, though with such a large portion split between just two people I found the sweetness of the sauce a bit much. I started dipping them in the chili oil from the ears and enjoyed that, but I’d still only get the eel again with more than 2 people to split it. For entrees the 8 delicacies was tasty, all the meat was nicely cooked and tender, and the sauce was pleasant. I wasn't super wowed by this dish compared to some of the more interesting things we tried but it was a solid well-cooked entree. The fried soft shell crab over the rice cakes was delicious and again a very unique experience. I found the sauce a tad sweet but I think I was still a little over the eel dish so I may have been extra sensitive. That being said, it was fun and delicious and I’d eat it again! I can’t remember the cocktails we bought, I know they were good but the food definitely distracted us! Little Alley was great overall and I’d love to go back to try some dumplings; sadly we were just too full at the end of the meal! (5 stars)

Overall great experience with all the dishes tasting pretty good; a few of my favorites were the whole steamed fish (great flavors from the soy sauce and ginger on top), salted egg fish fillet, the oxtail soup, all the dumplings. They also serve Sichuan dishes like Mapo tofu but given its a Shanghainese restaurant theres zero spice level to those dishes (still taste good though). Enjoyed dining in the old Shanghai vibes and ambiance (5 stars)

It's a nice place with premium priced dishes, OK quality food. The smoked carp has a strong earthy taste (土腥味）and overcooked; it doesn't deserves a premium price. The Xiao Long Bao (pork soup dumplings) are not my type since their wraps are too thick. A surprise is that the restaurant offers a curry fried rice where it's difficult to find among other Chinese restaurants. (4 stars)

bio_text: Little Myanmar is a vibrant Burmese restaurant located in the heart of New York City, offering an authentic taste of Myanmar's rich culinary heritage. The restaurant provides a warm and inviting atmosphere, perfect for both casual dining and special occasions, where guests can enjoy a unique blend of flavors and traditional dishes. Little Myanmar specializes in Burmese cuisine, featuring a diverse menu that highlights the country's unique flavors and ingredients. The restaurant focuses on traditional recipes and cooking techniques, ensuring an authentic dining experience.
menu_items: Tea Leaf Salad with Corn - Corn tea leaf salad - $19.00
review_snippets: Recently discovered this spot which I thought was a gem and shared with others . However, after returning for the second time I decided to try their noodles and chicken and quickly found out it was a terrible mistake. The food was so oily , noodles extremely overcooked , chicken tasted nothing like chicken and completely tasteless! After a day of fasting I was so hungry I think even food with not that much flavor would be appreciated but I took two bites and couldn’t have more. I think what was most disappointing was the way the staff responded to my reaction of not having properly cooked food. There was no apology or any moderation offered whatsoever. My excitement for finding this spot was short lived and unfortunate since supporting small businesses is essential. (1 stars)

August 31st, 2025 This was perhaps our seventh or eighth visit, and sadly, it was the first time we left disheartened. From the outset, there was a shift in atmosphere—most notably a new and rather puzzling policy that barred us from using the restroom, something we had always relied upon in past visits. The food, which has always been this establishment’s saving grace, fared no better. The goat curry—once the crown jewel of the menu—arrived drowning in oil, its once-balanced richness reduced to a greasy broth with tough cuts of meat. It took three requests before a proper serving of curry emerged, and even then, the anticipation of savoring a longtime favorite turned into disappointment. The chicken thali, another staple, was equally uninspiring: the chicken unexpectedly sweet and unyielding, the accompaniments stripped of the depth and nuance that once defined them. The service too fell short. We found ourselves repeating requests multiple times before being understood—an avoidable lapse that reflects not only inattentiveness but also a lack of basic common sense in guest service. For a restaurant once marked by warmth and efficiency, this decline was as noticeable as the dip in food quality. Not all was lost. The Yangon tea and fish cake skewers still carried a touch of the charm that first won us over. They remain bright spots amid an otherwise lackluster spread. We sincerely hope this decline is the result of a transitional phase or a new chef still finding footing. This restaurant has been a place we’ve cherished, and we would like nothing more than to see it flourish again. But flourish it will only if the kitchen and service return to form—because the food, after all, is its only true USP. (1 stars)
One of my favorite noodle dishes in New York. The room is a bit small so better to book a reservation. (5 stars)

How can a restaurant not have a restroom open to customers?! The waiter told me to go to Marshall’s to use the restroom, which is like 5 mins walk away and I had to get down 2 floors below - so inconvenient and customer-unfriendly! This place is also cash only as well. The food was good but in small portions that we still felt hungry after finishing each of our entrees plus an appetizer. We also highly doubt that the rice was frozen before or not fresh and was reheated in microwave because it came in lumps and didn’t taste freshly cooked that day. Almost no service at all. The waiter and waitress were mostly behind the curtain and has not come to us and ask us anything about the food, the water was also self-served through a big bottle. Not a good experience, wouldn’t come again. The no bathroom aspect was the most unacceptable part! (3 stars)

bio_text: The Lobster Club is a glamorously laidback Japanese restaurant located in Midtown Manhattan, designed by renowned architect Peter Marino. This modern dining establishment revives the vibrant spirit of its predecessor, The Brasserie, offering a unique atmosphere that blends sophistication with a relaxed vibe. The menu features deeply satisfying interpretations of Japanese classics, encouraging a communal dining experience with beautifully crafted dishes and an extensive selection of cocktails, sakes, and wines. The Lobster Club specializes in modern Japanese cuisine, offering a wide-ranging menu that includes gyoza, yakitori, and katsu-style wagyu sandos. Each dish is designed for sharing and is complemented by an extravagant array of sauces, with sushi prepared from fish flown in daily from Tokyo’s Toyosu market. Founded by Jeff Zalaznick, Chef Mario Carbone, and Chef Rich Torrisi, Major Food Group has been delivering celebrated culinary experiences for over a decade.

review_snippets: Food was good I wanted to try more yet didn’t have time would try again when I return to NYC. Price was stiff for the meals the drinks was fair had a soba old fashion Japanese whiskey definitely worth the taste. (4 stars)

We came to The Lobster Club on a Saturday evening for a celebratory dinner. The restaurant wasn’t too busy, but we were first seated in a high-traffic area and had to ask to be moved. It seemed like booths were reserved, which felt a bit limiting for a special occasion. The food was very good overall. We enjoyed the Wagyu Shiitake Fried Rice, Crispy Rice, Garlic Chicken, Branzino, and the Wagyu Truffle Sando. The Truffle Sando was absolutely delicious, though pricey at $66 for four small bites. For cocktails, the Cucumber Shiso was refreshing and memorable, while the Yuzu Paloma was watery and underwhelming. Service was fine, but there was no complimentary dessert, which many NYC restaurants offer and would have made the evening feel more special. Overall: great flavors, but celebratory touches didn’t quite match the price point. (4 stars)

I’ve only ever been here to take clients out (I’ve never dined here on my own dime), but every time I’ve been it’s been amazing. The food, service, and atmosphere are all special. One of my favorite meals I’ve ever had in the city was here at Lobster Club (5 stars)

I recently had the pleasure of dining at an exceptional Japanese restaurant, and it was an unforgettable experience! We kicked off the evening at the bar with a refreshing Lychee Martini, which set the tone for the night. Once our entire party arrived, we moved to a lovely table and ordered a variety of dishes. Every single item we tried was absolutely delightful—I loved them all! Our sommelier was fantastic and recommended the perfect bottle of sake that paired beautifully with our meal. I can't wait to return to this gem of a restaurant! Highly recommend it to anyone looking for an amazing Japanese dining experience! (5 stars)

review_snippets: An intimate and charming spot for British cuisine. We started with the scotch eggs, which were outstanding - deeply spiced and easily the highlight of the starters. The sausage roll was solid with a rich center and crisp edges, while the squash salad fell short with a slightly bitter finish. The rabbit pie was a standout: incredibly flaky and fragrant with tender, well-seasoned meat and a perfectly crisp crust. Overall, a cozy spot for British fare with some satisfying dishes. (5 stars)

always a bit skeptical of the “only X burgers served per night” but that feeling evaporated after the first bite of the welsh rarebit burger. still thinking about that rarebit sauce — prime blend patty & bed of onions is such a treat. tangy, powerful, yet balanced. and those chips are some proper thick boys and a wonderful companion burger was stellar + service was amazing. incredibly lovely evening and an experience I look forward to revisiting in the near future (5 stars)

Kind of mid? Service was great, very attentive and chill which i enjoyed. Gave us a good pace. Oysters were delicious but $5 a pop is a little absurd and should come as 3 a piece because they are that good. The pig head was delicious and was not expecting the outerlayer to have a cripsy chicken cutlet vibe, it was tasty. The mushrooms were an absolute miss, did someone accidentally spill too much of the sauce on them or does it come like that? It honestly doesn’t even need the sauce at all. The burger was the most anticipated but let us down the most. Don’t get me wrong it’s a good burger, but not worth it at all. Quite lacked. The seasoning such as SALT. Idk how you underseason a burger it’s very simple. The fries were honestly the worst part because they do not even taste good. Just boiled potato thrown into a fryer. No seasoning such as SALT. The sticky toffee ice cream was also meh, came melty and not what i expected. Also a $17 moscow mule is a crime and it did not even taste that good lol. Very cozy, but would not go back (3 stars)

I wish there was little more mash with the pie (or an option to make it larger) , I thought the oysters were a little hard to eat - piping hot while the oyster meat didn’t come off so easily. bio_text: Loring Place is a vibrant American restaurant located in the heart of Greenwich Village, New York City, offering a warm and inviting atmosphere that celebrates local ingredients and the spirit of New York. Under the guidance of Chef Dan Kluger, the restaurant provides a unique dining experience with both indoor and outdoor seating, allowing guests to enjoy market-driven dishes in a convivial setting. The design reflects a blend of urban-rustic aesthetics, featuring natural materials and a minimalist approach that enhances the overall dining experience. Loring Place focuses on seasonal, local American cuisine, featuring a menu of small and large shareable plates. The culinary techniques include cooking over an open fire using a wood-burning grill and wood-fired oven, which impart unique flavors to the dishes. Chef Dan Kluger, known for his work at ABC Kitchen and ABC Cocina, opened Loring Place in December 2016 as the culmination of a lifelong dream. The restaurant is named after the street where Kluger’s father grew up, and it reflects his deep connection to New York's culinary landscape.
menu_items: brown butter COFFEE CAKE - with grapes and oat crumble - $9
cinnamon morning bun - maple pecans and orange cream cheese glaze - $16
Hummus - with housemade pita - $16
BUTTERNUT 'FRIES' - lemon-parmesan dressing - $18
BAKED RICOTTA - kabocha squash, chilies, mint and grilled sourdough - $22
roasted BEETS salad - ginger, orange, toasted cashews and crispy sunchokes - $22
review_snippets: I went to this almost 10-year-old New American restaurant a while back with a few others, having passed by it numerous times as I used to go to Rasa, a Malaysian place just up the block. The inside was chic with the lighting slightly dark for photos, and the staff were friendly. I believe I had a glass of wine or perhaps a spritz, but I'm unsure. My appetizer was the Wood Grilled Broccoli Salad for $23, with orange, pistachios, and mint. The broccoli had a light char, a mildly smoky flavor, and a very mild sauce underneath. The bit of orange added citrus, and I liked the crunch from the pistachios. However, I think this would work a little better if the broccoli were cut into smaller pieces rather than one large stalk, as the textures would blend a bit better. Still, I liked it overall. If I recall correctly, another person had the Shaved Brussels Sprouts, and another had the Baked Ricotta, and both enjoyed their appetizers. That night, I decided not to have any meat or fish, unlike usual, and went with the Gemelli, a type of pasta. For $25, this was served with tomatoes, herbs, and lemon crumbs, which was a bit pricey for a plain pasta, but hey, it's the Village. Apparently, this pasta has been made with crab and chili before, which sounds a bit more substantial, but I'm presuming there would be a price difference if that were the case. The pasta was a bit past al dente for my liking, and it had a surprising amount of kick. It almost reminded me of an arrabbiata, though with tomato instead of the usual tomato sauce. Otherwise, the lemon crumbs added a unique and fun crunch, and overall, it was decent, but it felt a bit one-note, as the spice overpowered whatever other flavors there were. Another person had the same dish as me and wasn't a big fan due to its heat level. One of the other people had the $35 Skate "Fish & Chips," which came with three pretty big pieces of fish and a bunch of crunchy French fries, which were shared with a few others at the table. Another had one of their signature whole-wheat pizzas, the Grandma-Style, for $20, with tomatoes, mozzarella, and basil, which seemed like a decent portion for the price, and I would probably get that or a fancier pizza next time. This was a good neighborhood spot, and I can see why it's been around for as long as it as as the food is unique enough while remaining approachable. I wish I could give this place a 3.5, but since that rating doesn't exist, I'll bump it up a bit, as it is closer to a 4 than a 3. I wouldn't go out of my way for this place, but I would stop in again. (4 stars)

I live in London and was in NY for a couple of days with my husband. I’ve never had an experience like the one we had at Loring Place. All the staff seemed so joyful and they served us so kindly - they were prompt to give us recommendations and I mus say that we were very happy to take them. The food was definitely full of flavour - the kind that you only eat at a great restaurant. We had the squash fries for an entrance and I must say that if that was the only thing I had there, I would be already delighted. The main courses were spotless and the desert was to die for. Very sadly I forgot to ask the name of the person who served us. I hope if you read this and you remember us (a young couple seated at the window table last Tuesday) you’ll be able to know that your service made our evening even better. I don’t have plans to come to NY again soon, however, when I do, I know that I will be coming to Loring Place. (5 stars)

Wow, what a treat. Loring Place is the perfect balance between modernism, comfort, progressiveness, and homely, all at the same time. This seemingly impossible yet perfect balance can only be felt, starting from the interior and the decor, to the server interaction, all the way down to the focused yet sophisticated menu. Loring Place oozes of modern-day charm. Not snooty. But classy. Not awkward. But familiar. The food is an Californian / American cuisine where you have a mixture of great appetizer concoctions, fabulous salads, creative pizzas, and a solid variety of main course. There is no theme other than probably what came to the chef's mind. The Fall Seasonal menu had a generous mix of butternut squash and chili infused into many of its dishes. Again, no dish was simply mainstream but also not overly complicated. And each one of them definitely had a perspective. The chef doesn't just play it safe, but rather chooses to test you if you dare. And you are handsomely rewarded for it. The list of ingredients may raise your eyebrows but soon all is understood as you spread the flavors in your mouth. Pretty much everything was phenomenal. The ricotta cheese with butternut squash was wonderful and paired amazingly with the sour dough bread. The salad was rock solid and this slice of chili really added a welcome twist. The Date pizza was such a joy while the short ribs was soft and succulent. All the dishes were absolutely made with care, just like the decor, just like the service. Loring Place is a joyful place. It's not boring, yet it wants to be subdued for all the right reasons. This is a place where you can come over and over again, knowing you'll have a good time, but not worry about the superficiality of trying to be fancy. Everything is right here. Go enjoy. (5 stars)

This is an above average spot but nothing worth rushing to. Burger was medium well even though we ordered medium, and the grandmas pizza was decent. The crudo/ceviche was probably the best thing on the menu. Seemed like they only had one person serving for lunch. (4 stars)

bio_text: Lungi is a vibrant restaurant located in the Upper East Side of New York City, dedicated to showcasing the rich culinary traditions of South India and Sri Lanka. Under the ownership of Mervyn Winston and the culinary expertise of Chef Albin Vincent, Lungi offers a warm and inviting atmosphere that reflects the cultural heritage of its dishes. The restaurant aims to provide an authentic dining experience that celebrates the flavors and warmth of home-cooked meals and street food from these regions. Lungi specializes in South Indian and Sri Lankan cuisine, featuring a menu that highlights traditional dishes and innovative fusion techniques. The restaurant offers a variety of dining experiences, including unique Dosa preparations and other classic South Asian offerings, crafted with a focus on bold flavors and authenticity. Chef Albin Vincent, who hails from Kanyakumari, India, was inspired by his grandmother's cooking, which ignited his passion for traditional Sri Lankan and Southern Indian cuisine. The restaurant also features the expertise of Chef Andrew Simethy from Kerala and Chef Rushdhun Ramzy, known for his innovative approach to classic Sri Lankan flavors.
menu_items: Banana Leaf Special Meal - Comes with appetizer, veg - nonveg karis, rice, biryani, pickle, poriyal, papadum, and dessert. - $49.99
Thakkali Melagu Rasam - Plum tomato, freshly ground black pepper, and coriander with madras chilies and tamarind. - $9.00
Cauliflower 65 - Cauliflower fritters tossed in oriental sauce. - $17.00
Mutton Roll - Spiced ground lamb, potatoes, filled in a pastry sheet and deep fried. - $19.00
Deafman Shop Tawa Fish Fry - King fish fry recipe from our village shop. - $20.00
Sura Puttu - Steamed shredded baby shark fish with shallots, veggies and spices made into a stir-fry. - $20.00
review_snippets: Lungi in NYC is one of those spots you leave already planning your next visit. The cocktails are excellent, layered with traditional South Indian and Sri Lankan flavors that feel intentional and well balanced. They complement the food beautifully instead of competing with it. And the food really shines. The beef chukka was bold and deeply spiced. The Malabar parotta came out flaky and perfect for tearing and scooping. The fish cutlet had that crisp shell and soft, flavorful center. The goat biryani was fragrant and rich without feeling heavy. The black short rib kari was slow cooked, tender, and packed with depth. We ended with the mango guava gelato for dessert and it was the perfect finish. Bright, fruity, and refreshing after all those spices. Service was efficient and cordial throughout. Highly recommend Lungi if you’re craving soulful South Indian and Sri Lankan flavors done right. (5 stars)

Ambiance (5/5): The interior decorations feel modern, sleek, and elevated. It is a wonderful place for an upscale meal. Two areas for dining, divided by a wall which both makes the room feel smaller but the whole restaurant feel bigger. Comfortable dining chairs and booth seating. Service (5/5): Staff is dressed very professionally and treated us with respect/courtesy. Whenever asked for help, they were quick to service. Kerala Beef Chukka (4/5): Not as much of a fan as I thought I would be. The small bites were flavorful but dry. Kori Ghassi (5/5): Mangalorean chicken curry was packed with flavor. The chunks of chicken were juicy and went well with the rice. Lamb Biryani (5/5): Comes with a hard boiled egg on top. It was very flavorful Roti (5/5): I loved the accompaniment of the roti (I would have preferred if it had a bit more of a crunch slash more fried) Hopper (3/5): I was not a fan of the dish but mostly because I’ve never had it before and it doesn’t have enough substance to go with the meal (like naan would). Separately, the dips were tasty. Before dining in, I had a good experience with their takeout (cant remember what I ordered but I remember both dishes were uniquely flavorful!) (5 stars)

Lungi is one of the few really good spots in Manhattan for this style of cuisine. The vibe is welcoming, and the spacious seating makes it a great choice for both small groups and larger gatherings. We started with a few appetizers: Cauliflower 65, Kanyakumari Nethali Varuval, and Kerala Beef Chukka. The Cauliflower 65 was fresh, crispy, and packed with flavor. The Nethali Varuval was tasty, though it felt slightly over-marinated for our preference. The Kerala Beef Chukka was the clear standout — an absolute must-try with bold, authentic flavors. For the mains, we had the Ambur Biryani and String Hopper Kothu. The biryani was decent but could have been more flavorful, while the kothu was above average and enjoyable. Overall, Lungi is a solid spot in NYC for authentic South Indian flavors, great ambiance, and a satisfying dining experience. (5 stars)

Food was 6 out of 5! It was so good. Ambur mutton Biriyani was authentic and tasted great! Poricha Kozhi and Kothu were amazing. I usually eat less spicy, spice level matches exactly what you get in India, a little more than what I could handle but the taste was so good that I didn’t mind it and kept digging for more. Staff were very polite and service was good. Overall a great experience. Best authentic South Indian food in NYC! (5 stars)

With a focus on creating memorable dining experiences, the restaurant combines traditional dishes with a modern twist, making it a perfect spot for both casual meals and special occasions. The culinary focus is on authentic Vietnamese cuisine, featuring a diverse menu that highlights fresh ingredients and bold flavors. The restaurant emphasizes a casual dining format, allowing guests to enjoy a variety of dishes in a relaxed setting.

review_snippets: I stopped by for dinner here and it was an amazing experience, from the drinks to the wings, ofc the pho and the unexpected incredible coffee flan. Everything came together perfectly. The pho was incredibly fragrant and felt nourishing, the wings had an amazing sauce on it, and the Bahn mi went perfect with the pho as a dip as well. The flan coffee dessert was so good that I ordered another one to go. I’m not a big fan of flan but this one might have opened me up to a new world. (5 stars)

Everything was sooo good! For apps, the salt and pepper squid was super crispy and flavorful. Hawker rice was delicious too. Lemongrass chicken was distinctly lemongrass flavored. Loved every bit of dinner. Such a giant piece of short rib with the UES pho. Definitely a neighborhood must go! (5 stars)

Lyly Vietnamese is a fantastic spot for pho lovers. The pho is excellent — rich, aromatic broth, tender meat, and perfectly cooked noodles that feel comforting and authentic. Every bite shows real care and quality. It’s no surprise that Lyly Vietnamese is mentioned in the Michelin Guide, as the food truly stands out. A must-visit for anyone craving great Vietnamese cuisine. (5 stars)

Really flavorful dishes depending on what you order. Cooked to perfection. The inside has a nice casual atmosphere as if you’re eating at an eatery in Saigon. Prices are usual New York fare with appetizers averaging $10-15 and entrees around $23. Also love their Thai iced tea because it’s not too sweet. Make sure to reserve in advance! (5 stars)

The restaurant emphasizes a casual dining format, allowing guests to enjoy a variety of dishes in a relaxed setting. VIETNAMESE FRUIT COCKTAIL - coconut milk, pandan & coconut jelly, jack fruit, longan, pomegranate - $7 BÁNH FLAN - Vietnamese black coffee caramel, condensed milk drizzle, crushed ice - $7 SALT & PEPPER SQUID - gently breaded and fried, jalapeño, cherry tomato, crispy garlic, onion - $12 BEEF WRAPPED IN BETEL LEAF - prime beef, scallion, peanuts, fried shallots, rice vermicelli, served with nước chấm - $16 VIETNAMESE CREPE - pork belly, shrimp, bean sprout, shallot, scallion, served with nước chấm - $15 SAIGON CHICKEN WINGS - 4 pieces, caramelized with nước mắm, tamarind & garlic - $11 I stopped by for dinner here and it was an amazing experience, from the drinks to the wings, ofc the pho and the unexpected incredible coffee flan. Everything came together perfectly. The pho was incredibly fragrant and felt nourishing, the wings had an amazing sauce on it, and the Bahn mi went perfect with the pho as a dip as well. The flan coffee dessert was so good that I ordered another one to go. I’m not a big fan of flan but this one might have opened me up to a new world. (5 stars) Everything was sooo good! For apps, the salt and pepper squid was super crispy and flavorful. Hawker rice was delicious too. Lemongrass chicken was distinctly lemongrass flavored. Loved every bit of dinner. Such a giant piece of short rib with the UES pho. Definitely a neighborhood must go! (5 stars) Lyly Vietnamese is a fantastic spot for pho lovers. The pho is excellent — rich, aromatic broth, tender meat, and perfectly cooked noodles that feel comforting and authentic. Every bite shows real care and quality. It’s no surprise that Lyly Vietnamese is mentioned in the Michelin Guide, as the food truly stands out. A must-visit for anyone craving great Vietnamese cuisine. (5 stars) Really flavorful dishes depending on what you order. Cooked to perfection. The inside has a nice casual atmosphere as if you’re eating at an eatery in Saigon. Prices are usual New York fare with appetizers averaging $10-15 and entrees around $23. Also love their Thai iced tea because it’s not too sweet. Make sure to reserve in advance! (5 stars)

CROQUETAS - black truffle | manchego | sunchoke - $15
MARKET SALAD - aged pecorino | hazelnuts | white balsamic - $21

review_snippets: I came to have my birthday brunch on Saturday the 21st & wanted to sit at the bar. They had a seat waiting for me and the bartender, Lindsay, greeted me with a warm birthday welcome and a glass of Prosecco. :) To start, the drink with the rum and lemongrass was strong but also perfectly balanced. Really enjoyed that. She made me a gin cocktail, which I also loved and the prosecco was good! Since I was by myself, I ordered the croquettes, the shrimp & their famous french toast. The shrimp?! ORDER 2 ORDERS OF IT, insanely flavorful and an underrated dish on their menu. I wanted to lick the place. I would have loved bread with it to dip in the leftover sauce ;) Their french toast is now made with milkbread and what a smart choice!! DIVINE! Order that. They even put a candle in it for me - again, a small gesture that meant a lot. Shout out to Lindsay who took great care of me. She was attentive but not in your face. And she makes a fantastic cocktail! Thanks, Lindsay ;) & the manager, I forget her name, she was also very lovely and kind. I'd like to come back and try their dinner!!! (5 stars)

I’ve been wanting to come to MADRE for quite a some time so I finally snagged a reservation a few weeks before. First off, the vibe inside is so cool - I love how they used the lights to give an intimate yet fun vibe. The service was great and the food was good, just good however. The lamb chops were the best dish of the nights for us but tasted like good quality chops, nothing special. The flavors were okay but I wish they did more with the dishes. The drinks were strong which is a plus, you just need one for the evening. Not sure if I’d come back or recommend someone to come out of their way for a meal. Still a great place but the food was just okay. (4 stars)

We sampled nearly every item on the menu and loved it all, from the creative cocktails to the delicious appetizers, entrées, and desserts. We even ordered two of the chocolate soufflés to finish the night. It was a fun evening of great food and company in a trendy Greenpoint, Brooklyn restaurant. (5 stars)

First & foremost, both the bartender HK & the waitress Francesca were absolutely lovely- personable & attentive without being overbearing. On top of the amazing service, the ambiance of the place is great and the food is top notch as well. I only tried the miso brussel sprouts & truffle croquettes but both were great. I also had the Formula One drink which was unique and tasty as well. Last but certainly not least, I had the soufflé which is 110% well worth the wait. I will definitely be back again, hopefully for their brunch! (5 stars)

bio_text: Maison Passerelle offers a fine dining experience that seamlessly blends classic French cuisine with modern techniques, set against a backdrop of stunning architectural design. Located in the heart of New York City's Financial District, the restaurant features an ambiance enriched by soaring frescoes and luminous stained glass, creating a transportive dining atmosphere that connects the elegance of fine dining with a vibrant downtown edge. Under the direction of Chef Gregory Gourdet, Maison Passerelle focuses on modern French cuisine inspired by the French diaspora. The menu showcases a variety of distinctive dining experiences, emphasizing vibrant flavors and refined techniques, with a commitment to using sustainable ingredients. Chef Gregory Gourdet, an award-winning chef and restaurateur, leads the culinary vision at Maison Passerelle. He is classically trained and has a rich background in the culinary arts, having worked with renowned chefs and opened several acclaimed restaurants.
menu_items: Salt Cod Fritters - lemon, fermented chili remoulade
Citrus Cured Kampachi - smoked coconut milk, persimmon, ginger, pickled jicama
Smoked Beet Salad - nuoc cham, star fruit, cashew, coconut cream crumbles
Fall Fruit Salad - pear, fig, grape, squash juice, coconut dressing
Sweet Potato & Peanut Soup - caramelized plantain, pickled apple, chili-maple
Daily Oysters - pikliz, mignonette
review_snippets: I am such a huge fan of this place! My boyfriend found this restaurant online, and once we saw that most of the menu was gluten free and dairy free, I got so excited! I was even more excited that the head chef and creator was Black. We made a reservation for the same night. We really enjoyed our meal. Walking in, the restaurant was elegant, and I loved the open kitchen. The 2 seater tables were a bit tight, similar to most restaurants, but the seats were comfortable. Our server was nice and the other staff were great. It was also great to see so many Black chefs, and I loved the RnB and soul music. We ordered off the restaurant week menu as well as the regular menu. Looking at the both menus, it’s evident that a talented chef created these dishes. My boyfriend is Haitian, so we appreciated seeing some Haitian staples being converted to fine dining. Our favorites were the lobster pasta, which had plenty of lobster, but we wanted more noodles and more of the entire dish. The gumbo was interesting, but really good. The Sòs Pwa Nwa with the Pickled red onions was next level. The light coconut cake with the sorbet was fantastic. The only disappointment was the cornbread. I was so excited to try to gluten-free bread. It seems like some nights they have mini muffins and some nights they have the bigger loaf. We were only given 1 mini muffin for two people, so I asked for more and was charged $12. I was annoyed since the mini loaf is clearly much bigger than the mini muffin. Even if it was only 1 mini muffin per person who ordered off the regular menu, we spent so much money, it feels like it’s ridiculous to charge for an extra mini muffin on a $350 bill. That made me a bit upset. Otherwise, I’m a huge fan and highly recommend. Thank you for offering delicious Haitian food that’s gf/df. We will be back. (4 stars)

Ate here for a birthday lunch. I was not disappointed. I loved the hand cut tile mosaic floor and the open kitchen. The staff were attentive and enthusiastic. Excellent cocktails. Every dish was a wonderful melange of flavor combining French, Asian and African influences. Even the French fries were notable. .My wife described them as like a good baguette...crusty on the outside and fluffy on the inside. My favorite was the the Duck Confit Curry. (5 stars)

The most marvelous dining experience in Manhattan—I find myself returning over and over again. Every dish showcases a blend of exciting flavors, drawing from Caribbean and southeast Asian cuisine. The food is as visually stunning and luxurious as the beautifully designed interior. The prix fixe format may seem pricey initially—but is very reasonable when considering the portions are more substantial and the cooking technique more refined than many modern restaurants that have opened in the last years. (5 stars)

This is the cool new restaurant inside the beautiful Printemps building downtown. The restaurant is eclectic with bright colored tiles and stand out chandeliers, a great spot for striking conversations over a small dinner. We visited for restaurant week - and apparently got some new testers on the menu. Food is inspired by French colonial cuisines - lots of Thai, south east asian, New Orleans, etc. The dishes were tasty. Some flavours were a bit boring compared to other places in NY but overall pretty good. Service still working out some kinks. (4 stars)
