bio_text: Mango Bay is a vibrant culinary destination located in the heart of Fort Greene, Brooklyn, offering a unique cultural experience that transports guests away from the urban hustle. With a focus on feel-good vibes and exceptional company, the restaurant's ambiance is enhanced by vibrant decor inspired by Afro-Caribbean heritage, creating an inviting atmosphere for diners to enjoy extraordinary flavors. Mango Bay specializes in Afro-Caribbean cuisine, featuring a menu that includes dinner, brunch, and specialty drinks. Signature dishes such as Jerk Chicken, Oxtail, and Goat Curry Puff Pastry highlight the chef's expertise and commitment to using fresh, local ingredients. Chef Chase's culinary expertise and unique flair are central to the restaurant's offerings.
menu_items: Ackee And Saltfish Eggroll
Braised Oxtail
Goat Puff Pastry
Mango Bae London Chase
review_snippets: Everyday on my way to work, I would glance at the restaurant on my left named Mango Bay. It is located inside a beautiful Brownstone building. I checked the menu and decided one day I'm going to visit. Well, on 2/6/26 my work family celebrated my 65th birthday/retirement from The Brooklyn Hospital Center. The atmosphere is sheer ambience. As I sat there relaxing with my work family enjoying the smooth music, the waitress took our drink orders. We all had the Mock Drinks, the favorite was The Mango Baby. I had the ice tea with pineapple juice. The menu had been pre-selected. Everyone had a chance to enjoy every dish that was selected. We started with the salad and short ribs, then the oxtail and two different types of rice, then the fish (becareful of the bones), then the leg of lamb with whipped sweet potatoes. Everything was delicious, everything was delicious, and again everything was delicious. Since my birthday was being celebrated I expected the "surprise" slice of cake, but nothing came. I figured, oh well, but to my surprise a whole cake was presented to me and only my work family sang happy birthday. Don't worry, this is a swank establishment, no birthday song and clapping hands by the staff. That is totally up to your peeps😄. I wish I had gotten everyone's name but from the Greeter, Waitress, Busser, Bartender and Chef the service was very good. I highly recommend Mango Bay. We had a great meal, and a wonderful experience. (5 stars)

Mango Bay is a charming Caribbean-themed restaurant that truly stands out. The ambiance is delightful, with a cozy and upscale vibe that feels like a warm, inviting home. The venue features both a downstairs area and an upstairs section, which is beautifully decorated with a bookshelf and a "Do the Right Thing" sign, adding a unique touch. The service was impeccable; our waiter was attentive and made sure we had everything we needed. As for the food and drinks, it was nothing short of exceptional My favorite drink was the Brooklyn love .The ackee and saltfish egg rolls were a standout, and the whole fish was cooked to perfection. I also enjoyed a ras pasta dish that was absolutely delicious. We visited for a friend's celebration, and the experience was memorable for all four of us. The pricing was reasonable, making it great value for money. I thoroughly enjoyed my time at Mango Bay and will definitely return in the future. (5 stars)

As an afro-latino, New Yorker, and foodie, I had very high expectations for Mango Bay. There are tons of spots in Brooklyn that often sacrifice ambiance for what we actually go to the restaurants for, the food, and this place surpassed my expectations. Starting off with the decor and ambiance, this felt like dining in an authentic NY townhouse, with art that represented the Black diaspora and the culinary experience one was going to embark on. The spiral staircase, the large windows, and the open space filled the room with some much energy and visual interest. By far one of the most well designed restaurants I've been to in some time. For the food, this is where they really shined. Every app hit harder than the last, our favourite was between the pork ribs and the special, baked oysters. Think oysters Rockefeller but on STEROIDS. The flavor was as if the Caribbean and high society had a baby. And as for the pork ribs, tendernism was an understatement and the pomegranate glaze made me want to walk into the kitchen and bribe the chef for the recipe. The entrees were delicious as well, I will certainly have the braised oxtail again the next time we go, as well as the Ras and Pasta. The lamb shank was delicious but a bit too game-y for me. Lastly, as for the service they were very attentive despite what seemed like an understaffed evening. We went 2 days before Valentines Day, what I would assume is one of the busiest days of the year, and we had to wait a bit for our waiter to get back to us a few times for orders. Someone from the staff did come check on us periodically so I can tell they take great care of their guests even at their busiest! Overall, this was a great experience and Mango Bay has quickly shot to the top of my favourite spots to eat in my city. (5 stars)

Everyone in both dining rooms were dressed to impress including the very good at their jobs servers. Perfect place to bring your family and friends or enjoy date night. Watch Chef Maguette and her team rise to fame in real time, cause it’s only up from here. Well done Chef, congratulations!! (5 stars)

bio_text: Manhatta is a modern New American restaurant located sixty floors above the bustling streets of New York City, offering breathtaking views and an atmosphere that embodies the vibrant spirit of the city. The restaurant features an ever-evolving menu that highlights the versatility of local ingredients, providing guests with a dining experience that is both familiar and inventive, whether they choose to dine in the elegant dining room or the lively bar. Manhatta focuses on New American cuisine, offering a multi-course dinner and a la carte lunch options. The menu is crafted with traditional techniques and global influences, complemented by an award-winning wine list and a thoughtfully curated prix-fixe food menu. Manhatta is a restaurant from Danny Meyer's Union Square Hospitality Group.

Caramelized Nuts - Espelette Pepper, Smoked Paprika - $12
Hand-Cut Chips - Idaho Potatoes | Onion Dip - $12
Steakhouse Fries - Au Poivre - $19
House Pickle Plate - Selection of Pickled Vegetables - $18
Market Crudité - Seasonal Vegetables and Fruits, Lime and Fresno Salt - $15
review_snippets: We had an absolutely incredible experience at Manhatta for my friend’s birthday! From the moment we walked in, the entire staff made her feel so special—everyone went out of their way to congratulate her. We were lucky enough to get a stunning window seat with a breathtaking view of the city. There was even a thoughtful birthday card waiting for us on the table! The food was of the highest quality and the service was flawless. They truly know how to make an occasion feel grand. Highly recommend! (5 stars)

We had dinner at Manhatta, located on the 60th floor of a skyscraper in the Wall Street district, and the experience was impressive overall. From the moment you arrive, the welcome is highly professional. The hostess team, maître d’, and sommelier all contribute to a very polished and well-organized atmosphere. The service is attentive, refined, and genuinely professional throughout the evening. The view is truly spectacular. One side overlooks the Brooklyn Bridge and Brooklyn, while the main façade faces Uptown Manhattan, showcasing the iconic, glittering skyline in all its glory. At the entrance, there is a stylish and functional bar area with a stunning backdrop view. Walking to the right, the restaurant opens into an L-shaped dining room with approximately 30 tables. The staff-to-guest ratio is excellent, and service flows smoothly. They offer a 3- or 4-course prix fixe menu. Each course (starter, main, dessert) includes about five options, which keeps the selection focused and prevents the menu from feeling overwhelming. The concept feels standardized, elegant, and based on quality ingredients rather than excessive variety. My wife and I both chose the four-course menu. I started with the raw shrimp, which was excellent — easily the highlight of my meal. I then had scallops, followed by a vegan main course that, unfortunately, felt underdeveloped and barely cooked — surprisingly so, to the point that it felt almost unfinished. I ended with a chocolate mousse. I paired my meal with a mezcal-based spicy cocktail, which was well balanced and enjoyable. My wife chose burrata as a starter, a lentil-based dish, tagliatelle, sea bass as her main course, and sorbet for dessert. She paired her meal with a Blanc de Blancs champagne, which complemented her dishes beautifully. Overall, the food was good but somewhat mediocre in execution, with a few highlights (especially the raw shrimp). I would rate the food 4 out of 5. However, the atmosphere, views, and the professionalism and friendliness of the staff easily deserve 5 out of 5. A unique and charming touch: the restaurant provides binoculars placed around the space for guests to enjoy the skyline up close — a thoughtful and memorable detail. Additionally, the small “bites” served between courses were delightful and well executed. In summary: go for the view, the ambiance, and the impeccable service. The food is good, but the overall experience is what truly stands out. (5 stars)

The view is so awesome! The sun comes out after we sitting at the table! Services is so warm. The food is so so delicious! My very first time beef burger, great taste! It is couple special occasions we celebrate today, best decisions made to come here. Cheers! (5 stars)

Visiting Little Italy in New York City with my family was like stepping into a small slice of Europe right in the heart of Manhattan. The moment we walked down Mulberry Street, the atmosphere felt lively, colorful, and full of character. Italian flags hanging across the street, outdoor seating areas, and the aroma of garlic and fresh tomato sauce instantly made us hungry. What I loved most was simply strolling together and exploring the many snack outlets and restaurants lined up one after another. Small bakeries displayed cannoli, biscotti, and pastries that looked too good to resist. We stopped to try fresh cannoli filled on the spot — crispy shells with sweet, creamy ricotta inside. It was absolutely delicious. The restaurants offered everything from classic pasta dishes and wood-fired pizzas to seafood and rich lasagna. Many places had outdoor seating, which made the experience even more enjoyable. Sitting there with my family, enjoying authentic Italian food while watching the crowd pass by, felt special and relaxed. The drinks were just as enjoyable — refreshing mocktails, Italian sodas, espresso, and cappuccino that completed the meal perfectly. There were also small souvenir shops and specialty stores selling Italian sauces, olive oils, and sweets, adding to the cultural charm of the neighborhood. The entire area had a warm, welcoming vibe that made us slow down and truly enjoy the moment. Little Italy is not just about food — it’s about culture, tradition, and togetherness. Visiting with my family made it even more memorable. (4 stars)

(5 stars) We had dinner at Manhatta, located on the 60th floor of a skyscraper in the Wall Street district, and the experience was impressive overall. From the moment you arrive, the welcome is highly professional. The hostess team, maître d’, and sommelier all contribute to a very polished and well-organized atmosphere. The service is attentive, refined, and genuinely professional throughout the evening. The view is truly spectacular. One side overlooks the Brooklyn Bridge and Brooklyn, while the main façade faces Uptown Manhattan, showcasing the iconic, glittering skyline in all its glory. At the entrance, there is a stylish and functional bar area with a stunning backdrop view. Walking to the right, the restaurant opens into an L-shaped dining room with approximately 30 tables. The staff-to-guest ratio is excellent, and service flows smoothly. They offer a 3- or 4-course prix fixe menu. Each course (starter, main, dessert) includes about five options, which keeps the selection focused and prevents the menu from feeling overwhelming. The concept feels standardized, elegant, and based on quality ingredients rather than excessive variety. My wife and I both chose the four-course menu. I started with the raw shrimp, which was excellent — easily the highlight of my meal. I then had scallops, followed by a vegan main course that, unfortunately, felt underdeveloped and barely cooked — surprisingly so, to the point that it felt almost unfinished. I ended with a chocolate mousse. I paired my meal with a mezcal-based spicy cocktail, which was well balanced and enjoyable. My wife chose burrata as a starter, a lentil-based dish, tagliatelle, sea bass as her main course, and sorbet for dessert. She paired her meal with a Blanc de Blancs champagne, which complemented her dishes beautifully. Overall, the food was good but somewhat mediocre in execution, with a few highlights (especially the raw shrimp). I would rate the food 4 out of 5. However, the atmosphere, views, and the professionalism and friendliness of the staff easily deserve 5 out of 5. A unique and charming touch: the restaurant provides binoculars placed around the space for guests to enjoy the skyline up close — a thoughtful and memorable detail. bio_text: Marea is a modern and chic institution located in Central Park South, New York City, that redefines high-end coastal Italian cuisine. It attracts discerning diners who appreciate luxury and seek to elevate their dining experiences with exquisite food, unmatched service, and a vibrant atmosphere. Marea seamlessly blends the authentic flavors of coastal Italy with the dynamic style of New York, creating a unique culinary experience that celebrates life's moments. Marea specializes in coastal Italian cuisine, focusing on meticulously crafted pasta and seafood dishes. The menu features a combination of signature crudo and handmade pastas, presented in a tasting format that highlights the bracing flavors of the sea. The restaurant is known for its elegant presentation and high-quality ingredients. Marea is the recipient of the 2010 James Beard Award for Best New Restaurant and has received three stars from The New York Times. It has also been recognized as Best New Restaurant by Bon Appetit, Esquire, and GQ Magazines, and named NYC’s Best Italian Restaurant by Zagat.

review_snippets: Second time visiting Marea during my New York trip and it was even better than the first! The service was excellent — attentive, professional, and warm from start to finish. The pasta here is 100/100! Highly recommend the Pappardelle Granchio Reale — the king crab was sweet and generous, perfectly balanced with garlic butter. For appetizers, the Polipo (grilled octopus) and Scampi on “Scampi” were both phenomenal. Every dish was fresh, beautifully presented, and packed with flavor. A true NYC fine-dining highlight. Must recommend to all my friends traveling to New York — you can’t miss it! (5 stars)

Excellent meal, excellent service! My husband and I were celebrating our anniversary and a couple of other milestones and the entire staff was welcoming and warm. All of our dishes were delicious and we can’t wait to go back on our next trip. Our server Robert was delightful and friendly. He had excellent wine pairing suggestions! Everything on the menu is delectable, you cannot go wrong. Definitely make room for dessert! (5 stars)

We came on Christmas Eve and it was extremely crowded. The restaurant previously held a Michelin star, and after this visit, I can see why it might have lost it. Perhaps it was due to the holiday rush, but the service that night was fairly mediocre. We ordered the white truffle pasta, $110 for 4g. While the presentation was fine, it definitely did not feel Michelin-level. The risotto was more enjoyable than the tagliatelle and had a much richer flavor. For the starter, the Cannolicchio was quite creative, and the Astice was excellent!! The lobster was very bouncy, fresh, and sweet, and the burrata was rich and milky. Unfortunately, the Ricci was a big disappointment; the uni had a strong fishy taste and the quality was poor. For the primi, we tried the Capellini, which I was really excited about but ended up disappointed. It was overly acidic, and the butter was not well incorporated. We also ordered half portions of the Pappardelle Granchio Reale and Fusilli, and surprisingly, these simpler pasta dishes were more enjoyable than the so-called signature ones. For the main course, we chose the Anatra. It was already portioned when served, and the duck skin was beautifully crispy, one of the best dishes of the night. We ordered two desserts and both were very good; I especially liked the tiramisu. Overall, the portions here are quite generous. Some shortcomings help explain the lost star, but I would still recommend coming when it’s less crowded. (5 stars)

We chose here to celebrate Chinese New Year and had a really lovely experience. I’m allergic to olive oil, and to be honest, many restaurants either can’t accommodate that or simply say no, which makes dining out pretty stressful. The staff at Marea were incredibly understanding and accommodating. They were able to adjust the dishes so I could enjoy the meal without olive oil, and everything was still absolutely delicious. It felt great to be able to relax and actually enjoy our celebration without worrying about my allergy. Great food, thoughtful service, and a memorable way to celebrate the New Year. Really glad we picked this spot！ (5 stars)

bio_text: Mari is a Michelin-starred restaurant located in Hell’s Kitchen, New York, that offers a unique dining experience centered around contemporary Korean cuisine. With a focus on accessibility and tradition, Mari invites guests to explore the playful yet refined world of Korean hand rolls in a warm and inviting atmosphere. The restaurant's design and ambiance reflect a modern take on Korean culinary heritage, making it a perfect destination for both casual diners and culinary enthusiasts. Mari specializes in contemporary Korean cuisine, with a particular emphasis on hand rolls. The menu features an imaginative tasting format that begins with an amuse-bouche course, followed by seasonally inspired hand rolls, and concludes with a refreshing two-part dessert. Signature techniques include the meticulous preparation of rice using a sesame seed and sesame oil base, and the use of delicately textured gim for wrapping. Mari is the second Michelin-starred restaurant from the team behind Kochi, opening its doors in late 2021.

review_snippets: Location: very accessible via public transit .If driving in make sure to check for a parking lot in the area (it a busy area and might not have street parking) Service: Just one sound - WOW .The staff is incredible and looks like they truly enjoy their craft which makes it a delight to watch them work. The team knew it was my friends' birthday and allergies,even had a special birthday menu printed so she could have a memento which I found very thoughtful Ambiance: Very intimate and relaxed, we sat at the counter and enjoyed seeing the team at work.The space is very welcoming Now to the most important part- the FOOD. We had the chef's tasting menu. The starters were light and fresh . The first starter with egg and caviar was so beautiful it was a shame to eat it, and it tasted like a hug. The handrolls were magnificent.Each one had layers of flavors and textures condensed to a single bite. My favorite ones were the Spicy Tuna with a crunch and the Chef's special with sea urchin. The handmade noodle and soup were a very nice savory dish , great on a cold day like today. For dessert there was an assortment of items, my personal favorite was the Coconut sorbet and lemon curd.But all were wonderful, not too sweet and perfect ending to a greateal All and all 10/10 definitely recommend for special occasions (5 stars)

Very special tasting menu! The first course was immediately one of the bests - caviar over an egg cake in mentaiko butter sauce. All 7 hand rolls were layered with flavor and so elegantly plated. Works of art! The noodle + banchan course was a simple contrast to the rolls and had the most perfectly cooked shrimp. Lastly, the desserts were excellent. The service was very gracious, but the pacing a little slow so I’d recommend sitting at the counter to keep the momentum. (5 stars)

Such an amazing place, perfect for any celebration! They made the night so special for us, we were celebrating a birthday. Highly recommend making reservations and doing counter seating (set menu). Food was beautiful and delicious. Staff was incredible. Thank you for the detailed touches and thoughtfulness! Note: Service was a bit slow in the beginning so don’t arrive starving. (5 stars)

Very good food. It is inevitable that one might compare it to an omakase although some of the offerings might be more unique. Price wise you could probaby do two omakases for the price of mari. I was not a big fan of the sorbet but the rest of the desert was great. The egg +rice cake appetizer was the standout dish of the evening. (5 stars)

bio_text: Maria Restaurant, located in New Rochelle, NY, offers a unique dining experience that blends old and new Italian cuisine within an industrial modern farmhouse setting. The restaurant features striking design elements such as massive chandeliers, sapphire blue banquettes, and whitewashed brick walls, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere for guests. Recognized as Westchester's Best New Restaurant in 2019 and awarded five MICHELIN Guide accolades from 2020 to 2024, Maria Restaurant is a testament to culinary excellence and heartfelt hospitality. Maria Restaurant specializes in Italian cuisine, focusing on a modern interpretation of traditional dishes. The menu is designed to provide a delightful dining experience, emphasizing quality ingredients and innovative techniques. The restaurant is an homage to the owner's mother, reflecting a family legacy in its culinary offerings and ambiance.

We were in town for a wedding. I checked out the Michelin Guide to pick out a place to eat and am so happy we came here! The food was absolutely incredible. They were also very accommodating of my food allergies. Wish we lived close by so we could come here more often! (5 stars)

Walked in Monday night with my friend and were seated right away. The food was great — I ordered the lamb chops and she had the black linguine. Unfortunately, when I got home, I realized my two leftover lamb chops weren’t packed, only the potatoes. There was also an empty bone packed in my friend’s linguine. It was disappointing to discover this after getting home, especially since the meal itself was otherwise excellent and expensive. (3 stars)

bio_text: Markette is a Modern European restaurant infused with Caribbean influences, located in the vibrant Chelsea neighborhood of New York City. The restaurant offers an elegant yet welcoming atmosphere, perfect for romantic dinners, celebrations, and pre-show dining. With a focus on seasonal dishes and creative cocktails, Markette provides a refined dining experience that emphasizes comfort and connection among guests. The culinary focus at Markette blends refined European techniques with vibrant Caribbean flavors. The menu is designed for sharing and features an ever-evolving selection of inventive plates and inspired flavor pairings. Signature techniques include a thoughtful composition of dishes that balance comfort and creativity. Markette is an intimate dinner destination created by Chef India Doris and hospitality veteran Alex Pfaffenbach, reflecting Chef India's experiences cooking throughout Europe and her Caribbean heritage.

review_snippets: Amazing experience at Markette! We had a lovely anniversary dinner here. I couldn’t get a reservation on resy but I called the restaurant and they were able to get us in at a reasonable time. The food and drinks were delicious - especially loved the fish, pita, and rice. The cocktails were amazing and the dessert was out of this world. Exceptional service as well. Will definitely be returning! (5 stars)

Markette is definitely upscale. I dined solo and chose the Braised Oxtail Gratin, it was very well done, layered, flavorful with a bit of a kick. It felt authentic, elevated and enough for a whole meal for me! Drinks were also well done by the lovely bartender Rika, I had the Snake in the Grass! Decor is tasteful, bathrooms are clean and vibey with a designer candle burning. I loved all the details! Would for sure bring girlfriends or family back here. (5 stars)

Food was delicious nice blend of flavors with Caribbean influences. Moody lighting and atmosphere creates a great date vibe. There is also a nice lounge downstairs with a separate menu that’s just as good. The staff are on point with everything keeping the room flowing smoothly. The one and only note I have is the portions are a little small so if there is a few things on the menu you’re choosing btwn just get them all! Plates are meant for sharing so order plenty. We had the cod fish fritters, caviar and hash browns, rock shrimp linguine, and the pan seared dorade with the stracciatella ice cream for dessert. Everything was 10/10. We will definitely be returning! (4 stars)

This was yummy! I liked the lamb a lot. And the cod fish fried ball things. The tuna appetizer was fresh & fun. The pasta was a skip for me. It was fine but very basic. Desserts were also OK but I wouldn’t get again. Service is a bit odd. You have to add all the food at once so they can time it? Idk sounds a bit like poor kitchen process management. (5 stars)

The food and drinks were delicious - especially loved the fish, pita, and rice. The cocktails were amazing and the dessert was out of this world. Exceptional service as well. Will definitely be returning! (5 stars) Markette is definitely upscale. I dined solo and chose the Braised Oxtail Gratin, it was very well done, layered, flavorful with a bit of a kick. It felt authentic, elevated and enough for a whole meal for me! Drinks were also well done by the lovely bartender Rika, I had the Snake in the Grass! Decor is tasteful, bathrooms are clean and vibey with a designer candle burning. I loved all the details! Would for sure bring girlfriends or family back here. (5 stars) Food was delicious nice blend of flavors with Caribbean influences. Moody lighting and atmosphere creates a great date vibe. There is also a nice lounge downstairs with a separate menu that’s just as good. The staff are on point with everything keeping the room flowing smoothly. The one and only note I have is the portions are a little small so if there is a few things on the menu you’re choosing btwn just get them all! Plates are meant for sharing so order plenty. We had the cod fish fritters, caviar and hash browns, rock shrimp linguine, and the pan seared dorade with the stracciatella ice cream for dessert. Everything was 10/10. We will definitely be returning! (4 stars) This was yummy! I liked the lamb a lot. And the cod fish fried ball things. The tuna appetizer was fresh & fun. The pasta was a skip for me. It was fine but very basic. Desserts were also OK but I wouldn’t get again. Service is a bit odd. You have to add all the food at once so they can time it? Idk sounds a bit like poor kitchen process management. (5 stars)

bio_text: Masa is a culinary destination in New York City, helmed by acclaimed chef Masayoshi Takayama. The restaurant embodies the philosophy of shibui, where tradition meets artistry, and every detail reflects a dedication to craft and precision. With a minimalistic decor that serves as a blank canvas, the dining experience is designed to highlight the purity and character of each ingredient, creating an immersive and elevated omakase experience. Masa specializes in traditional Japanese cuisine, focusing on an omakase format that showcases seasonal ingredients at their peak freshness. Chef Masa employs precision and creativity in his techniques, ensuring that each dish maintains the innate character of its components. Chef Masa Takayama is renowned for his precision and creativity, bringing together traditional Japanese techniques and modern artistry.
menu_items: Masa Lunch Omakase - Focus primarily on sushi and sashimi, featuring Chef Masa's signature Toro Tartare Caviar followed by a seasonal nigiri selection and light seasonal fruit for dessert. - $495
Hinoki Counter Omakase - Guests are seated at the Hinoki Counter with one of our skilled sushi chefs, who personally guides you through your omakase journey. - $950
Masa Table Seating Omakase - Guests are seated in the main dining room, where a dedicated service team member guides the experience, featuring a seamless progression of flavors and textures. - $750
review_snippets: I was very happy with my experience at Masa NYC Hinoki Counter for $950 per person. You can get more detail at my youtube channel Noah Eats. This is not the Bar Masa location. This place down the hall from Bar Masa. This Masa is next to the another 3 Star Michelin Per Se. As opposed to the Blue Door at Thomas Kellers spot, Masa has a Blue Curtain signifying the are open and if located outside would provide shade. After you pass the curtain a Huge Cypress door guards whats inside. You are quickly acknowledged and locked into your bar height chairs. And you can put your elbows on the Inviting Hinoki Counter and you will find a block of ice to keep some ingredients chilled for service. Unfortunately there is a no photo policy so for my video review I had to tap my artistic side, so I hope you enjoy my youtube review. It's definitely a bucket list item for most of the world. I hope you do enjoy my Channel, Noah Eats well! (5 stars)

I got the hinoki experience. Everything was amazing and, dare I say, perfect from taste to presentation. It was the best 3-Michelin meal that I had in NYC. The sushi was out of this world. The sake recommendation was on point. The no photo policy is a shame since everything was so pretty. (5 stars)

Sat at the counter. Incredible experience. Favorite dishes were: 1. Taro tartare with caviar. Every restaurant I've been to tries to upselm you caviar at exorbitant prices and then is stingy with it. Here it's just part of the menu and it is an extremely generous portion, and paired with the best cut of tuna. 2. Omi wagyu and truffles. Omi is the best cut of the agyu called the emperors beef because it was saved for the emperor. But the emperor never had truffles on it. What. Surprisingly good combination. 3. The rest was a tasting menu of pieces of sushi and every one was really good. 4. The Japanese melon was special. Sometimes they have a strawberry. Either way it's the same place that gives erewhon their $19 strawberry. We skipped lunch to fully enjoy it but it wasn't a crazy amount of food. Felt happily full after. If it's your anniversary or birthday you get some lady M cake at the end, which was great. Otherwise the only dessert is the melon so you can even plan to go have dessert somewhere after if you didn't want to have lady M. Overall I feel like the innovativeness of the caviar and truffle dishes will be lost on more casual diners but those two make the price tag pretty worth it in my opinion. (5 stars)

The quality of the food and the level of service were undeniably excellent. However, one very important issue significantly affected the overall experience. Although the pricing at this restaurant already includes gratuity, this was never clearly explained or communicated to us in advance. As a result, we added an additional tip after the meal, which led to nearly $600 being paid in gratuity alone. At this level of fine dining, clear disclosure about whether gratuity is included is essential, especially for international guests. This is not a minor detail and should be explicitly communicated before or during the dining experience. The issue is not the price itself, but rather the lack of transparency, which ultimately left a disappointing impression. For those considering a visit, I strongly recommend confirming the gratuity policy beforehand. (3 stars)

bio_text: Massara is a refined dining establishment located in New York City, dedicated to the authentic regional cuisine of Campania. The restaurant embodies a warm and inviting atmosphere, reminiscent of a familial gathering, where guests can enjoy a thoughtfully curated menu inspired by Chef Stefano Secchi's childhood memories of Southern Italy. With a focus on seamless service and a commitment to providing an exceptional dining experience, Massara invites patrons to indulge in the rich flavors and culinary traditions of the Campanian region. Massara specializes in Campanian cuisine, featuring dishes that highlight the region's abundant farms and fisheries. The menu is crafted around cooking techniques utilizing a wood-burning oven and grill, offering a unique and flavorful dining experience. Massara, meaning 'matriarch' and 'head of the household' in Campanian dialect, draws inspiration from Chef Stefano Secchi’s childhood memories of visiting Southern Italy.
menu_items: Carpaccio Sgombro - mackerel, horseradish & prosciutto broth - $20
Arctic Char - pickled kolrabi & tomato water - $20
Hamachi - apple, almond & fennel - $24
Carpaccio - thinly sliced beef - campania way - $26
Della Zona Classico Antipasto - prosciutto di parma & bufala d.o.p. - $29
Polpo - salsa verde, slow cooked beans & mosto cotto - $25
review_snippets: My husband and I had an amazing experience at Massara on the Park! From the moment we arrived, the staff was kind, welcoming, and very attentive throughout our meal. The décor is simple and understated, which makes the space feel relaxed and comfortable. We started with the Griglia Ciabatta (Classico with olive oil, garlic & salt) and it was so good we completely forgot to take a picture before eating almost all of it! Perfectly crisp on the outside, soft on the inside, and incredibly flavorful. The Candele with ragù genovese and parmigiano was absolutely delicious, with deep, rich flavor in every bite. The portion was on the smaller side but with the rich flavor, any larger would have been too heavy. The standout of the night was the Smoked Pork Chop with pancetta and quince mostarda, hands down the best pork chop we’ve ever had! It was unbelievably tender, juicy, and packed with flavor. The waitress gave us a heads up that it takes 20 mins, which worked for us because we were able to start with the Candele, which gave us some time to truly enjoy it. We also enjoyed two sides: Sunchoke, roasted with fig gremolata and the Zucca Calabrese with squash with hazelnut & peperoncino, both beautifully prepared and full of flavor. Finally for dessert we had the Torta di Ricotta e Pistachio. Which had great flavor and texture and a little crunch on top. Everything we ordered was outstanding. Incredible food, attentive service, and a welcoming atmosphere. We can’t wait to go back! (5 stars)

A really spectacular brunch at Massara! While we had been to the restaurant multiple times for dinner and loved every moment, this was our first time tasting their daytime menu, and it did not disappoint. The signature pastas are, of course, not to be missed (the candele and quadratti are both out of this world) but the brunch specific offerings were also delicious—the eggs in purgatory had one of the best tomato sauces I’ve ever eaten! The new space is beautiful and spacious, and the service, as always, was impeccably warm and attentive. Will definitely be adding this to the “return” list ASAP! (5 stars)

Honestly thought booking a reservation would be harder, but I guess that month ahead planning worked out! We went in as a duo at around 7:00pm. At the temporary location, we asked for a coat check and got seated at a dark, isolated location. As there were still open tables, we were curious on why we were led so far away from the center of the restaurant. We asked to sit somewhere where the ambiance was felt and they said okay! After moving, we quickly ordered our food: paccheri, candele, and swordfish. The pasta tasted so fresh and felt homemade, like in Italy! The paccheri was so flavorful and the candele was definitely unique! The swordfish was cut open but very little meat to be blunt. However, it was a charming experience and we definitely enjoyed the food! (4 stars)

We booked a last minute reservation on Friday night and were blown away. We’ve been to Rezdora and had been meaning to visit Massara for some time. Turned out to be a lovely date night for us. All team members we interacted with were very warm and knowledgeable. We were checked on multiple times throughout the meal and our water glasses were always full. We shared several dishes - the chicory salad, fluke crudo, quadrati (lobster ravioli), cheesemaker’s ravioli, corteccia, veal cheek, torta di pistachio / ricotta and a cross between a lemon meringue tart / olive oil cake and gelato. Can’t remember the name of the tart but I included a pic of it. The texture was perfect and it seemed there was actual drizzled olive oil in the center. It was truly a special dessert. The attention to detail here was refreshing. Can’t wait to come back! (5 stars)

bio_text: MayRee Thai Kitchen is a Michelin-recognized restaurant located in the heart of Manhattan’s East Village, offering an authentic Southern Thai dining experience. The restaurant features a cozy and charming atmosphere, where guests can enjoy a vibrant mix of traditional and bold Southern Thai dishes, complemented by bespoke cocktails. With a focus on high-quality ingredients and traditional recipes, MayRee delivers an unforgettable culinary journey that has garnered acclaim from both locals and critics. MayRee specializes in Southern Thai cuisine, showcasing a compact menu that includes signature dishes such as spicy Kua Kling pork curry and classic Pad Thai. The dining experience is enhanced by bespoke cocktails inspired by Thai folklore, making each visit unique and memorable. Inspired by the Thai folktale 'Twelve Sisters', MayRee brings the rich traditions of Southern Thailand to New York City.
menu_items: Jor Rang - Southern style curry with shrimps, coconut milk, fresh turmeric, lemongrass, shallot, shrimp paste and bell pepper served with jasmine rice and fresh salad. - $25

Roti Nam Keang (V) - Southern Thai style massaman curry with potato, onion, peanut, coconut milk topped with fried shallot served with pan fried roti with a choice of Chicken or Tofu. Substitution: Beef for $3.00 Extra. - $23

Vegan Gai Tod Hat Yai - Deep fried chicken Southern style with Thai spices battered topped with fried onion and fried garlic served with sweet chili sauce, house made spicy tamarind sauce and sticky rice. - $21
Kee Mao Talay - Sautéed spaghetti with shrimps, squids, mussels, fresh basil, onion, fresh green pepper corn, bell pepper and chili in a spicy basil sauce. - $29

Pad Mee Kati (GF) - Sautéed vermicelli noodle with lump crab meat, Southern Thai style with coconut milk, dried chili pepper, shallot, bean sprout and chive topped with green mango, crabmeat and omelet. - $27

Kra Prow - Sautéed spicy basil sauce with ground chicken or ground pork, fresh Thai basil, chili pepper, garlic, string bean and onion served with jasmine rice and fried egg on top. Substitution: Beef for $3.00 Extra. - $23
review_snippets: MayRee Thai Kitchen has been selected for the Michelin Guide three years in a row, and it truly deserves it. We loved the hed tod (fried seafood mushrooms) — crispy and delicious. The bacon hor ham was huge and customizable with chili, onions, and peanuts. The grilled shrimp mango salad was super refreshing with large shrimp and fresh mango. For mains, the kee mao talay (seafood drunken noodles) was mildly spicy and loaded with mussels, squid, and shrimp. The kra prow (ground pork) was so flavorful and addictive — perfect with rice. Thai iced tea and Thai iced coffee are both great choices. The coconut ice cream, served in a heart-shaped coconut shell, was rich and fragrant. Beautiful ambiance and great atmosphere. Would definitely come back! (5 stars)

Finally visited this Michelin-recommended Thai spot after having it saved for over a year — totally worth the drive. Small, cozy, great prices, and every dish we ordered was excellent. About $50 per person after tax and we were stuffed. Top picks: 🔥 Keang Phed Ped — fragrant roasted duck with rich but not heavy curry, plus lychee, pineapple, and tomato. 🔥 Mee Kaeng — thin noodles with a generous portion that soak up the curry perfectly. 🔥 Mango Sticky Rice — not on the menu, but they have it; even my non-dessert friend loved it. Highly recommended! (5 stars)

MayRee is hands down one of my favorite Thai restaurants in NYC. The food is absolutely delicious, and the service is just as good—friendly, attentive, and genuinely welcoming. Their Pad Thai is perfectly balanced and full of flavor, and the Pad Krapow Moo is a must-order—rich, savory, and incredibly satisfying. You can really tell they care about authenticity and quality in every dish. What really sets MayRee apart is the atmosphere and drinks. They have beautiful Thai culture–inspired cocktails that are creative, well-crafted, and fun without being gimmicky. It’s the kind of place that feels special but still relaxed. This is 100% a restaurant I’d bring friends to—whether it’s their first time trying Thai food or they already love it. Consistently great food, great vibes, and a spot I’ll keep coming back to! (5 stars)

Mayree totally lives up to the Michelin Guide (2023–2025). One of the best Thai meals I’ve had in NYC. The curry was rich and flavorful with a nice balance of sweetness and spice. The soup pot was bold and comforting, with super fresh seafood. The Thai basil pork with fried egg over rice was simple but done perfectly — mixing the yolk into the rice was so satisfying. Cozy, intimate vibe and friendly service. Best part? It’s actually affordable — around $30–50 per person, which feels like a great deal for this level of quality in Manhattan. Definitely coming back. (5 stars)

bio_text: Ma•dé is an Indonesian restaurant located in the vibrant SoHo neighborhood of New York City, offering a warm and inviting atmosphere inspired by the coastal beach bars of Indonesia. The restaurant, which means 'second born' in Balinese, is a collaborative effort by Chef Cédric Vongerichten, his wife Ochi Latjuba Vongerichten, and their business partner Ezra J. William. With a focus on community and connection, Ma•dé provides a unique dining experience centered around Padang-style cuisine, where dishes are served family-style, encouraging sharing and interaction among diners. Ma•dé specializes in Padang-style dining, featuring a menu influenced by Indian and Middle Eastern cuisines. The culinary offerings revolve around three main elements: gulai (curry), lado (chili pepper), and bareh (rice), often incorporating coconut milk and spicy chili. The dining experience emphasizes bold flavors and communal eating, traditionally enjoyed with hands. Ma•dé was opened by Chef Cédric Vongerichten and his wife Ochi Latjuba Vongerichten, alongside their friend Ezra J. William, as a follow-up to their first restaurant, Wayan.
menu_items: Fried Chicken - sweet chili sambal - $78
Lamb Ribs - kecap manis, black pepper - $78
Butterfish - calamansi glaze, lime - $78
Roasted Romanesco - coconut, cherry tomatoes - $78
Lobster - sauce padang, sugar snap peas - $90

review_snippets: Interior design was beautiful, warm and intimate. Staff was friendly, efficient and helpful. Dinner at Ma-dé was such a delight! I truly didn't know what to expect here, but I was so pleasantly surprised with everything I had. Upon arrival, the interior is beautifully decorated and has a whimsical feeling. The padang dinner was exceptional with so many different dishes and flavors to try! The side dishes are a bit more vegetarian forward but I thoroughly enjoyed them. For choosing the main proteins, we did the lamb ribs and butterfish. Both were exquisite and so wonderfully tender. You won't leave hungry here! I will happily recommend this place for others to try and can't wait to return myself. (5 stars)

This is my third time here and oh my god everything just gets better. Tried their original menu (dumplings are a MUST) but LOOOVED their new Padang-style concept. Tried their Liwetan Feast during Restaurant Week in January & LOVED that too. As an Indonesian, Ma•dé really SERVED all the dishes. Elevated, but surely a fantastic introduction to Indonesian cuisine. And don’t get me started on their desserts. Although the cookies remind me of the ones I had back home as a child, the pandan crepes (dadar gulung) and passionfruit sorbet stole the show. Will definitely be back to try their spring & brunch menu!!! Heard VERY GOOD things on their lamb ribs 🥰 (5 stars)

I really really want to like this place, but the execution isn’t fully there. There were great elements but I thought the seafood wasn’t super fresh for the price, and some of the dishes were a bit bland. The hot menu items were actually the best part, and the presentation was beautiful. Loved the cocktails. This is still a newer restaurant so I hope they can get better! (4 stars)
search_text: Ma•dé Ma•dé is an Indonesian restaurant located in the vibrant SoHo neighborhood of New York City, offering a warm and inviting atmosphere inspired by the coastal beach bars of Indonesia. The restaurant, which means 'second born' in Balinese, is a collaborative effort by Chef Cédric Vongerichten, his wife Ochi Latjuba Vongerichten, and their business partner Ezra J. William. With a focus on community and connection, Ma•dé provides a unique dining experience centered around Padang-style cuisine, where dishes are served family-style, encouraging sharing and interaction among diners. Ma•dé specializes in Padang-style dining, featuring a menu influenced by Indian and Middle Eastern cuisines. The culinary offerings revolve around three main elements: gulai (curry), lado (chili pepper), and bareh (rice), often incorporating coconut milk and spicy chili. The dining experience emphasizes bold flavors and communal eating, traditionally enjoyed with hands. Ma•dé was opened by Chef Cédric Vongerichten and his wife Ochi Latjuba Vongerichten, alongside their friend Ezra J. William, as a follow-up to their first restaurant, Wayan. review_snippets: Came during restaurant week for brunch. It was $45 pp and well worth it. Firstly, every single dish was perfection. Had the muffin to start and it was warm and fluffy on the inside yet crisp on the outside. Same for the empanadas - crispy but the filling was soft and delicious. Probably one of the best omelettes, it was evenly cooked and the fillings (spinach and mushroom) were also seasoned and cooked to perfection. Not a bad bite throughout. Finished with sorbets and it was the most flavourful sorbets, especially the lemon and raspberry. I was surprised how jam packed the flavour was. Only downside was we order coffees and those took a really long time to come to the table. This place used to have Michelin stars but now it feels more like a neighborhood spot. Little pricey for a casual meal but great for a first date, or to make someone’s day. (5 stars)

We visited Meadowsweet on a snowy Sunday for brunch and were immediately impressed by the warm and polished experience from the moment we walked in. The restaurant was fairly quiet because of the weather and our group of four was seated right away. Water was brought to the table immediately and the front of house staff seemed completely in sync. The service felt smooth and professional without ever being stiff. None of us ordered cocktails and instead stuck with coffee which everyone at the table kept praising. It was rich, balanced, and exactly what you want on a cold morning. To start we ordered the donuts and the empanadas. The donuts were fun and reminded me of sugar coated munchkins. They were good but not particularly memorable. The empanadas on the other hand were excellent in terms of flavor. The filling was well seasoned and satisfying. The only critique is their size. At nineteen dollars for three empanadas we all felt they could be a bit larger to really showcase the filling. For my main dish I ordered the duck pastrami hash with sunny side eggs and it was phenomenal. The dish had great depth of flavor and the eggs were cooked perfectly. In hindsight I should have ordered the sourdough bread with the hash instead of as a starter. The bread would have been perfect for soaking up everything on the plate. My girlfriend originally ordered the bacon omelette but was accidentally served the mushroom spinach omelette. Luckily the mistake worked in our favor because it ended up being one of the best dishes on the table. The eggs were incredibly fluffy and cooked perfectly. The mushrooms absorbed a ton of flavor and created a savory richness that balanced beautifully with the spinach. Nothing felt overpowering and every bite was well composed. I tried a bite myself and was equally impressed. Another friend ordered the burger and really enjoyed it. It was simple, satisfying, and executed exactly how a good brunch burger should be. Overall the experience was excellent. The atmosphere was comfortable, the service was attentive, and the food showed strong technique and balance across the board. If brunch is this good I can only imagine how strong their dinner service must be. Considering the price point, the quality of the food, and the level of hospitality, Meadowsweet easily earns five out of five stars. I would happily come back for brunch again. (5 stars)

My wife (has celiac / gluten allergy) and I came here for my birthday, and it was an excellent experience. The servers here are kind, and knowledgeable/attentive about gluten cross contamination. And the food was fresh and very well cooked. The chicken roulade was juicy and the burger slapped. Definitely looking to come back again! (5 stars)

I came here for my birthday brunch with friends and had the best experience ! Staff was very kind and service was excellent. All the dishes were very tasty and you could tell the ingredients were fresh and very good quality (they use seasonal produce from their farm). I took the biscuit & poached eggs and French toast: each dish was flavorful and well balanced. They also had freshly squeezed orange juice so 10 / 10 for me. Thank you for the hospitality; will be back for dinner soon :) (5 stars)

bio_text: Meju is a distinguished traditional Korean fermentation restaurant located in Long Island City, NY, within the Little Banchan Shop. Under the guidance of Chef Hooni Kim, Meju offers a unique dining experience that emphasizes the art of Korean fermentation, creating a harmonious blend of flavors and textures that reflect the rich culinary heritage of Korea. The restaurant's intimate setting and carefully curated atmosphere invite guests to explore the depth of Korean cuisine through a thoughtfully designed tasting menu. Meju specializes in traditional Korean fermentation techniques, showcasing a tasting menu that highlights the complexity of fermented ingredients. The restaurant also offers natural wine pairings, enhancing the overall dining experience with carefully selected beverages that complement the dishes. Meju is Chef Hooni Kim's third restaurant, following the successful ventures of Danji and Hanjan. It represents the culmination of his extensive experience as a Korean chef.
review_snippets: Unlike most of the other high end Korean restaurants in NYC, the food at Meju is very simple and straightforward and easily recognizable from typical Korean BBQ restaurants that you might find in Ktown or Flushing. The primary difference is the laser focus on superior quality ingredients in every component in every dish, particularly the "jang" that serves as the guidepost for flavor of each course. The sourcing and significance of each item is described in passionate detail by the chef, making the experience both educational and theatric. Being completely honest, I'm unsure if the level of the ingredients and amount of food are justified by the price. But it's still an experience I'd return to in the future. (4 stars)

It was an amazing experience where you really felt the intentionality behind the food and the knowledge from Chef Kim. It's not often where you get to have a Michelin meal that satisfies both your intellectual and physical hunger. It was great having an intimate experience, being able to ask questions and learn about traditional Korean cooking and fermentation methods. You'll definitely leave healthier than when you came in 😁. (5 stars)

Probably the most fun Michelin starred meal I’ve had. Loved learning about traditional Korean approaches to food and fermentation methods. Food was delicious, with lots of rich, deep, and comforting flavors. Also loved the fermented ginger tea. The quantity of food is more than pictured, you get multiple rounds of fried dishes and multiple cuts of meat plus refills of vegetable sides. I thought it was plenty for me. Great service in an elegant atmosphere. If you’re a nerd who likes learning about food (and especially if you dine solo) this is a great place. (5 stars)

Let me begin by saying that Chef Kim took me back to my childhood. My mother passed away 4 years ago. She rarely cooked with a recipe. As a kid, I would watch her cook and eventually helped in the kitchen and she developed in me a love for cooking. My wife and I really enjoyed our experience at Meju. The dishes here are not going to be laden with caviar or have bits of gold foil just for the opulence. The dishes here are crafted with love and simplicity with a strong homage to the Korean art of fermentation. Many foods I consumed took me right back to my childhood as they were elegant, elevated versions of what many would consider Korean home cooking. This was the first restaurant in a very long time that actually inspired me to "do" as well as eat. Leaving this restaurant I felt like a more mindful person and renewed interest in learning the fermentation processes for Korean cuisine which I have gotten away from. Also, Chef Kim wears Melin hats which I absolutely love because I can never find any other brand of hat that fits so well for my big head. Thank you and your team for making a night so wonderful for us. (5 stars)

bio_text: Melba's is a celebrated comfort food destination located in New York City, known for its warm and inviting atmosphere that feels like home. Founded by Melba Wilson in 2005, the restaurant emphasizes exceptional customer service and a commitment to quality, making it a beloved spot for both locals and visitors alike. The dining experience is characterized by a welcoming environment where guests are treated like family, often greeted by Melba herself. Melba's specializes in classic comfort food with a modern twist, focusing on hearty, flavorful dishes that evoke nostalgia. The menu features a variety of options that cater to diverse tastes, ensuring a satisfying experience for all diners. Signature techniques include the use of high-quality ingredients and traditional cooking methods that enhance the authenticity of each dish. Melba's Restaurant opened its doors in 2005 and was founded by Melba Wilson, who aimed to create a nurturing dining experience in her hometown of Harlem. With a background in notable restaurants, Melba's vision was to combine great food with remarkable service.

review_snippets: I was hungry and saw this $5 peace of chicken menu option. 1/2 breast or thigh, drumstick fried or roasted. I’m glad I didn’t read the reviews cause this is one of the best fried chicken thighs I’ve ever had and I lived in the South for many years. Juicy, perfect fried, NOT old, NOT greasy!!! and just as importantly not over or under seasoned. I came at 12:30 on the Monday after many holidays and the staff were kind and friendly with smiles. The thigh was a generous size, definitely the best value you can get in Grand Central and frankly it’s cheaper and 500x less work than if you bought the chicken and fried it yourself. Give it a try! (5 stars)

I wish I had checked reviews before ordering here. The chicken sandwich was tiny and mostly batter instead of chicken. Chipotle mayo was good. The fries were tasteless and mealy almost like they were boiled instead of fried except even boiled potatoes have flavor and these tasted like almost nothing despite being dusted with a dry rub. The portion was also tiny for the price (see photo). The cashier upsold me on mac and cheese and that was okay, but mostly bland and not worth $9 at all for the size or quality. The staff was quick and nice at least . Overall recommend to skip this place! (2 stars)

honestly didn’t expect to have this good of a meal inside Grand Central, but Melba’s completely changed my mind. Grand Central is usually all about movement people rushing, grabbing something quick, not really stopping. Walking into Melba’s felt different right away. It felt warm. Familiar. Like a little pocket of Harlem planted in the middle of Midtown. I ordered the fried chicken and mac and cheese, because if you’re at Melba’s, you kind of have to. The chicken was exactly what you hope for: perfectly crispy on the outside, juicy inside, and seasoned all the way through. Not bland, not greasy just done right. The mac and cheese was rich and comforting without being over the top, the kind you keep going back to even when you’re full. The collard greens really stood out to me. They weren’t an afterthought. They had depth, balance, and that slow-cooked flavor that tells you someone actually cared while making them. Everything tasted like it came from a real kitchen with real standards not something thrown together for foot traffic. What I appreciated most was that it didn’t feel “touristy” or watered down just because it’s in Grand Central. The food still tastes like Melba’s. The portions are generous, the flavors are bold, and the spirit of the place comes through. You can tell this is the same Melba’s people love uptown, just in a different setting. There’s something really special about sitting there with a plate of soul food while trains come and go all around you. It’s grounding in a way. Comfort food in the middle of chaos. If you’re passing through Grand Central and want something that actually feels like a meal, not just fuel, Melba’s is worth stopping for. It’s one of the few places in the terminal where you can sit down, take a breath, and leave genuinely satisfied. (5 stars)

I had a really disappointing experience at Melba’s in Grand Central yesterday. I ordered chicken fingers and fries along with fried chicken and collard greens, and unfortunately the food was nearly inedible. The fries and chicken tenders tasted stale, like they had been sitting around for days. The fried chicken was even more concerning. It appeared undercooked and still had visible flour from the frying batter. Instead of being crispy, the coating was soggy and unpleasant. For a place located in a busy commuter hub like Grand Central, where so many people rely on quick but quality meals, I expected a much higher standard. Spending over $50 on food that I ultimately could not eat was extremely frustrating. I understand that high traffic locations can get busy, but basic food quality and proper cooking should never be compromised. (1 stars)

bio_text: Mesiba is a vibrant Levantine restaurant located in Brooklyn, NY, inspired by the celebratory culture of the Levant and the diverse flavors of Israel. The name 'Mesiba' translates to 'party' in Hebrew, reflecting the restaurant's lively atmosphere and focus on communal dining. With a design-forward space, the restaurant offers a unique dining experience that combines contemporary Levantine cuisine with innovative cocktails, creating an inviting environment for guests to enjoy a festive meal. Mesiba specializes in contemporary Levantine cuisine, featuring a menu that emphasizes fresh, seasonal ingredients and traditional flavors. The dining format encourages sharing, with recommendations for 2-3 plates per guest, showcasing signature dishes like homemade flatbreads, hummus, and various skewers. The culinary approach is complemented by innovative cocktail offerings that enhance the overall dining experience. Mesiba is inspired by the childhood memories of Elad Zvi, a founding partner of Bar Lab Hospitality, and aims to recreate the diverse flavors of Israel.

review_snippets: Made a reservation wanting to try the restaurant week menu only got told after arrival that they don’t serve it on Saturday, which was a bummer. BUT - all the food we ordered were really nice. My favourite was the shrimp skewer and the tomato sauce fish. Overall a bit overpriced and there’s no train nearby but will def come back for the food! Fab service as well. (4 stars)

I appreciate all the help from the Director of Events- Sydney & Manager Chris and staff, I had an amazing time! The food was excellent and the service and hospitality was more than accommodating! I will be returning soon for a dinner as the falafel, especially was fresh and delicious. I had a prix fix , family style dinner for 11 ppl and it was was such a success. by the end of the dinner, we had a birthday cake that most of us were too full to indulge in, The staff cut the cake evenly and packed individual to go boxes for each person. Everyone got to enjoy the left overs and cake the next day and it was even better ! Overall just a great experience!! (5 stars)

beautiful ambiance. great food. went on a calm wednesday evening and it did not disappoint. i’ve said this before and will say it forever.. customer service will always take the cake. our server michelle was excellent, attentive and pleasant. didn’t get to take many photos but will be back. (5 stars)

This Mediterranean spot is fire! The vibes were amazing last night and the décor is stunning. The food? Every dish was delicious. You must get their freshly made, hot frena bread and the melt-in-your-mouth lamb shank so worth every penny. Service was a 10/10. (5 stars)

bio_text: Mile End Delicatessen, located in Boerum Hill, Brooklyn, offers a warm and inviting atmosphere that captures the essence of Montreal-style Jewish cuisine. Since its inception in 2010, the restaurant has become a beloved neighborhood spot, known for its bold flavors and comforting dishes that blend tradition with modern culinary techniques. Whether for brunch, lunch, or a casual dinner, guests can enjoy a delightful dining experience that celebrates the rich heritage of Jewish and Canadian comfort food. Mile End specializes in Montreal-style Jewish cuisine, featuring signature dishes such as smoked meat sandwiches, house-made hot dogs, and rich poutine. The menu is crafted using fresh ingredients and scratch-made techniques, with a focus on honoring traditional recipes while adding a contemporary twist. Mile End Delicatessen was founded in 2010 by co-founder Joel Tietolman, who was inspired by his Montreal upbringing and a lifelong love for Jewish food. The restaurant aims to continue the legacy of grandmothers' cooking and introduce authentic Montreal-style cuisine to New York.

Smoked Meat Hash - Smoked meat, potatoes, caramelized onions, two fried eggs - $20
Breakfast Poutine - Hand-cut fries, cheese curds, gravy, maple bacon, two sunny eggs - $20
The Leo - Three egg scramble, smoked salmon, rye toast - $22

Safta's Pancakes - Cottage cheese hot cakes, butter, maple syrup - $18
review_snippets: I had high hopes for this place. After trying Schwartz’s in Montreal and Katz’s in New York, I didn’t expect to be served supermarket-style pastrami. We ordered the smoked meat sandwich, Caesar, and poutine, and then tea and chocolate babka. Everything except the smoked meat was fine. The smoked meat itself was very disappointing, I’d probably give it one star. it’s also over priced. Update (two days later): Since eating the smoked meat sandwich here, my husband has had an upset stomach. I don’t know how long the pastrami had been sitting, but this made the experience even more disappointing. (2 stars)

Got the flight of latke and they were all great. We also got the brisket poutine, I would have it again but I really want to try some of the other poutine they offer. Will definitely back if not soon then for Hanukkah next year. Oh yeah and the chocolate babka was fantastic (5 stars)

Mile End in Brooklyn has been on my list of places to check out for a long time, and it did not disappoint at all! I got a couple of sandwiches to go, but the inside looks like a family-run, hospitable, and cozy diner... exactly what you want! Love the Canadian soul too! I followed Ali's recommendation and tried the Montreal Smoked Meat sandwich (their special), and I also got the one with chicken liver. Both super Yummy! Will come back to dine in 10/10 See you soon :) (5 stars)

I’m a big foodie for brisket, pastrami, and corned beef — give me all of it! My go-to is the Reuben, and they’ve got a double-meat version called the “Eli Reuben” that’s an absolute must if you go. The ambience is cozy and classic diner-style. Their breakfast menu looks top-tier, too. Service can be a bit on the slower side, but with this Montreal-style smoked meat deli, it’s absolutely worth the stop. (5 stars)

bio_text: Minetta Tavern, located in the heart of New York City, offers a unique blend of Parisian steakhouse ambiance and classic New York tavern charm. Originally opened in 1937, this historic establishment has been a gathering place for notable figures in literature and the arts, creating a vibrant and storied atmosphere for diners. The restaurant's design and decor reflect its rich history while providing a warm and inviting dining experience. Minetta Tavern specializes in classic American cuisine with a focus on high-quality steaks and traditional tavern fare. The menu features a selection of signature dishes, including their renowned Black Label Burger, crafted with premium ingredients. The dining format is a la carte, allowing guests to enjoy a variety of offerings tailored to their preferences. Minetta Tavern originally opened in 1937 and has been frequented by notable figures such as Ernest Hemingway, Ezra Pound, and Eugene O'Neill.
menu_items: Burrata - fig chutney, hazelnuts, frisée, mâche, toasted levain - $25
Risotto - white truffle purée, morel mushrooms, Parmesan, chives - $31
Grilled Prawns - marble potatoes, chorizo Iberico, Calabrian aioli - $27
Niman Ranch Strip Loin - pommes frites, charred spring onion, truffle butter - $49
Atlantic Cod - crushed Yukon potatoes, black trumpet mushrooms, lemon brown butter - $37
Housemade Ravioli - butternut squash, mascarpone, shaved black truffles, brown butter, sage - $36
review_snippets: Order the GRILLED OYSTERS!! They are spectacular. Always a great time at Minetta. We made our reservation for late lunch or early dinner and this was lovely around 3pm on a weekday. Still a great menu. Cocktails are great. Husband got the espresso martini and it was very well made as was my Bloody Mary. I ordered us both prosecco as well that was delicious. The waitstaff was wonderful- Ashlyn was our server and she was very accommodating as was the manager on duty, Clark. From the fresh warm bread to our entrees everything was delicious. The Duck Ragu with Pappardelle pasta was great, al dente, homemade to perfection. The filet mignon was cooked very well, charred nicely on the outside. Sides was lovely and the desert was rich and delicious! Highly recommend for a nice brunch or dinner or even just cocktails and the grilled oysters. (5 stars)

I was so excited to finally try this classic spot! Service overall: 10/10. The restrooms were clean, which is always a good sign. For food, we tried the Black Aged Burger (medium) and… wow. Honestly, it was orgasmic 😂 A burger without cheese? Yes — and it was incredible. You could really taste the flavor of the meat: soft, juicy, buttery, and perfectly cooked. We didn’t have cocktails, but we ordered wine and it was great. Also, they definitely pour more than 4oz, which makes it even better 😉 Totally recommend! (5 stars)

Came in for a late lunch excited to try this place. The atmosphere is great - old school tavern, unassuming from the outside, lively bar. The service was excellent from start to finish and the cocktails and drinks were delicious. The food left a little bit to be desired. The apps we tried were great (bone marrow 8/10; steak tartare 7/10). We had a range of entrees at the table... the moules frites were the highlight. The pappardelle was nothing special. The steak frites included a generous portion of steak that paired well with the bearnaise sauce and the fries were outstanding. However, there was no difference between the medium and medium rare that was ordered for the table, the kitchen went a bit overboard on the pepper seasoning, and the steak knives we received were less sharp than the butter knives we already had. Overall, worth checking out at least once. I'd come back if I was in the area to try the burger. (4 stars)

What a NY gem. So glad we planned my Birthday weekend to include Minetta. Was concerned about even while having a reservation that we would have to wait but luckily got seated within 3 minutes! Front room by bar is super crowded due to people waiting on their tables, but was so happy to be in the back room. We had a table facing out and appreciated the epic table! You can see the old school NY vibe in the pics. Our server was super efficient as well as the staff that helped with water and bread. My water glass was filled every few minutes! Husband had the maple Old Fashioned and said it was one of the best he’s ever had (and he’s for sure an OF snob)!! For food we started out with the onion soup which was excellent and the petit salad (not so petit)! For an entree we actually split the black label burger PLUS cheese which was absolutely incredible. Fries were insane too. Passed on dessert as we were just so maxed out! (5 stars)

bio_text: Miss Ada is a charming neighborhood restaurant located in the vibrant Fort Greene area of Brooklyn, offering a modern twist on Mediterranean cuisine. The inviting atmosphere is complemented by a focus on local and seasonal ingredients, with fresh herbs sourced from their backyard garden enhancing the flavors of both dishes and cocktails. The name 'Miss Ada' is derived from the Hebrew word for restaurant, symbolizing the essence of gathering around the dinner table with family and friends. The restaurant specializes in modern Mediterranean cuisine, featuring a menu that includes mezze, hummus, and skewers. Signature techniques include the use of fresh herbs and local ingredients, with a focus on creating unique flavor profiles. Miss Ada is led by Israeli-born Chef/Owner Tomer Blechman, who draws inspiration from his heritage to craft a distinctive dining experience.
menu_items: RED SNAPPER CEVICHE - COCONUT, PINEAPPLE, LIME, SERRANO - $19
HIRAMASA CRUDO - PEACH AND GINGER AGUACHILE, SESAME - $19
WHIPPED RICOTTA - BROWN BUTTER, HONEY, SAGE - $14
LABNE - ZA'ATAR, OLIVE OIL - $12
BABAGANOUSH - GINGER AIOLI, ZA’ATAR - $13
MUHAMMARA - ROASTED RED PEPPER, WALNUT, BREADCRUMBS - $14
review_snippets: I honestly wish I could give the service a 6/5, but I will make do with what I got! My fiance and I came here on NYE to do the pre-set menu of house favorites. The place was decorated so cute and they had little party favors everywhere for NYE. When we arrived, we got seated at the bar even though we made a reservation at the back patio on Resy. When I let the manager know, she was so apologetic about the Resy app incorrectly placing guests into the wrong areas of the restaurant and asked us if she could purchase our first round of drinks to make up for it. No problem! So we are eating dinner at the bar and she kept coming up to us after we were done with the cocktails offering us wine, refills, and even a great dessert wine that the bartender recommended with the babka. When I tell you this is some of the best food AND service i’ve ever experienced- what an incredible way to end 2025!!! At the end we expected to pay for the drinks completely and were told they were all on the house. Shocked and on cloud 9, beyond full, we left the restaurant so happy and a little tipsy. As for the food, obsessed with the hummus and ricotta cheese, as well as the kofta was the best I’ve ever had. Babka was amazing and everything else was so yummy, my fiance never had Israeli food before and was cautiously optimistic going into the dinner I chose, and left saying that was his favorite meal from our NYC trip! Thank you so much to the team of Miss Ada!! highly highly recommend!!!! (5 stars)

Celebrated my husband's birthday and had the most wonderful experience!! Every single bite of food was absolutely delicious. We especially loved the short rib hummus, halloumi skewers, falafel, and pita bread 😊 Super friendly and sweet staff as well. They even surprised us at the end with a little cup of gelato with a candle in it. This was our 4th time dining at Miss Ada and we will definitely continue to come back!! 🧡🧡🧡 (5 stars)
This is now one of my favorite steak and eggs. The whipped ricotta is so good and very similar to Theodora’s though it is served with pita bread. Service was great! (5 stars)

Cute and cozy vibe. Food was delicious, the fish was super tender. Good selection of wines and friendly service. Great example of what to expect in the fort Greene neighborhood. Verdict: will return and recommend! (4 stars)
