bio_text: Miss Lily's is a celebrated Caribbean oasis located in New York City, Negril, and Dubai, offering a vibrant and colorful dining experience that embodies the spirit of Jamaica. With a lively atmosphere featuring vintage-style booths and a state-of-the-art music system, guests can enjoy modern Caribbean cuisine alongside a vast selection of the Caribbean's finest rums, all while immersing themselves in the rhythms of reggae, soca, afrobeat, and dancehall. The restaurant is dedicated to providing an unparalleled experience filled with good vibes and great food. Miss Lily's focuses on modern Caribbean cooking, showcasing dishes with Jamaican roots and global influences. The menu features island specialties like jerk chicken, escovitch fish, and oxtail, prepared using traditional recipes and modern techniques. The dining format is casual, allowing guests to enjoy a lively atmosphere while savoring innovative culinary creations. Miss Lily's has been serving modern Caribbean cooking for over 15 years, with a culinary team that includes Chef Brittney 'Stikxz' Williams, who has experience in Michelin-starred restaurants, and Chef Andre Fowles, a three-time Food Network Chopped Champion. The restaurant draws inspiration from the diverse roots of Jamaican cuisine.
menu_items: Tamarind Glazed Plantain - $9
Shoestring Jerk Fries - $8
Mac & Cheese - $10
Coco Bread - $6
Seasonal Greens - $9
Coconut Rice & Peas - $6
review_snippets: Really enjoyed my experience at Miss Lily’s 7a. I came here for the first time in 2018foir a birthday brunch and remember the food and drink being fantastic. Today (2026), I came again and was happy to see that not much had changed. Today I had the jerk chicken and the tamarind glazed plantain. My husband did the restaurant week deal with codfish fritters, jerk hash, and coconut cream cake. We also indulged in the boozy brunch deal for $25 bottomless drinks. The jerk chicken was really good, and a great portion. The sweet potato jerk hash was a little lighter but it still was a nice serving. Everything we had was delicious. The best drink was definitely the rum punch. The only problem with the restaurant is that it’s pretty small and there are some tables that feel on top of each other. Otherwise the staff was friendly and the music was good. (5 stars)

Miss Lily’s is one of the most consistent Jamaican restaurants you’ll find in Manhattan. Everything on the menu is always available which is rare for a Jamaican spot! The food is very good, and you can tell they take pride in maintaining quality. The aki and saltfish leans more on the saltfish side they’re not too heavy on the aki but it’s still delicious and well-seasoned. The roti is always soft and fresh, which is a big plus. The decor really captures the vibe of a bar straight out of Jamaica colorful, lively, and full of energy. On weekends, there’s usually a live DJ playing great dancehall and reggae, adding to the island feel. Overall, Miss Lily’s delivers both in atmosphere and flavor a must-visit if you want a true taste of Jamaica in NYC. 🇯🇲🔥 (5 stars)

A great, casual spot with cool vibes for Jamaican food. We went for brunch and loved it. I've had my fair share of Jamaican food in NYC and Jamaica and will share that while there was a different twist, food flavors were on point. We shared the Jerk Chicken roti - a burrito stuffed with all the Jamaican flavors - and the Jamaican breakfast. The ackee and saltfish, steamed veggies and plantain were great. The only thing we didn't love was the festival (it was a little heavy...I prefer fried or boiled dumplings with this kind of breakfast). We both had sorrel ginger beers to drink. These were fine (light on the sorrel flavor). Service was lovely and the decor and music just right. (5 stars)

I’ve visited for brunch before, but I’d always wanted to experience dinner here—and during Restaurant Week, it did not disappoint. The thoughtfully designed décor and inviting ambiance set the perfect tone for our meal. We dined later in the evening, which gave the space a calm, relaxed energy, complemented by the smooth sounds of old-school reggae playing in the background. The cocktails were both strong and well-crafted, adding a nice touch to the evening. I wouldn’t recommend this spot for parties larger than four indoors, as the space is more intimate. The outdoor seating can accommodate groups up to six, though it did appear a bit snug. If you’re craving authentic Jamaican cuisine, this is a must-visit. According to my partner—who may be slightly biased as a proud Jamaican—it’s home to the best jerk chicken in all five boroughs. (5 stars)
search_text: Miss Lily's Miss Lily's is a celebrated Caribbean oasis located in New York City, Negril, and Dubai, offering a vibrant and colorful dining experience that embodies the spirit of Jamaica. With a lively atmosphere featuring vintage-style booths and a state-of-the-art music system, guests can enjoy modern Caribbean cuisine alongside a vast selection of the Caribbean's finest rums, all while immersing themselves in the rhythms of reggae, soca, afrobeat, and dancehall. The restaurant is dedicated to providing an unparalleled experience filled with good vibes and great food. Miss Lily's focuses on modern Caribbean cooking, showcasing dishes with Jamaican roots and global influences. The menu features island specialties like jerk chicken, escovitch fish, and oxtail, prepared using traditional recipes and modern techniques. The dining format is casual, allowing guests to enjoy a lively atmosphere while savoring innovative culinary creations. Miss Lily's has been serving modern Caribbean cooking for over 15 years, with a culinary team that includes Chef Brittney 'Stikxz' Williams, who has experience in Michelin-starred restaurants, and Chef Andre Fowles, a three-time Food Network Chopped Champion. The restaurant draws inspiration from the diverse roots of Jamaican cuisine. Tamarind Glazed Plantain - $9 Shoestring Jerk Fries - $8 Mac & Cheese - $10 Coco Bread - $6 Seasonal Greens - $9 Coconut Rice & Peas - $6 Really enjoyed my experience at Miss Lily’s 7a. I came here for the first time in 2018foir a birthday brunch and remember the food and drink being fantastic. Today (2026), I came again and was happy to see that not much had changed. Today I had the jerk chicken and the tamarind glazed plantain. My husband did the restaurant week deal with codfish fritters, jerk hash, and coconut cream cake. We also indulged in the boozy brunch deal for $25 bottomless drinks. The jerk chicken was really good, and a great portion. The sweet potato jerk hash was a little lighter but it still was a nice serving. Everything we had was delicious. The best drink was definitely the rum punch. The only problem with the restaurant is that it’s pretty small and there are some tables that feel on top of each other. Otherwise the staff was friendly and the music was good. (5 stars) Miss Lily’s is one of the most consistent Jamaican restaurants you’ll find in Manhattan. Everything on the menu is always available which is rare for a Jamaican spot! The food is very good, and you can tell they take pride in maintaining quality. The aki and saltfish leans more on the saltfish side they’re not too heavy on the aki but it’s still delicious and well-seasoned. The roti is always soft and fresh, which is a big plus. The decor really captures the vibe of a bar straight out of Jamaica colorful, lively, and full of energy. On weekends, there’s usually a live DJ playing great dancehall and reggae, adding to the island feel. Overall, Miss Lily’s delivers both in atmosphere and flavor a must-visit if you want a true taste of Jamaica in NYC. 🇯🇲🔥 (5 stars) A great, casual spot with cool vibes for Jamaican food. We went for brunch and loved it. I've had my fair share of Jamaican food in NYC and Jamaica and will share that while there was a different twist, food flavors were on point. We shared the Jerk Chicken roti - a burrito stuffed with all the Jamaican flavors - and the Jamaican breakfast. The ackee and saltfish, steamed veggies and plantain were great. The only thing we didn't love was the festival (it was a little heavy...I prefer fried or boiled dumplings with this kind of breakfast). We both had sorrel ginger beers to drink. These were fine (light on the sorrel flavor). Service was lovely and the decor and music just right. (5 stars) I’ve visited for brunch before, but I’d always wanted to experience dinner here—and during Restaurant Week, it did not disappoint. The thoughtfully designed décor and inviting ambiance set the perfect tone for our meal. We dined later in the evening, which gave the space a calm, relaxed energy, complemented by the smooth sounds of old-school reggae playing in the background. The cocktails were both strong and well-crafted, adding a nice touch to the evening. I wouldn’t recommend this spot for parties larger than four indoors, as the space is more intimate. The outdoor seating can accommodate groups up to six, though it did appear a bit snug. If you’re craving authentic Jamaican cuisine, this is a must-visit. According to my partner—who may be slightly biased as a proud Jamaican—it’s home to the best jerk chicken in all five boroughs. (5 stars)

bio_text: Miss Mamie's Spoonbread Too is a beloved soul-food restaurant located in Morningside Heights, New York, where guests can enjoy a warm and inviting atmosphere reminiscent of home cooking. The establishment caters to a diverse clientele, including students from nearby Columbia University and local residents, all drawn to its comforting dishes and friendly service. With a focus on family recipes, the restaurant has become a staple for those seeking hearty, flavorful meals in a relaxed setting. The restaurant specializes in Southern comfort food, offering a menu that features classic dishes such as fried chicken, shrimp, and short ribs. Signature items include the 'Miss Mamie Sampler' and a variety of sides like mac and cheese and collard greens, all prepared with a focus on traditional techniques and generous portions. The owner, Norma Jean Darden, is a former Wilhelmina model who draws inspiration from her family's recipes, which she compiled in her best-selling cookbook, 'Spoonbread and Strawberry Wine.' The restaurant has been a cherished part of the community for nearly three decades.

Papa Darden's Wingettes - Fried, Jerk, or BBQ - $14.00

review_snippets: We thoroughly enjoyed delicious catering from Miss Mamie's Spoonbread Too for a the launch of a new perfume. Little did we know we were in for such a surprise to actually meet the iconic former fashion model Norma Jean Darden, known for her role in "The Battle of Versailles" battle between French and American fashion designers, and subsequent documentary and book prior to founding her restaurant, Miss Mamie’s Spoonbread Too, which catered our event. What really helped our team was the helpful thoughtful discussion we had prior to the event, to be sure our selection would delight guests. The catfish bites, jerk wingettes, deviled eggs, fruit kebobs, and brownies were perfect and delivered with care. (5 stars)

I ordered a delivery, and I'm very impressed. There's quite a few soul food places in the area, but I haven't liked any of them, although they have higher rating. Food is delicious. String beans are tender yet crunchy and garlicky. Potato salad has just right amount of mayo. Beef ribs are saucy but the sauce isn't overpowering. You can still taste the tender meet. Great food overall Oh and they made sure to wrap the to go box with a plastic wrap so the sauce and juices didn't leak through. Thanks! (5 stars)

We went to experience American southern food. Unfortunately, they told us they can't make their signature Gumbo nor Banana Pudding😔 So we ordered a sampling plate. Oil used for deep fried stuff didn't taste fresh. I didn't feel life in food 🙁 Collard green on the side was extremely salty😐. Lastly, they got the order wrong and served us extra sides which we didn't notice until bill came. (2 stars)

This place is the epitome of Southern cuisine best in the entire neighborhood or New York for that matter. If you’re going to judge southern food off of anything, the collar greens, here are the best I’ve ever had in my entire life. I will never be able to experience eating collard greens in any other restaurant or location the same again because they are the top of the pedestal of flavor to compare too. Just blown away buy the food and flavor this small place produces. The staff is wonderful and the speed of the dishes are served quick and hot and with the best smile and vibe you can ask for. I can’t wait to come back!! This is a must experiment NyC location!! Taking the # Number 1 spot for NYC Must Eat locations. (5 stars)

review_snippets: First time dining here and can't wait to return. There were so many ceviches to choose from but we went with the mixed seafood and everything was good especially in the tigers milk. The filet mignon roll gets torched tableside and was delicious. For our main we had the red snapper thats deboned in a sweet chili sauce and is designed to share. I tried the sweet plantains which were good but had too much goat cheese for my liking. I also tried the margarita al pastor which was a very interesting drink. The Penicillin was also very tasty and strong. I was too full for dessert,so maybe next time. Staff was very nice and our server Natalie was very helpful guiding us through the menu. (5 stars)

Jasmin our waitress was just awesome! She was attentive but not intrusive…perfect balance of what we appreciate. We have been looking for an elevated Peruvian restaurant for a while and are so happy we found this one. The food was so delicious we kept rolling our eyes and making “yum” sounds . To start we had the yuca fries, the seafood mix ceviche and the shrimp tempura. Let me just say, we would order all of those again without hesitation ! It’s important to note that the shrimp tempura has a kick(but we love that). For our main we had the filet dish (lomo saltado) and the tiger shrimp with noodles dish( Tallarín saltado). Both cooked to perfection and large portions. We passed on dessert due to being super full, but we went to the downstairs lounge for a couple drinks after and we love when restaurants have a lounge option. Having that helps keep the good vibe going when you’re having a nice night out. All in all, a great restaurant and experience…we most certainly will be back! (5 stars)

When I’m telling you everything was perfect…it was perfect! From the moment you walk in the ambience was incredible. The music was such a vibe. The host was really friendly sat us down pretty quick. Our waiter was super friendly and attentive. The drinks were perfect not water down or too strong. The appetizers the food dessert were amazing and the food came out really quick. Overall, I’ll definitely be coming here again. It is worth the hype!! And they gave us free chicha morada sour shots ☺️ (5 stars)

Absolutely in love with this place! Every visit feels like a little celebration. My husband and I come here often, and it never disappoints. The food is bursting with authentic flavors — you can truly taste the freshness and quality, especially in the seafood. Their ceviche is out of this world, the rolls are delicious, and I could rave forever about their variety of pisco sour — it’s the best I’ve ever had! The staff is warm and attentive, always making us feel welcome. The cocktails are creative and amazing, and the interior is stunning — stylish, cozy, and perfect for a great night out. They also have fantastic midweek specials, which makes it even more exciting to come back again and again. This place has our hearts. Highly recommend! 💛 (5 stars)

bio_text: Momofuku Noodle Bar is a vibrant and innovative dining destination that embodies the spirit of modern Asian cuisine. With a casual yet energetic atmosphere, it invites guests to enjoy a unique culinary experience that celebrates bold flavors and fresh ingredients. The restaurant specializes in Asian-inspired noodle dishes, focusing on ramen and other noodle preparations. The menu features a variety of options, including signature bowls and small plates, emphasizing fresh, high-quality ingredients and inventive flavor combinations.
menu_items: Large Format Fried Chicken Meal - Two whole chickens, Southern-style and Korean-style, plus favorite sides. - $225
Spicy Scallop Kimbap - Scallops, rice, seaweed, and assorted vegetables.
Fried Chicken - Buttermilk brined fried chicken with savory chive biscuits and white BBQ sauce. - $45
review_snippets: Dinner at the flagship location was excellent. My coworker and I started off with the spicy tuna roll which we constructed ourselves. Drinks were artisanal; I tried the Bad Therapy which has bourbon, cold brew and brown butter. My main was the spicy mushroom ramen which had a great garlicky flavor. Dessert was a delectable slice of chocolate pie. Highly recommend this location. Busy dining room but service was efficient and plates came out fast. Leisurely walk from Union Station. (5 stars)

Food was delicious. One server who was probably a manager was spectacular; the others were kind of stand-offish. We were seated by the entrance and felt a cold draft every time the door opened, and the seating strategy was such that it didn’t feel like a laid back dinner. That said, the food was delicious (4 stars)

It’s a great vibe definitely geared towards younger crowd. The tables are small and the have stools without backs. A bit on the loud side. Food and service are great. Price is reasonable for what they serve. The hand rolls and pork belly baos are delicious. So was the ginger scallion noodles. The milk chocolate pie was really good. The smoked pork ramen was our least favorite. My expectations were much higher for the broth. (5 stars)

Cannot see the hype about this place. Ramen broth is purely salty for both garlic chicken and smoked pork. The chicken and pork are pretty tasty but the broth is undrinkable. I have to dilute it with water. The best item is the fried potato, 10/10. The lychee cosmo is a refreshing drink to have for happy hour price. The arrangement of their seating is also uncomfortable, and extremely crowded, there are no small tables for 2-4 people, it’s either big table or the counter. We had to share a large table with no place to put our coats. I understand the limited space and trying to accommodate as more customers as possible, but it makes the whole experience awful. (2 stars)

bio_text: Moody Tongue Sushi, located in the vibrant West Village of New York City, offers a lively and intimate dining experience that combines the art of sushi with a curated selection of specialty beers, cocktails, and wines. The restaurant emphasizes a unique culinary journey, where each dish is thoughtfully paired with beverages crafted by the acclaimed Moody Tongue Brewery, known for its chef-driven beers. The restaurant specializes in an exclusive omakase experience, featuring a hyper-seasonal and elevated sushi menu. Each course is meticulously crafted to highlight the freshest ingredients, complemented by expertly curated beer pairings. The omakase experience is led by Executive Sushi Chef Hiromi Iwakiri, alongside brewmaster Jared Rouben from the MICHELIN-starred Moody Tongue Brewery.
menu_items: FLUKE PICO DE GALLO - pico de gallo, micro cilantro - $8
SPICY TUNA - bluefin tuna, calabrian chili spicy mayo, arare, chives - $9
HAMACHI MOLE - mole, micro cilantro, sesame seeds - $9
NEW YORK CITY BAGEL - ora king salmon, yuzu cream, capers, red onion, tomato, chives - $11

review_snippets: Will say this place is okay for a date. If you are a foodie or crazy about sushi, the nigiri set is okay, quality is great but not impressive. The temaki was given a very heavy flavor source, not recommended. The salad and curdo is okay also very heavy in seasoning and sauce. Overall, good for beer lovers, not for sushi lovers. (4 stars)

Completely lackluster experience. We had better sushi at the market on the way down to our reservation to compare, and pre-game. Wife and I have traveled the world and dined at Michelin restaurants, and street food stalls in a dozen countries. Beers were good but completely overpriced for dine in. Definitely would never come back for the food, but would get a 6 pack to go if I was in the neighborhood. (2 stars)

Classy spot! Went in a group of 5 which was perfect to share a bunch of small plates. I was most impressed with the vibrant flavors in the cucumber salad and corn gyoza but can’t go wrong with anything on the menu, especially the torched corn scallop. And we also loved the cocktails. Great atmosphere for conversation, busy but not too loud! I would come back in a heartbeat (5 stars)

I highly do not recommend the omakase at Moody Tongue Sushi. At $160 per person, the quality and experience fell far short of expectations. The biggest issue was the timing; there were 10+ minute gaps between every course, making the meal feel incredibly slow and disjointed. Furthermore, the "16 courses" consisted of nothing but one single piece of nigiri per round. There was nothing extravagant or unique about the selection to justify the high price tag. It is far too expensive for such a basic, poorly-paced meal. Save your money and go elsewhere. (1 stars)

review_snippets: Beautiful upscale spot for a celebration, but come hungry for a heavy meal! The ambiance here is perfect for a date night. The food is high-quality and punchy, though the menu leans quite rich. • Spicy Fried Chicken: Perfectly juicy and garlicky. I loved that the sauce was served on the side so the crispiness could shine. • Assorted Pancakes: Great variety; the shrimp was the standout. • Galbi-jjim: Very decadent. Definitely pair this with rice to cut through the richness. • Uni Sotbap: Incredibly flavorful and satisfying. Note: The meal is definitely on the "heavier" side. I felt a bit sluggish afterward and wished there were lighter dessert or side options to balance the richness. Still a delicious, high-end experience! (4 stars)

We came at 5 PM on a Wednesday and it was calm and peaceful. The food tasted clean with a focus on the ingredients natural flavor. The chicken was fried very well and it's taste was fairly light with a hint of MSG. The galbi-jjim was tender and youll find yourself dipping it back in the sauce after each bite. Nothing was excessive in flavor which might be a downside for someone expecting heavy pocha style flavors. Even the kimchi wasn't too sour and had a crunch to it. It's unique and healthy, plus the place is gorgeous and a great place for a date. (5 stars)

The interior of Moono is so beautiful and the service and food is always top-tier. I’ve been here twice now, most recently for the restaurant week menu. The chicken is some of the best I’ve had and the Galbi-jjim is so tender. The sides are also phenomenal and all unique. For the restaurant week menu we got the wine pairings as well and I definitely recommend that, they go perfectly with each course. Overall, love this place! I’ve also had the bossam and naengmyeon before which are also good, but I think my favorite dish so far has been the Galbi-jjim! (5 stars)

Stopped by Moono with friends after spending the day in New York City, and it was such a great meal. We ordered Pyongyang-style cold noodles, stir-fried cuttlefish, and mixed sashimi salad, and everything was spot on. The Pyongyang cold noodles had a clean, deeply flavorful broth that was light but satisfying, with great texture on the noodles. The stir-fried cuttlefish was full of smoky flavor, not overly spicy, and went perfectly with rice. The mixed sashimi salad was fresh and well balanced, with bright, refreshing flavors. Overall, the food was thoughtful and well executed, making it perfect for sharing with friends. The atmosphere was relaxed and comfortable, which made it easy to enjoy the meal and spend time together. Definitely a place I’d come back to with friends again. (5 stars)

The ambiance here is perfect for a date night. The food is high-quality and punchy, though the menu leans quite rich. • Spicy Fried Chicken: Perfectly juicy and garlicky. I loved that the sauce was served on the side so the crispiness could shine. • Assorted Pancakes: Great variety; the shrimp was the standout. • Galbi-jjim: Very decadent. Definitely pair this with rice to cut through the richness. • Uni Sotbap: Incredibly flavorful and satisfying. Note: The meal is definitely on the "heavier" side. I felt a bit sluggish afterward and wished there were lighter dessert or side options to balance the richness. Still a delicious, high-end experience! (4 stars) We came at 5 PM on a Wednesday and it was calm and peaceful. The food tasted clean with a focus on the ingredients natural flavor. The chicken was fried very well and it's taste was fairly light with a hint of MSG. The galbi-jjim was tender and youll find yourself dipping it back in the sauce after each bite. Nothing was excessive in flavor which might be a downside for someone expecting heavy pocha style flavors. Even the kimchi wasn't too sour and had a crunch to it. It's unique and healthy, plus the place is gorgeous and a great place for a date. (5 stars) The interior of Moono is so beautiful and the service and food is always top-tier. I’ve been here twice now, most recently for the restaurant week menu. The chicken is some of the best I’ve had and the Galbi-jjim is so tender. The sides are also phenomenal and all unique. For the restaurant week menu we got the wine pairings as well and I definitely recommend that, they go perfectly with each course. Overall, love this place! I’ve also had the bossam and naengmyeon before which are also good, but I think my favorite dish so far has been the Galbi-jjim! (5 stars) Stopped by Moono with friends after spending the day in New York City, and it was such a great meal. We ordered Pyongyang-style cold noodles, stir-fried cuttlefish, and mixed sashimi salad, and everything was spot on. The Pyongyang cold noodles had a clean, deeply flavorful broth that was light but satisfying, with great texture on the noodles. The stir-fried cuttlefish was full of smoky flavor, not overly spicy, and went perfectly with rice. The mixed sashimi salad was fresh and well balanced, with bright, refreshing flavors. Overall, the food was thoughtful and well executed, making it perfect for sharing with friends. The atmosphere was relaxed and comfortable, which made it easy to enjoy the meal and spend time together. Definitely a place I’d come back to with friends again. (5 stars)

bio_text: Muku is a Japanese restaurant in New York City that embodies the philosophy of purity and intention in its culinary offerings. With a focus on seasonality and simplicity, Muku creates a dining experience that is both expressive and respectful of traditional Japanese cuisine. The restaurant's atmosphere is designed to reflect harmony, allowing guests to appreciate the true character of each dish without unnecessary embellishments. Muku specializes in nihonryori, or Japanese cuisine, with a menu that celebrates the five classical techniques of Japanese cooking: raw, grilled, simmered, steamed, and fried. The dishes are crafted with a focus on seasonal ingredients, ensuring that flavors are clear and direct, while also allowing for a quietly inventive approach to traditional recipes. Led by award-winning Chef Manabu Asanuma, who has trained under esteemed masters in Japan and has worked in acclaimed kitchens in New York, Muku represents a culmination of his diverse culinary experiences. Chef Asanuma's journey includes recognition in Japan's RED U-35 competition and a commitment to expressing his philosophy of seasonality and purity in every dish.
menu_items: Kani Gayu - crab, crab broth, rice, salt
Mokuzugani - Japanese mitten crab, binchotan charcoal
Kobako Gani - female snow crab, roe
Yamagata Soba - buckwheat flour
Grilled Eel - eel, sauce
Mizugashi - seasonal fruits, traditional Japanese sweets
review_snippets: It was a very delicious kaiseki meal at Muku. It’s a bit more understated than the other Kaiseki places of a similar price point in terms of presentation and pulling out all the stops. It doesn’t look very fancy but it’s still super delicious. Muku has a more like it was made at home taste but still elevated. Service was good. What stood out to me was the white miso soup, wagyu, crab rice and the orange soda/sake ice cream dessert. But they could’ve served another mini dessert course and given diners a little treats bag to go that all the other restaurants are doing. (4 stars)

Went for the seasonal menu focused on crab, was excellent. Felt no different than a high end kaiseki joint in Japan (aside from price). Standard repertoire of Japanese dishes, with the more unique offerings being the fried tempura dish and the 'hometown' soba. Was very surprised to hear that the chef changes menu monthly, which sounds exhausting from a creativity perspective, but mad respect. Looking forward to trying future menus out for sure. The somm was also 100/10. (5 stars)

I’ve been to Muku twice at this point and chef Asanuma never failed to impress us with their innovative menu. The quality of the food was supreme, the service top notch, and the ambiance cozy and relax. I especially enjoyed the chatter with the chef and the sous chef who came all the way from Japan just for the month. (5 stars)

This is probably the best Kaiseki/Nihonryori style restaurant in NYC. Chef Manabu showcases seasonal flavors in a very balanced and beautiful way. Menu changes almost weekly or biweekly so there is always a pleasant surprise. (5 stars)

bio_text: MáLà Project is a vibrant dining destination that celebrates neo-Sichuanese cuisine, offering a cozy atmosphere perfect for gathering with friends and family. The restaurant's centerpiece is the Málà Dry Pot, where guests can customize their meals with a variety of meats, seafood, and vegetables, all wok-fried in a signature sauce crafted from a complex blend of 24 herbs and spices. Complementing the main offerings, the menu features a selection of Dim Sum, Noodles, and Specialty Rices, alongside a curated drinks menu that includes traditional Chinese beverages and innovative cocktails. MáLà Project specializes in neo-Sichuanese cuisine, focusing on the Málà Dry Pot as the main attraction. The menu is designed for customization, allowing diners to choose from a wide array of ingredients, all enhanced by a unique sauce developed through traditional techniques. MáLà Project was founded with the mission to deliver joy through its culinary offerings, although specific details about the chef or the timeline of opening are not provided.
menu_items: Málà Peanuts - $7
Málà Fries - $12
Málà Pickles - $7
Marinated Cucumbers - $12
Crispy Duck Salad - $26
Eggplant With Roasted Garlic - $12
review_snippets: A great Chinese restaurant offering tasty Sichuan cuisine in a relaxed setting. This is a fairly casual restaurant, but they serve some expertly mad dishes. The dry pot is their specialty and it’s deliciously spicy, fragrant, and mouth-numbing from Sichuan peppers - I strongly recommend you try the dry pot, but the marinated pickles and popcorn chicken were excellent too. They have a great happy hour special where food is discounted (our beer was full price), so take advantage of that before 7pm. (5 stars)

OMG...the endless hunt for authentic mapo tofu is finally over. This is legit mapo tofu. We asked for extra spicy and they did not disappoint. So damn good!! Excellent with their purple rice. We also got their mala dry pot with beef tenderloin, lamb, wood ear, enoki, broccoli, and bean curd sheet, with their extra spicy base of 24 spices. This took me back to my study abroad in China. Absolutely 💯 amazing!!! Super flavorful, bold, and truly authentic. Everything was next level. Drinks were good and pair well with the spicy dishes. Service was friendly and attentive. The atmosphere is cute with their corrugated metal roof ceiling and the exposed brick floor. The haw flakes at the end threw me back to my 90s childhood! Will definitely be coming back for sure! What a treasure! Please don't change. It's hard to find such authentic, truly spicy, quality Sichuan cuisine! (5 stars)

A solid spot for comforting Mala dry pot - the menu is extensive and customizable with plenty of meat and veggie options. I ordered about six items (definitely a bit much for one person) plus a hearty bowl of purple rice. Everything was flavorful with just the right level of spice. Generous portions, great flavors, and an overall satisfying solo dining experience. (5 stars)

First time coming to this establishment, and I must say I was very impressed. I decided to step out of my comfort zone and try new cuisine. My server Cody was very attentive and could tell I was nervous. He took his time to explain the menu to me, recommended some tasty options. The restaurant itself has a great ambience, good music and very cozy. I appreciate the different spice levels they have and you can customize the food to your liking. I will definitely be coming back to try other dishes from the menu. (5 stars)

review_snippets: Good food!! I liked the appetizers better than the temaki, personally. The spicy tuna dip and fried chicken were both great. I loved the salmon sashimi. The rolls were good!! They taste like.. sushi. Idk, I don’t have the most refined fish pallet. One big minus was that the churros didn’t come with enough custard, so we asked for more. And then they charged us extra for it (even though our original serving was really small). The atmosphere is super bright and well lit. They did a great job of timing out our bites. (4 stars)

This place is sleek, the food is fresh, the tamaki counter is a delightful experience - worth every penny! Everything here is gluten free, I couldn't go wrong. I would love to try their Williamsburg, BK location. All of the items we had were fantastic, but we especially loved the salmon! The food was so good, I forgot to take more photos....Sorry! (5 stars)

The food was incredibly fresh and delicious 😍🍻— the flavors were so clean and naturally sweet that I was impressed with every dish. What truly surprised me, and what I can’t stop thinking about, was the wasabi cucumber tataki🥳. Who would have thought that something as simple as a cucumber dish could taste that amazing? I’ll definitely be coming back! (5 stars)

A favorite we go to regularly and for years has never disappointed. So delicious, fish and shellfish quality always fresh, inventive dishes. Highly recommend eating at the counter and getting your tenaki handrolls fresh one by one. Love the fries, the spicy tuna dip, and even the churros. Wonderful staff from the host to the bus people. (5 stars)

bio_text: Neta Shari is a contemporary dining establishment located in Brooklyn, NY, offering a warm and inviting atmosphere for guests. The restaurant emphasizes a commitment to quality and authenticity, providing a unique culinary experience that reflects the vibrant culture of its cuisine. Neta Shari specializes in Japanese cuisine, focusing on sushi and sashimi. The menu features a selection of fresh, high-quality ingredients, prepared with traditional techniques to enhance the natural flavors of each dish.
review_snippets: Hands down my favorite omakase/sushi takeout spot. The fish is so fresh and every single piece is so delightfully delectable that it leaves you craving for more. The customer service is impeccable and and the quality is remarkable! Definitely worth every single penny. Isn't my first time eating from here and definitely won't be my last! P.S. If you choose the omakase option, their black cod is to die for! 😋 (5 stars)

I go here quite often, and I’d have to say it’s always amazing each time I go. The fish is always seasonal so the menu changes slightly depending on what’s in season. The flavors are always new and I always look forward to what new fish they come up with. Each time I leave, I get a satisfying high from the flavors. It’s extraordinary how good this spot is compared to places in Manhattan! Worth the trip if you’re in Brooklyn. I’d highly recommend coming here for a special occasion. This place is reservation only, don’t miss the reservation time! (5 stars)

Came here for the first time for Valentine’s Day dinner and it did not disappoint! Everything was beautifully put together and so delicious. Every piece was fresh. They even gave us complimentary heart shaped uni! 18 courses for 125 is a steal. Will be coming back (5 stars)

Amazing omakase. Had the full course (steam egg cup/chawanmushi + 14 sushi + dessert). The price is a bit steep but it's all worth it. I guess the service can be improved, seems like waiters are a bit new in serving customers. But the food is really delicious which is more important. (5 stars)

review_snippets: I chose this place for my husband's birthday dinner, and the entrance alone set the tone. Walking into the secret space and waiting for the curtain to drop felt like the start of a show! Every single dish was delicious. I’m usually a huge Uni lover, but the other courses here were so outstanding that they stole the show. My personal favorite of the night was definitely the Unagi absolutely amazing. The service was truly next-level. Both the manager and the chef were incredibly attentive and observant; they anticipated our needs without being intrusive. As introverts, we really appreciated how they balanced friendly small talk with giving us space. They really knew how to "read the room" perfectly. A few minor notes: Even though I mentioned it was a birthday celebration, there wasn't a special dessert dish or candle. They did offer a celebratory shot at the end, but since we don't drink alcohol, we missed out on that. Regarding drinks, I had read other reviews mentioning a potential push for alcohol orders (since there are no add-on options), but we didn't feel that pressure at all. As soon as we ordered soft drinks, they immediately took the hint and didn't force anything on us, which we appreciated. Overall, I highly recommend this spot for a delicious Omakase meal and a unique vibe, rather than strictly for a special "event." (5 stars)

No words! We went last night and the whole experience start to finish was an exceptional experience. From the ambiance, the service, the professionalism and quality of food… and sake lol. One of the best omakase experiences I’ve had. And the best in NYC hands down. Can’t wait to go back!! Shout out Tim, chef Noda & Jimmy! You guys are incredible! (5 stars)

This is such a special place — you're in for a treat! We've been coming here for our anniversary for the past two years and it's wow'd us each time. There are only two seatings a day and 8 seats in the entire restaurant, so a very intimate experience. The chef and staff are chatting with you the whole time and are so knowledgeable and talented. They often research their guests as well — they knew all about my partner's work and running hobby. (I guess I was harder to find info on!) The food (as well as sake/wine pairing, which I highly recommend) is SUCH an experience. The best sushi I've had, hands down. Everything is presented so beautifully as well — each new sake and/or wine is brought in a new gorgeous glass. This is always at the top of my recommendation list for friends and family seeking the right spot to celebrate a special occasion. (5 stars)

I had a best experience with this omakase. First, the food was amazing, 20 course menu including sushi and appetizers, all really good, well balanced! Secondly, the service was amazing, chef, bartender, and hosts were all friendly and welcoming and we felt really comfortable and had a good time! Third, atmosphere is amazing! Very unique and I feel like different from other normal sushi omakase for sure! I can’t wait to come back again! (5 stars)

bio_text: Noreetuh is a modern Hawaiian restaurant situated in the East Village of New York City, offering a vibrant and casual dining experience. The restaurant aims to create a welcoming atmosphere where guests can savor artfully crafted dishes paired with an approachable wine list, featuring approximately 300 selections, predominantly from France and Germany. The name 'noreetuh,' meaning 'playground' in Korean, reflects the restaurant's commitment to providing a fun and enjoyable dining environment. Noreetuh specializes in modern Hawaiian cuisine, focusing on fresh, high-quality ingredients and traditional flavors. The menu features a variety of dishes, including musubi, poke, and unique takes on classic Hawaiian fare, presented in a family-style format. Signature techniques include the use of local and seasonal ingredients, as well as innovative preparations that highlight the essence of Hawaiian cooking. Noreetuh is co-owned by Chef Chung Chow and General Manager Jin Ahn, who have crafted a unique dining experience that blends their culinary expertise with a passion for Hawaiian culture.
menu_items: musubi - popular Hawaiian snack made with rice and ingredients wrapped in a sheet of nori seaweed - cut into three bite-sized pieces - $35
caviar supplement - add 15g of ossetra caviar to any musubi - $35
SPAM classic - $6
spicy SPAM - pickled jalapeño, soy mayo - $7
SPAM & cheese - gruyere, mozzarella, dijonnaise - $8
SPAM & kimchi - chipotle mayo - $7
review_snippets: Great food and a great vibe, I actually don’t think Ive been to a dedicated Hawaiian restaurant before so this was really nice! Started with three of the Musubi. The Yellowtail was incredibly fresh with a touch of yuzu that was awesome. The Spicy Salmon was good but kinda standard. The Galbi was stellar, had a nice flavor to the meat and the kimchi delish. Got the Mochiko Chicken Loco Moco. Lots of tastes that work so well together here from the gravy to the breading to the egg. I actually didn’t even realize this had a macaroni salad because I started eating from the rice side so the macaroni was a nice surprise and it was so good. If I had to give one critique though Id say that the breading did not stay on the chicken when you cut into it so it was hard to get both in one bite! Also got dessert because Macademia is my favorite nut but for some reason I never thought to put it in a brownie, so when I saw the Macademia Brownie I knew I had to have it. Brownie itself was fire, it had the taste and texture of a dense brownie but it was not dense itself if that makes sense. Also it came with coconut ice cream but I saw Thai Tea ice cream on the menu and asked for that instead and they provided! DEEEEELISHHHHH that ice cream was perfection. So concentrated and creamy and the perfect thai tea flavor YUM. The vibe inside was curated so well and the playlist was actually really good! (5 stars)

I think we ordered wrong because I thought the food was just okay. The spam misubi and the haupia dessert was our favorites though! Simple and delicious. The loco moco felt different and not in the best way. Katsu and cabbage were just okay. Randomly the cucumbers with the katsu though were phenomenal. The staff was amazing and drinks were fantastic. The vibe was also great. Maybe would order some different plates next time. (3 stars)

Everything at Noreetuh was delicious and super flavorful! The octopus was tender with the perfect amount of spice and char. The poke was fresh, bright, and packed with flavor. The pork was juicy on the inside and crispy on the outside—absolutely delicious. The salmon main had the best miso glaze with just the right sweetness. The crab rice had lovely popping texture and just enough salt. The loco moco was tender and juicy, and the mac salad was delicious too. The desserts were killer: the pineapple upside-down cake was warm and sweet, perfectly paired with ice cream, and the same went for the banana pudding. The drinks were a wonderful balance of sweet and alcohol.Outstanding service made sure allergies were taken serious and very informative. Would recommend 10 out of 10. (5 stars)

Amazing! Huge recommend! I got the kalua pork off the brunch menu and it was perfect! Tender, rich, and smoky (such a strong appetizing aroma!) shredded pork on a bed of rice, accompanied by bright, tangy macaroni salad and premium jidori egg with a creamy yolk. Crunchy cabbage comes to the rescue once you get tired of the soft creamy textures. The salt and acidity felt just right. I normally dislike macaroni salad but I could’ve eaten a tiny bowl of this. The whole time my mind was just bombarded with the word “delicious”. I would not change a thing. Noreetuh has an exciting wine program, clearly curated by someone who loves wine. Drop by here to discover new, interesting wines by the glass like a crisp white Nebbiolo. Much of noreetuh’s menu can be had as bar snacks to pair with the wines. (5 stars)
search_text: Noreetuh Noreetuh is a modern Hawaiian restaurant situated in the East Village of New York City, offering a vibrant and casual dining experience. The restaurant aims to create a welcoming atmosphere where guests can savor artfully crafted dishes paired with an approachable wine list, featuring approximately 300 selections, predominantly from France and Germany. The name 'noreetuh,' meaning 'playground' in Korean, reflects the restaurant's commitment to providing a fun and enjoyable dining environment. Noreetuh specializes in modern Hawaiian cuisine, focusing on fresh, high-quality ingredients and traditional flavors. The menu features a variety of dishes, including musubi, poke, and unique takes on classic Hawaiian fare, presented in a family-style format. Signature techniques include the use of local and seasonal ingredients, as well as innovative preparations that highlight the essence of Hawaiian cooking. Noreetuh is co-owned by Chef Chung Chow and General Manager Jin Ahn, who have crafted a unique dining experience that blends their culinary expertise with a passion for Hawaiian culture. musubi - popular Hawaiian snack made with rice and ingredients wrapped in a sheet of nori seaweed - cut into three bite-sized pieces - $35 caviar supplement - add 15g of ossetra caviar to any musubi - $35 SPAM classic - $6 spicy SPAM - pickled jalapeño, soy mayo - $7 SPAM & cheese - gruyere, mozzarella, dijonnaise - $8 SPAM & kimchi - chipotle mayo - $7 Great food and a great vibe, I actually don’t think Ive been to a dedicated Hawaiian restaurant before so this was really nice! Started with three of the Musubi. The Yellowtail was incredibly fresh with a touch of yuzu that was awesome. The Spicy Salmon was good but kinda standard. The Galbi was stellar, had a nice flavor to the meat and the kimchi delish. Got the Mochiko Chicken Loco Moco. Lots of tastes that work so well together here from the gravy to the breading to the egg. I actually didn’t even realize this had a macaroni salad because I started eating from the rice side so the macaroni was a nice surprise and it was so good. If I had to give one critique though Id say that the breading did not stay on the chicken when you cut into it so it was hard to get both in one bite! Also got dessert because Macademia is my favorite nut but for some reason I never thought to put it in a brownie, so when I saw the Macademia Brownie I knew I had to have it. Brownie itself was fire, it had the taste and texture of a dense brownie but it was not dense itself if that makes sense. Also it came with coconut ice cream but I saw Thai Tea ice cream on the menu and asked for that instead and they provided! DEEEEELISHHHHH that ice cream was perfection. bio_text: Norma Gastronomia Siciliana is an authentic Sicilian restaurant located in the heart of New York City, offering a warm and inviting atmosphere that transports guests to the soul of Sicily. With a focus on traditional Sicilian cuisine, the restaurant prides itself on familial service and a rustic yet elegant ambiance, making it an ideal setting for various dining occasions, from intimate date nights to lively family gatherings. The restaurant specializes in traditional Sicilian cuisine, featuring a menu that highlights authentic dishes and exclusively Sicilian wines. Signature techniques include time-honored cooking methods passed down through generations, ensuring each dish reflects the rich culinary heritage of Sicily. Chef Salvatore Fraterrigo, who grew up in Trapani, Sicily, opened the first location of Norma Gastronomia Siciliana in Murray Hill in 2016, followed by a second location in Hell's Kitchen in 2021. His culinary journey began by learning from his mother and grandmother, and he aims to bring a taste of Sicily to America through his passion for cooking.
menu_items: Arancini - Filled with meaty ragù, peas, mozzarella, and tender rice cooked in chicken stock, presented in a pool of excellent, light tomato sauce. - $16
Rianata Pizza - Traditional pizza from Trapani. - $12
Anelletti al Forno - Baked pasta dish with rich flavors. - $18
Caponata - Sicilian eggplant dish with sweet and sour flavors. - $10
Pasta alla Norma - Pasta with eggplant, tomato sauce, and ricotta salata. - $14
Sicilian Cannoli - Crispy pastry filled with sweet ricotta cheese. - $8
review_snippets: We stopped by for a quick bite and were delighted to discover this little gem while walking around the area. The food is delicious, the Sicilian vibes abound in warmth, and the service was just on point. Loved the combination of four cheeses on the thin-crust pizza, the bruschetta was delicious, the arugula salad mouth-watering, and the Prosecco hit the spot! Definitely coming back when around! (5 stars)

Great Italian Restaurant. We had a waiting time of 15 mins for group of 3 and for 2 people it is relatively faster. The Pizza felt so fresh with Tomatoes and Cheese. Also tried Schrimp Pasta that was delicious as well. The Staff were nice and friendly and ambience is perfect for a cozy dinner. (5 stars)

If I could give Norma a 6 I would. I suffer from severe food allergies and they could not have handled them better. From answering any question I had, to suggestions options of their own, they made me feel safe and at low risk of an allergic reaction. I got the plain margarita pizza, it was very tasty, warm and cleary cooked to perfection. Finally, the atmosphere was so cosy, my only issue would be the music was a tad loud. Otherwise it felt warm, homely, and authentic! Thank you Norma! I will definitely be back! (5 stars)

1 star for the really great food but I do need to leave a poor review for the way they packaged our food to go. They put hot soup in a box and it ended up seeping through on our walk home and all of the food was spoiled from dropping on the floor and being soiled from the broth . This really should not have happened and it's a shame considering we had a lot of left overs . (2 stars)

bio_text: Novità is a beloved trattoria located in the heart of Gramercy, New York City, known for its warm and inviting atmosphere that reflects a deep passion for Italian culture and cuisine. Since its opening in 1994, the restaurant has become a staple in the community, offering a dining experience that celebrates the rich traditions of Italian cooking through seasonal ingredients and authentic recipes. The restaurant specializes in authentic regional Italian cuisine, focusing on seasonal dishes that highlight the flavors of Italy. The menu features a variety of traditional offerings, crafted with a commitment to quality and authenticity. Opened in 1994 by chef Marco Fregonese.
menu_items: Funghi misti - Grilled portobello, shiitake and oyster mushrooms with parmigiano shavings - $21.00
Insalata di caprino - Warm goat cheese with rucola and walnut vinaigrette - $20.00
Funghi ripieni - Pan-fried shiitake mushrooms filled with shrimp and scallions - $24.00
Melanzane alla parmigiana - Breaded baby eggplant baked with tomato, mozzarella and parmigiano - $23.50
Carpaccio di manzo con tartufi neri - Kobe beef carpaccio with rucola, parmigiano and black truffles - $27.50
Insalata di calamari - Calamari salad with rucola, cannellini beans and avocado dressing - $23.50
review_snippets: From the moment we stepped down into the space, we knew we were in for a great experience. The main dining room was filling up, and the buzz felt like classic NYC. Service was warm and immediate…water arrived right away, along with a generous bread basket featuring the best toast sticks (honestly worth mentioning on their own). We started with the eggplant appetizer, which was spot-on: the right balance of tomatoes and fresh mozzarella, and the perfect way to wake up the palate. The wild mushroom salad was equally delicious…earthy, satisfying, and beautifully composed. For mains, we had the pappardelle with lamb ragù. The flavor and texture were excellent, though I was a little surprised to find the lamb was ground rather than shredded. The true standout, though, was the swordfish Milanese…perfectly crisp, not heavy, and made even better by the fresh tomato salad layered on top. We paired it all with a lovely Italian red and finished with tiramisu. All in all, a fantastic evening…the perfect escape from the cold. (4 stars)
Amazing cozy luxury vibe. Service was fast and people are very welcoming. Love the pasta. (4 stars)

Such a beautiful Italian Restaurant about a min walk from the Friends Experience NYC. The atmosphere is incredible. Quiet enough to talk to each other. The waitress is was so nice and attentive. I loved it (5 stars)

Delicious food, good service, nice atmosphere. One thing to watch out for is the additional charge to split a dish. I haven’t come across anything like this before. We wanted to share the chicken dish and we were charged this for splitting. But we didn’t even mean to say we wanted it split as having it on one dish is fine. Just something to look out for since I’m not a fan of the more “hidden” fees. We enjoyed the outdoor seating. The road is not very busy with cars/pedestrians so it was peaceful. The only thing I’d fix is the tables for two were pretty small. Great service from our waiter and the rest of the staff. All outdoor tables were covered by one waiter so I thought he was doing a great job! Food was great. The clam dish was interesting in that it wasn’t a traditional clam sauce as it was pretty light. A bit lacking in flavors because of that The lobster ragu was great. Lots of lobster, good flavors. The pasta here was interesting in that it was very much like lo-mein, kinda odd but thought it was cool The chicken dish was unique with the stuffings. It was a bit dry. The sauce and potatoes were perfect though. The profiteroles were good. Not too sweet and a good mix with the ice cream in the center. Overall, expensive for what it is but I’d be willing to come back to try some of their other dishes (4 stars)

bio_text: Noz 17, located in Chelsea, offers a Michelin-starred dining experience that transports guests to a traditional Japanese sushi-ya, away from the bustling energy of New York City. The restaurant is designed in the Sukiya style, reminiscent of historic tea houses, creating a cozy and tranquil atmosphere enhanced by the aroma of Hinoki wood and soft lighting. Guests are invited to immerse themselves in a memorable omakase experience, where each dish is meticulously prepared by Chef Junichi Matsuzaki at the intimate Hinoki counter. Noz 17 specializes in Edomae-style omakase, featuring a 15-course tasting menu that includes seasonal nigiri, signature miso soup, and a seasonal dessert. The menu is crafted daily with ingredients imported from Japan, showcasing traditional sushi techniques and flavors. Chef Junichi Matsuzaki, born in Chiba, Japan, began his culinary journey as an apprentice at Sushi Yasuda after moving to New York in 2002. He joined the opening team of Sushi Noz in 2018 and was later appointed as the Head Chef for Noz 17, where he has been dedicated to Edomae craft since its inception in 2021.
menu_items: Amuse Bouche
Seasonal Nigiri
Miso Soup
Tamago
Seasonal Dessert
review_snippets: Visiting NYC from Arizona for a business trip and had the opportunity my last night to dine at NOZ 17. Easily the best decision I made during my trip. Incredible hospitality and even better food. My phone was at 12% when I got to the restaurant and the front of house staff was more than happy to take my phone and charge it while dining. With limited space the restaurant feels very intimate and getting to know my fellow guests and chef was a huge highlight. Chef Matsuzaki was very friendly and professional throughout the night, helping guide us through the courses. Hands down the best Scallop and Mackerel I’ve ever had. I look forward to dining at NOZ 17 again with Chef Matsuzaki! (5 stars)

It was an amazing experience. Thanks to Teppei, who made our night unforgettable. The food was absolutely delicious. We went to the private room for four people, and it was excellent. We will definitely come back. (5 stars)
it was my first time having sushi in new york city. overall very delicious and satisfying - my one complaint was that there was no uni :( (4 stars)

In its current iteration, Noz 17 may be the only sub-$250 sushi establishment in NYC worthy of its Michelin star and is certainly one of the finest in the city. It’s clear that Chef Matsu takes great care in both seasonality and balance in his menu, as well as nods to true Edomae tradition throughout. Our meal started with a perfectly cured Kohada (gizzard shad) and ended with a pillowy, custard-like Tamago (egg omelette), both considered traditional measures of a chef’s skill and yet conspicuously absent from so many so-called omakase restaurants in the city. I actually went back a second time almost immediately because of how impressed I was, and both Chef Matsu and Sous Chef Kenta separately delivered an incredible meal of highlight-after-highlight, including delicious cuts of Kasugo (young sea bream) and Aori Ika (bigfin reef squid), and in Chef Matsu’s case a soft shell crab bouillabaisse that was probably the most delicious otsumami I’ve ever had. Subtle details, such as the delicate roasting of the seaweed over charcoal (Jiro-style, one might say), are where the magic lies. The meal does have some limitations, namely the absence of any significant amount of bluefin tuna (I received only a single piece of chutoro over the course of two meals, and wasn’t particularly blown away) and a high charge of $25 per piece for extra orders. That being said, if you’re looking for a traditional Edomae-style establishment in a serene environment that won’t serve you a blowtorched wagyu-uni-caviar monstrosity or insultingly half-sized nigiri pieces, as seems to be increasingly the norm these days, you can stop searching as I don’t think you’ll find much better and certainly not for under $200. Thank you Noz 17 for keeping the art alive and (relatively) accessible. I look forward to hopefully returning soon! (5 stars)

bio_text: Nudibranch is a vibrant dining destination in New York City that celebrates the playful and bold nature of food. Drawing inspiration from a scuba trip in Indonesia, the restaurant embodies the diversity and character of its namesake, the nudibranch sea slug. Since its inception as a pop-up in 2021 and subsequent opening as a brick-and-mortar establishment in 2022, Nudibranch has quickly gained recognition, being featured in prestigious lists such as Esquire’s Best New Restaurants in America and the Michelin Guide. Nudibranch focuses on a unique fusion of Korean and Spanish cuisines, creating colorful and experimental dishes that reflect the dynamic culinary landscape of New York City. The menu is designed to be ever-evolving, showcasing the chefs' creativity and commitment to bold flavors. Nudibranch started as a pop-up in 2021, made possible by the support of friends and industry professionals, and opened its brick-and-mortar location in 2022. Chef Jeffrey Kim and Chef Matthew Lee, both with extensive backgrounds in renowned kitchens, co-founded the restaurant.
review_snippets: Total Gem. From the moment you walk in, the staff makes you feel genuinely welcome. The atmosphere strikes a perfect balance—versatile enough for an intimate date, a solo dinner, or a lively group gathering. While he frog legs, soba noodles, and mushrooms were all expertly prepared, the beets in cashew ajo blanco were an absolute revelation. The wine list is equally thoughtful; I tried a Chilean Orange Semillon that was completely eye-opening. I love the cohesive perspective here—the food, wine, service, and decor all feel intentional. I'm looking forward to trying other dishes on their menu. Highly recommended. (5 stars)

If I could, I'd give 4.5 stars, and the only reason I'm holding back is because this place was great but we ordered a limited amount. The interior is cute and comfortable and all the servers were attentive and knowledgable. We had a reservation and had no issues being seated immediately. We started with the hamachi which was 10/10 delicious. Light and refreshing and a great start to the meal. I'll admit the chicken sandwich was bigger than we anticipated and could absolutely be a meal on its own. We split it, pretending it might be too large to finish but it was too good not to. I will say the pork chop was the star of the show. This was so good that I watched my husband gnaw at the remains, not wanting to leave anything behind. The kimchi was nothing to phone home about but good, and the scallion pancake was absolutely a notch above the rest. We didn't plan on getting dessert, but the masala chai tres leches looked too good to pass up and we left nothing behind. It was rich, cinnamon-y, and super satisfying in texture. I will be dreaming about that cake! We agreed we would return at some point, and should we have a similar experience, I will bump this to 5 stars! (4 stars)

Pretty good! I liked the celery salad the most, and the duck croquettes. I found some dishes missing somethings, though it was all still good. The frog legs were a bit salty and over battered for my taste, really tasted like old bay which I don't love. The pork chop was really good I just wish they put more sauce and a little bit more vegetable vegetables because splitting one mushroom and one small piece of bok choy was a little annoying especially because it was so delicious there should've been more of it. Sea bream was yummy. Really liked the coconut semifreddo, really well balanced with sweet tart creamy and pepper. Refreshing and a great way to end the meal not too sweet at all. Really like the ambience, nice wooden furniture, good art, great lighting, good volume level. (4 stars)

We ordered the course, and all the foods were very flavorful and the portion was decent. It was two ppl and with 4 drinks, (2 wines + 1 cocktail + 1 beer) it cost 200+ w/o tax. Personally the entrees were better than the main, and the dessert was amazing too. The entrees were 5 stars, amazing and I would love to come back for those, and please try the beer and wine, they were good. Cocktail was alright. (4 stars)
search_text: Nudibranch Nudibranch is a vibrant dining destination in New York City that celebrates the playful and bold nature of food. Drawing inspiration from a scuba trip in Indonesia, the restaurant embodies the diversity and character of its namesake, the nudibranch sea slug. Since its inception as a pop-up in 2021 and subsequent opening as a brick-and-mortar establishment in 2022, Nudibranch has quickly gained recognition, being featured in prestigious lists such as Esquire’s Best New Restaurants in America and the Michelin Guide. Nudibranch focuses on a unique fusion of Korean and Spanish cuisines, creating colorful and experimental dishes that reflect the dynamic culinary landscape of New York City. The menu is designed to be ever-evolving, showcasing the chefs' creativity and commitment to bold flavors. Nudibranch started as a pop-up in 2021, made possible by the support of friends and industry professionals, and opened its brick-and-mortar location in 2022. Chef Jeffrey Kim and Chef Matthew Lee, both with extensive backgrounds in renowned kitchens, co-founded the restaurant. Total Gem. From the moment you walk in, the staff makes you feel genuinely welcome. The atmosphere strikes a perfect balance—versatile enough for an intimate date, a solo dinner, or a lively group gathering. While he frog legs, soba noodles, and mushrooms were all expertly prepared, the beets in cashew ajo blanco were an absolute revelation. The wine list is equally thoughtful; I tried a Chilean Orange Semillon that was completely eye-opening. I love the cohesive perspective here—the food, wine, service, and decor all feel intentional. I'm looking forward to trying other dishes on their menu. Highly recommended. (5 stars) If I could, I'd give 4.5 stars, and the only reason I'm holding back is because this place was great but we ordered a limited amount. The interior is cute and comfortable and all the servers were attentive and knowledgable. We had a reservation and had no issues being seated immediately. We started with the hamachi which was 10/10 delicious. Light and refreshing and a great start to the meal. I'll admit the chicken sandwich was bigger than we anticipated and could absolutely be a meal on its own. We split it, pretending it might be too large to finish but it was too good not to. I will say the pork chop was the star of the show. This was so good that I watched my husband gnaw at the remains, not wanting to leave anything behind. The kimchi was nothing to phone home about but good, and the scallion pancake was absolutely a notch above the rest. We didn't plan on getting dessert, but the masala chai tres leches looked too good to pass up and we left nothing behind. It was rich, cinnamon-y, and super satisfying in texture. I will be dreaming about that cake! We agreed we would return at some point, and should we have a similar experience, I will bump this to 5 stars! (4 stars) Pretty good! I liked the celery salad the most, and the duck croquettes. I found some dishes missing somethings, though it was all still good. The frog legs were a bit salty and over battered for my taste, really tasted like old bay which I don't love. The pork chop was really good I just wish they put more sauce and a little bit more vegetable vegetables because splitting one mushroom and one small piece of bok choy was a little annoying especially because it was so delicious there should've been more of it. Sea bream was yummy. Really liked the coconut semifreddo, really well balanced with sweet tart creamy and pepper. Refreshing and a great way to end the meal not too sweet at all. Really like the ambience, nice wooden furniture, good art, great lighting, good volume level. (4 stars) We ordered the course, and all the foods were very flavorful and the portion was decent. It was two ppl and with 4 drinks, (2 wines + 1 cocktail + 1 beer) it cost 200+ w/o tax. Personally the entrees were better than the main, and the dessert was amazing too. The entrees were 5 stars, amazing and I would love to come back for those, and please try the beer and wine, they were good. Cocktail was alright. (4 stars)

bio_text: Nyonya is a hidden gem in the heart of New York City, specializing in authentic Malaysian-Chinese cuisine. The restaurant boasts a casual ambiance, making it an ideal spot for families and friends to gather. With a diverse menu featuring traditional dishes like Roti Canai and Hainanese Chicken, Nyonya is dedicated to providing a unique dining experience characterized by flavorful food and attentive service. Nyonya focuses on Malaysian-Chinese cuisine, offering a wide range of traditional dishes. The menu includes favorites such as Roti Canai, Curry Mixed Vegetables in a Clay Pot, and Hainanese Chicken, showcasing signature techniques like clay pot cooking and flavorful stir-fries.
menu_items: Roti Canai - Indian pancake - $8.00
Roti Telur - $9.75
Roti Prata - $7.95
Pasembur - $11.50
Nyonya Rojak - $10.95
Nyonya Satay - $16.95
review_snippets: Great Malaysian food with great flavor and prices! Avoid getting seated at the two tables next to the entrance window - it was really cold :’) Would def come back tho With tip, it was $25 for 3 people. - Roti canai: 11/10, the roti was SO crispy (ASMR level). The curry dipping sauce was so flavorful. MUST GET - Beef rendang: 11/10, fav dish. So flavorful, and the beef was so tender. MUST GET - Pineapple fried rice: 8/10, I’m not usually a fan of getting fried rice, esp at restaurants, but this was surprisingly so good!! There could be more pineapple tho. Would get it again! - Hainanese chicken (1/2): 7/10, not sure I’m the biggest fan, but my friends really liked it. I didn’t expect there to be cartilage but there was some. The 1/2 portion was very large for 3 people, could’ve gotten 1/4. The sauce it came with was okay *Note: They’re cash only (5 stars)

We ordered Crispy Pork Intestines , a bit smelly, but crispy and yum ! Shrimp Puff was so good, Roti Canai and Nyonya Satay were yummy as well. For entree we ordered a lot such as Penang Asam Laksa was yummy. This on was recommended. Steamed fish has a slightly fishy smell but sauce was good. And my favorite was Hainanese Chicken with Rice Chicken rice subtly flavored with steamed chicken with bone come with delicious sauce, We all love this menu so much. Fried Bun with condensed milk, were so good ! Love it. This restaurant so wide , staff friendly and helpful. Specifically, my friend have shrimp allergy , He try to explain and ask for awareness the dish that contains with shrimp in ingredients. Nice!! (4 stars)

been craving malaysian food lately and nyonya seriously hit the spot. everything was sooo flavorful and such a good value. the satay was cooked perfectly and the peanut sauce was extra creamy and savory. the roti canai was perfectly crisp on the outside with the best curry for dipping. i also loved the pearl noodle dish and as a noodle girly, this one gets my full approval. the water spinach had such a great umami flavor, and you absolutely can’t miss the hainanese chicken. so tender, so flavorful, and paired perfectly with the chicken broth rice. overall, a must check out malay spot if you’re craving comforting and homey meals (5 stars)

Lucky to get reservation for a fairly big group for a Sunday lunch. This is a Michelin Guide Malaysian restaurant. Great food and good service. I love that they gave me condensed milk for my roti! Must try the coconut rice. Note it’s cash only! (4 stars)

bio_text: Nōksu is an exclusive 15-seat tasting counter located 20 feet underground in the Herald Square Subway Station, offering a unique dining experience that captures the essence of New York City. The restaurant features a meticulously crafted 10-course menu predominantly focused on seafood, showcasing the finest finned fish, shellfish, and a single savory livestock course, all praised for their exceptional quality and creativity. Nōksu specializes in a seafood-centric tasting menu that highlights fresh and innovative dishes. The culinary approach emphasizes seasonal ingredients and unique flavor combinations, with signature techniques that include intricate preparations and presentations. Noksu is a 2024 & 2025 Michelin star recipient.
menu_items: Rice Flower Shrimp Tartare - Gochujang, Lime - $255
Butterfly Mackerel - Horseradish, Brown Rice Vinegar Custard - $255
Peekytoe Crab - Kristal Caviar, Foie - $255
Pine Smoked Katsuo - Oscietra Caviar, Avocado, Radish - $255
Sujebi - Zucchini, Clam, Anchovy Broth - $255
Ocean Trout - Husk Cherry, Elderflower, Dill - $255
review_snippets: I’ve had Noksu on my must-try list since they first opened, so expectations were understandably high. We finally visited for an early Valentine’s Day + anniversary dinner, and unfortunately, the experience didn’t quite live up to the expectation—or the price. The meal itself felt very light. Even as light eaters, my boyfriend and I left hungry, despite ordering add-ons. For a tasting menu at this price point, we expected to feel at least satisfied. Service was inconsistent and, at times, disappointing. When I asked one of the sommeliers for a sweeter drink option, I was simply told to choose from the mocktails—without any recommendations or guidance while giving me a stinky face and left straight away. Another sommelier later made up for this by offering to turn the mocktails into alcoholic drinks, which I appreciated. One moment that stood out was during dessert, when the head chef made rounds to speak with every other table except ours. I'm not sure why—whether it was because we looked younger, or because earlier in the meal I had sent back a dish due to a visible fuzz/fiber (likely from a towel) in my food. Instead of remaking the entire dish, the kitchen moved the burdock vegetables and short rib onto a new plate and gave me fresh rice. While I appreciated the acknowledgment, I wasn’t entirely comfortable with how it was handled. Food-wise, some dishes were stronger than others. For example, the rice flour dish with shrimp tartare really relied on the uni add-on to bring out depth and flavor—we both felt it would have been quite flat without it. Overall, while there were highlights, the experience fell short of expectations given the cost. Between the portion sizes, uneven service, and how certain situations were handled, it didn’t feel like the value matched the price. I truly wanted to love this meal, but left feeling more disappointed than impressed. (3 stars)

A Hidden Gem Beneath the City Nōksu Delivers a True Fine Dining Experience Dining at Nōksu was a memorable experience. Tucked away in a rather unexpected location, beneath the subway I’ll admit I was a little hesitant at first. But once inside, all worries disappeared. The atmosphere is elegant and intimate, a hidden gem that feels worlds away from the busy city above. The service was impeccable from start to finish. Staff were attentive without being intrusive, and every course was presented with precision and care. The space itself was also immaculately clean everything from the tableware to the open kitchen reflected a clear commitment to excellence. The food was beautifully crafted and thoughtfully plated, a level that absolutely speaks to Michelin star quality. Each dish felt balanced, creative, and expertly executed. We opted for the premium wine pairing, which turned out to be an excellent decision. The selections were not only well matched to the menu but also diverse and exciting including a standout sake that paired perfectly with one of the courses. Overall, Nōksu offers a refined and elevated dining experience that goes far beyond its unconventional location. It's a perfect example of how incredible things can be found in the most unexpected places. Highly recommended for those seeking a sophisticated, modern take on fine dining in NYC. (4 stars)

Excellent dining experience. Food was extremely delicious, with depths of rich flavors. Watching the smooth flow of teamwork in the open kitchen was quite impressive; attention to detail, efficiency of movement and immaculate cleanliness was quite evident. The space is very elegant and service was perfect: professional but not cold, attentive but not overly so, very welcoming. The plating of the dishes was also elegant, but not as “jewel box art” as I was expecting from the website photos. A very minor quibble that did not detract at all from our wonderful experience. Highly recommend. (5 stars)

This restaurant honestly deserves more than one Michelin star!!!! From the beautiful interior to the stunning plating, everything was amazing—and the food tasted absolutely heavenly. Even the word “luxury” feels too small for this place. If anyone asks me for a Michelin restaurant recommendation in New York, this would be my number one pick without hesitation. For a special day with a special person, you really don’t need to think twice about where to go. It was the happiest birthday meal I could have asked for, and one I’ll never forget. I’m already trying to book another reservation soon. It was even better than I expected. (5 stars)
