bio_text: Oceans is a seafood restaurant that embodies a blend of local and global influences, offering a timeless and approachable dining experience. Located in the heart of New York City, the restaurant features a menu crafted by Executive Chef Andy Kitko, showcasing the freshest seafood from the Pacific, Atlantic, and Mediterranean shores, complemented by seasonal ingredients. The ambiance is designed to be elegant yet welcoming, making it an ideal destination for both casual diners and special occasions. Oceans specializes in seafood, sushi, and a raw bar experience. The menu is inspired by various coastal cuisines and emphasizes the use of locally and globally sourced ingredients. Signature techniques include a focus on simplicity and freshness, allowing the natural flavors of the seafood to shine. Founded by Vancouver’s award-winning Toptable Group, Oceans is led by Executive Chef Andy Kitko, who has a rich background in esteemed kitchens and Michelin-starred restaurants. Kitko's passion for seafood-focused cuisine was honed during his tenure at New York’s Estiatorio Milos.
menu_items: OYSTERS - East and West - $2
SHELFISH PLATEAU - For One - $35
SALMON AVOCADO ROLL - $15
SPICY TUNA ROLL - $15
TSUNAMI - $18
FRIES - $8
review_snippets: One of the Best Seafood Spots in NYC! From the moment we walked in, the hostess set the stage for an amazing dinner experience—so professional and pleasant. The service was top-notch, with an incredibly attentive staff. A special shout-out to the gentleman from Bangladesh, who made sure everything was perfect throughout the evening. I dined with a friend, and we started with oysters—fresh from the ocean (pun totally intended!) and absolutely delicious. For my main course, I had the Pandora fish as a substitute for red snapper, and it was outstanding, beautifully presented. My friend chose the black cod, another excellent choice with incredible flavor and freshness. The restaurant has the vibe of a high-end spot, reminiscent of its Michelin star in 2022. I’ll happily recommend Oceans to friends and family visiting from out of town as a fantastic option for something special beyond the usual holiday dinner. Can’t wait to go back—this is a must-visit! (5 stars)

A good restaurant with a few standouts food-wise in a nice setting. BUT be careful leaving the place, those steps are a little tricky with or without cocktails. Typical NYC restaurant: NOT GREAT but good. EXCEPT- THE SUSHI ROLLS were EXCELLENT. Spicy Tuna and ROCKETMAN were A+. In addition, there are a few dishes that were outstanding. My family had oyster rights in the Chesapeake Bay and I understand the business and what to look for in a good oyster. Here last night THE OYSTERS were succulent and tasty. They were spot on. Another dish that the chef knocked out of the park was the WAGYU steak. Moreover, the bar sent out two solid cocktails. In the other hand, The big no no of the evening was the CAESAR salad. They would have been better off serving bottled dressing. This salad was tasteless and I did not eat it. They kindly took it off the menu. But the major disappointment for me was THE DOVER SOLE- DO NOT ORDER. THEY would have been better off serving a lemon butter sauce. Their sauce was a sauce. It was there, you could see it all over the plate but it added nothing to the sole. It was not a perfect marriage. I specifically came here because of the sole. Sadly, now don’t cringe when I say this. It was soulless. I have a rule about eating out and I eat out a lot. I hate returning anything but since the waiter realized that I was not going to finish the salad and neither was my guess he said he would take it off the bill. Now, after that do you really think I would send back the sole. No way plus it’s expensive. A restaurant doesn’t have much invested in a salad but they would with the sole . The finale those hot or not hot donuts they serve with sauces did not end the evening with a highlight. Even the flavor of the sauces were limp. Those donuts remind me of our cook as a child. She would roll up left over dough into balls and deep fry them and she placed in a paper bag with cinnamon and sugar and tossed them around. Actually in an emergency for a quick breakfast before crabbing she took canned biscuits and did the same thing. Hers had a little more zip than those served at OCEANS. Sadly it was the service that I could not figure out…… I still am puzzled why they served the wine that was ordered for dinner was brought out, placed on the table almost at the time we received our drinks. There was no tasting, it was just placed on the table. The service lacked coordination and consistency. Maybe Tuesday night is not their A game but for roughly 400 dollars for two we deserve the A GAME. In conclusion, I would stick to the sushi! (4 stars)

A restaurant with high ceilings and nice decor. The service was impeccable and friendly from the moment we arrived. Brian, our server, was extremely pleasant and helpful in explaining the menu and in accommodating our dietary requirements. We couldn't have asked for better service. He recommended the squid ink risotto with king crab meat and white truffles as one of our main courses and the dish was delicious. The mushroom soup was tasty with a rich and intense flavour. The crab cake starter was delicious with chunks of fresh crab meat and minimal binders. The Hokkaido scallops were fresh and cooked just right (crispy crust and tender inside). The Molten cake dessert was super yummy. (5 stars)

The food is absolutely delicious. Their filet mignon is one of the best in NYC, and this was my third visit because of it. Their seafood is incredibly fresh, and the black cod is just so good. But the service… I was expecting much better for a restaurant of this quality. It’s almost sad that they seem to have plenty of staff, yet it still feels understaffed. It’s hard to get ahold of a server for anything except when placing the initial order and when paying the bill. I noticed other tables having the same issue, trying to flag down any server who walked by to clear plates or order something extra. Once the food arrives, the servers seem to pay far less attention to the tables. We found ourselves trying to catch our server’s eye just to ask for something, and eventually we gave up on ordering more. I revisited solely because of the food which was worth it. After three tries, I think that’s enough. I don’t think I’ll be back. (4 stars)

We couldn't have asked for better service. He recommended the squid ink risotto with king crab meat and white truffles as one of our main courses and the dish was delicious. The mushroom soup was tasty with a rich and intense flavour. The crab cake starter was delicious with chunks of fresh crab meat and minimal binders. The Hokkaido scallops were fresh and cooked just right (crispy crust and tender inside). The Molten cake dessert was super yummy. (5 stars) The food is absolutely delicious. Their filet mignon is one of the best in NYC, and this was my third visit because of it. Their seafood is incredibly fresh, and the black cod is just so good. But the service… I was expecting much better for a restaurant of this quality. It’s almost sad that they seem to have plenty of staff, yet it still feels understaffed. It’s hard to get ahold of a server for anything except when placing the initial order and when paying the bill. I noticed other tables having the same issue, trying to flag down any server who walked by to clear plates or order something extra. Once the food arrives, the servers seem to pay far less attention to the tables. We found ourselves trying to catch our server’s eye just to ask for something, and eventually we gave up on ordering more. I revisited solely because of the food which was worth it. After three tries, I think that’s enough. I don’t think I’ll be back. (4 stars)

bio_text: OCTO is a distinguished Korean-Chinese restaurant located in the vibrant heart of New York City. The establishment aims to create a unique dining experience that transcends traditional restaurant boundaries, inviting guests to relive cherished memories through food while exploring elevated authenticity in Korean-Chinese cuisine. With an elegant and comfortable dining room setting, OCTO fosters a nurturing environment for both its team members and guests, embodying the essence of community and growth. OCTO specializes in Korean-Chinese cuisine, celebrating classic dishes that have evolved since the late 19th century in Korea. The menu features a blend of traditional favorites alongside unique signature desserts and cocktails, ensuring a rich and diverse culinary experience. OCTO was inspired by the high demand for Chinese dishes uniquely developed in Korea and aims to honor the rich history and traditional foundations of Korean-Chinese cuisine.

review_snippets: Nice interior spot that has attentive service. But food is nowhere close to being worth for the price point. Malatang is extremely spicy and inedible. Tangsuyuk was all fried batter and no protein, sauce consistency was entirely corn starch. Restaurant was empty, theres much better options nearby. Sad to be called korean food charged at this price point. (1 stars)

It’s hard to come by a place that does good jjajangmyun, jjamppong, AND tangsuyook, but Octo does all three really well for a reasonable price. This is definitely my new go-to spot for my Korean-Chinese food cravings. We split those three dishes between two people and were completely full with plenty leftover, so portions are pretty generous. (5 stars)

Had a really nice dinner at Octo on a friday night. Booked for two people and we were able to be in the private room. Soup dumplings were delicious, duck was so tender and the skin was crispy. Jjajangmyeon and jjambbong were very very good. I will go back to try other dishes for lunch as well. Thank you! (5 stars)

Amazing private dining experience on a Tuesday night in their Starry Night room (fits 12 people). I had a wonderful time working with Hazel and Christina over email, and Hazel + staff on the night of the dinner. Food was fantastic, we were all so full half way through the prix fixe meal. One of our guests was vegetarian so did the vegetarian prix fixe menu, another guest was allergic to nut/sesame (including nut and sesame oil) so ending up choosing some options off the normal menu. They are so accommodating and easy to work with. I will definitely be back. (5 stars)

bio_text: Odo is a sophisticated dining establishment located in a hidden speakeasy setting, where Chef Hiroki Odo presents a contemporary interpretation of traditional Kaiseki cuisine. The restaurant embodies a unique blend of cultural exchange and culinary innovation, providing guests with an exceptional dining experience that emphasizes seasonal ingredients and meticulous preparation. Odo specializes in Kaiseki, a traditional Japanese multi-course meal that adheres to established culinary rules. The menu features thoughtfully curated dishes made from seasonal ingredients sourced from trusted local fishermen, butchers, and farmers. Chef Odo's signature techniques focus on freshness and authenticity, ensuring each dish reflects the highest standards of Kaiseki cuisine. Chef Hiroki Odo, originally from Kagoshima Prefecture, Japan, trained at Kyoto Wakuden and later helped launch Yakumo Saryo in Tokyo. After moving to New York in 2012 and earning a Michelin Star at Kajitsu, he opened Odo in 2018, which received its first Michelin star in 2020 and two stars in 2023. Odo is part of a series of unique establishments created by Chef Odo, including Odo Lounge and Odo East Village.

review_snippets: I’m already thinking of going back—yes! I love their attention to detail. They don’t overload the dishes with seasoning or sauces, and each course is prepared with the freshest ingredients and exceptional skill. From start to finish, the entire meal was outstanding. Their service and the thoughtful descriptions of each course were impossible to miss. They truly bring Japan to NYC. I would say they’re on their way to becoming a three-star restaurant, slowly but surely. (5 stars)

A 2 Michelin star restaurant that deserves it’s 3rd star! Chef Hiroki Odo orchestrates the most wonderful symphony of tastes I’ve ever had. All in a Zen atmosphere!! If you can try it, will not disappoint! Also the. Manu changes every month. Bravo 👏 Odo is a highly-regarded, Michelin-starred Japanese restaurant in NYC by Chef Hiroki Odo, known for its traditional kaiseki (multi-course) dining, emphasizing seasonal ingredients and precise execution, with a new, more casual "kaiseki-izakaya" concept, Odo East Village, recently opening. The original Odo offers an intimate, high-end experience, while the new East Village location blends kaiseki artistry with izakaya warmth, focusing on rice and offering a gluten-free menu. (5 stars)

Odo Omakase: Our Anniversary Odo is a triptych of transformation, and my boyfriend and I experienced its magic firsthand for our one-year anniversary. We entered from the bustling New York street, taxis whizzing by, and found ourselves immediately transported to Shibuya. The lively bar, crowded and convivial, felt like a hidden gem you'd stumble upon after midnight in Tokyo, filled with the energy of collective catharsis. But this was merely the threshold, a tantalizing hint of what was to come. As luck would have it – and fortune is indeed the operative word for securing a reservation here – we were invited through a secret back wall. This antechamber revealed the omakase counter, where the true alchemy began. Under the chef's meticulous hands, raw ingredients were transformed into small miracles. We watched in awe as each delicate piece of uni was prepared, a beautiful balance of sea and subtle sweetness. The premium drink pairing, which we gratefully indulged in, began its journey here, perfectly setting the stage for the culinary wonders ahead. Then, the third layer. Past the antechamber, we were led to a more intimate setting, reclining in unexpected luxury. This giving over of our body’s usual dining posture felt indulgent and special. What followed was a symphony of brilliance and fun, that rare combination where technical mastery doesn't preclude joy. Each dish of our set menu, particularly the melt-in-your-mouth Wagyu, was a testament to this philosophy. (5 stars)

My husband booked a lunch tasting at Odo to celebrate my birthday, and the experience was wonderful. The food and service were both amazing, and we also learned some new and interesting facts about kaiseki cuisine. Every course was delicious, and we truly felt it was worth the price. It was a memorable birthday lunch at Odo. (5 stars)

review_snippets: the prix-fixe menu was such a good deal!! there 4 courses and you get very different flavor throughout each course, i so so enjoyed it. i think the bibimbap with oysters at the end with the warm soup was a very filling, warm ending to the whole experience. staffs were the cutest too!! (5 stars)

I visited Odre NYC with my family to celebrate my mother’s birthday, and it was one of those rare meals that stay with you long after the night ends. We had come for the summer menu a few months ago and were so impressed that we decided to return for this special occasion. What moved us the most was the thoughtful gesture at the end of the meal—Odre replaced the final course’s soup with miyeok-guk, the traditional Korean birthday seaweed soup. It was unexpected, deeply considerate, and genuinely touching. What sets Odre apart is its ability to surprise even someone like me, who grew up with Korean cuisine. The menu is consistently fresh, inventive, and remarkably harmonious, offering combinations I would never think of, yet they come together flawlessly. Every course is plated with precision and beauty, but beyond aesthetics, the flavors and textures are balanced at a level that’s rare to find. The seasonal sotbap bibimbap and broth course—which changes throughout the year—remains one of my favorite endings to any tasting menu in New York. The care put into the rice, the depth of flavor, and the comforting warmth of the soup always feel like the perfect conclusion. On this visit, it became even more meaningful with the birthday miyeok-guk. Desserts such as the sweet potato cheesecake and persimmon shaved ice were equally thoughtful and beautifully executed. Every dish felt intentional, refined, and full of quiet confidence. It’s honestly hard to believe Odre hasn’t received a Michelin star yet, given the consistency, creativity, and heart in every part of the experience. This restaurant continues to be one of the most memorable and inspiring places to dine in New York. (5 stars)

Dining at ODRE was one of those experiences that stays with you long after you leave the table. From the first bite to the last, it genuinely felt like I was experiencing Korean cuisine in a way that was both deeply familiar and completely new at the same time. The dishes were undeniably Korean at heart, but each one carried a sense of creativity and refinement that made them feel truly special — not something you can easily find elsewhere. This felt like ODRE’s story of Korean food, not a copy of tradition, but a thoughtful and respectful evolution of it 🌿 What impressed me most was how delicate and precise every flavor was. The seasoning across all dishes was incredibly balanced — nothing too salty, nothing too heavy. Everything tasted clean, fresh, and intentional, making the entire meal feel surprisingly light and comfortable. I never felt overwhelmed, only curious and excited for the next dish ✨ The namul dishes especially stood out. Their flavors were unmistakably Korean — earthy, subtle, and familiar — yet presented in a way that felt elevated and modern. It brought a quiet sense of nostalgia while still feeling fresh and refined, which honestly isn’t easy to pull off. The white wine pairing was another highlight 🍷 The brightness and acidity of the wine complemented the dishes beautifully, enhancing the freshness of the ingredients and the subtle seasoning rather than overpowering them. It felt like the food and wine were in constant conversation with each other. Beyond the food, the atmosphere of the restaurant added so much to the experience. The space feels calm, intimate, and thoughtfully designed, allowing you to slow down and truly focus on what’s in front of you. It’s the kind of place where you naturally end up lingering a little longer, savoring each moment. Overall, ODRE offers more than just a great meal — it offers a unique, one-of-a-kind experience of Korean cuisine in New York. Refined but warm, innovative but respectful, and above all, deeply satisfying. A place I’d happily return to, and one I’d recommend without hesitation 🤍 (5 stars)

My husband and I came here for the first time to try their winter pre-fix menu. (it was worth it). I'm so glad we came because the food was delicious and was just on another level compared to what you get to try at normal restaurants. The presentation was beautiful, and the food tasted just as good as it looked! The staff was all super nice and friendly as well, and everything was prepared pretty timely. They really go out of their way to make you feel special and welcome. We HIGHLY recommend the Abalone Mandoo, Citrus Shrimp Naengchae, the Jokpyun, and the Jujube Tea! (5 stars)

bio_text: Oiji Mi is a contemporary Korean dining establishment located in the Flatiron district of New York City, offering a unique and creative culinary experience. Under the leadership of Owner and Executive Chef Brian Kim, the restaurant reinterprets traditional Korean flavors into a modern context, creating an inviting atmosphere that embodies the Korean concept of 'jeong'—a warm feeling of love and attachment. The dining experience at Oiji Mi is designed to make guests feel at home, with a focus on hospitality that resonates through the food, service, and ambiance. Oiji Mi specializes in contemporary Korean cuisine, presenting a fresh take on traditional flavors. The restaurant features a 5-course Prix-Fixe menu in the Main Dining Room, while an a la carte menu is available in the Bar & Lounge, showcasing the evolution of familiar tastes through creative culinary techniques. Oiji Mi is an evolution of the original Oiji restaurant, which opened in 2015 in the East Village and became a beloved staple for refined Korean dining. Chef Brian Kim, who has a rich background in diverse culinary cultures, aims to elevate the original concept with this new venture.

review_snippets: This place is fantastic! Every dish was thoughtfully designed and executed. The flavors were on point and I still dream of that ouji bowl. One of things I really liked about their tasting menu was each course came with option so my wife and I could try so many dishes instead of both of u as getting the same meal. Also, service and our server were very attentive and knowledgeable. Will def go back. (5 stars)

We celebrated our 11th wedding anniversary here and the experience was absolutely fantastic. We arrived a little earlier than our booked time, but our table was already ready and we were warmly accommodated, which set the tone for the evening. The service was excellent throughout, and the food was outstanding — very tasty, beautifully presented, and genuinely artistic. We went with their 7-course holiday special, and every single course ranked highly, making it a memorable dining experience from start to finish. A special mention for the thoughtful gesture at the end: we were surprised with house-made mini cupcakes, beautifully plated with a handwritten note celebrating our anniversary. That personal touch truly made the night extra special. An unforgettable experience and a perfect place for celebrating meaningful occasions. Highly recommended. (5 stars)

Opted for a la carte bc I heard there’s some misses in the tasting. Everything we got was great. Lobster ramyun was simple but done well, but my fav dish was probably the sea bass and clams with truffle seafood broth; it was so rich and flavorful (5 stars)

Elevated Korean to its finest! I can't even begin to tell you how amazing the food was. We had the most decadent food and only ate at the bar. The bartender gave us wonderful suggestions on what to order as well as attentive service. We can not wait to try the formal dining room or Bo. The beet tartare on toast was delicate and delicious. The chili lobster ramyun had the most velvety flavors. The Oiji bowl with sea urchin was phenomenal. There was so much thought put into these bites and gorgeous presentation. Highly recommend trying. (5 stars)

One of things I really liked about their tasting menu was each course came with option so my wife and I could try so many dishes instead of both of u as getting the same meal. Also, service and our server were very attentive and knowledgeable. Will def go back. (5 stars) We celebrated our 11th wedding anniversary here and the experience was absolutely fantastic. We arrived a little earlier than our booked time, but our table was already ready and we were warmly accommodated, which set the tone for the evening. The service was excellent throughout, and the food was outstanding — very tasty, beautifully presented, and genuinely artistic. We went with their 7-course holiday special, and every single course ranked highly, making it a memorable dining experience from start to finish. A special mention for the thoughtful gesture at the end: we were surprised with house-made mini cupcakes, beautifully plated with a handwritten note celebrating our anniversary. That personal touch truly made the night extra special. An unforgettable experience and a perfect place for celebrating meaningful occasions. Highly recommended. (5 stars) Opted for a la carte bc I heard there’s some misses in the tasting. Everything we got was great. Lobster ramyun was simple but done well, but my fav dish was probably the sea bass and clams with truffle seafood broth; it was so rich and flavorful (5 stars) Elevated Korean to its finest! I can't even begin to tell you how amazing the food was. We had the most decadent food and only ate at the bar. The bartender gave us wonderful suggestions on what to order as well as attentive service. We can not wait to try the formal dining room or Bo. The beet tartare on toast was delicate and delicious. The chili lobster ramyun had the most velvety flavors. The Oiji bowl with sea urchin was phenomenal. There was so much thought put into these bites and gorgeous presentation. Highly recommend trying. (5 stars)

bio_text: Olmo is a vibrant cantina neoyorquina that embodies the spirit of New York City dining. With a focus on creating a lively atmosphere, the restaurant invites guests to enjoy a unique blend of flavors and culinary experiences that reflect the diverse culture of the city. Olmo specializes in contemporary interpretations of traditional dishes, emphasizing fresh, locally sourced ingredients. The menu features a variety of options, including small plates and shareable dishes, designed to encourage communal dining.
menu_items: Mushroom Tostada - Confit oyster mushroom tostada with plum mole - $16
Chicharrón - Crispy pork rinds, guasacaca, crema, cabbage, escabeche veggies, salsa roja (Vegetarian option: Corn tostada) - $17
Sopes - Heirloom corn masa topped with black beans, queso fresco and plantains - $18
Queso Fundido - Melted cheese, chile poblano, fresh corn, chiles toreados with harina tortilla - $18
Roti Potato Tacos Dorados - Crispy tacos filled with roti-style potatoes, tamarind salsa and sesame crema - $18
César Salad - Little gems, creamy garlic and anchovy dressing, breadcrumbs, fried garlic - $17
review_snippets: What an excellent experience! I dined at a fantastic new Mexican pop-up where the food was a revelation, offering unique dishes far beyond traditional tacos. I'd highly recommend it for gathering with friends and family; everyone will find something to love. (5 stars)
Everything was great! My favorite was los sopecitos, the variety of salsas and the potato chips. We needed a bigger table haha, I guess they could bring the dishes little by little. (5 stars)

pretty good went with my girlfriend for her birthday. first thing i noticed was it was very “trendy” tiny tables and weird design but cute. like many nice restaurants in new york i can’t imagine the average american even fitting in the chairs there food was great we got some of the little tacos as well as a caesar salad. then of course the steak what’s that called. carne asada i think and some sort of pasta dish. honestly when i was single i never age salads but now i have a trendy girlfriend in brooklyn i feel like im constantly buying $16.00 caesar salads not even with chicken. staff was great very helpful and kind and welcoming and cool i thought there’d be more happy hour but they didn’t really have much outside of 10 dollar margaritas, which of course i had a few of but they weren’t very good, maybe too strong ! i forget what it was but my gf did not like her mixed drink much either. we were happier when we switched to beer overall great time and experience, a little sticker shock at the price but hey i ordered the steak. what can i expect. (5 stars)

Olmo is that kind of Mexican food that’s not the usual tacos or burritos everyone knows. It’s real “chilango” food from Mexico City… like the homemade dishes my grandma used to cook on Sundays, but taken to a premium NYC level. As someone from Mexico City, I can say every plate is a treat for your taste buds, your eyes, and even your sense of smell. The vibe is awesome: the music, the decor, the cantina-style concept, everything feels super authentic. The staff is warm and welcoming, which makes the whole experience even better. The bar is also amazing. You’ll find everything from a classic Mexican michelada to creative mezcal cocktails. It’s the perfect spot for a date night or just to hang out, disconnect for a while, and feel like you’re in a little corner of Mexico City right in the middle of Brooklyn. (5 stars)

bio_text: One White Street is a welcoming neighborhood restaurant located in a historic Tribeca townhouse in downtown New York City. The restaurant embodies a spirit of hospitality and inclusivity, inspired by a legendary love story from the 1970s. With a relaxed atmosphere, it invites guests to enjoy a re-imagined dining experience that celebrates global ideas and local ingredients. The culinary focus at One White Street is on ingredient-driven, globally inspired cuisine. The menu features an a la carte selection as well as a five-course chef’s tasting menu, highlighting seasonal offerings. Signature techniques include sourcing exceptional ingredients from Rigor Hill Farm in Columbia County, New York.
menu_items: Tuna Crudo - ponzu, trout roe, chives - $125
White Asparagus - comte, almonds, vin jaune - $125
Carrot Ravioli - rabbit confit, horseradish - $125
Lamb - beer braised onion, ramps, pine nuts - $125
Rhubarb & Meadowsweet - wildflower honey, sherbet - $125
review_snippets: Had a great evening at One White Street. The service was outstanding, and they gave me a perfect seat at the bar with a great view of the chefs in action. I started with a salad that was incredibly fresh and flavorful, full of green beans, cherry tomatoes, and cucumbers sourced from the restaurant’s own farm. For my main, I went with their much-hyped burger since it was my first time here—and wow, did it deliver. So beefy and juicy, and the Stilton just took it over the top. Definitely one of the best burgers in the city. Finished with the fig tart, which was an outstanding way to end the meal. Overall, a fantastic dinner. I’ll definitely be back. (5 stars)

We had the 5 course tasting menu with intermezzo included. Food was excellent. I really enjoyed the breads (free seconds) and Waygu beef. However, when I peaked over to the couple next to us, I wish I ordered a la carte. The burger looked so yummy. That wasn’t included in the tasting menu. Overall, I believe a la carte would have been a better value. (5 stars)

One White Street is simply one of the most chic night outs one could ask for. A subtle yet glamorous atmosphere lends way to one of the most fabulous gastronomic journey you will ever embark upon. Very accommodating to a gluten free diet!!! Big thanks to our server Sam, for their knowledge, and fine dining finesse! We started with the Rigor Hill Farm Salad, which stars radicchio, its bitter taste uplifted with the house made blood orange vin, shaved fennel, and honey goat Gouda. A definite must have for your table. Up next was the tamari glazed mushrooms. Earthy and delicately seasoned. The flavors used really complimented the umami rich mushroom. For our next round we ordered the 1WS burger. A mouthwatering premium meat burger with house made pickles and bun. Truly a showstopper. Our sides included: an order of crispy potatoes, which had such a lovely texture, the pickled garlic scapes really added an extra wow factor; and the celery root and leek gratin, which was so wholesome and really celebrated both of the vegetables natural flavors without adding too much. For dessert we were treated to a gluten free chocolate cake which was to die for, and separately a horchata ice cream served with jam. An absolutely stellar way to end the dinner. Overall it was such an amazing experience I’m already planning on going back with my whole family. The entire team at 1WS is one of the best and most accommodating I’ve experienced in the entire city. Thank you for giving me and my sister an incredible night!!! (5 stars)

I visited this restaurant on the 7th of October and had a reasonably good time. I ordered the Wagyu Burger, which was absolutely lovely. It was perfectly cooked and full of flavour. I had a brief chat with the chef (lovely south asian girl) while I was there, and she was so warm and genuine. I complimented her on the burger, as it really was excellent. The service was okay - I had three different servers throughout my visit. They all seemed nice enough, though a bit ambivalent or slightly off in their interactions. It might’ve just been the start of their shift or a quiet moment, but the energy felt a little subdued. Overall, though, it’s a nice spot and one I’d certainly recommend. (4 stars)

bio_text: Orsay is an iconic Upper East Side French restaurant that embodies the charm of a classic Parisian brasserie. With its sophisticated yet warm ambiance, the restaurant features dark mahogany paneling, Art Nouveau arches, and elegant chandeliers, creating a refined dining experience. Guests can enjoy a sidewalk terrace that enhances the Parisian feel, making it a perfect spot for everyday dining. Orsay specializes in modern French cuisine combined with classic brasserie fare. The menu is complemented by an award-winning wine list featuring 225 predominantly French and American varietals. The dining format emphasizes a balance of traditional and contemporary techniques.
menu_items: Velouté d’Artichaut - Artichoke soup, goat cheese cream, sumac - $18
La Selection d’Huitres - 6 Oysters east & west coast, mignonette & lemon - $27
6 Escargots de Bourgogne - Classic garlic and parsley butter, bread crumbs, mist of Pastis. - $21
Artichaut Vinaigrette - Poached artichoke, balsamic vinaigrette - $19
Salade Orsay - Organic mesclun, crudités vegetables, Cherry tomatoes, grana padano cheese, Truffle dressing - $19
Salade Lyonnaise - Frisée salad, croutons, bacon, organic egg - $21
review_snippets: Couldn't be happier with our brunch choice. We stopped in without a reservation, and they kindly accommodated us. We frequent Paris a few times a year, and this restaurant-- from hostess to manager to servers to clientele-- all made us feel like we were in Paris. Beautiful yet understated. Elegant and not arrogant. Reservations highly recommended if weekend brunch, as every table is occupied. Outdoor seating as well. Food-- delectable and they prepare everything to perfection. Perfect temperature, perfect seasonings... beautiful presentation. Our new 'go to' spot. Could tell there were many 'regulars.' (5 stars)
I had the Eggs Norwegian, coffee and the Orsay Sidecar. Everything was tremendous and the Eggs Norwegian was in some way exploding with different flavors. Just awesome (5 stars)

Service was attentive and very friendly. Full disclosure: I’m not much for French food generally so I went for the burger which was excellent. The artichoke appetizer was delicious with its balsamic dressing. Others raved about the cheese soufflé, French onion soup and escargot. Desert of the day was toffee pudding. Loved that it was not too sweet. (5 stars)

I used to actually like this place. The food was solid, the vibe was decent, and it felt worth the price. Clearly, those days are long gone. What showed up at my table this time felt like a sad, reheated tribute to what the menu used to be. The flavors were flat, the portions mysteriously shrank, and everything tasted like it had been sitting under a heat lamp contemplating its life choices. And then there's the manager. If indifference were an Olympic sport, they'd be on the podium. Rude, dismissive, and somehow annoyed that customers expect edible food and basic courtesy. When we politely mentioned an issue, we were met with eye-roll energy and a tone that suggested we had personally inconvenienced them by existing. It's impressive, really -- not every restaurant manages to downgrade both its food and its customer service so dramatically. If you're feeling nostalgic for how good it used to be, save yourself the heartbreak. Some memories are better left untasted. (1 stars)

bio_text: Oso is a vibrant dining destination located in Harlem, New York, offering a warm and inviting atmosphere that reflects the rich cultural tapestry of the neighborhood. The restaurant is designed to provide a relaxed yet sophisticated dining experience, making it an ideal spot for both casual gatherings and special occasions. Oso specializes in contemporary cuisine with a focus on seasonal ingredients and bold flavors. The menu features a variety of dishes that highlight local produce and innovative cooking techniques, ensuring a unique dining experience.
review_snippets: Shoutout to the staff for their flexibility in accomodating my order. I really loved their camarones a la diabla but they took that off the menu last month. I was really craving it and the server checked with the chef to see if they could still make it. They were able to make it and I had a good lunch. Thank you Oso! (5 stars)

Restaurant is a Bib Gourmand location, reasonable price for outstanding food. There is a Dia de los Muertos theme, but the decoration is simple and the restaurant is clean. “Oso” means “Bear” in Spanish, which patrons were constantly inquiring after. It wasn’t busy when we visited, the service and the food were outstanding. We had a mix of tacos and fish dishes, to include ceviche and a tuna tostada. Just off the north end of the CUNY campus. Highly recommend. (4 stars)

César’s service was simply spectacular — out of this world. 🙌 The drinks he made for us, the food — everything was incredible. Very talkative, friendly, and with a super cool vibe — he truly made the whole experience even better. He prepared a spicy mezcalita and a michelada that, honestly, not even in Mexico had I ever had ones that good! 🔥🍹 I 100% recommend César and his amazing service. Without a doubt, an experience worth repeating many, many times. (5 stars)

My colleagues and I were looking for a lunch spot, and one of them lives nearby and recommended this place. As soon as we walked in, I loved the vibe cozy and chill, exactly the kind of spot I enjoy. The food was great and affordable, but the best part? They have a happy hour with Buy 1 Get 1 Free cocktails! When you break it down, it’s about $8 per drink, which is an awesome deal and they’re delicious too. The waitress was super attentive and had a great sense of humor, she definitely made the experience even better! Highly recommend, and I’ll definitely come back next time I’m in uptown! (5 stars)

bio_text: Oxomoco is a vibrant Mexican eatery located in Brooklyn, NY, known for its warm atmosphere and innovative approach to traditional Mexican cuisine. The restaurant features a wood-fired cooking method, which enhances the flavors of its dishes, creating a unique dining experience that celebrates the richness of Mexican culinary heritage. Oxomoco specializes in modern Mexican cuisine, focusing on wood-fired dishes that highlight fresh, seasonal ingredients. The menu includes a variety of options from tacos to creative appetizers, with an emphasis on bold flavors and artisanal techniques. Oxomoco was founded by Executive Chef Justin Bazdarich and Chef de Cuisine Maria Barriga, who bring their passion for Mexican food and culture to the forefront of the dining experience.
menu_items: Mango - chili, lime - $8
Papitas - valentina powder - $7
Popcorn - mole negro oil, escabeche powder - $8
Chips and Salsas - variety of salsas, heirloom corn tostadas - $19
Oxomoco Guacamole - roasted cherry tomatoes, queso fresco - $21
Ensalada Caesar - romaine, cotija masa crunch - $21
review_snippets: We felt genuinely welcomed from the moment we walked in, almost as if we were dining with family. My daughter, who is usually a very selective eater, ended up having one of the best meals she’s ever had thanks to the thoughtful recommendation from the team at Oxomoco. The service, the flavors, and the atmosphere all exceeded expectations. Highly respected, highly recommended, and I truly can’t wait to go back. (5 stars)

This Mexican place is fusion but has its own character. We enjoyed the twist in octopus and fish ceviche because the charred octopus added more flavor. The catch of the day tacos are amazing, with Thai basil and other fresh herbs make it so refreshing to balance the fried fish! Beef cheek tacos are also very flavorful and tender :) Lastly dont miss to finish with chocolate mousse with espresso ice-cream, you won’t regret that! (4 stars)

Went there for Lunch and had an amazing. Our waiter John did an amazing job explaining the offerings in the menu and recommended things we ended up absolutely loving. The bar had an incredible selection of quality tequila and mezcal. Great for connoisseurs. The food is $$$. But worth every penny with how delicious it is. Will definitely go back again. (5 stars)

Being my first time in New York City I was taken to a quaint little Mexican restaurant in Brooklyn. Now coming from Los Angeles where we have exceptional Mexican food all over the city. Try some outside of California is a bit of a treat. Oxomoco has some very good dishes on an elevated level. They use high quality ingredients for all there dishes lending to elevated taste. The fish tacos were great tender flaky fish with a nice not too spicy slaw on top. Chips and salsa that had multiple levels of heat you get five salsas to try. The crab tostada was nice a flavorful and the wagyu beef cheek were tender with a nice mole sauce. They also have a nice mix of tequila and mezcal drinks for you to choose from. The menu is small but has something for everyone. All the dishes we had were very delicious and the atmosphere was great. Indoor and patio dining is available. Oh make sure you make reservations so you don’t have to wait if you want inside. If you’re in Brooklyn swing by and give them a try. You won’t be disappointed. (4 stars)

Oxomoco was founded by Executive Chef Justin Bazdarich and Chef de Cuisine Maria Barriga, who bring their passion for Mexican food and culture to the forefront of the dining experience. Mango - chili, lime - $8 Papitas - valentina powder - $7 Popcorn - mole negro oil, escabeche powder - $8 Chips and Salsas - variety of salsas, heirloom corn tostadas - $19 Oxomoco Guacamole - roasted cherry tomatoes, queso fresco - $21 Ensalada Caesar - romaine, cotija masa crunch - $21 We felt genuinely welcomed from the moment we walked in, almost as if we were dining with family. My daughter, who is usually a very selective eater, ended up having one of the best meals she’s ever had thanks to the thoughtful recommendation from the team at Oxomoco. The service, the flavors, and the atmosphere all exceeded expectations. Highly respected, highly recommended, and I truly can’t wait to go back. (5 stars) This Mexican place is fusion but has its own character. We enjoyed the twist in octopus and fish ceviche because the charred octopus added more flavor. The catch of the day tacos are amazing, with Thai basil and other fresh herbs make it so refreshing to balance the fried fish! Beef cheek tacos are also very flavorful and tender :) Lastly dont miss to finish with chocolate mousse with espresso ice-cream, you won’t regret that! (4 stars) Went there for Lunch and had an amazing. Our waiter John did an amazing job explaining the offerings in the menu and recommended things we ended up absolutely loving. The bar had an incredible selection of quality tequila and mezcal. Great for connoisseurs. The food is $$$. But worth every penny with how delicious it is. Will definitely go back again. (5 stars) Being my first time in New York City I was taken to a quaint little Mexican restaurant in Brooklyn. Now coming from Los Angeles where we have exceptional Mexican food all over the city. Try some outside of California is a bit of a treat. Oxomoco has some very good dishes on an elevated level. They use high quality ingredients for all there dishes lending to elevated taste. The fish tacos were great tender flaky fish with a nice not too spicy slaw on top. Chips and salsa that had multiple levels of heat you get five salsas to try. The crab tostada was nice a flavorful and the wagyu beef cheek were tender with a nice mole sauce. They also have a nice mix of tequila and mezcal drinks for you to choose from. The menu is small but has something for everyone. All the dishes we had were very delicious and the atmosphere was great. Indoor and patio dining is available. Oh make sure you make reservations so you don’t have to wait if you want inside. If you’re in Brooklyn swing by and give them a try. You won’t be disappointed. (4 stars)

bio_text: Papa San is a vibrant Nikkei izakaya located in New York City, where the culinary traditions of Peru and Japan converge to create a unique dining experience. The restaurant invites guests to explore a fusion of bold flavors and innovative dishes, all set in a lively atmosphere that encourages storytelling and connection. With a focus on both food and cocktails, Papa San offers a culinary journey that is as exciting as it is delicious. The restaurant specializes in Nikkei cuisine, blending Peruvian flavors with Japanese techniques. The menu features a variety of dishes that highlight this fusion, complemented by cocktails that incorporate Latin American influences. Signature techniques include the use of fresh, local ingredients and creative presentations. The restaurant was created by a team including Erik Ramirez, Juan Correa, Orland Delgado, Sang Lee, and others, who aimed to bring a slice of culinary chaos to life, connecting Lima, Tokyo, and Buenos Aires in New York City.
menu_items: Fluke Ceviche - Avocado, Sweet Potato, Capers - $23
Scallop Ceviche - Dragon fruit, Yuzu kosho - $26
Spicy Tuna Tartare Gunkan - Crispy Sushi Rice, Nori, Wasabi Tobiko - $16
Bok Choy Salad - Kabosu Vinaigrette, Shio Koji Caesar, Sliced Honey Crisp Apple - $17
Cucumber Salad - White Sesame Dressing, Pickled Wood Ear Mushrooms - $17
Udon Noodles Cacio e Pepe - Edamame, Pecorino Cheese - $19
review_snippets: Five stars all around. Chef Sergio is one of the best: creative, humble, and warm. My husband and I love sitting at the chef’s counter and seeing the food come together. The atmosphere of the restaurant is modern and sleek but still welcoming. The cocktails are creative and well-made, although the wine selection is even better, and their wines pair excellently with the food. Their ceviches are always good and well-balanced in flavor. Some of my favorite dishes are: the blue crab rolls; the hake chowder; bok choy salad; mussels; eel pizza; skate cheeks; udon noodles; and the miso black cod. Everything here is delicious, and you really can’t go wrong with anything on the menu. (5 stars)

The food was good but nothing else just good, the service was slow. We went for Valentine's Day, and it was not very busy, we arrived late for our reservation, but we were seated right away. Ordered the Wagyu Maki Rolls which was good but again nothing special. Drinks were 2 Chicha Morada which was not good seemed like poured from a bottle and way too much ice I think it was a block of ice. I added a Papa Sour again nothing special it was very sour with very little Pisco. Wife ordered the Pork Ribs which were good and tasty I ordered Wagyu Tri-tip, Yuzu Bearnaise both were very small portions. Funny thing our neighbors ordered the EEL Pizza and boy did they regret it the smell was strong and their faces said a lot. We went ahead and ordered dessert which saved the dinner we both shared Lucama Soft Serve and other ice cream can't find the name. Both Ice Creams were good and we left happy, but we will more likely not return. (4 stars)

Weird that this place isnt packed every night. The location has probably something to do with it, but still considering how good it was. IMO this is the best one yet from the Llama Group. While some may not agree with the authenticity of the Nikkei offerings, the flavors were def there. I tried all the top mentions and the sleeper hit is actually the Mussels. Some of the best I had in years if not decades. Def get the Udon as well, and the pizza. A good choice right now especially to pair with the holiday lights in Hudson Yards. (5 stars)

TLDR: Papa San is the next chapter of the same team that brought us Llama San, etc. Very flavorful but pricey and smaller portions - good for that corporate expense card. Cacio e pepe udon, burger sando. I was always a fan of Llama San so when I heard of Papa San coming - I was excited. The space is right at the corner of 34th and 10th and it's cool to have a nikkei (Japanese/Peruvian) option available. The dishes are well thought out and overall tasty but portions are on the smaller side. It also gets pricey quick. On a most recent visit, the spicy tuna gunkan maki. Basically it's a spicy tuna crispy rice wrapped in nori - solid. The burger sando I think is a must order. It's served on fluffy milk bread that's toasted, the patty itself reminds me of a Dominican chimi. Definitely add-on the fries, I'm not sure what the seasoning is but it's good. For some reason it reminded me of Dorito's ranch seasoning. Cacio e pepe udon. Mind you this is a modern iteration, so it's not as aggressively punchy or thick as a classic pasta. The udon I'd have preferred a bit more chew but the flavors were good. We added on the squid which is marinated in this spicy sauce - kind of similar to a Korean squid stir-fry. I'd add that in and mix as you go to change the flavor. Eel pizza, typically this is good. It's very thin and has bonito shavings, the eel, pecorino and chives. It was a bit too heavy on the sauce last time but I'd still order it again. I'm curious to try the dinner menu one day. Also if you go for lunch, probably one of the greatest potato salads I've had. (4 stars)

bio_text: Patricia's offers a unique dining experience that seamlessly blends the sophistication of a fine Ristorante with the casual charm of a classic Italian Bar/Restaurant. The restaurant emphasizes a philosophy centered around the finest ingredients, innovative preparation, and a commitment to exceptional service, creating a memorable atmosphere for guests. Patricia's specializes in Italian cuisine, focusing on seasonal ingredients and traditional preparation techniques. The menu reflects a deep passion for the diverse regions of Italy, showcasing both classic and innovative dishes. A Dream That has Been Cooking for Years
menu_items: LOUIE'S SCHIACCIATA - Grilled Chicken, Grilled Eggplant, Tomatoes with Extra Virgin Olive Oil - $16
PROSCIUTTO - Prosciutto Di Parma, Tomato, Mozzarella and Basil - $17
BRESAOLA - Air Cured Beef, Goat Cheese, Arugula and Truffle Oil - $17
ORTOLANO - Grilled Eggplant, Zucchini, Tomatoes and Mushrooms - $14
TONNO - Tuna, Red Onions, Arugula and Capers with Olive Oil - $17
PRIMAVERA - Sauteed Broccoli, Spinach, Mushrooms and Peppers - $15
review_snippets: Wow! What an incredible Value. Family style delivers!! Very good food with too many appetizers and mains to count. Includes unlimited Beer, wine or sangria, Desert and coffee as well. We’ve been coming here since they first opened there doors and we are happy we decided to revisit. Will continue to visit Patrizia’s and recommend. Party atmosphere on a Friday night which we both enjoy. (5 stars)

The pizza was great, the ingredients fresh and flavorful, the dough chewy and delicious. Same as the bread with garlic oil that they brought for the table. The pasta bolognese was good, but nothing special. It was a little overcooked and bland. The service was friendly and quick, though initially they forgot to take the order. (4 stars)

After a day spent at NYU hospital, we stopped here for an early dinner. Our waiter, Jose was friendly and accommodating. The four of us completely enjoyed our meals. The special, Pumpkin Ravioli, was excellent. We thoroughly enjoyed our meal, even having dessert! Highly recommend their Tiramisu— they got it just right! Great food, atmosphere and service! (5 stars)

After a day out in Manhattan we decided to try this restaurant out. I had seen this restaurant on YouTube before and they are known for their Star shaped pizza. We decided to try it out for lunch and I'm glad we did. We ordered the fried anchovies, pizza egg rolls, carbonara pasta, and a margarita star shaped pizza. The appetizers were spot on! It's not the salty anchovies that have been fermented, but Fresh anchovies! The egg rolls were actually really good and it made sense. The Carbonara was solid, but the Star -shaped pizza was amazing. I imagine that all the pizza is really good there. I say this because the crust was crispy and fluffy at the same time. The star pieces were also stuffed with cheese! In terms of pizza, one of the best slices I've had in a while. I would recommend this place for any visitor or tourist. The pizza itself is worth it. (5 stars)

bio_text: Peak with Priceless is a stunning sky-high restaurant located on the 101st floor of 30 Hudson Yards, offering breathtaking views of New York City. Managed by Tao Group Hospitality, this modern American destination combines a vibrant atmosphere with warm hospitality, making it an ideal spot for both dining and private events. The restaurant's stylish design, crafted in partnership with renowned architect David Rockwell, enhances the overall dining experience, inviting guests to return time and time again. Peak with Priceless features a seasonal modern American menu that emphasizes the purity of ingredients, inspired by the chef's relationships with local fishermen, farmers, and purveyors. The menu includes a variety of gluten-free, vegetarian, and vegan options, ensuring a delightful experience for all guests. The restaurant also boasts an award-winning wine program and a diverse selection of cocktails. Managed by Tao Group Hospitality, Peak with Priceless was designed in collaboration with architect David Rockwell, creating a stylish setting for dining at the summit of a 1,296-foot tall tower.
menu_items: SELECTION OF OYSTERS - $29 / $52
JUMBO GULF SHRIMP (3 pcs) - $27
ALASKAN KING CRAB LEG (1/4 lb) - $49
CHILLED MAINE LOBSTER (whole tail) - $36
The 'Only' Caviar Supplement - add 10g Oscietra Caviar - $59
PEAK PLATEAU - East Coast Oysters, Jumbo Gulf Shrimp, Alaskan King Crab, Chilled Maine Lobster - $151
review_snippets: I had a wonderful experience at Peak with Priceless during lunch. The staff was incredibly attentive, friendly, and professional, and made me feel very welcome throughout my visit. Since I was celebrating my birthday, they kindly congratulated me and surprised me with a lovely compliment, which made the day feel even more special. The food was delicious and beautifully presented, and the view was absolutely breathtaking. Having lunch with such an incredible panorama over New York made the experience truly unforgettable. Thank you for such a memorable visit — I would love to come back again. (5 stars)

The overall experience was incredible. They greeted us at the hostess stand with a Happy Anniversary and that flowed throughout the service with most of the staff. The views were beautiful all around, and going to the Edge prior allowed us to see all angles. The food was delicious (we did the Prix Fixe window seating). The scallops, porterhouse, and dark chocolate soufflé were delectable. The drinks were solid, though I definitely liked my second one more (Cosmo Colada tastes a bit like Fruity Pebbles). I will say there was no soap in the bathroom when I went, but fortunately I carry a hand sanitizer at all times. It was quite the experience, and I’d definitely return! (5 stars)

This is a difficult review to write as this restaurant is no doubt beautiful and the view even more so. Dining just before sunset is perfect as you can catch the skyline in all lights. Unfortunately there are a few things that need mentioning, especially as paid well over $200pp (set window menu) and were expecting top notch food and service. To start with, when querying about the wine list, the sommelier came to assist us. He kept trying to push the most expensive wines and wouldn’t consider our budget when repeatedly asked. When we picked a cheaper wine, it was conveniently out of stock. When the (red) wine arrived, it was cold and when questioned on it, the sommelier said it just needed time to ‘warm up’. We also found some things wildly overpriced - no matter the setting, chips should not be $30! They also kindly brought out a birthday cake as we were celebrating a birthday, which we assumed was free as we had not asked for it, but then charged us for it on the receipt and only took it off when questioned. Overall, the view is stunning and most members of staff are lovely and very accommodating. However, it felt as if we were being squeezed for as much money as possible throughout and some of the food/drink didn’t live up to the standard expected given the price. (4 stars)

I went to the restaurant last year for my birthday and the food was top tear. It was clean, refreshing and was extremely quality. I was not only impressed by the view but I was impressed by the food. It was clean, refreshing I was extremely quality and top tier. The Brussels sprouts were out of this world not pictured but it had I believe pork rinds that were fried to where they were crispy and those peaks of flavor that came through. Man oh man! The complimentry hors d'oeuvre...a blessing! The food was so grand I had to speak to the Chef! (5 stars)

bio_text: Penny is a vibrant walk-in seafood spot located in the heart of New York City, offering a casual yet inviting atmosphere for seafood lovers. The restaurant emphasizes accessibility and spontaneity, welcoming guests to enjoy fresh seafood without the need for reservations. Penny specializes in seafood cuisine, focusing on fresh, high-quality ingredients. The menu features a variety of seafood dishes that highlight the natural flavors of the ocean, presented in a straightforward and approachable manner.
menu_items: Oysters - $4.95
Countneck Clams - $3.95
Shrimp Cocktail - $26
Ice Box - Oysters / Countnecks / Shrimp / Mussels / Crudo - $45
Ice Box + - Razor Clams / Live Scallop - $120
Ice Box ++ - Lobster / Vichyssoise / Seafood Sausage - $195
review_snippets: The ice box is wonderful. I will go back for this and a glass of sherry. The ice box featured Gaia Oysters from New Brunswick, the most perfectly prepared shrimp cocktail, fresh clams, a sea bass ceviche, and perfectly marinated mussels. The Oyster Confit was outstanding. The concept of slow-cooking the oysters in rich chicken fat and serving them with crème fraîche and crackers is a stroke of genius. I would gladly go back for this item alone. The Stuffed Squid was very nice. The squid was tender, and the sauce was rich and flavorful. Be sure to save some of the bread to fully soak up every drop of that excellent sauce. Both the Seaweed Salad and the Beet Boquerones were excessively acidic, which overpowered the flavor of the otherwise perfectly prepared ingredients. I enjoyed a Dr. Brown's Cel-Ray here as well. The service was impeccable. (5 stars)

If you can get a reservation and you enjoy seafood then you are definitely going to enjoy Penny! Every dish is expertly prepared and beautifully presented. The shrimp cocktail was succulent and so delicious. Tuna carpaccio, tender with subtle marinade, the Halibut with spinach just melted in your mouth... I could go on all day! A very knowledgeable sommelier is on hand if you want pairing reccomendations, and every member of the team were approachable professionals. Amazing! (5 stars)

I’m still in love with Penny. Everything about it is dialed in — the interior, the lighting, the little details, the vibe… it feels effortless but you can tell it’s insanely intentional. The fish is unreal, the flavors are clean and confident, and the wine program is on another level. It’s that rare kind of seafood bar where every bite tastes like someone actually obsessed over it before it hit the table. What’s honestly crazy is this: you can’t get this anywhere else… but here. And that’s coming from someone from South Florida — because no place in Miami even comes close to this level of “fancy seafood bar” done right. Down here, most seafood spots with a bar vibe lean more divey. This concept? If it opened in SoFlo it would be booked out for weeks without even trying. Penny is special. Period. (5 stars)

Very good food, I particularly liked the raw bar. The dover entree was surprisingly bland and a little dry. The red snapper crudo had a bit too much orange. The chocolate mousse was pretty good, though the olive oil made it a bit too rich. I loved the music, 70s punk and post punk. However, it was easy too loud and I couldn't hear the person next to me very well. It's only bar seating, and it wasn't very comfortable. Overall, I found it expensive and given how hard it is to get a reservation, I wouldn't recommend it. (4 stars)

The ice box featured Gaia Oysters from New Brunswick, the most perfectly prepared shrimp cocktail, fresh clams, a sea bass ceviche, and perfectly marinated mussels. The Oyster Confit was outstanding. The concept of slow-cooking the oysters in rich chicken fat and serving them with crème fraîche and crackers is a stroke of genius. I would gladly go back for this item alone. The Stuffed Squid was very nice. The squid was tender, and the sauce was rich and flavorful. Be sure to save some of the bread to fully soak up every drop of that excellent sauce. Both the Seaweed Salad and the Beet Boquerones were excessively acidic, which overpowered the flavor of the otherwise perfectly prepared ingredients. I enjoyed a Dr. Brown's Cel-Ray here as well. The service was impeccable. (5 stars) If you can get a reservation and you enjoy seafood then you are definitely going to enjoy Penny! Every dish is expertly prepared and beautifully presented. The shrimp cocktail was succulent and so delicious. Tuna carpaccio, tender with subtle marinade, the Halibut with spinach just melted in your mouth... I could go on all day! A very knowledgeable sommelier is on hand if you want pairing reccomendations, and every member of the team were approachable professionals. Amazing! (5 stars) I’m still in love with Penny. Everything about it is dialed in — the interior, the lighting, the little details, the vibe… it feels effortless but you can tell it’s insanely intentional. The fish is unreal, the flavors are clean and confident, and the wine program is on another level. It’s that rare kind of seafood bar where every bite tastes like someone actually obsessed over it before it hit the table. What’s honestly crazy is this: you can’t get this anywhere else… but here. And that’s coming from someone from South Florida — because no place in Miami even comes close to this level of “fancy seafood bar” done right. Down here, most seafood spots with a bar vibe lean more divey. This concept? If it opened in SoFlo it would be booked out for weeks without even trying. Penny is special. Period. (5 stars) Very good food, I particularly liked the raw bar. The dover entree was surprisingly bland and a little dry. The red snapper crudo had a bit too much orange. The chocolate mousse was pretty good, though the olive oil made it a bit too rich. I loved the music, 70s punk and post punk. However, it was easy too loud and I couldn't hear the person next to me very well. It's only bar seating, and it wasn't very comfortable. Overall, I found it expensive and given how hard it is to get a reservation, I wouldn't recommend it. (4 stars)

bio_text: Peppercorn Station offers a unique dining experience that transcends traditional meals, immersing guests in a vibrant atmosphere inspired by the industrial era. The modern and sleek design is complemented by a dynamic ambiance featuring neon colors and a carefully curated playlist, creating an engaging environment that stimulates all senses. The restaurant specializes in Szechuan cuisine, blending traditional recipes with innovative interpretations that reflect the essence of New York. The menu includes both classic dishes and reimagined plates, emphasizing fresh, locally sourced ingredients and authentic Szechuan spices. The culinary team, led by the head chef, boasts over 50 years of experience in Chinese cuisine.
menu_items: Szechuan Green Pepper Bamboo Shoots - Green pepper paste, Spring bamboo shoots - $10
Sliced Beef and Ox Tongue in Chili Sauce - Beef tripe, Beef tongue, Beef tendon, Celery, Peanuts - $14
Sweet and Sour Ribs - Baby back rib, Home made sweet and sour sauce - $13
Mouth-watering Chicken with Chili Sauce - Chicken, Peanuts - $13
Clear Noodles in Chili Oil - Mung bean noodles, Soy bean, Peanuts - $9
Hot and Sour Glass Noodles - Sweet potato noodles, Pork, Bok-choy, Bean sprouts, Soy bean, Peanuts - $12
review_snippets: I had a great time dining here! It’s one of my friends favorite delivery places so I had to try it. Everything was so yummy! We had the seasonal lamp soup and it was so good for winter. Service was fast and attentive as well. Great location too. Would recommend. (5 stars)

Michelin Guide Authentic Sichuan Secrets! Glad ai found this hidden gem. From tender Mouth-Watering Chicken in bold chili sauce to melt-in-your-mouth Braised Beef with Potato, every dish is a flavor adventure. Dive into silky Crab Meat Sauce Noodles and finish with the perfectly balanced Sweet & Sour Fish — a mix of spice, umami, and tangy goodness. Sichuan like you’ve never tasted before! Follow me @foodie.elite on IG and TikTok for more great finds! (5 stars)

The food here is exceptional — full of flavour, well cooked, and genuinely memorable. It’s the main reason I’d consider returning. Unfortunately, the service seriously let the experience down. The waitstaff were rude, abrupt, and unwelcoming, with little sense of basic hospitality. There was no warmth, no courtesy, and interactions felt dismissive rather than attentive. It’s disappointing because great food deserves service to match. If management addressed customer service and staff manners, this place could easily be outstanding. As it stands, the food is the saving grace but the poor service overshadows what should have been a great dining experience. (3 stars)

My 6th time eating here and I’ve finally decided to write a review! Dishes are extraordinary and on an authentic note. Some dishes I really recommend are their truffle fried rice (very fragrant and umami), braised beef with potato (tender), peppercorn chicken (numbing addictive), string beans (crunchy and delicious), and their brown sugar mochi sticks are soooo crispy and chewy. However, if u can’t handle spicy, definitely tell them to lower the spice!!! The only issue is their service. Workers seem slow and a little rude? But that doesn’t stop me coming back for the 6th time! (5 stars)

bio_text: Persepolis is a distinguished restaurant located in the Upper East Side of New York City, celebrated for its authentic Persian cuisine and gracious hospitality. With over 35 years of dedication to sharing the rich flavors and traditions of Persian culture, Persepolis offers an elegant dining experience that invites guests to indulge in the warmth and vibrancy of this ancient culinary heritage. Persepolis specializes in authentic Persian cuisine, featuring a diverse menu that includes signature dishes such as Beef-Kubideh, Saffron Chicken, and various traditional stews. The restaurant emphasizes homemade ingredients and traditional cooking techniques, providing a true taste of Persia in a modern setting. Persepolis has been serving the New York City community for over 35 years, earning recognition in the Michelin Guide 2025 for its commitment to authentic Persian cuisine.
menu_items: Kashke Bademjan - Baked eggplant purée, Persian sour cheese, walnuts, onion, garlic and mint - $16
Eggplant Mirza - Roasted eggplant purée, mint, tomato, garlic and tangy yogurt - $14
Dolmeh - Vegetarian stuffed grape leaves - $15
Sambusa - Dumplings stuffed with seasoned potato, carrot and green peas - $15
Yogurt & Cucumber - Homemade yogurt with cucumber and mint - $12
Yogurt & Shallots - Homemade yogurt with aged shallots - $13
review_snippets: One of the most delicious meals I've had in awhile. We got the shirazi salad and dolma to start which were delightful, perfectly seasoned. Then for our mains we shared the soltani chicken kebabs and the khoresht fasenjoon with the sour cherry and barberry rices. We were joking that we were glad this restaurant isn't super close to where we live in the city because we'd be here every day 😆! If you're in the UES or just looking for one of the best meals in the city, come here! (5 stars)

The it was my first time ever trying Persian food and this was such a wonderful introduction. The food was spectacular and the service was even better. The waiters are very attentive and the food came out very quickly. The portions are sizable and everything comes out super quick. I had the chicken and beef duo and it was amazing. The cherry rice was such a unique addition but I couldn’t recommend it more. Drinks were good too!! Absolute 10/10 vibe, food, and service. (5 stars)

Take your money elsewhere!! Flavor profile is standard for cuisine like this, but the portion size is insulting. I am a small woman and I’m pretty sure a toddler would still be hungry. We paid 45$ per person and still left hungry. We ordered the lunch special, I got the Shirazi salad (see photo attached for portion size), barley soup (which was a standard metric cup’s worth of soup), and some beef stew that came with no beef and some rice. Only beans. I kid you not there were maybe two pieces of meat total in the entire stew. The dessert was mediocre, the cotton candy tasted like sand in my mouth and the rice pudding was just really lacking any sort of flavor, texture, etc. Definitely not an authentic place. Go elsewhere. Plenty of nicer places in the city that won’t rip you off. Also the toasted bread they brought us was burnt. ☺️ (2 stars)

I had a great dining experience at Persepolis, a well-established Persian restaurant that has been serving New York City since 1991. I started with the barley soup appetizer (barley, chickpeas, red kidney beans, and herbs), served with Persian bread. It was warm, comforting, and flavorful. For the main course, I ordered Gaimeh – vegan option, made with tomatoes, split peas, cinnamon, eggplant, and dried lime, along with steamed white basmati rice. The dish was rich, balanced, and very satisfying. Gaimeh is usually offered with beef or as a vegetarian dish, so I asked the server for clarification and was pleased to learn that the vegetarian version is actually fully vegan. The staff was knowledgeable and helpful. While dessert options were not vegan, I was happy with the overall meal. Persepolis offers solid choices for both vegans and meat eaters, making it a great place to dine with friends who have different dietary preferences. I highly recommend it for authentic Persian food and friendly service. (5 stars)

bio_text: Peter Luger Steak House, established in 1887, is a renowned family-owned steakhouse located at the foot of the Williamsburg Bridge in Brooklyn, New York. Celebrated for its classic American vibe, the restaurant has maintained its status as a top destination for steak lovers for decades, offering a warm and inviting atmosphere that reflects its rich history and commitment to quality. Peter Luger specializes in USDA Prime beef, which is hand-selected and dry-aged on-site to ensure optimal flavor and tenderness. The menu focuses on traditional steakhouse offerings, with a particular emphasis on broiled steaks prepared using time-honored techniques. Originally opened as 'Carl Luger’s Café, Billiards and Bowling Alley' in 1887, the restaurant was purchased by Sol Forman in 1950, who revitalized it and has since kept it in the family. Under Forman family management, Peter Luger has been rated the top steakhouse in New York since 1984.
menu_items: Peter Luger Gift Certificate - $50
review_snippets: We had to try Peter Luger while in New York, it just iconic, so we made a reservation for lunch. Service was really good! The steak was also amazing, being from an Alberta ranch I have to be partial to Alberta beef, but this was a close second 😁. We also got the German fried potatoes, which were good. The house steak sauce was different than I was expecting, similar to a cocktail sauce, but it went really well with the perfectly cooked steak. We were happy we had made a reservation as there was quite a lineup otherwise. Thanks so much for the amazing lunch! (5 stars)

I went to the famous Peter Luger steakhouse in Brooklyn, and honestly, the food quality was excellent. We ordered a few different cuts to try them out, along with the burger, which I’d seen highly recommended. As expected, the meat was top-tier full of flavor and cooked to perfection. It met all my expectations, as did the burger. A special shout out goes to the French fries; they were spectacular. Obviously, you come here for the steak, but the fries were on another level. While I have nothing but praise for the food, the service didn't come close to what you'd expect from such a famous restaurant. The waiters are almost rude to you, as if it’s part of the 'style' of the place, which I just don't get. You have everything you need to be the best, yet you fail at customer service. In short, I think the price to quality ratio is fair, and the food/portions are very generous. (4 stars)

As always a great experience. I love the beer hall atmosphere. Our Server “Aloisius” was the absolute best! Incredibly attentive and accommodating. The Steaks of course perfect as always. Bacon appetizer is always a good start. The Luger Beer is great, wish it came in a bigger glass though. Dessert was the hidden Star, the Apple Strudel with a tower of whipped cream. Delicious as if you were in Salzburg to eat it. Love this place! They accommodated our 11 month old and he loved the steak too. Servers were entertaining him and making jokes and read every wish for him off our minds! (If you read this, thank you to all the Staff for being so awesome) (5 stars)

I've been going to Luger for several years now (including for my birthday twice) and I've never had a bad experience. I truly don't get the hate it gets. I've never had a rude waiter (they can be no-nonsense though, which I actually respect) and I've never had a bad steak here. Yes it is expensive, but which steak house (that isn't a chain) isn't? My piece of advice is to order one size steak below your party size. The steak for two can feed 3 and the steak for three can feed 4 easily. And don't forget to order the bacon. And every dessert comes with their famous "schlag". And remember to bring cash as they don't accept credit cards. (5 stars)

bio_text: Phayul is a hidden gem located in Jackson Heights, offering an authentic taste of Tibetan cuisine in a cozy and inviting atmosphere. The restaurant is known for its homestyle cooking, where each dish is crafted with care and attention to detail, creating a warm dining experience that celebrates Tibetan food culture. With an open kitchen concept and limited seating, diners can enjoy their meals in a relaxed environment, making it an ideal spot for those seeking genuine flavors and exceptional service. Phayul specializes in authentic Tibetan cuisine, focusing on freshly made momos and hand-pulled noodles. The menu features a variety of traditional dishes, including steamed and fried options, complemented by unique spicy sauces. The culinary techniques emphasize freshness and authenticity, with ingredients sourced thoughtfully from local suppliers. Phayul has become synonymous with authentic Tibetan cuisine since its establishment above a watch repair store. The restaurant began as a humble endeavor to share the rich culinary heritage of Tibet and has since received recognition in prestigious guides for its exceptional momos and traditional dishes.
menu_items: Steamed Beef Momos - Beef, dough, chili oil - $16
Spicy Potatoes - Potatoes, spices - $12
Laphing Hot Sauce - Laphing, spices - $8
Hand-Pulled Noodles - Noodles, broth - $14
Ping Khatsa - Sweet potato noodles, mild soup - $10
Tsak Sha La Ko Hot - Beef, radish, herbal clear soup - $15
review_snippets: We visited here following the 13th annual momo crawl in Jackson Heights which this establishment did not participate in in 2025. Looking forTibetan cuisine on Yelp, this place came up. There are actually 2 locations on the same street, right across from each other. One location upstairs and the other on ground level. This is for the newer ground level spot. Small dining area, but 1 or 2 tables for groups available. Full bar and bottled bear selection. This are some tradional Tibetan dishes,and they do have momo, but dishes seem more a fusion of the Himalayan regions and and other fare. I really wanted to try the laphing appetizer, a spicy, cold noodle dish. I liked the texture of the noodles. The filling was super hot! I am not sure if chili oil was the only thing inside, but seemed like it was. We also had the stirred fried beef with radish which did have a nice flavor, although some of the meat slices were chewy. The chicken lollipops, which were originally ordered dry, came to the table with sauce and were not dry. The owner seemed perturbed with us, asking us if we were sure we ordered it dry. They took it back. The other main dish came out and the correct chicken dish took a good amount of time to arrive. Service was cold. There were no checks ins and we did feel a little ignored and had to ask for drink refills and the check when someone walked by. We were told the check had to be paid at the bar (it was never brought to our table) but when going to pay, no one was at the bar. Little confusing. I did not look carefully enough at the check to see if the automatic 18% tip was charged as other reviews pointed out. We left a generous cash tip. Cozy atmosphere and the restroom was relatively clean. (3 stars)

First of all people need to understand food and culture. There isn’t a “maitre d” here this is a homely hole in the wall with great food. If you sant to be waited on hand and food this isn’t the place for you. If you appreciate good food and culture this is a perfect representation of such. Authentic to it’s theme and the amazing food speaks for itself Momo’s are amazing and juicy and bok choy and beef stir fry top tier. Visit Eat Enjoy (5 stars)

Hello everyone, I want to share one of the worst experiences I’ve had this year. I’ve been to many restaurants in my life, with both good and bad experiences, but I have never encountered service this terrible before. • The ordering process was a complete disaster. They didn’t even bother to listen properly, brought the wrong order twice. • The waiting time was ridiculous. It felt like they forgot about us, and we had to remind them multiple times. • The staff were extremely rude and careless. Even to simple questions, they gave cold or disrespectful answers. A smile? Forget about it. • The place was messy and poorly maintained. Tables were dirty and the overall atmosphere felt neglected. • The food quality didn’t match the price at all. The dishes were tasteless, and the portions were surprisingly small. Honestly, this place was nothing but a waste of time and money. When you go to a restaurant, you at least expect basic respect and decent service—here, you get neither. So my advice is: if you’re looking to enjoy a nice meal or a pleasant evening, do yourself a favor and stay away from this place. For me, it will always remain the restaurant with the worst service I have ever experienced (1 stars)

It’s a very simple yet pretty place. Has minimum decoration but it looks neat n clean. Service is fast n good momos we’re really good. They were with potato and Veges. A very different combo but would just slither in the mouth (3 stars)
