There isn’t a “maitre d” here this is a homely hole in the wall with great food. If you sant to be waited on hand and food this isn’t the place for you. If you appreciate good food and culture this is a perfect representation of such. Authentic to it’s theme and the amazing food speaks for itself Momo’s are amazing and juicy and bok choy and beef stir fry top tier. Visit Eat Enjoy (5 stars) Hello everyone, I want to share one of the worst experiences I’ve had this year. I’ve been to many restaurants in my life, with both good and bad experiences, but I have never encountered service this terrible before. • The ordering process was a complete disaster. They didn’t even bother to listen properly, brought the wrong order twice. • The waiting time was ridiculous. It felt like they forgot about us, and we had to remind them multiple times. • The staff were extremely rude and careless. Even to simple questions, they gave cold or disrespectful answers. A smile? Forget about it. • The place was messy and poorly maintained. Tables were dirty and the overall atmosphere felt neglected. • The food quality didn’t match the price at all. The dishes were tasteless, and the portions were surprisingly small. Honestly, this place was nothing but a waste of time and money. When you go to a restaurant, you at least expect basic respect and decent service—here, you get neither. So my advice is: if you’re looking to enjoy a nice meal or a pleasant evening, do yourself a favor and stay away from this place. For me, it will always remain the restaurant with the worst service I have ever experienced (1 stars) It’s a very simple yet pretty place. Has minimum decoration but it looks neat n clean. Service is fast n good momos we’re really good. They were with potato and Veges. A very different combo but would just slither in the mouth (3 stars)

bio_text: Pierozek is a vibrant Polish restaurant located in Greenpoint, Brooklyn, known for its authentic handmade pierogi. The establishment combines a modern yet comfortable decor inspired by the Polish Folk Art movement of the 1960s and 70s, creating an inviting atmosphere for both Polish cuisine enthusiasts and newcomers alike. With a commitment to quality and tradition, Pierozek offers a unique dining experience that celebrates the rich flavors of Poland. Specializing in pierogi, Pierozek features a diverse menu that includes classic varieties such as Ruskie (Potato & Cheese) and Sauerkraut & Mushroom, as well as modern interpretations like Jalapeño and Murray’s Cheese Pierogi. The restaurant also serves a selection of traditional Polish dishes, including Red Borscht, Croquettes, and Gołąbki (Stuffed Cabbage). Pierozek is operated by an all-women team of experienced pierogi-makers, many of whom are from Poland, and the restaurant produces roughly 2,000 handmade pierogi daily. The culinary techniques used are passed down through generations, ensuring authenticity in every dish.
menu_items: Potato & Cheese - filled with potato & farmer cheese, topped with caramelized onions - $14
Sauerkraut & Mushroom - filled with sauerkraut & mushroom, topped with caramelized onions - $14
Meat - filled with pork shoulder meat, topped with caramelized onions - $15
Jalapeño - filled with potato & cheese, fresh jalapeño, topped with crispy bacon and fresh jalapeños - $15
Spinach - filled with spinach & garlic - $14
Murray's Cheese - filled with Murray's savory Irish Cheddar, bacon & creamy potato topped with crispy bacon, and fresh chives - $16
review_snippets: Pierozek is one of my favorite polish spots in the neighborhood. The food is consistently great and their servers are always patient and friendly. It’s awesome they do local collabs on pierogis. Solid vodka selection. The interior is adorable and warm. Their weekend special grill bowl is my favorite on the menu. In the warmer months, their back patio space is quiet and chill. (5 stars)

This was my first time having pierogis. This spot was so cute, clean, menu was comprehensive and not overwhelming. I was recommended to try the cheese & potato first; which were a generous 6! There was a side of sour cream and sour cream with dill. They were so delicious and filling I only got through half. I ended up ordering other pierogis to go (Bacon & jalapeño and pork), which were also delicious. The staff were friendly smiling and attentive. Menu reasonably priced. They have a cute back patio lots of seating indoor; clean, cute and id definitely come back! (5 stars)

A wonderful dining experience. The kielbasa and pierogies were delicious! The pierogies are made on premise and the kielbasa is made in NJ. The restaurant is small and nicely decorated. The staff is friendly and efficient. This is a Michelin rated restaurant and certainly worthy of their rating. I highly recommend this restaurant in “Little Poland” in Greenpoint (5 stars)

Absolutely delicious! Pierozek is such a gem — everything tastes homemade and full of love. The pierogi are soft, flavorful, and perfectly balanced (you can tell they use quality ingredients). The staff is warm, welcoming, and happy to share recommendations. The atmosphere is cozy, making it feel like a little slice of Poland right here in the city. Whether you’re a pierogi lover or trying them for the first time, this place will win you over. Highly recommend the potato & cheese pierogi and the dessert options — pure comfort food heaven! (5 stars)

bio_text: Pinch Chinese is a vibrant dining destination located in the heart of New York City, offering a modern twist on traditional Chinese cuisine. The restaurant's atmosphere is lively and welcoming, making it an ideal spot for both casual dining and special occasions. With a focus on high-quality ingredients and authentic flavors, Pinch Chinese provides an exceptional culinary experience that celebrates the rich heritage of Chinese gastronomy. The restaurant specializes in a variety of dumplings, including pork, crab, and vegetable options, alongside a selection of small plates and large dishes. The menu features signature items such as Peking Duck and Wind Sand Chicken, showcasing traditional cooking techniques and bold flavors. Diners can enjoy an all-day menu as well as a weekend brunch offering.
menu_items: Pork Soup Dumplings - bite sized explosions of porky goodness - $18.00
Crab Soup Dumplings - fresh blue crab + niman ranch pork - $21.00
Chicken Soup Dumplings - good for the soul - $18.00
Fish Dumplings - house chilli soy - $18.00
Vegetable Dumplings - bok choy, free range egg + glass noodle - $16.00
Mushroom Dumplings - shiitake + truffle - $16.00
review_snippets: Came here again for Christmas dinner and it was great overall. We always love coming here for their Peking duck and it’s consistently so good. The duck skin was super crispy, the quality of the meat was excellent, and it paired really well with the sides. The slices of pie were also chewy and served hot which made them really good. The duck was better than the beef short rib. The short rib tasted more like an American style short rib, which was not that good and outstanding. The scallop was very soft, and the sticky char siu pork rib was delicious. The desserts were a bit disappointing though. The red bean layer for redbean chocolate cake was so thin I could barely taste it and both the cake and pear cake were just okay, nothing special. Loved their veggies! Brussel sprouts and pea shoots were so good. (4 stars)

Service was stellar. Every course exceeded expectations. The pecking duck was phenomenal- it is a build your own taco style. Brussels sprouts were amazing and perfectly cooked. You cannot go wrong with any soup dumplings. Dan Dan noodles were great with a mild kick. (5 stars)

Welcoming spot with great bar seating for multiple people or eating solo. Staff is welcoming and ask right away if you have allergies. They make suggestions and are attentive. The decor is festive with subtle music. Can hear yourself talk . Food is clean and fresh, .Vegetables are crisp, cooked oerfectly and main dish was very savory. The rice is perfectly cooked to compliment the dishes.Highly recommend for anyone needing a tasty meal and friendly environmentStop in!!!. (5 stars)

This place has the best Chinese food hands down. Don’t think just go, do not hesitate. it’s very affordable not expensive! Service is stellar, food is very memorable will definitely come back here. (5 stars)

bio_text: Place des Fêtes is a charming neighborhood wine bar and seasonal restaurant located in the heart of Clinton Hill, Brooklyn. Operated by Redwood Hospitality, the venue offers a warm and inviting atmosphere, perfect for intimate dinners, celebrations, and group dining. The restaurant features a thoughtfully curated selection of natural wines from Spain and France, with a focus on the Catalan regions and southwest France, complemented by a menu of seasonal small plates and sustainable, seafood-forward dishes that emphasize simplicity and creativity. The culinary focus at Place des Fêtes is on seasonal small plates and sustainable seafood dishes. The menu is designed to highlight the freshness of ingredients through creative preparations, with an emphasis on natural wines that pair beautifully with the food. Place des Fêtes is part of Redwood Hospitality, the team behind notable establishments such as Cafe Mado, Laurel Bakery, Golden Ratio, and Oxalis.
menu_items: bangs island mussels en tinta
fluke, rhubarb, pea tendrils
sardine toast, smoked butter, kosho
bien cuit sourdough with spanish olive oil
cantabrico anchovies
tempesta mortadella
review_snippets: I had high hopes for Place des Fêtes but I was pretty disappointed, especially for all the high reviews it received. For the price they’re charging here, you either have to increase the portion size or really knock the customers socks off. Some of the dishes were comically small, I get this is tapas but come on. My favorite dish was the sardine toast but that’s the only thing that was good. The pasta tasted like something you’d make at home and the cod was lukewarm, not appealing at all. The freshness of the ingredients was spot on, you can definitely taste the quality but it’s the actual delivery that flopped. I do have to shout out to our waiter who was great and offered some solid suggestions. There are some great restaurants in Brooklyn, especially in this area but PDF is not one of them. (3 stars)

The sardines toast was definitely the highlight for me! But the maitako mushroom with black garlic sauce & corn with eel bonito were delightful. Super cute place inside, very cozy and nice bar seating area. All the staffs were super helpful, attentive and sweet. Perfect date spot, light not too dim, portions are on the smaller end and pretty vibey. (4 stars)

Sleek and bustling spot. The swordfish, the pasta and the daily special mushrooms were very memorable, although really everything was good. Great wine choices and solid service too. A strong recommend for a weekend outing for groups of 2-4. (5 stars)

Had a really great experience here end-to-end. We came for my boyfriend’s birthday and I really appreciated that they wished him happy birthday on the walk in, had a card at our seat at the bar and poured us glasses of champagne as we sat down. It made the dinner feel very special before we even made it to the food. The food was delicious! Every sauce and broth was so unique and well curated. Each dish got better and better with each bite. I know I’ll be craving another visit very soon. My personal faves from the night were the sardine toast (I called it a sushi toast) and the mafaldine which had notes of almost a seaweed like flavor, but everything was great. My only note was with the asparagus and salt cod dish the flavor of the asparagus drowned out the cod - I appreciated the cod and the ramp more on their own or with the sourdough. Definitely get the sourdough to sop up any and all of the leftover sauces. They’re that good (5 stars)

bio_text: Portale is a contemporary Italian restaurant located in the heart of New York City's Chelsea neighborhood. The restaurant, housed in a beautifully renovated carriage house, offers a relaxed and convivial atmosphere, perfect for enjoying a thoughtfully crafted dining experience. With a focus on seasonal ingredients and a modern Italian flair, Portale aims to delight guests with its inviting ambiance and stylish decor, designed to provide both comfort and sophistication. Portale specializes in contemporary Italian cuisine, showcasing a menu that features an abundance of roasted vegetables, market salads, pastas, and assorted grilled meats and fish. The culinary approach is inspired by Italy's seasonally driven cooking traditions, emphasizing fresh and high-quality ingredients. Chef Alfred Portale, the Executive Chef and Owner, brings his heritage and passion for Italian cuisine to the restaurant, creating a menu that reflects his dedication to the culture and flavors of Italy.
menu_items: FOCACCIA - castelvetrano olives, rosemary, whipped ricotta, olio verde
ZUPPA DI FUNGHI - white mushroom soup, asparagus custard, pickled pearl onions
INSALATA DI CESARE - baby gem lettuce, toasted breadcrumbs, parmigiano, caesar dressing
INSALATA DI CAVOLO NERO - baby kale, quinoa, dried black currants, marcona almonds, pecorino toscano
BURRATA - prosciutto di parma, flame beets, toasted pistachios, saba
CRUDO DI TONNO - yellowfin tuna tartare, cucumber, radish, calabrian chili, citrus emulsion
review_snippets: Food Ratings: (keeping prices in mind) - Focaccia: 7/10 The bread was soft and crispy at the same time. I liked the pairing with the olive oil and cheese. - Crudo Di Capesante: 6/10 Tastes fresh, the scallops were good. Nothing out of this world tasty. - Risotto: 3/10 This was my first time eating risotto and it was not a good one. I don’t know if risotto is supposed to be extremely salty but this one was so salty. If there was any other flavor it was overpowered by the salt. Very disappointing. - Anatra: 5/10 I like meat and usually have no complaints but this dish was $42 if i recall correctly…for this price I’d expect the meat to melt in my mouth but it was chewy. I haven’t had duck in a while so not sure if duck is supposed to be chewy. Very average dish. - Lumache: 4/10 I love pasta, and maybe I prefer my pasta to be cooked a little more but I felt that the pasta wasn’t cooked enough. This is just a personal preference. However, this dish was so salty as well. I don’t understand why the lumache and risotto were both so heavily salted. All I could taste was salt. Restaurant Atmosphere: 8/10 Everyone was polite. The vibes are nice. I would not go to this restaurant again nor recommend to a friend unfortunately. I don’t think the prices match the taste of the dishes. (2 stars)

Each time I visit, they never disappoint. The food is great, especially the ravioli, which is my favorite so far. The sauce on the filet mignon was a bit too salty, but still tasty. And the service, especially from our server Jeffery, was amazing. His excellent service definitely elevated our experience. I’ll definitely be coming back. (5 stars)

Bustling downtown NYC restaurant. It was hopping on an ice cold Saturday night. Beautiful inside with very nice if not a little strained staff. I mean management stop making the waiters also bus their tables. The food was excellent. Everything was fresh and well made. I highly recommend you try this restaurant (5 stars)

Visited a few weeks ago for a work dinner with colleagues after hearing them rave about the food, and I’m glad to say it lived up to the hype. Since we had a large group, we ordered a wide variety of dishes to share, which gave us a great taste of the menu—and honestly, everything was a hit, even the desserts. Our server went above and beyond with excellent wine recommendations and pairings that really elevated the whole experience. Highly recommend if you’re looking for a quality meal in the city. (5 stars)

jellyfish tiger salad - cilantro, chinese celery, scallion, spicy sesame - $16
berkshire pork & chive potstickers - house-made chili crisp, sweet soy - $15
woodear & oyster mushroom potstickers - house-made chili crisp, sweet soy, corn - $15
endive salad - dragonfruit, cara cara orange, pistachios, pecorino - $24
cold sesame noodles - sesame soy-milk, chili crisp, cucumber, scallion - $20
review_snippets: This was my first time here, and I instantly fell in love with both the vibes and the food. I walked in, put my name on the waitlist, and luckily got seated right away. Once seated, we started with appetizers and wow!! Berkshire pork & chive potstickers are a must-order ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ super juicy inside with crispy skin, topped with a special homemade chili oil. Endive salad is also a must ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ so refreshing, with dragon fruit and a perfectly balanced dressing. For mains, we ordered: Salt & pepper chicken with scallion biscuits—crispy chicken served with scallion biscuits might sound unusual, but the combination is amazing, especially with the dipping sauce and pickled jalapeños. Tiger shrimp with candied walnuts ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (100/10!)—my absolute favorite. So flavorful and delicious, served with fried romanesco cauliflower. For drinks, we had the Golden Bee and Crouching Tiger both paired beautifully with the food. The staff were incredibly nice and friendly. The vibe is cozy and charming, giving a classic theater feel mixed with a modern atmosphere. This may have been my first visit, but it definitely won’t be my last. I already can’t wait to come back and try more dishes. (5 stars)

Overview: Come for the excellent, elevated yet authentic Chinese cuisine, stay for the chill vibes, decor and pleasant service. A completely recommend checking out Potluck Club when in Chinatown or in need of a nice yet chill dining experience. Food: 4.5/5 The dishes came out pretty quickly and the portion sizes were shareable. Everything was pretty delicious with robust, satisfying flavors. Yes the price point is steeper than a mom and pop restaurant in Chinatown but the overall experience justifies the costs. We ordered: Braised Short Rib, Oyster Mushroom Noodles, Spicy Eggplant and Tiger Shrimp. No regrets on any of those items and I'm looking forward to exploring the rest of the menu. In terms of adult beverages I had the Puffed Rice Chinese Pale Ale and it was really delectable. I general don't go for Pale Ale but this one was very smooth with notes of fruits. Service: 5/5 We were well taken care of by all. Even the bartender helped out by picking up one of our napkins that fell on the floor. Ambiance: 5/5 The decor is excellent and makes the environment welcoming for dining with friends, a chill date, etc. Evening the dining ware is pleasing. Did I check out the plate manufacturer? I sure did. They're excellently designed (if sleek and modern is your style) and hefty. (5 stars)

Well crafted, tasty, and memorable experience. The place, the food, the staff, and the environment all came together to presented something charming. I liked the braised beef and the rice roll with steak most but everything we tried was delicious. Thanks for a great meal. (5 stars)

Everything here was great - we loved all of the dishes we got, especially the rice roll noodles. The service was prompt and super attentive, even took a great photo for us! I walked in, put my name on the waitlist, and luckily got seated right away. Once seated, we started with appetizers and wow!! Berkshire pork & chive potstickers are a must-order ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ super juicy inside with crispy skin, topped with a special homemade chili oil. Endive salad is also a must ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ so refreshing, with dragon fruit and a perfectly balanced dressing. For mains, we ordered: Salt & pepper chicken with scallion biscuits—crispy chicken served with scallion biscuits might sound unusual, but the combination is amazing, especially with the dipping sauce and pickled jalapeños. Tiger shrimp with candied walnuts ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (100/10!)—my absolute favorite. So flavorful and delicious, served with fried romanesco cauliflower. For drinks, we had the Golden Bee and Crouching Tiger both paired beautifully with the food. The staff were incredibly nice and friendly. The vibe is cozy and charming, giving a classic theater feel mixed with a modern atmosphere. This may have been my first visit, but it definitely won’t be my last. I already can’t wait to come back and try more dishes. (5 stars) Overview: Come for the excellent, elevated yet authentic Chinese cuisine, stay for the chill vibes, decor and pleasant service. A completely recommend checking out Potluck Club when in Chinatown or in need of a nice yet chill dining experience. Food: 4.5/5 The dishes came out pretty quickly and the portion sizes were shareable. Everything was pretty delicious with robust, satisfying flavors. Yes the price point is steeper than a mom and pop restaurant in Chinatown but the overall experience justifies the costs. In terms of adult beverages I had the Puffed Rice Chinese Pale Ale and it was really delectable. I general don't go for Pale Ale but this one was very smooth with notes of fruits. Service: 5/5 We were well taken care of by all. Even the bartender helped out by picking up one of our napkins that fell on the floor. bio_text: Pranakhon Thai Restaurant in NYC invites diners to immerse themselves in the vibrant and diverse street food culture of Thailand. Inspired by the bustling outdoor alley food scene of Bangkok, the restaurant offers a unique dining experience that reflects the rich culinary traditions and lifestyles of the Thai people. Guests can enjoy a journey through various flavors and dishes that represent the essence of Thai culture. Pranakhon focuses on authentic Thai street food, showcasing a variety of dishes that highlight the unique flavors of Thailand. The menu is designed to reflect the diverse offerings found in Bangkok's soi, or alleyways, providing a true taste of Thai culinary heritage. The inspiration for Pranakhon restaurant comes from the vibrant atmosphere of the outdoor alley food scene in Bangkok, the original name of Thailand's capital city.
menu_items: LARB GAI GROB - Crispy battered chicken, red onion, cilantro, culantro, chili powder, shallots, mint, toasted rice powder with Thai chili-lime dressing. - $18
KUI CHAI - Steamed chive cake with savory chive filling, served with sweet & spicy soy dipping sauce and crispy chive pancake. - $18
SOM TUM POO NIM - Crispy soft-shell crab, shredded papaya, peanut, string beans, tomato, chili, garlic with Thai chili-lime dressing. - $22

review_snippets: Highly recommended! The fish dishes are must-try. Crab rice was good! Service was amazing (and definitely looking for their recommendations if you have never been there before). Sundae was made of corn, peach and sticky rice with coconut ice cream. Big bite would be enjoyed. Great treat if you walked whole day. Thai iced tea and Thai iced coffee are both good for spicy foods while I do see many people who come here often order cocktails (from I have observed) Also I usually do not enjoy sitting on the bar and this time I would say the people who serve on the bar make this experience great! (5 stars)

At Pranakhon, you can taste and experience various foods, inspired from outdoor alley (soi) of Thailand. After my friends and I had dined here for a birthday celebration, we can see how they earned Michelin Stars for three years! For starters, we ordered Klui Goong and Gai Manow. The Klui Goong was light, crispy, and the combination of pork and seafood was delicious. The sauce added a nice sweet-sour taste too. We also ordered various entrée such as Khao Soi Haeng, Khao Na Ped, Kang Dang Moo, Moo Grob Prik Khing, and Ped Ruan. The Kang Dang Moo was creamy with the coconut milk and fragrant with the basil leaf. Luckily, it was not too sweet, although I would prefer it a little bit spicier. The highlight of the night was definitely the Moo Grob Prik Khing, stir-fried crispy pork with string beans, kaffir lime, and chili paste! The pork had a nice crisp crunch. It was perfectly cooked so it was not too tender and not too crispy. The seasoning made the crispy pork flavor burst and it was a delight to share amongst the table! (4 stars)

So good. All the food hit. Not too oily or salty, but strong flavors and good spice. Underrated starters were the curry pancakes. They had an Indian profile and the sweet sauce on the side paired so well either way it. Khao soi was a dry dish which was interesting. Steak was cooked to perfection. Service was fantastic. Server came up periodically to refill in the water. She was present but never pushy despite the long line of people waiting for weekend dinner. Interior vibes are cool and take me to Thailand. (5 stars)

There were so many options it was hard to choose. We got the pad thai and mussaman short ribs. Both were delicious. The short ribs were very tender with a nice sauce. The pad thai was also really tasty and had a fun presentation. Although, it was not the best pad thai I have ever had. Looking around at other tables’ orders, the presentation of many dishes looked really good. For a popular place, the restaurant was huge and had plenty of seating, so there was hardly any wait time during a busy hour. (4 stars)

bio_text: Per Se is an exquisite dining establishment that embodies the essence of fine dining with its elegant atmosphere and meticulous attention to detail. Guests are welcomed into a refined space that reflects the artistry and passion of its culinary offerings, creating a memorable experience that transcends the ordinary. Per Se specializes in contemporary American cuisine, offering two distinct nine-course tasting menus: a chef's tasting menu and a vegetable tasting menu. Each menu is thoughtfully curated, ensuring that no single ingredient is repeated throughout the meal, showcasing the chef's commitment to creativity and seasonal ingredients.
review_snippets: It was a wonderful meal! Service was amazing and friendly, the food was so good. They've still got some Per Se classics and honestly, they don't feel aged at all. The staff are all ready to talk, but also know when to walk away. The bourbon milk punch was so good, as well! This place is generally out of my budget, but if I were to dine for a special occasion again, I would definitely come back. I took the worst photos in the world, unfortunately. (5 stars)

Per Se impressed me, I ordered the Evolution Menu which came with 19 courses. I found the range of tastes, flavoures throughout the dining experience to be considerate, with culinary ideas on the bolder side. The service was exceptional also, and the location if you can get a window seat overlooking Colombus Circle is very enjoyable also. (5 stars)

An unforgettable dining experience at Per Se, and one that truly lives up to every one of its three Michelin stars. From the moment you step into the main dining room, you’re immersed in elegance, a beautiful, serene setting overlooking the park, elevated further by the warm glow of the fireplace that creates an inviting and refined ambiance. The tasting menu offered both vegetarian and meat/fish options. I chose the vegetarian menu, and it was hands down the most delicious tasting menu I’ve had in a long time. Every dish was thoughtful, balanced, and impeccably executed. The mushroom pie was absolutely out of this world- a luxurious blend of exotic mushrooms, seared to perfection, rich yet incredibly refined. The Doppio Agnolotti with butternut squash emulsion and chestnut confit was a standout as well, a flawless combination of sweetness, depth, and texture. The meat menu was equally impressive. The perfectly seared Mediterranean Lubina and the delicately cooked farmed venison showcased remarkable technique and flavor, leaving nothing to be desired. Service elevated the experience even further. Samantha, our server, was exceptional- warm, attentive, and impressively knowledgeable about every dish, making the meal feel both personal and seamless. Per Se is truly worthy of each and every star. A flawless culinary journey from start to finish, and an experience I will remember for a long time to come. (5 stars)

Background Per Se is synonymous with a rigorously precise, French inspired tasting menu experience. Even its shorter menus are designed to reflect the full philosophy of the kitchen rather than serve as a compromise. Ambience The dining room is dimly lit and serene. While we were not seated in the main dining hall, our table faced the New York skyline, which added a cinematic calm to the evening. The space felt formal yet not stiff, elegant without intimidation. Service Service was impeccable and precise. Staff were attentive without hovering and thoughtful without excess. The presence of a vegetarian menu executed with equal seriousness deserves special praise. Food and drink The four course menu was skilfully crafted and coherent from start to finish. Each plate showed restraint and clarity. The true revelation was the dessert course. It was a masterpiece of balance and whimsy, arguably the most compelling and memorable sequence of the meal. It is one of the best if not the best dessert. Kudos Overall Per Se proves that greatness is not dependent on length or spectacle. Even a shorter menu delivers depth, confidence and emotional payoff. (5 stars)

bio_text: Pylos Restaurant offers a warm and inviting atmosphere that celebrates the rich traditions of Greek cuisine. Nestled in the East Village, the restaurant combines rustic charm with contemporary elegance, providing a comfortable dining experience that honors the culinary heritage of Greece. Guests can expect a menu filled with wholesome, traditional dishes served in a setting that reflects the artistry of ancient Hellenic life. Pylos specializes in traditional Greek home cooking, featuring a diverse menu that showcases fresh ingredients from all regions of Greece. The restaurant offers a prix fixe option and emphasizes lighter fare that aligns with modern dining preferences, while maintaining the authentic flavors of Greek cuisine. Proprietor Christos Valtzoglou, a native of Athens, Greece, has a rich background in managing successful New York restaurants since the 1970s. At Pylos, he aims to bring the time-honored foods and wines of Greece into a contemporary setting, ensuring that the essence of traditional Greek dishes is preserved while making them accessible at reasonable prices.
menu_items: Greek Village Salad - fresh tomatoes, cucumbers, onions, capers, kalamata olives, feta, extra-virgin olive oil, red wine vinegar - $24
Greek Salad - lettuce, fresh tomatoes, cucumbers, onions, stuffed grape leaves, feta, kalamata olives - $20
Two Eggs Any Style - $14
Greek Island Frittata - potatoes, country sausages, orange zest - $17
Smoked Salmon and Chive Omelet - $20
Mushroom-Herb Omelet - $17
review_snippets: Food was incredible server was incredible, just a bit pricier than average Mediterranean/greek food! Tables were also very close to one another, so very intimate seating and dining experience. The meatballs were incredibly juicy and flavorful, the blend of meats was perfect! The spicy feta presentation was unlike I had ever seen, you had to cut into the pepper to get the feta; made me a bit confused as to, should I eat this on pita? Or is it to be eaten alone? Overall, it was incredibly tasty and whether I ate it with Peter or solo, I would definitely order it again. Unfortunately, only stopped in for apps in a drink, but the rest of the menu was very expensive and atypical Greek would be well worth a return visit. (4 stars)

Greek Cuisine That Will Steal Your Heart ❤️ ​Stepping into this Greek establishment in NYC wasn't just a meal; it was an absolute revelation... hands down, one of the best Mediterranean dining experiences I've ever had in the city. Every element, from the first bite to the moment I left, was pure gold. ​The baked feta wrapped in crisp black sesame and served with a side of sweet marmalade was stunningly complex and a perfect balance of salty, savory, and sweet that you’ll dream about later. The dolmades (or tolma) in their bright, rich lemon sauce are a must-try. They left me desperately in love with them 😁 and instantly planning my next visit. Even the simple things shine, like the old Greek salad, served in a truly huge portion, it’s refreshing, authentic, and amazing. ​Beyond the fantastic plates, the experience is enhanced by the generous spirit of the house. The wine pours are legendary and truly, a "glass" is more than a glass in volume! Most importantly, the service is excellent. Host Tamara is fabulous, greeting guests with warmth, and the entire staff makes you feel like family. ​If you’re looking for fantastic food, generous drinks, and impeccable hospitality, go go go. I will absolutely be back soon! (5 stars)
Great food and great service. Nice selection of Greek wines too. Went for restaurant week and the food was really tasty with large portions. Would definitely go back! (5 stars)

We had a great time here. The food was delicious! When we were the restaurant was pretty empty so the staff were even more so attentive. The ambiance was exactly what I needed for a day after work to be wined and dined. (4 stars)

bio_text: R40 is an innovative Argentinian restaurant situated in the vibrant heart of Long Island City. With an open kitchen featuring a custom parrilla and a seasonal backyard oasis, R40 emphasizes a dining experience that celebrates community, culture, and creativity. The restaurant is dedicated to providing exceptional hospitality and a warm atmosphere for its guests. R40 specializes in Argentinian cuisine, focusing on locally sourced ingredients and traditional cooking techniques. The menu highlights the use of a custom parrilla for grilling, offering a unique take on classic dishes. The dining format encourages a communal experience, enhancing the connection between food and culture.
menu_items: HOUSE MADE FOCACCIA - rosemary, sea salt, whipped ricotta, hot honey - $16
ENDIVE CITRUS SALAD - red & white endives, blood orange, gorgonzola dolce, candied pecans, citronette - $22
BONE MARROW STEAK TARTARE - grass-fed coulotte, shallots, capers, cornichons, pickled mustard seeds, sherry, hot sauce, sourdough - $29
CONFIT LEMON PEPPER CHIMICHURRI WINGS - brown butter, smoked white alabama sauce, celery - $18
ARROZ NEGRO - squid ink rice, grilled head-on prawn, fried calamari, saffron aioli - $26
CHORIPAN - locally sourced chorizo, sourdough, garlic aioli, chimichurri, salsa criolla - $16
review_snippets: From the moment we walked in, R40 delivered a true five-star experience. Warm greeting, intimate atmosphere, and a room that feels thoughtfully put together without trying too hard. Service was excellent. David our server was attentive and precise, and the general manager stopping by our table was a great touch. The pacing felt natural and unforced. The food was outstanding. The skirt steak was perfectly cooked with clean, intentional plating, and the red snapper was bright, crisp, and well balanced. This kitchen clearly understands restraint, proportion, and timing. The cocktails were equally dialed in and thoughtfully executed. Everything worked together seamlessly. Food, service, and atmosphere all aligned. R40 is doing something special, and I’ll definitely be back. (5 stars)
Pretty good spot,, but prices are a bit steep For the type of food. The pasta was rich, the fish excellent but next time i will stick to steak. Enjoy (4 stars)

My first time here, everything was just perfect. I wanted a nice date with my boyfriend and the lights, the jazz live music and the food made everything just perfect. Shout out to Allison, our server, for so friendly and delicate service. She dame sure that we had our food as we wanted and at the time we wanted. My favorite dish was the crab empanada, it was different from what I’m used to but that empanada just hits different. The atmosphere was calm and nice. Remember that the live music is only Wednesday. Great experience, we will definitely come back. (5 stars)

We arrived 5 minutes prior to reservation but waited around 20 to 30 minutes until our table was ready. Service was amazing, the wait time can't be blamed on the staff as those who occupied the table we were waiting for seemed to just be sitting there sipping water. The food was amazing overall and staff was very friendly. Totally would recommend the wings and rosemary fries! (5 stars)

The cocktails were equally dialed in and thoughtfully executed. Everything worked together seamlessly. Food, service, and atmosphere all aligned. R40 is doing something special, and I’ll definitely be back. (5 stars) Pretty good spot,, but prices are a bit steep For the type of food. The pasta was rich, the fish excellent but next time i will stick to steak. Enjoy (4 stars) My first time here, everything was just perfect. I wanted a nice date with my boyfriend and the lights, the jazz live music and the food made everything just perfect. Shout out to Allison, our server, for so friendly and delicate service. She dame sure that we had our food as we wanted and at the time we wanted. My favorite dish was the crab empanada, it was different from what I’m used to but that empanada just hits different. The atmosphere was calm and nice. Remember that the live music is only Wednesday. Great experience, we will definitely come back. (5 stars) We arrived 5 minutes prior to reservation but waited around 20 to 30 minutes until our table was ready. Service was amazing, the wait time can't be blamed on the staff as those who occupied the table we were waiting for seemed to just be sitting there sipping water. The food was amazing overall and staff was very friendly. Totally would recommend the wings and rosemary fries! (5 stars)

bio_text: Raf's is a charming French and Italian bakery located in the heart of New York, NY. The restaurant offers a warm and inviting atmosphere, perfect for enjoying freshly baked goods and artisanal pastries. With a focus on quality ingredients and traditional techniques, Raf's provides a delightful dining experience that celebrates the rich culinary heritage of both France and Italy. Raf's specializes in French and Italian baked goods, featuring a menu that includes a variety of pastries, breads, and desserts. The culinary focus is on traditional baking methods, ensuring each item is crafted with care and precision.
menu_items: Marinated Olives - Calabrian Chiles, Rosemary - $6
Selection of Daily Breads - Beurre de Baratte & Sicilian Olive Oil - $14
Warm Fresh Ricotta - $8
Anchovies - $12
Arancini - Mortadella, Taleggio, Lemon - $18
Steak Tartare - Aged Parmigiano Reggiano, Anchovy, Grilled Baguette - $26
review_snippets: I’ve been to my fair share of Michelin Stars and other Top Tier restaurants, but I don’t kid when I say this place is amazing. Not only did the hospitality feel authentic but the restaurant offers experiences that are way more rewarding that what meets the eyes at first glance. It feels like a hidden gem with beautiful entrees and food choices that seem casual but are far from. The chicken was phenomenal and raised my expectations for food in general—I didn’t know chicken could taste so aquatic, moist, and flavorful. The bread was good or better-than-France level and paired well with the entire meal. I love this place and will definitely be back. (5 stars)

Raf's came alive right as I was about to leave at 9! What a lovely spot! Do not skip the steak tartare - such a unique serving. It's worth a shot for room for 1 at the bar, dont be scared to wait and grab a drink next door at tom and Jerry. Explore the wine list and top off with a cocktail. Seasonal pasta non-negotiable. (5 stars)

Beautiful breakfast. Highly recommend for a special brunch. Lovely omelette. Update, went for dinner, so delightful. The Dorade fish was marvelous, as were the pastas. It's a beautiful little gem of a restaurant. Lovely spot, make reservations. (5 stars)

We had a great lunch here. We both ended up getting the seared tuna salad. The salad was excellent. The tuna was seared nicely. The atmosphere is great. Really cute place. The pastries looked awesome. Very much like a place you would find in Paris. (4 stars)

bio_text: Raoul's is a vibrant dining destination located in the heart of New York City, offering a unique blend of classic and contemporary culinary experiences. With a commitment to exceptional service and a lively atmosphere, the restaurant invites guests to enjoy dinner seven days a week and brunch on weekends, all within a stylish setting that reflects its rich heritage. Raoul's specializes in French cuisine, featuring a menu that highlights traditional dishes with a modern twist. The restaurant is particularly known for its Burger Au Poivre, which is exclusively available at the bar during dinner service, emphasizing a casual yet refined dining experience. Executive Chef David Honeysett leads the culinary team at Raoul's, bringing a wealth of experience and passion for French gastronomy.
menu_items: Baguette / Sourdough Boule with Ploughgate butter - $7
Artichoke Vinaigrette with Raoul's dressing - $24
Fishers Island Oysters with mignonette and cocktail sauce - $30
Caspian Sea Ossetra Caviar with buckwheat blini, dulse crème fraîche and traditional garnish - $145
Jumbo Lump Crab Beignets with charred corn and Fresno chili rémoulade - $27
Oysters Granité with Anchoiade butter and bread crumbs - $30
review_snippets: Went for brunch today.We started with the Long Island oyster which were excellent. My wife had the goat cheese salad and crab beignet The goat cheese salad had a great dressing and fresh. The crab beignet I highly recommend ,it was delicious . For my main I had the steak au poivre with a delicious sauce. The taste and how it was cooked were outstanding. The profiteroles with ice cream were very good. Amy our server was very professional and efficient. Our main took a little longer than usual but she let us know the kitchen was aware. We didn't ask as we were in no rush but that was great customer service. The placed was packed. I really liked the decor . The art on the gives the place a nice Parisian vibe. It was loud but with the amount of people and the size it's probably normal for Brunch. I have never had dinner here but would love to. However, reservations are extremely difficult between 630 and 8. Since it was brunch I saw a family with young children. They were really enjoying their burger which is supposed to be excellent. I strongly recommend this restaurant. We had a wonderful Brunch! (5 stars)

My favorite thing about this place was the atmosphere. Really enjoyed the art and overall decoration. It was really hard to find a reservation but eventually booked for Sunday 9:45pm a month prior. Their specialty is the Steak au Poivre which was okay for what you pay. Really recommend the crab beignets as an appetizer My favorite aspect of this place was the ambiance. I thoroughly enjoyed the art and overall decor. Although it was challenging to secure a reservation, I eventually managed to book a table for Sunday at 9:45 p.m. a month in advance. Their specialty dish, the Steak au Poivre, was satisfactory considering the price. However, I highly recommend the crab beignets as an appetizer. They serve 12 burgers a day, so if you want that, I recommend going as soon as they open. (4 stars)

We scored our second reservation here this year on a cold, snowy day when everyone was canceling. The inside is comfy and warm and tight but a great homie feel. We are set up with our same waitress. We had early this year, Aimee, who is hands-down with the best personalities and waitresses we’ve had in New York. She remembered me because no one else ever orders the cocktail the Paper Plane. We went with the classics again and got the stick off of a burger up above with the artichoke vinaigrette. All hands down one of the best steaks, the best burgers any of us have had in a long time. Thanks Amy for the recommendation to head to Pete’s Tavern afterwards for the full Christmas bar feel. (5 stars)

I had an exceptional experience at Raoul’s. Truly beyond expectations. The food was outstanding; I ordered the steak, which was cooked to perfection and incredibly flavorful. The wine pairing complemented the meal beautifully, enhancing every bite. The service was warm, attentive, and made the entire evening feel special. Raoul’s consistently delivers a memorable dining experience, and this visit was no exception. Highly recommend! (5 stars)

bio_text: Red Hook Tavern is a charming establishment located in the waterfront village of Brooklyn, offering a warm and inviting atmosphere where friends can gather to enjoy classic American tavern fare. The restaurant's beautiful old space creates a nostalgic vibe, making every visit feel special and memorable. The culinary focus is on classic American tavern fare, inspired by legendary food establishments in New York City. The menu features a selection of traditional dishes that encourage sharing and camaraderie among diners. The restaurant has been open for almost five years, and the owner expresses a personal connection to the space, highlighting its significance from the first visit.
menu_items: Demi Baguette - Cultured butter, sea salt - $12
East Coast Oysters - Seasonal Accompaniments - $24 / $38
Shrimp Cocktail - Bun’s fancy cocktail sauce, Old Bay - $12 / $20
Mortadella - Truffle pecorino, olive oil, bread, cultured butter - $20
Steak Tartare - * Whole grain mustard, cornichon, caper, horseradish, matchstick potatoes, egg yolk, grilled sourdough - $26
Country Ham Croquettes - One-year aged white cheddar, dijonnaise, rye bread crumbs - $16
review_snippets: Red Hook Tavern feels like one of those neighborhood spots that’s been there forever. It’s warm and a little dim, with candles on the tables. Simple and comfortable. We had a reservation, so we didn’t have to wait, but outdoor seating looked nice too, and the wait seemed around 30 minutes on a Tuesday night. The burger was the reason we came, and it really was great. It’s dry-aged, so the flavor is strong and a little different, in a good way, but definitely something to know before you order. The potato chips were thick and fresh, the cheese was melted perfectly, and the pickle was honestly one of my favorite parts. I never thought I’d say that about a pickle, but it was that good. It’s not a cheap meal, and you can tell part of what you’re paying for is the place’s reputation. The food’s solid, the space feels genuine, and the whole experience just fits together nicely. (5 stars)

Great joint. Their burger is delicious, cooked rare as requested, and ranks high in my personal list of all time great burgers globally. Note to self: I should have avoided the unnecessary shrimp cocktail, that was bland at best (and probably recently defrosted) The young team running the show is dynamic and friendly, not to mention very efficient, and the vibe is neighbourhood-ish. I was there 30 minutes before their lunch opening and joined a small queue which grew much bigger by the time they flung the doors opened. Reservation is therefore highly recommended. (5 stars)

Didn't know how popular this place was but found out very quickly. Got a lucky open reservation that opened up and was sat down by 8pm. When I say this burger ranks up there with the best in NYC, not hyperbole. Got to try it yourself. Otherwise everything else we got, the wedge with thick bacon, the squid ink pasta, and the mussels were amazing. Will definitely come back. A+ (5 stars)

Came on a Monday without a reservation at 5pm and sat at the bar. Ordered the Dukes martini, croquettes, wedge salad, oxtail cavatelli and the burger. The place filled up after about 20 mins. Wedge salad was delicious and large! The sauce on the croquettes was delectable. The burger was buttery and big. Brought the cavatelli home as I was stuffed (the sauce was lovely, a hint of sweetness). They were playing 60s and 70s tunes 🥳 (4 stars)

bio_text: Red Paper Clip is an intimate neighborhood restaurant located on Christopher Street in New York City's West Village, offering a modern dining experience that reflects the vibrant energy of the city. The restaurant is dedicated to serving seasonal cuisine influenced by Asian-American flavors, with a strong emphasis on local and sustainable ingredients. With a Michelin star awarded for three consecutive years, Red Paper Clip strives to uphold its reputation through thoughtful and curious culinary creations. The restaurant focuses on modern seasonal cuisine with a strong influence from Taiwanese-American culture. Guests can choose from an a la carte menu or opt for one of the thoughtfully crafted coursed menus, showcasing the chef's commitment to seasonal ingredients and innovative techniques. Founded in 2019 by Chef/Owner Kevin Chen, Red Paper Clip has quickly gained recognition for its unique interpretation of Taiwanese-American cuisine. Chef Chen's culinary journey began in his family's bakery and has included experiences in prestigious kitchens such as Alinea and Blue Hill at Stone Barns.
menu_items: Oysters - Widow Hole, Tian Jing, Mignonette - $25
Cauliflower - Agridulce, Candied hazelnut, Black Garlic - $18
Celtuce - Parsnip, Cucumber broth, Chive oil - $18
BEEF Carpaccio - Teres Major, Chili Oil, Chicharron - $22
Beet Carpaccio - Boursin, Sunflower Seed - $16
Radicchio - Treviso, Cara Cara, Black Bean - $20
review_snippets: We came here to celebrate a friend’s birthday on a Saturday evening and all of us chose the prix fixe menu(they were able to accommodate for a vegetarian version which was a plus!). The meal started off strong — the first three appetizers were served together, and each was beautifully presented. The tomato salad with matcha sauce was probably my favorite, such a simple dish yet it had so many layers of flavor! The pie was amazing, and the dumplings were perfectly al dente. Unfortunately, the main course was where things started to dip. It felt quite plain and underwhelming compared to the earlier dishes, and the dessert didn’t really stand out either. The staff were nice and friendly, but perhaps because it was a busy Saturday night, they kept forgetting our drinks. We had to remind them several times. The service felt a bit disorganized, which was surprising for a Michelin-starred restaurant. Overall, we still had a great time, and the food especially the appetizers were memorable! (4 stars)

one of the best meals I’ve had in NYC! from the oysters, to their everything brioche, and XLB agnolotti - I love how creative every dish was and everything was pulled off with amazing attention to detail my friend and I also thought the cocktails really packed a punch and also appreciated how nice and attentive the servers were (5 stars)

The first course; oysters, potatoes, and Hamachi crudo; was unbelievable! Truly a flavor explosion. The Summer Zucchini had the perfect amount of heat and was delicious, and the Everything Brioche was solid. I could’ve skipped the Agnolotti XLB and the brisket, though. Dessert was very good, especially the matcha gelato, which was out of this world. It was an odd night overall, when we arrived, only two tables were taken, and by 9 p.m. we were the only ones left. My guess is that the tasting menu price doesn’t quite match the experience, especially given how inconsistent the dishes were. (4 stars)

Wow! What an incredible experience. We did tasting menu which was perfect for dinner. The food was delicious , and spaced apart evenly. The service was knowledgeable &friendly without being overbearing. Ambience was minimalist and clean. (5 stars)

bio_text: Restaurant YUU is a modern French dining establishment located in Greenpoint, Brooklyn, offering a unique blend of traditional Japanese hospitality and high-quality French cuisine. With an intimate setting of only 18 seats, the restaurant provides a serene atmosphere that reflects both the calm and youthful culture of the neighborhood. Guests can expect a thoughtfully curated dining experience complemented by modern interiors and exquisite Arita ware tableware. Restaurant YUU specializes in a new form of French cuisine, influenced by traditional Japanese 'OMOTENASHI'. The menu features a creative approach to classic French dishes, showcasing the talents of passionate young chefs. Restaurant YUU was founded by Chef Yuu Shimano, who aims to redefine French cuisine through a Japanese lens.
menu_items: Amuse Bouche - Duck Consommé, Black Truffle; Foie Gras Miso Marinade, Honeycrisp Apple; Langoustine, Beet
Smoked Salmon - White Asparagus, Ikura, Yogurt Sauce, Dill; King Crab, White Miso, Yuzu, Caviar
Uni - Hokkaido Uni, Onion Velouté, Uni Espuma
Carabinero - Carabinero, Pear, Celeriac, Vinaigrette; Shirako (Cod Milt), Uni, Chardonnay, Tomato
Abalone - Abalone Risotto, Abalone Liver Butter, Seaweed Powder
Sawara - Sawara, Pistachio Emulsion, Watercress, Bergamot Ponzu
review_snippets: Restaurant Yuu is where Japanese omakase meets French cuisine in the most thoughtful and refined way. This was truly a one-of-a-kind dining experience — every course felt intentional, balanced, and beautifully executed. Chef Yuu is an artist. The precision, creativity, and harmony of flavors were on another level. What made the evening even more special was the unique collaboration with a chef from Edinbane Lodge from the Isle of Skye in Scotland — such a rare and inspired partnership that added depth and character to the experience. We celebrated our 15th wedding anniversary here, and we couldn’t have chosen a better place for such a meaningful night. The atmosphere, the storytelling through food, and the overall care put into the experience made it unforgettable. A truly exceptional restaurant. (5 stars)

Yuu in Williamsburg delivers an excellent dining experience blending French technique with subtle Japanese influence. The service was absolutely top-notch: attentive, polished, and perfectly paced. The atmosphere is breezy and calm, with very little noise. Seating is aligned so you’re not distracted by other guests, and facing the open kitchen adds a wonderful sense of theater — it truly feels like part of the experience. The tasting menu is excellent, with around ten courses that feel thoughtfully curated. The crab and the sweetbread were standouts and among my favorite dishes of the night. The salade de homard was very good, though it mixed quite a few savory elements — it might even benefit from being split into two separate dishes. The grouper was cooked to perfection, as was the pie, with an impressively thin, delicate crust. We’re not big dessert people, but both desserts were surprisingly great — light, fresh, and well balanced. I took the wine pairing, which was not my favorite but more from a taste than quality perspective. Pairing is expensive but they serve high-end wines which I was happy to discover. The meal ends in a separate lounge area, where you relax on a couch with a tisane and mignardises, which I found especially pleasant and thoughtful. Overall, a fantastic experience from start to finish. I will definitely be going back. (5 stars)

An unforgettable dining experience in Brooklyn. My husband and I agreed this was one of our favorite meals and we eat out a lot! The tasting menu flows effortlessly from one course to the next, each dish thoughtfully presented and full of subtle surprises. The service is attentive in a way that feels natural, and the atmosphere manages to be elegant while still completely comfortable. People will rave about the food, and rightfully so, but what truly sets Restaurant Yuu apart is the personal touch. After dinner, we were invited to relax in the lounge for tea and additional desserts, which made the night feel even more special. We were not rushed out like many other restaurants. The chef even stepped outside into the freezing cold just to thank us for coming. That level of care is something you don’t forget. (5 stars)

A perfect balance of Japanese and French sensibility. Each dish was elegant, thoughtful, and beautifully composed. The wine pairing elevated the experience without overpowering it. I recommend sitting at the counter to fully appreciate the choreography of the kitchen. Definitely going back soon! (5 stars)
search_text: Restaurant Yuu Restaurant YUU is a modern French dining establishment located in Greenpoint, Brooklyn, offering a unique blend of traditional Japanese hospitality and high-quality French cuisine. With an intimate setting of only 18 seats, the restaurant provides a serene atmosphere that reflects both the calm and youthful culture of the neighborhood. Guests can expect a thoughtfully curated dining experience complemented by modern interiors and exquisite Arita ware tableware. Restaurant YUU specializes in a new form of French cuisine, influenced by traditional Japanese 'OMOTENASHI'. The menu features a creative approach to classic French dishes, showcasing the talents of passionate young chefs. Restaurant YUU was founded by Chef Yuu Shimano, who aims to redefine French cuisine through a Japanese lens. Amuse Bouche - Duck Consommé, Black Truffle; Foie Gras Miso Marinade, Honeycrisp Apple; Langoustine, Beet Smoked Salmon - White Asparagus, Ikura, Yogurt Sauce, Dill; King Crab, White Miso, Yuzu, Caviar Uni - Hokkaido Uni, Onion Velouté, Uni Espuma Carabinero - Carabinero, Pear, Celeriac, Vinaigrette; Shirako (Cod Milt), Uni, Chardonnay, Tomato Abalone - Abalone Risotto, Abalone Liver Butter, Seaweed Powder Sawara - Sawara, Pistachio Emulsion, Watercress, Bergamot Ponzu Restaurant Yuu is where Japanese omakase meets French cuisine in the most thoughtful and refined way. This was truly a one-of-a-kind dining experience — every course felt intentional, balanced, and beautifully executed. Chef Yuu is an artist. The precision, creativity, and harmony of flavors were on another level. What made the evening even more special was the unique collaboration with a chef from Edinbane Lodge from the Isle of Skye in Scotland — such a rare and inspired partnership that added depth and character to the experience. We celebrated our 15th wedding anniversary here, and we couldn’t have chosen a better place for such a meaningful night. The atmosphere, the storytelling through food, and the overall care put into the experience made it unforgettable. A truly exceptional restaurant. (5 stars) Yuu in Williamsburg delivers an excellent dining experience blending French technique with subtle Japanese influence. The service was absolutely top-notch: attentive, polished, and perfectly paced. The atmosphere is breezy and calm, with very little noise. Seating is aligned so you’re not distracted by other guests, and facing the open kitchen adds a wonderful sense of theater — it truly feels like part of the experience. The tasting menu is excellent, with around ten courses that feel thoughtfully curated. The crab and the sweetbread were standouts and among my favorite dishes of the night. The salade de homard was very good, though it mixed quite a few savory elements — it might even benefit from being split into two separate dishes. The grouper was cooked to perfection, as was the pie, with an impressively thin, delicate crust. We’re not big dessert people, but both desserts were surprisingly great — light, fresh, and well balanced. I took the wine pairing, which was not my favorite but more from a taste than quality perspective. Pairing is expensive but they serve high-end wines which I was happy to discover. The meal ends in a separate lounge area, where you relax on a couch with a tisane and mignardises, which I found especially pleasant and thoughtful. Overall, a fantastic experience from start to finish. I will definitely be going back. (5 stars) An unforgettable dining experience in Brooklyn. My husband and I agreed this was one of our favorite meals and we eat out a lot! The tasting menu flows effortlessly from one course to the next, each dish thoughtfully presented and full of subtle surprises. The service is attentive in a way that feels natural, and the atmosphere manages to be elegant while still completely comfortable. People will rave about the food, and rightfully so, but what truly sets Restaurant Yuu apart is the personal touch. After dinner, we were invited to relax in the lounge for tea and additional desserts, which made the night feel even more special. We were not rushed out like many other restaurants. The chef even stepped outside into the freezing cold just to thank us for coming. That level of care is something you don’t forget. (5 stars) A perfect balance of Japanese and French sensibility. bio_text: Rezdôra is a distinguished Italian restaurant located in New York City's Flatiron neighborhood, celebrated for its authentic cuisine inspired by Emilia Romagna. With a warm and inviting atmosphere, the restaurant offers a refined dining experience that emphasizes traditional Italian hospitality, making it a perfect destination for both casual diners and culinary enthusiasts alike. The menu at Rezdôra focuses on house-made pasta, showcasing the rich culinary heritage of Emilia Romagna. Guests can enjoy a regional pasta tasting menu and a vegetarian tasting menu, both highlighting traditional techniques and high-quality ingredients. The wine selection features Northern Italian wines that complement the dishes beautifully. Rezdôra is a New York Times three-star restaurant and a Michelin Star recipient from Chef Stefano Secchi and Partner David Switzer, recognized for its excellence since 2021.
menu_items: Caseificio Fett' Unta - toasted bread with extra virgin oil - $10
Burrata - Prosciutto di parma "24 mesi" - $28
Burrata Reale - miatake mushroom, black truffle & parsley - $32
Stracciatella con Fave - favas in three ways - $24
Della Zona Gnocco Fritto - Prosciutto di parma, mortadella & guanciale - $18
Affettati Misti - prosciutto di parma, mortadella, capocollo, guanciale, pesto modenese, robiolo, parmigiano & tigelle - $38
review_snippets: Rezdora was an experience and I would strongly recommend it. The standout was definitely the Nonna Walking Through the Forest, 100 percent recommend. The desserts were incredible and absolutely worth ordering. The service was also incredible and very welcoming. I do not often comment on service, but it felt like everyone at the restaurant was on the same team and moving together. The endive salad was very good as well. Now a few things to avoid. The mushroom pasta was maybe one of the worst things I have ever put in my mouth. It was horrendous, just one black clump of noodles stuck together. Do not order this. The Gramigna Giallo e Verde was quite good, but the portion was weak, and I wish there had been a little more, especially with that yummy sausage in it. Finally, the toasted bread was very weak, an excuse for garlic bread. Bread with just some olive oil is honestly a ripoff and could have been better presented. The Gnocco Fritto with prosciutto di Parma, mortadella, and guanciale was honestly just salty and lacked flavor. It felt incomplete. (3 stars)

My husband scored us a reservation to Rezdôra as a Christmas present so that we could finally experience our first Michelin star restaurant, and what a place to start at! First, I really appreciated that we could enjoy a fine dining experience without it feeling pretentious. The vibe was relaxed, and our server was so friendly. He helped answer any questions we had, and we definitely didn’t leave hungry. We stated with a Parmesan tasting, then went into the pasta tasting, which was timed well between courses. Though they were smaller portions, we were happy to experience a variety of their offerings, especially with it being our first time! We split a steak entree as well, which was cooked perfectly. We were glad to have the extra protein to feel fully satisfied. We split the tiramisu for dessert, and it was one of the best I’ve ever had! Truly a memorable meal and a treat for date night in the city. We would definitely make another trip from CT to experience Rezdôra again! (5 stars)

Rezdora is wonderful, and I’d absolutely recommend it for an elevated Italian dining experience. The space itself is charming and intimate, with roughly 15 tables, and things like coat and bag check are always a bonus in my book. As for the food, there wasn’t a single dish I wouldn’t recommend. Everything ranged from good to excellent. The spaghetti allo scoglio and gramigna giallo e verde were the clear standouts. The rest of the menu was solid and well-executed, though not really groundbreaking. I have minor nitpicks about certain dishes but that’s about it. So, does it deserve its Michelin star worth setting an alarm to snag a reservation? Debatable… but it’s undeniably a great meal. (4 stars)

One of the worst experiences I've ever had in NY. I was expecting so much more that it really disapointed me. Servers were not paying attention at all. The appetizer came really quick (and was good), but the main courses took 45 minutes (30 after the appetizer). The pasta was al dente, BUT, the anolini dough was to thick, and raw on the edges. The filling tasty, but not enough, same with the sauce. I even had to ask for salt because the dish was tasteless. Pasta cooked without any salt also. The Waiter was refusing to grate cheese, even though asking twice. The lobster pasta had 5 tiny pieces of lobster and it was gummy. Sauces not emulsified with the pasta. On top of it all, I had to ask 2 times how long would it take for the main dishes. And it took 45 min to get these, which is not a great pasta. The music was really loud and had nothing to do with the ambience. After asking for the check, I told the waiter I was really surprised that nobody even asked how the food was, and he simple replied "tap your card here". Really rude. Honestly, I wouldn't recommend, and I'm really sad we had this expierence because I was really looking forward to try this restaurant. (1 stars)

bio_text: Risbo is a vibrant French rotisserie restaurant and bar located in the heart of Prospect Lefferts Garden, Brooklyn. This Michelin-recommended establishment offers a welcoming atmosphere where guests can enjoy healthy comfort food, natural wines, and a beautiful garden setting. With a focus on community and inclusivity, Risbo serves as a neighborhood spot for those seeking nourishment for both body and soul, open daily for lunch, dinner, and brunch. Risbo specializes in French rotisserie cuisine, featuring marinated and dry-brined proteins that are cooked to perfection. The menu includes a variety of roasted meats such as chicken, pork, duck, leg of lamb, and whole branzino, complemented by seasonal plant-based sides. The restaurant offers a unique Brooklyn twist on classic French dishes, with options available for lunch, dinner, and brunch. Established in September 2017 by owner and executive Chef Boris Ginet, Risbo draws inspiration from Chef Boris' Parisian roots and his experiences living in New York City for nearly three decades. The restaurant reflects a blend of global influences and celebrates the diverse community of Brooklyn.

review_snippets: Got the chicken, mashed potatoes and sautéed greens platter $20. A bit overpriced for portion size. I don’t like how you can’t seamlessly sub out different sides without incurring lots of extra cost. Additionally the house made aioli doesn’t seem to be the right dipping sauce for the chicken if it doesn’t come with crispy potatoes or fries or anything. The sautéed greens were fairly tasteless but the mashed potatoes were good. I def recommend that. (3 stars)

I picked up dinner to go, the platter with roasted chicken and everything was amazing. It was a lot of food so ended up making two meals out of it. I especially loved the hummus and cauliflower that was included. The food is well worth the price and it's a super cute place inside. (5 stars)
Love! Our food was amazing, and we will be back! The chicken and waffles are...*chef's kiss* and I highly recommend stopping by for brunch. (5 stars)

I could eat this place every day. Hands down one of the Best restaurants in New York. Juicy Rotisserie chicken .. Best Mac and cheese ...roasted veggies... creamed mashed potatoes. Love the dining and atmosphere. Everyone super friendly. (5 stars)

bio_text: Roberta's is a vibrant dining destination known for its exceptional Neapolitan-inspired pizzas and a diverse menu that celebrates seasonal ingredients. With locations in NYC and LA, the restaurant offers a lively atmosphere that reflects the eclectic spirit of Bushwick, making it a must-visit for pizza enthusiasts and food lovers alike. Roberta's specializes in wood-fired Neapolitan pizza, complemented by house-cured meats, handmade pasta, and seasonal seafood and vegetable dishes. The menu is designed to highlight the best seasonal ingredients, ensuring a fresh and innovative dining experience.
menu_items: MARINATED OLIVES - $9
CHEESE PLATE - St. Stephen (Cow), Four Fat Fowl, NY, Clothbound Cheddar (Cow), Cabot, VT, Bayley Hazen Blue (Raw Cow), Jasper Hill Farm, VT - $8 / $22

review_snippets: Great all around. Came off peak time and ordered a fresh Bee Sting as many have reviewed. It did not disappoint and this would be my go-to pizza many times! People around me were drinking and the drinks looked fantastic. I'm sure the rest of the food is great as well since my pizza was so good. Would love to come again and try a different pizza and any other foods. New York has so many good restaurants and I'm glad I found this one! (5 stars)

I met my friend in NYC, she was coming from Connecticut and I was coming from New Jersey and we stumbled apron Roberta’s at Penn Station. We were so happy we did, from the moment we walked in to the moment we left! Our server was Camilo, the food runner was Nisaun, the bar tender was Hadji, they made the experience even better everything was great! We had a small issues which was corrected immediately and we could not have been happier! When we were ready for our check Jema, not sure if she was the GM or AGM came out to make sure all was good! She was just as amazing as her staff! Please keep this staff, now a days good staff is so had to find, I know because I am constantly looking! It is so wonderful to eat at a restaurant where the staff is happy and like there jobs! Thank you for a great meal and experience! We will definitely be back soon! (5 stars)

Really delicious meal here. I had heard a lot about the pizza, so was excited to try it. However, the pizza was actually not the star of the meal. The stracciatella and anchovies was far and away the strongest item we had. The caesar salad was also phenomenal, but the cheese was amazing. The pizza was decent as well, but if we came back, we would likely lean on the appetizers more! (5 stars)

Roberta’s Pizza at Penny Station is such a hidden gem in New York! The location is super convenient, and the pizza… oh, the pizza is absolutely delicious — perfectly made, full of flavor, and with that authentic taste that wins you over right away. What I really love is the little details: they have a bathroom (which is rare around here!), and right outside there’s a lovely square where you can sit and enjoy your slice in the open air. It makes the whole experience even more charming, with that laid-back city vibe. It’s the kind of spot that combines convenience, amazing food, and a touch of charm in the atmosphere. A place I truly loved discovering and one that’s already on my list of must-stops! 🌿🍕 (5 stars)

bio_text: Rolo's is a modern American restaurant located in Ridgewood, Queens, offering a warm and inviting atmosphere that emphasizes community and comfort. The restaurant features a wood-fired grill, creating a unique dining experience centered around essential cooking with a focus on seasonal and local ingredients. Rolo's specializes in modern American cuisine, highlighting house-smoked meats and dishes prepared over a wood fire grill. The menu is designed to showcase the best of seasonal produce, ensuring freshness and quality in every dish.
menu_items: Wood-fired polenta bread - olive oil & flaky salt - $8
Housemade mortadella - $15
Prosciutto di parma - $18
Fennel salami - $12
Stracciatella cheese - cheese, silk, chili, sumac - $13

review_snippets: Delicious delicious delicious. I’m so glad we decided to dine here on our trip. The food was phenomenal. I don’t think there is a bad thing on the menu. The tortellini and the lasagna were so good. The fish was fresh and so yummy. The polenta bread with the chili butter was so good and the mortadella was delish as well. (5 stars)

I went there earlier when it first opened and they had their fresh pasta market. But I recently came back for my birthday and was pleasantly surprised on how everything tasted. Definitely get each of the polenta bread as the appetizers are small portion sizes. I had the ravioli pasta dish and it was only like 8 pieces which was disappointing of a portion size. Food was however delicious. They also do not do complimentary dessert. (3 stars)

My best friend and I have been frequenting Rolos since we watched that one video about how their lasagna is made. It's been a special treat when we can manage to get a table (one that's well worth the wait). The staff here is truly incredible. A lot of restaurants in the city can be condescending and rude, but the entire staff at Rolos is beyond kind and accommodating. If you're able to snag a res, which we were today, you're in for a real treat. When I put in the res notes that this would be our last dinner together given my leaving NYC, the staff made it truly special! Standout dishes: chili polenta bread, cheeseburger, skirt steak, and of course, the lasagna! While we went back and forth about where to have our "last supper" as our server called it, we knew Rolo's was the only right choice. The food is always consistent, outstanding, and a memorable experience. I couldn't have imagined a better way to close out my NY days. Thank you so much to the Rolos staff for such a considerate, caring, and extraordinary experience. (5 stars)

Made reservations walked in and was pleasantly surprised..this is a busy establishment reservations are recommended..Natalie who was our waitress was an absolute doll. So informative with a wealth of knowledge about the food. The food hands down was a ten out of ten. We ordered the crispy potatoes for the table, yum and yum. A second order was made immediately don't judge. I ordered the eggs with the polenta bread sooo good.my friend ordered the French toast which was to die for..need I say more. The food is very filling and so very delicious. (5 stars)

But I recently came back for my birthday and was pleasantly surprised on how everything tasted. Definitely get each of the polenta bread as the appetizers are small portion sizes. I had the ravioli pasta dish and it was only like 8 pieces which was disappointing of a portion size. Food was however delicious. They also do not do complimentary dessert. (3 stars) My best friend and I have been frequenting Rolos since we watched that one video about how their lasagna is made. It's been a special treat when we can manage to get a table (one that's well worth the wait). The staff here is truly incredible. A lot of restaurants in the city can be condescending and rude, but the entire staff at Rolos is beyond kind and accommodating. If you're able to snag a res, which we were today, you're in for a real treat. When I put in the res notes that this would be our last dinner together given my leaving NYC, the staff made it truly special! Standout dishes: chili polenta bread, cheeseburger, skirt steak, and of course, the lasagna! While we went back and forth about where to have our "last supper" as our server called it, we knew Rolo's was the only right choice. The food is always consistent, outstanding, and a memorable experience. I couldn't have imagined a better way to close out my NY days. Thank you so much to the Rolos staff for such a considerate, caring, and extraordinary experience. (5 stars) Made reservations walked in and was pleasantly surprised..this is a busy establishment reservations are recommended..Natalie who was our waitress was an absolute doll. So informative with a wealth of knowledge about the food. The food hands down was a ten out of ten. We ordered the crispy potatoes for the table, yum and yum. A second order was made immediately don't judge. I ordered the eggs with the polenta bread sooo good.my friend ordered the French toast which was to die for..need I say more. The food is very filling and so very delicious. (5 stars)

bio_text: Rose Marie is a charming bar located in Brooklyn, NY, offering a cozy atmosphere that pays homage to classic Americana cuisine. With a focus on comfort food and a welcoming vibe, it serves as a perfect spot for casual gatherings, featuring a selection of martinis, cold beers, and a curated wine list. The culinary focus at Rose Marie is slightly Southern, with an ode to olde Americana foods. The menu includes comfort classics such as patty melts, fried catfish, and cheese curds, designed to evoke nostalgia and warmth. Little sister to Yellow Rose, Rose Marie is named after a song from The Basement Tapes.

Old Bay Marinated Castelvetrano Olives - $10
