review_snippets: 3 out of 5 stars Rose Marie has a super cozy atmosphere and the kind of warm, welcoming energy you want from a neighborhood spot in Williamsburg. The staff was genuinely great and made us feel right at home the entire time. I came in knowing they are well known for the patty melt, but we didn’t try it on this visit. I went with a drink to start and it was a little watered down for me, so I ended up switching to a beer which worked out better. For food, the pork chop had good flavor but it was slightly overcooked and could have used a bit more seasoning. A sprinkle of flaked sea salt would have lifted the whole dish. Portions overall felt like they could be a touch bigger. The little gem salad was fine but missing something. Some beets for contrast would have helped, and the cheese they used didn’t really complement the greens. The chicken cutlet was really solid. Crispy and well seasoned, but it still felt like it needed one more element. Honestly it would shine in a brioche bun as a sandwich. Overall it was a decent first visit but a little underwhelming. I would come back to try more items on the menu because the place itself feels great and the service was excellent. Just hoping the food hits a bit stronger next time. (3 stars)

I know this is popping up on all the lists right now but it is soooo deserved. The patty melt was really spectacular and so are the potatoes. It’s sort of classic American food but done so well. Everything is full of flavor and I loved my pickled tomato martini! Definitely a great addition to the neighborhood! (5 stars)

Overall thoroughly enjoyed my experience here! It was a really busy night so we walked in and sat at the bar. Can’t remember the bartender’s name, but he was such a fun person to chat with. Also really kind. There was one drink with gin that I didn’t end up liking and he switched it for the passionfruit spritz (10/10 drink). My friend got the patty melt, which was solid dish for $18. The star of the night was 100% the flounder perfectly fried and the sauce was everything. Would also recommend the corn and loaded potatoes for apps (5 stars)

Loved everything about this place! The food, atmosphere, wine, and service! We had the absolute pleasure to be served my Margret! She was amazing, attentive and welcoming. She really elevated our experience. The food was divine, the party melt was next level and all must try. (5 stars)

bio_text: Rosella is a dining establishment that embodies a commitment to sustainability and taste, creating a unique atmosphere where the interconnectedness of our ecosystem is celebrated. The restaurant offers a seasonal menu that features both beloved classics and innovative dishes, complemented by a thoughtfully curated wine list that emphasizes regional selections. Rosella focuses on sustainable seafood and locally sourced ingredients, highlighting often overlooked domestic species. The menu is designed to reflect seasonal availability and includes dishes that are both environmentally conscious and flavorful. Rosella was founded by Chef Jeffrey Miller and Managing Partner TJ Provenzano, who bring their extensive culinary experience to the restaurant.

review_snippets: Our favorite sushi place and maybe restaurant in NY 🤔. We had high expectations and they were delivered. The service was good, they had good recommendations except that they told us not to repeat and now we want to go again to eat their tuna hand roll. Our ranking was: 1. Tuna hand roll 2. Bagel on Hudson 3. Ceviche 4. Miso Carrot Cake 5. Fish slider 6. Nigiri’s 7. Spicy tuna toll 8. Coconut ice cream 9.Salmon avocado rolls (5 stars)

Took my out-of-town parents here so they could experience fine dining. They had an amazing time—excellent food, phenomenal service and a cozy but not cramped space. Our server was one the most knowledgeable I’ve ever had. She even had anecdotes about the local farmers who sourced one of the ingredients. And don’t skip dessert! We were not rushed at all, which I find to be rare in New York. I highly recommend this place! (5 stars)

It's no secret that Rosella is an East Village standout, but it's taken me a while to visit finally. I met a friend for an obscenely early dinner, but we were glad for it. There were still plenty of people in the dining room, but the staff were super attentive. Most of the seating is counter seating, either in the window, at the bar, or in the back over the sushi chef. There doesn't seem to be a bad seat in the house. There is a happy hour menu, which we ordered a couple of things from, but we were primarily focused on the fish. To get a feel for the menu, we ordered several things. The tuna with pesto and watermelon was terrific, a must-try. My friend said he never seeks out pesto, but this was something special. Next up were two spicy tuna handrolls, which were as promised, spicy and with a nice crunch added for texture. Next up came the sushi, and while my friends were a little delayed by the kitchen, our server was quick to offer us their cucumber salad with yogurt and microgreens to keep us munching. All were delicious and consumed quickly. In terms of beverages, we didn't stray from sake, which was offered on the happy hour menu, but there were many options, including a house-made orange wine from LI. All in, this is a great place to meet a friend, and have a quick bite or sit and chat while you graze the menu. Either way, you will not be disappointed by anything; it's a lovely spot. (5 stars)

What a special dining experience! Don’t be fooled by the small and unassuming format, this place is special. Unique flavors in the best way every time that are different in a good way not just for the sake of being different. Speaking of sake, some of the best sake pairings I’ve ever had! Plus it’s just oozing with an air of cool hospitality that is so rare. Every dish was incredible I truly can’t pick a favorite. Nothing is “too weird”, it all works way better than you’re expecting so just go for it. (5 stars)

bio_text: Ruffian is a pioneering wine bar and chef's table that specializes in Eastern European natural wines and seasonal dishes, creating a vibrant and immersive dining experience. Established in 2016, it has become a beloved neighborhood fixture, recognized as a NY Times Critic's Pick and awarded a Michelin Bib Gourmand each year since 2020. The restaurant offers a dynamic atmosphere where guests can enjoy a variety of tasting and à la carte menus, curated wine flights, and engaging wine classes. Ruffian focuses on Eastern European cuisine, featuring seasonal dishes that complement its extensive natural wine selection. The menu includes both tasting and à la carte options, emphasizing creative small plates and dynamic pairings. Ruffian has been a neighborhood fixture since 2016 and has received a Michelin Bib Gourmand each year since 2020.

review_snippets: Perfect experience! Exquisite wines, delicious food, attentive service. Some places should be much more hyped than they are, such as this one! We ordered the duck pastrami and the mushroom dumplings, both were delicious! Bread was so fresh. (5 stars)

great eastern european wine. loved the variety and quality of natural wine. good service and fun vibe. love the bar vibe and 2 sides of the restaurant. would recommend for a drink before dinner. (5 stars)

A true East Village gem! Cozy ambiance, amazing selection of natural European wines, and delicious food. What really makes it special is the staff - bartender, servers, and chef are all so warm and welcoming. Highly recommend! (5 stars)

Ruffian was an incredible experience overall, from their delicious bites to their extensive wine list! There are sparkling wines, orange wines, white wines, and even pink wines! The sparkling wine pictured below was SO crisp and also subtly sweet. A perfect combination for summer. The menu primarily has shareable plates so I would order a lot if you’re a big party. The portions were quite small. The quality of the produce was top tier. We could also tell that they put a lot of thought into the flavor combos. One of my favorites probably had to be the one with beets. I would go back again and again and again!! (5 stars)

bio_text: Runner & Stone is a vibrant restaurant and bakery located in the Gowanus neighborhood of Brooklyn, co-founded by Chef Chris Pizzulli and Head Baker Peter Endriss in December 2012. The establishment embodies a communal dining experience, emphasizing the connection between cooking, eating, and the local community. With a focus on seasonal ingredients and a warm, approachable atmosphere, Runner & Stone invites guests to enjoy hand-crafted food and beverages in a convivial setting. The culinary focus at Runner & Stone includes naturally leavened breads, viennoiseries, and a menu that features seasonal salads, soups, sandwiches, and house-made fresh pastas. The restaurant emphasizes the use of local whole grain flours, dairy, and fruit, showcasing a commitment to responsible sourcing and traditional techniques. Runner & Stone was co-founded in December 2012 by Chef Chris Pizzulli and Head Baker Peter Endriss. The name 'Runner & Stone' refers to the two stones used in traditional milling, symbolizing the restaurant's philosophy and connection to its historic Gowanus location, near the site of New York City's first tide water grist mill.

review_snippets: Ate here recently for my birthday and everyday was so delicious! We ordered a half portion of the squid ink calamarata, roasted beet salad and two specials crispy fried sea bass over white beans and a duck confit rotolo. Everything tastes so delicious and my favorite was the squid ink pasta (5 stars)
The Beet Salad is AMAZING and the best you'll ever have (nothing beets it). Di's service was friendly, honest and welcoming - give her a raise. :-) (5 stars)

I stopped by their stand at the McCarren Park farmers market and all of their baked goods looked amazing, but I grabbed a chocolate almond croissant for $6.25. Steep price but this is one of the best croissants I have ever eaten. Why do more places not mix the almond and chocolate together?!?!? This is one of the best things I have ever eaten. (5 stars)

The restaurant has a nice atmosphere and interesting decor. The service is great. The pretzel was somewhat dry. The arancini was good, a bit dense, the sauce was flavorful. The squid ink pasta was slightly overcooked, both the pasta and the squid and the sauce didn't have a lot of flavor. Overall the food was fine but nothing was memorable. (3 stars)

bio_text: Runner Up is an intimate American café located in Brooklyn, NY, offering a cozy dining experience with just 12 seats at the bar. The restaurant serves a pre-fixe dinner menu that emphasizes seasonal ingredients and a warm atmosphere, making it a perfect spot for a casual yet refined meal. The culinary focus at Runner Up is on American cuisine with a modern twist. The menu features a pre-fixe format, offering three courses for $50, highlighting dishes like roasted cabbage and Spanish mackerel. Signature techniques include the use of seasonal produce and creative flavor pairings. Runner Up is the sibling neighborhood restaurant to WINNER Bakery.

review_snippets: Mili’s pop up here was outstanding. Truly a great experience. The rating should go to Jose and Alexis. The dishes were simple but beautifully balanced and every detail accounted for. We loved them all. I think the cheese dish was one of my favourite things I ate all year. The pork was expertly cooked and so flavourful. Would love to come again to any popup here because the space is also lovely and intimate. Thanks for a great meal! (5 stars)

This place is stellar. We went for Valentine's Day, and the tasting menu was legitimately some of the best food I've had in New York. The food was inventive and delicious. It's small and intimate, which gives it a lovely atmosphere. Perfect for date night or when you want a damn good meal. I will be going back regularly. (5 stars)

runner up is SUCH a wonderful place. snagged a last minute resy after eating winner sandwiches for a year, and WOW. food was outstanding — a nice meal, without being too stuffy / over fancy. love the intimacy of the space & the experience of sitting at the counter while everything is being fired. super accommodating to allergies, too. we ordered the focaccia+whipped ricotta, meats & cheeses, the bitter greens salad, and the short rib. short rib came with a bowl of baby purple lettuce, pickled radishes and cucumbers to wrap the meat into. Loni & Freddie were so welcoming and passionate, we had a lovely time! (5 stars)

Today I visited this cafe with my colleagues (a group of about 20 people). We sat on the second floor, it’s a converted apartment, but the atmosphere is simply unique and authentic, which I’m delighted with. Service at the highest level. The food is incredibly tasty, I liked the salads, especially the yellow beet salads. It should be noted that I ate it for the first time and was pleasantly surprised at how tasty it was. My colleagues were delighted with the pork and even took extra. The chicken is definitely delicious. In general, this is an ideal place for a company to have a great lunch or dinner. (5 stars)

My colleagues were delighted with the pork and even took extra. The chicken is definitely delicious. In general, this is an ideal place for a company to have a great lunch or dinner. (5 stars)

bio_text: Russ & Daughters Café is a celebrated establishment that embodies the rich culinary heritage of New York City, offering a warm and inviting atmosphere for both locals and visitors. The café is renowned for its dedication to quality and tradition, providing a unique dining experience that pays homage to the iconic Russ & Daughters appetizing store. The café specializes in Jewish deli cuisine, featuring a menu that includes classic bagels, smoked fish, and traditional spreads. Guests can enjoy a variety of dishes in a casual dining format, with an emphasis on fresh, high-quality ingredients and time-honored recipes. Russ & Daughters has a long-standing legacy, having been established in 1914, and is known for its commitment to preserving the cultural significance of Jewish culinary traditions.
review_snippets: Russ and Daughters has been feeding the Lower East Side since 1914 and the cafe on Orchard Street is the sit-down extension of everything that made the original appetizing shop legendary. The smoked salmon and cream cheese on a fresh bagel is perfection in its simplest form. The fish is silky the cream cheese is hand-whipped and the bagel has that perfect New York density that you cannot find anywhere else on earth. I have eaten bagels in a hundred cities and nothing comes close to what Russ and Daughters puts on the plate. The matzo ball soup is the benchmark warming golden with a matzo ball that is fluffy and dense at the same time which should be impossible but here we are. The egg cream is a New York institution and they make it the old-fashioned way. The room is simple and bright with tiles and a counter that pays respect to the original shop without trying to be a museum. This is living history. Four generations of the Russ family have kept this standard and the fact that the line is still out the door more than a century later tells you everything about quality and commitment. New York food culture starts here. Not at the trendy spots that open and close every year. Here at the place that has been doing one thing better than anyone else for over a hundred years. That is the standard. That is Russ and Daughters. (5 stars)

Had a great time! Loved the food and vibe. Bar service / tender was very attentative. Visiting from UK. I could not find any faults. Tge Kippered Salmon was different/ interesting. Bought some merchandise (a mug). Sorry as ate a bit before taking the pics 😞 (5 stars)

Save your time and money and don’t eat here. The wait wasn’t bad on New Year’s Day, they said a half hour and it was about 20 minutes total. We were excited for the food given the Anthony Bourdain endorsement, but it was incredibly disappointing. The kreplach was the only saving factor, it was delicious but the bagels and the Pastrami Russ were under mediocre. The gluten free bagel should not be called a bagel. I’m an advocate for if you can’t do it well, don’t do it at all. The gluten free bagel was crumbly, dense, dry, and flavorless. From the first bite I was disappointed. (On the left in the overhead photo, in the front in the other photo) The pastrami salmon was not particularly interesting in flavor and there was hardly any of it. The bites largely tasted of sauerkraut. The pickle was actually bad, I couldn’t eat it. My partner said the pretzel bagel was just fine, absolutely nothing special. Neither of us finished our food. For $25 a bagel, it was incredibly disappointing. Overpriced and overhyped, I wouldn’t send anyone here. (2 stars)

Ok COOK Rus & his highly highly skilled daughters. Wow. 10 stars. Don’t leave the continent of North America without trying the Kreplach. I’d sacrifice running water for a week to eat that again. The latkes are very good. The bagel & pastrami cured smoked salmon slapped. The coffee is really good coffee. But I repeat. The Kreplach. Get your hands on that asap pls. It has no business being that good. Their gluten free bagel is the best I’ve ever had. We got there 9:40am on a Saturday and waited around 35 minutes for a table (waitlist via text). Very reasonable. The service was top tier. Sorry to our server for my friend accidentally flexing her income. She didn’t understand your comment about the floor lol. (5 stars)

bio_text: Saga is a premier dining destination located in a historic Art Deco tower at 70 Pine Street, offering breathtaking views of the New York skyline. Since its opening in 2021, the restaurant has garnered critical acclaim, including two Michelin stars, for its innovative approach to fine dining. Under the leadership of Executive Chef Charlie Mitchell, Saga provides an intimate and sophisticated atmosphere where each multi-course tasting menu is a narrative of emotion and culinary craftsmanship. Saga specializes in a multi-course tasting menu that emphasizes bold yet refined flavors. The cuisine is inspired by a blend of nostalgia and classic techniques, utilizing humble ingredients elevated to new heights. Each dish is thoughtfully crafted to tell a unique story. Opened in 2021 by Chef Jamal James Kent, Saga has maintained its Michelin two-star status since its first year. Chef Charlie Mitchell became the Executive Chef in July 2024, continuing the restaurant's legacy of pushing culinary boundaries.
review_snippets: A hidden gem!! Beautiful location, amazing hospitality. As soon as we got there we were greeted with a drink from the bar. The experience wasn’t rushed at all and the view is breathtaking. Everything we tasted was delicious but the deserts were another level of perfection! All the cocktails 100/10, shout out to Tony ! He’s such a gem !! We asked for a list of places to visit after saga since we wanted to experience night life in NYC and the server came through with a list of recommendations. Overall we had the best experience at Saga and will be back next time we are in NYC (5 stars)

Saga offers an unforgettable dining experience. The seasonal tasting menu was beautifully curated, with each course thoughtfully presented and full of bold yet refined flavors. The service was exceptional — attentive, knowledgeable, and perfectly paced throughout the evening. The atmosphere feels elegant and intimate, with stunning panoramic views that truly elevate the entire experience high above the Financial District and New York City skyline. 🍽️ Seasonal, multi-course tasting menu with ingredient-driven dishes 🌆 Spectacular city views ✨ Top-notch service and polished ambiance — ideal for celebrations An excellent spot for birthdays and special occasions. Everything was perfectly executed, making it a truly memorable fine-dining experience. Highly recommended for an unforgettable evening. (5 stars)

Saga is a remarkable top tier 2 star Michelin rated restaurant that is big on flavor & views. Perched high on the 63rd floor, this incredible restaurant wows with its tasters menu & spectacular 360 degree views of NYC! We had the honor of meeting the man behind the creations, Chef Charlie Mitchell. What a class act! Our dishes were awesome, our server was great, the views were spectacular and our evening was a memory we will not forget. We highly recommend Saga NYC! (5 stars)

Come here for a special occasion. The service is exceptional—from the booking process through arrival. I fell in love with the entire dining experience: perfectly paced courses and perfectly sized portions. The views were spectacular as well. Thank you Saga for a memorable and truly special night. (5 stars)

bio_text: Sailor is a charming neighborhood bistro located in Fort Greene, Brooklyn, offering a warm and inviting atmosphere for diners. Led by the talented Chef April Bloomfield and Gabriel Stulman, the restaurant is part of the esteemed Happy Cooking family, known for its commitment to quality and community. Sailor focuses on a contemporary American cuisine, emphasizing fresh, seasonal ingredients. The menu features a variety of dishes that reflect the bistro's casual yet refined dining experience. Sailor is a new addition to the Happy Cooking family of restaurants, which includes Jeffrey's Grocery, Joseph Leonard, and Fairfax.
menu_items: Egg T onnato + Chives - $6
Roasted Nuts with Bourbon + Rosemary - $6
Fried Anchovy with Sage + Lemon - $17
Ribollita with Cranberry Beans + Kale - $15
Green Salad with Oregano Vinaigrette - $17
Caesar Salad with Parmesan + Croutons - $20
review_snippets: Such a cute little brunch spot. We decided to share everything, which felt like the right move because we could sample each dish. The burger was delicious, cooked perfectly medium rare with that juicy, just right center. But my personal favorite? The Turkish eggs. Absolute saucy perfection. They came with a puffy flatbread that paired amazingly with all that rich, flavorful goodness, though I do wish the bread had been bigger. The sauce was just too good, and I needed more to soak it all up. The true star of the meal, though, was the French toast. Thick and drenched in a maple syrup with a vanilla cream dollop. I highly recommend ordering it almost as a dessert and eating it right away. We waited a bit while finishing the savory dishes, so it wasn’t piping hot by the time we dug in, still delicious, but it definitely would’ve been even better warmer. Definitely a spot worth returning to 🍳 (5 stars)

We had a really great experience here, the food was excellent and the atmosphere was great. The inside is decorated with lots of ships and nautical-themed items. The bar itself feels a bit like a ship with almost gantry-like washrooms. The burger was fantastic, among the very best I’ve had in NYC and while maybe not top 3, worth a mention to anyone who likes burgers. The cocktails were also great - while I don’t think they were the very highest in mixology, they were delicious and inventive. The orchard margarita was very interesting and tasted super unique. (5 stars)

I would give this a 4.5. The waitress was a sweetheart and the atmosphere was beautiful—I loved all the decor. We started with the deviled eggs, sunchokes, and squid salad, and the appetizers were amazing. For entrées, I ordered the cod and my husband had the pork shoulder. The pork shoulder was absolutely delectable with a delicious sauce; however, with only olives on the plate, there wasn’t anything to soak up and fully enjoy the sauce. A mashed potato or even a piece of toast would have really elevated the dish. The cod was cooked perfectly—flaky, light, and fresh—but the flavor was a bit subtle and could have benefited from a sauce or crust to add more depth and punch. Overall, a lovely experience with excellent service and thoughtfully prepared dishes. (5 stars)

This was such a treat! A $100 brunch for two isn’t usually in our budget, but this time it was absolutely worth it. The French toast was our favorite—so delicious! I highly recommend it!!! The thick-cut bacon and fries were also amazing. The croque monsieur wasn’t my personal favorite, but it seemed to be a crowd favorite since everyone around us was ordering it. The décor and boat-inspired theme were adorable, and the atmosphere was a perfect 10/10. Highly recommend! (5 stars)

bio_text: Saint Julivert Fisherie is an award-winning coastal wine bar located in the charming neighborhood of Cobble Hill, Brooklyn. This French-inspired establishment offers a unique dining experience that transports guests to various coastal regions through its carefully curated menu and exceptional wine selection. With a focus on fresh, seasonal ingredients and a vibrant atmosphere, Saint Julivert serves as a local haven for seafood lovers and wine enthusiasts alike. The restaurant specializes in seafood, drawing inspiration from coastal ingredients and seaside wine regions around the world. The menu features a diverse array of global flavors, complemented by a chef-driven cocktail list. Saint Julivert emphasizes authenticity and innovation in its culinary offerings. Saint Julivert is curated by chefs Alex Raij and Eder Montero, known for their iconic establishments, including the Michelin-starred La Vara and Txikito. Their commitment to creating a seafood haven in Brooklyn has solidified Saint Julivert as a culinary gem.
menu_items: Spicy Peanuts - chile de árbol, shrimp salt - $6
Sorullitos - turmeric-spiced Puerto Rican hushpuppies, chili-caper mayo - $11
Whipped Mackerel - piri piri, dill, grilled sourdough - $14
Cantabric Anchovies - aged beet butter, salsa verde chaud-froid, pickled things - $21
Shiso Tacos - raw scallop, salsa macha, sweet pickled onion - $21
Head on Shrimp - flash fried, salt & pepper, yuzu mayo - $16
review_snippets: A quote from my boyfriend after our appetizers: "ill never be a mother, but i imagine this feeling is the equivalent of holding your child for the first time" My new fav spot, how this place isn't packed out is actually beyond me because it was easily one of the best meals I've ever had in New York and I've eaten a lottttt. Everything I could hope for from an NYC seafood restaurant comes alive here. Ambience is so nice lighting is perfect doesn't get too noisy but still feels alive, service is excellent, cozy but cool. The food is just outstanding, I literally recommend everything like truly. Each dish was like wow I've never had something like that before and I need it again and again. In fact, I went two days in a row because I just had to get some appetizers again and try some more mains. I'm actually obsessed. I would be here much more often if I lived somewhat closer, but I will with no hesitation make the trek from Manhattan anytime I start craving it. I honestly recommend every single dish that I have posted in this review (it's also every single dish that I've ordered in my times coming here) , but I think for me (i really love raw seafood) I can't go here without ordering the wild shrimp appetizer and the lobster tostada. The lobster tostada is one of the craziest things I've ever had I don't know how they made it taste like that and the textures (im salivating as i write) and they give you so much lobster i was swooning. Not that everything else isn't also perfection because it all really is in their own ways, but as a lobster lover this just tickled me. Love their drink menu, non alcoholic list is pretty limited but what they do offer is tasty, for low ABV they have a lot of options featuring sherry, sweet wines, and amaros etc Dessert was great im forgetting what it is called atm, but alongside the creamy looking one is their italian ice and flavors rotate. (5 stars)

This is our second time coming back to this restaurant. It’s a small cozy spot where I love sitting by the bar to see the action. The food was still amazing. It’s our first time trying the violet hour though. We should have totally done that the first time. $45 PP - we can choose 3 dishes each. It was a tasing menu where dishes were supposed to come in half portion. It’s definitely bigger than half portion, we feel it’s almost like 2/3 of a real portion. The 2 of us with 6 dishes to share - we were full! Great value! Will definitely do this again if we come back between 5-6. One star deducted to the service was because it seems we didn’t have a dedicated server. No one told us about violet hour nor special of the day x 2. We had to keep asking about it. Imagine if we didn’t overhead about the violet hour from the table next to us, we’d have totally missed it. So does the special of the day (5 stars)

The lighting is not photo friendly, so don't judge the dishes by my pics. The food was excellent. Don't skip the anchovies or the iberico steaklette. Cocktails were just as good and they even served me something off menu that turned out to be my favorite drink of the night. Excellent find in the neighborhood. (5 stars)

Incredible meal, no- experience. We got the chefs counter and were greeted by Winnie. She was helpful with an amazing drink recommendation. Then came the scallop tacos which I hear are only available on Friday/Saturday and Sunday if you’re feeling lucky (they run out)! The stars of the show were the seafood sausage and the squid. Can’t wait to go back! (5 stars)

bio_text: Sal Tang's is a Cantonese American restaurant located in Carroll Gardens, Brooklyn, offering a cozy and family-oriented dining experience. With a design that features classic old-school Chinese-American elements, including green and black vinyl floors and antique flower pots, the restaurant aims to create a welcoming atmosphere for guests. Open for dine-in and takeout, Sal Tang's emphasizes warmth, comfort, and exceptional hospitality, making it a beloved spot for both locals and visitors. The restaurant specializes in Cantonese American cuisine, focusing on traditional dishes with a modern twist. The menu is designed to cater to a variety of tastes, offering a blend of classic flavors and contemporary presentations. Sal Tang's is the third Brooklyn restaurant from Sal Lamboglia and managing partner Giovanna Cucolo, and the first for Wilson Tang. The restaurant reflects Chef Sal's understanding of community dining preferences and aims to recreate the charm of classic Chinese-American dining.
menu_items: Crab Rangoon - scallion, sweet chili sauce - $15
Mozzarella Sticks - $15
Wonton Chips - plum sauce & Chinese mustard - $5
Salt & Pepper Chicken Wings - Holland chiles, lemon - $13
Cucumber Salad - scallion aioli, peanuts, sesame - $8
Wonton Soup - $11
review_snippets: TLDR; Original Brooklyn style Chinese takeout with a little flair. The vibe in here is great, maybe a little too many things hanging from the ceiling, but otherwise the design and decor was nailed. For the order we got two drinks, which were really good- interesting flavors with Lyle pops of spice and flavor. The good here was cooked extremely well….. BUT!! The good dishes we tried: - egg roll was stellar - cold noodles were good but the noodles are pasta🤨 - shrimp and broccoli are great - daiquiri and margarita were good The flavoring was off…not in a bad way, but I’ll explain. - Chicken wings: cooked perfectly, the salt/pepper was not existent - tuna crudo: sauce was amazing, cut of tuna was good however it was not great- mating the cut could be thinner, but the texture more resembles tuna steak - crispy crab Rangoon: this was a complete miss here. The mozzarella in the Rangoon is not a good idea. The texture inside doesn’t align with the name, and the flavor spent hot on any level. The crab inside also is unevenly placed. The whole dish needs a rework, otherwise this dish is a DOA. (4 stars)

A true neighborhood gem! The cocktails are fantastic, and the food — though a bit salty for my taste — is still worthy of a Michelin Guide mention. Excellent service, a cozy ambiance, and a spotless bathroom make this spot a definite must-visit! (4 stars)

Sal Tang’s is an excellent addition to the neighborhood. There is comfortable seating outside, however the interior of the restaurant is worth checking out and might provide an even cozier atmosphere. The menu has some delicious dishes that mix Cantonese, American, and Italian. This is Chinese-American comfort food done really well. (5 stars)

I really liked the salad and the crispy tofu. Good dressing on both of them. The beef pancake disappointed me, it was too salty and sweet, and I could take neither the pancake nor the beef. The ambiance is strongly American Chinese and upscale in a good nostalgic way. However, it is very loud inside and the tables are packed together, so it's hardly a cozy place to eat. I had eaten at a restaurant that used to be in the same location and it was a much more welcoming space. (4 stars)
search_text: Sal Tang's Sal Tang's is a Cantonese American restaurant located in Carroll Gardens, Brooklyn, offering a cozy and family-oriented dining experience. With a design that features classic old-school Chinese-American elements, including green and black vinyl floors and antique flower pots, the restaurant aims to create a welcoming atmosphere for guests. Open for dine-in and takeout, Sal Tang's emphasizes warmth, comfort, and exceptional hospitality, making it a beloved spot for both locals and visitors. The restaurant specializes in Cantonese American cuisine, focusing on traditional dishes with a modern twist. The menu is designed to cater to a variety of tastes, offering a blend of classic flavors and contemporary presentations. Sal Tang's is the third Brooklyn restaurant from Sal Lamboglia and managing partner Giovanna Cucolo, and the first for Wilson Tang. The restaurant reflects Chef Sal's understanding of community dining preferences and aims to recreate the charm of classic Chinese-American dining. bio_text: Sami & Susu is a vibrant Michelin-Bib Gourmand restaurant and wine bar located in the Lower East Side, offering a unique blend of Mediterranean influences, New York City flair, and cherished family recipes. The dining experience is characterized by a dynamic menu that features a variety of small to large plates, all served by a passionate staff eager to share their culinary knowledge and cultural heritage. The restaurant focuses on seasonal, fun cuisine that is regularly updated throughout the year. The menu offers a mix of small and large plates, showcasing the diverse flavors of the Mediterranean. Co-founded by Amir Nathan and Jordan Anderson in June 2020, Sami & Susu began as a delivery and pickup service during the pandemic and transitioned to a brick-and-mortar establishment in July 2021. The restaurant was awarded a Michelin Bib Gourmand in 2022.
menu_items: DIPS - comes with pita - $13 (each) / $32 (all three)
LABNEH - za’atar - $13
MUHAMMARA - roasted red pepper, walnut - $13

TUNA CARPACCIO - strawberries, pickled fresno, brown butter - $28

review_snippets: What a hidden gem! Sami & Susu is charming, intimate, rustic place where one wants to come back again and again. You feel welcomed from the moment you step inside. Dim lighting ambiance is perfect for a romantic dinner or friends get-together. Lets talk about THE FOOD. Freshest ingredients, creative menu and unique flavors! Every dish was delicious and memorable. The dips (seemingly a common staple of many Mediterranean restaurants) were so tasty and flavorful! Tuna crudo with brown butter - must try. Sweetbread, beef cheeks, risotto - every dish was "This-is-my-favorite"😃 Chicken with tzatziki- juicy, tender, succulent, and perfectly seasoned with spices. Well curated wine list made the evening even more unforgettable. Cannot wait to be back to try other dishes. Oh, do yourself a favor don't skip the chocolate dessert:) (5 stars)

LOVED the whole branzino with leeks (the leeks are super), the risotto and sweetbread skewers - these are recommended by the waiter and they do not miss! we enjoyed how wholesome and cozy this spot is! the service is amazing as well! please make a reservation or walk in early! (5 stars)

Awesome restaurant! A great place for a date night. The venue is very little but the size allows for a more personal feel to the service. The food was delicate but full of flavor. We had gotten the Muhammara and the Hanger Steak. Both were amazing! We will definitely be coming back again! (5 stars)

We had the sunchoke bureka, rissoto, and tuna and they were all incredible especially the bureka. They had a good combination of vegeterian and non-veggie options. They are on inkind. They also offered to move us to a better table when one become available. (5 stars)

bio_text: Santi is a stylish Italian restaurant located in Midtown East, NYC, helmed by world-renowned and Michelin-starred Chef Michael White. The restaurant offers a pan-Italian menu that reflects Chef White's extensive culinary journey, drawing inspiration from his experiences in Imola, the Amalfi coast, and the South of France. With a commitment to beautifully crafted cuisine, Santi provides an elegant dining atmosphere that emphasizes simplicity and inspiration in every dish. Santi specializes in Italian coastal cuisine, featuring a pan-Italian menu that showcases seasonal ingredients and traditional techniques. The dining experience includes both a la carte and prix fixe options, allowing guests to explore a variety of dishes that highlight the essence of Italian culinary artistry. Chef Michael White, a titan of the NYC food scene, has earned numerous accolades, including six Michelin stars and multiple James Beard nominations. Santi represents his latest endeavor in a long and celebrated culinary career.
menu_items: CRUDITÉ DI MARE RICCIOLA* - amberjack, ligurian olivada, finger lime, basil - $36
TROTA* - cured sea trout, cucumber, trout roe, crème frâiche - $32
CANESTRELLI* - bay scallop, celery root, puffed buckwheat, black truffle - $36
TONNO* - bluefin tuna, honeydew, cucumber, pickled fresno chili - $37
INSALATA - italian chicories, pears, gouda, apple-mustard vinagrette - $27
GRANCHIO - jumbo lump crab salad, green goddess, white asparagus - $34
review_snippets: Every time I have the pleasure of dining at Santi I leave full and beyond satisfied. The front of house staff is always friendly and welcoming. On top of Chef Michael White and the kitchen staff being so talented they are the kindest individuals. I've gotten to enjoy Santi's lunch menu and dinner menu. I've also experienced service from the dining room and bar. No matter where I am sat or the time of day I always have a fabulous experience. Aside from the restaurant's wonderful atmosphere the food is truly out of this world good. I am always pleasantly surprised with every dish. Their dishes have opened my eyes to foods I would never usually try or order and I always end up LOVING them! Some of my favorite dishes I've had from past visits have been the Faraona, Garganelli, Mare, Insalata, and the Gamberi Rossi. You must have dessert at Santi too. The Sole e Luna I had at my most recent visit was life changing to say the least. I dream of that dessert daily! Santi is a must try if you are looking for a new spot to dine at in the city! (5 stars)

Everything about this restaurant was absolutely wonderful — the food was incredible, and the service from the staff was truly top-tier. Every dish was beautifully presented and unbelievably delicious. It really felt like a high-end dining experience in every sense. Unfortunately, the only thing that significantly impacted my overall impression was the experience with the hostess. I arrived earlier than my friend and checked in my coat. I was told to wait for my friend before they could check for a table, which I understood. However, I was not offered a seat at the bar, even though there were many empty bar stools available. Instead, I was asked to wait in a corner, which felt very uncomfortable and unwelcoming. When my friend arrived, I was then immediately told that I could sit at the bar and wait for our table. This left me genuinely confused as to why I wasn’t allowed to sit there earlier and feel comfortable while waiting. In addition, the hostess’s overall attitude felt quite unfriendly. For a restaurant of this level, I believe the front-of-house experience should match the excellence of the food and service. A more professional and welcoming approach would truly elevate the entire experience. (4 stars)

Advanced cuisine in an incredibly chic setting in midtown east. Stunning raw appetizers and great pastas, we also enjoyed the steak which was cooked perfectly. Cocktails are expensive but very very good. Great vibes for an intimate group dinner. Gorgeous bar! Staff was so welcoming and helpful in keeping our dinner on pace before the show we were seeing. Very thoughtful all around! (5 stars)

An exceptional dining experience in the heart of Midtown East. The cuisine is refined and beautifully executed — the raw appetizers were stunning and both the fish and crab cakes were cooked to perfection. Definitely on the pricier side, but worth it. The atmosphere is incredibly chic with a gorgeous bar and perfect ambiance for an intimate group dinner. The staff warm and attentive. A seamless, sophisticated experience all around. (5 stars)

review_snippets: 11/10 experience at Sarantom Thai!!!! My bestfriend recommended this restaurant for girls night being that it has 5 years straight of Michelin awards! We didn’t have reservations just walk in and were seated within 20 minutes! All with smiles and patiences we were ready to feast! Our waitress Cream was phenomenal, personable, and knowledgeable! She made our experience even more memorable. The cocktail glasses were too cute for words too (definitely Instagram worthy)!! As a vegetarian I was able to order plenty of options and the food was A+! We already decided we will be coming back for another girls night! Thank you for the hospitality 🙏 (5 stars)

Everything we tried from appetizers to entrees were amazing. The restaurant brought us back to our Thailand trip from the food to the amazing Thai hospitality. Sadly, we were too full to try their desserts, but there will be a next time. Prices are very reasonable for a Michelin Bib restaurant as well. Highly recommend but get a reservation if you can. (5 stars)

It was decently good but for the wait and the hype, it didn’t really live up to my expectations. Not that I was expecting too much but I thought they might have an edge over other Thai restaurants. The dishes were still tasty, a little on the sweeter side. Don’t think I’d actively go again but wouldn’t stop anyone from trying it out. (4 stars)

I came here for a weekday dinner and was seated right away. I ordered Pad See Ew noodles, fried oyster pancake, and an iced Thai milk tea. We waited about 10-15 minutes for the dishes to arrive. Everything tasted delicious. The prices were affordable. The waiter was attentive, nice, and friendly. This is a great place to check out if you’re looking for authentic Thai food. (5 stars)

bio_text: Sawa embodies the rich hospitality culture of Beirut, where dining transcends mere sustenance to become an experience of care, safety, and connection. The restaurant offers a warm and inviting atmosphere, designed to evoke feelings of home and togetherness, making it an ideal setting for shared meals with loved ones. Sawa specializes in Lebanese cuisine, focusing on traditional dishes that celebrate the flavors and ingredients of the region. The menu is designed for communal dining, encouraging guests to share and enjoy a variety of beautifully presented meals.
menu_items: hummus - chickpea, tahini, lemon - $13
baba ghannouj - charred eggplant, tahini - $13
labneh - strained yogurt, grilled garlic chives, garlic scape, olives - $13
muhammara - charred red pepper, walnut, pomegranate molasses - $14
extra pita - $4
tabbouleh - parsley, tomato, onion, bulgar - $17
review_snippets: Bookmarked this spot for a while and finally paid a visit. I completely agree with the other reviews about the dreamy pitas — soft, fluffy, and freshly baked to perfection. The aroma alone was incredibly inviting. Our favorite dish of the night was the special: the smoked cabbage. Such unique, layered flavors from the combination of sauces. The lamb ribs were just okay for me, a bit too sweet and saucy. The whole dorade was unfortunately disappointing; despite the heavy spices and sauces, the fish tasted quite fishy and didn’t seem very fresh. There are still many items on the menu we didn’t get to try, like the lamb baked pita pie, so would love to be back again. (4 stars)

Overall rating: 4.5 Price: $62 pp (total 2x w/ tax & tip) Leans more fusion than I was expecting. I didn’t like my drink and my waitress was able to swap it out easily. She was so sweet! Items my friend and I ordered: - Green with Envy cocktail: 5/5 delicious - Muhammara/ Rstd swt ppr dip: 3/5 not worth it - Little Gem: 6/5 obsessed - Lamb Ribs Shawarma: 3/5 too small for price Seems to serve more seasonal items so doubt you’ll be able to get this. Recommend giving it a try! (4 stars)

Love this place. I’ve been 4 times and holds the crown of best Lebanese food in the city. On top of the amazing food, it’s cozy in the winter and the backyard patio in the summer is unbeatable. You can tell the owner Samaya works hard to make the place filled with amazing food and love, everyone is so sweet and welcoming. (5 stars)

Sawa NYC is hands down my favorite Lebanese restaurant in New York City. The moment you walk in, you’re welcomed by the warmth of their brick oven and the irresistible aroma of freshly baked pita. The staff is genuinely friendly, the décor strikes a perfect balance of simple and elegant, and the atmosphere feels cozy and inviting. The service is warm and attentive, and the cocktails are creative, unique, and absolutely delicious. Every dish bursts with authentic Lebanese flavor. I highly recommend the Hummus, Muhammara, Tabbouleh, Batata Hara, Kafta, and Lahm Meshwi — but my absolute favorites are the Lamb Ribs and Beiruti Samke Harra. If you’re looking for a true taste of Lebanon in NYC, this is the place to be. (5 stars)

bio_text: Secchu Yokota is a contemporary Japanese restaurant that offers a unique dining experience centered around the art of omakase tempura. The ambiance is refined yet inviting, making it an ideal destination for both casual diners and culinary enthusiasts seeking an elevated experience in London. The restaurant specializes in contemporary Japanese cuisine, with a focus on omakase-style tempura. Diners can expect a carefully curated menu that highlights seasonal ingredients and traditional techniques, ensuring a memorable culinary journey.
menu_items: Omakase Tasting - Seasonal tempura, four delicate starters, light concluding course, choice of standard closing dish or Miyazaki A5 wagyu steak (5 oz), dessert - $145 / $175
review_snippets: Cozy and intimate omakase tempura restaurant where everything is fried fresh to serve. Great ambiance with excellent customer service and a rotating menu depending on what's in season. Reserve ahead of time since there is only 6 seats. (5 stars)

Food 5/5 Service 5/5 Ambiance 5/5 My hubby took me here for my birthday and it was such a unique experience. I never had a tempura omakase before! The setting is super intimate with only 6 seats, and the chef explains each piece before you eat it, which made it feel extra special. The menu starts with 2 appetizers, followed by 8 tempura omakase pieces, and we added on the Miyazaki A5 wagyu (highly recommend) then dessert. Each bite tasted incredibly fresh, surprisingly light and clean for tempura. What we had for tempura: Tiger shrimp Shishito pepper Eel Japanese water eggplant Japanese Spanish mackerel Sweet potato Hokkaido uni Hokkaido scallop And the Miyazaki wagyu? Hands down one of the best I’ve had outside of Japan, it literally melts in your mouth. Dessert was my least favorite part but overall, this was such a special and memorable experience! (5 stars)

This experience really reminded me of Japan. Everything cooked here was made with excellent quality and care. Food: The course I had ended with a Cod entree, which was very good. Made to perfection. The ingredients were very fresh. I don't know if the food is worth the price, however, it is definitely worth it for the experience if you miss Japan. Environment: Cozy restaurant that would make you feel like you stepped into a restaurant in Japan. The Chef, kitchen, environment all would make you feel like you're in a different country. (5 stars)

I went Secchu Yokota yesterday for my birthday. Secchu Yokota, was by far the best eating experience I've had in NYC in a very long time. This was my first Omakase experience and it was delightful. Thank you to the hostesses, Ari, the manager, Diamon, and the amazing Chef. We will definitely be back! (5 stars)

The restaurant specializes in contemporary Japanese cuisine, with a focus on omakase-style tempura. Diners can expect a carefully curated menu that highlights seasonal ingredients and traditional techniques, ensuring a memorable culinary journey. Omakase Tasting - Seasonal tempura, four delicate starters, light concluding course, choice of standard closing dish or Miyazaki A5 wagyu steak (5 oz), dessert - $145 / $175 Cozy and intimate omakase tempura restaurant where everything is fried fresh to serve. Great ambiance with excellent customer service and a rotating menu depending on what's in season. Reserve ahead of time since there is only 6 seats. (5 stars) Food 5/5 Service 5/5 Ambiance 5/5 My hubby took me here for my birthday and it was such a unique experience. I never had a tempura omakase before! The setting is super intimate with only 6 seats, and the chef explains each piece before you eat it, which made it feel extra special. The menu starts with 2 appetizers, followed by 8 tempura omakase pieces, and we added on the Miyazaki A5 wagyu (highly recommend) then dessert. Each bite tasted incredibly fresh, surprisingly light and clean for tempura. What we had for tempura: Tiger shrimp Shishito pepper Eel Japanese water eggplant Japanese Spanish mackerel Sweet potato Hokkaido uni Hokkaido scallop And the Miyazaki wagyu? Hands down one of the best I’ve had outside of Japan, it literally melts in your mouth. Dessert was my least favorite part but overall, this was such a special and memorable experience! (5 stars) This experience really reminded me of Japan. Everything cooked here was made with excellent quality and care. Food: The course I had ended with a Cod entree, which was very good. Made to perfection. The ingredients were very fresh. I don't know if the food is worth the price, however, it is definitely worth it for the experience if you miss Japan. Environment: Cozy restaurant that would make you feel like you stepped into a restaurant in Japan. The Chef, kitchen, environment all would make you feel like you're in a different country. (5 stars) I went Secchu Yokota yesterday for my birthday. Secchu Yokota, was by far the best eating experience I've had in NYC in a very long time. This was my first Omakase experience and it was delightful. Thank you to the hostesses, Ari, the manager, Diamon, and the amazing Chef. We will definitely be back! (5 stars)

bio_text: See No Evil Pizza is a vibrant dining destination located in a subway station in Times Square, New York City, exuding an 80s punk vibe. The restaurant offers a laid-back atmosphere where guests can enjoy iconic thin-crust pizzas alongside flavorful small plates, making it an ideal spot for both casual dining and special events. The restaurant specializes in thin-crust pizzas, featuring unique offerings such as the spicy Hell Pie. The menu also includes small plates like sardine toast and seasonal beans in walnut sauce, with a signature dessert of vanilla soft serve topped with olive oil and sea salt.
menu_items: Winter Salad - $15
Funghi - mushrooms, panna, roasted garlic, parmigiano, fontina, arugula, lemon - $27
Nepo Pie - sauce, cetara anchovies, garlic, capers, olives, calabrian chili, oregano, pecorino - $25
Pepperoni - sauce, pepperoni cups, mozzarella, oregano, pecorino, basil - $26
Margherita - sauce, basil, fresh mozzarella - $23
Hell Pie - sauce, hot soppressata, pepperoni, smoked mozzarella, pecorino, calabrian chili - $29
review_snippets: This is pizza done right 👍 I wanted to try the Johnny Peppers since it seems like it would be the most packed flavor pie. And I was right. Bell peppers, hot cherry peppers, onions, garlic, sausage all incorporated with gooey cheese and tomatoey sauce. Dispite all those toppings this pizza manages to taste light. I didn't feel heavy after eating. The location is on the smaller size and the day that owner it was a little too warm inside the restaurant. Staff wasn't that great. But definitely go for the pizza 🍕 (4 stars)

Nothing scream more New York than a hidden pizza shop in a subway entrance. Have being passing this little hidden spot every time we are taking the 1 train home on 50th street after a show nearby and we finally sat foot in. One pie is good for sharing. The pie came out fast, love the doughy crust although a little sloppy just be careful not to burn your tongue because you just want to gaucho it down once you start. The space reminds me of a 80’ vibe, a little small but they have many tables and can be joined together to sit a large group. For those big group who wants to get a late night snack after a show all together, head there asap it gets filled up quickly as many others are thinking of the same. (5 stars)

What a cool experience! This is more of a casual pizza spot in downtown 1 subway at 50th Street. It's a retro kind of feel, the place was popping! It was definitely a mix of tourists and locals. It felt like a unique but authentic experience in NYC, which is rare, usually 'unique' experiences can end up being kitschy/overpriced. The pizza was SO delicious- Neapolitan style. We were actually struggling with all of the choices, because everything sounded so good. We went to their bar next door afterwards, Nothing Really Matters, and it was super lively at around 10 pm, and was actually going to get even livelier, according to the host. Oh! And there was an awesome dj. (5 stars)
The staff was super kind and very prompt. The food was amazing, and the vibes were vibing. I loved having the smaller dining area, makes NYC feel a little less crowded (5 stars)

bio_text: Seis Vecinos is a vibrant restaurant located in the Bronx, NYC, specializing in authentic Central American and Mexican cuisine. With both indoor and outdoor seating options, the restaurant offers a warm and inviting atmosphere, perfect for casual dining or special events. The establishment prides itself on providing a welcoming environment for families and friends to gather and enjoy delicious meals together. Seis Vecinos focuses on traditional Central American and Mexican dishes, showcasing the rich flavors and culinary techniques of the region. The menu features a variety of options suitable for dine-in, delivery, and takeout, ensuring a versatile dining experience.
menu_items: Seis Vecinos - Carne asada, chorizo, maduros, frijoles, crema y huevos - $24
Carne Asada y Huevos - Grilled steak with eggs - $21
Chuleta a la Plancha o Ahumadas con Huevos - Grilled or Smoked pork chops with eggs - $21
Huevos con Mortadela - Grilled bologna with eggs - $15
Huevos revueltos con verduras y Casamiento - Scrambled eggs with onions, peppers, tomatoes & cilantro. Served with central american style beans & rice - $14
Huevos a la Mexicana - Scrambled eggs with onions, jalapeños, tomato & cilantro - $14
review_snippets: Omg this place was amazing!! Everything was super freaking delicious where we were happy to spend the money. I do have one small complaint that we opted to order the LARGE Henny Colada cocktails but were not warned that they were $60 each!! Luckily,we could afford it but I know that it could be a problem for some people. The drinks were tasty, strong and had 3 small Hennessy bottles as floaters do they were totally worth the $ but still, a little warning would've been nice. Every single dish had soooo much flavor!! (5 stars)

I had am amazing time at Seis Vecinos. Shelley was my waitress. She was amazing. The food was fantastic as well. I ordered the Seafood Paella. It was perfectly seasoned and came with a salad . They sung Happy Birthday to me and made me feel so special. I will definitely be back. I'm so lucky to have this gem of a restaurant so close in my neighborhood. You don't need to go to Manhattan for excellent service. (5 stars)

It ridiculous how you spend your money here because its not a charity you are paying your hard worked money and the service is unprofessional the orders are wrong and its not worth it. Sorry Seis Vecinos you have lost your touch even the quality and taste of the food you will be loosing customers well I know you already have. Get it right you had a dream and made it happen so be consistent and don't try to run your own people for their money. (1 stars)
This has become my new favorite place to eat… I highly recommend it!! Food is so good and if you want to drink this is the place…ask for a large drink, I dare you…incredible…so good!!! (5 stars)

bio_text: Semma is a vibrant culinary destination that showcases the rich traditions of Southern Indian cuisine, particularly from Tamil Nadu. The restaurant, a creation of the Unapologetic Foods team, offers a unique dining experience that emphasizes bold flavors and regional ingredients, inviting guests to explore the depth of South Indian culinary heritage. With a commitment to authenticity and a focus on family recipes, Semma provides a memorable journey through the tastes and aromas of Southern India. Semma specializes in Southern Indian cuisine, with a menu that features a variety of dishes inspired by the traditions of Tamil Nadu. The restaurant offers a diverse selection of small plates and larger entrees, highlighting signature techniques such as the use of layered spices and regional ingredients. Brought to life by Chef Vijay Kumar, Semma is part of the Unapologetic Foods group, which includes notable establishments like Dhamaka and Adda.
menu_items: Mulaikattiya Thaniyam (v) - sprouted mung beans, coconut, smoked chili - $12
Paniyaram - rice & lentil dumpling, asafoetida, paatti’s chutney - $16
Uzhavar Santhai Poriyal (v) - beets, squash, mustard greens, coconut - $18
Eral Thokku - tiger prawn, green chili, fenugreek, curry leaves - $25
Odiyal Kool - scallop, squid, and prawn soup, tamarind (limited) - $25
Annasi Pazham - day-boat scallops, pineapple pachadi, jaggery - $23
review_snippets: Getting a reservation at Semma in NYC is one of the hardest in the city, but after finally dining there, it’s easy to see why. Every dish felt thoughtful, bold, and deeply rooted in authentic South Indian flavors while still presented in a refined, elevated way. The lobster dish was one of the biggest highlights of the meal. The lobster was perfectly cooked and coated in a rich, creamy spiced sauce that had incredible depth and balance. It was indulgent, flavorful, and truly unforgettable. The dosa was beautifully crisp and golden, with that perfect fermented tang. Paired with the chutneys and accompaniments, it was simple yet executed flawlessly. The lamb curry completely stole the show. Served bone-in with a deeply aromatic gravy, the lamb was incredibly tender and packed with bold spices. Eating it with the flaky parotta made every bite comforting and rich — easily one of the best dishes of the night. Beyond the food, what made the experience even more special was meeting the chef at the end of the meal. Despite running one of the most sought-after restaurants in NYC, he was incredibly down-to-earth, warm, and humble, taking the time to chat with guests — which made the experience feel even more memorable. (5 stars)

Semma has been on my list forever, so I was thrilled when my partner managed to score a coveted reservation for my birthday dinner last night. We both love Indian food, and this was a total hit from start to finish. Service was lovely, and they gave us a great table for two tucked into a nice corner of the restaurant. Every dish was beautifully composed and had just the right amount of spice. We started with the mung beans, which were bright, spicy, and a perfect way to kick things off. That was followed by their signature dosa, which was incredible. I’ve had my share of dosas, and this one really stood out—paper thin, crispy, and full of flavor. Next came the rabbit leg, lobster curry, and lamb chops. Each dish was unique, but the lamb was probably my favorite of the night—so tender and served in a wonderfully savory gravy. We also ordered a parotta, which was buttery and flaky and the perfect way to mop up all the sauces. We finished by sharing the coconut dessert, which was light, refreshing, and a perfect ending after so much food. Such a great evening. I’ll definitely be back. (5 stars)

Amazing food! Prices are very fair for a 1 Michelin star restaurant. Chef came out and greeted every table individually. Highly recommend the gunpowder dosa! Only downside is the difficulty in getting reservations/waiting time for bar seating. Highly recommend if you can snag a table! (5 stars)

Reservations required. Michelin star rated, high expectations. Did not disappoint, attentive wait staff, we tried quite a few dishes. Favorites were the dosa and the lamb chops. They were amazing. Presentation of food was delicious. Lamb was so tender and flavorful. We did pre order the crab, it get a little messy, but was delicious. Spice level was on the lower end for Indian food in my opinion, but was still delicious. From the appetizers to the desserts, recommend all of it. (5 stars)

bio_text: Sempre Oggi is a contemporary Italian restaurant located in New York, NY, that embodies the philosophy of celebrating each day through the art of dining. With a focus on seasonality and mindfulness, the restaurant offers a casually elegant atmosphere where guests can enjoy thoughtfully crafted dishes that reflect the best ingredients of the moment. The design and ambiance are inspired by the Italian countryside, modern architecture, and the joy of living well, making it a perfect spot for those who appreciate the pleasures of the table. Sempre Oggi specializes in modern Italian cuisine, with a menu that changes daily to highlight seasonal ingredients. The restaurant features hand-crafted pastas made fresh each morning and offers a variety of small plates during its Aperitivo Hour, showcasing a commitment to quality and simplicity. Sempre Oggi, meaning 'always today,' draws inspiration from the Italian nonnas and the mindfulness of yogis, aiming to create a dining experience that emphasizes the beauty of the present moment.
menu_items: Marinated Olives - None - $8.00
Focaccia - pianogrillo sicilian extra virgin olive oil - $12.00
Housemade Stracciatella - with oven roasted beets, beet vinaigrette & mint - $22.00
Salumi Misti - with prosciutto, mortadella & sopressata - $27.00
Sicilian-Style Crudo, Faroe Island Salmon - red onion, lemon & capers - $24.00
Fried Calamari - with calabrian aioli, fried herbs & lemon - $27.00
review_snippets: Very large restaurant with a really nice decor. Famous dishes are focaccia bread, the gem salad, pasta with amatriciana sauce, and tiramisu. I had all of them, and can say that the rumors are true. Focaccia is very soft, gem salad has the perfect cold and crispy texture, amatriciana tastes great, and tiramisu is memorable. We also had the duck leg parcelles. The tastes were good and well mixed. Also, they carry good wine that pairs well with food. I liked the cream of the tiramisu the most. Also, they make a good effort to make your special day memorable. Suggestion: they should add a sweet bite to the bag they give you when you are leaving the restaurant on your special they - some others restaurants do it so it makes this kind of expected. (5 stars)

Absolutely a must try. Food was delicious served at perfect temperature. Great atmosphere the Waitress was were extremely knowledgeable about the Menu. Tender chicken with a slight light skin that tasted like fried chicken. Salad were robust and flavors combined perfectly. Just go!! Well worth the money!!! (5 stars)

FABULOUS OUTSTANDING food I am vegetarian pescatarian and very picky. I ordered the cauliflower antipasto and a couple of vegetable cotorni. All spectacular. My mom and my daughter said their pasta was absolutely delicious. The interior is so nicely done. Great service lovely waitstaff. Thaddeus was our server, very charming and friendly as were many others there whose names I did not get. It was a perfect evening. They didn’t rush us at all. So appreciated. Highly recommend. And quiet!!! You can converse!! (5 stars)

Came to Sempre Oggi for a drink at the bar prior to going for a show at Beacon Theatre.. although the restaurant was quite full we were able to get seats at the bar rather quickly. Very friendly service and our mixologist. Kevin gave us a tasting of their house special martini and I wound up getting two more.. great service.. really pretty restaurant.. very clean bathrooms. We didn’t get a chance to eat, but we’ll definitely be back to try. The food smelled and looked delicious. (4 stars)

bio_text: Seoul Salon is a contemporary dining establishment located in the heart of New York City, offering a unique blend of traditional Korean flavors and modern culinary techniques. The restaurant's ambiance is designed to create a warm and inviting atmosphere, perfect for both casual dining and special occasions. Seoul Salon specializes in Korean cuisine, focusing on authentic dishes that highlight the rich flavors and ingredients of Korea. The menu features a variety of options, including traditional favorites and innovative interpretations, all crafted with precision and care.
menu_items: PINE NUT SALAD - PINE NUT, ROMAINE, BLACK SESAME SEED - $10
KOREAN BEEF TARTARE - GOCHUJANG, NAPA CABBAGE, MICRO WASABI - $15
SIGNATURE SOY SCALLOP WITH GIM RICE - SCALLOP, EGG YOLK, GIM RICE - $21
CUTTLEFISH SUKHWE - CUTTLEFISH, VINEGARED RED PEPPER PASTE, SESAME OIL - $21
SIGNATURE SPICY RAW CRAB NOODLES - RAW CRAB, WHEAT NOODLES, SESAME SAUCE - $29
NEW SEOUL SALON PASTA - SEAWEED, BUTTER, PINE NUT - $21
review_snippets: Awesome food and fun, lively environment. The portions are pretty sizable and everything was mouthwateringly delicious! Gejang (raw crab) was flavorful and didn't have any off flavors. Rose tteopoki was creamy and yummy. Jokbal was solid. The spicy octopous with creamy rissoto was kind of like the rose tteopoki. Spicy flavors alternated with cream/dairy. The banana milk bingsoo also tasted just like banana milk which was fun (5 stars)

My friends and I have needed a spot for girls night and scored a reservation for Seoul Salon. This place was absolutely packed for a Thursday night, so definitely grab a reservation before you go. We were seated in a smaller room allowing for a more intimate dining experience. We ordered their limited time yellowtail platter, grilled tteokgalbi, rose tteokbokki with gimmari, Seoul salon pasta, and jokbal platter. The yellowtail platter came with a seasonal porridge, cuttlefish, whelk salad, sauces, aged kimchi, and gim. While it's recommended for 2, it easily fed the three of us. Their rose tteokbokki was really flavorful but we enjoyed it even more after it had cooled down and the flavors seeped in more. Their seoul salon pasta was the perfect amount of umami and one of our favorite bites of the night! The jokbal platter was MASSIVE. It was cooked and seasoned to perfection. Needless to say, this is the place to go for good food and drinks with friends! We will be back! Check out my foodsta @chiuventure for a closer look and more details of my dining experience here as well as other establishments in NYC and around the world! (5 stars)

Seoul Salon has a modern twist on classic Korean dishes, infusing them with fresh culinary twists. The soy scallop with gim rice was fresh, light, and scallops were sweet and creamy in texture. The rose tteokbokki was very creamy and almost felt like a fusion between Italian flavors and Korean textures. The basil was herby, flavorful, and stracciatella cheese slightly acidic, creamy, and infused the dish with a lightness and break in richness of the rose sauce. The tteok texture was soft, but still al dente to create a great bite. Lastly the spicy octopus with risotto was another blend of Italian & Korean flair, introducing soft, creamy Arborio rice with the crunchy, spicy, and flavor-packed octopus. Seoul salon’s menu is unique and curated to be filled with robust flavor & great textures. My only callout is the space is narrow so it can be difficult to have a conversation as it feels like tables are cramped/on top of each other. (4 stars)

Seoul Salon, as described by them, is a Sool Jib inspired Korean restaurant with a modern take on Korean alcohol and Korean foods. The vibe itself was nice, dim but not too loud, even with the edm/club music playing. The tables can feel a bit cramped, but it wasn't overbearing and we could talk even with all the background noise. The food was phenomenal, well priced and well portioned for sharing. We got the octopus kimbap, soy scallop with gim rice, and the raw marinated crab noodles. The Banchan was a ramen snack with ketchup, a good palate cleanser and tasty. The octopus kimbap was good, we didn’t think it was outstanding but it did taste good. The octopus was a bit uneven in the dish though, as some of our pieces had no octopus while others had a lot. The raw marinated crabs were a highlight, with a large portion of noodles accompanying it. As per their instruction, we mixed the raw crab meat into the noodles, which elevated the already tasty crab and noodles to make a spicy yet delicious noodle dish. The spice was a little on the spicier side, but nothing too spicy. A highlight was the soy scallop with gim rice. It had a great taste to it, a great portion of scallop, and each part of the dish worked perfectly together. The price is also really good for all the food we got, probably one of the highest quality meals we've gotten at the price we paid. (5 stars)

bio_text: Seppe Pizza Bar is a modern, family-friendly neighborhood pizzeria that combines high-quality food with genuine service in a welcoming and laid-back atmosphere. With a focus on comfort and classic touches, Seppe aims to provide an approachable yet elevated dining experience, making it an ideal spot for casual dinners or gatherings over craft cocktails and small plates. Seppe specializes in Italian-American cuisine, offering a menu inspired by cherished family recipes. The restaurant emphasizes high-quality, thoughtfully prepared dishes, utilizing locally sourced ingredients and importing the finest from Italy, including pasta from Torre Annunziata. The dining format is casual, with a focus on family-style sharing. Seppe is rooted in generations of Italian-American culinary tradition, celebrating the importance of family and togetherness through food. The restaurant is a result of a commitment to honoring these traditions while providing an honest and approachable dining experience.

review_snippets: Noel was more than accommodating this evening. Give that man a raise. Your polenta fries were outstanding. The beet and farro salad perfection. The half red half spicy vodka topped the list. I would dare someone to eat this pizza and not fall in love. Welcome to the neighborhood. (5 stars)

Seppe Pizza Bar in lower Manhattan is great. Friendly service, with all hands available to keep guests comfortable and happy. The menu is creative and the food never fails to delight. Everything I've tried so far has been well prepared and thoughtfully presented. And the House pies? To die for. My faves are the Aunt Honey and the Spicy Vodka. The wine list offers a good range, and the cocktails are creative and delicious. Seppe is a sure bet if you're looking for a good place for appetizers, pizza, and a nice dining experience. (5 stars)

We enjoyed this restaurant so much, we went back the next day! Pizza was amazing, bolognese and cacio Pepe were delicious! Staff were very attentive and friendly! We went as a family of six and everyone was happy! (5 stars)

bio_text: Shabushabu Mayumon offers a unique dining experience centered around shabu-shabu, transitioning from an Omakase-style service to a more personalized DIY approach. Guests are invited to explore a variety of premium ingredients and handcrafted sauces, allowing for a customizable and interactive meal that emphasizes quality and flavor. The restaurant's inviting atmosphere encourages relaxation and enjoyment, complemented by a curated selection of sake and wine. The restaurant specializes in shabu-shabu, featuring high-quality A5 Miyazaki Wagyu Ribeye and seasonal vegetables. The menu allows for a DIY experience with a choice of seven handcrafted sauces and artisanal cheeses, enhancing the depth of flavors. Signature techniques include house-made sauces and a focus on customizable pairings. For the past six years, Shabushabu Mayumon has been serving the world's only Omakase-style shabu-shabu, evolving its concept to enhance guest interaction and choice.

review_snippets: Delicious! A restaurant that’s really worth visiting — the broth is flavorful, the service is great, and the meat is exceptionally good. Everything is fresh, tender, and perfect for a comforting meal. (5 stars)

Had a very nice dinner here in an intimate and beautiful setting! It was my first time trying shabu omakase; they cooked the meat in front of us and placed each piece on our plate like sushi omakase. While the cooking is the fun part of shabu shabu and I would’ve liked to control the degree to which the meat was cooked (it wasn’t equal and I kept receiving the more raw piece), it was also pleasant to watch. The pace was a bit too fast for me, because we were the only party in the restaurant. It would’ve been better had they paced it like a full house instead of cooking the next as soon as the previous piece was gone from the plate. (I just kept half a piece on my plate so we wouldn’t get the next one so quickly.) We got yuzu sake and umeshu in the beginning as refreshments, then got sake for the course which paired well with the heavy meat. The A5 wagyu truly melted in my mouth, but I personally preferred the wagyu after the first bite bc it was less fatty. The whole course might be a bit too much of meat after meat, especially if you’re a smaller person (I couldn’t eat any more after 5-6 slices). Better pacing might have helped with this, or maybe it’s just a lot. At any rate I was happy by the end of the night and it was quite memorable. Just make sure you can stomach everything or bring someone who can take their portion as well as yours. (4 stars)

18 courses - interesting experience as it feels like you are eating hot pot but in a more fancy way hahaa - perfect for the rainy/cold days. The meat truly melts in your mouth. They serve wagyu and pork belly. The only thing I didn’t like was the chicken rice (it’s quite dry and also not warm). Overall interesting experience. Pricing is quite high for the value imo. (4 stars)

Delicious The appetizers and dessert were ok, but the star of the meal is the shabu shabu and they’re generous delicious bites that switch up the sauces to keep it fresh each course. We were out by 7, and it was quick and efficient service, which I appreciated too! Reservations were easy to make - 3 seatings noon, 530, and 7pm(I think). We were running late and showed up ten minutes late to a 530 reservation on a Tuesday but the staff was super chill about it and turns out it was just us and one other guy. (5 stars)

bio_text: Shalom Japan is a unique dining establishment located in South Williamsburg, offering a cozy and intimate atmosphere that reflects the harmonious blend of Jewish and Japanese culinary traditions. Founded by married chefs Aaron Israel and Sawako Okochi, the restaurant serves as a celebration of their diverse backgrounds and shared passion for food, inviting guests to experience a meal that embodies their love story and cultural heritage. The restaurant specializes in an innovative fusion of Jewish and Japanese cuisine, featuring dishes that creatively combine elements from both cultures. The menu includes unique offerings such as Matzoh Ball Ramen, showcasing the chefs' commitment to authenticity while embracing a playful, inauthentic twist. Opened in 2013, Shalom Japan was founded by chefs Aaron Israel and Sawako Okochi, who draw inspiration from their respective Jewish and Japanese roots, as well as the vibrant culinary scene of Brooklyn.
review_snippets: I came here because Barbara Corcoran mentioned she loved it on Shark Tank and damn Barbara...I can see why! Living in NYC, it's genuinely hard to be surprised by restaurants anymore. The bar is just so high across the board that you start to feel like you've seen it all. But Shalom Japan is truly something else!!! The Jewish-Japanese fusion concept sounds like it could easily go sideways, but it actually somehow makes a lot of sense. Innovation without feeling overworked and tortured. The Jew Egg was incredible (yes it's actually called that), with such a unique and memorable flavor profile. I don't really like scotch eggs but I looooved this. And the Okonomiyaki with wagyu pastrami was TO DIE. I have never had better pastrami in my life. The other dishes were excellent as well, but those two were the clear standouts and alone worth the visit. The ambiance was warm and relaxed. We arrived around 6:30 on a Thursday to a quiet room, which filled up nicely by 7:30. Service was attentive and wonderful throughout. Definitely worth the schlep to Williamsburg from South Brooklyn, and that is truly saying something. Highly recommend. (5 stars)

Finally got a chance to go to Shalom Japan a few days ago with my wife and nieces who live in Bklyn. Saw their bit on Shark Tank and it was a pleasant surprise! A small place but they have outdoor tables (for warmer weather - it was a brutality cold day when we went). Parking was a pain because the streets were still snowed in. Typical bklyn street parking. Brunch menu was very good. Had the challah and the karaage (Japanese chicken) for the table for apps. The star of the show, however, was the matzoh ball ramen! This is their signature dish and why we went there! Did not dissapoint! I made mine spicy and loved it! Paired it with the pear saki (pun intended) and had a very good lunch! We want to go back and try some of the other menu items. Service was excellent! Not your typical Japanese restaurant and well worth a try! (4 stars)
I’ve been wanting to try this place for a long time! I’m so happy I did. Everything we tried was delicious and flavorful. The drinks were great as well! (5 stars)

When I first came across Shalom Japan on IG, I thought the concept was very intriguing. Therefore, I had to pay them a visit the next time I was visiting NYC. I got a reservation on Resy and I'm so happy we made the trek out to Brooklyn. Everything was fantastic, I loved the combination of both Jewish and Japanese cuisine. Poor waiter/Bartender was the only one working the floor, I could tell he was getting quite anxious as the night progressed. I would definitely return the next time I'm in town. (5 stars)
