bio_text: Shmoné is an intimate dining destination in New York City's West Village, where the culinary artistry of Executive Chef Eyal Shani comes to life through a highly seasonal and market-driven approach. The restaurant offers a dynamic and ever-evolving menu that reflects the freshest ingredients available, creating a unique dining experience that encourages spontaneity and creativity. Guests are invited to engage directly with the chefs, making each visit a personal and interactive culinary journey. Shmoné specializes in a seasonal, market-driven menu that changes daily, focusing on vibrant flavors and fresh ingredients. The cuisine is influenced by Mediterranean traditions, with an emphasis on vegetables, seafood, and local produce. The dining format allows for a spontaneous and creative exploration of dishes, reflecting the chefs' inspirations. Founded by Chef Eyal Shani, who has a rich culinary background stemming from his upbringing in Jerusalem, Shmoné opened its doors in 2023 and quickly earned a Michelin star, which it retained in 2024. Chef Orianne Shapira, originally from Tel Aviv, leads the culinary team, bringing her artistic flair and experience from HaSalon NYC.

review_snippets: SHMONÉ NY. A True Culinary Experience, Not Just a Meal What an incredible night! My friend told me SHMONÉ was amazing, so we decided to walk in and grab two seats at the bar. Best decision ever. From the moment we sat down, the staff made us feel like regulars. Everyone was super friendly, professional and clearly passionate about what they do. The open kitchen setup is something special, it feels like you’re part of the show. The chef himself came over to chat with us, explained the specials and even served a few dishes directly from the kitchen to the bar. You can see and taste the creativity and care that goes into every plate. We had several small plates, each one beautifully presented and full of flavor. The fig salad was refreshing and perfectly balanced, the meat skewer was juicy and smoky, and the short rib absolutely unreal, melt- n your mouth good. Every dish looked like a piece of art. The atmosphere is cozy, elegant and energetic the kind of spot where you lose track of time and just enjoy great food, drinks, and conversation. Must-try: The short rib and the chef’s seasonal specials. Pro tip: Sit at the bar if you can — you’ll get the full SHMONÉ experience. A memorable dining experience from start to finish. Can’t wait to come back! (5 stars)

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Last night at SHMONÉ felt like one of those perfect New York nights you wish you could replay again and again. We walked in early, thinking we’d just grab a quick dinner… and then four hours later, we were still sitting at the bar, eating, laughing, drinking, and watching this wild kitchen ballet happening right in front of us. 🔥 We had front-row seats — chefs flying, pans sizzling, olive oil dripping like gold. You could feel the energy. Everyone’s working hard but smiling, throwing jokes around, pouring martinis, and making it all look effortless. 🥯 We started with that famous Jerusalem bagel — warm, fluffy, olive oil and za’atar dripping off the edges — honestly, I could’ve stopped right there and called it a night. But then came the tuna, so fresh it practically winked at us, and the octopus, smoky and soft with those beans… unreal. 😋 The sweetbreads hit the table next — I don’t even know how to explain it — crispy, tangy, creamy, somehow a salad but not really a salad. The pistachio pesto pasta was so good we stopped talking for five minutes. 🥩 And then the 76-layer Wagyu. Oh my God. The waiter brought us challah after and said, “you’ll need this to soak up the juice,” and he was absolutely right — we cleaned that plate like it was the last supper. 🍷 Between bites and martinis, we kept saying, “just one more dish,” but we didn’t want to leave. Everything was shareable, everything was perfect, and every bite was better than the last. Must-haves: 🥩 Beef short rib ❤️ Sweetbreads 🐙 Octopus 🐟 Tuna 🥯 Jerusalem bagel If I could move in and sit at that bar every night, I would. This isn’t just dinner — it’s a whole New York moment. SHMONÉ, you got me. I’m hooked. (5 stars)

Five stars — without question. The atmosphere is relaxed and welcoming, with great music that sets the mood just right. When we arrived, our table wasn’t ready yet, but the host was incredibly kind and suggested we wait at the wine bar next door. We were warmly welcomed there, had a lovely drink, and honestly didn’t mind the wait at all. Our server Anya was absolutely fantastic — knowledgeable, attentive, and full of warmth. She could tell us about every dish and drink in detail and made the whole evening feel special. The open kitchen is beautiful to look at, and it’s genuinely fun to watch the chefs work — the whole team is impressive. As for the food: everything was spot on. Our favorites were the tuna, grilled vegetables, beef rib, sweetbreads, and the lamb kebab. All were must-tries. Shmone isn’t flashy or over-the-top — it’s the kind of place you want to keep coming back to. I only wish I’d discovered it sooner. Already planning my next visit. (5 stars)

We sat on the bar and enjoyed the amazing chefs making the food in front of us. The food was fantastic, fresh and flavorful, just like we love it. The drinks were great and the vibes happy. We will definitely come back here again. (5 stars)
search_text: Shmoné Shmoné is an intimate dining destination in New York City's West Village, where the culinary artistry of Executive Chef Eyal Shani comes to life through a highly seasonal and market-driven approach. The restaurant offers a dynamic and ever-evolving menu that reflects the freshest ingredients available, creating a unique dining experience that encourages spontaneity and creativity. Guests are invited to engage directly with the chefs, making each visit a personal and interactive culinary journey. Shmoné specializes in a seasonal, market-driven menu that changes daily, focusing on vibrant flavors and fresh ingredients. The cuisine is influenced by Mediterranean traditions, with an emphasis on vegetables, seafood, and local produce. The dining format allows for a spontaneous and creative exploration of dishes, reflecting the chefs' inspirations. Founded by Chef Eyal Shani, who has a rich culinary background stemming from his upbringing in Jerusalem, Shmoné opened its doors in 2023 and quickly earned a Michelin star, which it retained in 2024. Chef Orianne Shapira, originally from Tel Aviv, leads the culinary team, bringing her artistic flair and experience from HaSalon NYC. bio_text: Shota Omakase is a distinguished dining establishment located in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, offering an authentic and immersive omakase experience. The restaurant embodies a harmonious blend of traditional Edomae-style sushi and modern culinary innovation, creating a unique atmosphere that celebrates the art of sushi-making. With a commitment to sourcing the finest ingredients, Shota Omakase invites guests to indulge in a meticulously crafted dining journey that reflects the chef's passion and dedication. Shota Omakase specializes in Edomae-style sushi, emphasizing techniques such as marination, curing, and aging to enhance the natural flavors of each ingredient. The menu is presented in an omakase format, allowing the chef to showcase seasonal and premium ingredients through a curated selection of dishes. Signature techniques include a blend of traditional practices and modern creativity. Chef-Owner Cheng Lin began his culinary journey in 1997 at Hatsuhana in New York City and has since worked in prestigious kitchens, including Sushi Seki and Blue Ribbon. Inspired by the book 'Shota No Sushi', he opened Shota Omakase to fulfill his dream of creating a restaurant that reflects his dedication to sushi. The restaurant was recognized with ONE MICHELIN STAR just one year after opening.
menu_items: Premium Omakase - An 18-course menu featuring small bites, nigiri, a hand roll, and tamago, thoughtfully curated based on seasonal availability. - $195
Gentei Omakase - A 19-course exclusive experience led by our chef-owner Cheng Lin, featuring rare seasonal fish and premium cuts. - $255
review_snippets: Dining at Shota was nothing short of phenomenal. From the moment we sat down, the chef created an experience that felt both personal and educational. He was incredibly warm and delightful, taking the time to explain the proper etiquette of fine Japanese dining and the philosophy behind each course. It felt less like a meal and more like being guided through a masterclass in traditional omakase. The most memorable moment for me was trying uni. I’ve never been a fan before, but the chef encouraged me to give it another chance—and I’m so glad I did. It was, without question, the best tasting uni I have ever had: incredibly fresh, delicate, and perfectly prepared. It completely changed my perspective. Shota isn’t just dinner—it’s an experience that deepens your appreciation for Japanese culinary tradition. A truly exceptional omakase that I would highly recommend to anyone who wants to understand sushi at its highest level. (5 stars)

A truly unique and meditative omakase experience Shota Omakase delivers an experience unlike anything else. The atmosphere is calm, intimate, and almost monastic — a quiet space where attention is fully focused on the food and the moment. Service is entirely dedicated to creating a flawless experience, with an impressive level of care, precision, and respect for timing and flow. We chose the omakase with premium sake pairing, and it was exceptional. The selection of sakes was outstanding — complex, elegant, and perfectly matched to each course. The highlights included the premium sakes shown in the pairing, all impeccably chosen. Every dish was surprising and beautifully executed. Special mention goes to the uni, which was remarkably sweet, clean, and creamy, with absolutely no bitterness or unpleasant aftertaste — a clear sign of top-quality sourcing and handling. This is not just a meal, but a complete sensory experience. Refined, thoughtful, and deeply memorable. An outstanding destination for those seeking omakase at the highest level in New York City. (5 stars)

There are two menu options: Premium Omakase - 18 courses featuring small bites, nigiri, a hand roll, and tamago, curated around the best seasonal ingredients. $195 per person. Gentei Omakase - 19 courses led by chef-owner Cheng Lin, featuring rare seasonal fish and premium cuts for a more elevated journey. $255 per person. I chose the Premium Omakase, and every course reflected incredible balance, precision, and freshness. My personal standouts were the hatate (Hokkaido scallop), tamago (egg), and the Japanese crown musk melon since each bite was beautifully prepared and bursting with clean, delicate flavor. What really sets Shota apart from other omakases in New York is the knowledge and hospitality of the team. Our chef, who has over 20 years of experience, shared his passion and insights with us throughout the meal. He explained each piece in detail and even showcased four different types of uni side by side, which was such a treat for anyone who loves uni. The interior is minimalist, clean, and beautifully maintained, allowing the food to take center stage. Service was warm and professional, and the pacing of each course was perfect. I've been to many omakase spots in NYC, but Shota stands out for its attention to detail, high-quality fish, and genuine passion for the art of sushi. (5 stars)

Booked 7 seats at the bar for a team omakase. Fresh ingredients, nice variety of dishes, and felt like it was just enough food. The chefs were lovely and I appreciated how they shared information about the ingredients and dishes served. (4 stars)

bio_text: Smithereens is a seafood restaurant located in the East Village, offering a unique dining experience that celebrates the flavors and culinary traditions of New England. With a commitment to sourcing the finest ingredients from the Northeast and beyond, the restaurant provides a cozy yet sophisticated atmosphere for guests to enjoy a thoughtfully curated menu and an ever-evolving wine selection. The culinary focus at Smithereens is on seafood, with a menu that highlights the best seasonal offerings. The wine list is carefully curated and changes daily, emphasizing varietals such as riesling.
menu_items: apple cider donut - $8
vanilla ice cream scoop - $8
boston cream pie - $18
celery ice cream float - $12
candied seaweed with licorice & citron - $14
anadama bread with seaweed butter - $9
review_snippets: Had a delicious meal here recently. Our favorites: the buckwheat pancake with the smoked bluefish (absolutely delicious), the lobster roll, the monkfish with the kumquot, walnut and mint jams, the chicory salad (sublime). We also ordered the golden eye snapper with beets and yuzu (interesting but neither of us would order again). Do NOT pass up on the desserts. We ordered the celery ice cream float and the candied seaweed cake with licorice and citron - both amazing!!! In terms of ambiance, very nice - my only complaint is for the stools with no backs that are at the tables at the front. Not very comfortable. Fortunately they re-sat us at a much more comfortable table. Also big shout out to our server - super knowledgeable with good recommendations. (5 stars)

I love this restaurant. Hard to describe-but amazing flavors. Everything was a revelation. Have never gone wrong with any choice—but the bbq mackerel is my go to. The celery float dessert is my new obsession. The staff were gracious, helpful and willing to engage and ensure that our interests/adventures were realized. (I requested chop sticks to eat the bay scallops dish and the appeared!—I am sure they would have gone to the nearby take out to get them, but they had some available from a recent ramen pop up.) Extensive wine list and sommelier found us a bottle at our price point and delivered! Funky under street level space. So nice to have a relaxing and fun meal without the pretentiousness that has become far too common. (NYT review gets it so right) (5 stars)

From the warm welcome when we arrived to the moment we left, this experience was not just about discovering a new restaurant – it was a true destination! Their specialty is fish, and even as someone who usually prefers meat, I completely changed my mind! This restaurant comes close to excellence in every way — creativity, flavors, and presentation. Nothing is missing! The lentils with foie gras, for example, were absolutely delicious, the lobster roll possibly the best of my life and the donut dessert was simply divine. Highly recommended — a must-try culinary gem! (5 stars)

Loved this place. Food and service was solid. The menu is thoughtful without trying too hard. The obvious favorite was the buckwheat pancake and crudo while the puntarelle salad was a pleasant surprise: fresh and crisp, a little bitter in the best way, and perfectly balanced. (5 stars)

bio_text: Sobaya is a cherished Japanese restaurant located in the East Village of New York City, celebrated for its authentic handmade soba and udon noodles. Since its inception in 1996, Sobaya has embodied the essence of Japanese culinary tradition, offering a serene dining atmosphere that reflects true Japanese hospitality. The restaurant's warm wooden interiors and soft lantern lighting create an inviting space for guests to enjoy thoughtfully crafted dishes that emphasize quality and authenticity. Sobaya specializes in traditional Japanese soba and udon, with a menu that features freshly made noodles, rice bowls, tempura, and bento sets. The culinary focus is on using premium ingredients sourced directly from Japan, with an emphasis on handmade preparation and time-honored techniques. Founded in 1996, Sobaya has been dedicated to the art of handmade noodles, with a philosophy rooted in the Japanese principle of 'shokunin'—the artisan's spirit. The head chef, a veteran of Japanese culinary arts, leads the team in honoring traditional techniques and respecting the ingredients.
menu_items: Agedashi Tofu - Crispy tofu with hot dashi broth, delicate soy flavors. - $14.00
Goma Ae - Boiled spinach tossed in creamy sesame sauce, subtly nutty. - $7.00
Shrimp Shumai - Steamed or fried shrimp dumplings, homemade and lightly savory. - $14.00
Edamame - Steamed soybeans with sea salt. - $14.00
Homemade Shumai - House-made shrimp and pork dumplings, steamed to perfection. - $14.00
Buta Kakuni - Braised pork belly, sweet soy-rich, tender, and flavorful. - $18.00
review_snippets: Fantastic and flavorful Japanese food! Everything I ate was good and the service was kind and attentive. I'll be honest I don't remember the name of what I got but it was a rice dish, it might've been some kind of tonkatsu, and it was awesome. Same with the appetizer, it was some kind of seared salmon belly and it was buttery, and smooth, so so good. (5 stars)

Love this place! Been multiple times, and is one of the best places I’ve gone for soba in nyc. Would recommend a res tho bc it can get busy depending on time of day. Their lunch specials are VERY value - Sake oyako don lunch set w/ hot udon: 8/10: The salmon bowl was yummy, and the udon texture was good, but would prob get the cold dipping soba instead (better imo) - Una ju lunch set w/ cold dipping soba: 10/10, The eel was really yummy, and I love their cold soba. Dipping sauce is light and refreshing (5 stars)

This is a quietly confident spot that rewards a spontaneous visit. I stopped in late in the day while walking by and was seated immediately, which set a relaxed tone from the start. The menu is relatively small but thoughtfully curated, focusing on quality rather than excess, and the food delivers on that promise. The atmosphere is calm and understated, making it an excellent place for conversation, something that’s increasingly rare. While it’s not the most budget friendly option, the overall experience feels worth the price. If you happen to pass by, it’s absolutely a place worth stopping for a satisfying and unrushed meal (5 stars)

This place is really good! The portions are good, the noodles are good. My issue is I’m not a big soup for a meal guy. That’s a me issue and not a Sobaya issue. This is probably some of the best soup I’ve had ever, but it’s just soup. Really good spot if you like soup and noodles though! (4 stars)

bio_text: Sobre Masa is a vibrant Tortilleria and Restaurant located in the heart of Bushwick, Brooklyn, offering a modern take on Mexican cuisine. The establishment is dedicated to honoring the rich cultural heritage of heirloom corn while providing a contemporary dining experience that emphasizes house-made tortillas and innovative dishes. The restaurant specializes in modern Mexican cooking, focusing on the use of heirloom corn and traditional nixtamal techniques. The menu features a variety of dishes that highlight the craftsmanship of their house-made tortillas, creating a unique dining experience. Everything we make begins with heirloom corn and the culture behind it. At Sobre Masa, we honor these foundations while creating a space for contemporary Mexican cooking in Brooklyn.
menu_items: Guacamole - Flowering cilantro, onion, lime.
Tuna Tostada - Yellowfin tuna, chipotle aioli, leeks.
Chicken liver Tostada - Fennel, pico de gallo, candied citrus.

Delicata Salad - Requesón, pomegranate molasses vinaigrette, pistachio.

review_snippets: Very authentic inventive Mexican cuisine. Enjoyed the experience. Sat at the bar since we didn’t have a reservation but still had a great dinner. Not cheap, however (5 stars)
Excellent good and fantastic ambiance. The main room is very cozy. I loved their salsas and that they have many interesting dishes on the menu. (5 stars)

Very mixed feelings. Food was not bad, the salsa flight and carnitas were far and beyond the highlights, and I would encourage anyone to order them. The ceviche and tuna tostada were decent, good quality and a fair price, but they wouldn’t blow your mind. The chocolate cremeaux and coconut pudding were good as well. The issue was with the service, specifically at the end. The bill was paid for not even two minutes and we had just finished signing the receipts before the waiter came around and told us to leave. We were there for less than 1.5 hours, caused no problems (no one made complaints to my knowledge and there we no comments about my party), and we get kicked out? I understand the restaurant is busy, but I would appreciate a few minutes to wrap up the night and leave myself. It’s a shame, the dining experience would have been good otherwise. Overall, based on the dining experience alone, I would not come back here. There are plenty of other restaurants with similar quality that would not leave a bad taste in my mouth. (3 stars)

I was really excited to try this place, but overall I left feeling underwhelmed. The steak was delicious and cooked very well, and the proteins in general were prepared nicely. That said, the portions and overall experience did not justify the price point. One thing that stood out was the pricing of the menu. There was a mole dish with broccolini and no protein that was still priced quite high, despite not including any particularly expensive ingredients. Because of that, I ended up ordering the steak to make the meal feel more worthwhile, but even then, the prices felt difficult to justify and seem like they need to be reevaluated. The drinks were the least enjoyable part of the meal. They tasted watered down. We ordered a Paloma and a michelada, and when the bill came, I noticed the michelada was charged as two separate items , one for the beer and one for the michelada add-ons. Since a michelada is typically priced as a single drink, this was surprising and off-putting. We were also charged for a second round of salsa. While I understand charging extra in some cases, the refill portion was very small, which added to the overall feeling that the value didn’t match the cost. (3 stars)

bio_text: Soda Club is a vibrant dining destination that celebrates the joy of natural wine and fresh pasta, creating an inviting atmosphere for good times and memorable experiences. With a focus on plant-based cuisine, the restaurant has garnered recognition as one of the best vegan/vegetarian establishments in New York City, making it a popular choice for both casual diners and culinary enthusiasts alike. Soda Club specializes in vegan and vegetarian dishes, with a menu that prominently features fresh pasta. The restaurant emphasizes the use of natural wines to complement its culinary offerings, creating a unique dining experience.
menu_items: FOCACCIA - miso bagna cauda - $8
CASTELVETRANO OLIVES - nduja, feta, orange - $8
ARANCINI - tomato sauce - $10
HERBED RICOTTA - oregano, marjoram, parsley, house focaccia - $16
WATERCRESS - roasted grapes, pine nuts, feta - $18
ARUGULA & RADICCHIO - blue cheese, pumpkin seeds, sweet potato - $19
review_snippets: came here for my last dinner on my nyc trip and was very impressed. we dined on a monday and the restaurant was still quite busy and had a great ambience. the wine list is extensive and their chilled red is honestly one of the best that i have tried. we ordered arancini, the grape salad, tagliatelle, and radiatori. all were incredible, i especially loved the radiatori. the pasta tasted very fresh and the service was attentive. we also tried the date cake for dessert which was delicious. i wish we had somewhere like this in australia but i will definitely be returning on my next nyc trip. (5 stars)

Here’s the thing… I find nothing more appealing than when a restaurant has high principles and strong technique but does not show them off in flashy and attention grabbing ways. We walked into Soda Club off the street, drawn in by perfect lighting, cozy decor and that feeling that these folks knew exactly what they were on about. Service was 💯 on point and friendly. The herbed ricotta was creamy, decadent with jammy confit cherry tomatoes. The watercress salad sang with perfectly complimentary silky feta and sweet roasted grapes. The light, crisp Roman style carbonara pizza was perfectly balanced with gently fried artichokes, smoked mushrooms and bright, lemony arugula. We finished with gigli pasta showcasing white truffles, crispy leeks and a velvety cream sauce. Overall, a spectacular, thoughtfully prepared, soul satisfying feast. Now… here is the twist, half way through the meal, we asked about the spice level of the chorizo on another pizza. The server said, the -tofu- chorizo… wait… what? Tofu chorizo… is this place vegetarian?? !Vegan! We were shocked and delighted. And this brings me back to my opening gambit. This was the best vegan dining experience we had ever had (and we have enjoyed many) and there was not a hint of the virtue signaling that drags down most of the field. —Nothing— about the experience was sacrificed to promote ideals or a lifestyle imperative. There was clearly some masterful chemistry happening in the kitchen but no floating spheres or insubstantial foams. The meal was decadent yet sat lightly with us. Not a sliver of texture or flavor was compromised in the pursuit of healthy living. This was a delightful dining experience, executed with style, finesse and attention to every detail, and, oh, by the way, the food was vegan. Also noteworthy is the substantial, well curated natural wine list from which a glass of the Georgian Sapervani was a perfect compliment to our meal. Hats off to everyone involved. We could not be more impressed. (5 stars)

Service super, vibes are immaculate. Congrats to the chef for those dishes and flavours … wow wow. Never had these kind of combinations before. Highlights for us were the Carbonara Pinsa and the Date Cake (accompanied w the Hungarian Furmint which balanced perfectly) (5 stars)

I am going to attempt to relate what a delightful, even joyous experience. It was eating at soda club last night. I think I could be classified a carnivore, in that I don’t remember going to a vegan only restaurant. But when I was doing my research for new places to dine here last week, I was so intrigued by the menu, I somehow missed the fact that it was vegan only. Honestly, I don’t think I would have chosen it. Now… I’m considering going vegan. But I’m not sure there’s another place like this. It didn’t start off good. We had gotten up at 3 AM in Austin To catch the flight and were beat And ready to eat dinner early. After a cold walk/ long cab drive from where we staying near the park. we found ourselves at an innocuous corner a bit early a few minutes before it opened at 5:00. It is difficult to see before they open the door, but at five, a young man walked up and rolled up a graffiti covered garage door to reveal the inviting entrance. We walked across the street to the friendly Niagara bar for a drink before ( recommended- great Village vibe ) Still unsure as to what we would find, we walked in to a wonderful cozy spot. We started off with a delightful French cab , exquisite. By the time we had the focaccia, we knew we were in a kind of a magical space. We’ve had focaccia bread all over the world from California to Italy. This was undoubtedly the best. Dipped in a fresh garlic sauce that I can only describe as divinely inspired. I had the carbonara which had an incredible smokey flavor with mushrooms and artichokes tempura . Uniquely delicious. My wife loved the Butternut Squash Medaglioni, and I was lucky enough to get a few bites. Never had anything like this. The intimate dark setting is small but very well designed, and clean. Our server Owen was gracious and very helpful with selections. After dinner, Katy stopped by our table and we went on even more than this review about how much we enjoyed the experience. She obviously really cared about our experience, as was evident by every detail of this restaurant. I’ve never read the review this long. Bordering on a short story. But I was inspired … I think you will be too. (5 stars)

bio_text: Sofreh is a modern dining establishment that embodies the warmth and hospitality of traditional Persian homes, set within a bright and minimalist environment. The restaurant invites guests to gather and share authentic, well-crafted dishes that celebrate the rich culinary heritage of Persia, all while fostering a cozy and welcoming atmosphere. Sofreh specializes in authentic Persian cuisine, focusing on homemade ingredients such as yogurts and fresh-baked breads. The menu features a variety of traditional dishes, presented in a way that highlights the cultural significance of sharing meals with family and friends. Sofreh was opened in the summer of 2018 by Nasim Alikhani, who spent twenty-five years pursuing her dream of owning a restaurant. Her culinary journey began in childhood, influenced by her family's strong cooking traditions, and she honed her skills through various experiences before launching her restaurant.
menu_items: EGGPLANT AND WHEY DIP - ROASTED EGGPLANT, CRISPY ONIONS, CURED WHEY YOGURT, MINT OIL - $18
SHALLOTS & YOGURT - STRAINED YOGURT, PERSIAN SHALLOTS, CHIVE - $12
MAITAKE MUSHROOMS - MAITAKE MUSHROOMS, SUNCHOKE, WHEY - $20
GRILLED CARROTS & YOGURT - BABY CARROTS, STRAINED YOGURT, WHOLE SPICE HONEY, FRESH HERBS - $16
GRILLED ASPARAGUS - LIGHVAN CHEESE, SPICED PUMPKIN SEEDS, FRESH HERBS, SUMAC DRESSING - $14
ROASTED CAULIFLOWER - TOMATO & CHILI GLAZE, SHALLOT YOGURT, PICKLED VEGETABLES, PISTACHIO - $16
review_snippets: Absolutely delicious food and its own mix on a variety of Persian cuisine. Service was great with thoughtful staff. Only note I would make is that we were 5people for a 6person reservation and they charged us 20$ ( yes I agreed to it when I made reso but this change is completely normal for dinner). I told them immediately when we arrived. This is despite the table really only being for 5 people to begin with. 5 stars for everything but management. I would give it 2 stars. The extra star is for decor music and design, last for service which was great. I would recommend the lamb shank and steak. Egg plant was delicious and a variety of very tasty drinks. I would recommend this spot, but for a second time visit for me, this far in BK and poor management where it took almost 90 mins for our meal to be served...I'm likely not to go back. Worth the trip but only once (4 stars)

Absolutely loved Sofreh. Every dish was full of flavor and beautifully presented. The atmosphere feels calm, elegant, and truly special. The staff were kind and attentive, and the whole experience had that warm Persian charm that makes you want to come back. Definitely one of the best restaurants in New York City. (5 stars)

I don’t say this lightly: Sofreh is truly one of the city’s standout restaurants. Every dish reflects a level of mastery that’s hard to overstate. The kitchen takes authentic Persian flavors and elevates them with real creativity—the ribeye “kebab” is a perfect example. I was equally taken with the eggplant and whey dip; it was so good that I bought their cookbook afterward just to understand the sorcery behind it. And a special shoutout to the wonderful service team, who made the experience even better. (5 stars)

I absolutely loved the atmosphere at Sofreh. The space is so beautiful and thoughtfully designed, and even the staff uniforms added to how stylish and put together everything felt. The whole place has such a cute and welcoming vibe, and the staff were beyond nice. The food was fantastic. The dishes had small creative twists while still staying very authentic to traditional Persian flavors. The tahdig is an absolute must. It was the best I have ever had in my life. Just note that it is limited to one order per table. Portions are not very sharable unless you order several different dishes, which is what we ended up doing. I also tried the kabob, which was delicious, especially with the pomegranate sauce. That said, it was more like a steak than a traditional kabob, so just something to keep in mind. Sadly, I could not get a picture of it because it was so good we ate it right away. Overall, Sofreh is a beautiful restaurant with amazing food, wonderful staff, and a great atmosphere. I would definitely come back and recommend it to anyone looking for an elevated Persian dining experience in New York. (5 stars)

bio_text: Soothr LIC, located in Long Island City, NY, offers a vibrant and immersive dining experience inspired by the bustling heart of Bangkok's Yaowarat Chinatown. The restaurant combines fresh ingredients and authentic flavors with a lively atmosphere, where guests can enjoy a unique blend of culinary delights and enchanting performances. With a focus on creating memorable moments, Soothr transforms every meal into a celebration of food, fun, and fantasy. Soothr specializes in Thai cuisine, featuring a menu that highlights traditional recipes with a playful twist. The dining format encourages exploration of various dishes, allowing guests to experience a range of flavors and textures. Signature techniques include the use of fresh, locally sourced ingredients and innovative presentations that reflect the vibrant culture of Chinatown. A-Mei, the restaurant's spirited host, brings recipes passed down from her sister, J'Hong, infusing them with her own creative flair. Soothr LIC aims to create an immersive journey through Chinatown life, evolving from a comforting tea house by day to a nostalgic jazz club by night.
menu_items: Dungeness Crab Karee - Fresh Dungeness crab, sautéed and swathed in our signature golden curry-rich, velvety emulsion of egg and spice, studded with crisp celery, scallion, sweet onion, and peppers.
Yaowarat Roasted Duck - Succulent, five-spice roasted duck, perfumed with ginger and garlic, rests in a pool of its own lightly creamy, aromatic ginger jus. - $58.00
Steamed Branzino - A whole branzino, steamed to glistening perfection in a delicate ginger-soy broth, dramatically finished with julienned ginger and vibrant scallions. - $49.00

Tiger Prawns Ginger - Tamarind - Flour-dusted tiger prawns, fried to a delicate crunch, perched atop a nest of crispy vermicelli and drizzled with a captivating sweet-and-citrusy ginger-tamarind glaze. - $38.00
Spicy Crab Mian - Pan-fried potato noodles wok-tossed in a bold spicy sauce with sesame oil, shallots, shiitake, and peppers, laden with jumbo lump crab and finished with micro celery. - $30.00
Ba Mii Ka Moo - Dry egg noodles topped with steamed Gailan and meltingly tender, braised pork leg. The accompanying spicy vinaigrette cuts through the richness for a perfect balance. - $25.00
review_snippets: Our dinner was absolutely spectacular! Our server, Nina was warm, attentive, and offered excellent recommendations that truly elevated the entire experience. It was a great dining experience thanks to her! We started with the Lobster and Ha Gao from the Lunar New Year menu. The lobster was incredibly delicious which perfectly cooked and generously coated in a spicy sauce that complemented the sweetness of the meat beautifully. The Ha Gao were delicate and flavorful, with a satisfying bite. The Hoo Johr was also a standout! It was crispy on the outside, savory on the inside, and perfect as an appetizer to share. For our mains, the Panang Duck Lychee Curry was hands down the best rich, creamy, and packed with bold flavors, with just the right balance of sweetness from the lychee. The Shrimp Pad Thai was equally impressive, featuring plump shrimp, well-balanced seasoning, and perfectly cooked noodles. We ended the meal with mango sticky rice. Even though mango isn’t in season, the dessert was absolutely amazing! The sticky rice was warm and fragrant, paired with sweet coconut milk, mango Ice cream and fresh mango.. it was the perfect ending to a fantastic dinner. Highly recommend! (5 stars)

This restaurant really blow my mind and reset my taste for thai food. I have always like it. Been on several restaurants. But none like Soothr. Food was amazing. Unique experience with each bite. Service was fantastic, and staff supper friendly . Restaurant overall is everything you need if u looking for great food. We start with some crispy Chiken, fried dumplings 10/10 pad thai 😍, duck in curry sauce, wow 👌 those too were also fantastic. Can't wait to go back . Dessert was sweet and delicious... While im writing this im having a smile in my face,enjoying my food again (5 stars)

Had a great experience at Soothr today! Jesse provided excellent service, she was very attentive, friendly, and made us feel very welcome throughout the meal. The crab roe curry noodles (Karee Pu Noodles) were absolutely delicious, rich in flavor and perfectly balanced. The food came out quickly, and the overall service was efficient and very nice. Definitely would come back again! (5 stars)

I was in town for the weekend and couldn't wait to co to Soothr because of their reputation. I was starting to get packed and it was tight. It was like a Thai-Chinatown (Yaowarat) vibe. We were given an hour and a half time limit which is normal but I feel like we were being rushed. Started off with drinks, I wasn't a fan of my cocktail. Duck egg rolls had more wood ear mushrooms than duck. I was excited about Karee Pu (crab curry) the texture of the noodles were great. The curry was extra thick and had a strong cumin taste to it, we weren't a fan. We also got the duck noodles, once again the noodles were great. The duck was cooked perfectly but the gravy was so sweet and that was it, sweet. I love Thai food because of the mix of flavors, sweet, spicy, sour, salty, but this place didn't do it for us. I really wanted to like it but we were pretty underwhelmed. (3 stars)

Soothr LIC aims to create an immersive journey through Chinatown life, evolving from a comforting tea house by day to a nostalgic jazz club by night. Dungeness Crab Karee - Fresh Dungeness crab, sautéed and swathed in our signature golden curry-rich, velvety emulsion of egg and spice, studded with crisp celery, scallion, sweet onion, and peppers. Yaowarat Roasted Duck - Succulent, five-spice roasted duck, perfumed with ginger and garlic, rests in a pool of its own lightly creamy, aromatic ginger jus. - $58.00 Steamed Branzino - A whole branzino, steamed to glistening perfection in a delicate ginger-soy broth, dramatically finished with julienned ginger and vibrant scallions. - $49.00 Tiger Prawns Ginger - Tamarind - Flour-dusted tiger prawns, fried to a delicate crunch, perched atop a nest of crispy vermicelli and drizzled with a captivating sweet-and-citrusy ginger-tamarind glaze. - $38.00 Spicy Crab Mian - Pan-fried potato noodles wok-tossed in a bold spicy sauce with sesame oil, shallots, shiitake, and peppers, laden with jumbo lump crab and finished with micro celery. - $30.00 Ba Mii Ka Moo - Dry egg noodles topped with steamed Gailan and meltingly tender, braised pork leg. The accompanying spicy vinaigrette cuts through the richness for a perfect balance. - $25.00 Our dinner was absolutely spectacular! Our server, Nina was warm, attentive, and offered excellent recommendations that truly elevated the entire experience. It was a great dining experience thanks to her! We started with the Lobster and Ha Gao from the Lunar New Year menu. The lobster was incredibly delicious which perfectly cooked and generously coated in a spicy sauce that complemented the sweetness of the meat beautifully. The Ha Gao were delicate and flavorful, with a satisfying bite. The Hoo Johr was also a standout! It was crispy on the outside, savory on the inside, and perfect as an appetizer to share. For our mains, the Panang Duck Lychee Curry was hands down the best rich, creamy, and packed with bold flavors, with just the right balance of sweetness from the lychee. The Shrimp Pad Thai was equally impressive, featuring plump shrimp, well-balanced seasoning, and perfectly cooked noodles. We ended the meal with mango sticky rice. Even though mango isn’t in season, the dessert was absolutely amazing! The sticky rice was warm and fragrant, paired with sweet coconut milk, mango Ice cream and fresh mango.. it was the perfect ending to a fantastic dinner. Highly recommend! (5 stars) This restaurant really blow my mind and reset my taste for thai food. I have always like it. Been on several restaurants. But none like Soothr. Food was amazing. Unique experience with each bite. Service was fantastic, and staff supper friendly . Restaurant overall is everything you need if u looking for great food. We start with some crispy Chiken, fried dumplings 10/10 pad thai 😍, duck in curry sauce, wow 👌 those too were also fantastic. Can't wait to go back . Dessert was sweet and delicious... While im writing this im having a smile in my face,enjoying my food again (5 stars) Had a great experience at Soothr today! Jesse provided excellent service, she was very attentive, friendly, and made us feel very welcome throughout the meal. The crab roe curry noodles (Karee Pu Noodles) were absolutely delicious, rich in flavor and perfectly balanced. The food came out quickly, and the overall service was efficient and very nice. Definitely would come back again! (5 stars) I was in town for the weekend and couldn't wait to co to Soothr because of their reputation. I was starting to get packed and it was tight. It was like a Thai-Chinatown (Yaowarat) vibe. We were given an hour and a half time limit which is normal but I feel like we were being rushed. Started off with drinks, I wasn't a fan of my cocktail. Duck egg rolls had more wood ear mushrooms than duck. I was excited about Karee Pu (crab curry) the texture of the noodles were great. The curry was extra thick and had a strong cumin taste to it, we weren't a fan. We also got the duck noodles, once again the noodles were great. The duck was cooked perfectly but the gravy was so sweet and that was it, sweet. I love Thai food because of the mix of flavors, sweet, spicy, sour, salty, but this place didn't do it for us. I really wanted to like it but we were pretty underwhelmed. (3 stars)

bio_text: Speedy Romeo is a celebrated neighborhood restaurant located in Brooklyn, NY, known for its neo-neapolitan-style pizza and extensive natural wine selection. The establishment combines a kitschy décor with modern touches, creating a unique dining atmosphere that appeals to both locals and visitors. With a menu that features perfectly charred pizzas, mouthwatering pastas, and seasonal American dishes, Speedy Romeo has earned acclaim from critics and holds a Michelin-rated status. The restaurant focuses on neo-neapolitan-style pizza and Italian-influenced seasonal American cooking. The menu includes a variety of options such as pizzas, pastas, greenmarket salads, and a tasty burger, catering to diverse tastes. Founded in 2012 by college roommates Justin Bazdarich and Todd Feldman, Speedy Romeo was transformed from an old auto parts shop into a unique dining establishment. The restaurant is named after co-owner Todd's family champion race horse, whose portrait is displayed in the kitchen.
menu_items: S.R. CAESAR - romaine, parm, anchovy, lemon - $16
KALE APPLE SALAD - goat cheese vinaigrette, seasonal fruit, walnuts - $16
S.R. WEDGE - iceberg, ranch, gorgonzola, pancetta, cherry tomato, herbs - $18
BEETS AND RICOTTA - ricotta, hazelnuts, watercress, horseradish, lemon - $17
BUTTERNUT SQUASH SOUP - roasted brussels, walnut cream, pancetta, pepitas, black pepper - $14
STUFFED PEPPERS - salami, cheese, bread crumbs, tomato - $14
review_snippets: Speedy Romeo has some of the best pizza in the city. The crust is just PERFECT. Thin but with enough consistency, crunchy in all the right places… just wow. We order a pizza approximately once a week and are always impressed. We like eating there too - it’s casual and the food is delicious. Good wine and craft beer selection. Their Caesar salad is top notch. Just go and thank me later. 🍕 (5 stars)

As a St. Louis transplant, I’ve spent decades searching for a St. Louis style pizza in NYC to poor success, but everyone pointed to Speedy Romeo as my last, best hope. So, for better or for worse, I’m going to endeavor to compare this pizza to the square beyond compare. The wood-fired crust at Speedy Romeo does not resemble the cracker-thin St. Louis slab, but it sure is tasty. These sauces and toppings feel too high falutin to be found in my favorite St Louis takeout, but, oh, I enjoyed them, too. The cheese- I made sure to order a pizza with provel cheese- the cheese instantly took me back home. It hit the mark and even made me a little homesick. I loved it and will be back soon. In the end, Speedy Romeo felt a little bit like New York, a little bit St. Louis, but it was mostly its own unique and delicious style. I’d recommend it to anyone from the Lou, anyone from the city- anyone at all. (5 stars)
Speedy Romeo’s is such a cute spot for great pizza. The crust has a nice chew without being super thick. Super relaxed environment with great wait staff. (5 stars)

Found this place on the Michelin Bib Gourmand list, which denotes establishment that have high quality food at reasonable prices. Speedy Romeo definitely lived up to the description. I went with some friends and had four different pizzas so we could try a few things. St.Louie - Bar style pie, where the pickled peppers and provel cheese shine Dangerfield - a deconstructed meatball sub and my wife’s favorite King salami - nice meat lovers pie, I was excited about the fennel salami ( finocchiona ) but couldn’t really taste it with all the other flavors Truffle shuffle - this was my favorite one, pepperoni with a little truffle ranch made for a nice savory experience I will definitely be back to try the pasta (5 stars)

bio_text: Sunday in Brooklyn is a beloved neighborhood restaurant located in Williamsburg, offering a warm and inviting atmosphere that celebrates American culinary traditions. With a focus on community and comfort, the restaurant serves a variety of American staples, making it a perfect spot for casual dining any day of the week. The restaurant specializes in New American cuisine, featuring a menu that highlights seasonal ingredients and classic dishes with a modern twist. Guests can enjoy a range of offerings from breakfast to dinner, including a popular brunch service.
menu_items: Coconut Shrimp - Sweet Chili, Lime Zest - $20
Chicken Yummos - Cobanero Buffalo, Fancy Ranch - $15
Cheese Fries - Frank's Hot Sauce, White Cheddar - $14
Fried Calamari - Wild Caught Rhode Island Squid, Spicy Marinara - $16
Wood Fired Pita Herb Butter - Ofira's Original Pita - $14
Hummus - Pistachio Tahini, Sumac Yogurt - $20
review_snippets: What a great spot!! We came here for a lovely dinner that most certainly did NOT disappoint! Sunday in Brooklyn is a delightful little corner spot that seems small initially, but actually has plenty of seating throughout - including in an upstairs space. Regardless, we were promptly seated (without a reservation) in a table downstairs, and had very friendly, hospitable service throughout our visit. While dining, we ordered a few of the cocktails, and I found each one I tried to be a good amount of strength while also creative in the flavors and heat. My personal favorite was the Ski Lift, which is a hot cocktail with bourbon, coffee, and other ingredients - soooo soothing, STRONG, and flavorful! Now on to main event - the food! My wood-fired lasagna was INCREDIBLE - so much flavor, texture, and uniqueness to each bite. My partner's chicken pot pie was similarly unique and yet familiar in its excellent textures and taste! Sunday in Brooklyn had a wonderful ambiance, lovely food, and great service - I highly recommend! (5 stars)

The service amazing. For 2 people they offered a 2 person table, outside or inside, they sat us right away. The food was Fast and tasted fresh. Eggs were done perfectly, soft scrambled, bacon crispy, potatoes were a little too salty, and the shakshuka was a little disappointing, like salsa with pouched eggs, but the bread was crisp and yummy when dipped into the bowl. However, the Sunday pancake was amazing. It’s was like a mini fluffy yellow cake with delicious buttered maple all over. not a maple taste but like a chocolaty buttery nutty flavor. “It was like a reward”. We enjoyed it the most. Overall we understand the hype and definitely recommend to try it for yourself. (5 stars)

Visited Sunday in Brooklyn for brunch and honestly, wow. We got the pistachio hummus with wood-fired flatbread — probably the richest, most flavorful meze I’ve ever had. A total must-try (and so generous we couldn’t even finish it!). Also ordered the warm grain bowl, and it arrived in what felt like 5 minutes — unbelievably fast service. The bowl itself was pure comfort: warm, rich, and beautifully balanced. The eggs were cooked like a soufflé — soft and melting — topped with a gigantic half avocado and a generous handful of pepitas (which I love and rarely see done this well). The rice underneath was so delicious. Finished with a cappuccino, served instantly in a lovely porcelain cup — the perfect touch to end brunch. Our server was incredibly kind and attentive, checking in often to make sure everything was perfect. Honestly, one of the best brunch experiences we’ve had in (5 stars)

I've been to Sunday in Brooklyn several times for both brunch and dinner. Brunch certainly gets busy but its a fun time - make a reservation. The food, service and drinks are always lovely - Thomas the bartender is incredible! I recommend trying the Sage Fright brunch cocktail, the Wood Roasted Half Chicken for dinner and the S'mores soft serve for dessert. The S'mores latte is fun too for all the s'mores fans. (5 stars)

bio_text: Superiority Burger is a vibrant lacto-ovo vegetarian restaurant located in the East Village of Manhattan, known for its welcoming atmosphere and commitment to innovative plant-based cuisine. With a focus on sustainability and creativity, the restaurant offers a unique dining experience that caters to both vegetarians and vegans alike, making it a popular destination for health-conscious diners. The restaurant specializes in vegetarian and vegan dishes, featuring a diverse menu that includes house-made breads and a variety of creative burger options. Superiority Burger emphasizes fresh, seasonal ingredients and offers a full bar to complement its culinary offerings. We opened our doors on June 25, 2015 at 430 east 9th Street in the East Village of Manhattan. On April 1, 2023 we relocated around the corner to 119 Avenue A across the street from Tompkins Square Park.
review_snippets: This spot used to be a diner and Superiority Burger totally carries the legacy forward with the paper daily specials and slices of pearl pie in the refrigerated case. That said, the menu here is unlike any restaurant anywhere. Honestly we didn’t even really know what we were ordering but the side of cabbage, fries, yuba sandwich and panelle were mind-blowing. Super wild flavors. Service was phenomenal. I’m hooked. The pearl pie with fresh passion fruit was amazing. (5 stars)

We went early on a Sunday and there was no wait at all. I loved the vibe and the old photos on the wall...in particular, a photo of Dojo on St Marks which brought back a lot of memories... Service was laid-back, friendly and quick. On to the food...three in my party got the Superiority Burger with fries in three different ways. It was all spot-on and after tasting it, it is a strong vegetarian burger. But forget that and go for the TFT - a fried tofu sandwich which was simply outstanding. The fries are some of the absolute best I've had in NYC. We also had a side of burnt broccoli which was ok, but nothing too special. Go for the TFT, fries and the vibe. (5 stars)

This place is magic - the founder brings his eclectic taste to create something truly special. The Superiority Burger (the namesake!) is pure perfection. The tanginess from the pickles, the soft yet crunchy patty… every bite feels special, like I’m blessed or something. And when I’m in the mood to cheat, I’ll pair it with the fries — also perfection. Everything here tastes so fresh and high-quality. Burnt Broccoli - again, perfection. It comes with a sauce on the side that’s such a nice surprise, and I go every week and NEVER get bored. The Date Shake… who would’ve thought it’d be so interesting? The founder always sneaks in elements that elevate the flavor profile - the surprise this time is the orange zest. Their specials are always exceptional and super creative. I guarantee you won’t see anything like them anywhere else. And the service - truly great. I’ve seen the same staff for years, which brings a sense of community and continuity that’s rare in the city these days. So yes… I come here all the time, and I’m never bored! Oh yes it is worth the hype btw! (5 stars)

Almost never misses. Love the integration with local and seasonal produce. Phenomenal desserts. Unlike other nyc institutions with staid menus and no variation you can have different food every time or rely on old favorites. Underrated for sure (5 stars)

bio_text: Sushi Akira is an intimate 12-seat omakase restaurant located on the Upper East Side, offering a unique dining experience that combines Michelin-level precision, artistry, and exceptional service. The restaurant aims to make high-quality omakase accessible to a wider audience, providing a warm and inviting atmosphere for sushi enthusiasts and newcomers alike. Sushi Akira specializes in omakase, featuring expertly crafted nigiri and seasonal small plates. The culinary focus is on traditional Japanese techniques, with an emphasis on fresh, high-quality ingredients and meticulous presentation. Chef-Owner Nikki honed her craft at renowned sushi establishments in New York City, including Masa and Sushi Nakazawa. Her culinary journey began in Tokyo, where she worked as a dishwasher in a Michelin-starred restaurant, igniting her passion for gastronomy. Despite the challenges of being a female sushi chef, Nikki has built a reputation for her exceptional skills and dedication to her guests.
menu_items: Omakase Menu - 19-course omakase experience featuring seasonal ingredients flown in from Japan. - $220
review_snippets: I had an incredible omakase experience here. All of the sushi was so fresh, flavourful, and beautifully presented. There was such a wide selection of high quality dishes but some ones that stood out were the hairy crab with uni, fatty tuna, and Spanish mackerel. The staff/chefs were incredibly welcoming and accommodating. The atmosphere was a very clean and intimate venue providing the best sort of environment for an omakase. Overall, really happy with my experience here and will be looking forward to coming back. (5 stars)

I had an unforgettable dinner at Sushi Akira. Every single bite offered a unique and thoughtful flavor, and the chef absolutely nailed each course with precision, creativity, and balance. It was truly remarkable from start to finish. The service was warm, attentive, and perfectly paced, enhancing the overall dining experience. The ambiance is elegant yet inviting, calm, intimate, and ideal for appreciating a high-quality omakase. I paired my meal with a glass of Mâcon-Villages, which complemented the earlier courses beautifully, and finished with a Riesling for dessert, a perfect way to complete the experience. Overall, an outstanding and memorable meal. Highly recommended. (5 stars)

An incredible omakase experience at Sushi Akira. Every course was beautifully presented and incredibly fresh, with fish flown in from Japan and prepared with amazing precision. The chef’s attention to detail and the intimate counter experience made the entire meal feel special. One of the few female omakase chefs in NYC, Chef Nikki has refined her craft at Masa, Sushi Nakazawa, and Sushi of Gari, bringing Michelin-level precision, artistry, and service to Sushi Akira’s intimate 12-seat setting, 19-course omakase experience. Truly one of the best omakase experiences in NYC—can’t wait to come back. 🍣✨ (5 stars)

An absolutely amazing dining experience! The ingredients were incredibly fresh and full of flavor, each dish uniquely crafted with great attention to detail. Our chef was super friendly and took the time to explain every ingredient and course, making the omakase feel truly authentic. A genuinely memorable meal — we’ll definitely be coming back again! (5 stars)

bio_text: Sushi Ikumi, located in the serene neighborhood of SoHo, Manhattan, offers a unique dining experience that harmonizes the art of sushi with a commitment to sustainability. The restaurant embraces the philosophy of wholeness, utilizing local and seasonal ingredients while striving for zero waste. Guests can expect a creative and exciting menu that reflects the rich traditions of Kaiseki cuisine, all within a vibrant urban setting. Sushi Ikumi specializes in Omakase dining, featuring a Chef's Tasting Menu that showcases the best seasonal ingredients. The culinary focus is on traditional Kaiseki techniques, emphasizing the natural flavors and artistry of sushi preparation. At Sushi Ikumi, the culinary vision builds upon the expertise of Chef Hiro from their sister restaurant, Hirohisa, who is known for his meticulous approach to seasonal ingredients.
review_snippets: Great experience! The space felt cozy but spacious. Service was very attentive. Compared with other omakase places at similar price point, you get lots of course. All the appetizer/amuse dishes were delicious, especially the fired unagi and the Japanese amberjack sashimi. Super fresh fish and seafood and you get a great variety, and uni from Hokkaido was sweet and creamy. Ikumi also has two seaweed pieces which I don’t see commonly in other places, and both were very flavorful, and my guess is that these are their way to replace the more commonly-seen hand roll. Chef doesn’t talk too much but is very friendly :) Would love to see Ikumi receive a star soon. (5 stars)

In the age of accelerated inflation, $220pp for quality omakase in NYC w/ thoughtful ingredient selection & top-notch balance between shari and neta is hard to come by. Excellent bang for the buck and would highly recommend. (5 stars)

Been here three times and honestly this is one of the best omakase in the city. Every dish is art and seafood quality is top notch. Service is wonderful, too. There’s too many omakase doing those “wagyu+uni” or “salmon + turuffle” those kinds of things. I love how Sushi Ikumi only focus on bringing out the best flavor of the fish, and not over complicating it. Highly recommend. (5 stars)

I had a chance to eat here this weekend and Chef Jeong delivered just an amazing line up of 19 beautiful and delicious courses. He started off strong with an egg custard with sweet corn. We’re at the summer peak of corn season and it just captured the essence so well while wetting the appetite for what was to come. From there we moved on to the fish and nigiri courses and they were just so good. The chefs keeps to a traditional style which I very much prefer - just enough to elevate the fish without too many elements getting in the way. The quality of fish was excellent for the price point - some of the plumpest and delicious shrimp I’ve had, an incredible sea perch, and two cuts of tuna from Montauk among my favorites. One of the new dishes for me were cockles which were served live and tasted fresh out of the ocean. No wagyu on the menu here but I think it’s been overdone at omakase restaurants and again, the fish was divine. The atmosphere was perfect for the experience - intimate with just a small simple counter and the chef working his magic. I will return. (5 stars)

review_snippets: Sushi Nakazawa has been on my list for a while, so I was glad to finally check it out last weekend. It’s definitely larger and less intimate than many of the other omakase spots I’ve been to in the city, but the service and quality more than make up for that. The meal was perfectly paced and never felt rushed. Every piece of sushi was incredibly fresh and exquisitely prepared. You can tell they know exactly what they’re doing. It’s definitely on the pricey side, but overall I’d say it was worth it. (5 stars)

This was a pretty good omakase experience, but not necessarily incredible. The sushi tasted excellent, and having 20 pieces was ideal. The selection and presentation, though, was a bit uninspired and seemed to just check the boxes of what you expect at omakase. The atmosphere was the weakest point. The lights were bright, white walls, grey carpets, and black tables gave a monochromatic look, and even the counter was all white. Most other omakase places keep low warm lighting with spotlights for the food, natural colors and earth tones like bamboo for the counter, furniture, and walls. Being the *complete* opposite was really jarring. If you're only looking for good sushi, this is a good choice. But I'm not likely to come back to this restaurant. (4 stars)

New York trip. Hubby took me to this Sushi restaurant and we ordered Omakase. Surprisingly price was very decent for also being 1 Michelin Star. There were 2 selections for Omakase we picked the higher one which only $220 per person adding truffle shave on one of the Sushi piece was $35. So total $255 per person not bad at all. We ordered a bottle Sake $135. Food tasted very good. The Omakase included 3 appetizers and 17 Sushi pieces tasted very fresh. Staffs were nice from host to our servers. We uber there. Never drive in NY cuz parking and driving is crazy lol. We made rsvp so we got in no problem. Totally recommended here. (5 stars)

always wanted to try this omakase spot & have only heard good things about it - so happy that my bf took me here for my birthday dinner! 😋⭐️ easily one of my favorite omakase places in NYC - the quality of the fish is unmatched, service was fantastic as well. our favorite has to be the wagyu nigiri and eel - but every bite was delicious and we were honestly shocked how consistently good each piece was. would definitely come back here for a special occasion - def on a pricier side but totally worth it! (5 stars)

bio_text: Sushi Noz offers an intimate and elegant dining experience that transports guests to a serene world reminiscent of ancient Kyoto temples. The restaurant's design features exquisite Sukiya-style architecture, highlighted by a 200-year-old hinoki wood sushi bar and a traditional hinoki ice-chest refrigerator, creating a harmonious atmosphere that enhances the sensory experience of dining. With a focus on refinement and artistry, every detail is curated to evoke a sense of well-being and appreciation for the culinary journey. Sushi Noz specializes in Edomae-style sushi, offering a meticulously crafted tasting menu that begins with 5-6 otsumami small plates, followed by 12-14 courses of seasonal nigiri. The menu emphasizes the use of both aged and freshly-caught fish, paired with traditional vinegar-seasoned rice, showcasing Chef Noz's dedication to authentic sushi techniques. Chef Nozomu Abe, inspired by his grandfather's seafood company in Hokkaido, began his culinary journey as an apprentice in Sapporo before mastering Edomae techniques in Tokyo. After moving to New York in 2007 and working at Sushiden, he opened Sushi Noz to share his unique culinary vision with an American audience.
menu_items: Otsumami - seasonal fish and vegetables
Seasonal Nigiri - seasonal fish
Miso Soup - traditional miso
Tamago - Japanese omelette
Dessert - seasonal dessert
review_snippets: We spent our special night at Sushi Noz when we visited NY. We were informed during the reservation that Chef Nozomu Abe would not presented at that day. It was okay for us as we once had the worst experience at the world-most famous sushi omakase place so nothing can be worse than that. We arrived just a little bit early so we were first asked to wait in front of the ash room while the chefs prepared for the very last bit. Then, we got invited to the Hinoki room right on the reservation time. The dinning room definitely brought us back to Japan. Feel warm and familiar. There was a little sealed letter set in front of us. I found it such a lovely setup. Then, we ordered different Sake for that night Omakase. The price was quite high for a glass. They started off with 6 dishes before followed by 11 sushi (including a hand-roll) then finished off with Miso soup, Tamakoyaki and the sweetest melon. All 6 dishes definitely one of the best combination of best ingredients. However, I found this far from Edomae style. It’s more of western style for us. Although, we still like all the dishes. For the sushi, I found it interesting the way they chose to serve us each ingredient like Ika was served fresh, chewy and crispy (usually served super soft). Then, the rest of the sushi lines were served in a softer texture manner in a good interesting way. But to be honest, we found the ingredients a bit simple than any other Omakase we’ve been to. Nothing beyond expectation. The meal finished with the sweetest melon from Hokkaido. I miss this course ending. I think a lot of Omakase places stop serving melon and replace with other type of dessert. Definitely you will be satisfied with the Omakase course but I found it a bit pricey and not valued for paying $1,500 (including drinks and tip) for 2. (5 stars)
Small Omakase sushi on the UES, that has a great standing counter with a good lunch special! I totally recommend it. (5 stars)

An omakase experience well worth their Michelin stars. The sushi is top notch, and the service and attention to detail are excellent, as should be expected at this caliber of restaurant. The atmosphere and venue are unique. I believe there are multiple counters, but they are separated from each other so diners have a very intimate experience with their sushi chefs. It was a very quiet and serene experience. If you you're looking for something quiet and calm, this is the place. I've been to a number of omakase places, and I think this one was memorable for me because the vibe was so different than the others. Don't get me wrong- the food was still incredible, though. (5 stars)

I love Sushi Noz. Aside from Atomix, it is my favorite restaurant in the city. The service, atmosphere, and most importantly food are spectacular. My favorite part of the experience is as it should be -- the sushi. They use wasabi in a way I've never really experienced before and there are many bites that you just wish that experience again. The flavor of each dish typically has many layers and you can amplify that even further with their drink pairing. Often high end restaurants provide a pairing that detracts from the meal but that is very much not the case here. I have been three times at this point and will go again. Side note: their gift at the end of the meal rules 9.5/10 (5 stars)

bio_text: Sushi Sho is an intimate Omakase restaurant that has been serving exquisite sushi since 1983. With a seating capacity of just six at the sushi bar, the dining experience is highly personalized, allowing guests to savor a carefully curated selection of dishes crafted by master chef Aki Kawata. The ambiance reflects a commitment to traditional Japanese culinary artistry, where each meal is a celebration of simplicity and the unique flavors of the finest ingredients. Sushi Sho specializes in Edo-mae and Kansai style sushi, offering a chef's choice Omakase menu that features a 16-item course of assorted nigiri-based sushi. The restaurant emphasizes purity and balance in its dishes, showcasing the natural flavors of each ingredient. Sushi Sho was established in 1983 by master chef Aki Kawata, who has dedicated over 30 years to preserving the traditions of Japanese sushi. His early training took place at his family restaurant in Wakayama, Japan.
menu_items: OMAKASE - Chef's choice of assorted nigiri-based sushi. - $190
Tsukemori - Assorted Japanese pickles - $15
Chawan-Mushi - Steamed seafood custard soup - $15
Ankimo - Monk fish liver steamed with sake and served with PONZU sauce
Sunomono Salad - Served with our house special sesame seed dressing. - $5
Kyurimomi - Cucumber - $5
review_snippets: I came here for my birthday and opted for the sake pairing, and it turned out to be one of the most memorable dining experiences I’ve ever had. The food was immaculate, deeply rooted in Japanese culture while preserving the art of sushi-making that has been practiced for hundreds of years. Every course came with a story, which made the experience feel thoughtful. One highlight was learning about ice aging, a technique they use for one of their pieces, which completely changed how I think about texture and flavor in sushi. The staff was incredibly welcoming and meticulous, taking the time to explain not just what we were eating, but the process, technique, and history behind each piece. The sake pairing was top notch, with responsible pours that enhanced the meal without getting wasted. During the okonomi section, I added eight extra pieces as a birthday treat and to explore more of the menu. My favorite was the ankimo sushi with pickled watermelon. The ankimo melted in my mouth and was genuinely life-changing, worth the extra cost. To end the night, the chef surprised me with a gift of chopsticks and a chirashi box, which you usually need to get for $70. Again, top notch hospitality. If you’re looking for a special experience and appreciate the artistry of Japanese culinary, this is absolutely worth it. (5 stars)

Very different experience omakase with traditional Japanese bites. The omakase was unique in that the flavors, fish, and selection was extremely different from your normal Omakase of trying 20 different sashimi. Lots of bites were ranging from fish, to tofu, to fruit. You had to eat a pear, different soups, and a small ice cream and cold noodles at the end. Strictly no pictures allowed inside. It is definitely different and if you prefer the original sushi only type of omakase this place isn’t for you. (5 stars)

I was Dining at Sushi Sho few weeks ago. It felt less like sitting down for dinner and more like stepping quietly into an artist’s studio. The multi-course tasting unfolds slowly, thoughtfully—each piece presented with the precision and beauty of a small sculpture. Every bite is perfectly balanced: the rice warm and delicate, the fish pristine, the flavors layered in a way that feels both simple and profound. Nothing is rushed. Nothing is excessive. Just purity, technique, and extraordinary taste. What makes the experience unforgettable is the intimacy of the counter. You watch the chef create each course just inches away. His hands move with calm confidence, shaping rice, slicing fish, placing each piece together as if composing a painting. You can see the concentration, the pride, the quiet joy of someone who has dedicated a lifetime to mastering a craft. Each course arrives like a small masterpiece—beautiful, intentional, and fleeting. For a moment it exists only for you, before dissolving into a perfect bite. By the end of the tasting menu, you realize you haven’t just had an exceptional meal. You’ve witnessed devotion, artistry, and the rare magic that happens when skill and passion meet at the same counter. An unforgettable experience, and truly one of the most extraordinary culinary performances in New York. (5 stars)

In my opinion, this is the only destination-worthy sushiya outside of Japan. Nakazawa-san is a legend and his style is singular, with many original creations. His NYC shop evolved the legacy of his Yotsuya and Honolulu locations. The focus of the meal here is mastery of the history of sushi, including various forms of preservation and fermentation. It is not the place to come to if you expect piles of toro, uni or caviar. Diners should also be aware that at all Sushi Sho locations, service is split between two chefs. So a reservation does not guarantee that you will be seated with the more senior chef. There is no detectable impact on the food or pacing in my opinion. Similarly, at all Sushi Sho locations the okonomi portion of the meal, including presentation of all the add-on items, is typical. Whether this format suits you is a matter of personal taste. (5 stars)

ohitashi - seasonal vegetables in a light soy dashi - $9.25
kinpira - stir-fried burdock and lotus root - $9.00
edamame - boiled Japanese soy beans - $11.00
karasumi daikon - salt cured Japanese bottarga with daikon radish - $18.00
hone senbei - flash fried sea eel’s backbone - $12.00
review_snippets: Absolutely amazing. You could not ask for better food, fresh ingredients, traditional, well presented and a fast and efficient service. I could not have asked for more. I recommend the omakase, I could have gone on eating until I burst but had to say stop eventually. Bravo. The best sushi I have eaten in the US, Europe, and Japan. (5 stars)

In an era where the omakase experience is getting increasingly commercialized, this longtime institution clearly stands out with its professionalism and excellent quality fish. They’ve been around since the 90s and honestly, it shows. It was a breath of fresh air to come here and not eat the exact same pieces of fish you get at the majority of omakase spots in NYC. Highlights include saltwater eel, mackerel (both kinds), firefly squid and more. Even the toro tastes superior to most other places. (5 stars)

We had sushi there yesterday and it was truly an amazing experience. The chef was not only highly skilled and professional, but also very funny, which made the whole dining experience even more enjoyable. The sushi and sashimi were incredibly fresh—honestly the freshest and best I’ve ever had. Every bite was full of clean, natural flavor. Highly recommend! (5 stars)

TLDR: Visiting from LA. Beautiful, upscale sushi bar better suited for omakase or a proper sit-down. Toro and Spanish mackerel were excellent. Pricey for a quick bite. We dropped a rental nearby and walked into Sushi Yasuda looking for some rolls. It’s really a reservation-leaning spot with a calm, minimalist counter setup, ideal for omakase at lunch or dinner. Staff was professional and kind; the manager felt a bit stressed, but our chef at the back counter was friendly and helpful. We kept it simple with a few cut rolls and a couple of nigiri. The toro and Spanish mackerel were standouts clean flavor and perfect rice. Rolls were well made. For a light order, the bill was about $120 before tip, so expect premium pricing. If you want a fast, casual sushi stop, there are easier options. If you want a refined counter experience with top fish, this is a strong choice. Pro tips • Book a counter seat for omakase to get the full value. That’s the chef’s specialty. • Come at lunch if you want a calmer vibe. • Expect premium prices even for a small order. (4 stars)

You could not ask for better food, fresh ingredients, traditional, well presented and a fast and efficient service. I could not have asked for more. I recommend the omakase, I could have gone on eating until I burst but had to say stop eventually. Bravo. The best sushi I have eaten in the US, Europe, and Japan. (5 stars) In an era where the omakase experience is getting increasingly commercialized, this longtime institution clearly stands out with its professionalism and excellent quality fish. They’ve been around since the 90s and honestly, it shows. It was a breath of fresh air to come here and not eat the exact same pieces of fish you get at the majority of omakase spots in NYC. Highlights include saltwater eel, mackerel (both kinds), firefly squid and more. Even the toro tastes superior to most other places. (5 stars) We had sushi there yesterday and it was truly an amazing experience. The chef was not only highly skilled and professional, but also very funny, which made the whole dining experience even more enjoyable. The sushi and sashimi were incredibly fresh—honestly the freshest and best I’ve ever had. Every bite was full of clean, natural flavor. Highly recommend! (5 stars) TLDR: Visiting from LA. bio_text: Szechuan Gourmet 39 offers a vibrant dining experience that celebrates the rich and dynamic flavors of Szechuan cuisine. With nearly 20 years of culinary expertise, the restaurant prides itself on delivering high-quality, handmade meals that evoke the warmth and nostalgia of traditional Sichuan culture. The inviting atmosphere and commitment to accessibility ensure that guests from all walks of life can enjoy the robust and full-bodied flavors that define this beloved cuisine. Szechuan Gourmet 39 specializes in authentic Szechuan cuisine, focusing on bold, spicy flavors and intricate dishes. The menu features a variety of options, including signature dishes like Spicy Lamb Pot and Smoky Wok-Tossed Chicken with Roasted Chili. The restaurant employs traditional cooking techniques that highlight the unique characteristics of Szechuan ingredients, particularly the use of red pepper. The restaurant has nearly 20 years of experience and has gained recognition from esteemed culinary platforms, including a spot on the Michelin Bib Gourmand list.

review_snippets: Amazing Asian Cuisine! By far some of the best Chinese food I have ever enjoyed. The duck was fabulous - crispy and moist. The orange chicken was by far the best I have ever had. It was not sweet, perfectly seasoned with veggies intricately sliced. The Chow Fun noodles were smoky and beef was tender and moist. The service was impressive. Overall, an excellent dining experience. Everyone walked away satisfied and happy! (5 stars)

Ordered the mapo tofu with egg drop soup and the General Tso’s chicken with wonton soup. Portions were on the smaller side, and the mapo tofu was a bit heavy on the chili paste, but the rice and egg drop soup were spot on. The service really stood out: the waiters were excellent and very kind. Overall, a pleasant experience 😊 (4 stars)

The food was excellent! especially the Ma Paul Tofu (Mapo Tofu). The flavor was rich and perfectly balanced. I arrived a little before noon, so I was lucky to get a table immediately without waiting. The taste definitely lives up to the Michelin award. (4 stars)

Phenomenal Sichuan food! Every dish was authentic and packed with flavor. The restaurant is very comfortable and has a great vibe, but what really stands out is the staff—they are incredibly friendly and attentive. Highly recommend! (5 stars)
