bio_text: Tamarind Tribeca is a premier Indian restaurant located in the vibrant heart of Tribeca, NYC, offering an exquisite dining experience that marries traditional Indian flavors with contemporary elegance. Under the guidance of owner Mr. Avtar Walia, the restaurant aims to redefine the perception of Indian cuisine, presenting it in its purest form while embracing the sophistication of modern dining. Guests are invited to embark on a culinary journey that showcases the rich cultural diversity of India through artfully crafted dishes and an exceptional wine selection. Tamarind Tribeca specializes in authentic Indian cuisine, focusing on classical flavors presented with a modern sensibility. The menu features a variety of options, including a la carte selections and expertly paired wine offerings, designed to enhance the dining experience. Signature techniques include the use of traditional Indian cooking methods combined with innovative presentations. Mr. Avtar Walia, the owner, has a rich background in the culinary world, having previously co-owned the renowned restaurant Dawat and later opening the original Tamarind in Flatiron, which received a Michelin star. With the establishment of Tamarind Tribeca, he aims to elevate Indian cuisine within the fine dining landscape of New York.

Punjabi Mutton - Slow-cooked mutton with spices - $28

Dal Makhani - Black lentils cooked with butter and cream - $14

review_snippets: Tamarind Tribeca — Elegant space, strong service, inconsistent kitchen (Lunch visit) Tamarind Tribeca makes an excellent first impression. The restaurant is visually grand, with a refined fine-dining ambience, a well-designed interior, and a fully stocked bar with a respectable wine list. Service during our lunch was warm, professional, and attentive throughout. We were seated by the window near the bar, which was a pleasant spot. Drinks Raj Royal (Old Fashioned variation): Nicely presented with a rosemary garnish and competently made. Slightly sweeter than I prefer, but acceptable. 5/10 Lychee Martini: Very sweet, with no noticeable pineapple flavor despite it being listed on the menu. Essentially tasted like lychee juice with alcohol. 3/10 Starters Bhagare Jhinga: Appealing presentation — sautéed shrimp with tomato chutney and a mustard seed–curry leaf tempering. However, the dish lacked basic seasoning, the chutney tasted undercooked, and the shrimp felt underdone and slightly crunchy. Punjabi Thike Kebab (Chicken Tikka): Bright red in color, suggesting heavy food coloring. The chicken lacked proper marination, was undercooked, chewy, and difficult to cut. Presentation was fine but execution was poor. 2/10 To their credit, the staff promptly replaced this dish with: Tellicherry Pepper Murgh: A clear improvement. Well plated, properly cooked, and nicely seasoned with a bold black pepper profile and a slight tamarind tang in the sauce. Chicken was tender and flavorful. 7/10 Main Course Punjabi Kukkad: A standard North Indian chicken curry with onion-ginger-garlic gravy and whole spices. Unfortunately, this felt under-finished — the gravy tasted like a pre-prepared base that wasn’t fully cooked out, and the chicken was again firm and under-seasoned, as if added separately. For such a fundamental dish, this was disappointing. 3/10 Dale-e-Tamarind (Dal Makhani): Somewhat better, but still seemed undercooked. Dal makhani benefits from slow simmering for depth and creaminess, which appeared lacking here. 4/10 Breads Tandoori Roti & Pudina Paratha: Both were well made. The pudina paratha used dried spearmint, which gives a slightly different flavor than traditional mint — not unpleasant, but unconventional. 7/10 Dessert Complimentary Pista Kulfi: Pleasant, well portioned, and enjoyable. 7/10 Final Verdict Tamarind Tribeca excels in ambience and service, and the dining room experience feels premium. However, during this visit the kitchen performance was inconsistent, with several dishes lacking seasoning, depth, or proper doneness — particularly concerning for core North Indian menu items. A good choice for ambience and drinks, but based on this experience, the food did not match the setting or expectations. Overall: 3/10 (service and ambience strong; kitchen execution needs improvement). (3 stars)

Stopped in for lunch in January 2026. It was a cold day so some Indian spice and curry was the perfect for lunch. It was also restaurant week so the lunch menu was nicely put together in 3 courses which was jus perfect. The place is upscale Indian with an expansive bar area. The sitting are is also nicely put together. The decor was appropriate and the ambiance balanced. The wait staff was good and courteous and served well. They were attentive. The dining options are expansive and changes frequently. I was very happy with my choices. Will definitely revisit here when in the area. It is comparatively expensive for Indian cuisine, but this is upscale so not unexpected. Will revisit again. (5 stars)

One of the best fine dining Indian cuisine that I had in my life. Everything was cooked to perfection! We ordered the lunch menu which was a 3 course meal with tomato soup, rice, chicken and a veggie side. It was served very well and the seasoning was perfect! We also ordered venison on the side which is an exotic game meat dish, but it was cooked well enough to get rid of the gamey taste. The service was also swift and detailed. I would recommend everyone to try this place out if you have plans for fine dining in Manhattan. (5 stars)

MLK lunch. Nice special allowing variety. We tried most in Executive Lunch menu (both appetizer, all entree except lamb both dessert) plus chicken and extra nan. Was with Indian food novice so good treat. Starter nice. Shrimp (Tawa Jhinga) appetizer very good. For entree, chicken fish very easy picking. Rice and vegetables add flavors. Smoked mashed eggplant (Baingan Bharta) also nice. Fish and chicken breast tasty, easy for those whose prefererence less spicy. Dessert both not so sweet, subtle. Glass enclosed open kitchen to see tandoori at work. High ceiling, good bench tables, bar as well spacious. Good bright decor with silhouette curtains. Service excellent. Moving table to make way. Initial metal plate then clean bright china plates. Water filled frequently. Checking up making sure. Also language very polite. Overall pleasant dining experience. Will recommend others. (5 stars)

bio_text: Tanoreen is a celebrated Middle Eastern restaurant located in Brooklyn, known for its warm, home-style dining experience that invites guests to share in the flavors of Palestinian cuisine. Founded by Chef Rawia Bishara, the restaurant embodies a commitment to culinary heritage while embracing new influences, creating a vibrant atmosphere reminiscent of family gatherings. With a focus on hospitality and community, Tanoreen offers a menu that evolves with the seasons, showcasing a blend of traditional and contemporary dishes. Tanoreen specializes in Palestinian and Middle Eastern cuisine, emphasizing home-style dishes meant for sharing. The menu features a variety of mezze, stews, and desserts, all crafted with a blend of classical techniques and multicultural influences. Tanoreen opened in 1998 as a ten-table storefront in Brooklyn, founded by Chef Rawia Bishara. The restaurant has since expanded and taken on Jumana Bishara as a partner, and has published two cookbooks, celebrating an intergenerational legacy of culinary passion.

review_snippets: This place never disappoints. I’ve been here with my friends before, and this time I came with my husband. I tried to bring him for Valentine’s Day, but it was already fully booked, so I definitely recommend making a reservation, especially for important dates. We went during the week, and my husband absolutely loved it.🤗 The food was delicious. I always recommend starting with the eggplant Napolitano appetizer and the mini shawarmas. The Figtini cocktail🍸 and the Harissa 🥥dessert were amazing 😋 The place feels very warm and cozy, with soft Arabic music playing in the background. The service from everyone was exceptional. I 100% recommend it🔥👌🏻 Sent from my iPhone (5 stars)

Early 6pm dinner and only 3 other tables occupied. Inattentive, but friendly staff, left quite an impression. It was the bartender that noticed us waiting and signaled the staff. Mezcal was great and Shepard beer was good too. Warm Nusakhan was tasty. Baked kibbie was simple. Chicken curry decent giant dish. Flavors were 3 out of 5. Will we return? No unfortunately. Maybe we'll try their sister location. (3 stars)

A wonderful mediterranean restaurant offering family style set meals including a variety of mezzes and your protein of choice. Go with a group to sample different entrees. The atmosphere is relaxed, quiet and conducive to conversation. (5 stars)

Most resturant reviews are about the food, service, and atmosphere, and rightfully so. But occassionally there is a restaurant that goes above and beyond. They realize the value of their relationship to the neighborhood and the community. Tanoreen is such a resturant. The food, service, and atmosphere are all exceptional. We do not live in NY but were visiting our kids that do. I was treating dinner for 7 of us. I did not realize that there is an automatic gratuity for that party size. I tipped $70 on top of the included $68 gratuity and did not realize it until the day after. When I called I was told the credit card billing was already submitted. They offered to refund the $70 in cash. However we were leaving and couldn't get back to the restaurant. They held the money in an envelope for my son to pick up a week later. Now that is customer service! Thank you! (5 stars)

bio_text: Taqueria El Chato, located in Brooklyn's Greenpoint neighborhood, is a culinary gem that has quickly become a favorite among taco enthusiasts. With a commitment to authentic Mexican flavors, the taqueria offers a vibrant atmosphere where diners can enjoy generously portioned tacos crafted from carefully sourced ingredients. The owner, hailing from Guanajuato, ensures that each dish bursts with rich, traditional tastes, making it a must-visit destination for anyone craving an unforgettable taco experience in New York City. Taqueria El Chato specializes in authentic Mexican cuisine, focusing on tacos made with fresh, in-house tortillas crafted from nixtamalized Masienda corn. The menu features a diverse selection of fillings, including suadero brisket, al pastor, and chorizo, complemented by a vibrant self-serve salsa bar that enhances each dish with bold flavors. The owner hails from Guanajuato, ensuring a rich connection to traditional taco crafting.

review_snippets: Don’t let this small taco spot fool you…they don’t mess with the flavor! It was delicious! I’m creature of habit and I tend to go to the same taco spot all the time but I decided to venture out. It did not disappoint! It’s a small space so please don’t expect to sit down and dine but if you’re on a solo date you might get lucky and find a spot on their counter. (5 stars)

Amazing experience. All the tacos were PACKED with flavor and delicious taste. Easy to order on a self order screen to go back up and order as many as you want. Tacos came out fast, delicious picos to add by the front door, not cheap with the meat. I will be back! (5 stars)

These tacos in NYC are unreal. If they were in Mexico, I’d honestly eat them every day. The lengua taco was spectacular — tender, flavorful, and perfectly cooked. Easily some of the best tacos I’ve had outside Mexico. (5 stars)

Been wanting to try el Chato for a couple months and finally popped in. In general, I love Al pastor and so I got it in quesadilla form and it was excellent. I always love the lil’ crispy pieces that are charred and this had plenty of them! I also tried the asada, suadero, & lengua and i enjoyed them in that order. With a commitment to authentic Mexican flavors, the taqueria offers a vibrant atmosphere where diners can enjoy generously portioned tacos crafted from carefully sourced ingredients. The owner, hailing from Guanajuato, ensures that each dish bursts with rich, traditional tastes, making it a must-visit destination for anyone craving an unforgettable taco experience in New York City. bio_text: Tatiana, located in New York City, is an Afro-Caribbean restaurant that serves as a heartfelt tribute to the diverse culinary landscape of the city and the cherished memories of Chef Kwame Onwuachi's childhood. The restaurant embodies a vibrant atmosphere where flavors, aromas, and textures come together, reflecting the rich heritage and culture of the Bronx and beyond. With a commitment to community and philanthropy, Tatiana aims to nourish not only the palate but also the spirit of the neighborhood. Tatiana focuses on Afro-Caribbean cuisine, blending a variety of global flavors inspired by Chef Kwame Onwuachi's upbringing. The menu is a tapestry of dishes that celebrate the culinary traditions of New York City, served with care and love. Signature techniques include the use of traditional cooking methods and locally sourced ingredients. Tatiana is inspired by Chef Kwame Onwuachi's sister, Tatiana, who played a significant role in his early culinary experiences. The restaurant reflects his upbringing in the Bronx and is a tribute to the neighborhoods that shaped his culinary journey.
menu_items: Fluke Crudo - Pickled Sungold Tomato, Carrot Nage, Escovitch
Crispy Okra - Wildflower Honey, Mustard Spice, Cucumber Yogurt
Black Bean Hummus - Berbere Spiced Lamb, Sweet Pickled Sultana, M’semen
Curried Goat Patties - Green Seasoning Aioli, Mango Chutney
Green Caesar - Baby Gem Lettuce, Fried Anchovy, Pickled Corn
Crab & Oxtail Patties - Calypso Aioli, Pimento, Peking Jus
review_snippets: I recently dined at Tatiana by Kwame Onwuachi, the celebrated restaurant by Chef Kwame Onwuachi, and overall it was a memorable culinary experience with several standout dishes that showcased bold flavors and creativity. I began with the Honeynut Piri Piri Salad, which was vibrant and beautifully balanced. The sweetness of the honeynut squash paired nicely with the smoky heat of the piri piri, creating a refreshing yet flavorful start to the meal. The Black Bean Hummus was a unique and satisfying take on the classic dish—smooth, rich, and full of depth. One of the highlights of the evening was the Crab & Oxtail Patties. The combination of delicate crab and deeply flavorful oxtail inside a perfectly flaky pastry was indulgent and inventive. The BBQ Collard Greens were another standout, delivering smoky, soulful flavors while still feeling refined and elevated. Mom Duke’s Shrimp was packed with flavor and personality, cooked perfectly and coated in a sauce that balanced spice and richness. The Short Rib Pastrami Suya was equally impressive—tender short rib with bold suya seasoning and a subtle nod to New York pastrami that made the dish both exciting and satisfying. I also ordered the Nut Cracker cocktail, which unfortunately was not to my liking. I had hoped the server might check in to see if I was enjoying the drink, but that never happened, which was disappointing. Additionally, throughout the meal I had to request clean plates and utensils after each course, something I would typically expect to be handled proactively in a restaurant of this caliber. Despite these service issues, the food itself was creative, flavorful, and clearly crafted with care. Chef Kwame Onwuachi’s ability to blend cultural influences and tell a story through his dishes is evident in every plate. With a bit more attentiveness in service, the overall experience could easily match the excellence of the cuisine. (5 stars)

We ordered the suya pastrami, oxtail crab appetizer, and brownie. Starting with the positives — the food had some highlights, but overall the experience didn’t fully match the price point. The oxtail crab appetizer was good, but nothing particularly memorable. It came with four pieces and tasted similar to a samosa — enjoyable, just not special. The Wagyu short rib suya pastrami ($120) was clearly the star of the menu conceptually. The flavors worked better when everything was eaten together, but separately the components didn’t shine. The bread was coconut-based but didn’t taste like coconut, the meat was a bit too salty and spicy, and the cabbage pickle felt bland and added little balance. For the price, we expected a bit more refinement. The brownie dessert was actually the best part of the meal — rich, delicious, and absolutely worth ordering. Service, decor, and plating unfortunately didn’t feel aligned with the premium pricing. The space and presentation weren’t as impressive as expected, and the service felt a bit lacking. Overall, some good flavors, but not quite the elevated experience the prices suggest.Now i see why this place is Michelin Guide not Starred. (3 stars)

One of the hardest reservations to land in NYC, I finally had the pleasure of experiencing Tatiana recently for my girlfriends birthday celebration. We have both been following Chef Kwame for some time. We were excited to finally see what it was all about. The dinner overall was fantastic! Our server was attentive thru the night. The energy of the space is lively. The playlist was bumping, but the music never drowned out the conversation we were having. If you are looking for a serene evening this is not the space for that. We ended up getting a number of staples. From the Curry goat patty, to the crab rangoon, to the fried fish dish and finally ending with a childhood staple from my local bodega growing up, their play on a cosmic brownie and powdered "donuts". It was an awesome ending to the meal. Cocktails were varied and definitely booze forward. Well worth the overall experience. It is a bit pricey but the food combined with the service made it worth it. Well done 👏🏼 (4 stars)

A few weeks ago I walked in and was able to sit at the bar after a brief wait on a Saturday night. While I waited, the staff at the front were very kind, offered us drinks, and kept us updated as it was a full house. I ended up making a friend while waiting and we both sat at the bar to take it all in. I had the Black Bean Hummus with lettuce cups which was very, very yummy. I am eating plant based these days. So, my server was able to chat with the chefs to help me understand what I could eat on the menu. Once they showed me what was possible, I was able to pick from a few items. My friend had 2-3 small plates and got full after the first one. She endured, we had drinks, and it was a wonderful time! It was an unexpectedly fun night and when I come back to the area, I'd definitely return! The atmosphere was incredible!! (5 stars)

bio_text: Taverna Kyclades, located in Astoria, Queens, is celebrated as one of New York City's premier Greek dining establishments. The restaurant offers a vibrant atmosphere characterized by its dedication to authentic Greek cuisine, efficient service, and a warm, welcoming environment. With a decor that features elements of Greek culture, including a striking taxidermy swordfish, Taverna Kyclades provides a unique dining experience that reflects the rich culinary heritage of Greece. Taverna Kyclades specializes in traditional Greek cuisine, with a particular emphasis on fresh seafood. The menu features classic dishes made from original Greek recipes, showcasing the use of high-quality ingredients. Signature offerings include fish soup and moussaka, presented in a casual dining format.
menu_items: KIDONIA GEMISTA/PSITA - Stuffed Clams w.Crabmeat/ or Grilled
OKTAPODI - Grilled Octopus
ATHERINA - Spearings
LOUKANIKO PSITO - Grilled Sausage
KALAMARI - Fried Calamari
KYCLADES VEGGIE CHIPS - Crispy Eggplant & Zucchini Chips w. Tzatziki Dip
review_snippets: Such a delicious meal!!!! The oysters were so fresh; all of their seafood is super fresh. The grilled octopus was cooked perfectly it was soft with a slightly crispy outside from being char grilled. It had a great char flavor paired with the olive oil and vinegar was perfect. The pork souvlaki was my favorite of the night. The pork was juicy and had great flavor. I really like their tzatziki it’s very fresh with lots of cucumber. The lamb chops were also pretty good. I don’t usually like lamb because it’s gamey but this wasn’t and it was also cooked perfectly. They also gave delicious bread with a mashed olive dip at the start and a custard baklava type dessert for free! 8.5/10 (5 stars)

This is the place to get seafood. Very busy, but do t let that discourage you because at the end you'll be rewarded with some real, real fresh and delicious seafood. The octopus is simply fenomenal, the special combo seafood for two is amazing and the stuff filet of sole very tasty. All this complemented with a glass of sangria. Can't beat it. If you don't have reservation get ready to wait for at least 45 minutes, but it will be worth it. (5 stars)

This elegant, authentic greek seafood restaurant constantly has a 45 minute wait on Friday and Satueday nights. The meal is worth it, crispy olive bread with tapenade in olive oil, greek salads, a dozen varieties of fish including shark and swordfish as well as beef, chicken and lamb. The seafood pasta and the salmon were exceptional. Greek sides such as chard and lemon potatos follow the large entree portions. Excellent wine selection. Complementary house dessert with every meal. A staple of Ditmars, Tavern Kyclades never disappoints. (5 stars)

We visited Taverna Kyclades and had a wonderful experience. The service was impeccable—every staff member, even those who weren’t our primary server, made sure we had everything we needed. For appetizers, we enjoyed crab cakes with fried zucchini. For dinner, my husband had a white fish stuffed with crab meat, while I had a pasta dish featuring five types of seafood: octopus, mussels, clams, scallops, and shrimp. Every bite was full of flavor, and the portions were incredibly generous—we had to take half of our food home and enjoyed it for a couple more days! Overall, the combination of excellent service, delicious food, and large portions made this a truly delightful dining experience. (5 stars)

bio_text: Tempura Matsui offers a refined dining experience centered around the art of tempura, a culinary tradition that dates back to the mid-16th century. The restaurant embodies a commitment to quality, utilizing the finest ingredients and a meticulously crafted batter that is light and delicate, allowing the natural flavors of the ingredients to shine. Guests can expect an elegant atmosphere that reflects the rich history of tempura while enjoying a modern interpretation of this classic dish. Tempura Matsui specializes in traditional Japanese tempura, focusing on the use of high-quality ingredients and a signature batter technique known as 'The Matsui Way.' The menu features a selection of seasonal and unique ingredients, prepared to highlight their natural flavors. The restaurant is named in honor of its grand chef, Mr. Matsui, who has dedicated himself to perfecting the art of tempura.
menu_items: Sakizuke - Assortment of seasonal starter
Sashimi - Seasonal selection of fresh sashimi
Lobster - Whole lobster tempura
Tencha - Tendon (tempura over rice) with dashi
Shrimp - The star ingredient for tempura. Prepared and to be enjoyed every inch of it.
Matsutake - The king of autumn flavors.
review_snippets: Not sure why I haven’t reviewed this spot before bc I’ve been about 6 times over the past 10 years, but this is hands down one of the best restaurants in NYC. TM offers an elevated take on tempura and literally every bite is incredible. I’ve never seen this level of dedication to tempura outside of Japan. Tempura at most spots is a bit of an afterthought. Not here! Each bite comes with a special salt or flavoring that heightens the experience. And the additions like Japanese custard with shrimp or rice with green tea to the tasting menu are pretty hard to beat. It skews towards seafood and veggies. Service is very precise but understated. It’s definitely pricey but worth every cent. There are plenty of Japanese restaurants or Japanese inspired places but Tempura Matsui is pretty unmatched. (5 stars)

Tempura Matsui – A True Once-in-a-Lifetime Dining Experience Tempura Matsui was a fantastic and truly unforgettable dining experience. If you’re planning to visit, please come hungry and with an open mind—you will be rewarded in every way. Despite what many online videos suggest about small portions, our experience was quite the opposite. We were served about 14 dishes throughout the evening, and every single one was excellent. The service was absolutely top-notch from start to finish. The chefs preparing your food are very friendly and engaging, which adds a personal and welcoming touch to the entire experience. You can really feel the care, pride, and precision that goes into every dish. The menu encourages you to be adventurous, featuring ingredients like conch that some people might not initially find appetizing. However, everything—from the fried tempura dishes to the delicate egg custard soup—was prepared to perfection. Each course was beautifully presented and full of flavor. While the experience is definitely on the pricey side, believe me when I say it is worth every penny. You will not regret it. This is truly a one-in-a-lifetime dining experience and one that I would highly recommend to anyone looking for something exceptional. (5 stars)

Superb from start to finish. It’s hard to explain how tempura can be so elevated, but it is. There are also other dishes I haven’t had before and all were excellent. The foie gras chawanmushi and the persimmon with shrimp were standouts. The service was precise yet welcoming and warm. It is also a lot of food in total, so expect to feel full by the end! Small and intimate setting, perfect for a dinner with a date or a good friend. (5 stars)

An experience of absolute refinement, quality and respect. A gorgeous, spare room where we had seats at the bar to see the preparation of our lunch. Every course was beautifully presented with detailed instructions on how to eat it optimally. The respect for the ingredients, the attention to detail, the care for us…all of it was top notch. From the pumpkin, hen of the woods mushrooms, shrimp heads and smelt that had arrived from Japan just prior to service, the ingredients were of the best quality and expertly prepared. No wonder they have maintained their star for many years. An experience not to be missed. (5 stars)

bio_text: Tha Phraya is a vibrant culinary destination that celebrates the rich flavors and memories of Thai cuisine. With a focus on high-quality ingredients and authentic family recipes, the restaurant offers a dining experience that is both visually appealing and deeply rooted in tradition. Guests can expect a warm atmosphere that invites them to explore the diverse tastes of Thailand, making it a must-visit for food lovers. Tha Phraya specializes in traditional Thai cuisine, emphasizing the use of fresh, high-quality ingredients. The menu features a variety of dishes that highlight the complex flavors of Thai cooking, including sweet, salty, sour, and spicy elements. Signature dishes like 'Miang-kum' showcase the restaurant's commitment to authentic flavors and presentation. Tha Phraya was founded by a group of Thai restaurateurs and chefs who share a passion for the culinary heritage of Thailand.
menu_items: Sai Ua Spring Rolls - Crispy spring rolls stuffed with pork sausage & Thai herbs - $18
Miang-Kham - One-bite wraps in fragrant betel leaves with lime, ginger, chili, peanut, roasted coconut flakes, dried shrimp, & shallot with caramelized sauce - $18
Peek Gai Ta-Krai - Lemongrass marinated fried chicken wings served with nam jim jeaw sauce - $17
Curry Puffs - Crispy golden brown puffs stuffed with minced chicken, onion & curried potatoes served with cucumbers relish - $17
Ka-Nom Jeeb - Savory rice crepe wrapped sweet radish, red onion, peanut - $15
Pak Mor - Savory rice crepe wrapped sweet radish, red onion, peanut - $16
review_snippets: This place is so homey. As a Thai who hasn't been back home for years, the dishes here really hit the spot. Their crab curry is very aromatic and rich in flavor (with a nice kick too). The softshell crab was so divine and the pork was delicious. We would definitely recommend! (5 stars)

I had a great dining experience at Tha Phraya! The restaurant offers some of the best Thai flavors I’ve had in New York, and the dishes were fresh, well-seasoned, and beautifully presented. My favorites were the Spicy Crab Mango Salad, the Roast Duck Red Curry, and their signature Cha No.5—each one stood out in flavor and balance. The seafood platter and lava crab fried rice were generous in portion and perfect for sharing. The space feels cozy and welcoming, and the service was friendly throughout our meal. Definitely a spot worth visiting if you’re looking for authentic Thai food on the Upper East Side. (5 stars)

Great ambiance and amazing staff was super welcoming and attentive. I had the Sai Ua Spring Rolls and the Ka-Prow Stewed Beef, and both were delicious. The garlic chili sauce had the perfect amount of spice. I really wanted to try the Miang-Kham, but it wasn’t available. I’ll definitely be back! (5 stars)

Really loved my dinner at Tha Phraya! NYC has a ton of Thai restaurants, but this one definitely stands out. The menu has a variety of distinct dishes, the space is cozy, and the staff was super attentive. Everything we tried was delicious! We shared the Thai Corn Salad (super fresh), the Crab Fried Rice Lava (really good, though the rice was a bit dry), and the Goong Karee with shrimp, which ended up being my favorite dish of the night. The sauce was so good, I kept going back for more. Would love to come back to try one of their winter specials and the Basque cheesecake👏 (5 stars)
search_text: Tha Phraya Tha Phraya is a vibrant culinary destination that celebrates the rich flavors and memories of Thai cuisine. With a focus on high-quality ingredients and authentic family recipes, the restaurant offers a dining experience that is both visually appealing and deeply rooted in tradition. Guests can expect a warm atmosphere that invites them to explore the diverse tastes of Thailand, making it a must-visit for food lovers. Tha Phraya specializes in traditional Thai cuisine, emphasizing the use of fresh, high-quality ingredients. The menu features a variety of dishes that highlight the complex flavors of Thai cooking, including sweet, salty, sour, and spicy elements. Signature dishes like 'Miang-kum' showcase the restaurant's commitment to authentic flavors and presentation. Tha Phraya was founded by a group of Thai restaurateurs and chefs who share a passion for the culinary heritage of Thailand. The restaurant specializes in authentic Thai cuisine, focusing on fresh ingredients and bold flavors. The menu features a variety of dishes that highlight traditional recipes with a modern twist, ensuring a memorable dining experience.

review_snippets: The funny thing about this place is I didn’t know anything about it until recently. My coworker. I work at food for workspace would constantly talk about how this is her favorite place and constantly talk about. The funny thing is that I booked a reservation here with my partner and then the next night my coworker took us all to Thai Diner so I had this place two times in a row completely different experiences The food here is amazing. The portions are large. It’s authentic the papaya salad alone makes you wanna come back for so much more the way it’s made is perfect and I’m literally salivating as I talk about it. I haven’t had a dish here I haven’t liked we also had a loaded disco fries, which is extremely crispy and tasty. They were even delivered to work one day and got cold and I still ate them which I don’t recommend in that way they’re delicious fresh All the noodle dishes were good but there’s also a big sundae dessert thing that is highly recommended. Oh my God it blew me away Huge beautiful and exciting. See the pictures. The ambience alone is stunning. It’s very warm. I got a great feel inside and out. The look is so cool like a New York City diner mixed with a Thai restaurant, stunning authentically, beautiful all the way through they thought of everything Go here or go often the staff is amazing. I really don’t have anything bad to save this place. It’s one of my top restaurants in 2025. (5 stars)

The service was great and the food was delicious. Oysters were fresh and loved the green sauce, the duck wonton soup had really great flavor and wonton filling was juicy and flavorful, the crab fried rice had nice large pieces of crab and came with the delicious green seafood sauce. The cocktails were strong. The coconut sundae was big and good to share the candied peanuts added a nice crunch and caramel flavor whipped cream was creamy and ice cream delicious. I understand the hype and its worth a try. (4 stars)

This was an unexpected surprise and I enjoyed every minute of it! I was in the area and happened to search for a breakfast spot, and this popped up as a nearby recommendation. I was intrigued because I have never seen breakfast at a Thai restaurant. What’s sit out most was the Elephant Ear French toast. The wait was quick just 20 minutes and we were seated for a party of two. The service was just as quick despite it being a busy and packed restaurant. I’m so happy I ordered the French toast. It was so unique and delicious. It has the flavors of a chai tea wrapped up in a delicious elephant ear French toast. Highly recommended. I will be back soon for more! (5 stars)

drunken dumplings 4/5 - dipping sauce was to die for, so flavorful and had a spicy kick to it! phat thai w/chicken 5/5 - cant go wrong with a classic, right amount of tamarind sauce so the noodles weren’t dry at all (though they could have given us half a lime not barely 1/4 of it) panang neuh 5/5 - braised beef was soooo tender, curry was so yummy though my friend found it a bit salty but would def recommend and get again, a must have!! cheesesteak phat bai horapha w/fries 2/5 - probably wouldnt order this again… was thrilled at first to make it before the cut off time to order this but (saying this as a big lover of cheese) the one they used made this overly salty and hard to eat… had about 1-2 bites before i set it to the side, removed the contents and ended up pairing it with the white rice from the panang neuh to dilute the saltiness of it. loved the fries though, were very crispy! aside from the food, cant say too much about the atmosphere from INSIDE the actual diner, I understand adding a secondary attachment to the business to being able to serve more customers but it was 18 degrees outside when we went. We got seated on the outside attachment near the windows and had to keep our coats on with how much draft air was coming in, noted about 3 or so space heaters on the roof but could barely feel them working at all especially when you aren’t seated under one. Also note the lack of space between each table and the servers having to wait at the end of the row because there was only enough room for people to leave in a single file line (all while having to make sure that none of their garments aren’t accidentally ending up in your food as they’re leaving or arriving). This caused them to barely notice when we had to set plates to the side and stack them so we had more room on our table, (also note again if you are seated at a table for 2 you have to play tetris to have multiple plates fit on such a small table). Or when we were ready for the check (couldnt flag someone down to come/took a while for them to finally ring us up). Would definitely come again to try their other dishes but maybe during the warmer months or if they’re able to seat us inside next time/come during a slower period. :) (4 stars)

bio_text: The Commerce Inn is an early American tavern and cookery located in the heart of the West Village, New York City. With a focus on craftsmanship and heirloom recipes, the restaurant offers a warm and inviting atmosphere that celebrates seasonal cooking and material honesty. The interior design pays homage to the architecture of the early 1900s, creating a space that feels both historic and welcoming, perfect for enjoying straightforward fare and expertly crafted cocktails. The Commerce Inn specializes in American cookery, featuring a menu inspired by heritage recipes. Dishes include piquant pickled oysters, comforting rarebit, and fortifying pot pies, all prepared simply and served casually. The restaurant also offers a selection of deftly crafted cocktails and a curated wine list highlighting small American producers. The Commerce Inn has been welcoming guests for almost a century and is brought to life by esteemed New York chefs Rita Sodi and Jody Williams.

review_snippets: We came for their famous pancakes, and they didn’t disappoint. The place is very cozy and the staff is friendly. We walked in on a Saturday morning without a reservation and were seated after about 30 minutes. We left our phone number on the waiting list and received a message as soon as our table was ready, which was very convenient. (5 stars)

Had to come try their famous pancakes and I can confirm they are worth it! Very fluffy and adding the extra berries really makes it. Their orange juice was the best I’ve had. Their other dishes are also very well executed. Definitely try this place if you get the chance. Very cozy during the winter. It’s much nicer during the week when they’re less busy. We just walked in with no reservation and were seated right away! (5 stars)

Beautiful experience, very knowledgeable and kind staff. We had stopped by for brunch and got their steak & potatoes with their beautiful butter pancakes 🥞. It was so fluffy, it melts in your mouth, perfection. The steak was cooked beautifully and seasoned to perfection. I’m looking forward to joining them for their dinner service. (5 stars)

Very warm and cozy space; perfect for the fall and winter. We got the specials, clam chowder, rabbit stew, and their take of the Sunday roast. The rabbit stew was probably the best out of the specials; nice flaky pastry with a flavorful and filling stew. The carrots and kale were good side dishes. We also tried the spoon bread, mainly bc we were intrigued. It’s a generous portion, and the taste/ texture is similar to a cornbread or cornmeal. The apple tart was good, but it was more pastry dough than apple. (4 stars)

bio_text: The Dining Room at The Guesthouse offers a sophisticated and inviting atmosphere, perfect for both casual dining and special occasions. With a focus on providing an exceptional dining experience, the restaurant features a beautifully designed space that complements its upscale menu and attentive service. The Dining Room specializes in a diverse menu that includes breakfast and weekend brunch options served all day. The culinary focus is on high-quality ingredients and seasonal flavors, ensuring a fresh and delightful dining experience.

review_snippets: I had a really great experience here. The space is beautiful and calm, with a warm, elegant vibe that instantly makes you slow down and enjoy the moment. It feels upscale but not intimidating, which I appreciated a lot. The food was solid across the board. The steak was cooked perfectly, juicy with a nice char and simple seasoning that let the quality of the meat shine. The Caesar salad was fresh and crisp with generous parmesan and crunchy croutons. The oysters were clean and briny, super fresh, and the shrimp cocktail was chilled perfectly with a classic, flavorful sauce. Service was attentive without hovering. Everything came out at a relaxed pace, which matched the atmosphere really well. This is the kind of place that works great for a date night, a quiet dinner with friends, or even a special occasion when you want something classy but comfortable. Overall, I would definitely come back. Great food, beautiful setting, and a very polished but welcoming experience. (5 stars)

The Dining Room at RH Guesthouse New York 🏙️ offers a pleasant and elegant environment, making it suitable for family dinners and social gatherings 🥂. However, the dining space can feel somewhat noisy, which may detract from privacy — for a quieter experience, consider the downstairs or upstairs areas. In terms of food, I found the overall offerings to be solid: the Grilled Avocado with Caviar 🥑🐟 presents a creative and well‑balanced starter, pairing creamy avocado with briny fish roe; the Roasted Lamb Chops 🍖 are tender, flavorful, and generously portioned — highly recommended; and the Whole Branzino 🐟 is fresh and light without being overly oily. The pacing of the meal was well‑managed and dishes arrived promptly. The service staff were friendly and professional, which added to an enjoyable dining experience. Overall, this restaurant delivers a refined atmosphere, reliable dishes, and attentive service — a great pick for relaxed family or group dining. (4 stars)

Such a pretty restaurant but it was freezing which is surprising since it is just newly built. I guess modern ginormous windows can still leak in a lot of cold air. The chilly (but pretty) marble tables don’t help for insulation. Our waitress was a bit surly and seemed to do her best to try to avoid understanding what we were asking for. She never warned us that the crispy artichoke is more of a sharing dish and less of an individual starter. The champagne bar below the main restaurant looked stunning but again it was like arctic. If you go, we recommend taking plenty of layers if it’s winter, share your starters and ask lots of questions about the dishes on the menu as not everything is as described. I prefer the RH Rooftop. Better value for money and more healthy. (3 stars)

Server was good. Brunch service can be chaotic but attention to detail is critical. Don’t forget sugar with coffee for exemple. Also service stations are so close to table. Service must be very mindful guests hear everything. Also although beverage menu is large and variated still was surprised that there is no bar to order a different cocktail. Food was at a very good level. (4 stars)

review_snippets: Sublime. We ordered every dish on the menu except the clams and it was consistently excellent across very single dish - I don’t remember the last time I had a meal like that, because most restaurants have clear stars in their menus and then other dishes are just ok, but here everything was a banger. Favorites - scallop and leek custard, egg and blue crab, wagyu crostini, and the panna cotta (I don’t even like panna cotta and yet this was one of the best desserts I’ve ever had). Can’t wait to come back for dinner or in another season! (5 stars)

Bravo. I’ve determined that this would officially be my last meal. Everything was perfect. The restaurant itself is super cosy. The service was excellent, relaxed. The food was interesting and flavourful. We tried a number of fun wines that paired well our food. My only complaint is how hard it was to get a reservation 😆 (5 stars)

An excellent operation with a chill vibe and a creative menu, taking amazing meals up a notch in unique ways. The Tartare Crostini is well formed and very flavorful, the salad’s cream and seasonings took some mixing up to get used to but that was good. Brown butter Crab with bread was great, and my two favorite starters the Grilled Octopus and the Seafood Rice. The octopus had perfect char and a sweet delicious taste paired great with the egg. The Seafood Rice was a great blend of fish stocked rice and cold fish as a topping. Then the Pork Collar, I loved this it’s a perfect preparation. Great portion with a beautiful seasoned top layer and a wonderful fatty center. We didn’t care much for the side, which for a dish this pricey you’d like solid side as a base but this gets a pass. Lastly to finish off the Panna Cotta was straight up great, safest dessert option. (5 stars)

Yes, it is hard to get in. But once you are in, good lord it is great. First off, you are made to feel like you are a regular at a neighborhood eatery. Then every course is perfect and beautiful. The suggested wines were outstanding and unique. The bartender, Sam, obviously enjoyed talking to me about the pairings even though I was a stranger. Sure didn't feel like one! (5 stars)
search_text: The Four Horsemen Sublime. We ordered every dish on the menu except the clams and it was consistently excellent across very single dish - I don’t remember the last time I had a meal like that, because most restaurants have clear stars in their menus and then other dishes are just ok, but here everything was a banger. Favorites - scallop and leek custard, egg and blue crab, wagyu crostini, and the panna cotta (I don’t even like panna cotta and yet this was one of the best desserts I’ve ever had). Can’t wait to come back for dinner or in another season! (5 stars) Bravo. I’ve determined that this would officially be my last meal. Everything was perfect. The restaurant itself is super cosy. The service was excellent, relaxed. The food was interesting and flavourful. We tried a number of fun wines that paired well our food. My only complaint is how hard it was to get a reservation 😆 (5 stars) An excellent operation with a chill vibe and a creative menu, taking amazing meals up a notch in unique ways. The Tartare Crostini is well formed and very flavorful, the salad’s cream and seasonings took some mixing up to get used to but that was good. Brown butter Crab with bread was great, and my two favorite starters the Grilled Octopus and the Seafood Rice. The octopus had perfect char and a sweet delicious taste paired great with the egg. The Seafood Rice was a great blend of fish stocked rice and cold fish as a topping. Then the Pork Collar, I loved this it’s a perfect preparation. Great portion with a beautiful seasoned top layer and a wonderful fatty center. We didn’t care much for the side, which for a dish this pricey you’d like solid side as a base but this gets a pass. bio_text: The Grill is a sophisticated dining establishment located in Manhattan's iconic Seagram Building, renowned for its midcentury elegance and exceptional service. As the successor to the legendary Four Seasons restaurant, it offers a unique blend of classic American chophouse cuisine and a luxurious atmosphere, making it a premier destination for both locals and visitors. Guests are treated to a meticulously curated dining experience, complete with a stunning wine and spirits collection and a commitment to impeccable service. The Grill specializes in American chophouse cuisine, featuring expertly prepared dishes that highlight the tradition of prime cuts of meat. The menu includes a signature Prime Rib, which is carved tableside, enhancing the dining experience with a touch of theatricality. The restaurant emphasizes high-quality ingredients and classic cooking techniques. The Grill is housed within the only landmarked dining rooms in the United States and is celebrated as the successor to the famed Four Seasons restaurant.

review_snippets: The Grill was incredible. I was a bit worried when picking this place for an anniversary dinner because of some of the more recent reviews. However, once I entered the restaurant I knew those reviewers didn’t know what they were talking about. Every course was incredible and unique. The steak was perfectly cooked and being the star of the show. Lastly, desert was a stand out with hand picked strawberries from Malagas Spain. A memorable evening to say the least! (5 stars)

This is a place to go to impress anyone that general do not to fancy restaurants. I would say the food is good but not astounding. Probably not worth the price. There's many better choices for the price. We did the Christmas set menu. To be honest, I kind of regret the choice. It would have been better to just order from the regular menu. The Christmas menu is good but you can see they kind of went the cheap choice. A good example is instead of Spanish ham they went with American. YKYK. (5 stars)

⭐️🌟✨💫I had such a wonderful experience at The Grill, and a huge part of that was thanks to our waitress, Anne. She was the perfect balance of professional and personable — attentive without being intrusive, warm without being over the top. She knew the menu inside and out, gave great recommendations, and made sure everything arrived exactly as we ordered. What really stood out was her genuine attitude; she made us feel welcome and taken care of the entire time. It’s rare to find service that feels both polished and authentic, but Anne absolutely delivered. I’ll definitely be back, and I’ll be hoping she’s working when I do! (5 stars)

We went here last night for dinner after the show, and absolutely loved it. They have later reservations available, which was perfect for us. We had pasta with white truffles (they’re in season now) — so delicious. The oysters were super fresh, the steak was amazing, and for dessert we tried the lemon cake and another one that reminded me of a fancy version of a Snickers bar — both were incredible. Everything was just perfect — the food, the service, the atmosphere. We’ll definitely be back! (5 stars)

bio_text: The Lambs Club is a sophisticated American restaurant located in the heart of New York City, within The Chatwal Hotel. It offers a vibrant atmosphere that combines elegance with a playful twist on classic American cuisine, making it an ideal destination for both casual diners and those seeking a refined dining experience. The culinary focus at The Lambs Club is on elevated American classics, creatively interpreted through a New York lens. The menu features a variety of dishes that highlight seasonal ingredients and innovative techniques, ensuring a memorable dining experience. Chef Jack Logue leads the kitchen, bringing his expertise and vision to the restaurant.

review_snippets: Seriously good…the perfect Valentine’s pre-fixe dinner. A mark of an excellent restaurant is not just great food but great cocktails, dessert, and coffee- all of which were exquisite. The service was very attentive. Each dish was intentional. We loved it. Thank you (5 stars)

My wife and I had an absolutely wonderful breakfast at The Lambs Club. From start to finish, the experience was flawless. The service was top notch — the staff were warm, attentive, and made sure everything was perfect without ever being intrusive. The food was incredibly fresh, beautifully presented, and full of flavor. The coffee was strong and perfectly brewed, just the way a morning should start. The atmosphere truly sets The Lambs Club apart — from the elegant furniture to the historic photos on the walls, every detail exudes character and sophistication. You can feel the rich history of the place paired seamlessly with genuine hospitality. A perfect breakfast experience in every way — highly recommend to anyone looking for a memorable and refined start to their day. (5 stars)

Absolutely delightful dinner at the Lambs Club NYC 🥰 The lamb (as expected) was exquisite. I also had the steak tartar with caviar. I have not had caviar in a while, so that was such a treat! 🥰 Special thanks to Lydia who has been very attentive and accommodating. Definitely a five-star experience! (5 stars)

Our reservation was at 7pm and was able to get seat on time. The staff were friendly and helpful. Once we ordered, food came in decent time. The duck was tender and melts in your mouth. The scallops were delicious but too creamy for my taste. Otherwise we enjoyed the food and experience. (5 stars)

bio_text: The Leopard at Des Artistes was a celebrated Italian restaurant located in New York City, known for its warm ambiance and commitment to creating memorable dining experiences. Over its 15 years of operation, it fostered a sense of community among its guests, who gathered to celebrate life's special moments in a welcoming environment. The restaurant's dedication to quality service and culinary excellence made it a beloved destination for both locals and visitors alike. The Leopard focused on authentic Italian cuisine, offering a menu that highlighted traditional dishes with a modern twist. The restaurant was known for its use of high-quality ingredients and classic cooking techniques, providing guests with a rich and flavorful dining experience. The Leopard at Des Artistes opened its doors 15 years ago and was operated by the Sorrentinos and their dedicated team. The restaurant faced significant challenges in recent years, leading to its closure, but it left a lasting impact on the community it served.
review_snippets: Upscale Italian restaurant. High end service. We both order the ossobucco which came with a saffron risotto and shared the ragu as a starter. We also ordered a side of mixed vegetables which was the strangest mix I had seen at an Italian restaurant -- corn, tomatoes, cut asparagus. I also ordered a red wine per the suggestion of the server which was delicious. (4 stars)

bio_text: The Modern is a two Michelin-starred contemporary American restaurant located at the Museum of Modern Art, offering a refined dining experience with stunning views of the Abby Aldrich Rockefeller Sculpture Garden. The restaurant features three distinct dining options, each showcasing Executive Chef Thomas Allan's innovative approach to seasonal ingredients and exceptional culinary craftsmanship. The Modern specializes in contemporary American cuisine with a focus on seasonal ingredients. Guests can enjoy a prix fixe menu in the main dining area, an à la carte selection in the lively Bar Room, or a bespoke tasting menu at The Kitchen Table, all complemented by an extensive and award-winning wine program. Founded by Danny Meyer's Union Square Hospitality Group, The Modern has been serving guests since its debut in 2005 and has received numerous accolades, including four James Beard Awards and a Grand Award from Wine Spectator.

review_snippets: The Modern @ 9W 53rd st. NY NY 10019 To the right of The Museum of Modern Art is the magnificent Michelin starred restaurant serving all the top shelf hits! It doesn't have the most obvious entrance- nor is it the most beautiful doorway- that being said-the food is definitively on par with a Michelin rating! I must say, my wife & I had a great evening sampling the exquisite tasting menu. The drinks were delicious as well. We were seated in the main dining room, in a beautiful white table clothed booth- facing a large courtyard. The service was very good, but not excellent. I was expecting excellent. Our main server eventually disappeared but we were in great hands with Izzy & Vanessa. Our evening was topped off with a quick tour of the kitchen. The kitchen was in tip top shape- as Id expected. We always confer after an evening out and we both agreed we would definitively return & we do recommend The Modern. (5 stars)

The service was great. Upscale atmosphere with the New York pace. I really enjoyed the mini crab appetizer, it gave you the punch of the ocean. I love how the chef made the light cream full of strong scent, of orange and bonito without any curdling. Seafood is so delightful and fresh, you can taste the sweetness of the fish. The mini pumpkin dumplings are so creamy and tasty with the fried spinach leaf, the sweet lobster with the super thin slices of lemon was delicious. The duck special is on the chef(thank you!) and its skin is so crispy the melt in your mouth meat! Five course menu is enough for me; it will be too much! Highly recommended you to go and find out your own! Or finding little excuses to celebrate there! It’s a lovely restaurant to dine in with or without a company (prefer to share with other friends and family though)! P.s. I also saw an older lady with her family there, it remind me of my family growing up going out with grandparents every week to have a family meal together. (5 stars)

I went to The Modern for lunch and did the tasting menu. The food itself was great, everything was thoughtfully done and delicious. I especially loved the “eggs on eggs on eggs” and the little tartlet served at the beginning. Overall, the food absolutely lived up to expectations. That said, the service really fell short, which was disappointing given that this is a Michelin-star restaurant where service is a big part of the experience. We felt quite rushed throughout the meal. There was an event happening at MoMA, and we were one of the last lunch reservations before they closed for the rest of the day, which clearly affected the pacing. Even if there’s an event afterward, guests are paying a lot for the full experience, and it shouldn’t feel like you’re being pushed out. It took away from what could’ve been a really special meal. I do think the experience might be better at a time when there isn’t an event happening or for dinner, and I’d be open to coming back under different circumstances. The food was excellent, I just wish the service had matched it. (4 stars)

The food was interesting, but they had their own unique styles. Each carefully curated menus were great to experience and staffs were very well trained. I especially loved the menu eggs on eggs on eggs. Name sparked my interest and the presentation was stunning as well. Great place to visit. (5 stars)

bio_text: The Musket Room is a globally-inspired fine dining restaurant located in downtown Manhattan, known for its intimate atmosphere and thoughtful approach to cooking and hospitality. Since its opening in 2013, it has retained a Michelin star for a decade, becoming a beloved dining destination that offers a chef’s prix fixe menu alongside seasonal à la carte options. The restaurant features cozy nooks, a long cocktail bar, and a lush outdoor garden, making it a favored spot for al fresco dining. The Musket Room focuses on New American cuisine, emphasizing seasonal ingredients and bold flavors. The menu is crafted by Executive Chef Mary Attea and Chef de Cuisine Noah Ponjuan, featuring a prix fixe format complemented by rotating à la carte dishes. Signature techniques include a playful approach to bread service and desserts, overseen by Executive Pastry Chef Onika Brown. The Musket Room was established in 2013 and is the first restaurant of Elizabeth Street Hospitality, founded by sisters Jennifer and Nicole Vitagliano. The restaurant has maintained a Michelin star for a decade and is shaped by a diverse team whose backgrounds and travels inform its culinary and hospitality approach.

review_snippets: We recently visited The Musket Room and had an unforgettable experience. We tried the Chef’s Tasting – Artist Series (Fall 2025) Vegan Menu, and every course was outstanding. The flavors were beautifully balanced, the presentation was stunning, and the creativity behind each dish truly shined. From the truffle tartlet to the parsnip course, each plate was thoughtful, unique, and absolutely delicious. The only element we didn’t love was the sourdough, which we found a bit too hard to bite—but everything else more than made up for it. The service was warm, attentive, and made the evening even more special. We truly appreciated how accommodating the team was and how seamless the entire experience felt. Highly recommend The Musket Room to anyone looking for an elevated, plant-based dining experience. We can’t wait to return! (5 stars)

The Musket Room is not to be missed! My partner and I came for a birthday-engagement celebration and it was truly a divine experience. We opted for the Omnivore tasting menu, which changes regularly. However, no matter what day you go, the menu is unparalleled. Highlights from tonight included the most impeccably cooked venison. I also want to spotlight the team who served us. Vanessa and Charles are the best in the biz. Their timing was perfect, their service unmatched. They also went out of their ways to ensure the experience was unforgettable. We’re already planning our next visit. The ambience is also welcoming, elegant, and provides the perfect amount of space. I highly recommend the Musket Room for your next special occasion. Thank you to Vanessa, Charles, and the rest of the Musket Room team for a wonderful birthday dinner. Percy (and Conner) PS: the espresso martini is A+ (5 stars)

I was honored to be one of the first to enjoy the new vegan tasting menu and DEAR LORD it was great. The non-alcoholic pairings were fabulous too. Everyone working there was lovely, they made me feel like a million bucks. This restaurant is good for the body and soul. Well worth the money. Highly recommended. (5 stars)

My husband took me to Musket Room for our anniversary, and the whole evening felt like slipping into a secret world. The restaurant sits on my favorite street ,peaceful, a little romantic, the kind of block that makes you walk slower. Musket Room itself is so discreet from the outside you could mistake it for someone’s private studio. I love that. It already feels like you’re being let in. Inside, the space unfolds into two calm dining rooms that look straight out of Scandinavia: warm woods, soft lighting, chairs carved with the kind of intention you feel before you notice. We had a corner table, quietly tucked away, basically the “VIP of intimacy.” You can see outside through the little windows which are very cozy and special. And along the wall, bottles of wine arranged almost like sculptures, a simple but thoughtful installation. The music is also very good, the service is fantastic, they have almost every different waiter for each dish, makes us feel very special. And then I learned the menu was inspired by a local artist. Suddenly everything made sense — the colors, the shapes, the way every plate had the confidence of a small canvas. No wonder the dishes looked like little artworks. They weren’t just cooked; they were curated. The cocktails are also very delicious, cherry on the top! Now let’s talk about the main characters! House-made Sourdough & Anchovy Butter A warm sculpture of a loaf, spiked like a mountain range. The anchovy butter melted like salted silk. Honestly, museum-worthy carbohydrates. Æbleskiver with Truffle A tiny golden sphere wearing a delicate truffle “painting.” One bite, but it gave big fairytale energy. Razor Clam with Potato, Leek & Sourdough Presented in a soft white bowl like a minimalist artwork. Subtle, clean, almost Japanese in spirit like tasting the memory of the ocean. Beets with Huckleberry, Caviar & Amaranth This one looked like a neon-purple mosaic. Vivid, textured, playful. Pure art plate. Jamón Ibérico with Mussels, Potato & Saffron Layers of color and texture. The saffron yellow against the pale ham felt like a gentle watercolor. Potato Gnocchi with Chanterelles, Pistachio & Sorrel Woodland tones. Greens, golds, browns. Eating this felt like being inside a forest painting. Scallop with Squash, Lime & Tamarind The scallop was bronzed like it had been seared under gallery lights. The squash added this glowing orange brushstroke. A beautiful contrast of colors. Lamb Shoulder with Black Garlic, Maitake & Cabbage Rich, dark, dramatic. The charred cabbage petals looked like a charcoal sketch. By the end, the whole experience felt like a quiet European escape disguised as dinner: Scandinavian design, French warmth, Japanese precision, New York creativity. And all wrapped inside a menu shaped by a local artist, which explains why each dish came out like a tiny edible artwork. A perfect anniversary , intimate, low-key, beautifully designed, and curated just for us, you can feel you had a little getaway to Europe somewhere but yet without leaving Nolita! My husband impressed me once again! 💖💖💖 (5 stars)

Since its opening in 2013, it has retained a Michelin star for a decade, becoming a beloved dining destination that offers a chef’s prix fixe menu alongside seasonal à la carte options. The restaurant features cozy nooks, a long cocktail bar, and a lush outdoor garden, making it a favored spot for al fresco dining. The Musket Room focuses on New American cuisine, emphasizing seasonal ingredients and bold flavors. The menu is crafted by Executive Chef Mary Attea and Chef de Cuisine Noah Ponjuan, featuring a prix fixe format complemented by rotating à la carte dishes. Signature techniques include a playful approach to bread service and desserts, overseen by Executive Pastry Chef Onika Brown. The Musket Room was established in 2013 and is the first restaurant of Elizabeth Street Hospitality, founded by sisters Jennifer and Nicole Vitagliano. The restaurant has maintained a Michelin star for a decade and is shaped by a diverse team whose backgrounds and travels inform its culinary and hospitality approach. Cornbread - black truffle, soured honey - $24 Breads & Spreads - beurre de poulet, housemade farmer cheese with leek oil, smoked fish rillettes - $18 Snapper Crudo - cured snapper, satsuma, jasmine-lemongrass nuoc cham - $26 Oysters Three Ways - raw with pink peppercorn granita, fried oyster croquette, pickled fennel, Herbsaint chargrilled with beurre de Créole - $28 Kristal Caviar - tempura fried collards, whipped buttermilk - $125 Fava Beans - grilled with smoked tofu, opal basil - $22 We recently visited The Musket Room and had an unforgettable experience. We tried the Chef’s Tasting – Artist Series (Fall 2025) Vegan Menu, and every course was outstanding. The flavors were beautifully balanced, the presentation was stunning, and the creativity behind each dish truly shined. From the truffle tartlet to the parsnip course, each plate was thoughtful, unique, and absolutely delicious. The only element we didn’t love was the sourdough, which we found a bit too hard to bite—but everything else more than made up for it. The service was warm, attentive, and made the evening even more special. We truly appreciated how accommodating the team was and how seamless the entire experience felt. Highly recommend The Musket Room to anyone looking for an elevated, plant-based dining experience. We can’t wait to return! (5 stars) The Musket Room is not to be missed! My partner and I came for a birthday-engagement celebration and it was truly a divine experience. We opted for the Omnivore tasting menu, which changes regularly. However, no matter what day you go, the menu is unparalleled. Highlights from tonight included the most impeccably cooked venison. I also want to spotlight the team who served us. Vanessa and Charles are the best in the biz. Their timing was perfect, their service unmatched. They also went out of their ways to ensure the experience was unforgettable. We’re already planning our next visit. The ambience is also welcoming, elegant, and provides the perfect amount of space. I highly recommend the Musket Room for your next special occasion. Thank you to Vanessa, Charles, and the rest of the Musket Room team for a wonderful birthday dinner. Percy (and Conner) PS: the espresso martini is A+ (5 stars) I was honored to be one of the first to enjoy the new vegan tasting menu and DEAR LORD it was great. The non-alcoholic pairings were fabulous too. Everyone working there was lovely, they made me feel like a million bucks. This restaurant is good for the body and soul. Well worth the money. Highly recommended. (5 stars) My husband took me to Musket Room for our anniversary, and the whole evening felt like slipping into a secret world. The restaurant sits on my favorite street ,peaceful, a little romantic, the kind of block that makes you walk slower. Musket Room itself is so discreet from the outside you could mistake it for someone’s private studio. I love that. It already feels like you’re being let in. Inside, the space unfolds into two calm dining rooms that look straight out of Scandinavia: warm woods, soft lighting, chairs carved with the kind of intention you feel before you notice. We had a corner table, quietly tucked away, basically the “VIP of intimacy.” You can see outside through the little windows which are very cozy and special. And along the wall, bottles of wine arranged almost like sculptures, a simple but thoughtful installation. The music is also very good, the service is fantastic, they have almost every different waiter for each dish, makes us feel very special. And then I learned the menu was inspired by a local artist. Suddenly everything made sense — the colors, the shapes, the way every plate had the confidence of a small canvas. No wonder the dishes looked like little artworks. They weren’t just cooked; they were curated. The cocktails are also very delicious, cherry on the top! Now let’s talk about the main characters! House-made Sourdough & Anchovy Butter A warm sculpture of a loaf, spiked like a mountain range. The anchovy butter melted like salted silk. Honestly, museum-worthy carbohydrates. Æbleskiver with Truffle A tiny golden sphere wearing a delicate truffle “painting.” One bite, but it gave big fairytale energy. Razor Clam with Potato, Leek & Sourdough Presented in a soft white bowl like a minimalist artwork. Subtle, clean, almost Japanese in spirit like tasting the memory of the ocean. Beets with Huckleberry, Caviar & Amaranth This one looked like a neon-purple mosaic. Vivid, textured, playful. Pure art plate. Jamón Ibérico with Mussels, Potato & Saffron Layers of color and texture. The saffron yellow against the pale ham felt like a gentle watercolor. Potato Gnocchi with Chanterelles, Pistachio & Sorrel Woodland tones. Greens, golds, browns. Eating this felt like being inside a forest painting. Scallop with Squash, Lime & Tamarind The scallop was bronzed like it had been seared under gallery lights. The squash added this glowing orange brushstroke. A beautiful contrast of colors. Lamb Shoulder with Black Garlic, Maitake & Cabbage Rich, dark, dramatic. The charred cabbage petals looked like a charcoal sketch. By the end, the whole experience felt like a quiet European escape disguised as dinner: Scandinavian design, French warmth, Japanese precision, New York creativity. And all wrapped inside a menu shaped by a local artist, which explains why each dish came out like a tiny edible artwork. A perfect anniversary , intimate, low-key, beautifully designed, and curated just for us, you can feel you had a little getaway to Europe somewhere but yet without leaving Nolita! My husband impressed me once again! 💖💖💖 (5 stars)

review_snippets: Came here for a birthday dinner, and the fish was incredibly fresh and flavorful. The servers were attentive, friendly, and very accommodating to allergies. Highly recommend! (5 stars)

I can’t think of a more perfect place for an anniversary dinner! The Office of Mr Moto delivered on exceptional high quality food and wonderful service. We had Kenji as our head chef and he is so talented and kind as he prepared 21 courses at the counter for us. Every piece of fish is so fresh and the presentation was so beautiful. The Japanese snapper, king salmon and tuna’s were my favorite. And the oyster starter was the best I’ve ever had. I also loved the truffle and caviar course, it melts in your mouth. I highly recommend the sake pairing - they match every dish perfectly and the apple one was incredible! You have to check out the speakeasy downstairs before you leave. It is so charming and there’s a piano that plays itself, it’s so enchanting! If you’re looking for a phenomenal and memorable omakase experience, this is the place to go. (5 stars)

Had dinner at Office of Mr. Moto last Saturday, and I have to say I enjoyed the experience. The whole speakeasy concept and backstory leans heavily into branding, but it’s a fun setup and they commit to it. That said, the real highlight was the omakase. The sushi was excellent—super fresh, delicately prepared, and seasoned just right to enhance the natural flavors of the fish. There were some unique and rare selections that stood out. And their uni roll? Absolute bomb. I don’t think I’ve ever seen that much uni packed into one roll. You’re definitely paying extra for the concept though. I agree with other reviewers who’ve said it feels overpriced compared to some of the other high-end omakase spots in the city. Still, the quality was there and I did enjoy the meal overall. (4 stars)

The fish was delicious and the omakase style fantastic. If I were the proprietor I would probably lose all of the Mr Moto stuff and focus on the food and beautiful dining room. In fairness once you are in and seated that’s pretty much what they have done anyway. (5 stars)

bio_text: The River Café is an exclusive fine dining American restaurant located under the iconic Brooklyn Bridge, offering breathtaking views of the NYC skyline. Since its opening in 1977, it has established itself as a romantic culinary destination, renowned for its elegant atmosphere, exceptional service, and a Michelin-starred menu that celebrates classic American cuisine. The restaurant's ambiance is enhanced by live piano music and exquisite floral arrangements, making it a favored venue for special occasions. The River Café specializes in classic American cuisine, with a menu that evolves with the changing seasons. It features a fine dining format that emphasizes elegance and refinement, complemented by one of the world's most outstanding wine lists. The River Café has been delighting guests since 1977, founded by Chef Brad Steelman, who focuses on sourcing the finest ingredients to enhance the dining experience.
menu_items: Seasonal Vegetable Strudel
Grilled Artichoke “Hummus,” Candied Lemon, Crisp Crouton
Goat Cheese Crostini, Niçoise Olive and Red Piquillo Pepper
Ginger Tempura Vegetable Skewers
Potato Pancakes, Rosemary, Fresh Apple Purée
Cauliflower “Mousseline” Caviar and Crème Fraîche
review_snippets: From the beginning to the end our birthday dinner was an incredible experience. We were celebrating her birthday and she truly enjoyed it! The simplicity, but sophisticated restaurant ambience, to the mellow live music in the background complemented with an amazing view of the city and Brooklyn bridge at night time made our experience to be out of this world. The food was absolutely incredible, with a bold flavor and every bite taking us to a different level of joy, more gratefulness and sharing each other's dishes for more discoveries of childhood and times when food actually had taste. Each dish was unique in its own way and the chef's complementary side or dishes took us to heaven. Now, the drinks, outstanding and well done, strong as they should always be made. The attention of the staff was incredible, from the moment we entered until the moment we received the check. An absolute dreamy birthday that came to life in the city that never sleeps, they say, but we slept like babies after this incredible diner at the River Cafe. (5 stars)

Visiting this restaurant is an experience, not just a meal. Everything about it our visit here was fabulous. For us it was a splurge while visiting New York, to celebrate our Engagement, and The River Cafe kindly gave us a window table for this special occasion. The skyline looking back across New York from under the Brooklyn Bridge was truly spectacular. New York even decided to have it start snowing while we were there which meant we walked out into a winter wonderland. There was also someone playing the piano which added so beautifully to the ambiance. The food was flawless. Everything we ordered was taste profile balanced and so yummy. There were complimentary little entrees before our chosen entrees arrived. The pace of food coming to the table was not rushed. The service was excellent. The only thing I can think of to enhance the meal/experience would be a palate cleanser. I would highly recommend a visit to the River Cafe. (5 stars)

An absolutely unforgettable dining experience. From the moment we arrived, The River Café delivered everything you hope for in a truly special New York evening. The setting alone — with breathtaking views of the Manhattan skyline and the Brooklyn Bridge — creates an atmosphere that feels both romantic and timeless. Service was impeccable: attentive without ever feeling intrusive, warm, professional, and perfectly paced throughout the night. Every dish was beautifully presented and executed with precision. The flavors were refined, balanced, and clearly crafted with care. Each course felt intentional, turning dinner into an experience rather than just a meal. The wine selection complemented the food perfectly, and the overall ambiance was elegant, calm, and exactly what fine dining should feel like. In a city filled with dining options, The River Café truly stands out. Worth every moment and a place I would gladly return to for another special occasion. (5 stars)

Dining at The River Café is truly about the experience. We had the three-course meal, and the overall presentation was elegant. The environment was very cozy and romantic, with beautiful views under the Brooklyn Bridge, and the staff was nice, attentive, and amazing throughout. While the courses were well presented, the desserts felt quite costly and didn’t fully meet expectations for a Michelin-level experience, as the flavors were a bit bland. I’d recommend visiting in the summer if you want to fully enjoy the atmosphere and surroundings. Overall, it’s a memorable place mainly for the setting and service. (5 stars)

bio_text: Theodora is a contemporary dining establishment that showcases a refined approach to Mediterranean cuisine, led by chef and owner Tomer Blechman. The restaurant features an open fire kitchen, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere where guests can enjoy a thoughtfully curated selection of seasonal dishes paired with a natural wine program. Theodora specializes in Mediterranean cuisine with a focus on seasonal produce and dry-aged fish. The menu is designed to highlight the flavors of the region while incorporating innovative cooking techniques, particularly through the use of an open fire. Theodora is the latest venture from chef/owner Tomer Blechman, who is also known for the popular Mediterranean restaurant Miss Ada in Fort Greene and its sister concept Nili in Carroll Gardens.

Hiramasa - Finger Limes, Avocado, Dashi - $20

Mussels & Clams - Braised Sorana Beans, Basil Salmoriglio - $25
