Black Cod - Miso Beurre Blanc, Wood-Fired Asparagus - $31
review_snippets: Finally snagged a reservation! And yes, it was worth the hype. The atmosphere is amazing and warm. Our server was wonderful and kind. Love the sourdough with whipped ricotta. The mackerel toast was delicious. Red snapper ceviche excellent. And the whole dry-aged branzino, so good. The server also helped debone the fish and he did a great job. Would definitely come back again! (5 stars)

100/10. The culinary highlight of our NYC trip. We ordered a bunch from the menu, and there wasn’t a dish we didn’t love. We loved the Hiramsa to start, fresh and had a tang to it. The grilled mackerel is a must and comes on beautiful sourdough made fresh. It may not be visually appealing for some, but I recommend you try it! The black cod was perfectly cooked, covered in an amazing sauce and salad. The whole butterflied trout was the standout item, packed full of Smokey flavour and different experiences you get switching from one side of the fish to the other is unique and delicious. This dish was what brought Theodora to my attention and it did not disappoint. The service was fantastic and the waiters were tentative but we loved the chefs table experience. Eating in front of the grill and watching the food go through different stages if cooking so much fun. The chef was very friendly and made time to talk to us over the course of our dinner. If you are a small part, book the countertop table. We spent about $200 for 2 people, we didn’t have alcoholic drinks. Theodora is fully booked out weeks ahead, a reservation is a must, good luck getting one. I absolutely recommend this place and will be back the next time I’m in NY. (5 stars)

We absolutely LOVED this place! The hype is real!! We were lucky to be sat at the chefs counter right next to the expo. We got to watch everyone work and they are a well oiled machine. This is the best Mediterranean food we’ve had in NYC. All the dishes benefit from the wood firing even if they aren’t directly prepared on the grill which was a beautiful surprise. For example the oil on the hummus. Mind blown Favorite bite of the night…the tilefish ceviche with wood fired pineapple. Wow! Also and most importantly, the service was elite. Our server Zoe was just so great, friendly knowledgeable, attentive, all the things! We also got to meet and chat a bit with the GM, Katie. So nice! We can’t wait to go back and try everything we don’t get to try this time. (5 stars)

Theodora Restaurant absolutely lives up to the hype—even if getting a reservation feels like winning the lottery. Every dish is bold, flavorful, and confidently executed, especially the seafood-focused menu. The appetizers were flawless across the board, and the fish dishes truly shine. Don’t miss the sourdough (elite), yellowfin tuna, salmon king crudo, and the ceviche—standout bites that justify the buzz. The lamb was a bit too strong on aroma for my taste, and while the octopus was good, it wasn’t the star. Still, an exceptional meal overall and 100% worth the chase. (5 stars)

bio_text: Tobalá is a vibrant Oaxacan-inspired restaurant located in the heart of Riverdale, New York. Owned and operated by the López family, the restaurant embodies a deep-rooted love for Oaxacan cuisine and culture, offering a warm and inviting atmosphere that celebrates family, community, and tradition. With a focus on authenticity and innovation, Tobalá provides an unforgettable dining experience, whether for a casual meal or a special occasion. Tobalá specializes in modern and traditional Oaxacan cuisine, featuring a menu that highlights rich and complex flavors. Signature dishes include callos y mole verde, Pulpo de Puerto, and enmoladas de pato, all crafted with traditional ingredients and techniques. The restaurant also offers a carefully curated beverage program that includes traditional Mexican cocktails and a selection of small-batch mezcals. Tobalá is owned by Chef Moisés López, his wife Eluisania López, and their family, who have spent over a decade perfecting their craft through learning from artisans and chefs in Oaxaca and New York. The name 'Tobalá' is inspired by a revered species of agave in Oaxaca.

Guacamole - smoked corn, queso fresco, corn tortillas chips
Esquites - off-the-cob roasted corn, chicatana mayo, cotija cheese
Picadita de Hongos - oyster mushrooms, salsa taquera, beets, frijoles, radish
Fluke Tostada - molcajete sauce, crema de aguacate, onions, epazote
Tamal de Hongos - mole verde, corn and squash tamal, mushroom paste, watercress
review_snippets: Tobala is so worth the visit! We decided to give Tobala a try and we were not disappointed. The initial entry was warm and inviting, and we were immediately seated. The ambiance was romantic and cozy and the layout was efficient and flowy. The playlist was great, the service was excellent and the food was impeccably delicious! We almost did not want to disturb it. Everything was spot-on! The appetizers were small , but fresh, tasty and delish! The entrees were a bit larger in portion, delicious and filling! The prices were steep, but this place serves authentic high quality foods. We were glad that we chose Tobala for our date night! We enjoyed the desserts— the bunuela and the tres leches, I preferred the center of my tres leches not be so distinctively orange-flavored. We plan to return to Tobala, it was worth the trip! (5 stars)

Dairon is the most incredible bartender you could ever experience at this establishment. He makes you feel at home & gives every single guests the best experience possible. He is so knowledgeable and passionate about his craft, he makes guests excited to try every single cocktail on the menu. Although the restaurant is pricey, the experience is worth every dollar. My partner & I visit this place at least once every other week for the past six months, it has never disappointed us. As someone in hospitality, management here is certainly doing something right (5 stars)

This is a very laid back place, with a charged atmosphere. Impossible? Not at all. It's an experience. The food was delicious. I had the baked fish and my wife had the grilled steak, we were both pleased. The wait team was at our back and call. Nice please for a romantic outing. (5 stars)

We stopped by Tobala in Riverdale this time just for drinks and dessert. I had their hibiscus margarita, which was really good — refreshing and perfectly balanced. We also tried their flan de maíz, our first time having flan with that flavor, and it was delicious! It came with a side of sapote, which had a great flavor and texture. Overall, a really nice experience — great place to relax and enjoy something different. (4 stars)

Trío de Moles - amarillo, rojo, negro, corn tortillas Guacamole - smoked corn, queso fresco, corn tortillas chips Esquites - off-the-cob roasted corn, chicatana mayo, cotija cheese Picadita de Hongos - oyster mushrooms, salsa taquera, beets, frijoles, radish Fluke Tostada - molcajete sauce, crema de aguacate, onions, epazote Tamal de Hongos - mole verde, corn and squash tamal, mushroom paste, watercress Tobala is so worth the visit! We decided to give Tobala a try and we were not disappointed. The initial entry was warm and inviting, and we were immediately seated. The ambiance was romantic and cozy and the layout was efficient and flowy. The playlist was great, the service was excellent and the food was impeccably delicious! We almost did not want to disturb it. Everything was spot-on! The appetizers were small , but fresh, tasty and delish! The entrees were a bit larger in portion, delicious and filling! The prices were steep, but this place serves authentic high quality foods. We were glad that we chose Tobala for our date night! We enjoyed the desserts— the bunuela and the tres leches, I preferred the center of my tres leches not be so distinctively orange-flavored. We plan to return to Tobala, it was worth the trip! (5 stars) Dairon is the most incredible bartender you could ever experience at this establishment. He makes you feel at home & gives every single guests the best experience possible. He is so knowledgeable and passionate about his craft, he makes guests excited to try every single cocktail on the menu. Although the restaurant is pricey, the experience is worth every dollar. My partner & I visit this place at least once every other week for the past six months, it has never disappointed us. As someone in hospitality, management here is certainly doing something right (5 stars) This is a very laid back place, with a charged atmosphere. Impossible? Not at all. It's an experience. The food was delicious. I had the baked fish and my wife had the grilled steak, we were both pleased. The wait team was at our back and call. Nice please for a romantic outing. (5 stars) We stopped by Tobala in Riverdale this time just for drinks and dessert. I had their hibiscus margarita, which was really good — refreshing and perfectly balanced. We also tried their flan de maíz, our first time having flan with that flavor, and it was delicious! It came with a side of sapote, which had a great flavor and texture. Overall, a really nice experience — great place to relax and enjoy something different. (4 stars)

bio_text: Tolo is a vibrant dining destination located in New York City, offering a unique blend of traditional Chinese cuisine and contemporary dining aesthetics. The restaurant features an open kitchen and vintage furniture, creating an inviting atmosphere for guests to enjoy a diverse menu that ranges from raw seafood to comforting rice and noodle dishes, all complemented by a carefully curated wine list of over 300 selections. Tolo specializes in modern Chinese cuisine, showcasing a variety of dishes that highlight fresh ingredients and bold flavors. The menu includes options such as raw seafood, rice, noodles, and signature dishes like sweet & sour crispy fish, presented in a casual yet refined format. Tolo is helmed by Chef Ron Yan, who has spent the past decade immersed in New York City's culinary scene.
menu_items: east coast oysters with Sichuan oil - $10
razor clams with black garlic & puffed rice - $20
bamboo shoot salad with sesame chili crisp - $11
cucumber & wood ear with wasabi - $11
salt & pepper tofu with chili aioli - $14
seaweed “shake shake” fries - $14
review_snippets: Absolutely stunning — inventive, impeccably executed food and service that truly impressed: the cucumber & wood ear with wasabi delivered a perfect sesame-paste + wasabi mix that honestly resembled Liang Pi, the water spinach with fermented tofu and garlic brought complex, layered umami, the salt & pepper pork chop with hot green-pepper sauce (the green-pepper-sauce + side-salad combo was unbeatable) was wildly satisfying, and the duck breast with black garlic, onion cream and chicory felt like a French take on Peking duck — the charred cabbage on the side was a lovely, smoky touch; both desserts were stunning, especially the black sticky rice with mango sorbet, and service was on point with a waiter whose recommendation was thoughtful — loved this place. (5 stars)

been here a few times and each time is so good. the salt & pepper tofu with chili aioli is one of my fave things along with little rice noodles with XO sauce but truthfully, everything here is good!! highly recommend it (5 stars)

Everything is seasoned terribly. We couldn’t finish the dish. The sweet and sour fish’s sauce taste like tomato sauce in pasta. The service is fine but the table we were given is terrible. It was right by the door so very cold and the butt the people who are still waiting is right by my face. Very expensive for what it is (1 stars)

A friend recommended this spot, and based on the reviews, I was expecting more. The restaurant itself is cozy and romantic, but it was louder and more tightly packed than I anticipated—conversation required a raised voice even across a small table. The menu descriptions promised bold, unique flavors, but the dishes didn’t quite follow through. They only offer wine at the moment, I was hoping for a Chinese-inspired cocktail option, don't think they have a liquor license? We started with the Sticky Rice with Chinese sausage, which tasted overcooked and a bit too mushy. For mains, we shared the Sweet & Sour Fish and the Duck Confit 'Zhajiang' Noodles. The fish was the highlight of the night, though still fairly simple, and the noodles felt surprisingly ordinary. We didn't finish any of the things we ordered other than the glasses of wine. Overall, I left underwhelmed given the reviews and especially the price point. Maybe I didn’t order the right dishes, but with a menu that small, I expected more consistency and stronger flavors. (2 stars)

bio_text: Tonchin is a celebrated ramen restaurant that originated in Tokyo, Japan, in 1992. With a mission to create a welcoming space for all, Tonchin has expanded from its humble beginnings to multiple locations, including a flagship in Midtown New York, a full-menu restaurant in Brooklyn, and a new site in Larchmont Village, LA. The restaurant embodies a spirit of community and connection, offering a unique dining experience centered around the art of ramen. Tonchin specializes in Tokyo-style ramen, particularly their signature Tokyo Tonkotsu broth, which is a lighter version of traditional pork broths. The menu features hand-kneaded, medium-thick noodles that are prepared fresh daily, ensuring optimal texture and flavor. The culinary approach emphasizes quality ingredients and innovative techniques to create a harmonious balance of flavors. Tonchin was founded by brothers Katsuhiro and Motohiro Sugeno, who were inspired by the evolving nature of ramen. After 25 years, Anan Sugeno expanded the brand to the global stage, continuing the legacy of experimentation and community connection.
menu_items: original TEBASAKI - fried chicken wing, teriyaki sauce, chef’s spicy seasoning - $18 / $24 / $26
Curry+Cheese tebasaki - fried chicken wing, teriyaki sauce, chef’s curry seasoning, parmigiano cheese, fresh chive - $19 / $25 / $27
gyoza - ground pork, chinese cabbage, ginger, sesame oil, scallion, rice vinegar, soy sauce, spicy sauce - $16
Tokyo rice ball chashu - aburi chashu, spicy mayo, sesame, radish sprout, seaweed - $7
UNAGI - eel, pickled ginger, sansho pepper, seaweed - $8
ume - roasted sesame, pickled plum, salted kelp, seaweed - $7
review_snippets: The Smokey miso noodles was SO GOOD! The dipping noodles was also excellent. Love the thick noodles. Both noodles had a nice texture and chew while the broth popped with flavor. I used to work in the offices above over 20 years ago. It would have been great to have a noodle shop here back then. This is definitely in my top 10 ramen spots in NYC. Don’t need to fly to Japan for an excellent bowl of noodles. Come here. (5 stars)

Lunch special for me, $28. Started with the tsukune (chicken “meatball” bun) very tasty. I got the spicy Dan Dan Ramen, which was flavorful and delicious, the noodles were cooked to perfection, and the broth had just the right amount of spice. The place has a kind of basic/funky vibe, servers were very nice and efficient and the place was quite busy at lunchtime. (4 stars)

Great tonkotsu broth - I am a big fan but tan tan was alright. I was a bit underwhelmed with it. Good selection of drinks and the service is quick and very friendly. Would go back again 100%. Definitely need a reservation unless you want to wait 30mins to an hour for a table. (5 stars)

This place has a Michelin star for a reason. Got the classic tonkatsu ramen and one of the Chashu Tokyo rice balls. The rice ball was fire. Ramen I’ve had a lot of good ramen in my life so this wasn’t the best I’ve had but very good anyway. Great vibe. And one person seating is much faster than a group :) (5 stars)

bio_text: Tong is a vibrant dining destination located in Bushwick, Brooklyn, offering an authentic Thai culinary experience. The restaurant's atmosphere is lively and inviting, making it an ideal spot for both casual dining and special events. With a focus on sharing plates, Tong encourages guests to enjoy a variety of flavors in a communal setting, complemented by a selection of cocktails and beverages. Tong specializes in authentic Thai cuisine, featuring a menu rich in small dishes and snacks inspired by various regions of Thailand. The culinary focus includes bold flavors and spices, with signature dishes such as Isaan style spicy beef tartare and crispy fried chicken. The dining format encourages sharing, making it perfect for groups and gatherings. Tong, which means gold, aims to provide a wealth of authentic Thai flavors and has quickly become a favorite among locals and visitors alike.
menu_items: GOI - spicy beef tartare with shallot, cilantro, toasted rice, served with taro chips and lettuce
Gai Tod - fried crunchy chicken thigh topped with crispy shallot served with sweet chili sauce
Pork Jowl - succulent grilled pork jowl with spicy tamarind jaew dipping sauce
Tum Tang - cucumber, chili, tomato, lime, fermented anchovy sauce
Yum Naem - crispy rice with fermented pork sausage, chili, roasted peanuts, shallot, scallion, cilantro, ginger
Taro Fritter - fritters of taro, sweet potato, black bean with sweet chili sauce
review_snippets: Tong in Bushwick is where you go to experience authentic Thai small plates known as kub klaem. The sleek dining room wrapped in rustic metal walls captures that raw NYC energy while still feeling clean and cozy with lighting that mirrors how vibrant the food tastes. Tong does not hold back on spice and a simple medium Thai spicy is no joke, definitely not for first timers and even seasoned spice lovers might find it daring but that heat brings out the true and unapologetic deliciousness of Thailand. From cocktails to small plates everything is thoughtfully crafted and plated like edible art. If you love Thai cuisine or crave bold spicy flavors, Tong is the perfect spot for incredible food creative drinks and warm hospitality with genuine smiles that go the extra mile. (5 stars)

Came here to say with my brother and his finance. Pretty nice restaurant. The prices were decent. Large portion sizes. The tom yum soup was amazing. It was spicy but full of flavor and texture. I had the green curry with tofu and it was one of the best I have ever had. The curry was smooth and the rice was fresh and not sticky. I’m he tofu was the perfect texture for the broth. My brother and his fiancé got the drunken noodles and I know they loved it because they finished the bowl. (5 stars)

Went on a date night to Tong, a Thai restaurant in Bushwick recognized by the Michelin Guide. Because of how popular it has become, it’s definitely best to make a reservation ahead of time since the space fills up quickly and many people come specifically for the food. The atmosphere makes it a really nice date spot. Dim lighting, warm wooden tables, and thoughtful plating give it an intimate feel without being overly formal, and the staff were warm and welcoming from the moment we walked in. To start, I ordered the Jolean cocktail made with gin, lychee, butterfly pea flower, orange blossom water, lime, and egg white. It was light, floral, and well balanced, with the egg white giving it that silky foam texture. My boyfriend kept it classic with a Thai iced tea, served in a mason jar with the familiar gradient of dark tea and creamy milk that gives it that rich sweetness and deep caramel color. For appetizers we started with the Som Tum Thai, one of Thailand’s most iconic salads. Traditionally from the Isan region in northeastern Thailand, som tum is all about balancing the four core Thai flavor elements: sour, spicy, sweet, and salty. The dish came with long strands of shredded green papaya piled high with peanuts, cherry tomatoes, long beans, dried shrimp, fresh chili, and a wedge of lime on the side. The green papaya itself is mild and crunchy, almost like a vegetable version of a green apple, which makes it perfect for soaking up the lime heavy dressing. The dried shrimp added a deep umami note while the peanuts gave it texture. It was refreshing but still packed with flavor, with the dressing lightly pooling at the bottom so everything could be tossed together. We also ordered the Truffle Spring Rolls, filled with glass noodles, shiitake mushrooms, and oyster mushrooms. Glass noodles, made from mung bean starch, absorb flavor really well and give that slightly chewy texture that works perfectly inside crispy spring rolls. The mushroom filling was earthy and rich, and the truffle added an aromatic depth that made it feel slightly more elevated than a typical vegetable roll. The fry was clean and crisp without feeling greasy, which made them really enjoyable. For mains, I ordered the Pad Cha Talay, a seafood stir fry known for being bold and aromatic. Pad cha refers to a style of stir fry loaded with herbs and spices that create a fragrant, slightly spicy dish. This one had shrimp, squid, and mussels with bamboo shoots, eggplant, long beans, kaffir lime leaf, fresh green peppercorn clusters, and krachai, also known as fingerroot, a traditional Thai herb with a peppery, ginger like aroma. The seafood was cooked well and the vegetables still had a nice bite to them. The bamboo shoots and eggplant absorbed the sauce nicely, while the fresh peppercorns added small bursts of spice throughout the dish. It was served with a dome of fluffy jasmine rice that paired perfectly with the aromatic sauce. My boyfriend ordered the Khao Soi, a Northern Thai curry noodle soup from the Chiang Mai region known for its rich coconut curry broth and the contrast between soft noodles and crispy noodles on top. Flavor wise, the broth was really delicious, warm, creamy, and comforting. However, the presentation and balance could definitely be improved. The chicken was mostly hidden under the broth and noodles, and the portion leaned heavily toward noodles compared to the bean sprouts and other components. If the ingredients were distributed more evenly, visually showing the chicken, noodles, and bean sprouts, it would elevate both the presentation and the overall balance of the dish. Service overall was great, though water refills could have been a little more attentive. For a restaurant recognized by Michelin, the food here is already strong in terms of flavor and execution, but there are small areas where things could be elevated further, particularly presentation and balance in certain dishes. With a few refinements, it could better match the level that the pricing suggests. I would definitely come back to try more of the menu. (4 stars)

Food was ok, not the most flavorful, warm. I would not come back. Great service though Update: upon paying the waitress was rude and annoyed at us asking for a fork. It was the reason why I lowered my score. (2 stars)

bio_text: Tong Sam Gyup Goo Yi is a vibrant Korean restaurant located in Flushing, NY, offering a warm and inviting atmosphere for diners. With a commitment to authentic Korean flavors and a focus on quality ingredients, the restaurant provides a unique dining experience that caters to both traditional and modern tastes. The restaurant specializes in Korean cuisine, featuring a diverse menu that highlights grilled meats and traditional dishes. Guests can expect a menu format that emphasizes communal dining, allowing for a shared experience of various flavors and textures.
menu_items: Samgyeopsal - Thin sliced pork barbecued - $19.99
Dwaeji Bulgogi - Pork marinated in our special sauce barbecued - $20.99
Gochang Gui - Marinated in chef's special sauce barbecued - $19.99
Kimchi Naengmyeon - Cold noodle with kimchi - $12.99
Bibimbap - Rice with sliced vegetable in spicy sauce - $11.99
Sliced Duck - $12.99
review_snippets: I wasn’t a big fan of pork belly before I found this restaurant. I highly recommend to try their pork belly. So good, so good, I LOVE IT!!!!!! Every time we went there, we ordered at least four plates of pork belly, I never get tired of their pork belly. Kimchi is great too! The fired rice , the way the mixed the ingredients is so perfect to eat as the last meal of that moment. Also, the way the set up their grill pan makes me feel like they are taking me back to retro korean bbq spot in Kdrama. (5 stars)

I have been going to this spot for years. The old couple who used to own the place sold it, and currently in the hands of new owners. Great food, great vibes, reasonable prices. Wait staff is great, especially the petite Hispanic lady very attentive and generous with portions. My go to spot when I'm craving for some Pork belly bbq. 100% recommend. Not kid friendly though, young kids / toddlers can easily burn themselves in the hot plate in the middle of the table. (5 stars)

We came here for lunch on a Saturday and our party of 2 was seated quickly. The service here is no frills, very to the point, getting the job done (which was fine) but I felt a bit confused at times. For food, we got 2 servings of the pork belly, fried rice w/ cheese, and the cold noodles. Overall, I thought the food was okay. The banchans were good and had a bit of variety. The servings of the pork belly were decently sized although for the price and the area, I thought they could've been a bit bigger. If I came again, I would pass on the cold noodles - felt store bought and the ice bowl felt like a gimmick. (4 stars)

Another place for authentic Korean BBQ! The meat portion was not a lot but various side dish options to enjoy with. 🥄✨Fried rice: this will be the one I recommend the most, adding rice and some topping to fry on the pan at the end of the meal. The rice took the oil from pan, mixing with egg, and what we ordered (roe, cheese.) super flavored and tasty. 🥣🥢Cold noodles was outstanding too. The soup was refreshing! (4 stars)

I highly recommend to try their pork belly. So good, so good, I LOVE IT!!!!!! Every time we went there, we ordered at least four plates of pork belly, I never get tired of their pork belly. Kimchi is great too! The fired rice , the way the mixed the ingredients is so perfect to eat as the last meal of that moment. Also, the way the set up their grill pan makes me feel like they are taking me back to retro korean bbq spot in Kdrama. (5 stars) I have been going to this spot for years. The old couple who used to own the place sold it, and currently in the hands of new owners. Great food, great vibes, reasonable prices. Wait staff is great, especially the petite Hispanic lady very attentive and generous with portions. My go to spot when I'm craving for some Pork belly bbq. 100% recommend. Not kid friendly though, young kids / toddlers can easily burn themselves in the hot plate in the middle of the table. (5 stars) We came here for lunch on a Saturday and our party of 2 was seated quickly. The service here is no frills, very to the point, getting the job done (which was fine) but I felt a bit confused at times. For food, we got 2 servings of the pork belly, fried rice w/ cheese, and the cold noodles. Overall, I thought the food was okay. The banchans were good and had a bit of variety. The servings of the pork belly were decently sized although for the price and the area, I thought they could've been a bit bigger. If I came again, I would pass on the cold noodles - felt store bought and the ice bowl felt like a gimmick. (4 stars) Another place for authentic Korean BBQ! The meat portion was not a lot but various side dish options to enjoy with. 🥄✨Fried rice: this will be the one I recommend the most, adding rice and some topping to fry on the pan at the end of the meal. The rice took the oil from pan, mixing with egg, and what we ordered (roe, cheese.) super flavored and tasty. 🥣🥢Cold noodles was outstanding too. The soup was refreshing! (4 stars)

bio_text: Torien is a distinguished dining establishment in New York City that offers a traditional yakitori omakase experience, inviting guests to immerse themselves in the rich tapestry of Japanese food culture. The restaurant emphasizes a sensory dining experience where customers are the focal point, ensuring that each visit is memorable and engaging. Torien specializes in yakitori, a Japanese style of grilling skewered chicken, presented in an omakase format. The menu showcases a variety of expertly prepared dishes that highlight the nuances of Japanese culinary techniques. Torien is inspired by its sister restaurant, Torishiki, located in Tokyo, Japan, and aims to extend the authentic Japanese dining experience to New York City.
review_snippets: Incredible date night at Torien! This is easily the best yakitori experience in NYC. The omakase journey was flawless—each skewer was grilled to perfection over binchotan charcoal, with that unmistakable smoky aroma and juicy texture. A few highlights were the chicken oyster and the liver, both were melt-in-your-mouth tender. The atmosphere is intimate, dark, and sophisticated, making it the perfect spot for a special occasion with my girlfriend. The service was impeccable and attentive throughout the night. It truly felt like a piece of Tokyo in the heart of NoHo. Can’t wait to return! (5 stars)

From the second we walked in, the vibe was amazing. Everyone working there was so friendly — you could literally feel the good energy. The small touches made such a difference: everyone personally greeting you, pulling and pushing the chairs, even the chef walking you out when you leave, asking if you need help getting into your Uber. It’s hospitality done right. And the food… insane. Not one bad bite. Everything was so well done. I also loved the open-kitchen omakase setup — watching them cook everything right in front of you made it even cooler. And unlike a lot of omakase spots, I actually left full. Like, genuinely full — in the best way. Also, random shoutout to their ceramics — the plates, bowls, cups… all of it. Super nice and added to the whole aesthetic. Overall just a 10/10 night. Would absolutely go back. (5 stars)

The food was outstanding, and this has been one of the best dining experiences I’ve had in NYC so far. The chef and staff are clearly passionate and highly professional, and every dish was exceptional. They serve unique and hard to find items that truly set this place apart in New York. I enjoyed every moment of the experience and will definitely be back. Great job to the entire team! (5 stars)

We has a warm and heartfelt evening here. Aki was our grill master! Super delicious, juicy and flavorful chicken dishes made with care and precision. Simple but really beautiful food with high quality ingredients. Definitely will be coming back with family next time :) (5 stars)

bio_text: Torrisi is a distinguished Italian restaurant located in the iconic Puck Building in Nolita, New York City. With its elegant interior featuring vaulted ceilings and remarkable artwork, Torrisi offers a refined dining experience that pays homage to the rich culinary history of New York. The restaurant's atmosphere is sophisticated yet inviting, making it a premier destination for both locals and visitors seeking an exceptional meal. Torrisi specializes in Italian cuisine with an à la carte menu that emphasizes high-quality ingredients and creative execution. The menu features classic dishes alongside nightly specials, showcasing a unique blend of Italian-American influences and nods to diverse culinary traditions found in New York City.
menu_items: Our Giardiniera - $22
Cucumbers New Yorkese - $20
Sicilian Tuna - $30
Fennel and Grapefruit Cocktail - $25
Insalata Testarossa - $28
Charred Pizza Dough with Clams - $20
review_snippets: Amazing experience and delicious food! We were lucky to walk in last week, grab seats at the bar without a reservation, and had no wait at all. Our bartender gave us excellent recommendations. The New York–style cucumbers were refreshing. The pasta was outstanding. The chicken was good, and the mushroom sauce was delicious, but I wish it had been served on top rather than underneath as it didn’t quite coat the chicken as well as it could have. The date cake and affogato were both fantastic and the perfect way to end the meal. (4 stars)

Tonight we had our first experience at Torrisi Restaurant, and it was absolutely unforgettable. It was my friend’s birthday, and the entire evening felt so special. Mark took wonderful care of us — his recommendations were spot on and truly elevated our dining experience. Every dish was exceptional. Torrisi gave us a completely unique and memorable culinary experience. Thank you to the whole team, and especially to Mark! (5 stars)

I’ve been wanting to try this for so long and they definitely delivered. I’m so impressed. The inside is gorgeous and the bar is incredible. I got the ham appetizer and it was a fun way to eat. The tortellini is probably the best I’ve ever had. It just melts in your mouth (5 stars)

Best of the best in New York City. Impressive crowd, understanding service and a charm to be there. Be thoughtful on what to order, flavors are numerous and choices have to be made well. Out of the larger glamorous restaurants in the city this one did impress. Only small issue is how there are only two bathrooms, otherwise its amazing. (5 stars)

bio_text: Trattoria Tra di Noi is a charming Italian eatery located on Arthur Avenue in the Bronx, offering a warm and inviting atmosphere that feels like a slice of Tuscany. This family-run trattoria prides itself on serving authentic Italian cuisine with a seafood twist, ensuring that every dish is crafted with love and care. With a focus on exceptional service and a BYOB policy, Tra di Noi creates a memorable dining experience for foodies, families, and couples alike. The restaurant specializes in authentic Italian cuisine, particularly seafood dishes. The menu features regional specialties such as lasagna bolognese, shrimp francese, and artichoke ravioli, showcasing traditional cooking techniques and fresh ingredients.
menu_items: Calamari Fritti - $10.95
Mussels Marechiaro - $10.95
Vongole Posillipo - baby clams in a light tomato sauce - $9.85
Clams Oreganate - $8.95
Mozzarella Ala Caprese - $9.95
Antipasto Freddo - $11.95
review_snippets: We go down to Arthur Ave for dinner from time to time and always like to try a new place. Tonight we decided on Tra Di Noi. It's on 187th street around the corner from Arthur Ave. The restaurant is small and cozy and has the old school Italian restaurant red checkered table cloths. We were greeted warmly by the hostess and seated at table against the wall in the dining Area. The table had salt, pepper, bread dishes, utensil set ups with a napkin and an olive oil bottle. A waiter came over and explained the specials to us and took out drink order. The waiter then brought us bread and water to start. They only have beer and wine and I asked for a non alcoholic beer but they don't serve it. The menu is small but has something for everyone and the specials more than make up for the smaller size menu. We ordered fried calamari and a mussels special for the appetizers. The calamari was ok. It was fried a little harder then I like but it was a nice size for 2 people and came with tubes and baby octopus. The Marinara with it was a little bland for my taste. The mussels in white wine appetizer was fantastic and a great portion. For the entree we had an order of the pork chop with vinegar peppers specials and a rigatoni special. Both entrees were delicious and they came with a small plate of fingerling potatoes and string beans that were nicely sauteed with garlic and oil. We split a piece of homemade Italian cheesecake and I had an espresso and both were absolutely delicious. The staff was friendly and knowledgeable and attentive. The waiter came by and offered us more bread which a lot of places dont do. This is a real Italian restaurant owned and operated by real Italians which is something that is hard to come by these days in the Italian restaurant business. The food is as close to homemade as you can get. It's not mass produced so you are not going to get heaping portions like you may get in other places but what you do get is a dish that is crafted with care to be as authentic as possible. The restaurant is quiant and cozy and is staffed by friendly people. We left the restaurant happy and you will as well. (5 stars)

Delicious and totally legit – I could eat here every day. The waitstaff are extremely attentive and knowledgeable. The old-school tablecloths and classic tunes create the perfect nostalgic vibe. Easy to hold a conversation, and overall a great experience every time. Whether you’re popping in for a quick lunch or kicking back for a chill dinner, Tra Di Noi always hits the spot. Totally worth it. (5 stars)

Phenomenal, Exquisite, Delicous. The best Veal Limon I have experienced. Traditional home-cooking style meals. Quick service. Quaint but sophisticated. Very friendly staff. 10/10 reccomend this hidden gem. (5 stars)

We had an excellent lunch here, having found our way from the Botanical Garden’s orchid show (Mr Flower Fantastic this year.) We were given a lovely table by the window, and everything that followed was perfect—attentive waiter, interesting specials, good food. (5 stars)

bio_text: Tsukimi is a refined dining establishment located in the vibrant East Village, specializing in a modern interpretation of kaiseki, a traditional multi-course Japanese dinner. The name Tsukimi, meaning 'moon viewing', reflects the restaurant's dedication to celebrating seasonal ingredients and the beauty of nature, particularly during the mid-autumn harvest festival. With an intimate setting of only 12 seats, guests are invited to experience a thoughtfully curated tasting menu that evolves with the seasons, complemented by a selection of premium beverages. The restaurant focuses on kaiseki cuisine, offering a seasonal tasting menu that showcases the artistry of Japanese culinary traditions. Signature techniques include meticulous ingredient selection and presentation, with an emphasis on fresh, high-quality components. The dining experience is enhanced by an optional sake and wine pairing curated by a passionate beverage team. Chef Takanori Akiyama leads the culinary team at Tsukimi, bringing expertise and creativity to the modern kaiseki experience.
menu_items: Takenoko
Hotaru Ika
Awabi - Rice
Shiitake - Dashi
Kaluga Caviar - Uni, Oyster, Nori
Shirauo - Shungiku, Asari, Udo, Snow Pea
review_snippets: Tsukimi is one of the most memorable dining experiences in NYC. The atmosphere is intimate and elegant, and every course is beautifully presented and thoughtfully paced. The seasonal ingredients truly shine, especially the pristine sashimi and refined warm dishes. Exceptional food, warm hospitality, and flawless execution. Absolutely worth it. (5 stars)

A top notch kaiseki in NYC. Every detail here is perfection. The chef showcases extraordinary technique and artistry, curating seasonal courses that feel both authentic and inventive. Service is impeccable—professional yet genuinely welcoming—and the extensive sake menu elevates the experience even further. I look forward to returning each season to savor the evolving menu. (5 stars)

Lovely kaiseki spot with a good range of high quality dishes. Service is attentive and intimate, while the space feels like you’re walking into someone’s very nice home. Loved all the dishes especially the truffle rice and Wagyu rolls. Well paced as well. (5 stars)

Fourth or fifth time here. My favorite dish and the highlight tonight was the persimmon soufflé with cashew ice cream. In the past I’ve had banana soufflé which was also out of this world. My first time here I had the dry-aged slow-cooked low-charcoal-fired duck. Tonight they had the same, but it was not dry-aged long enough, and not slow-cooked long enough over the charcoal fire. The meat was a bit wet and did not have a “snap” to it as the first time, nor was the skin crispy enough like the first time. Also, another slight mishap tonight was a bone in one of my fish dish. Not a big deal to me, but to others it may be. I wish them good luck and hope they will earn an additional Michelin Star next year. (4 stars)

bio_text: Tuome is a Michelin-starred restaurant located in the East Village of New York City, offering a unique blend of contemporary American cuisine infused with Asian influences. The restaurant embodies a warm and inviting atmosphere, reflecting Chef Thomas Chen's culinary journey and cultural heritage, making it a celebrated destination for both locals and visitors seeking an exceptional dining experience. Tuome focuses on ingredient-driven fusion cuisine that combines classical techniques with Asian flavors. The menu features a variety of dishes that highlight Chef Chen's first-generation Chinese-American roots, showcasing a harmonious blend of tastes and textures. Chef Thomas Chen opened Tuome in 2014 after transitioning from a career in accounting to pursue his passion for cooking, having trained at the renowned Eleven Madison Park.

review_snippets: Overall the food was amazing!! We got the snow crab pasta, chicken liver appetizer, kabocha squash appetizer, and the beignet dessert. Honestly I love all of them and they all came in huge portion. We went during NYC restaurant week so we got a lot of food for a great deal. Quite cute interior, but the space was a bit tiny. Please keep in mind that they do not take apple pay 😭. Make sure you have either cash or physical card to pay (the nearest atm is 15 minutes away) (3 stars)

Andy came to our table and really made sure we were enjoying our meal which I appreciate. We came for restaurant week and I really appreciate that they put their best dishes on the menu. I would love to come back again and try more from the menu. The deviled eggs were some of best I’ve ever had, it was so interesting that they were crispy. I loved the snow crab and the chocolate mouse was so good. The inside is so cozy as well (5 stars)

Great vibes and very cozy atmosphere. I went on a snowy day, which made the experience even more perfect. The server was very kind and gave great recommendations. The food was excellent. I loved the scallop with foie gras. For mains, I had the snow crab and chicken. The snow crab came with al dente noodles in a creamy sauce topped with crab, and the chicken was served two ways - grilled and fried. I highly recommend this place for a date night or a special occasion. (5 stars)

Came during restaurant week. They got a time limit and seats are very tight. Food is pretty good and creative, taste great. The only personally think it’s ordinary is the chocolate dessert. The restaurant toilet is clean and cozy. But doesn’t make it a Michelin star grade restaurant. Maybe it comes with the old buildings in that area. The sink feel like the ones you use on a flight. (5 stars)

bio_text: Ulivo is a sophisticated Italian restaurant that emphasizes the use of high-quality olive oil as the cornerstone of its culinary offerings. Launched in 2016 by Fabio Camardi and Chef Emanuel Concas, Ulivo aims to elevate the dining experience by sourcing the finest Italian ingredients, including exceptional olive oils, cheeses, and cured meats. The restaurant fosters a unique atmosphere where culinary experimentation and customer interaction are paramount, ensuring a dynamic and engaging dining experience. Ulivo specializes in authentic Italian cuisine, focusing on the use of premium olive oils and artisanal cheeses. The menu features a variety of handmade pasta, crafted using professional machines imported from Italy. Signature techniques include the use of bronze dies for pasta extrusion, enhancing the texture and flavor of each dish. bio_text: Una Pizza Napoletana, located in New York's Lower East Side, offers an intimate dining experience centered around the artistry of Neapolitan-style pizza. The restaurant features a unique ambiance adorned with one-of-a-kind art pieces, where guests can observe Chef Anthony Mangieri skillfully handcrafting pizzas in a wood-fired oven. With a commitment to quality and detail, Una Pizza Napoletana has earned accolades as the #1 pizzeria in the world by 50 Top Pizza for multiple years and has been recognized by prominent media outlets. The culinary focus is on naturally-leavened, wood-fired pizzas, complemented by a selection of appetizers, made-daily ice cream, and seasonal sorbetto. The menu emphasizes high-quality ingredients and traditional techniques, with a limited number of pizzas baked at a time to ensure perfection. Anthony Mangieri, a pioneer of Neapolitan-style pizza in the United States, opened the first Una Pizza Napoletana in 1996. After several relocations, the restaurant returned to New York's Lower East Side in 2022, following a significant transformation of the space.
review_snippets: It did live up to the hype. Reservations are very tricky since they are open 3 days a week but we got it. Low key ambiance. Great service. And out of the world pizza since their all ingredients are either from Italy or locally sourced. I had high expectations since they are one of the best pizzas in the city and USA. Wait for the pizza was bit long. And they have limit that you can order one pizza per person so I guess no togo orders since they make limited dough. These small things do create inconvenience for customers but I resonate with their unique identity so I don’t mind it. We orders Bianca with spicy peppers and pepperoni topped margarita. They have tomato cans places along the wall as decor which is cute. It’s definitely once in the lifetime experience since the tricky reservations. (5 stars)

Overall a great experience. Reservation: hard to snag a spot but I got lucky in booking at 9 am two weeks before. Can do a walk in for 1-2 people and ask for bar seating if you're willing to to wait Drink: I had the Italian cola and highly recommend it. It's refreshing Pizza: I had the Margherita with extra topping of peppers (gives a nice kick to it). The pizza itself was incredibly well made. Minor criticism is that it does not come sliced. Also, it can be challenging to eat since the middle of the pie is thin and the sauce can be a bit watery. This is just how they make it. Taste wise incredible and filling Dessert: this was the highlight of my night. The cremolata is made fresh by Chef Anthony every morning. It was absolutely fabulous. I can't recommend it enough Staff: they are extremely polite and courteous. They want you to have the best experience and are always willing to share their suggestions Price: $75 pp with tax and tip (5 stars)

Long review short, this alone was worth going to NYC for. Definitely get a reservation before you come. I don’t have any experience with not getting a reservation, this was my first time, but from what I heard if you don’t get a reservation, you might not get in. I got a reservation for October 30, 2025 at 5 o’clock. Reservations were sold out so soon after (less than two minutes, as I heard before. So be prepared!). I heard this is ranked the world’s best, and couldn’t wait to see if that was true. I had authentic New York style pizza, deep dish pizza, and made pizzas in a pizza oven myself before. We live about 3.5 hours away from NYC, and I love coming. This time, this pizza was 75% of what I was coming for! We spent all day there, and arrived at Una Pizza at around 4:47. At 5 o’clock, they opened and we were given a seat as close to the oven/kitchen as possible! I was pleasantly surprised by that and enjoyed the hour and a few minutes we had to wait for our food. We tried both of their Italian soft drinks. For our pizzas, we got a Bianca and two margarita pizzas. I came here, definitely expecting a different style and flavor profile compared to other pizzas I tried. I knew what it might taste like, but was still extremely amazed by the flavor of the high-quality ingredients they use. I usually like meat on my pizzas, but this pizza was no doubt the best pizza I ever had. Both were so good. I don’t think I could pick a favorite! One pizza is enough as long as you get maybe an appetizer and/or a dessert. I got the almond cremolata. I don’t care for almonds that much, but they weren’t overpowering and that was really good! It’s a decent size of ice cream, but I would prefer more, maybe 25 to 50% more, especially for that price. That’s just a preference of portion, not something that disappoints me or gives it less stars in my review. Our service was great. The food was great. And I have no complaints about the difficulty of getting a reservation, because now I understand why it’s difficult: There’s demand — because it’s the best in the world. Good job, Una, and thanks! (5 stars)

100/10 in all aspects. Gus and Mako made the night so special and unforgettable with their hospitality. Best pizza in the world? Absolutely. Best service? Absolutely. It’s hard to get a reservation for a reason. Definitely a once in a lifetime experience, but I can’t imagine never being able to experience this again! (5 stars)

bio_text: Untable is a cozy dining destination in Carroll Gardens, Brooklyn, specializing in unconventional Thai cuisine. The restaurant offers a welcoming atmosphere where guests can enjoy innovative dishes crafted by Chef Un, making it an ideal spot for sharing meals with family and friends. Untable focuses on unconventional Thai foods, presenting a menu that features unique interpretations of traditional dishes. The dining experience is designed for both on-site enjoyment and takeout, allowing guests to savor the creativity of Chef Un's culinary artistry. Chef Un lets his creativity run wild, whipping up Thai dishes you've never seen before.
menu_items: Gaeng Som - Hot and Sour soup with pan-seared chilean sea bass, lotus roots, pineapple and long beans - $19
Evergreen Rolls - Kale | Carrot | Taro | Sweet Potato and Corn wrapped with rice paper served with Vegan black truffle mayo - $15
Crab Croquette - Breaded Crab Meat with Tom Yum Purée topped with crispy lemongrass - $19
Vegan Shrimp Skewers - Plant-based Shrimp with Vinaigrette sauce - $15
OKRA - Sautéed Okra topped with fried garlic - $15
Impossible® Rolls - Plant-based Impossible® meat with spicy herbs wrapped with rice paper served with Vegan black truffle mayo - $15
review_snippets: Already decided to come back with friends. Dinner for 2. We had the crab fried rice, the crab croquettes, and the branzino. I had the Mean Girl to drink. Everything was fantastic. Especially liked the spicy sauce on the crab fried rice and how it was easy to add your own heat level to the dish since we were sharing courses. Dined in on 12.04, Waitress was really sweet and attentive. We were late for our resy and she still sat us quickly which was so appreciated. (5 stars)

We had dinner here as a party of four. The interior was quite nice and had a pleasant atmosphere, but unfortunately, the food didn’t live up to the setting. We ordered two appetizers and four main dishes, and none of us left feeling satisfied. The portions were small, and overall the dishes were very average—nothing particularly flavorful or memorable. The only dish worth recommending would be the Khao Soi, which stood out as the highlight of the evening. Otherwise, the experience was rather disappointing for the price and expectations. (3 stars)

My partner and I had our wedding dinner here. Before deciding on this venue, we had dined here a couple of times. We were always impressed by the food but were deciding between other restaurants. We were already engaged but I wanted to surprise my partner with her own ring and propose during our visit, and in the end, the staff’s warmth and willingness to make it a special moment sealed the deal. For our wedding, we chose Beef Khao Soi and Veggie Duck Dry Green Curry as our main dishes, with Yum Samgler, Crab Croquette, and Evergreen Roll as appetizers. Almost all of our guests said they’d return again! The restaurant supported us throughout every step of the planning process. I would also like to sincerely thank the team — Jessie, Meen, and two members of the kitchen team whose names I unfortunately don’t remember — for their kindness, warm support, and constant smiles. I wholeheartedly recommend everyone to come here. (5 stars)

Came on a Friday night to celebrate my birthday and managed to get a seat at the bar w/o a reservation. I got the midnight train to Georgia which was like an old fashioned and my husband got the I’m walking on sunshine. Both were true to their descriptions. My husband’s was slightly sweeter, but more citrusy and interesting in flavor. Both were enjoyable! For appetizers we got the seasonal Thai pancake which was a slurry of pork and veg on a fried thin pancake, kind of reminding me of a giant nacho. We also got the baby corn fritters. The fritters came with a sauce that I could drink out of the plate, it was that delicious. Both appetizers knocked it out of the park. The entree is where I felt a twinge of disappointment. I was unsure of what to get, I told the waiter I liked spice but didn’t want to cry into my food. He recommended the crab fried rice which had a spicy sauce on the side. There was no chili pepper next to the dish to give it a heat level. He steered me away from another option which had 4 chili peppers next to it, telling me “it’s gonna be too spicy.” Sometimes I don’t understand why Thai restaurants offer spicy options but feel the need to gatekeep what they think you can tolerate. After trying the crab fried rice, it was good, but not exactly what I was looking for. I really came ready to feel the heat, but this was a dish I felt like I could have ordered at any Thai restaurant without a Michelin star. The “spicy” sauce on the side was sweet/sour, delicious, but without a twinge of heat. I regret not ordering something spicier or even being brave and ordering the “what the hell?!!!! fried rice” Dessert is where they really lost me - I ordered the truffle honey ice cream pie. Maybe this is on me; but I assumed the truffle flavor would be chocolate truffle. Or if it was the earthy dirty pig truffle, that it would be just a whisper of the odious flavor. I was wrong. First of all, the pie was inedible because it was more structurally similar to a block of ice than ice cream. They served it with a spoon. I think I’d be more successful carving out a bite if it was served with a knife or an ice pick. By the time I managed to sever off a piece, I was taken aback by the pungent truffle flavor. I felt like I was eating icy dirt. Thankfully they took it off the bill. Overall, id come back for the drinks and some appetizers, and maybe to be steered more in the right direction regarding spice. There is a wide spectrum of spice tolerance, and I’d like to think I can handle it! That being said, staff were incredibly polite and friendly! Service was stellar. (3 stars)

bio_text: Upland is a sophisticated brasserie that embodies a California-inspired culinary philosophy, harmonizing rustic charm with a global perspective. The restaurant features a dynamic yet intimate atmosphere, characterized by handsome natural wood and lush leather, creating a welcoming environment for diners. With an open kitchen that showcases the artistry of its culinary team, Upland offers a thoughtfully crafted menu that highlights seasonal American dishes, wood-fired pizzas, and house-made pastas, all complemented by a curated wine list. Upland focuses on seasonal American cuisine with a California influence, offering a diverse menu that includes wood-fired pizzas and house-made pastas. The dining experience is enhanced by a food-friendly wine list and a selection of smart by-the-glass options.
menu_items: Clam & Lardo - pickled fresno pepper, mascarpone and roasted garlic - $29
Margherita - mozzarella, passata, basil and espelette - $22
‘Nduja Margherita - mozzarella, passata, basil and espelette - $25
Vodka - spicy soppressata and confit cherry tomatoes - $24
Sausage & Kale - young pecorino, stracciatella and parmigiano - $26
Limone - meyer lemon, scamorza, aleppo and wild arugula - $22
review_snippets: First time here and WOW. The server, Joel was super attentive and nice, I think my water was refilled 9 times, new plates/silverware with each course, very impressed with the service. The food was outstanding, starting with the complimentary bread, so soft and amazing butter. Then the burrata, margarita pizza, cacio &peppe and rigatoni for our table, all so tasty and you can tell it’s made with fresh ingredients and homemade pasta! We didn’t leave a crumb behind. We got the olive oil cake too and they put a candle in it for my bday. To top it off, the atmosphere was intimate with lovely booths yet lively! Can’t wait to return! (5 stars)

We were so excited to try this restaurant after seeing its aesthetic interior on our Instagram feed. The food was just as good and the flavors of each dish were really well-balanced. We tried the pappardelle and the salmon. ALSO there's free bread. It was the fluffiest ever and we devoured the loaf. I was surprised that the miso caramel cheesecake had a thick drizzle of caramel but was somehow not too sweet, and the olive oil cake was also amazing. (5 stars)

I went here for dessert because I couldn’t get in at dinner time. We were 4 people, and the service was very friendly and attentive. The dessert was both excellent and exactly what we needed after a long, rainy day walking around NYC. We got the following: Cheesecake, Limoncello Olive Oil Cake, Affogato, and Decaf Cappuccino. Highly recommend for a post-dinner treat. (5 stars)

Busy active Resturant with mix of regular dinners and business lunch crowd. Buzzing but still comfortable level to talk. Food came out in a timely manner, staff was very accommodating and attentive. Group of 7 and we all truly enjoyed our lunch. Will be back! (5 stars)

I was surprised that the miso caramel cheesecake had a thick drizzle of caramel but was somehow not too sweet, and the olive oil cake was also amazing. (5 stars) I went here for dessert because I couldn’t get in at dinner time. We were 4 people, and the service was very friendly and attentive. The dessert was both excellent and exactly what we needed after a long, rainy day walking around NYC. We got the following: Cheesecake, Limoncello Olive Oil Cake, Affogato, and Decaf Cappuccino. Highly recommend for a post-dinner treat. (5 stars) Busy active Resturant with mix of regular dinners and business lunch crowd. Buzzing but still comfortable level to talk. Food came out in a timely manner, staff was very accommodating and attentive. Group of 7 and we all truly enjoyed our lunch. Will be back! (5 stars)

bio_text: Uzuki is a premier dining destination in Greenpoint, specializing in the art of Soba noodles. The restaurant offers a unique experience that combines exceptional craftsmanship with a deep appreciation for the nutritional benefits of 100% buckwheat noodles. Guests are invited to indulge in a menu that not only nourishes the body and soul but also educates them about the life-sustaining properties of Soba. Uzuki focuses on traditional Soba cuisine, emphasizing the use of 100% buckwheat in their noodle preparation. The menu features a variety of Soba dishes that highlight the health benefits and rich flavors of this ancient staple. Signature techniques include hand-making the noodles to ensure the highest quality and authenticity. Shuichi Kotani, the chef, has a notable background, having worked at Edo Soba Hosokawa in Tokyo, which has received a Michelin 1-Star rating. He is also recognized as a Goodwill Ambassador of the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries of Japan.
menu_items: Buckwheat Kanten Jelly
Soba Ice Cream
Matcha Madeleine
Soba Chocolate Cake
Uni Sushi
Tuna Sushi
review_snippets: All the soba tofu dishes were pretty good- I think those were the highlights of the meal. There was a soba tofu appetizer as well as a soba tofu (branded as mochi) dessert. Can skip soba sushi (we got yellowtail), got the duck (3 ways) shio and the black truffle curry - I think the duck shio is more classic and black truffle curry was more adventurous? I liked the classic broth better but…. Black truffle curry was def more unique. Their cucumber wasabi was great! Pricy meal though. (4 stars)

I was invited there and liked the decors right away. Japanese style drapes at the entrance, very nice arrangements and rooms. This is a soba focused place and I had the duck and Uni (with a touch of truffle) cold soba dish and it was exceptional! Balanced, flavorful, exceptionally clean taste. BTW, buckwheat (soba noodles base) are gluten free. The waitress then told us that the pottery (bowls and tea cup) were all made locally by the chef, making each dish served in a unique manner. I HAD TO see it and ... went on the back. The chef was very kind and explained a bit - of course I expressed that I was delighted. Frankly never went to a place where the food was so good, the decor so unique and the dishes hand made by the chef as well. My overall assessment is that this is a must-go place really (I had such a good vibe). (5 stars)

an awesome dining experience!! every detail here rlly makes my time so worthwhile. very spacious dining area with the friendliest staff. decoration was so amazing every corner looks extraordinary for photos. we got the duck shio soba, salmon ikuri soba, unagi & duck stamina soba, which were all very good. it came in huge portion and very pretty bowls (which i think the handmade them in the backroom??) oh and the monk mocktail was so delicious too!! yuzu soda was a little sour though amazing spot for any family and intimate occasions !! (5 stars)

The place really makes you feel as though you have been transported to Japan with its calm presence. We were able to walk in without having reservations. There is a small lounge and bar area when you walk in plus two separate eating areas and a private room in the back. We ordered two dishes to share: one hot/ one cold. They were both delicious and different enough from one another. The authentic soba noodles are made in house. The cold Salmon Ikura Soba with the sweet dashi was my preference. The Duck Shio Soba was served hot and came with 3 different preparations of duck. The two entree bowls were more than enough food, we could have easily shared one. Presentation is well thought out with the fresh ingredients being strategically placed for viewing. The food is presented in these gorgeous works of art one of a kind dishes that the owner/chef makes there. They are available for sale along with other pieces of his in the back of the restaurant. Our waitress was so informative and attentive. She really guided us on what to have. I can't wait to go back and try something else. (5 stars)

bio_text: Veerays, NYC's first Indian speakeasy restaurant, offers a unique dining experience that combines the charm of the Prohibition era with the rich flavors of Indian cuisine. Under the guidance of Michelin-starred Chef Hemant Mathur, the restaurant presents a menu that features regional classics, exotic grills, and modern interpretations of traditional dishes, all set in an ambiance that exudes old-world elegance and sophistication. Veerays specializes in Indian cuisine, showcasing a menu that includes regional classics and innovative twists. The dining format emphasizes a blend of traditional and contemporary techniques, with a focus on exotic grills and signature cocktails inspired by the 1920s. Veerays is the latest venture of Chef Hemant Mathur, the first Indian chef in the U.S. to earn a Michelin star. This marks his fifth restaurant in the New York/CT area and the third in New York City, reflecting his dedication to elevating Indian culinary arts.
menu_items: JACKFRUIT CUTLET - Jackfruit & potato cutlets spiced to the nines and pan-fried until golden. - $35
THE CLASSIC CHAAT - A lively medley of aloo tikki, chopped onion & tomatoes, tangy chutneys, and spiced yogurt. - $35
CAULIFLOWER TANGO - Crispy cauliflower florets in a bold garlic-infused tomato sauce. - $35
GATSBY KEBAB - Tandoor-grilled, tamarind and basil-spiced chicken kebabs. - $35
VINTAGE RAJASTHANI SULE - Lamb marinated with passionately fiery red chillies, sense tickling spices, and hung yogurt. - $35
ANGLO TUNA CAKES - Spiced tuna & potato cakes served with homemade relish. - $35
review_snippets: Came for restaurant week and ordered their 3 course option. For starters I had the anarkali chicken. It was pretty good and had a good marinade. My main was a salmon curry which I thought was fine, I didn’t feel it stood out. For dessert I had the mango panna cotta which was also very good and very similar to a mango lassi flavor. The inside is a small space but decorated well and very intimate. Overall I didn’t feel anything stood out to me but it was a decent meal (3 stars)

came here for restaurant week and the food was delicious. everything was flavorful without being too heavy or rich. i enjoyed the beet carrot kofta the most. staff is also very friendly. portions are a bit small though for the price which i guess is expected with fine dining- would recommend for food not drinks and i wouldn’t expect to get stuffed from the food here lol. service is also very fast and we got a complimentary little cup of dal! (4 stars)

You can immediately feel the hospitality from their team here, and it’s the perfect cherry on top to compliment the great food. The lamb chops were unbelievably tender and succulent. The goat bhuna gosht was flavorful and paired perfectly with garlic naan. To close it out, we got their guava cheesecake that was fresh and not too sweet, that’s great even for someone who’s not the biggest dessert fan. (5 stars)

Warm, modern, and intimate restaurant that has a creative take on Indian cuisine. Upon entry, we were greeted welcomingly. You’d notice the decor immediately—stunning and attention to detail from top to bottom! The menu had so much to choose from and the servers were extremely helpful with explaining the differences. But the star of the show has to be the presentation of the food and the flavorful sauces. Worth the city prices. Would definitely come back for another special occasion! (5 stars)

bio_text: Vert Frais brings the essence of Japanese comfort and culinary tradition to Long Island City, focusing on quality ingredients and thoughtful presentation. The restaurant's serene atmosphere, enhanced by botanical decor, creates a memorable dining experience that balances taste and aesthetics. The menu features a harmonious blend of classic Japanese flavors and modern techniques, offering dishes such as airy matcha soufflé pancakes and refined yoshoku cuisine. The selection reflects both traditional craftsmanship and contemporary flair.
menu_items: FRENCH FRIES - Parmesan Cheese, Parsley - $7.00 / $12.00
SALMON SASHIMI - $18.00
CHICKEN KARAAGE - Japanese Deep Fried Chicken with Fried Garlic - $9.00 / $16.00
EDAMAME - Choice of Salt or Ume Basil Seasoning - $8.00
CAESAR SALAD - Romaine Lettuce, Bacon, Poached Egg, Parmesan Cheese, Croutons - $18.00
BEET SALAD - Beetroot, Orange, Balsamic Vinaigrette - $13.00
review_snippets: Inspired by both classic Japanese flavors and modern techniques, Vert Frais brings the essence of Japanese comfort and culinary tradition to LIC. This restaurant offers a wide variety of drinks and dishes that reflects a harmonious blend of traditional craftsmanship and contemporary flair. Vert Frais offers popular delicious Japanese dishes such as Omurice, Hamburg Steak, and Souffle Pancake. While my friends and I didn't have the chance to try the Souffle Pancake, we were able to try the Omurice and Hamburg Steak. The Omurice was perfect, a nice blend of flavor between the rice and egg and ketchup. The ketchup added a good depth without overwhelming either the egg or rice. The Hamburg Steak was cooked perfectly, letting the knife cut right through. The demi-glace sauce was also beautifully made to balance the flavor. I highly recommend ordering a drink from here to. All of their drinks are aesthetically pleasing and definitely photogenic! A note of advice: mix the drink very well! You have to make sure the drink gets fully mixed otherwise it may taste overly sweet. It was like that for the Lavender Lemonade, Berry Bliss, and Blue Moon Latte. All tasted sweet despite the "mixing", but after mixing much more thoroughly, it becomes a nice blend where you can taste all the flavor. (4 stars)

We had the following Omurice - it was tasty and was a lot of food for one person so you share this for sure. Karaage (not pictured) - very well Seasoned and tasty as well. Katsu Don - great taste and tender meat as well. Matcha pancake - just the perfect amount of sweet. And very fluffy as well (5 stars)

Vert Frais in Long Island City is such a cozy find. It perfectly blends Japanese-inspired flavors with that relaxed New York café feel. I tried the Lavender Latte, Rose Latte, and their signature Vert Frais Matcha Souffle Pancake—light, airy, and full of flavor. The Ramen + Salmon Ikura Bowl was comfort in a bowl, and finishing with both the affogato and matcha affogato was the best decision. Everything tasted fresh and thoughtfully prepared, and the space had a calm, welcoming vibe that made me want to stay longer. If you’re looking for a brunch or dessert spot in Long Island City, Vert Frais deserves a spot on your list. (5 stars)

Japanese inspired brunch restaurant with beautiful hanging plants for a romantic yet casual environment. We came for dinner, and enjoyed the katsu don and omurice, which was flavorful and delicious. I don’t recommend quinoa salad, because it tasted bad. The entire restaurant is small, and the tables are quite close together, typical for NYC. The tables are quite (4 stars)

bio_text: Via Carota is a charming osteria located in the West Village, created by celebrated chefs Rita Sodi and Jody Williams. The restaurant embodies a spirit of relaxed care and warmth, offering a simple, seasonal menu that reflects the essence of home-cooked Italian cuisine. With an inviting interior adorned with heirloom keepsakes and a lovely terrazza for outdoor dining, Via Carota provides a welcoming atmosphere for leisurely lunches, family dinners, or late-night drinks. The culinary focus at Via Carota is on authentic Italian cuisine, emphasizing seasonal ingredients and traditional cooking methods. The menu features a variety of dishes, including grilled octopus and fried rabbit, presented in a way that tells a story. The dining experience is designed to be casual and continuous, in true osteria fashion. Via Carota was inspired by a 17th-century villa in the hills near Florence, which chef Rita Sodi once called home. The restaurant earned Sodi and Williams the James Beard Award for Best Chefs, New York City, in 2019.
menu_items: Olive all'Ascolana - fried green olives with pork sausage - $17
'Nduja Arancini - rice & spicy pork fritters - $23
Cibreo Toscano - chopped chicken livers & lemon - $18
Acciughe e Burro - cultured butter & salted anchovies - $20
Burrata - wilted bitter greens - $25
Bagna Cauda - winter caciocavallo & anchovy garlic bath - $20
review_snippets: We had been wanting to go to Via Carota for a long time and could never get a reservation. We decided to put our name down and were given a table in 45 minutes — worth every single minute of the wait. Absolutely sublime food. You can truly tell how much care goes into everything they do. The fresh egg pastas are outstanding, the salad was spectacular, and the bruschetta with house-made bread was incredible. Everything was flawless. The space is super cozy and beautiful, and the service was a solid 10/10. The egg tagliatelle with prosciutto was one of the best pasta dishes I’ve ever had in my life. That butter… simply wow. No words. 10/10 — we will definitely be back. 🍝✨ (5 stars)

We had a very memorable dinner here. The ambience is surprisingly calm and non pretentious. Had to wait for 20 mins on a Thursday night which was fine because there was excellent jazz being played next door at Arthur’s which you could enjoy. Folks in the restaurant were nicest. We ordered the specials pasta and bruschetta. Everything we had was just excellent. One of those places which makes west village special 💝 (5 stars)

Excellent classic Italian. Heard a lot about Via Carota and Chef Jody Williams, and when it was recognized by North America’s Best 50 last year, I finally decided to give it a try. We came for a weekday lunch and were seated without a wait at the communal table in the back. Still thoughtfully spaced, with an empty seat between groups. Given Chef Williams’s background, the menu was a mix of Tuscan and Roman. Territory I’m fairly familiar with coming from Boston. We ordered a few classics like the grilled artichoke, cacio e pepe, and potato ravioli ragu (daily special). Portions were a bit small for the price, but the execution was flawless. One thing we really loved was their iconic cacio e pepe. Most trattorias I’ve been to rely on dried pasta for a firmer al dente bite, but Chef Williams used fresh pasta across the menu. And it worked beautifully here. Silky and supple, yet still retaining a satisfying snap. More importantly, the sauce had a bold, unapologetic pepperiness that I’ve never felt before from other trattorias in the U.S. Perhaps Via Carota might not be a place people chase for excitement, but it’s the kind of restaurant I’d regularly visit if it was in my neighborhood. Highly recommend giving them a try for comforting, well-executed Italian classics. (5 stars)

We had been eager to visit Via Carota for quite some time—especially as it is said that Taylor Swift may have dined here before. On December 23, we decided to stop by at lunchtime on a whim, hoping to get a table, as reservations were already fully booked. Luckily, we were offered seats at the bar. From the moment we entered, we were struck by the restaurant’s authentic and cozy atmosphere. During our enjoyable 1.5-hour stay, we had the pleasure of tasting several delicious dishes, some of which were recommended by our server. The service—primarily provided by the gentleman behind the bar—was genuine, friendly, efficient, and perfectly suited to the character of this place. We enjoyed every single dish and treated ourselves to a Spagliato as well. The price-to-quality ratio felt right to us. While it was on the pricier side for lunch, we are true food lovers and are more than happy to spend money on high-quality ingredients and excellent cuisine. We can wholeheartedly recommend this restaurant. Thank you for a warm, delicious, and memorable lunch! (5 stars)

review_snippets: More of a 3.5 because the service and atmosphere were great but the food didn’t land. I was expecting a little more creative because I love Indonesian The star of the show was the Pandan passion fruit custard… honestly would not go back for the food, but would come back for the dessert. The lobster noodles and corn fritters were good, the tenderloin was okay but the Indonesian flavors fell flat, same for the escargo which was a miss. All in the portions are quite small and unimpressive for the price, you’re definitely going more for the vibes. (3 stars)

A sleek spot with a compact menu of contemporary Indonesian-inspired dishes. While the food was enjoyable, the flavors didn’t fully land, with more emphasis on presentation and vibe than authenticity. The satay skewers were on the smaller side for the price - the chicken was nicely nutty and the scallop tasted fresh, though the lamb leaned a bit dry. The hamachi tartare had a fun crunch from the crispy rice, and the octopus was a clear highlight with a great char and tender texture. The lobster noodles were flavorful and peppery, though the use of lobster felt more like a gimmicky twist than something essential to the dish. Overall, it’s a stylish spot with thoughtfully prepared plates, but the flavors leaned more refined and fusion than hearty or inventive. (3 stars)

I am late making this review. I visited Wayan back in December 2024 with a group of friends and the atmosphere was awesome, lively but still perfect to not be shouting over each other. The food was good and tasty, the veggies were bright, ordered the mango salad twice because it was that good, the rice was delicious; the satays were very good. Overall a great experience. (4 stars)

I really wanted to like this place and it was good. The food was fine (the corn side and the scallop skewers were the standouts), the service was fine and the decor was beautiful. It was just an overall underwhelming dining experience...the prices were too high for the portion and quality. While I'm no expert on Indonesian food, I definitely wasn't enlightened by this dining experience. The dish I was excited to try thanks to the hype was the lobster noodles - they were ok. Everyone in my group agreed...we weren't upset by the meal. It was fine, but we all agreed that once was enough. (3 stars)

The ambiance is warm and inviting, making it a perfect spot for both casual dining and special occasions. Wenwen focuses on traditional Taiwanese cuisine, featuring a menu that highlights the diverse flavors and ingredients of the region. The restaurant emphasizes fresh, locally sourced ingredients and traditional cooking techniques.
menu_items: Pickled Cucumber Salad - Pineapple Juice, Garlic, Szechuan Pepper, Sesame Oil - $8
Sacha Hot Honey Popcorn Chicken - Garlic, Thai Basil, Taiwan Dust* - $14
Beef Stock Braised Tofu - 16-Hour Grass Fed Beef Broth Braise, Garlic, Scallion - $12
